Author: Wang, L.; Li, Q.; Xu, S.; Zhang, S.; Shao, W.; Wang, Q.
Title: A Decentralized Federated Learning Framework with Enhanced Privacy and Optimized Fairness
Publication Title: 2025 28th International Conference on Computer Supported Cooperative Work in Design (CSCWD)
Abstract Note: Federated Learning is a widely used distributed machine learning framework that allows clients to collaboratively train a global model by uploading local gradients while keeping data stored locally, thus protecting user privacy. However, attackers can still infer local data from gradients. Recently, integrating differential privacy into FL has become a popular approach to ensure strong privacy guarantees. This paper proposes a Decentralized Federated Learning Framework with Enhanced Privacy and Optimized Fairness (DFL-EPOF). First, noise is added to local parameters before uploading, and a local differential privacy mechanism ensures data privacy. An adaptive privacy budget allocation strategy, based on data sensitivity, dynamically controls noise levels to balance privacy protection and model accuracy. Second, a weighted aggregation method based on clients' data volume, trustworthiness, and participation frequency is used to optimize fairness, ensuring balanced contributions. Finally, a decentralized blockchain-based architecture is implemented to enhance transparency and immutability, ensuring reliable model updates and data transmission. Experimental results show that DFL-EPOF improves privacy protection, fairness, and system robustness, balancing privacy and accuracy effectively.

Author: Gurusamy, S. P.; Sharma, S.; V, A. K.
Title: Integrate Blockchain and Federated Learning Approaches to Secure Multi-Cloud Data Exchange: An AI-Powered Trust Management System
Publication Title: 2025 5th International Conference on Emerging Research in Electronics, Computer Science and Technology (ICERECT)
Abstract Note: Multi-cloud environments have emerged as one of the leading methods to manage large-scale, distributed and diverse-situated heterogeneous data across different industries (healthcare, finance, smart cities) in the age of digital transformation. On the other hand, this widespread exchange of data across cloud boundaries, also known as Data Mesh has unleashed large security and trust issues. Federated Learning (FL) is a decentralized machine learning paradigm that incorporates the privacy-preserving technique, allowing multiple parties to train AI models cooperatively without having to reveal the raw data. While FL offers several advantages due to decentralized training, it still faces some challenges like poisoning attacks, trust management and lack of accountability across clouds. Thus, this research provides an integrated framework combining Federated Learning and Blockchain technology for the first time rendering a stable, transparent, and AI infested trust management system among multi-cloud data transaction while countervailing all these impediments. The architecture proposes using the immutability and decentralized consensus of Blockchain to validate and record trust scores, model updates, as well as participant behavior in a federated network. Smart contracts are used to enforce fine-grained access control dynamically and incentivize data providers and cloud nodes to behave honestly. To train models across various data silos, we use Federated Learning and deploy an AI-driven trust engine that continuously assesses the credibility of nodes based on behavioral analytics as well as quality and historical performance of contribution. This framework guarantees data sovereignty, integrity and auditability while still preserving user privacy. Extensive simulations and empirical analysis show that the proposed system can effectively defend against adversarial threats (e. g., model poisoning, unauthorized access, data tampering). In addition, the federation system was significantly improved about integrity and performance under heterogeneous data and cloud environments with AI models integrated trust-aware functionality. The framework also enables dynamic trust reconfiguration based on emerging threats or policy changes, thereby ensuring long-term scalability and resilience. This research hence serves as a very strong model towards trustworthy multi-cloud ecosystems, closing the gap between secure AI collaboration and transparent data governance.

Author: Kumari, J.; N, P.
Title: Lung Cancer Detection with Privacy Preservation Using Federated Learning

Author: Nie, S.; Gao, Y.; Li, K.; You, B.; Jiang, P.
Title: Homomorphic Encryption Based Privacy Protection Scheme Design for Tourism Big Data

Abstract Note: With the rapid development of tourism big data, data privacy and security issues are becoming more and more prominent. Author: Zhang, Y.; Ma, Y.; Liu, W.; Pang, Y.; Wang, Y.; Yuan, H.
Title: Dual-Key Verifiable Secure Aggregation for Federated Learning via Blockchain
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain (Blockchain)
Abstract Note: Federated learning (FL) is a rising form of distributed machine learning in which individual clients train models on their own devices and then send the resulting parameters to a central server that builds a global model. FL nonetheless faces two central challenges: client parameters may leak private information, and malicious participants can make it hard to guarantee that the aggregated model is correct. To overcome these obstacles, we design a blockchain based verifiable secure aggregation method for privacy preserving federated learning (PPFL). First, local parameters are encrypted with the distributed two trapdoors public-Key cryptosystem (DT-PKC), which keeps them confidential. Second, because the approach works without any private negotiation among users, it naturally handles the issue of clients dropping out. Third, a homomorphic hash technique is used to verify that the server returns an authentic aggregate. Security analysis shows that the proposed method guards client privacy and preserves the integrity of the entire training pipeline. Experiments on the real world datasets MNIST and CIFAR 10 confirm that it raises computational efficiency by roughly 23 percent compared with the baseline.

Author: Balakumar, C.; Shanmugapriya, N.
Title: Privacy-Preserving Multi-Dimensional Trust Evaluation Model for Secure VANET Communications
Publication Title: 2025 Third International Conference on Emerging Applications of Material Science and Technology (ICEAMST)
Abstract Note: Vehicular Ad-hoc Networks (VANETs) serve as the foundation for Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) and provide communication between vehicles and infrastructure. However, they are essentially dynamic and distributed, possessing weak security that renders them susceptible to many security threats, including message tampering, packet loss, and insider attacks. The conventional trust model employs a unidimensional metric, resulting in elevated false positive rates, diminished accuracy in attack detection, and inadequate privacy preservation. Consequently, policy-aware systems must be privacy-conscious and reliable. PriMT-Eval (Privacypreserving) This research introduces a privacy-preserving multi-dimensional trust evaluation framework to improve secure communication in VANETs. Furthermore, the trust model evaluates a vehicle’s dependence by taking into account all pertinent factors, including Packet Forwarding Ratio (PFR), Message Integrity Check (MIC), Node Behavior Consistency (NBC), communication protocols (CPs), and response time (RT); additionally, it utilizes token mechanisms among adjacent vehicles. This approach facilitates a lightweight trust exchange employing pseudonym-based cryptographic techniques, supplemented by lightweight homomorphic encryption to safeguard the identities of the vehicles involved in the process. A weighted trust fusion method is utilized, integrating direct and indirect trust values to compute an overall trust value, hence facilitating the accurate identification of malicious nodes. Simulation results demonstrate that PriMT-Eval exhibits superiority with enhancements of up to \9 \textbackslash{}%\ and \14 \textbackslash{}%\ in accuracy and false positive rates, respectively, along with higher precision, recall, and F1-score compared to previous trust assessment methodologies. These significant findings indicate that PriMTEval enhances detection capabilities and offers a viable alternative to provide privacy and scalability in the high mobility of VANETs. The forthcoming task is to enhance PriMT-Eval by integrating blockchain for secure, tamperproof trust storage and implementing federated learning in extensive vehicle deployments.

Author: Huang, Y.
Title: Trust-Aware Blockchain Security with Differential Privacy and Zero-Knowledge Proof for Resilient Digital Economy Communication Ecosystems
Publication Title: 2025 7th International Conference on Innovative Data Communication Technologies and Application (ICIDCA)
Abstract Note: With the rapid expansion of the digital economy ecosystem, blockchain has become the core technology and theoretical path to support data interaction and trusted transactions. However, it still faces significant challenges in terms of privacy protection, transaction traceability and anti-attack capabilities. To address the above challenges, this study proposes a dynamic trust-aware blockchain security algorithm (DTBCSA) based on differential privacy and zero-knowledge proof. This algorithm is used to improve the system robustness and privacy protection capabilities in multiple scenarios. The core design of the algorithm includes: (1) introducing a dynamic trust evaluation mechanism. This mechanism dynamically adjusts the trust level of the node by analyzing its behavioral characteristics and historical interactions. At the same time, the secondary authentication mechanism is activated when the risk threshold is triggered; (2) embedding a differential privacy mechanism in the computing power transaction and model training process. This mechanism protects sensitive data and model parameters through Laplace noise; (3) using zero-knowledge proof to ensure the non-repudiation of transactions. At the same time, the aggregation and parallel optimization strategies are adopted to significantly reduce the computational overhead of proof and verification. In the experimental part, DTBCSA reduced the acceptance rate of malicious transactions from 70% of the baseline to 8% in the computing power trading market simulation. At the same time, it reduced the reputation distribution imbalance (Gini) from 0.42 to 0.20. Author: Pandian, G.; Kesavan, K.
Title: Implementing a Decentralized Trust Management System with Machine Learning for Real-Time Device Authentication: The Role of Blockchain in Ensuring Secure IoT Networks
Publication Title: 2025 Global Conference in Emerging Technology (GINOTECH)
Abstract Note: The rapid expansion of the Internet of Things (IoT) poses essential security challenges, especially in relation to device authentication and trust management. Moreover, centralized authentication approaches pose significant single points of failure, latency issues, as well as risks due to DDoS (Distributed-Denial-of-Service) and MITM (man-in-the- middle) attacks. In this work, we aim to overcome these limitations and propose a Decentralized Trust Management System based on the Blockchain and Machine Learning for real-time device authentication in an IoT network. It is important to acknowledge that the permissioned integration of blockchain ensures immutability, transparency, and decentralized authority without a centralized trust authority. At the same time, machine learning models are used to compute device trust scores dynamically, relying on the behavioral analysis, the anomalies detected, and the historical interactions. This mechanism uses smart contracts to facilitate the trust assessment process and authenticate devices, therefore minimizing third-party reliance. A consensus mechanism adapted to IoT scenarios, like lightweight Proof-of- Authority (PoA) or Delegated Proof-of-Stake (DPoS), is adopted to maximize energy efficiency and accelerate transaction validation. The machine learning aspect involves using various algorithms for anomaly detection, including Support Vector Machines (SVM), Random Forest (RF), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to spot malicious or compromised devices in real-time. We conduct a proof of concept on a simulated IoT testbed to evaluate the effectiveness of the DTMS against unauthorized access, authentication latency, and network resilience. Evaluation, including accuracy, precision, recall and computational overhead show that integration of blockchain and machine learning can substantially secure and scalable IoT authentication frameworks. This will help improve the security of the IoT networks, as the presented trust-based, decentralized authentication framework autonomously identifies and neutralizes security attacks. In the future, optimialization in federated learning for distributed trust calculation, implementation of zero-knowledge proofs for privacy-preserving authentication, and the use of quantum-resistant cryptographic techniques in a blockchain system may provide richer development in this domain. The results underscore the promise of the blockchain-based decentralized, trust management systems for establishing a secure, robust and scalable security paradigm for next-generation, IoT networks.

Author: Sutaria, K.; S, M.; Paliwal, M.; Dange, P.
Title: Decentralized Federated Learning Framework with Blockchain for Verifiable and Trusted Collaboration
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Knowledge Engineering and Communication Systems (ICKECS)
Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) is an innovative distributed machine learning approach that allows multiple participants to collaboratively train a global model without sharing their private data. While effective, traditional FL frameworks often rely on centralized servers for model aggregation, making them susceptible to single points of failure, security breaches, and trust concerns. To address these challenges, this paper introduces a Decentralized Federated Learning Framework (DFLF) integrated with blockchain technology. The proposed framework eliminates the need for a central coordinator by utilizing blockchain’s immutable ledger and decentralized architecture. This integration ensures secure model sharing, verifiable updates, and incentivized collaboration among participants. Smart contracts automate key operations, including model aggregation, contribution validation, and reward distribution, thereby enhancing efficiency and transparency. The framework was implemented using a permissioned blockchain and tested on a healthcare dataset for patient diagnosis prediction. Experimental results demonstrate improved model accuracy, reduced latency, and enhanced trust compared to conventional FL approaches. The inclusion of blockchain ensures robust privacy preservation and builds trust in collaborative machine learning. This paper provides a comprehensive analysis of the framework, including its design, algorithms, mathematical formulations, and performance metrics. The results highlight the potential of combining blockchain with FL to establish a scalable, secure, and trustworthy ecosystem for decentralized machine learning applications.

Author: Li, B.; Xu, Z.; Zhang, Y.; Wang, H.
Title: Privacy-Preserving Blockchain-Enabled Vertical Federated Learning with Data Auditing
Publication Title: 2025 44th International Symposium on Reliable Distributed Systems (SRDS)
Abstract Note: Vertical Federated Learning (VFL) is a trending distributed learning paradigm that facilitates collaborative model training over feature-partitioned datasets while preserving data privacy. Traditional VFL heavily relies on a central coordinator, leading to single points of failure and risks of data tampering. Integrating blockchain to build a decentralized VFL is a promising solution to these issues, thereby ensuring the integrity of the training process and contributing to reliable model performance. However, the conflict between decentralization and the privacy requirements of VFL introduces new privacy risks. Moreover, blockchain inherently cannot provide robustness against low-quality data to prevent model accuracy degradation. To address the above issues in privacy and robustness, we propose BVFed, a privacy-preserving blockchain-enabled VFL framework with built-in data auditing capabilities. Specifically, BVFed leverages multiparty homomorphic encryption improved with secret sharing to enable privacy-preserving decentralized training with no single point of failure. To further enhance robustness against low-quality data, we design a data-auditable aggregate computation method to continuously evaluate the data contribution of each party and precisely adjust aggregation weights accordingly, without compromising data privacy. Rigorous security analysis and extensive experiments demonstrate that BVFed provides strong privacy guarantees and significantly improves system robustness with acceptable overhead.

Author: O, A. A.; Rajkumar, N.
Title: Enhancing Data Privacy and Security in Online Interaction Through Federated Learning and Differential Privacy
Publication Title: 2025 8th International Conference on Computing Methodologies and Communication (ICCMC)
Abstract Note: Social media platforms gather huge amounts of user-generated data to provide personalized content, but this data collection would cause severe privacy breaches. This paper introduces a decentralized learning system utilizing Federated Learning (FL) and Differential Privacy (DP) to provide privacy-preserving content recommendation. Unlike the conventional systems, our design trains models locally at the users' devices and applies differentially private noise before aggregating updates. We deploy the system with TensorFlow Federated and TensorFlow Privacy and test it with a synthetic dataset of user interaction behaviors. The system has over 90% top-k recommendation quality with a privacy budget ε = 0.5. We also compare performance with Laplace and Gaussian mechanisms, study utility-privacy trade-offs, and illustrate how our method considerably lowers privacy leakage risk with no compromise in personalization quality. This system provides an scalable solution for ethical social media personalization and in line with international data protection standards.

Author: Liao, B.-S.; Li, J.-S.; Liu, I.-H.; Liu, C.-K.
Title: Blockchain-Based Adaptive Historical Averaging for Client Dropout Resilience in Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2025 Seventh International Symposium on Computer, Consumer and Control (IS3C)
Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as an innovative paradigm that enables heterogeneous and geographically distributed clients to collaboratively train models in a decentralized and privacy-preserving manner. However, FL systems face numerous challenges in real-world deployments, particularly passive participation caused by malicious attacks, where clients drop out due to attacks. This issue, though not intentionally designed by the system, significantly impacts training stability. In this study, we propose BAHA-FL (Blockchain-based Adaptive Historical Averaging Federated Learning. Our approach integrates adaptive historical averaging with exponential decay weighting to effectively compensate for missing parameters due to client dropouts. Author: Bhamidipati, S. C.; Alarcon, M. L.; Kuchar, T.; Bernal, J. R.; Calyam, P.
Title: FedSecRPM: Federated Learning-Based Analytics for Sensor-Based Remote Patient Monitoring
Publication Title: 2025 Annual Computer Security Applications Conference Workshops (ACSAC Workshops)
Abstract Note: As wearable sensor technologies proliferate, remote patient monitoring (RPM) systems must ensure timely, secure, and privacy-preserving data analysis to support effective healthcare delivery. Current approaches in healthcare tend to centralize patient data for analysis, which increases risks to data security and privacy. This model also restricts patients’ ability to access and engage with their health information. Additionally, sharing data across institutions becomes complicated due to stringent privacy regulations, making effective collaboration challenging. In this paper, we address these gaps and propose FedSecRPM, a novel architecture combining: (i) federated learning at the edge to analyze data directly from wearable devices, enhancing privacy and security by keeping data local; (ii) an LLM-based chatbot that empowers patients to interact with the system and receive personalized health insights; and (iii) blockchain-based data access management to enforce HIPAA-compliant privacy and security controls. We demonstrate FedSecRPM’s feasibility through a case study on medication response classification using continuous fluid monitoring (CFM) data. Our results demonstrate how federated edge analytics preserves privacy without sacrificing utility, the LLM-based chatbot improves patient engagement, and blockchain mechanisms provide robust, auditable access control for regulated data-use scenarios.

Author: Su, J.; Guo, S.
Title: Chain-Verified Optimized Byzantine Fault-Tolerant Consensus Mechanism for Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2025 5th International Conference on Computer Science and Blockchain (CCSB)
Abstract Note: Traditional federated learning relies on centralized servers for model aggregation, which suffers from single points of failure and trustworthiness vulnerabilities. Blockchain technology, leveraging its decentralized and tamper-resistant properties, provides a distributed trust solution for federated learning. However, the open network architecture still exposes the system to persistent security threats. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an improved consensus scheme based on the Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance algorithm tailored for decentralized federated learning scenarios. In response to security threats posed by malicious nodes forging data or tampering with model update paths during distributed federated learning node collaboration, the proposed scheme reconstructs the submission verification process of traditional PBFT by integrating blockchain technology. This involves embedding chained pointers and a node identity public key verification mechanism into the message structure to enable integrity checks of model transmission paths, thereby preventing malicious nodes from altering parameter update routes. Additionally, a pre-verification phase is introduced during the consensus process, simplifying the original multi-round communication into a two-stage interaction and significantly reducing network overhead. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves higher fault tolerance, lower average consensus latency, and improved consensus throughput, validating its effectiveness in enhancing the security and efficiency of decentralized federated learning systems. Author: Sankaran, S.

Author: Babu, K. R.; Ramesh, M.; Prasuna, M. G.; Kumar, G. G.; Priya, R. B.; Pradhan, A.
Title: Adaptive Multimodal Federated Optimization with Privacy and Blockchain Trust
Publication Title: 2025 9th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
Abstract Note: This article presents the Adaptive Multi-Modal Federated Optimization (AMMFO) framework which was developed to tackle important challenges in data privacy, fairness, and accountability in learning in the context of federated learning. Author: S, S.; D, K. K.; P, J.; Kodhai, E.
Title: Advancing Data Heterogeneity Solutions in Blockchain-Enabled Federated Learning for IoT
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) offers a collaborative approach to training machine learning models across distributed devices without compromising user privacy. However, a persistent hurdle in its implementation is data heterogeneity— the uneven and diverse data distributions across participating devices—which becomes particularly challenging in Internet of Things (IoT) networks. By combining FL with blockchain, researchers have introduced decentralized, secure, and transparent methods to tackle these issues, yet several gaps and difficulties remain. This paper takes a fresh approach by compiling and analyzing the wide array of proposed solutions and ongoing challenges for managing data heterogeneity in blockchain-integrated FL systems, focusing on their relevance to IoT. We discuss techniques which seem feasible: personalization federated learning through group clustering of devices; adaptive aggregation methods; and blockchain-based reputation systems. In addition, they are mechanism-like reward-based participation and context-aware frameworks, to combat imbalance and thereby enhance fairness in heterogeneous systems. There are still unaddressed issues, including scalability, size of FL networks in blockchain, efficiency versus performance trade-offs, and, above all, the challenge of ensuring that heterogeneous systems can interoperate. By presenting an interconnected review of advances and bottlenecks, the current work is able to inform future developments of resilient and scalable FL systems for IoT applications.

Author: Zheng, X.; Yan, X.; Yang, F.; Ng, W. W. Y.; Li, Y.; Wu, S.
Title: Privacy-Preserving and Poisoning-Resilient Enhanced Cross-Silo Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
Abstract Note: Federated learning (FL) allows multiple parties to train an efficient deep-learning model collaboratively, without disclosing their data. However, there are two critical issues in FL: the privacy leakage of the gradient/trained model and the vulnerability to poisoning attacks. Existing methods are designed for cross-device FL, where the aggregator usually has access to the global model, which does not hold in cross-silo FL. Moreover, many existing privacy-preserving approaches continue to incur substantial computational and communication overheads. To overcome these limitations, we propose a privacypreserving and poisoning-resilient enhanced cross-silo federated learning, called P3RE-FL. Specifically, we design a suite of protocols, including a secure comparison protocol, a secure Euclidean distance computation protocol, a secure cosine distance computation protocol, leveraging secret sharing and masking techniques. The P3RE-FL scheme, built upon the above protocols, enables multi-metric poisoning detection with low computational and communication overhead while preserving privacy. Finally, a comprehensive security analysis and theoretical evaluation are conducted to demonstrate our scheme’s security and practicality. Experimental results on three benchmark datasets further validate the effectiveness of our scheme in detecting poisoned models, even as the proportion of malicious clients increases.

Author: Hossain, S.; Mohiuddin, M.; Iqbal, A.; Ontor, M. R. H.; Sarwar, M. G.; Tanvirahmedshuvo
Title: Integrated Privacy and Data Integrity Framework for IoT and Enterprise Systems to Enhance Secure Supply Chain Operations Through Federated Analytics and Differential Privacy

Federated Analytics enables the analysis of data in distributed networks in a collaborative manner without centralizing the data, and hence minimizing the chances of data breaches. At the same time, Differential Privacy methods protect the data of individuals by adding noise, which makes it impossible to identify particular information. The proposed framework has been shown to be effective in addressing the privacy threat, maintaining the integrity of data, and ensuring effective and efficient supply chain management, using simulation studies. The study contributes to the design of privacy-sensitive protocols of IoTbased systems, which would enhance trust and security in the modern supply chains

Author: Deng, X.; Yang, J.

Author: Gaspar, J.; Ribeiro, B.; Pessoa, J.; Martinho, D.; Santos, J.; Marreiros, G.
Title: Local Vs Server Differential Privacy Analysis Regarding the Trade-Off Between Security and Recommendation Quality

Author: Chen, F.; Li, Y.
Title: A Blockchain-driven and Verifiable Collaborative Paradigm for Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Data Management and Computer Science (ICDMCS)
Abstract Note: While Federated Learning (FL) preserves user privacy by keeping data local, its dependence on a central server creates critical weaknesses, including a single point of failure (SPoF), system bottlenecks, and potential malicious manipulation. Moreover, existing FL frameworks often lack transparent, fair, and automated incentive mechanisms, limiting the formation of a sustainable and trustworthy collaborative ecosystem. To overcome these challenges, we propose EcoFL, a blockchain-driven and verifiable collaborative paradigm for federated learning. EcoFL incorporates three key innovations:(1) Decentralized aggregation and governance, which replaces the central server with blockchain consensus, eliminating SPoF and ensuring rule enforcement through smart contracts. (2) A fair and privacy-preserving contribution evaluation model, which quantitatively assesses each participant’s contribution based on verifiable model feedback. (3) A dynamic token-based incentive mechanism, which automatically rewards honest contributors and penalizes malicious or low-quality behavior. Our theoretical analysis and prototype experiments show that EcoFL not only mitigates the security and trust limitations of centralized FL but also establishes a fair, autonomous, and sustainable foundation for collaborative learning, while maintaining competitive model performance.

Author: Wang, X.; Tian, L.; Yang, C.; Lin, F.; Li, M.
Title: Enhancing Federated Learning under Partial Participation via Proportional Variance Reduction
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 24th International Conference on Trust, Security and Privacy in Computing and Communications (TrustCom)
Abstract Note: Federated learning is a distributed learning framework with privacy protection; however, data heterogeneity poses significant challenges for federated training. Due to heterogeneous data, client models tend to overfit their local datasets during local training, leading to client drift. Variance reduction-based methods are currently the most popular solutions for addressing client drift; however, their performance deteriorates significantly under low client participation rates. We analyze the limitations of existing variance reduction techniques and attribute them to control variate drift and imbalanced global correction. To address these issues and further constrain client drift, we propose an easy-realization yet effective solution: Federated Proportional Variance Reduction (FedPVR). Specifically, we scale both client gradients and client control variates by a factor that is matched to the client participation rate. This can be viewed as replacing the outdated gradient information associated with each client in the global control variate with their most recent gradients, thereby deriving a closer overall update direction. This approach helps mitigate both client drift and the additional variance introduced by the staleness of control variates. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach under partial client participation. Specifically, under limited client involvement, our method achieves an average accuracy improvement of 2–3% compared to baseline methods and further accelerates the convergence rate.
Manual Tags: Federated Learning; Data Heterogeneity; Client Partial Participation; Variance Reduction

Author: N.Padmashri; V.V.Karthikeyan; P.Sumathi; Potnuru, S. K.; Aswathy, P. B.; V.Baby
Title: Blockchain and Federated Learning for Safe Collaborative Machine Learning Systems with Differential Privacy
Publication Title: 2025 5th International Conference on Emerging Research in Electronics, Computer Science and Technology (ICERECT)
Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) is a way to train a shared model using data from many different devices or users without actually sharing the raw data itself. This helps protect privacy and makes the process more efficient by reducing the need to move large amounts of data. However, FL still has some security risks, such as model inversion attacks, where someone tries to guess the original data, and poisoning attacks, where bad data is introduced to mess up the model. Also, if the person or system that combines the models isn't trusted, it could be a problem. This paper introduces a new system that combines Differential Privacy and Blockchain technology into the FL process. Differential Privacy adds a little bit of random noise to the model updates so that individual data points can't be guessed. Blockchain keeps a secure, transparent record of all the model changes and verifies who is involved. Testing this system on standard datasets shows that it makes the model more resistant to attacks without significantly lowering its performance. This setup is especially useful in areas like healthcare, finance, and smart cities, where keeping data private and secure is very important.

Author: Kamble, S.; Gourshettiwar, P.
Title: Blockchain and AI Synergy: The SecNet Approach to CPS Data Challenges

While data has the potential to enrich an organization, it also presents issues related to privacy, ownership, and security. Author: Nara, N.; Jyothsna, V.
Title: IoT Security Landscape: A Review of Threat Detection, Trust Management and Resilient Communication
Publication Title: 2025 4th International Conference on Innovative Mechanisms for Industry Applications (ICIMIA)
Abstract Note: Internet of Things is a quickly emerging disruptive technology where billions of heterogeneous devices are connecting in a wide range of domains. Title: Trustless and Incentivized Federated Learning with Blockchain and zk-SNARKs: A Design-First Framework for Privacy-Sensitive Domains

Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) gives opportunity to decentralized model training without the raw data's revealing. But in actual real-world implementation faces certain number of challenges. These include trust in client updates, verifiable end-to-end privacy promises, equitable contributor compensation, and accountable aggregation. This paper provides a design-first architecture that addresses these issues by integrating concise zero-knowledge proofs (zk-SNARKs) for trustless verification with smart-contract arrangements. Our design is consisting a structure of five-layer stack, named as Client, Proof, Blockchain, Incentive, and Governance. We specify clearly smart-contract interfaces called as aggregation, registry, incentivization, zk-circuit objectives, and several scaling controls like proofs/aggregated in batch or Layer-2/rollup rollouts and the anchor-Merkel. The design also implements Shapley-like contribution measures and ERC-compact reward settlement. It incorporates Sybil-resistance and vesting primitives to lean against game. We define a crisp threat model, discuss security and privacy trade-offs, and suggest evaluation using healthcare and IoT benchmarks. Moreover, by training and incentivization by smart contracts at design level, we create a foundation for future prototyping and rigorous empiric testing. Title: Federated Learning for Enhancing Internet-of-Drones Security: Formulation, Simulation, and Future Directions
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
Abstract Note: The Internet of Drones (IoD) connects unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) through networked communication to support coordinated sensing and mission execution across diverse applications. However, wireless exposure, high mobility, and limited onboard computation and energy resources make IoD systems vulnerable to cyber and cyber-physical attacks. This paper examines how federated learning (FL), which keeps raw data on-device, can support privacy-preserving security analytics for IoD deployments. We summarize the IoD threat surface and privacy requirements, then present a concise formulation that links the local model, binary cross-entropy (BCE) loss, aggregation rule, and per-round communication cost. Finally, we report a reference simulation based on Federated Averaging (FedAvg) and track per-round test accuracy, BCE loss, and communication cost using both a parameter-count estimate and measured bytes from a lightweight simulated networking layer.
Manual Tags: federated learning; security; privacy; machine learning; artificial intelligence; drones; IoD

Author: Kasu, V. R.; Deepalakshmi, P.
Title: Secure Data Transmission in Decentralized and Distributed Systems using Federated Learning and Blockchain for the Preservation of Individual Privacy
Publication Title: 2025 Global Conference in Emerging Technology (GINOTECH)
Abstract Note: The issue of secured data transmission in decentralized and distributed systems is still a challenge that needs to be solved in order to provide privacy of the individual as well as the integrity and security of the data. This makes traditional centralized approaches vulnerable to sensitive information leaks and unauthorized access, thus warranting investigation of more alternative privacy-preserving methodologies. In this paper, we propose a novel secure & privacy-preserving data transmission framework by integrating the advantage of federated learning and the benefit of blockchain technology. This means that data stays on the device and is not shared with the central vote processor, all but eliminating the risks of data centralisation. The incorporation of blockchain technology adds an extra layer of data security with its immutable and transparent nature, along with decentralized consensus algorithms, which prevent unauthorized changes and build trust among entities involved. We present a new framework that utilizes smart contracts to automate the process of regulating data access and enforcing privacy-protective policies while guaranteeing compliance with data governance policies. Furthermore, cryptographic approaches like homomorphic encryption or differential privacy have been integrated into these methodologies to protect data confidentiality and allow secure collaborative learning over distributed nodes. It leverages an optimized consensus algorithm to strike a balance between security and computational efficiency, alleviating latency concerns often related to blockchain solutions. Moreover, experimental assessments validate that the unification of federated learning—supported by blockchain—enhances data protection without compromising model accuracy and scalability over different networks. Results show that this method can both mitigate the risks of centralizing data storage and reduce vulnerability to adversarial attacks, while still keeping people’s individual privacy intact without degrading system performance.
Manual Tags: Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning; Homomorphic Encryption; Secure Model Aggregation; Differential Privacy; Edge Computing; Adversarial Attack Mitigation; Secure Multi-Party Computation; Data Integrity; Consensus Algorithms; Internet of Things (IoT) Security

Author: Liu, X.; Ding, H.; Cui, X.; Liu, J.; Piao, X.; Song, H.
Title: Efficient Distributed PV Power Prediction via Blockchain-Driven Personalized Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
Abstract Note: Accurate prediction of distributed photovoltaic (PV) power generation is crucial for efficient grid integration and energy management. Traditional centralized models often face challenges related to data privacy, heterogeneity, and transparency. This paper proposes an innovative framework that integrates blockchain technology with personalized federated learning (PFL) to address these issues in PV power prediction. In our approach, each participating node trains a local model on its dataset, preserving data privacy. Model updates are then securely aggregated using blockchain, ensuring transparency and immutability. This decentralized methodology accommodates the unique characteristics of each node's data, leading to improved predictin accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms traditional centralized and non-personalized federated learning models. The integration of blockchain enhances data security and fosters trust among stakeholders. These findings underscore the potential of combining blockchain-driven personalized federated learning to advance distributed PV power prediction systems.
Manual Tags: blockchain; federated learning; power prediction

Author: Ali, M. S. M.; Manhosh, M. M.; Alwahhab, A. B. A.; Srayyih, F. H.; Ahmed, M.; Al-kharaz, A. A.; Al-Mahmood, A.; Madhi, A. A.; Ahmed, M. R.
Title: Federated Learning for Financial Forecasting: A Privacy-Preserving Approach to Decentralized Data Sharin
Publication Title: 2025 3rd International Conference on Business Analytics for Technology and Security (ICBATS)
Abstract Note: This project examines the use of federated learning for financial forecasting, which focuses on a better prediction with privacy. Data aggregation in centralized models can break confidentiality, notably in finance. Our study offers a federated learning (FL) paradigm utilizing long short-term memory (LSTM) networks whereby diverse financial institutions collectively train strong forecasting models without data sharing. We employed NASDAQ-100 and S&P 500 datasets and utilized a differentially private LSTM network leveraging secure multiparty computing. The data reveal that performing an averaging federated (FedAvg) model was much superior to centralized and decentralized models with lower MAE and RMSE. The model's R2 values of 0.92 show its ability to capture the market's complexity and perform well. This framework secures privacy and enables scalability for realtime financial forecasting. According to our findings, federated learning has the ability to substantially impact the banking industry and give an accurate and secure alternative to the existing approaches. Future studies will aim at including sophisticated privacy-preserving approaches and increasing model applications across varied financial datasets.

Author: Fikri, M. L.; Lin, Y.; Du, Z.; Bao, W.; Wu, C.
Title: Enhancing Blockchain Scalability in Federated Learning: Sharding and Multithreading Approaches in Hyperledger Fabric
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Radio Frequency and Antenna Technologies (iWRF&AT)
Abstract Note: Blockchain technology has emerged as a promising solution for enhancing privacy and security in decentralized systems, particularly within the domain of federated learning. Federated Learning (FL) enables the collaborative generation of machine learning models while preserving user privacy by keeping data localized. Integrating blockchain with FL ensures trusted participation and safeguards against data tampering. However, blockchain networks face significant scalability challenges, known as the scalability trilemma. This research addresses these limitations by implementing sharding and multithreading techniques within Hyperledger Fabric to optimize its performance. The sharding partitions the blockchain network, enhancing its scalability, while multithreading improves resource utilization during transaction processing. The proposed framework is evaluated across three scenarios: roundrobin sharding, task-based sharding, and no-sharding. Results indicate that task-based sharding outperforms other approaches, achieving an optimal balance between system scalability and resource efficiency. This study provides valuable insights into the trade-offs between performance and resource allocation in blockchain-based federated learning systems.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; Decentralized Machine Learning; High-Performance Computing; Multithreading

Author: Yu, X.; Li, J.; Lu, Y.; Wu, C.; Chen, X.; Ni, Y.
Title: Generative Large Model Validation Mechanism for Blockchain Federated Learning Technology

Abstract Note: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) technology, more and more difficulties have been encountered in solving “data silos” and realizing data value sharing. In this paper, we propose a federated training scheme based on federated learning, by introducing the generative large model verification mechanism into federated learning and optimizing the encrypted communication technology, we design a set of efficient FedPT algorithms, which can effectively solve the problems of the existing federated learning technology in practical applications.

Author: Gupta, V.
Title: Blockchain-Enabled Access Control Framework for Federated Learning in IoT Environments
Publication Title: 2025 First International Conference of Advances in Engineering and Computing Technologies for Sustainable Development (AECTSD)
Abstract Note: The unprecedented opportunities of distributed intelligence and the severe security and data exchange challenges have been posed by the high rate of the development of the Internet of Things (IoT) devices. Federated Learning (FL) enables training models on decentralized IoT devices without having to gain access to raw data but is susceptible to unauthorized access, poisoning, and manipulation in distributing model updates. The purpose of the paper is to create a Framework of Blockchain-based Access Control (BAC-FL): a framework that integrates smart contracts, decentralized identification, and cryptographic verification as a model of exchange of updates into the model in a safe fashion. The empirical evaluation of the framework is conducted on a private Ethereum based test network and an IoT simulation set up of 1,000 devices. It has been shown that there is an increase of 34percentage points in secure access control and decline of 22percentage points in unauthorized update attempts, threshold degradation of less than three percent in model accuracy, and no significant degradation (less than one percent) in model accuracy compared to baseline FL. The latency of transactions was not very high in the IoT setting. The findings prove the application of blockchain as a useful tool in the application of trustful FL in the heterogeneous IoT ecosystems. The next step, which is scaling and cross-chain interoperability, will be optimized.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; Federated Learning; IoT; Accuracy

The research findings indicate that the amalgamation of machine learning and federated learning can substantially improve the identification and mitigation of security threats in both blockchain systems and devices. This paper provides significant insights into the advancement of more resilient and intelligent security strategies, thereby promoting the secure adoption of these rapidly evolving technologies. Author: Balan, S.; Thilagavathi, K.; Raman, P.; Pundir, S.; Rakesh, R.; Manikandan, G.

The system’s efficacy in enhancing model accuracy, operational efficiency, and trustworthiness, while simultaneously ensuring robust data privacy and security, is demonstrated by experiments. Author: Adhikari, T.; Sen, D.; Shaw, M.; Dey, D.; Das, A.; Hoque, F.

Abstract Note: Healthcare, transportation, and smart cities marked revolutionary growth in the market. The decentralized, scalable function of IoT devices leaves them uniquely at risk of cyberattacks or breaches. Many security schemes depend on centralized approaches that just don’t fit in this scenario. A technology like blockchain addresses existing security concerns by facilitating automation using smart contracts and secure communication. This article offers a coherent and thoughtful exposition on the growing security threats to IoT. It addresses gaps in IoT architecture and configuration within pseudo-omnichannels. The discussion further emphasizes latency, energy efficiency of connected devices, and the costs tied to rigid cyber infrastructures that may fall short. The impacts of security are examined using frameworks dependent on artificial intelligence, lightweight blockchains, and post-quantum cryptography as a basis of secure omnichannel architecture. Author: Shabana, S.; Kumar, H. S. Ranjan; Raju, K.; Puttegowda, K.
Title: Homomorphic Encryption for Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning in Medical Applications
Publication Title: 2025 5th International Conference on Mobile Networks and Wireless Communications (ICMNWC)
Abstract Note: The growing reliance on machine learning (ML) in healthcare raises critical concerns regarding data privacy and security. While federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training without centralized data sharing, it remains vulnerable to inference attacks through model gradients and unauthorized access by third parties. To address these challenges, this work proposes a privacy-preserving federated learning framework that integrates homomorphic encryption (HE) with logistic regression for secure medical data analysis. In the proposed approach, local model parameters are encrypted using homomorphic schemes before aggregation on a centralized server, ensuring that neither raw data nor model updates are exposed. Experimental evaluation with BFV, BGV, and CKKS encryption schemes demonstrates that the framework achieves competitive accuracy (\textbackslash{}gt 85 \textbackslash{}%\) while safeguarding patient information. Among the tested schemes, BGV provided the highest accuracy (\textbackslash{}sim 89.81 \textbackslash{}%\), whereas BFV achieved optimal training efficiency. The results highlight that combining federated learning with homomorphic encryption can effectively balance model performance and data confidentiality, making it a promising solution for privacy-preserving healthcare applications.
Manual Tags: privacy-preserving machine learning; secure multi-party computation; medical data security; logistic regression; encrypted model aggregation; healthcare data privacy

Author: Olajobi, T.
Title: Towards Secure Coordination in Multiagent Systems: Privacy-Preserving Techniques

Abstract Note: Multi-agent systems (MAS) are positioned among the major technical advances of distributed artificial intelligence, whereby independent agents can cooperate and coordinate to meet complex and evolving tasks. But the privacy problem is also of considerable importance, especially in situations where sensitive information is to be subjected to sharing because of the given decentralization and heterogeneity of the MAS in question. The paper is a critical study of the literature on the privacy-preserving techniques (PPTs) to ensure safe and secure coordination of the designs of the MAS. The most significant of these, including the technique of differential privacy, the secure multiparty computation, homomorphic encryption, federated learning and blockchain integration, are also dealt with critically from the point of view of their suitability in the different fields treated respectively by the way of example. These include health care, smart grids, autonomous vehicles and swarm robots. The review sense of depth will be found from the elaboration of the many definitions of privacy for the purposes of MAS design and implementation. The paper will also attempt to identify gaps in the literature and suggest future lines of research in terms of how it relates to the MAs designed.

Author: N, P. S.; Shelke, N.; Saini, D. K. J. B.; Pimpalkar, A.; Pal, M.; Chirchi, V.
Title: Explainable Federated Learning for Secure and Transparent Medical Diagnosis in IoT-based Smart Hospitals
Publication Title: 2025 5th International Conference on Soft Computing for Security Applications (ICSCSA)
Abstract Note: The fast uptake of IoT-enabled medical devices to create smart hospitals has revolutionized healthcare delivery, affording real-time monitoring and personalized diagnostics. But, the central training of AI models based on patient data raises serious issues of privacy, transparency, and trust. This work proposes an Explainable Federated Learning (XFL) framework that jointly integrates Explainable AI (XAI) mechanisms with Federated Learning (FL) to enable a secure, privacy-preserving, interpretable medical diagnostic across decentralized healthcare systems. The proposed XFL framework uses edge-based federated optimization to train deep neural models on decentralized patient data, maintaining the locality of that data. The framework enables mutual co-existence of model-agnostic explainability mechanisms such as SHAP and LIME which generate human-comprehensible justifications for a diagnostic decision, improving clinical trust and accountability. To enhance model robustness and confidentiality of the data, we integrate differential privacy, secure aggregation, and lightweight blockchain logging, allowing for auditability and protection against adversarial attacks. We provide experiments using real-world healthcare datasets such as COVIDx and MIMIC-III to demonstrate that our framework can build diagnostic models with competitive accuracy, while providing strong privacy assurances and information for clinicians. This work responds to an urgent requirement in AI-enabled healthcare; not only should it ensure what a model predicts, but also why, so that smart hospital ecosystems may be ethically aligned, safe, and transparent.
Manual Tags: Differential Privacy; Secure Aggregation; Blockchain and Healthcare data security; Explainable Federated Learning (XFL)

Author: Shah, K.; Kumari, A.; Solanki, B.; Al-Humairi, S. N. S.; Al-Hakimi, A. M. H.
Title: ZTSec-FedSDN: A Privacy-Preserving Federated Framework for SDN Attack Detection Using Zero-Trust Blockchain and 6G Terahertz Networks
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Computer, Information and Telecommunication Systems (CITS)
Abstract Note: This research presents ZTSec-FedSDN, a privacy-preserving federated framework for SDN attack detection that integrates zero-trust blockchain architecture with 6G terahertz networks. The framework enables collaborative training of Deep Neural Network models across distributed clients while maintaining data privacy and leveraging the high-speed capabilities of 6G terahertz communication. Using the SDNFlow dataset containing diverse network traffic patterns and attack types, we implement four federated optimization strategies: Federated Averaging (FedAvg), Federated Proximal (FedProx), Federated Adam (FedAdam), and Federated Adagrad (FedAdagrad). The zero-trust blockchain layer provides an immutable ledger for recording and verifying model updates, ensuring transparency and trustworthiness in the federated learning process. The integration with 6G terahertz networks enables ultra-low latency communication between federated clients, crucial for real-time intrusion detection in SDN environments. Multiple clients collaboratively train the shared DNN model on local traffic data without exposing sensitive information, preserving data privacy while benefiting from collective intelligence. This work systematically evaluates the performance of different federated learning algorithms by comparing model accuracy, convergence speed, robustness, and efficacy in multi-class network attack classification. The results provide comprehensive insights into each optimizer’s suitability for secure, transparent, and trustworthy intrusion detection systems in next-generation SDN environments powered by 6G terahertz networks.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; Federated Learning (FL); Software-Defined Networking (SDN); Deep Neural Networks (DNNs)

Author: Ren, D.; Hong, S.; Li, M.
Title: Exploration of rice disease data sharing scheme based on blockchain and federal learning
Publication Title: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
Abstract Note: Rice diseases severely impact rice yield and quality, posing threats to food security and agricultural economies. Traditional manual identification of rice diseases exhibits multiple limitations, while deep learning, despite its potential, faces challenges in agricultural applications such as insufficient data volume, uneven data distribution, and data privacy-security concerns. This study proposes a rice disease data sharing and privacy protection scheme by integrating blockchain technology with a federated learning framework. Leveraging blockchain’s decentralized and tamper-proof features to replace traditional federated learning’s centralized servers, the approach employs smart contracts for global model aggregation. A differential privacy mechanism is introduced to process model parameters, ensuring data privacy protection. Experimental results demonstrate that this solution effectively safeguards data privacy without compromising federated learning accuracy, while enhancing data utilization efficiency and sharing effectiveness, thereby providing robust technical support for the advancement of smart agriculture.

Author: Khatri, R.; Pandey, P.; Pachauri, R.
Title: Blockchain-Enabled Federated Learning for Realtime Energy Prediction Using Stackelberg-Shapley-Based Privacy-Conscious Coalition Strategies
Publication Title: 2025 World Conference on Cutting-Edge Science and Technology (WCCEST)
Abstract Note: This research tackles the challenges of non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data, socio-political inequalities in decentralized energy networks, and the unpredictable nature of renewable energy sources. It integrates blockchain technology with federated learning (FL) and game theory. Cluster-based FL paired with Shapley value allocation helps mitigate data heterogeneity, while a combined Stackelberg-Shapley model implemented via smart contracts facilitates adaptive pricing strategies. To safeguard user privacy, the system incorporates zero-knowledge proofs, differential privacy \(\textbackslash{}varepsilon=0.5)\, and CKKS-based homomorphic encryption, achieving a 98% resistance rate against cyberattacks. Field tests in the EU's NER400 sandbox and blockchain-enabled microgrids in Kenya confirm the framework's effectiveness—achieving a 4.2% mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) in forecasting (improving from a 12% benchmark), curbing renewable energy certificate (REC) fraud by 89%, and cutting rural energy expenses by 40%. Leveraging a hybrid consensus model (PBFT with Sharding), the platform supports over 10,000 per second with sub-second latency, bridging interoperability gaps between Ethereum-based REC systems and Hyperledger platforms.

Author: Fan, X.; Song, Y.; Zhou, W.; Lu, X.; Tan, L.; Li, M.

Publication Title: 2025 2nd International Conference on Intelligent Perception and Pattern Recognition (IPPR)
Abstract Note: Escalating security threats in integrated elderly care systems necessitate architectures that simultaneously ensure data integrity, privacy preservation, and multi-party collaboration. This study proposes a novel security framework integrating three innovations: (1) A response entropy optimization model dynamically quantifies system vulnerability and adjusts defense strategies in real-time; (2) Lightweight federated learning with blockchain-based notarization achieves 100% raw data localization through gradient compression (62% overhead reduction) and zero-trust access control; (3) A cross-modal game architecture resolves medical-insurance-civil conflicts via Nash equilibrium solutions, reducing policy execution latency to 0.5s. Author: Shahid, J.; Cimato, S.

The solution relies on state channels technique to reduce on-chain transactions, contrast architecture latency, and reduce bandwidth consumption, alleviating the burden on the blockchain. State channels can be utilized to efficiently execute the tasks of federated learning models sharing and to solve the scalability problem.

Author: Patel, T.; Gupta, R.; Tanwar, S.

Author: Yang, C.; Mao, Y.; Ye, L.; Liu, X.; Qin, M.; Pan, L.; Liu, J.

Author: Lanka, S.; Moodhitaporn, T.
Title: IoT Security Enhancements in Smart Healthcare Using Federated Learning

Abstract Note: Federated learning (FL) is a distributive machine learning (ML) approach that makes use of a centralised server to assist several Internet of Things (IoT) devices in cooperatively training an ML model. Author: D, R.; Hegde, P.
Title: A Comprehensive Survey on Federated Learning-Enabled Chatbots: Privacy Concerns, Strategies, Challenges, and Future Directions
Publication Title: 2025 4th International Conference on Automation, Computing and Renewable Systems (ICACRS)
Abstract Note: The present survey examines the current integration of chatbot systems with the paradigm-shifting federated learning (FL) technology, which preserves privacy in a decentralized and distributed environment to conduct machine learning on disparate devices. Conversational agents are now in need of secure and smart communicative systems because sensitive information about users is being exchanged via the communication. The paper is an attempt to summarize and categorize the current research in the field of FL and chatbots, particularly the research aiming to maintain the confidentiality of data in a confidential manner without the adverse effects on performance. We look at two of the most glaring privacy risks associated with these kinds of systems including leakage of data when model parameters are updated and vulnerability to adversarial examples. In a bid to mitigate these concerns, we discuss assortment of mitigation methods that include secure aggregation protocols, differential privacy mechanisms and blockchain-based enhanced infrastructural strengthening data integrity and transparency. Also, we discuss some of the remaining technical limitations such as the computational overhead that federated communication imposes, the lack of known solutions to customizing models to various contexts that different users may have, and the challenges of scaling FL-based chatbot systems. Survey also highlights the transformational possibilities of the technologies in areas with high stakes like healthcare, finance as well as customer service, where the main issues are privacy and accuracy. Last, we provide a list of open research questions and make recommendations on future efforts that can be put in place to ensure much more resilient, adaptable, and secure FL-based chatbot systems.
Manual Tags: Security; Federated Learning; Privacy; Machine Learning; Chatbots

Author: Adnan, M. T.; Oroceo, P. A.; Lee, J.-M.; Kim, D.-S.
Title: PureLLM: A Blockchain-Driven Decentralized PFL for Robust and Resource-Efficient Next-Gen LLMs
Publication Title: 2025 Sixteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
Abstract Note: Large language models (LLMs) trained on extensive publicly available datasets have achieved groundbreaking performance across diverse domains. However, both contemporary and future LLMs face four major challenges: (i) Data Availability, (ii) Data Bias and Quality, (iii) Computational Resources, and (iv) Data Privacy and Security. To address these challenges, we propose PureLLM, a blockchain-driven decentralized personalized federated learning (PFL) framework for the development of high-performance, resource-efficient next-generation LLMs. By leveraging decentralized federated learning, PureLLM enables collaborative training across diverse data sources without exposing sensitive user information. A blockchain-powered consensus mechanism ensures data integrity, security, and fairness, mitigating biases and enhancing trust in model updates. Additionally, our approach optimizes resource utilization by dynamically allocating computational workloads across distributed nodes, reducing energy consumption and improving scalability. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that PureLLM achieves superior model performance while maintaining strong privacy guarantees and reducing computational overhead. This framework paves the way for democratized and secure LLM training, fostering an inclusive AI ecosystem where individuals and organizations can contribute to and benefit from cutting-edge language models without compromising privacy or efficiency.

Author: B, I. Y.; Iriyanta, K.; Hendra; SP, B. T. S.; Muhrial, H.; Prayitno, E.
Title: Blockchain-Enabled Secure Federated Learning for Electronic Medical Records: A Scalable and Privacy-Preserving Framework
Publication Title: 2025 8th International Seminar on Research of Information Technology and Intelligent Systems (ISRITI)
Abstract Note: The rapid digital transformation in healthcare has accelerated the adoption of Electronic Medical Records (EMRs), yet concerns about privacy, interoperability, and security remain major challenges. Centralized learning models expose data to leakage and adversarial attacks, reducing clinical reliability. To address these issues, this study proposes a Secure Federated Learning (FL) framework integrated with Blockchain to enable scalable, privacy-preserving, and trustworthy EMR management. A quantitative experimental design was conducted using the publicly available MIMIC-III dataset in a simulated multi-institutional environment. Federated learning enabled local model training across distributed nodes, while blockchain served as a permissioned ledger for update verification, node authentication, and access control. Homomorphic encryption and differential privacy were incorporated to enhance confidentiality. System performance was evaluated in terms of predictive accuracy, calibration, communication efficiency, and security resilience. The proposed framework achieved an average prediction accuracy of 94.7%, with balanced precision (93%) and recall (92%), and an AUROC of 0.97. Calibration also improved, yielding lower Brier and ECE values compared with baselines. Communication latency remained practical at 210 ms per iteration, while bandwidth consumption decreased by 18% relative to vanilla FL. Security analysis showed that the system detected anomalous updates under poisoning attacks with an 87% success rate, while differential privacy reduced membership-inference risk toward chance levels. The blockchain layer further ensured transparency and auditability of all transactions without degrading predictive utility. In conclusion, integrating federated learning with blockchain provides a scalable, auditable, and privacy-preserving solution for EMR management. This framework advances secure digital healthcare infrastructures and establishes a foundation for real-world deployment in hospital ecosystems.
Manual Tags: blockchain; privacy-preserving machine learning; federated learning; healthcare security; electronic medical records

Author: Kashyap, R.; AbdulHussein, A. H.; Al-Tameemi, A. R.; Adel, A.-H.; Bhagat, A.

Each client’s data attributes determine model changes using adaptive learning. Performance metrics, including memory, accuracy, and precision, improve. The system also incorporates safe aggregation and private stochastic gradient descent. These features protect personal data and reduce interaction. The suggested technique improves security using modern cryptographic technologies like trusted execution environments and secure enclave computing. The technique outperforms existing privacy-protecting systems in data privacy, scalability, and computing efficiency. The recommended structure follows rigorous data privacy regulations and improves healthcare app performance. Our technology provides a solid and scalable foundation for medical system shared learning. Patient data is protected, and real-time healthcare choices are accurate and dependable.

Author: Xu, Y.-S.; Idaya, A. M. K. Y.; Kassim, M. S. S.
Title: Towards Sustainable and Responsible Information Systems: Privacy and Security in the AI Era
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Modern Sustainable Systems (CMSS)
Abstract Note: As artificial intelligence (AI) technologies increasingly penerate digital infrastructures, concerns over information systems (IS) privacy and security have intensified. This study offers a comprehensive scientometric analysis of IS privacy and security research in the AI era, with an emphasis on its intellectual structure, thematic evolution, and global collaboration patterns. Drawing on a curated dataset of 4,967 publications from the Web of Science Core Collection database (2015–2024), the analysis employs performance indicators, co-authorship mapping, keyword co-occurrence, trend topic analysis, and factorial analysis to capture key developments and emerging directions in the field. Findings reveal a rapid surge in publication volume since 2018, with federated learning, blockchain, and data privacy emerging as dominant research themes. China, India, and the United States are identified as major contributors, with increasingly dense international co-authorship networks. The co-occurrence analysis highlights the convergence of AI, cryptography, and edge computing, suggesting a shift toward decentralized, privacy-preserving infrastructures. Recent evolving topic analysis indicates sustained interest in encryption, differential privacy, and federated learning. The study suggests a growing interdisciplinarity within the field and a potential alignment with broader sustainability agendas. Author: Du, R.; Zhang, M.; Tian, J.
Title: Carchain: A Blockchain-Based Federated Learning Optimization Scheme in Autonomous-Driving Scenario
Publication Title: 2025 28th International Conference on Computer Supported Cooperative Work in Design (CSCWD)
Abstract Note: The aggregation process inherent in federated learning lacks auditability, rendering it susceptible to the influence of malicious nodes that may upload compromised models, thereby undermining the accuracy of the global model or potentially preventing successful aggregation altogether. In response to these challenges, this paper introduces “carchain”, a blockchain-based ecosystem designed to counteract poisoning and deception attacks within federated learning, while also establishing a framework of trust and incentives. Carchain employs a committee consensus mechanism to verify the accuracy of model updates off-chain. Additionally, it incorporates a reputation calculation mechanism that assesses the quality of model updates, coupled with an incentive structure based on reputation values to motivate the participation of high-quality nodes in the federated learning process. The results of experment indicate that carchain significantly enhances the security and efficiency of the system: when subjected to an attack involving 50% malicious trainers, the final model's loss is reduced to 86.9% compared to that of the BLFC methods; under an attack involving 50% malicious evaluators, the final model's loss is only 25.2% of that observed with direct detection methods. Additionally, the new incentive mechanism allows participants who contribute more data to earn additional tokens, thereby increasing motivation. Lastly, the storage overhead associated with the blockchain is reduced to 50.6% of that required by a single-chain structure.

Author: Ji, S.; Yang, Y.; Duan, Y.; Fan, H.; Lu, Y.
Title: Progress in the Application of Privacy-Preserving Computation and Blockchain Technology in Electricity Market Transactions
Publication Title: 2025 5th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
Abstract Note: The in-depth development of smart grids has brought about massive amounts of data, but it has also raised risks such as user privacy breaches and market manipulation. Consequently, electricity market transactions are facing severe privacy and security challenges. To address these challenges, privacy-preserving computation and blockchain technology have garnered significant attention as emerging solutions. Privacypreserving computation enables data sharing and computation while protecting the privacy of transaction data, while blockchain technology provides features such as data tamper-resistance, traceability, and secure sharing, enhancing market transparency and trust. Therefore, this paper reviews the concepts of privacypreserving computation and blockchain technology, as well as their current application status in electricity market transactions. Analysis indicates that the application of these technologies can effectively improve the efficiency of electricity market transactions, reduce the risk of data breaches, and enhance market credibility and transparency. However, existing applications still face a series of challenges. This paper further explores the future development trends of privacy-preserving computation and blockchain technology in the electricity market, aiming to provide a reference for building a secure, efficient, and trustworthy electricity market.

Author: M.Jasmin; Rana, N. S.; Kumar, Y. J. N.; Hussein, R. R.; Yadav, S.; Hadi, E. H.; Saadi, M. A. M. Al
Title: Privacy-Aware Adaptive Federated Learning for Intelligent Edge AI in Next-Generation 6G Networks

Abstract Note: The accelerated development of 6G networks requires sophisticated Artificial Intelligence (AI) models with real-time decision-making at the edge and maintaining user privacy. This work suggests a Privacy-Aware Adaptive Federated Learning (PA-AFL) system that combines differential privacy, homomorphic encryption, and blockchain-based trust to protect federated learning with optimal model convergence. The method uses adaptive aggregation methods taking network status and computation power into account to maximize learning efficiency. Author: Chen, T.; Wang, F.; Hou, W.; Tang, S.; Zheng, Z.
Title: Dynamic Incentive Model for Federated Learning Model Trading via Evolutionary Game Theory
Publication Title: ICASSP 2025 - 2025 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP)
Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) is an emerging decentralized machine learning paradigm that addresses the data-silo problem through privacy-preserving collaborative model training, attracting significant attention from academia and industry. However, model trading in FL involves multiple stakeholders, including data owners, model requesters, and the cloud service platform, whose conflicting interests hinder the sustainability and stability of FL. To address these challenges, this paper considers the bounded rationality of the three parties involved in long-term dynamic decision-making and constructs a tripartite evolutionary game model based on evolutionary game theory, further taking into account collusion between data owners and cloud service platforms. We analyze the evolutionary dynamics involved, theoretically revealing the social dilemma of dishonesty in FL model trading. To prevent dishonest behaviors such as free-riding and false reporting, we apply the replicator dynamics and Lyapunov method to analyze the impact of rewards, punishments, and collusion costs on the evolutionary stable strategies of the three parties and propose incentive strategies. Simulation experimental results validate that our incentive model is effective in alleviating dishonest social dilemmas and improving social welfare.

Author: Mounira, R.; Majda, M.; Abdelmadjid, B.; Oumaima, B. S.; Derdour, M.
Title: A Comprehensive Survey on Blockchain, Federated Learning, and AI for Securing the Internet of Medical Things
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
Abstract Note: The Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) is transforming healthcare by enabling real-time monitoring and decentralized decision-making through interconnected medical devices, but collecting sensitive patient data creates a considerable privacy-related, security, and trust challenge. We classify the existing work into major technological families and examine systems that preserve patient privacy, decentralized authentication systems, and intrusion detection systems relying on AI models. Each approach has been analyzed based on its architectural design, use case, and security guarantees. Although recent progress has been made, we identify continued challenges in practical deployment, including computational complexity, interoperability issues, and regulatory constraints. The survey ends with a discussion outlining possible future developments, including lightweight consensus protocols for the Blockchain, post-quantum FL models, and scalable trust models for healthcare IoMT systems.

Author: Hayashitani, M.; Mori, J.; Teranishi, I.
Title: Survey of Privacy Threats and Countermeasures in Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2025 3rd International Conference on Federated Learning Technologies and Applications (FLTA)
Abstract Note: Federated learning (FL) has emerged as a privacy-preserving machine learning paradigm that enables collaborative model training without directly exchanging raw data among clients. While FL mitigates the privacy risks associated with centralized data collection, it remains vulnerable to various privacy threats that can compromise sensitive information. Existing literature has only focused on privacy threats and countermeasures within horizontal federated learning (HFL) and vertical federated learning (VFL) individually. This paper provides a comprehensive and systematic review of privacy threats across all three principal FL paradigms: HFL, VFL, and federated transfer learning (FTL). We introduce a unified taxonomy that categorizes privacy threats according to the data type targeted, and we discuss corresponding defense mechanisms.

Author: Mehrban, A.; Houda, Z. A. El; Moudoud, H.; Brik, B.; Khoukhi, L.
Title: A Blockchain-Enabled Multi-Layered Zero-Trust Security Framework for O-RAN

Abstract Note: O-RAN (Open Radio Access Network) is a set of open and interoperable radio access technologies, guided by the O-RAN Alliance, that, despite an open ecosystem, introduces significant security risks, expanding the threat surface in 6G networks. Traditional perimeter-based security approaches are inadequate for O-RAN’s highly distributed, multi-vendor environments, where Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA) becomes essential for robust security. To address these challenges, we propose a novel blockchain-based, decentralized Zero-Trust Framework specifically designed for O-RAN security. Our proposed framework comprises two key layers: the first layer utilizes Federated Learning (FL) and Transfer Learning (TL) for advanced attack detection, enabling distributed, privacy-preserving threat analysis across O-RAN nodes. The second layer enforces Zero Trust access control through a blockchain-based identity management system, ensuring tamper-resistant, real-time policy updates.
