Author: Jahin, G. T. Sharmin; Maliha, F.; Hassan, F. B.; Muztaba, A. Masud Ahmad; Patwary, M. J. Alam; Arefin, M. Shamsul
Title: Privacy-Preserving and Explainable Multi-Hospital CKD Prediction via Federated Learning with Blockchain Logging and Differential Privacy
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
Abstract Note: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) impacts millions worldwide and requires early detection for improved patient outcomes. However, clinical data remains scattered across institutions, and centralized analysis is hindered by privacy concerns. This work introduces a federated HistGradientBoosting (HGB) framework enriched with blockchain logging, differential privacy (DP-SGD), and SHAP-based explainability to enable transparent and secure CKD prediction. A multi-hospital benchmark was constructed using real (UCI, Kaggle) and synthetic datasets distributed across five hospitals, with careful consideration of heterogeneity in terms of class imbalance, missing features, and non-IID demographics. The proposed model achieved an accuracy of 0.97 and an AUROC of 0.99, outperforming baselines such as LR, SVR, ANN, LSTM, centralized pooling, and vanilla FL. Blockchain provided immutable integrity of model updates with negligible overhead, DP-SGD ensured differential privacy guarantees (ϵ = 3–8), and SHAP offered both global feature rankings and patient-level interpretability. These results highlight that our system enables robust, privacy-preserving, and explainable CKD prediction, paving the way for realistic use cases of federated healthcare AI.

Author: Nezhadsistani, N.; Sohrabati, K.; Bamakan, S. M. H.; Stiller, B.
Title: ChainFedTwin: A Blockchain-Based Federated Learning Framework for Secure, Explainable Digital-Twin Collaboration
Publication Title: 2025 7th Conference on Blockchain Research & Applications for Innovative Networks and Services (BRAINS)
Abstract Note: Federated Learning empowered Digital Twins may potentially provide a high-fidelity, privacy-preserving vision of distributed assets. However, verifiable trust, auditability, and interpretability at scale are difficult. This article presents ChainFedTwin, a seven-layered framework that tightly integrates federated learning with blockchain-supported governance and a multi-modal Explainable-AI layer. ChainFedTwin improves current DT frameworks by proposing advanced cryptographic methods, safe bias detection and protection mechanisms, and smart contract-based governance to realize security, privacy, and fairness upgrades. The XAI layer integrates SHAP and LIME for end-to-end interpretability and contains embedded bias detection per aggregation step with fairness validation services. Experimental evaluation on the NSL-KDD dataset proves that ChainFedTwin outperforms the baseline FedAvg algorithm substantially. Specifically, ChainFedtwin achieved a final test accuracy of 94.1% while FedAvg was 91%, an improvement of 3.1 percentage points. Apart from that, it converged to 90% accuracy in 48 iterations, a 47% iteration decrease from FedAvg’s 91 iterations, reflecting enhanced convergence speed and stability at the lower end final loss. While it causes about a 15% communication overhead due to privacy and auditing requirements, this is an acceptable compromise for increased security, trustworthiness, and interpretability in mission-critical DT applications.

Data sovereignty and integrity together with verifiable model training are achieved through decentralized data pipelines which operate without exposing raw dataset information. The developed framework delivers reliable data processing methods which optimize federalized system operations and features trust-building features involving differential privacy implementation and secure aggregation capabilities alongside blockchain auditing capabilities. Our work includes the presentation of engineering methodologies for monitoring and orchestration as well as fault-tolerance techniques when deploying FL models across multiple heterogonous platforms. Results from experimental benchmark tests establish advancements in model accuracy performance and reductions in communication demands and improvements in trustworthiness compared to standard centralized and naïve federated learning models. Author: Putchakayala, R.; Yallavula, R.; Jegajothi, B.
Title: Secure Data Governance in JavaScript-Driven Web Systems using Blockchain-based Hybrid Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on NexGen Networks and Cybernetics (IC2NC)
Abstract Note: Contemporary JavaScript-based web applications generate huge volumes of interactivity and connectedness data that is very sensitive and vulnerable to tight privacy and governance policies. To establish secure and responsible data management in such distributed environments, the approach requires a combination of decentralized control, privacy safeguards and effective collaborative learning. In this research, a hybrid federated learning/blockchain architecture, PSOAdam Federated Blockchain Governance (PA-FedGov) is proposed and aimed at meeting verifiable and privacyprotecting data governance. The new hybrid optimization approach is a combination of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm of adaptive global aggregation and the Adam optimizer of local model optimization which leads to faster convergence and better generalization on non-independent and identically distributed data sources. To achieve immutable, auditable and transparent governance mechanisms, smart contracts are used by the blockchain layer to store model provenance, different privacy budgets, and compliance metadata. To conduct experimental evaluations, the system utilized Benchmark datasets such as FEMNIST to identify user specific handwritings, CICIDS 2017 to detect intrusion in web systems and the Edge-IIoTset to analyze and govern edges, and IoT. These datasets are used in the publicly available CSV or JSON formats. The findings show that the suggested PAFedGov model is more accurate and more stable by up to 12 percent when compared to the conventional federated learning approaches like FedAvg and FedProx, with the same set of differential privacy restrictions. The architecture that ensures traceability and decentralized policy enforcement is blockchain based, and it provides a scalable and reliable foundation of safe data control within federated and privacy-sensitive JavaScript web environments.

Author: J, K. k; D, N.
Title: A Survey and Taxonomy of Privacy-Preserving IoT Anomaly Detection Systems Using Federated Learning and Blockchain for Sustainable Next Generation Networks
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE First International Conference on Innovations in Engineering and Next-Generation Technologies for Sustainability (ICINVENTS)
Abstract Note: The Internet of Things (IoT) is expanding at an unprecedented pace, making anomaly detection vital for ensuring security, reliability, and efficiency in smart systems. This paper fills that gap by presenting a systematic review of Blockchain-enabled FL approaches for IoT anomaly detection. We introduce a novel hierarchical taxonomy of privacy-preserving methods that highlights key architectural trends and technological synergies. A critical analysis of state-of-the-art techniques is conducted, focusing on privacy protection, energy efficiency, scalability, and the feasibility of real-world deployment. The study also identifies persistent research gaps, such as interoperability challenges and computational overhead in resource-constrained IoT environments. Finally, we propose a forward-looking roadmap to guide the development of sustainable and secure next-generation IoT ecosystems. This survey uniquely emphasizes originality, practicality, and sustainability relevance, making it highly timely for emerging smart infrastructures.

Author: B, S. K.; N, S.; K, S. C.; R, R.; Uma, G.; M, S.
Title: Zero-Knowledge Proof Mechanisms for Trustless Federated Learning on Blockchain
Publication Title: 2025 9th International Conference on I-SMAC (IoT in Social, Mobile, Analytics and Cloud) (I-SMAC)
Abstract Note: The interconnected digital systems have developed and grown at a very high rate, increasing the attack surface and exposing them to sophisticated cyber threats. Conventional centralized Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) have a privacy, scalability and latency problems. To address them, PrivGuardNet, a federated learning-powered IDS based on Transformer-based architectures and using Differential Privacy, is presented in this paper. PrivGuardNet uses decentralized training to allow several client devices to collaboratively detect anomalies without exchanging raw data, which is in compliance with privacy. The self-attention mechanism of the transformer learns intricate patterns of traffic in the high-dimensional network, and Differential Privacy defends against model inversion and reconstruction attacks. Tests on benchmark cybersecurity datasets demonstrate high detection rates, excellent generalization and high privacy leakage resistance over traditional IDS models. Concurrently, the paper introduces a federated learning model that is controlled by blockchains and supplemented with Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKP). Clients produce cryptographic evidences to authenticate updates in the model locally without exposing gradients or parameters. These proofs are documented in a blockchain ledger to ensure transparency and fairness and are automated by smart contracts to validate, issue incentives, and detect adversaries. What this integration provides is trustless, privacypreserving collaboration through untrusted environments like healthcare, finance, and IoT with high model accuracy at reduced communication overhead.

Author: Vadisetty, R.; Polamarasetti, A.; Aashna; Rongali, S. K.; Prajapati, S. k; Butani, J. B.

Author: Lakshmaiya, N.; Manikandan, J.; Rajendran, A.; Kaliappan, S.; Kamal, M. D. Raj
Title: A Novel Framework for Secure Data Sharing in IoT-Enabled Smart Cities
Publication Title: 2025 6th International Conference on Electronics and Sustainable Communication Systems (ICESC)
Abstract Note: Smart-city IoT must facilitate safe, live and scalable data connectivity amongst heterogeneous and resource constrained devices. Such methods in practice have poor latency, a centralized single point of linearity, excessive key-management cost, and a poor model on constrained nodes-leading to breaches in integrity, a slow incident response, and a reduced level of user trust. To this end, we present a framework that integrates lightweight end-to-end encryption, authenticated TLS/MQTT transport, blockchain-based access control using smart-contracts, and Device/user identity lifecycle management with continuous threat monitoring. We compare the framework based on operational metrics: data-integrity incidents, security-incident response time, correctly reflected data-sharing transactions, network latency, device-side energy consumption and user-trust ratings. Answers: compared to baseline practices, the framework (i) decreases the number of integrity breaches, (ii) decreases times to respond to the integrity breach, (iii) increases inter-stakeholder data-sharing transaction success, (iv) reduces communication latency, and (v) decreases device energy consumption-collectively increasing user trust and operational resilience in a manner that can be deployed on resource-constrained infrastructural devices common in smart cities.

Author: Bhuvaneshwari, P.; Shnain, A. H.; Kewte, S.; Swaraj, P. P.; Yuvaraj, K.; Abed, M. K.; Algburi, S.
Title: Blockchain-Enabled Federated Learning for Privacy-Preserving Credit Risk Assessment
Publication Title: 2025 3rd International Conference on Cyber Resilience (ICCR)
Abstract Note: Credit risk evaluations enable the financial sector to determine the eligibility of investments and loans. When used to manage private financial data shared across several organizations, centralized machine learning (ML) systems pose data privacy, security, and compliance issues. For competitiveness and regulatory purposes, financial companies may conceal customer information, which can reduce the accuracy of models and datasets. Cyberattacks on central archives complicate the development of secure, collaborative credit scoring systems. This study proposes the Blockchain-Enabled Federated Learning Credit Risk Assessment System (BFL-CRA) to address these issues. A permissioned Blockchain and Federated Learning (FL) protect raw data and decentralize model training across financial organizations. The BFL-CRA protocol requires each institution to establish a model and utilize blockchain smart contracts to deliver encrypted model modifications. Through agreement, the system verifies and safely aggregates alterations into a global model. Training is auditable, immutable, and visible on the blockchain, ensuring honesty and responsibility.

Title: Blockchain-Enabled Federated Learning: A Smart Contract-Based Architecture for Decentralized AI Systems
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent and Secure Engineering Solutions (CISES)
Abstract Note: Artificial Intelligence (AI) development in all major fields including healthcare, finance, and intelligent infrastructure raised the need for private, transparent, and secure learning systems. Federated Learning (FL) addresses data privacy by enabling parties to cooperate to train machine learning models without sharing their raw data; however, conventional FL paradigms are based on central aggregators, which introduce vulnerabilities such as single points of failure, decreased transparency, and trust issues among the cooperating parties. This work proposes a novel theoretical framework that integrates blockchain, smart contracts, and Federated Learning to develop a fully decentralized, secure, and auditable AI training platform where smart contracts manage major processes like model aggregation, verification, and reward distribution, disentangling third-party coordination. Blockchain is used as an immutable ledger that openly keeps track of all the updates to the models and participant behavior, enhancing auditability and building trust. The design further incorporates a token- based reward system that will be used to incentivize honest behavior and discourage malicious behavior, addressing root problems of data poisoning and free- riding. This decentralized approach not only improves data confidentiality and system resilience but also promotes fairness and accountability in multi- stakeholder settings. By conceptual analysis and theoretical modeling, the paper lays the foundation for an ethical and scalable AI system that takes advantage of the strengths of Federated Learning, blockchain, and smart contracts, which is a key step towards decentralized intelligence without compromising privacy, integrity, or trust.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; Federated Learning; Smart Contracts; Decentralized AI; Secure Model Aggregation; Data Privacy

Author: Gonugunta, K. C.; Gudepu, B. Kishore; Pemmasani, P. K.; Jegajothi, B.
Title: Federated Learning Framework for Secure Data Sharing and Governance in Oracle Cloud Environments
Publication Title: 2025 5th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
Abstract Note: In enterprise cloud infrastructures such as Oracle Cloud, secure data sharing, privacy protection, and policy-compliant analytics represent critical challenges in modern AI deployments. This paper presents Fed-OGNet, a Federated Oracle Governance Network, designed to facilitate federated learning with intrinsic support for data governance, client trust dynamics, and explainable AI. The architecture comprises three core modules: a Cross-Client Secure Embedding (CCSE) for differentially private feature extraction using transformer encoders; a Trust-Governed Adaptive Classifier (TGAC) for model updates influenced by dynamic client trust scores; and a Federated Control Orchestrator (FCO) that performs policy enforcement, federated version control, and audit logging through blockchain integration. To assess FedOGNet's efficacy, extensive experiments were conducted using the LEAF Sent140 benchmark, simulating a federated Oracle Cloud environment with heterogeneous client data. Results showed that Fed-OGNet achieved an accuracy of 91.6%, surpassing FedAvg (87.3%), FedProx (88.5%), and FedPer (89.1%). The system maintained high governance integrity, with 62% of clients achieving top-tier trust scores and effectively mitigating policy violations. Furthermore, the model exhibited enhanced convergence, reaching 85% accuracy in just 19 epochs, and demonstrated strong robustness against privacy noise. Blockchain-based metadata recording introduced minimal latency overhead, validating its feasibility for real-time enterprise deployment. Overall, Fed-OGNet provides a privacy-preserving, governance-aware, and scalable federated learning architecture suitable for Oracle-based smart governance applications.
Manual Tags: Federated Learning; Explainable AI; Secure Data Sharing; Data Privacy; Data Governance; Blockchain Audit; Oracle Cloud; Trust-based AI

Author: Baucas, M. J.; Spachos, P.
Title: Private Blockchain and Federated Learning-Based Edge-Iot Platform for Secure Urban Noise Monitoring
Publication Title: ICC 2025 - IEEE International Conference on Communications
Abstract Note: The Internet of Things (IoT) has enabled many services and applications that benefit the urban landscape. One of these services is urban noise monitoring. Noise pollution is an issue that can disrupt the lifestyle and well-being of the populace. An urban noise monitoring system can help analyze the noise levels around the different areas in the city to isolate and address disruptive locations. However, it is a service that heavily relies on its training data. It must remain secure to keep the monitoring system accurate and reliable. So, we propose a secure urban noise monitoring system using a private blockchain and Federated Learning (FL)-based edge-IoT platform. It combines the immutability of blockchain technology with the privacypreserving capabilities of FL, reinforcing the security of training data within an IoT network. Based on our tests, our proposed platform was able to preserve the security, privacy, and integrity of the urban noise monitoring system.
Manual Tags: Federated learning; Secure aggregation; Privacy preservation; Network access security; Private blockchain

Author: Daikha, M.-L.; Boukharrou, R.; Chaouche, A.-C.; Ilié, J.-M.
Title: Blockchain-Based Privacy Preservation in IoT Smart Environments: A Survey
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
Abstract Note: The rapid growth of the Internet of Things (IoT) has enabled the development of smart environments that enhance everyday life through seamless data-driven services. However, the massive and continuous collection of personal and contextual data introduces serious privacy concerns, especially when managed by centralized systems. Blockchain has emerged as a promising solution to mitigate these challenges by offering decentralized, transparent, and tamper-resistant data management. This paper provides a comprehensive analysis of blockchain-based privacy-preserving solutions in IoT-driven smart environments, with a focus on domains such as healthcare, smart cities, and industrial systems. We propose a multi-dimensional taxonomy that classifies existing works. In addition, we present a comparative analysis of key solutions, highlighting their strengths, limitations, and tradeoffs. The study also identifies current research gaps and outlines future research directions to guide the design of more secure, efficient, and privacy-preserving architectures.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; Privacy-preserving; Internet of things; Survey; Smart environment

Author: Mishra, R.; Vishnoi, Y.
Title: A Federated Learning-Based Intrusion Detection Framework for Blockchain-Enabled IoT Supply Chains
Publication Title: 2025 Seventh International Conference on Research in Computational Intelligence and Communication Networks (ICRCICN)
Abstract Note: The newest Internet of Things (IoT) networks in supply chain operations not only provide massive amounts of realtime information but also present new cyber-physical security challenges. This study presents a multidisciplinary simulation framework that merges blockchain and machine learning (ML) to boost the security and efficiency of blockchainbased IoT supply chain networks. In this regard, we consider federated learning (FL)-trained deep neural networks for distributed anomaly detection on IoT device data collections and report anomalies on a permissioned blockchain database to achieve tamper-proof auditability measures. When we simulated the network (using NS3 and a blockchain simulator) under various trouble scenarios, the ML-enhanced system could detect cyber-attacks (e.g., data exfiltration, DDoS, and malicious device behavior) with \textbackslash{}mathbf{{\textbackslash{}gt} 9 5 \textbackslash{}%}\ accuracy and also considerably reduced the false alarms compared with the baseline methods. Blockchain only provides data visibility and traceability for supply chain events. The following are our contributions: (1) proposing a new federated ML framework for distributed anomaly detection in IoT supply chains, (2) designing a layer on the blockchain to store alerts and trained models, and (3) performing a comprehensive simulation study of the overall system, which demonstrates how combining both systems surpasses non-ML or non-blockchain configurations. The results indicate that a robust collaborative ML-based IDS improves incident response, and the blockchain guarantees the trust and auditability of IoT Data streams in supply chains. This study lays the groundwork for the future realworld deployment of secure, smart IoT supply chain networks.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; Federated Learning; Supply Chain; DLT; Anomaly Detection Cyber Security; NS3 Simulation

Author: Sokhankhosh, A.; Hassan, K.; Rouhani, S.
Title: Enhancing Split Learning with Sharded and Blockchain-Enabled SplitFed Approaches
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain (Blockchain)
Abstract Note: Collaborative and distributed learning techniques, such as Federated Learning (FL) and Split Learning (SL), hold significant promise for leveraging sensitive data in privacy-critical domains. However, FL and SL suffer from key limitations—FL imposes substantial computational demands on clients, while SL leads to prolonged training times. To overcome these challenges, SplitFed Learning (SFL) was introduced as a hybrid approach that combines the strengths of FL and SL. Despite its advantages, SFL inherits scalability, performance, and security issues from SL. In this paper, we propose two novel frameworks: Sharded SplitFed Learning (SSFL) and Blockchain-enabled SplitFed Learning (BSFL). SSFL addresses the scalability and performance constraints of SFL by distributing the workload and communication overhead of the SL server across multiple parallel shards. Building upon SSFL, BSFL replaces the centralized server with a blockchain-based architecture that employs a committee-driven consensus mechanism to enhance fairness and security. BSFL incorporates an evaluation mechanism to exclude poisoned or tampered model updates, thereby mitigating data poisoning and model integrity attacks. Experimental evaluations against baseline SL and SFL approaches show that SSFL improves performance and scalability by 31.2% and 85.2%, respectively. Furthermore, BSFL increases resilience to data poisoning attacks by 62.7% while maintaining superior performance under normal operating conditions. To the best of our knowledge, BSFL is the first blockchain-enabled framework to implement an end-to-end decentralized SplitFed Learning system.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; Security; Federated Learning; Scalability; Sharding; Split Learning; SplitFed Learning

Author: Shakir, I. A.; Yaseen, W. Y.; Shalal, A. A.; Salman, D. S.; Ahmed, A. A.; Ibrahim, H. S.; Awad, A. S.; Rasool, Z. H.
Title: Byzantine-Resilient Federated Deep Learning for Secure and Privacy-Preserving Smart Healthcare Using Krum
Publication Title: 2025 3rd International Conference on Cyber Resilience (ICCR)
Abstract Note: Federated deep learning that said, the idea of federated deep learning is to be able to train models collaboratively over decentralized data sources without revealing sensitive data. Regarding to intelligent healthcare systems, federated deep learning is critical in enabling secure use of dispersed patient data collected by wearable sensors, medical equipment and electronic health records. In this work, we study the problem of privacy-preserving federated deep learning, to enable it while preserving the privacy of the training data and designing architectures that do not centralize the data. To cope with malicious updates in federated learning, we present a Byzantine-Resilient aggregation algorithm based on Krum. The methodology overcomes model vulnerabilities, adheres to privacy standards, and enables secure collaboration among heterogeneous healthcare organizations.
Manual Tags: Federated Learning; Deep Learning; Privacy Preservation; Smart Healthcare; Byzantine Fault Tolerance

Author: Gaspar, J.; Pessoa, J.; Ribeiro, B.; Martinho, D.; Santos, J.; Marreiros, G.
Title: Security-Enhancing Mechanisms to Strengthen Privacy on Federated Learning Based Recommendation Systems
Publication Title: 2025 International Workshop on Intelligent Systems (IWIS)
Abstract Note: In the current landscape of Artificial Intelligence solutions, Federated Learning emerges as one of the most promising techniques due to its collaborative nature across distinct clients as well as a privacy-preserving technique in information exchange. This preservation is accomplished by the node contributions being made in the form of model updates instead of sharing the raw data with the global server. However, there are challenges in this field that remain, such as inference attacks or model manipulations. This paper provides an overview regarding existing concerns on centralized data and how the concept of federated may be a valid tool to mitigate centralization problems, with particular focus in recommendation systems. The study then addresses different approaches to increase the privacy guarantees of federated learning, with resource to additional privacy mechanisms.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; Federated Learning; Privacy; AI; Machine Learning; Encryption; Cibersecurity

Author: Zhang, Z.; Pan, Z.; Feng, Y.; Shen, Q.
Title: BloP: A Trusted Computing Scheme Integrating Blockchain and Privacy-Preserving Computation
Publication Title: 2025 25th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability and Security (QRS)
Abstract Note: In today's era of rapid digitalization, industries with high data security demands increasingly rely on reliable systems. The requirements for data security and privacy protection in their operations have become more prominent. Although federated learning offers advantages in data privacy protection and collaborative modeling, it still faces privacy risks during model iteration and training interference. It has become an urgent challenge for industries with high data security requirements to build a sensitive information protection system to ensure security and efficiency of data processing. To address these challenges, we propose BloP, a trusted computing scheme that integrates blockchain with privacy-preserving computation. The scheme combines blockchain algorithms with various privacy-preserving computation technologies. BloP relies on trusted computing and measurement modules to maintain a set of trusted nodes, monitor trusted anomaly events, and establish a tamper-proof mechanism. In addition, BloP employs the PBFT consensus algorithm to accelerate the blockchain algorithm. BloP has been implemented and tested on 10 industry systems with high data security demands. During 17 months, the system detected 32,220 trusted anomaly events and 479 tamper-proof events. Furthermore, more than 90 % of these trusted anomaly events were caused by operational errors, while the rest were malicious attacks or unknown incidents.
Manual Tags: blockchain; anti-tempering; privacy-preserving computation; trusted computing

Author: Abbas, D.; Benmachiche, A.; Derdour, M.; Sedraoui, B. K.
Title: Privacy and Security in Decentralized Cyber-Physical Systems: A Survey
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
Abstract Note: With the growing demand on cutting edge technologies specially in the field of internet of things (IoT) cybersecurity the intersections between blockchain and federated learning (FL) is a promising research field. Blockchain based systems, which are inherently decentralized and trustless, allow local immutable logging for transparent, tamperproof security frameworks that support automated threat response via smart contracts while really being able to understand the integrity of the data being shared across a distributed network of machines. FL represents a powerful new paradigm, allowing organizations to create an accurate intrusion detection system (IDS) without needing to centralize sensitive data, a fundamental problem to solve in healthcare, finance, or Industrial IoT. Both technologies have important synergies within hybrid architectures that offer a balanced alternative by leveraging the privacy of FL and the security and auditability of blockchain to create a viable path to robust, scalable, and reliable cyber defense. There remain numerous challenges yet to be resolved around scalability, interoperability between devices and legacy systems, real-world deployment, and energy efficiency, but the cybersecurity landscape appears to be rapidly evolving to incorporate decentralized technologies. This survey material has highlighted the areas in which progress is being made, outlined the core strengths and limitations of the technologies and approaches employed today, and suggested innovative ideas to pursue in shaping secure, and privacy-conscience, adaptive technologies in forthcoming generation of distributed and networked environments.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; Federated Learning; Privacy; IoT Security; Intrusion Detection

Author: Demetrakopoulos, P.; Anagnostopoulos, T.; Tsekeridou, S.
Title: Distributing trust: A P2P SMPC protocol for secure federated learning
Publication Title: 2025 3rd International Conference on Foundation and Large Language Models (FLLM)
Abstract Note: In an era where privacy becomes increasingly crucial and thus heavily regulated, federated learning (FL) frameworks have emerged as a way to distribute training of machine learning models across many clients without sharing raw data. However, simple FL methods are still vulnerable to attacks that may leak sensitive data through model updates, transported across the network. Secure Multi-Party Computation (SMPC), coupled with FL, offers a promising distributed security approach to protect data privacy during the aggregation phase. In this work, we introduce a novel peer-to-peer (P2P) SMPC protocol that distributes trust among clients to remove the strict requirement of a trusted central aggregator, further posing a weak link in the distributed architecture. Our protocol enables decentralized secret sharing and aggregation of model parameters using additive secret sharing, ensuring end-to-end privacy even in the presence of honest-but-curious adversaries. The architecture, communication protocol and security guarantees of the proposed approach are presented along with performance evaluation results in different FL scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method preserves model accuracy while introducing a slight communication overhead. This work presents a scalable and trustless alternative to centralized SMPC, laying the foundation for privacy-preserving machine learning in untrusted environments.
Manual Tags: security; secret sharing; secure federated learning; P2P; SMPC; multiparty computation

Author: Zhang, K.
Title: Research on the Application of Homomorphic Encryption-Based Machine Learning Privacy Protection Technology in Precision Marketing
Publication Title: 2025 3rd International Conference on Data Science and Network Security (ICDSNS)
Abstract Note: Against the backdrop of the rapid development of the digital economy, as the online traffic dividend gradually fades, enterprises are shifting their strategic focus to the offline market, aiming to extract the deep value of consumer data to drive the intelligent upgrade of precision marketing. The combination of big data and machine learning enables more accurate analysis of user consumption behavior, thereby optimizing customer segmentation and personalized recommendation strategies. In the context of increasing risks of data privacy leakage, how to ensure data security while enhancing the scientific nature of marketing decisions has become a core issue in current research. To address this, this paper first conducts a systematic analysis of the domestic and international research status of machine learning privacy computing, explores the applicability of existing data protection technologies, and introduces vector homomorphic encryption technology to enhance the security of the data sharing process. In line with the demands of precision marketing, this paper designs a method for customer segmentation under privacy protection, using the K-means clustering algorithm to classify consumption data and optimizing the homomorphic encryption scheme to enable it to perform calculations on rational numbers, thereby improving the accuracy and applicability of ciphertext computations. To address the limitations of the K-means algorithm in clustering in the ciphertext domain, this paper proposes an optimization strategy by improving the initial center point selection mechanism, enhancing the accuracy of the clustering results and more precisely targeting the user base. Based on the above theoretical research, this paper further constructs a consumption data analysis system based on homomorphic encryption, designs a secure and efficient system architecture, and verifies the system functions to ensure its feasibility in the precision marketing scenario.
Manual Tags: data security; artificial intelligence; privacy computing; classification algorithm; personalized marketing

Author: Chauhan, M.; Khan, T.
Title: Adaptive Privacy and Lightweight Security in Healthcare IoT: Challenges, Solutions and Future Directions
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Innovation in Computing and Engineering (ICE)
Abstract Note: IoT in healthcare has transformed patient care by enabling and implementing the real-time monitoring for the end patients or users. However, the development of connected devices introduces significant privacy and security challenges, especially while securing the healthcare data. In this paper, a comparative review of adaptive privacy and lightweight security mechanisms in the area of healthcare IoT is shown. A comparison of current methods based on criteria including data security, privacy preservation, scalability, resource efficiency, and real-time implementation is one of the major contributions. Furthermore, this review recognizes the research gaps in the recent researches and highlights promising techniques, including advanced encryption, federated learning, and the edge computing. By addressing these challenges, the study aims to guide the development of robust, efficient, and scalable solutions that ensure privacy and security in dynamic healthcare IoT environments.
Manual Tags: Privacy Preservation; Healthcare IoT; Edge Computing; Real-Time Monitoring; Lightweight Security

Author: KVBL, D.; Samara, G.; Kumari, E. N. V.; Karthikeyan, G.; Pandi, V. S.; Mesilla, R. M.
Title: Establishment of Security Threats in 5G Networks with Blockchain-Integrated Authentication Protocols and Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
Abstract Note: Fifth generation of communication networks (5G) optoelectronic devices provide leapfrogging speed, latency and connectivity that are required for a variety of applications, such as smart cities, autonomous vehicles, and massive IoT ecosystems. Nonetheless, this development is also an alleged growing complexity of emerging threats, such as identity spoon, data manipulation, denial-of-service (DoS) attacks, or user privacy violation. Legacy cloud-centric security models are being complemented by localized security processing at the edge and individual cells, in part due to the fact that 5G is a distributed architecture with heavy reliance at the edge and on end user devices. In this study, we combat the emerging security challenges in 5G networks through a blockchain enhanced authentication framework with FL to provide secure access. The decentralized, immutable, and transparent property of blockchain is promising to protect identity verification, session integrity, and transaction logs in distributed 5G scenarios. Authentication requests are handled through smart contracts to maintain verifiability in a decentralized manner so that there are no single-point-of-failure risks. At the same time, federated learning is a privacy-preserving machine learning paradigm for the edge devices and UEs to collaboratively train on threat patterns without leaking raw data. This method enables sensitive feature information to be kept locally and to simultaneously to corporately improve defense capability of the whole system against new attacks. With the combination of FL and blockchain, the proposed model improves inaccurate threat detection, ensures safe authentication, and maintains the privacy of user data. We develop a comprehensive threat taxonomy to classify threats in 5G, where both inter-slice isolation attack, rogue gNodeB registration, and adversarial AI-based intrusion, and signaling storm are part of this taxonomy. The framework is verified on a simulation platform simulating a multi-slice 5G network and yields improved results for authentication latency, data privacy, and anomaly detection. By 35% faster validation time and 28% better anomaly detection than traditional authentication systems, hybrid model surpasses the traditional models. This study presents important progress towards a secure, distributed architecture for next-generation networks. The paper shows that how blockchain and federated learning could work together to resolve the key problems of the 5G security without compromising performance and privacy. This integration based on those methods provides a solution that looks ahead to an even future, from ultra-dense and hyper-dynamic communications that supports various ultra-dense and hyper-dynamic, cyber threat landscapes and future 6G deployment.
Manual Tags: Federated Learning; Privacy Preservation; Smart Contracts; Identity Management; Network Slicing; Threat Detection

Author: Pyari, D.; Infanta, A. V.; Mary, S. S. C.; Shah, N. H.; G, S.; Bala, B. K.
Title: Federated Learning for Secure Multi-Vendor E-Commerce Recommendations with Privacy-Preserving User Data
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Sustainability, Innovation & Technology (ICSIT)
Abstract Note: Recommendation systems play a key role in creating engagement on e-commerce platforms and improving sales, although such solutions are compromised due to security and data risks created by centralized architectures. In this paper, a type of privacy-preserving multi-horn collaboration capable of handling millions of vendors is presented, BlockFed, a Federated Learning framework designed to fit in large multivendor e-commerce scenarios. BlockFed uses Differential Privacy and Homomorphic Encryption to protect user data when training a model using a decentralized mechanism. To guarantee clarity and confidence between rival sales personnel, a Blockchain-based safe gathering is utilised. Experimental findings show that BlockFed records a high F1- score of 98.8 percent and zero privacy leakage, which provides a great privacy performance tradeoff. It is also modular and decentralized, which allows scaling easily with the participation of more vendors without either affecting performance. The suggested framework enables various vendors to jointly train a cross-domain recommendation model without sharing sensitive data, and as such, it has the potential to be implemented in a way to enable e-commerce personalization across platforms to be efficient, secure, and compliant with regulations.
Manual Tags: Federated Learning; Privacy Preservation; Differential Privacy; Ecommerce Recommendations; Multi-Vendor Collaboration

Author: Ameen, D. W. H.
Title: AI-Driven Secure Audit Trails for Financial Compliance Using Immutable Blockchain Logs
Publication Title: 2025 3rd International Conference on Cyber Resilience (ICCR)
Abstract Note: AI-driven secure audit systems are revolutionizing how financial institutions ensure compliance, transparency, and data accountability. By integrating immutable blockchain logs, audit trails can be made tamper-proof, enhancing trust and regulatory visibility. However, existing centralized compliance systems face significant challenges, including vulnerability to data breaches, a lack of transparency, and difficulties in maintaining cross-jurisdictional regulatory alignment. To address these limitations, this work proposes a novel framework that combines Federated AI with Blockchain-Integrated Audit Logging (F-AI-BC-AL). Federated learning enables decentralized model training across institutions without sharing raw financial data, preserving privacy and reducing data transfer risks. Concurrently, blockchain ensures every transaction, data access event, and AI-driven compliance check is logged immutably using smart contracts for policy enforcement. The proposed method is applied to real-time Anti-Money Laundering (AML) monitoring in cross-border financial transactions, enabling institutions to detect suspicious activities while collaboratively maintaining secure auditability. Results demonstrate enhanced detection accuracy, data confidentiality, and improved regulatory traceability, with a significant reduction in audit reconciliation time. The outcome establishes a secure, scalable, and regulation-aligned compliance ecosystem that is resilient to tampering and privacy violations.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; Federated Learning; Anti-Money Laundering; Audit Trail; Financial Compliance; Secure Logging

Author: Jin, Y.; Wang, R.; Liu, X.; Liu, D.; Liu, Y.
Title: Blockchain Based Hierarchical Federated Learning for EVs in Smart Grid Wireless Networks
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE Cyber Science and Technology Congress (CyberSciTech)
Abstract Note: In wireless smart grids and vehicle-to-grid (V2G) networks, centralized training of artificial intelligence (AI) models faces significant privacy, communication, and scalability challenges due to the transmission of sensitive electric vehicle (EV) and grid data. Although federated learning (FL) enables decentralized model training without raw data sharing, it is still susceptible to inference attacks, interception, and model tampering. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a hierarchical federated learning scheme enhanced with differential privacy and blockchain, referred to as HFL-DPB. The training process is structured across three tiers: electric vehicles (EVs), roadside units (RSUs), and elastic compute service (ECS). Differential privacy is employed using a moment-based noise calibration mechanism to ensure rigorous privacy protection with controlled utility degradation. In parallel, blockchain technology is integrated to establish decentralized trust, providing transparent model traceability and tamper-resistant coordination among participants.
Manual Tags: blockchain; federated learning (FL); differential privacy (DP); electric vehicle (EV); Wireless networks

Author: Sherif, B.; Zaghloul, Y.; Zamzam, M.
Title: Securing IIoT Data Integrity with Blockchain and Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Systems and Emergent Technologies (IC_ASET)
Abstract Note: The Industrial Internet of Things has revolutionized automation and decision-making across industries. However, it also brings challenges in maintaining data integrity and transparency in decentralized networks. This Research paper addresses these issues by introducing a blockchain-based framework combined with collaborative learning to protect data from tampering and enhance trust. Innovative algorithms detect and filter out malicious data, strengthening security. Tested on real-world datasets, this approach proves more effective than traditional models, especially in ensuring data authenticity and defending against data poisoning. When tested on the CIFAR10 and Fashion-MNIST datasets, the proposed framework outperforms traditional machine learning models. Specifically, it achieves higher accuracy compared to Random Forest by \4.05 \textbackslash{}%\ on CIFAR-10 and 3.95% on Fashion-MNIST. Similarly, it surpasses DecisionTreeAdaBoost by \8.73 \textbackslash{}%\ and \7.49 \textbackslash{}%\, respectively.
Manual Tags: Federated Learning; Industrial Internet of Things; Poisoning Attacks; Blockchain Technology

Author: Preetha, S.; Pallavi, G. B.; Pallavi, C. V.; Salve, P. R.; Chimankar, A. G.; Chaudhuri, R. R.
Title: Federated Learning-Based Privacy-Preserving Data Sharing System for Cloud Platforms
Publication Title: 2025 2nd International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Knowledge Discovery in Concurrent Engineering (ICECONF)
Abstract Note: Federated learning has emerged as a paradigm shift in facilitating privacy-sensitive data sharing on distributed cloud systems. This paper presents a Federated Averaging (FedAvg) algorithm with the PySyft framework, which offers secure aggregation and differential privacy capabilities to enhance the confidence of cloud-based data sharing. The system minimizes the risks of data leakage, adversarial attacks, and unauthorized access and enables training of models at scale and on heterogeneous devices. It has been experimentally demonstrated that the proposed approach can be employed to achieve high model accuracy with minimal communication overhead, and, therefore, it can be implemented in such applications as healthcare, finance, and smart cities. This privacy-sensitive framework offers a secure platform upon which responsible AI deployment in cloud-based collaborative environments can be attained.
Manual Tags: Federated Learning; Secure Aggregation; Federated Averaging (FedAvg); Cloud Platforms; Privacy-Preserving Data Sharing; PySyft

Author: Gopukumar, S. T.; Ahmed, S. J.; Kadhim, H.; Alazzam, M. B.; Majed, A. Eqab Muraay; Faizal, M. K. M.
Title: Blockchain-Driven Federated Learning for Real-Time Threat Defense and Forensic Insight
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Innovations in Intelligent Systems: Advancements in Computing, Communication, and Cybersecurity (ISAC3)
Abstract Note: Real-time, privacy-conserving forensic analysis is needed as cyber threats become more sophisticated. Centralized machine learning models face data privacy, security, and scalability issues, while traditional federated learning does not have integrity verification or adaptive threat indication. This paper presents a Blockchain-Integrated Federated Learning (BFL) framework for supporting digital forensics and real-time cyber threat defense. BFL facilitates forensic organizations to jointly train models without sharing raw data, ensuring data privacy. Blockchain guarantees tamper-evident forensic logs, safe model updates, and automated verification via smart contracts. Experimental outcomes verify that BFL greatly surpasses centralized and traditional federated learning methods, with a detection accuracy of 98.5% for cyber threats. Incorporating blockchain enhances model security, verifies latency, and increases adversarial robustness. By integrating distributed learning with immutable forensic logging, the framework proposed provides an scalable, reliable solution to real-time cyber protection. The research sets an encouraging basis for next-generation AI-based digital forensic systems in secure and smart cybersecurity investigations.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; Federated Learning; Smart Contracts; Digital Forensics; Privacy-Preserving AI; Cyber Threat Detection

Author: Ramesh, N.; Anwar, M.; K, K.
Title: Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning in Healthcare: Integrating Homomorphic Encryption, Smart Contracts, and Adaptive Strategies
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
Abstract Note: The exponential rise of healthcare data calls for strong privacy-preserving methods for collaborative learning. In this paper, an Integrated Federated Learning Framework integrating homomorphic encryption, blockchain, and adaptive learning approaches is introduced to meet the challenges of privacy, scalability, and heterogeneity of data in healthcare. Data confidentiality is provided by homomorphic encryption with the ability to carry out computations over encrypted data safely, and tamper-proof sharing of data by blockchain. Adaptive learning mechanisms such as weighted federated learning and SMOTE address data imbalance and heterogeneity. Evaluated on real-world data such as MIMIC-III, the framework achieves 93.2% model accuracy, outperforming traditional centralized and federated learning approaches. Experimental results are a 30% reduction in communication overhead with faster convergence, making it feasible for large-scale, privacy-sensitive healthcare applications. The proposed framework provides opportunities for secure, efficient, and collaborative analysis of healthcare data.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; Federated Learning; Privacy Preservation; Homomorphic Encryption; Healthcare Data

Author: Marathe, N.; Srivastava, K.; Pulgam, N.; Pandey, A.; Jasani, J.; Ghodawat, R.; Mehta, R.
Title: TransferFed: A Unified Framework for Blockchain-Secured, Privacy-Preserving, and Incentive-Aware Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2025 3rd International Conference on Data Science and Network Security (ICDSNS)
Abstract Note: Federated learning (FL) enables decentralized model training but faces persistent challenges from client data heterogeneity, potential privacy leaks, and a lack of incentives for participation. This paper introduces TransferFed, a novel and comprehensive framework designed to address these interconnected issues. The primary objective of TransferFed is to create a robust, secure, and efficient FL ecosystem. To achieve this, our proposed framework synergistically integrates four key components: (i) Transfer learning (TL) based initialization, which uses publicly pretrained models to warm-start client training, accelerating convergence and mitigating issues from non-IID data; (ii) A dynamic, adaptive aggregation mechanism that scores and weights client contributions based on utility gain and historical reliability, filtering out low-quality or anomalous updates; (iii) An adversarially-trained privacy bottleneck that enforces rigorous, information-theoretic privacy bounds on client data by minimizing mutual information leakage; and (iv) A dual-layer blockchain architecture that provides a secure and cost-efficient backbone for model provenance and incentive distribution. The research findings presented are theoretical, outlining a system that achieves provable convergence rates, formal privacy guarantees, and an honest-Nash equilibrium for its token-based economy. TransferFed establishes a deployable, incentive-compatible blueprint for real-world, TL-enhanced FL.
Manual Tags: Federated learning; blockchain; transfer learning; adaptive aggregation; economic incentives; privacy-preserving ML

Author: Garg, S.; Sagtani, A.; Hiran, K. K.
Title: Federated Learning over Blockchain-Enabled Cloud Infrastructure
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 5th International Conference on ICT in Business Industry & Government (ICTBIG)
Abstract Note: The rise of IoT devices and the uptake of cloud computing have informed a new era of data-driven intelligence. Traditional centralized machine learning models that require a large volume of data to be stored in a single location have therefore become more susceptible to data breaches, privacy violations, and regulatory non-compliance. This report presents a thorough examination of the merging of Federated Learning (FL) and blockchain technology in a cloud-edge setting, demonstrating it as an effective solution to the stated concerns. We are proposing a detailed four-dimensional architectural categorization that meticulously assesses coordination frameworks, consensus algorithms, data storage practices, and trust models that are significant to these integrated systems. The manuscript presents a comprehensive comparative examination of two cutting-edge frameworks: the Multi-Objectives Reinforcement Federated Learning Blockchain (MORFLB), which is designed for intelligent transportation systems, and the Federated Blockchain-IoT Framework for Sustainable Healthcare Systems (FBCI-SHS), elucidating their distinctive contributions and inherent limitations. Author: Latif, S.; Djenouri, D.; Ahmad, J.
Title: A Serverless Federated Learning Framework with Blockchain and Homomorphic Encryption
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 35th International Telecommunication Networks and Applications Conference (ITNAC)
Abstract Note: Traditional federated learning (FL) architectures are vulnerable to significant security risks. Centralized servers create single points of failure and are susceptible to adversarial attacks such as model poisoning. Additionally, they lack auditability and do not provide cryptographic privacy during model aggregation. This paper proposes a serverless FL framework that integrates blockchain technology with CKKS homomorphic encryption to address these challenges. The framework utilizes a decentralized consensus mechanism based on Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance (PBFT), eliminating the need for a central coordinator and ensuring robustness against Byzantine faults. It incorporates CKKS encryption to enable secure aggregation through computation on encrypted gradients, preserving data privacy throughout the training process. Furthermore, it introduces an auditable trust management system using smart contracts for immutable logging and decentralized reputation tracking. Experimental results on the MNIST dataset, with \20 \textbackslash{}%\ malicious clients, demonstrate that the framework achieves a final global accuracy of \98.68 \textbackslash{}%\ and attains \100 \textbackslash{}%\ precision in rejecting malicious updates without false positives. The computational overhead remains practical, with encryption and consensus times of 0.814 sec and 1.695 \ms\ per round, respectively. Compared to existing methods, the proposed approach improves accuracy by \1.68 \textbackslash{}%\ to \10.68 \textbackslash{}%\, demonstrating its effectiveness in enabling secure and privacypreserving FL.

Author: Sun, C.; Zhang, W.; Sun, P.; Wang, H.

Experiments verify the framework’s effectiveness in enhancing prediction performance, ensuring data security and compliance, and enabling controlled disclosure of sensitive information. Author: Reshma; Keyal, P. K.; Saini, S. S.

Author: Krishnamoorthy, P.; Prabhu, S. N.
Title: Adaptive Federated Learning Architecture for Privacy and Scalability in Smart Cities
Publication Title: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advances in Computation, Communication and Information Technology (ICAICCIT)
Abstract Note: The increased pace of smart city deployment demands intelligent, privacy-conscious and scalable systems to process diverse city data. The challenge posed by privacy and scalability of centralized machine learning models is especially in the situation where the data distribution is heterogeneous. The current paper proposes an Adaptive Federated Learning (AFL) architecture of smart cities. Compared to the existing methods, AFL introduces adaptive client selection, hierarchical model aggregation, sharing of parameters in a secure and homomorphic manner (through differential privacy and homomorphic encryption) and gradient compression to communicate. AFL is contrasted with centralized learning with the usual federated learning baselines in Chennai Smart City dataset. Results show that AFL enriches the accuracy by 92.4 percent and convergences by 24 percent and costs of communication by 32 percent, at the expense of increased privacy assurances. The contributions of this work can be listed as following: a hierarchical AFL organization is presented in heterogeneous smart city environments, privacy-enhancing techniques are integrated with adaptive aggregation, and comparative experiments are given with the baselines and the state-of-the-art. Findings indicate that AFL is a feasible and scalable privacy-sensitive smart urban application.

In terms of trust mechanisms, a lightweight blockchain architecture combined with a federated learning framework provides decentralized support for data consistency and trusted communication under highly dynamic topologies. In terms of content security, the use of frequency-spatial domain fusion watermarking and reinforcement learningdriven offloading strategies effectively achieves data embedding and traceability. However, these technologies still face real-time and stability challenges in low-orbit satellite links with frequency variations and high latency. Looking ahead, AIGC and cognitive security will become key to building a self-evolving security system. Through generative content modeling and attack graph reasoning, intelligent evolution of security mechanisms can be achieved. This model incorporates both Federated Learning (FL) to preserve the privacy of the user via non-exchange of raw data and blockchain technology as one of the highest levels of authentication to identify and verify that the identity has not been disturbed. This study presents a comprehensive survey and comparative analysis of recent FL methodologies tailored for healthcare applications, focusing on architecture design, client selection, model aggregation, and privacy-enhancing mechanisms. The MedMNIST v2 dataset is employed to benchmark six representative FL algorithms, in-cluding FedAvg, FedProx, FedBN, FedDyn, FedAvg with Differ-ential Privacy, and FedNova. Author: Samuelsen, M.; Dreibholz, T.; Mazumdar, S.
Title: FL+2: Multi-Layered Privacy Protection for Federated Learning-based Medical Diagnostic
Publication Title: 2025 24th International Symposium on Parallel and Distributed Computing (ISPDC)
Abstract Note: To build trust between patients and health institutions, implementing a privacy-preserving mechanism to handle personal health information is crucial. Therefore, federated learning (FL) is gaining popularity in health data analysis, due to its ability to enhance trustworthiness by sharing model-related information rather than data. Blockchain, with its decentralization, immutability, and traceability features, has also been integrated with FL to address existing privacy concerns. In this paper, we introduce FL+2, which is designed to address the infrastructural security and model-focused traceability challenges associated with FL-based medical analysis. FL+2 incorporates a first layer that utilizes a strict data transmission control mechanism using a P4 switch for infrastructural security. The second layer ensures model traceability (for better model privacy) and data access (including data delegation) control via blockchain. Here, we present the early results of the proposed FL+2 prototype, which was implemented in our in-house cloud/fog testbed. We discuss how a P4 switch as well as blockchain-based controlled data access and traceability mechanism offer specific security benefits and the associated development overhead.

Author: Lin, Z.; Zhang, J.; Guan, S.; Man, K. L.
Title: Adaptive Compression for Trusted Data Circulation of Federated Learning in Internet of Vehicles
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
Abstract Note: In the Internet of Vehicles (IoV), federated learning (FL) has been regarded as a promising solution for training distributed models while preserving data privacy, which is a critical requirement for trusted data circulation (TDC). However, due to the limited resources and the dynamic network structure of IoV, improving the data communication efficiency in FL training is still a huge challenge. Compressive sensing (CS) reduces communication overhead by enabling efficient data compression and reconstruction. In this paper, we take CS-enabled FL one step further by introducing an adaptive scheme to enhance communication performance. Specifically, we first select vehicles participating in FL based on moving conditions to maximize system stability and model convergence. Second, inspired by synaptic intelligence (SI) in the field of continuous learning (CL), we prioritize gradient information based on its importance in model performance to optimize the CS compression and reconstruction process. Experimental results show that the proposed scheme can achieve the same accuracy as the classical compression method with less or even less than half of the data, which indicates that it is a practical FL scheme for IoV.

Author: Guo, S.; Li, L.; Du, J.
Title: Joint-FU: Blockchain-Based Federated Feature Unlearning Method

Abstract Note: With the increasing attention to privacy protection issues in the field of distributed machine learning, how to empower users with the “right to be forgotten” in federated learning has become an important research direction. By assigning a learnable mask weight to each feature, dynamically adjust the contribution of each feature in the unlearning process. This method not only effectively avoids conflicts between features, but also significantly improves the stability and efficiency of the unlearning process. Meanwhile, sparse regularization ensures the focus of the unlearning process and avoids unnecessary feature unlearning. In addition, the integration of blockchain enhances the transparency and security of the system, ensuring the immutability and traceability of all update operations. Author: F, M. H.; Bhanu, S.; Janarthanan, S.; Alagumuthukrishnan, S.; Reddy, G. V.; Siddhan, S.
Title: Federated Learning Using Blockchain for Decentralized and Enhanced secure network management driven by Artificial Intelligence

Author: Wang, Z.; Zhang, L.; Zhou, H.; Kan, H.; Zhang, J.
Title: RESA: RLWE-Based Efficient Secure Aggregation For Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 24th International Conference on Trust, Security and Privacy in Computing and Communications (TrustCom)
Abstract Note: With the widespread application of federated learning in sensitive domains such as healthcare and finance, preserving the privacy of participants’ local data while maintaining model performance has become a critical challenge. Existing secure aggregation schemes based on homomorphic encryption or pairwise masking still suffer from substantial computational and communication overhead. To address this problem, this paper presents RESA, an efficient secure aggregation protocol based on Ring Learning with Errors (RLWE) encryption. By replacing pairwise masking with the RLWE-based encryption scheme, gradients can be efficiently encrypted and decrypted. Furthermore, by combining Paillier homomorphic encryption with the homomorphic pseudorandom generator (HPRG) to aggregate all clients’ RLWE keys, our scheme effectively protects the privacy of honest clients. Also, the proposed protocol is resilient to client dropouts due to the application of secret sharing. The experimental results show that the proposed protocol achieves 5-10× speedup in the server-side computation, compared to Bell et al. (USENIX Security’23).

Author: Govindaram, A.; Prasath, J. S.; Suganya, A.; Jayasakthi, K.; Rajkumar, N.; A, J. Anand
Title: Federated Learning in Big Data with IoT for Intrusion Detection

Author: Wang, R.; Liu, X.; Yang, H.; Liu, D.; Zhang, H.; Liu, Y.; Su, Z.

Abstract Note: Federated learning (FL) preserves privacy yet struggles to secure truthful participation and adequate effort. Utilities are formulated for coupled sensing and training energy under a global budget, and a contract menu specifies the minimum effective contribution and payment. Author: Camalan, E.; Celiktas, B.

Abstract Note: Blockchain-based Federated Learning (BFL) is an emerging decentralized machine learning paradigm that enables model training without relying on a central server. This work presents VerifBFL, a trustless, privacy-preserving, and verifiable federated learning framework that integrates blockchain technology and cryptographic protocols.
