Author: Reddy, S. M.; Mahesh, K.; GnanaPraneeth, K.; Rajula, S.
Title: Blockchain-Integrated AI for Secure Data Transmission in IoT Ecosystems
Publication Title: 2025 2nd International Conference on Recent Trends in Electrical, Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICRTEECT)
Abstract Note: The rapid proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices across critical sectors has introduced unprecedented security challenges. While Artificial Intelligence (AI) provides powerful tools for threat detection, AI models themselves are vulnerable to data poisoning and adversarial attacks. This paper introduces a novel hybrid framework that synergistically integrates AI with blockchain technology to create a secure and resilient data transmission ecosystem for the IoT. Our architecture utilizes AI-driven techniques, including simulated federated learning, for privacy-preserving anomaly detection at the network edge. A blockchain-based ledger then provides tamper-resistant data validation and immutable record-keeping. The system employs smart contracts on a private Ethereum testnet, combined with the InterPlanetary File System (IPFS) for efficient off-chain storage, ensuring both data integrity and provenance. We evaluated the framework in a simulated environment using benchmark datasets, including CICIDS2017 and UNSW-NB15. The results show a high efficacy in detecting sophisticated attacks, with a Random Forest classifier achieving 98.46
Manual Tags: Blockchain; Internet of Things (IoT); Federated Learning; Data Security; Smart Contracts; Anomaly Detection; Artificial Intelligence (AI)

Author: Ai, X.; Cao, Y.
Title: SATA: A Distributed Stealthy and Persistent Backdoor Attack via Trigger Association in Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 24th International Conference on Trust, Security and Privacy in Computing and Communications (TrustCom)
Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) enables decentralized model training while preserving data privacy, but it remains susceptible to backdoor attacks, especially under dynamic client participation and non-IID data. Existing attacks, such as Distributed Backdoor Attack (DBA) and Shadow Attack, often struggle to balance stealthiness, robustness, and persistence. To address these challenges, we propose the Stealthy Associate Trigger Attack (SATA), which integrates four key techniques: trigger splitting, associative learning, L2-norm control, and progressive backdoor injection. Experimental results on CIFAR-10 using ResNet-18 demonstrate that SATA achieves a 99.26% Attack Success Rate (ASR) with only 10% malicious clients, while maintaining L2-norm deviations within 0.1 to evade detection. Moreover, SATA achieves an ASR-100 of 86.68%, indicating strong persistence. Additional evaluations on MNIST and under defense mechanisms like Multi-Krum and FoolsGold validate the generalizability and adaptability of our method. These findings highlight critical vulnerabilities in privacy-sensitive FL systems and call for the development of more effective defenses. Future work will explore extending SATA to text and audio domains and improving efficiency on edge devices.
Manual Tags: Federated Learning; Backdoor Attack; Persistence; Stealthiness; Trigger Association

Author: Chen, J.; Sun, S.; Ge, W.; Li, Y.; Zhang, H.; Chen, X.
Title: REPChain-FL:A Secure and Incentive-Aligned Federated Learning Framework over DAG-Based Blockchain
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 11th International Conference on Edge Computing and Scalable Cloud (EdgeCom)
Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL), as a distributed machine learning paradigm, shows great potential in protecting data privacy. However, traditional federated learning frameworks face challenges in scalability, security, and incentive mechanisms. Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG)-based Federated Learning (DAGFL) enhances system scalability with its high concurrency and low latency features, but it also introduces new security risks and incentive difficulties. Malicious nodes can compromise the integrity of the global model through methods like model poisoning, while the lack of effective incentive mechanisms weakens the participation willingness of honest nodes. To address these issues, this paper proposes a security and incentive framework for DAG-FL. This framework includes two core mechanisms: a DAG-enhanced dual-validation mechanism and a reputationdriven incentive mechanism. The dual-validation mechanism accurately identifies malicious updates by combining “gradient trend consistency” and “dynamic baseline model validation,” effectively defending against various poisoning attacks. The reputation-driven incentive mechanism couples a node’s historical contributions, real-time behavior, and security compliance to construct a dynamic reputation score, which is used for fair and efficient reward and penalty distribution. We conducted experimental evaluations on the MNIST dataset. The results show that compared to baseline methods, the proposed framework improves model accuracy, attack defense strength, and convergence speed. It can effectively incentivize nodes for long-term and honest participation throughout the entire lifecycle of federated learning training while ensuring system security.
Manual Tags: Federated Learning; Incentive Mechanism; Directed Acyclic Graph; Model Poisoning; Reputation System; Security Validation

Author: Shahbazi, Z.; Johnsson, M.
Title: Incentive Mechanism Design Based on Blockchain and Federated Learning for Honest Participation
Publication Title: 2025 7th International Conference on Blockchain Computing and Applications (BCCA)
Abstract Note: Encouraging honest and continuous involvement is a major challenge in Federated Learning (FL). In FL, clients use their own data and computing power to help train shared models. Many existing methods aim to encourage participation, but they often overlook real-world issues. These include clients not being compatible, limited money for tasks, differences in data quality, and the possibility of dishonest or harmful participants. This study suggests a unified method to address these challenges. It combines matching tasks based on compatibility, ensuring rewards, and assessing participation based on trust. The method applies game theory and Shapley valuation, and it utilizes technologies like blockchain and smart contracts. These help make sure that reports about costs are honest, contributions are judged privately, and rewards are distributed fairly and securely without any tampering. The design of this method accommodates both helpful and unhelpful task requesters, and it can adjust based on changes in clients’ reputations and performances over time. Tests with real-world data show that these proposed methods significantly improve model performance, communication efficiency, and honest participation in FL settings. This approach establishes a foundation for sustainable, secure, and reliable federated learning by applying well-thought-out incentives.
Manual Tags: blockchain; federated learning; security; incentive mechanism

Author: Wang, J.; Guan, X.; Gao, C.; Yang, S.
Title: A Zero-Knowledge-Based Approach to Resist Poisoning Attacks in Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2025 2nd International Seminar on Artificial Intelligence, Computer Technology and Control Engineering (ACTCE)
Abstract Note: In the Internet of Vehicles (IoV) network, numerous vehicle terminals are required to continuously upload local data to maintain the latest service models, which supports intelligent transportation and personalized services. However, the privacy risks posed by this continuous data uploading cannot be ignored. Federated learning, as a distributed ma-chine learning paradigm, enables global model training without sharing original data. The introduction of blockchain further supports decentralization and immutability. However, federated learning also faces the risk of poisoning attacks, where malicious clients may upload abnormal or tampered model updates, severely impacting global model performance. To address this, this paper proposes a security framework that combines zero-knowledge proofs, federated learning, and blockchain. Clients use zero-knowledge proofs to ensure the legitimacy of uploaded updates, while the blockchain is responsible for verification and storage. Ultimately, a robust global model is obtained through federated aggregation. Experimental results demonstrate that this scheme effectively resists poisoning attacks, significantly improving system security and reliability while protecting user privacy.
Manual Tags: Federated learning; blockchain; secure aggregation; Internet of vehicles

Author: Krishnamoorthy, P.; Prabhu, S. N.
Title: Cybersecurity Implications of Federated Learning in Smart Cities: A Thorough Analysis of Obstacles, Attack Defenses, and Privacy Models
Publication Title: 2025 10th International Conference on Smart Structures and Systems (ICSSS)
Abstract Note: The fast evolution of smart cities, as derived from the Internet of Things (IoT), edge computing, and pervasive connectivity, has produced an exponential increase of cyber physical data. Cybersecurity in such dynamic and distributed systems is a daunting task-centralized learning model hardly protects user privacy and scales. To address this, Federated Learning (FL) is proposed to support collaborative training among edge devices without sharing complete data while the model is trained locally on each device. On the other hand, the application of FL in smart city ecosystems is not free from limitations. This survey paper offers an exhaustive examination of the cybersecurity considerations of FL in SCs, notably security vulnerability to privacy breaches, system scalability and potential attacks, communication overhead, and vulnerability to adversarial attacks. We classify and assess current FL-based cyber security solutions based on the used privacy-preserving methodologies including differential privacy, secure multi-party computation and homomorphic encryption, and we also analyze the associated vulnerabilities such as model inversion, data poisoning and backdoor attacks. The review also discusses the key challenges of applying FL to smart city infrastructure, such as diverse device capabilities, imbalanced data distribution, and communications. We also investigate advanced attack-resistance methods, collaborative defense operations, and federated systems that utilize blockchain to bring transparency and resilience. By summarizing current reborns, already spoiled spots, and future work directions, this work provides an overview for developing next-generation secure, efficient, and privacyconscious FL frameworks for smart cities. The obtained findings provide insights for academic research and practical deployments to enable secure DT in urban systems.
Manual Tags: Federated Learning; Smart Cities; Data Protection; Decentralized Learning; Adversarial Attacks; Privacy Models; Security Frameworks

Author: Wang, M.; Kang, T.; Dai, L.; Yang, H.; Du, J.; Liu, C.
Title: Scalable Multi-Party Collaborative Data Mining Based on Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2025 5th International Conference on Computer Science and Blockchain (CCSB)
Abstract Note: This paper proposes a federated learning-based method for multi-party collaborative mining and heterogeneous data source fusion. The goal is to address the shortcomings of traditional centralized learning in data privacy protection and cross-domain collaboration. To tackle the heterogeneity problem among multiple distributed data sources, the proposed method uses the federated learning framework to achieve collaborative training across different data sources. This approach avoids direct data transmission, effectively protecting data privacy. By transmitting model parameters to a central server for aggregation, the method enables efficient model fusion and collaborative learning across multiple data sources, significantly improving learning performance in non-i.i.d. data environments. Experimental results show that the proposed model demonstrates high accuracy and stability when handling heterogeneous data sources in multi-party collaborative learning. It outperforms other existing federated learning methods, such as FedAvg and SCAFFOLD. The model is able to ensure data privacy while improving data fusion efficiency and model generalization. This approach holds promising application potential. This study provides an innovative solution to the challenges of multi-party collaborative mining and data privacy protection, particularly in fields such as healthcare, financial risk control, and intelligent manufacturing, where data security is paramount. It offers technological support for real-world data sharing and crossdomain collaboration.
Manual Tags: Federated learning; data privacy protection; heterogeneous data fusion; multi-party collaborative mining

Author: Molose, R.; Isong, B.; Abu-Mahfouz, A.; Dladlu, N.
Title: Analysis of Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning’s Resilience against Adverse Attack in Internet of Things Systems
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE AFRICON
Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) enables Internet of Things (IoT) devices to learn from decentralized data, enhancing privacy, security, and efficiency. However, its vulnerability to adversarial attacks poses significant challenges. This paper evaluates various FL models: Hierarchical FedAvg, Decentralized FedAvg (D-FedAvg), Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM), Gossip Learning (GL), and Stochastic Gossip Learning (SGL), for anomaly detection in network traffic. We utilize NSL-KDD datasets and metrics such as accuracy, communication overhead, and computation time to analyse their performance under normal and adversarial conditions. The findings reveal that Hierarchical FedAvg achieves the highest accuracy (93.57%) in normal scenarios, while GL excels in convergence efficiency (1.1456s). After data poisoning, SGL shows superior resilience with an anomaly detection accuracy of 83.31%. The Hierarchical FedAvg and ADMM-based FL models exhibit lower communication and computational overhead, but experience significant accuracy drops during attacks. In addition, comparisons with existing techniques highlight a balance between accuracy, efficiency, and robustness, contributing to privacy-preserving anomaly detection systems for IoT networks.
Manual Tags: Internet of Things; Security; Federated Learning; Privacy; Software Defined Networks

Author: Ali, A.; Drlik, M.; Wadi, M.; Elmasry, W.
Title: Enhancing Privacy in Smart Grids and IOTs Systems by Using Federated Learning: Case Study
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Smart Applications, Communications and Networking (SmartNets)
Abstract Note: To enhance privacy in smart grids (SGs) and internet of thing (IoT) systems, a Federated Learning (FL) framework is proposed for practical application. By leveraging the idea of decentralizing model training and keeping raw data local, the framework addresses the privacy and security challenges associated with data collection on centralized servers. The framework achieves high accuracy (98.2% on MNIST, 85.6% on CIFAR-10) while resisting poisoning attacks and scaling efficiently by integrating differential privacy and secure aggregation. A case study on energy demand forecasting confirms its real-world applicability. The results demonstrate the potential of FL for scalable, privacy-preserving data analysis in IoT and SGs, with future work focused on integrating other privacy-enhancing technologies such as blockchain (BC).
Manual Tags: federated learning; privacy; smart grid; IOT

Author: Dabbakuti, J. R. K. K.; Pothula, L. S.; Chokkaku, V. K.; Yellina, N. K.; Yarrakula, M.
Title: Decentralized Framework for Enhancing Satellite Navigation Accuracy and Security: Integrating Blockchain with GNSS
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Advances in Modern Age Technologies for Health and Engineering Science (AMATHE)
Abstract Note: Distributed ledger technologies, particularly blockchain, have gained significant attention for applications like health data sharing. However, their utility in enhancing satellite navigation systems remains limited. This study addresses the existing challenges in satellite-based navigation and introduces a decentralized Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) data-sharing framework aimed at improving both accuracy and security. Unlike traditional centralized approaches, the proposed decentralized system utilizes multiple satellite signals to cross-verify positional data, reducing noise, increasing precision, and filtering out inaccuracies. Simulations indicate that the decentralized framework achieves high performance, processing 99.94 transactions per second with a 0.01-second response time, a 1.00 Cross-Validation Agreement Ratio, a 0.20-second convergence time, and a redundancy efficiency of 0.20. These findings underscore the advantages of decentralized GNSS systems over centralized ones, particularly in terms of scalability, reliability, and processing efficiency. The work lays a foundational framework for integrating blockchain operations into GNSS models, offering innovative solutions for secure and efficient satellites.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; Cross-validation; Decentralized Networks; Navigation Data Security; Positioning precision

Author: Saviour, M. P. A.; Samiappan, D.; Sethu, S.; Al-Shaikh, A.; Chadge, R.; Dinesh, M.
Title: Investigating Blockchain as a Confirmation Mechanism for Decentralized Computing Platform’s PrivacyPreserving Deep Learning Models
Publication Title: 2025 10th International Conference on Smart Structures and Systems (ICSSS)
Abstract Note: Emergence of decentralized computing infrastructures with the advent of privacy-preserving deep learning is a paradigm shift in data-centric models training and deployment. But maintaining the integrity, trust, and transparency of the computations in these decentralized environments presents an open challenge. Benefits of Blockchain Technology for Digital Identity Onboarding Blockchain technology has the advantages of decentralized ledger and cryptographic verification methods which provide an effective means of overcoming these worries. This study explores using the blockchain as a verification mechanism for privacy-preserving deep learning models across distributed computing platforms. More specifically, we investigate in this work how the interaction with a blockchain network can be used to validate correctness of model updates, preserve data privacy, and generate trust in a non-centralized manner. We focus on ensuring the security of the training process through blockchain-based solutions while leveraging advanced techniques, like Federated Learning and Differential Privacy to preserve the privacy of sensitive data. Blockchain is used through a combination of smart contracts and consensus algorithms to record and verify every step during the model’s training cycle, with the goal of preventing malicious participants from tampering with or corrupting the model. The second part of the study investigates whether such an integration can scale by evaluating the efficiency of blockchain, given the large number of model update transactions during training. Experimental results show that a blockchain is a suitable layer with transparency and guaranteed correctness that can be used alone or in a multi-party setup that simultaneously increases the security and privacy of decentralized AI. This work paves the way for more secure decentralized AI systems by making sure that future privacypreserving deep learning models are both secure and scalable.
Manual Tags: Federated learning; Differential privacy; Data privacy; Privacy-preserving; Smart contracts; Decentralized computing; Consensus algorithms

Author: Xie, L.; Luan, T.; Cai, W.; Yan, G.; Chen, Z.; Xi, N.; Fang, Y.; Shen, Q.; Wu, Z.; Yuan, J.
Title: dFLMoE: Decentralized Federated Learning via Mixture of Experts for Medical Data Analysis
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
Abstract Note: Federated learning has wide applications in the medical field. It enables knowledge sharing among different healthcare institutes while protecting patients’ privacy. However, existing federated learning systems are typically centralized, requiring clients to upload client-specific knowledge to a central server for aggregation. This centralized approach would integrate the knowledge from each client into a centralized server, and the knowledge would be already undermined during the centralized integration before it reaches back to each client. Besides, the centralized approach also creates a dependency on the central server, which may affect training stability if the server malfunctions or connections are unstable. To address these issues, we propose a decentralized federated learning framework named dFLMoE. In our framework, clients directly exchange lightweight head models with each other. After exchanging, each client treats both local and received head models as individual experts, and utilizes a client-specific Mixture of Experts (MoE) approach to make collective decisions. This design not only reduces the knowledge damage with client-specific aggregations but also removes the dependency on the central server to enhance the robustness of the framework. We validate our framework on multiple medical tasks, demonstrating that our method evidently outperforms state-of-the-art approaches under both model homogeneity and heterogeneity settings.
Manual Tags: decentralized federated learning; medical data analysis; mixture of experts

Author: SN, P.; Saini, D. K. J. B.; Shelke, N.; Pimpalkar, A.; D, S.; Kumar, G. H.
Title: AI-Driven Cyber Threat Intelligence with Blockchain: A Federated and Privacy-Preserving Approach (FPPA) for Secure Defense
Publication Title: 2025 9th International Conference on Inventive Systems and Control (ICISC)
Abstract Note: The growing complexity of cyber threats requires a smart, decentralized, and tamper-proof method of Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI). This work suggests a new combination of Blockchain and Artificial Intelligence (AI) to improve security, transparency, and real-time threat protection in cybersecurity environments. Our method utilizes blockchain's immutability to provide reliable CTI sharing and AI-based threat analytics for adaptive defense. In this work, a Smart Contract-based AI platform has been designed to facilitate automated threat validation, anomaly detection, and predictive security responses. The platform leverages Federated Learning (FL) and Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to ensure privacy-preserving and adversarial-resilient intelligence sharing. Our blockchain-driven decentralized platform eliminates single point of failure, enhances traceability, and promotes stakeholder collaboration in contrast to conventional centralized CTI platforms (e.g. G. governments, businesses, and security researchers). Robustness against adversarial attacks, reduced false positives, and improved detection accuracy are demonstrated by extensive experimental evaluation on real cyberattack data sets. The effectiveness of our solution in thwarting Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs) and zero-day attacks is demonstrated through comparative benchmarking with existing CTI frameworks. As we lay the groundwork for a next-generation, AI-powered blockchain platform for cybersecurity, also consider scalability, regulatory compliance, and integration challenges.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; Federated Learning; Smart Contracts; Artificial Intelligence; Cyber Threat Intelligence; Zero-Day Attacks; Adversarial Networks; Decentralized Security

Author: C.S, S. C.; Subramanian, R. R.
Title: A Blockchain-Enabled Framework for Privacy-Preserving Deep Learning Collaboration in Healthcare
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Computational Robotics, Testing and Engineering Evaluation (ICCRTEE)
Abstract Note: This paper suggests bringing together decentralized technology and artificial intelligence to secure and enable collaboration. Hospitals can exchange data about AI models in a confidential manner with help from the proposed framework, mixing blockchain and deep learning. Since the data is stored with Hyperledger Fabric and an accurate record using hashes, the system ensures there is no central control. Since the training is conducted within hospital organizations, the associated data is considered private and is subject to regulatory compliance. Before anything happens, the blockchain checks the model’s data and ensures it is not fraudulent. It is found that three organizations working on a Fabric network prototype can communicate and work safely and effectively. Using this system confirms that AI developed in healthcare is easy to scale, secure and comes together with different sources of information.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; Deep Learning; Smart Contracts; Hyperledger Fabric; Privacy-Preserving; Decentralized Learning; Healthcare AI

Author: Yan, K.; Chen, Y.; Fang, X.; Bian, G.; Crespi, N.
Title: A Distributed Personalized Federated Learning Method based on Siamese Neural Networks
Publication Title: 2025 International Wireless Communications and Mobile Computing (IWCMC)
Abstract Note: Federated learning allows multiple users to collaboratively train models while protecting data privacy. However, for some users, the non-independent identically distributed nature of user data often reduces the accuracy of the global model. Existing personalized federated learning methods usually focus on individual users, which leads to problems such as bias and overfitting. This paper proposes a new distributed personalized federated learning framework based on Siamese neural networks (DPFL-SNN). First, a novel similarity calculation method is designed using the dual-branch structure of the Siamese neural network to effectively identify local users with similar data. Second, by combining this similarity calculation with blockchain technology, a new consensus algorithm is developed to achieve decentralization and reduce security risks. Simulations conducted on publicly available datasets demonstrate that the DPFL-SNN achieves higher accuracy compared to state-of-the-art personalized federated learning methods, thanks to enhanced collaboration among users with similar data.
Manual Tags: Federated Learning; Distributed; Personalization; Siamese Neural Networks

Author: Vijaywargiya, R.; Bandhu, K. C.
Title: A Review on Security and Privacy Enhancement of Patient Data using Hyperledger Fabric
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Advances in Computing Research On Science Engineering and Technology (ACROSET)
Abstract Note: In healthcare blockchain technology's ability is recognizable for enhancing data privacy [1]. This paper looks at recent developments in the blockchain, with a particular significance on the Hyperledger Fabric framework [2]. The review shows away the rising trend of engaging blockchain to upgrade healthcare data governance, ensure data exchange in cyberphysical systems, and consolidate supply chain security by means of smart contracts [3] [4]. The review emphasizes the productiveness of Hyperledger Fabric, with its resilient and authorized architecture, in establish data integrity, confidentiality, and interoperability [5] [6]. Author: Yang, C.; Zhang, W.
Title: Research on Blockchain Data Sharing and Privacy Protection Scheme Based on Reputation Value Calculation
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Image Processing and Computer Applications (ICIPCA)
Abstract Note: The issues of data sharing and privacy protection have always been a major research focus in blockchain. In response to problems such as data security and personal privacy protection that are prevalent in medical big data, in order to protect patients' privacy while efficiently utilizing the medical data of various medical institutions, a blockchain data sharing and privacy protection scheme based on reputation value calculation is proposed. By screening members with high - quality data before training, the data sharing process is transformed into a model parameter sharing process, avoiding the upload of original data to the blockchain and thus preventing patient privacy leakage. At the same time, the reputation scheme is improved to select candidate hospitals with high-quality data and reliability to participate in the federated learning training model. The distributed consortium blockchain is used to store the reputation values of each hospital and the global model parameters, and hospitals that actively contribute high-quality data are rewarded. The experimental results show that the proposed scheme can screen out high-quality data sources, reduce the interaction time between edge nodes and malicious nodes. Even when the reputation value is above 0.5, a learning accuracy of 0.857 can be achieved. Compared with existing typical federated learning schemes, the performance of the proposed scheme is superior.
Manual Tags: Federated learning; Blockchain; Interaction time; Model parameters; Reputation value calculation

Author: E, D.; R, A.; R, B.; A, H. S.
Title: Optimized Biometric-Based Anonymous Authentication for Secure Mobile Edge Computing
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Electronics and Renewable Systems (ICEARS)
Abstract Note: We propose a novel biometric-based anonymous authentication system for facilitating operation in mobile edge computing networks. Hence, the proposed approach incorporates FaceNet to perform face embedding extraction for better reliability and Federated Learning (FL) for privacy-preserving model training. Therefore, dynamic learning rate optimization makes the system adjust effectively to the fluctuations in data distribution enhancing the models. An Android-based application acts as a front-end through which users can safely take and send templates to the back end for real-time processing. The performances obtained from experiments show a very high identification accuracy as well as effectively safeguarding users’ privacy; therefore, making the realisation of the system well suited for applications that requires high levels of privacy in edge computing.

Author: V, V.; Velmurugan, S.; P, N.; R, S.; Muniappan, R.; Thangarasu, N.
Title: Edge Sec: A Privacy-Preserving IoT-ML Framework for Smart Home Security Threat Detection
Publication Title: 2025 6th International Conference on Smart Electronics and Communication (ICOSEC)
Abstract Note: Smart homes increasingly utilize IoT-enabled products for automation and convenience; however, this also renders them vulnerable to several security and privacy issues. To alleviate this danger, we introduce Edge Sec, a lightweight and privacy-preserving machine learning framework for real-time threat detection. Our methodology involves implementing compressed Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models directly on edge devices to oversee motion sensor data, entry door logs, and ambient audio. Utilizing Federated Learning (FedAvg), devices collaboratively train local models while preserving raw data confidentiality, and Differential Privacy (DP) techniques provide robust user privacy during model updates. In comparison to cutting-edge methodologies utilizing synthetic smart home data, Edge Sec attains an accuracy of 98.2%, precision of 97.9%, recall of 96.4%, and an F1 score of 97.9%. The model maintains inference latency below 50 ms and functions at under 150 mW per device. The loss of privacy is maintained at under 5% with a privacy budget of ε = 1.0, while performance continues to uphold value preservation. These findings illustrate Edge Sec's efficacy, scalability, and privacy-conscious implementation for smart home security on resource-limited IoT platforms.
Manual Tags: Internet of Things (IoT); Federated Learning; Machine Learning; Privacy Preservation; Differential Privacy; Anomaly Detection; Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM); Edge Sec; Real-Time Threat Detection; Smart Home Security

Author: Khan, S. A.; Khan, F. A.; Srinivasan, S.
Title: Development of AI Models Driven by Blockchain for Privacy-Preserving Data Exchange in Personal Data Management and Healthcare Systems
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICACT)
Abstract Note: As reliance on AI in personal data management and health care systems increases, concerns about data privacy and security grow. Conventional AI models improve their predictions and performance by access to sensitive personal information, placing users at the risk of privacy concerns and data breaches. Blockchain is a decentralized, secure, and transparent framework for managing data - one that holds potential for answering these privacy challenges. This work looks into forming up AI models based on blockchain technology to support privacy-preserving data interchange in personal data management and healthcare systems. We aim to develop a system that embeds privacy in data sharing - to do so, we will leverage the benefits of blockchain, such as encryption, immutability and no central controller, augmented with advanced AI techniques. They proposed a framework based on smart contracts that can automatically grant data access and verify if the AI model was working on the encrypted data without showing personal or sensitive information. To address this challenge, federated learning and homomorphic encryption techniques are introduced to facilitate the training of distributed AI models while ensuring data privacy in decentralized networks. Finally, the research investigates blockchainpowered AI models in healthcare systems, which necessitate data privacy due to stringent regulatory frameworks, to assess their performance, scalability, and security. This research helps pave the way for more responsible, transparent and impactful AI-driven solutions for personal data management and healthcare systems by illustrating the synergistic capabilities of AI and blockchain supporting secure and privacy-respecting data exchange. The findings indicate that by leveraging the power of blockchain, it is possible to bolster the confidence and trustworthiness of Artificial Intelligence systems, without breaching data protection regulations while not impacting the advantages of AI innovation in crucial sectors.
Manual Tags: Federated learning; Homomorphic encryption; Smart contracts; Healthcare systems; Data exchange; Decentralized networks; Personal data management

Author: Goud, R. G.; B.Vittal; A.Sadanandam; Priya, R. B.; Kumar, G. G.; S.P.Santhoshkumar
Title: Efficient and Secure Big Data Analytics via Federated Mining Techniques
Publication Title: 2025 9th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
Abstract Note: The exponential growth of large data provides huge opportunities for discovery of knowledge, but also increases important concerns about privacy, security and scalability. Traditional centralized data mining approaches increase the risk by collecting sensitive information in a single repository. To solve these challenges, this study proposes a data sources without highlighting raw data. Framework integrates secured multipratis computation, homomorphic encryption and differential secrecy to ensure privacy, reduce overhead and maintain efficiency. Healthcare, finance and image dataset displays that the proposed system only receives high future accuracy (92%) with high future-staging accuracy (92%) with only a minor trade-band compared to centralized learning (94%). Statistical results show a decrease of 80% in privacy leakage risk, 25% decrease in communication costs, and acceptable computational overhead ( 1.5 ×). Strong tests confirm the flexibility against adverse hazards such as model inverted and data poisoning with a performance drop less than 5%. These findings validate the outline as a safe, accurate and scalable solution for real -world large data applications.

Author: Manthu, R.; Tripathi, R.; Sahu, T. P.; Killi, B. P. R.
Title: A Game-Theoretic Incentive Mechanism for Blockchain-based Semi-Asynchronous Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2025 13th International Conference on Intelligent Systems and Embedded Design (ISED)
Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) is a privacy-preserving technique that focuses on sharing intermediate training parameters rather than raw data, which helps to prevent privacy violations and facilitates effective data collaboration. The integration of blockchain technology with FL has generated significant interest due to its benefits, including decentralization and enhanced privacy protection for raw data. While existing asynchronous FL methods have successfully tackled the low training efficiency associated with synchronous approaches, they often overlook the need for incentives for participating parties due to the limitations of a centralized trust model. Numerous existing incentive models depend on centralized trust mechanisms, which can undermine the decentralized essence of blockchain and create potential vulnerabilities. To overcome these difficulties, an FL model is developed in the blockchain network to enhance the performance of the model. Further, the strategies of participants are analyzed by implementing the game theory model along with the incentive mechanism based on smart contracts. This incentive mechanism is helpful in minimizing malicious action based on the Nash equilibrium. In addition, the theory models based on the Age of Information (AoI) are considered to motivate the data sharing in a user-centric manner. Several simulations are conducted to evaluate the security model of the incentive mechanism. The experimental results demonstrate the validity of our proposed schemes.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; Age of Information; Game Theory Model; Semi Asynchronous Federated Learning

Author: Balakrishnan, T. S.; V.R.Vimal; Ponnaian, G.; Raj, T. S.; Thangam, S. A.
Title: Blockchain-Orchestrated Privacy Preservation for Cloud-Based Data Mining
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Recent Trends in Computing and Smart Mobility (RCSM)
Abstract Note: Data mining on the cloud makes it possible to perform analytics at a large scale using distributed computing resources, but data decentralization makes sensitive data vulnerable to non-trusted or semi-trusted conditions. Traditional security measures are not always sufficient to handle more complicated adversarial threats like data poisoning, model inversion, and unauthorized exploitation. The paper introduces a privacy preservation framework (BOPPF) designed using Blockchain as an orchestration layer; it combines a form of differential privacy, secure aggregation and optional homomorphic encryption. The blockchain guarantees immutable logging, access control using smart contracts and verifiable compliance tracking whereas the defence component utilises anomaly detection and strong aggregation to reduce interference by adversaries. The experimental analysis of MIMIC-III, Credit Card Fraud data and CIFAR-10 data can prove that the framework is highly utility, highly robust, and has a high degree of privacy protection with a low amount of computation overhead. The paper also addresses the concepts of scalability as more nodes are involved and the cost of energy analysis, with the practicality of implementing it being through containerized microservices. In general, the results confirm that blockchain can be used to improve transparency, trust, and auditability of secure cloud data mining processes that can be applied to various industries, including health, finance, and e-commerce.

Author: Gumasa, V. K.; Shilpi, S.; N, S.; Tewari, R.; Soni, M.
Title: Blockchain-Integrated Federated Trust Authentication Framework for Secure Mobile Payment System
Publication Title: 2025 2nd International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
Abstract Note: In recent years, mobile payment systems witnessed rapid adoption, but ensuring secure, privacy-preserving and fraud-resistant transactions remained an important challenge because of evolving cyber threats. Existing authentication models faced limitations in balancing security, usability and scalability especially in decentralized mobile environments. Therefore, this research proposes Blockchain-Integrated Federated Trust Authentication (BIFTA) to enhance mobile payment security by combining multi-factor, context-aware authentication with decentralized verification. Initially, digital wallet generates Federated Transaction Token (FTT) that encapsulates biometric, location, behavioral and contextual features in an encrypted format. Then, local federated learning model evaluates trust scores for each transaction without sharing raw user data. Next, permissioned blockchain network of validator nodes verify token by using smart contracts and achieves consensus for transaction approval. Finally, global fraud detection model is continuously updated through federated learning which enabled adaptive and privacy-preserving detection of emerging threats. From the overall analysis, the proposed BIFTA framework demonstrates strong performance across all execution times. At \textbackslash{}mathbf{8 0 m s}\, it achieves a transaction security ratio (TSR) of 480%, Protection Ration (PR) of 95%, and Regulatory Compliance Ratio (RCR) of 798% which indicated robust transaction security, enhanced data protection and high regulatory compliance.
Manual Tags: privacy-preserving; blockchain-integrated federated trust authentication; contextual features; federated transaction token; mobile payment system

Author: Bendada, A. M. R.; Korba, A. A.; Bouchiha, M. A.; Ghamri-Doudane, Y.
Title: BotDetect: A Decentralized Federated Learning Framework for Detecting Financial Bots on the EVM Blockchains
Publication Title: ICC 2025 - IEEE International Conference on Communications
Abstract Note: The rapid growth of decentralized finance (DeFi) has led to the widespread use of automated agents, or bots, within blockchain ecosystems like Ethereum, Binance Smart Chain, and Solana. While these bots enhance market efficiency and liquidity, they also raise concerns due to exploitative behaviors that threaten network integrity and user trust. This paper presents a decentralized federated learning (DFL) approach for detecting financial bots within Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM)-based blockchains. The proposed framework leverages federated learning, orchestrated through smart contracts, to detect malicious bot behavior while preserving data privacy and aligning with the decentralized nature of blockchain networks. Addressing the limitations of both centralized and rule-based approaches, our system enables each participating node to train local models on transaction history and smart contract interaction data, followed by on-chain aggregation of model updates through a permissioned consensus mechanism. This design allows the model to capture complex and evolving bot behaviors without requiring direct data sharing between nodes. Experimental results demonstrate that our DFL framework achieves high detection accuracy while maintaining scalability and robustness, providing an effective solution for bot detection across distributed blockchain networks.

Author: N, P. S.; Shelke, N.; Saini, D. K. Jang Bahadur; Balla, R.; Nixon, J. S.; Pimpalkar, A.
Title: Federated Deep Learning for DDoS Detection in IoT: Case Studies, Challenges, and Practical Insights
Publication Title: 2025 3rd International Conference on Intelligent Cyber Physical Systems and Internet of Things (ICoICI)
Abstract Note: The growing intensity and complexity of Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) attacks present vital security threats to Internet of Things (IoT) networks. Centralized solutions to DDoS detection are hampered by scalability, latency, and privacy issues, requiring decentralized and smart solutions. Federated Deep Learning (FDL) has emerged as a viable paradigm, facilitating collaborative model training without revealing raw data. This paper introduces a systematic case study-based investigation of FDL in IoT DDoS detection with a focus on its applications, challenges, and implications. We examine various case studies from a range of IoT environments industrial IoT, smart homes, and critical infrastructure and analyze how FDL is effective against developing attack patterns. Critical issues including heterogeneous data distribution, adversarial robustness, communication overhead, and real-time adaptability are examined and some solutions discussed. Our results reflect the excellence of FDL in providing high detection accuracy with maintained privacy and scalability. We also present future research directions in combining blockchain, reinforcement learning, and quantum computing to provide immunity to FDL-based DDoS detection systems. This research is a worthy reference for researchers as well as practitioners in promoting next-generation intelligent and decentralized IoT security architectures.
Manual Tags: Federated Learning; IoT Security; Intrusion Detection System (IDS); Privacy-Preserving AI; Blockchain for Security; DDoS Detection; Scalable AI in IoT

Author: Shakeel, N.; Prakash, S.; Shakeel, S.
Title: FedShield-IoMT: Blockchain-Federated Security for Collaborative Threat Learning in Healthcare IoT
Publication Title: 2025 3rd International Conference on IoT, Communication and Automation Technology (ICICAT)
Abstract Note: The proliferation of Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) devices in hospitals has increased reliance on connected systems for patient care while simultaneously expanding the attack surface. Traditional intrusion detection systems (IDSs) are limited by centralized architectures, raising concerns over scalability, privacy, and resilience to adversarial manipulation. This paper introduces FedShield-IoMT, a blockchain-enabled federated security framework designed to enable distributed hospitals to collaboratively train intrusion detection models without sharing sensitive data. FedShield-IoMT integrates TensorFlow Federated (TFF) for privacy-preserving model training with Hyperledger Fabric for secure model aggregation, authentication, and auditability. Two benchmark datasets, CICIDS2017 and IoT Botnet 2020, are used to evaluate performance. Results demonstrate that FedShield-IoMT achieves a detection accuracy of 96.8% and reduces false positives to 1.9%, outperforms both centralized IDS 89.3% and standalone federated learning 93.5%. Security analysis shows robustness against model poisoning, Sybil attacks, and data leakage, while audit logs ensure compliance with healthcare regulations. These findings establish blockchain-federated architectures as a promising direction for secure, privacy-preserving threat detection in IoMT-based healthcare infrastructures.
Manual Tags: blockchain; hyperledger fabric; federated learning; intrusion detection; healthcare security; IoMT

Author: Tajane, K.; Pitale, R.; Shende, S.; Singh, A.; Sinalkar, S.; Shinde, A.
Title: Privacy-Aware Task Placement Frameworks Integrating Predictive Models
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Quantum Computation-Based Sensor Application (ICAIQSA)
Abstract Note: The integration of predictive models with privacy-aware task placement represents one of the most critical challenges in modern distributed computing systems. This comprehensive report analyzes state-of-the-art solutions that address the fundamental gap between intelligent task scheduling and data privacy preservation [86]. Through a systematic analysis of over 60 research papers published between 2018–2025, we identify and evaluate four primary approaches: Differential Privacy, Federated Learning, Homomorphic Encryption, and Blockchain-based frameworks [42], [88]. Our findings reveal significant performance improvements ranging from a 20% reduction in privacy leakage to a 64% enhancement in throughput [4], [88], while also highlighting persistent challenges in computational overhead and system integration [61], [89]. The core problem lies in the absence of frameworks that ensure sensitive data remains protected during the scheduling process. This research provides a structured overview of existing solutions, identifies critical research gaps, and suggests future directions for this evolving field.

Author: Lian, W.; Zhuang, P.; Lin, S.
Title: Application of Federated Learning Algorithms in Cross-Border E-Commerce Data Compliance Sharing
Publication Title: 2025 2nd International Conference on Intelligent Algorithms for Computational Intelligence Systems (IACIS)
Abstract Note: Against the backdrop of global economic integration driving the continuous expansion of cross-border ecommerce, although data sharing is the key to improving operational efficiency and optimizing user experience, due to differences in data privacy protection regulations among countries, enterprises face compliance risks and data silos. Therefore, this article focuses on the application of federated learning algorithms in cross-border e-commerce data compliance sharing, constructs a layered architecture, and designs secure aggregation and differential privacy protection mechanisms, combined with supply chain scenario optimization training. The results showed that the experimental group had no data leakage, with an encryption strength of 256 bits (compared to 128 bits in the control group), a 2.7 point increase in access control, and a data integrity rate of 99.8% (3.3% higher), providing an innovative path for the secure circulation of industry data.

Author: Morabiya, R.; Kumari, A.; Borad, R.; Tanwar, S.; Kumar, P.; Shah, K.
Title: BFL: A Decentralized and Privacy-Preserving Framework for Lung Cancer Detection Using Federated Learning and Blockchain
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 12th Uttar Pradesh Section International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Engineering (UPCON)
Abstract Note: This paper presents BFL, a blockchain-enabled federated learning framework for privacy-preserving lung cancer detection. Unlike conventional deep learning approaches that require centralized data aggregation, BFL enables decentralized model training across multiple medical institutions, ensuring data privacy and regulatory compliance. The framework employs a ResNet152V2-based deep convolutional neural network (CNN) and a weighted Federated Averaging (FedAvg) algorithm for efficient model aggregation. Blockchain integration ensures transparency and traceability of model updates, fostering trust among stakeholders. Experimental evaluations on the LIDC dataset demonstrate superior accuracy (86%) and improved ROC-AUC performance over centralized models. BFL offers a scalable, secure, and efficient approach to lung cancer detection while addressing critical challenges in medical data sharing and decentralized AI training.

Author: Singh, A.; Pareek, V.; Sharma, A.
Title: Enhancing Trust and Security in Fintech with a Unified Integrity and Trust Framework
Publication Title: 2025 Second International Conference on Networks and Soft Computing (ICNSoC)
Abstract Note: The rapid growth of FinTech has necessitated robust security, trust, and integrity mechanisms in distributed systems. Existing frameworks lack a unified mechanism that integrates dynamic trust evaluation with blockchain-based privacy preservation while ensuring computational efficiency. This paper proposes the Unified Integrity and Trust Framework (UITF), which uses a dual-layered approach. The first layer, the Integrity Assurance Framework (IAF), uses a Multi-Trust Evaluation Indicator Model to combine scalable trust assessment, node reliability evaluation, adaptability analysis, and computational contribution measurement into a unified trust metric. The second layer, the Adaptive Blockchain Framework (ABF), uses blockchain technology to establish a decentralized, privacypreserving, and scalable integrity management system. Experimental results show that UITF improves trust accuracy by 23.5% and reduces computational overhead by 32% compared to conventional frameworks.

Author: Sandilya, R.; V.Mangaiyarkarasi; Laxmi, K. P.; Balassem, Z.; Ghosh, A. S.; Manaa, M. E.; Alhayaly, A. A.
Title: Hierarchical Federated Learning for Scalable and Secure Big Data Analytics in Edge Environments
Publication Title: 2025 3rd International Conference on Cyber Resilience (ICCR)
Abstract Note: The rapid expansion of edge computing has made large-scale data analytics possible, but it also raised concerns over scalability, security, and the effectiveness of communications. Under decentralized scenarios, conventional Federated Learning (FL) methods struggle with heterogeneous devices, constrained bandwidth, and security vulnerabilities. This work proposes a Hierarchical Federated Learning (HFL) framework that enhances resource efficiency, scalability, and privacy for large-scale data analysis in edge scenarios to mitigate the above problems. Our approach introduces a multi-level aggregation structure where the resulting model is enhanced by a global server, but intermediate nodes perform regional aggregation, and edge devices train models locally. By restricting the exposure of raw data, this hierarchical framework enhances data privacy, reduces communication cost, and relieves computing bottlenecks. Compared to traditional FL, experimental evaluations on real-world datasets indicate that it reduces bandwidth usage by 40%, improves model accuracy by 8–12%, and enhances training efficiency by 35%. Applications where safe and scalable analytics are crucial, like smart cities, industrial IoT, and personalized healthcare, gain significantly from the proposed approach. Federated learning in edge computing can be a solid basis for HFL, encouraging the development of safe, effective, and flexible AI-powered analytics, as per our investigation.
Manual Tags: Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning; Edge Computing; Big Data Analytics; Hierarchical Federated Learning (HFL); Scalability and Efficiency; Secure Distributed Learning

Author: Ulisi, U. M. Rao
Title: Decentralized Intelligence: Democratizing AI Development Through Blockchain and Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2025 3rd International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Applications Theme: Healthcare and Internet of Things (AIMLA)
Abstract Note: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence has been hindered by centralized control, leading to biases, monopolized innovation, and concerns over data privacy and governance. This paper introduces Decentralized Intelligence (DI), an innovative framework that synergizes blockchain technology with federated learning to democratize AI development and deployment. DI reimagines the AI lifecycle by enabling communities to contribute data, models, and computational resources in a decentralized and transparent manner. Blockchain ensures secure staking, consensus-driven model validation, and fair reward distribution, fostering trust and collaboration at scale. Federated learning (FL) enables individuals to refine machine learning models on their personal systems, safeguarding data privacy while leveraging diverse datasets for robust, bias-resistant models. This decentralized paradigm empowers diverse communities to develop bespoke AI solutions, addressing niche challenges while promoting inclusivity and innovation. The DI framework exemplifies how decentralization can revolutionize the AI ecosystem, providing a blueprint for equitable and collaborative technology development in the digital age.

Author: Gomathi, N.; Hussain, M. T.; Bharath; Pavitthiran

Author: R, V.; Charitha, B.; Kasarapu, B. Y.; Nair, M. C.
Title: Heart Disease Prediction using Secure Decentralized Data Sharing
Publication Title: 2025 8th International Conference on Trends in Electronics and Informatics (ICOEI)
Abstract Note: Heart disease continues to be a global health issue, causing much morbidity and mortality in spite of the advancement in medical science. Appropriate and timely prediction is crucial for successful clinical intervention, but conventional diagnostic measures are deficient in efficiency and accuracy to enable early-stage detection. Over the last few years, machine learning (ML) has been a high-powered tool used to predict heart disease by analyzing intricate patterns across various healthcare data sets like ECG signals and demographic data. Yet, most current ML-based systems are dependent on centralized repositories of data, which poses legitimate concerns about data privacy, security, and conformance to compliance with regulatory protocols like HIP AA and GDPR. This review looks at the state of heart disease prediction in the context of machine learning and decentralized data exchange technologies. We look at how techniques like federated learning and blockchain are being used in predictive health systems in order to overcome privacy and security constraints of the centralized approaches. The literature reports promising methods that allow collaborative training of models without sharing raw patient data, thus ensuring patient confidentiality while still enjoying high predictive accuracy. In addition, blockchain technology is emphasized to playa crucial role in ensuring data integrity, secure access management, and open auditing.

Author: Gayaki, U.; Madireddy, L.
Title: A Survey on Blockchain for Data Provenance and Security in Machine Learning Systems
Publication Title: 2025 6th International Conference on Electronics and Sustainable Communication Systems (ICESC)
Abstract Note: Blockchain and ML offer a potential way out of some of the biggest challenges to date with data provenance, security and decentralization. It therefore becomes increasingly relevant to preserve the integrity, traceability and privacy of data since ML algorithms are increasingly used to make and influence decisions within healthcare, the Internet of Things (IoT), finance and even in supply chains. Blockchain technology can provide a transparent, non-alterable ledger to enable a safe data sharing to train collaborative models, safely losing sensitive data. The survey explores basic framework and methods including federated learning, smart contracts, cryptographic improvements, and consensus algorithms, that underpin the union of blockchain and ML. In addition, it also explores some practical applications, uncovers the issues, including scalability, latency, and compliance with regulations, and proposes future development directions, aiming at the construction of lightweight, privacy-preserving, and interoperable systems. The results highlight the radical capabilities of blockchain to create reliable and stable ML systems concurrently with overcoming the current deficiencies of the technology.

Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) has gained attention as a decentralized machine learning paradigm, allowing the Internet of Things (IoT) edge devices to jointly train a model without sharing local data. But deploying FL in IoT ecosystems faces security threats, communication overhead, and diversity issues of devices. In this paper, we review FL frameworks that are secure and scalable for IoT networks considering adversarial attacks, differential privacy techniques and efficient aggregation strategies. Abstract Note: Healthcare 4.0 networks may monitor ailments in real time using shared learning and blockchain technologies. Author: Pradeepa, K.; Sottarov, A.; Deogaonkar, A.; Avasthi, V.; Rakhimov, R. R.; Singhal, A.
Title: Federated learning for secure and private data analysis in decentralized networks
Publication Title: 2025 Modern Electronics Devices and Intelligent Communication Systems (MEDCOM)
Abstract Note: Federated learning (FL), which allows collaborative machine learning without requiring the centralisation of sensitive data, has become a game-changing concept for private and safe data analysis in decentralised networks. FL enables edge devices or local nodes, such as smartphones, IoT devices, or healthcare facilities, to learn shared models remotely and send only model changes to a central server, in contrast to traditional methods that call for raw data aggregation. This framework lowers communication overhead, mitigates regulatory problems, and greatly improves data privacy and security. FL provides a workable and scalable way to create superior machine learning models in decentralised networks, where data is naturally dispersed and frequently subject to stringent privacy laws. Nevertheless, there are still issues to be resolved, such as managing non-IID data, making sure that systems are resilient to hostile attacks, and preserving effective communication. To further improve FL's privacy-preserving capabilities, recent developments like homomorphic encryption, safe multiparty computation, and differential privacy are being incorporated. This study examines the fundamentals of federated learning, goes over important methods for improving its security and privacy, and talks about how it may be used in a variety of industries, including as healthcare, finance, and smart cities. FL is one of the most important steps to safe and ethical AI in decentralized environments because it allows the collaboration of intelligence and preserves data ownership.
Manual Tags: Federated learning; decentralized networks; private data analysis

Author: Janaki, K.; Vani, B. G.; R, K.; Khrais, I. M.; Jain, A.; Karthikeyan, G.
Title: Novel Strategies for Integrating Blockchain and Deep Learning: Foster Ethical, Secure, and Transparent Artificial Intelligence Systems
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICACT)
Abstract Note: Blockchain technology and deep learning are converging to offer new means of building AI systems that are powerful and efficient as well as ethical, secure, and transparent. The decentralized, immutable and tamper-proof characteristics of blockchain mitigate many of the challenges that exist in deep learning, including data privacy, trust, and accountability. Deep learning, on the other hand, provides us with robust computational techniques for identifying tight relationships within massive datasets, which elevates the predictive power of AI systems. To overcome the challenges in information security, privacy, transparency, and ethical decision-making in AI, this study proposes new techniques of synergy between blockchain and deep learning AI. Some of the critical aspects of this integration are the usage of blockchain to create a verifiable audit trail of the AI model training process, data provenance, and enabling secure energy-efficient sharing of data between distributed entities. In this comprehensive study, latest findings on new areas on the Confines of Blockchain & deep learning applied to AI systems are reviewed and discussed along with how the mutual complementing security aspects of each other can be providing the solutions to the risk/metrology challenges faced in AI. In addition, blockchain's consensus mechanisms, smart contracts, and decentralized frameworks are investigated as tools to improve the transparency and fairness of AI decision-making processes. It also explored the combination of blockchain with federated learning, which allows the decentralized and privacy-preserving training of AI models, while maintaining the integrity of the training data. This study shows how the combination of blockchain and deep learning appears successful in constructing more ethical and trustworthy AI systems after a comprehensive review of the literature concerning existing implementations and case studies. By integrating blockchain with deep learning, the research tries to augment security and data integrity, besides addressing bigger ethical issues like accountability for AI decision making and potential data monopolization issues. This study ends with a consideration of the possible challenges to this integration, such as scalability, energy consumption and regulatory implications, and also proposes avenues for future research to improve the integration of blockchain technology with the IoT.
Manual Tags: Security; Federated Learning; Smart Contracts; Decentralization; Trustworthy AI; Data Privacy; Transparency; Ethical AI; Data Provenance

Author: Malaka, S. J. M.; Hunitie, M. F. A.; Shyyab, M. A.; Yakhlef, M.
Title: Federated Learning for Decentralized Smart City Infrastructure
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Business Intelligence for Technology Innovation (ICBITI)
Abstract Note: The emergence of smart cities has led to an unprecedented rise in the generation of data from a variety of sources such as traffic systems, energy grids, healthcare services, and IoT devices. The major problems with the centralized systems used in traditional data processing frameworks include data privacy risks, network congestion, and high computational costs. The innovative paradigm of Federated Learning (FL) facilitates decentralized data processing by means of the collaborative training of many models across different nodes without the sharing of any raw data. In this case study, we examine how Federated Learning can be applied within decentralized smart city infrastructures, at the same time as demonstrating the potential for improved data privacy, resource optimization, and scalability. We identify the most important use cases, such as traffic management, energy optimization, and healthcare monitoring, that help us demonstrate secure and effective decision-making with the help of FL. Title: Privacy-preserving Techniques: A Review

This paper comprehensively reviews these techniques, comparing their strengths, limitations, and applications in various fields like healthcare and Internet of Things (IoT). Author: Sathish, C.; Haldankar, D. D.; P, D. P. R.; V, S.; L, S.
Title: A Quantum-Resilient Privacy-Preserving Framework for Secure Medical Data Management
Publication Title: 2025 Third International Conference on Networks, Multimedia and Information Technology (NMITCON)
Abstract Note: The digitization of healthcare has ushered in an era of personalized medicine but has also heightened the risks to patient data security and privacy. In this paper, we introduce a novel framework for secure medical data management Q-PRISM(Quantum-Resillient Privacy-preserving Integrated Secuirty Model),that combines quantum-resistant cryptographic techniques with adaptive privacy mechanisms tailored for clinical settings. Our system utilizes SHA3-256-based entropy sources to generate quantum-resistant keys and employs a hybrid encryption methodology that integrates post-quantum cryptography with RSA. Furthermore, we present a novel Dynamic Privacy Budgeting model that leverages differential privacy principles while preserving the clinical validity of sensitive medical metrics. To ensure practical applicability, our framework incorporates field-specific sensitivity parameters and adaptive noise addition. Through extensive analysis, we demonstrate that our approach not only enhances security against future quantum threats but also achieves a balance between data utility and privacy. This pioneering work represents a significant step forward in safeguarding healthcare data, setting a new standard for security and privacy in digital health ecosystems.

Author: Meenakshisundaram, N.; G, S.
Title: Interpreting Blockchain-Coordinated Federated Models for Cervical Cancer Risk Prediction using SHAP and LIME
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Communication Networks and Application (ICSCN)
Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) is ideal for delicate healthcare applications since it allows for cross-institutional collaborative model training without exposing raw patient data. Nevertheless, federated models frequently hinder clinical confidence and acceptance because to their opacity. This research presents a paradigm for blockchain-coordinated FL in cervical cancer risk prediction using explainable AI (XAI). The framework uses XGBoost and Logistic Regression in a privacy-preserving FL setting. To derive interpretable, case-specific explanations without disclosing raw data, it uses SHAP (SHapley Additive Explanations) and LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations). By identifying critical risk factors, such as age and the number of sexual partners, therapists can have a better understanding of the model's decisions. The suggested method guarantees confidentiality, transparency, and clinical application while achieving high predictive accuracy, according to the experimental results. The approach demonstrates how real-world healthcare systems can benefit from federated learning that is both secure and easy to understand.

Abstract Note: The rapid development of Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) has enabled widespread applications. However, data aggregation in AIoT faces several security and privacy challenges that compromise the security and reliability. To address these issues, this paper proposes DPDA, a Decentralized Identity (DID)-based privacy-preserving data aggregation scheme for AIoT. DPDA utilizes DID and Paillier-based cryptosystem to ensure authenticity with privacy protection. Author: Lou, X.; Chen, X.; Zhang, Y.; Xu, X.; Ge, W.; Zhang, H.

Abstract Note: Federated learning, as a privacy preserving distributed machine learning paradigm, enables geographically dispersed clients to collaboratively train a shared model without exchanging raw data. Abandoning the forced convergence to a single global model, EG-DAG allows clients to selectively adopt model updates from other nodes based on contribution quality metrics and conduct specialized training on their local data. Compared with traditional architectures, EG-DAG demonstrates significant advantages in handling Non-IID data, it mitigates performance losses caused by forced convergence and introduces a topologically inherent contribution evaluation mechanism that is fairer and more robust against strategic manipulation. Author: Alipanahloo, Z.; Duchesne, M.; Zhang, K.
Title: RzkFL: a Verifiable, Fast and Privacy-Preserving Framework for Federated Learning Inference Using Recursive Zero-Knowledge Proofs and on-Chain Verification
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain (Blockchain)
Abstract Note: RzkFL is an end-to-end, privacy-preserving machine-learning framework that fuses Federated Learning (FL) with recursive zero-knowledge proofs (ZKPs) to protect data, models, and users while unlocking verifiable inference. Models are trained entirely on local devices, so sensitive data never leave the premises. The resulting model can be monetized by offering verifiable predictions on a pay-per-use basis. During inference, each customer independently computes predictions using private data, making it essential to verify that these inference results are computed correctly and honestly. Unlike existing approaches that rely on heavy communication or centralized trust assumptions, RzkFL allows each customer to generate a cryptographic proof of correct local inference, which can be succinctly verified without revealing input data or model parameters either by the customer or a third party. The core innovation lies in the use of recursive ZKPs, enabling each customer to generate small, composable proofs for intermediate layers of neural network inference. These proofs are then recursively aggregated into a single succinct proof using the Nova proof folding scheme. Nova’s design eliminates the traditional sequential dependency of recursive proofs by enabling incrementally verifiable computation through a folding scheme. RzkFL supports on-chain verification via Ethereum smart contracts, allowing AI results to flow directly into financial workflows. A decentralized file storage system maintains the integrity and availability of the global model. We introduce specialized circuits for input, hidden, and output layers to optimize proof generation time and gas costs. The customer can generate proof for the entire inference computation or delegate the proof generation for the intermediate layers and the output layer to another party. The design suits privacy-preserving machine learning scenarios where customer devices are resource-constrained. Our results show that RzkFL can significantly reduce proof size and verification costs while maintaining privacy, integrity, and scalability in federated inference. This makes it a compelling approach for real-world decentralized AI systems requiring strong verifiability guarantees.

Abstract Note: Healthcare is becoming an increasingly data-driven field, relying on elements like electronic medical records, sensor-based measurements, and genetic data to influence diagnostics, treatment, operational decisions, and more. This paper studies the convergence of big data, cyber security and blockchain technology within the healthcare infrastructure by focusing on two major methodologies, homomorphic encryption for secure big data processing and blockchain-based smart contracts for decentralized access control. Homomorphic encryption allows to compute on encrypted patient data without decrypting to preserve privacy for predictive analytics and clinical research. At the same time, blockchain systems are used to control permissioned data access, as to prevent unauthorized updates and provide auditable records. The proposed solutions are evaluated for scalability, latency and interoperability using real healthcare datasets as well as simulated model. It has also been found that the fusion of cryptography with technologies such as distributed ledger has the potential to enhance trust, transparency, and resilience of digital healthcare solutions.
