Author: Duan, D.; Zheng, X.; Zheng, Y.; Mu, C.; Wang, R.; Yan, K.
Title: Exploiting Parasitic Dependency for Free-Rider Elimination in Blockchain-Based Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE International Performance, Computing, and Communications Conference (IPCCC)
Abstract Note: Blockchain-based Federated Learning (BFL) facilitates collaborative model training with guaranteed transparency and accountability across distributed participants. However, BFL encounters a critical security vulnerability: advanced free-riders can exploit the public on-chain model histories to synthesize fabricated gradients without performing actual local training, which is indistinguishable from legitimate contributions. Previous efforts to defense free-rider attack mostly focus on anomaly detection, but they struggle to detect some advanced free-riders. To address this fundamental challenge, we propose BFLGR (Blockchain-based Federated Learning with Gresham's Reversal), which is a novel framework integrating reverse auction mechanisms and a dynamic reputation system. BFLGR employs a dynamic selection algorithm that can eliminate advanced free-riders by exploiting their profit-seeking motives and parasitic dependency on honest participants' contributions. This framework ensures genuine contributions prevail over deceptive submissions, and achieves a paradigmatic shift in BFL security, transforming the transparency-exploitation vulnerability into a strategic advantage for detecting and eliminating malicious participants. Theoretical proofs and extensive experiments show that BFLGR performs well in advanced free-rider attack situation and outperforms our baselines.
Manual Tags: Federated learning; Blockchain; Game theory; Free-rider attack

Author: Khan, S. A.; Balusamy, S.; Saviour, M. P. A.; Bojjawar, S.; M, C. C.; Sofia, D. S.
Title: Integrating Blockchain Technology with Artificial Intelligence to Create Scalable, Reliable, and Open Decision Support Systems
Publication Title: 2025 Global Conference in Emerging Technology (GINOTECH)
Abstract Note: Blockchain Technology (BT) is a promising approach for building scalable & reliable open Decision Support Systems and Artificial Intelligence (AI) could be integrated with BT to present a better approach towards the same. Transparency, trust, data security, and scalability are traditionally regarded as the major deficiencies of DSS models which may impede their efficacy in critical decision-making environments. Seamlessly integrating blockchain with AI-powered DSS can help with data integrity, as well as prevent manipulation and inconsistencies while improving trust with many different stakeholders, because all transactions on a blockchain are transparent immutable, owing to blockchain's decentralized ledger system. The paper investigates a hybrid Blockchain-AI framework that can overcome the main drawbacks of existing DSS systems. This means that AI predictive analytics and machine learning models can match massive datasets for decision making, while blockchain guarantees the integrity, traceability, and decentralization of the data's inputs and outputs. Smart contracts: automate decision processes & ensure tamper-proof execution for defined set of rules & policies In addition, blockchain consensus mechanisms (e.g., Proof-of-Stake, Byzantine Fault Tolerance) can facilitate transparency and verifiability, thus improving conflict-avoiding distributed decision-making. To enable privacy-preserving collaboration between organizations, we introduce a new Decentralized AI Decision Support System (Dai-DSS) framework that integrates federated learning and a distributed ledger. It enables real-time data sharing while preserving data sovereignty, which helps organizations comply with regulatory standards such as GDRP and HIPAA. We are also looking at various optimization techniques such as off-chain scaling solutions (sidechains, Layer-2 protocols, etc.) that improve system efficiency while still keeping the system decentralized. Our research shows that by comparing with the traditional DSS models, the Blockchain-AI integration strengthens system resilience, improves the elimination of single point failure and facilitates open, trustless decision-making processes. Practical applications and the benefits of the proposed model are demonstrated through case studies in healthcare, finance, and supply chain management. Lastly, we address the challenges including computational overhead, interoperability and regulatory challenges, and suggest future research avenues on AI-augmented consensus algorithms and quantum-resistant cryptography. The research demonstrates the ability of Blockchain-AI synergy to revolutionize decision-making systems through decentralized, clean, and scalable operating frameworks across industries.
Manual Tags: Federated Learning; Smart Contracts; Decentralization; Data Integrity; Privacy-Preserving AI; Scalable AI; Decision Support Systems; Trustless Computing

Author: Singh, A.; Sharma, D.; Goyal, A. K.
Title: Secure and Transparent Medical Data Sharing with Hyperledger Fabric and Cloud-Based Decentralized Framework
Publication Title: 2025 Global Conference in Emerging Technology (GINOTECH)
Abstract Note: The speed of healthcare digitalization requires a protected along with efficient framework to handle Electronic Health Records (EHRs). Traditional systems often struggle with disorganization, lack of clarity, and data breaches. This model solves primary healthcare data management problems by providing a dependable secure system for EHR management that protects user privacy during data exchange and management of Electronic Health Records ensuring regulatory compliances such as GDPR and HIPAA. This study develops a blockchain- operated conceptual model with Hyperledger Fabric to build a decentralized environment that secures healthcare information management. The enterprise-level features of Hyperledger Fabric combined with its permitted network architecture make it a secure solution for medical provider data exchange. The implementation process starts by installing core infrastructure through Docker and Docker Compose on cloud platforms, including AWS Azure or GCP. The system uses ECC and ZKP with MFA and an IAM framework to ensure strong security by enabling secure key creation, data protection, and enhanced user authorization. The React.js frontend engages in secure backend processes that handle data management operations alongside protected transaction functions that enable effective state control and secure storage of information. The implementation of IPFS off-chain storage solution improves system scalability alongside performance outcomes. Stealth Array ensures functional performance, data protection, and regulatory compliance such as GDPR and HIPAA. This model addresses healthcare data management difficulties to provide an effective approach for enhancing secure EHR management and security. Research should focus on deploying the model on real-world healthcare scenarios and optimize the model for scalability.

Author: K, M.; S, A. D.; E, C.; Joann, J. D.; M, A.; J, E.
Title: Blockchain Enabled Federated Learning for Privacy Preserving Lung Cancer Risk Prediction
Publication Title: 2025 3rd International Conference on Inventive Computing and Informatics (ICICI)
Abstract Note: A new architecture for prediction of lung cancer risk using survey derived data by incorporating federated learning in combination with blockchain technology has been discussed. The proposed approach allows multiple healthcare institutions to collaboratively train machine learning models without the need to share sensitive patient data, which is a significant advancement in privacy and regulatory compliance. The dataset was segmented across three hypothetical hospitals, consisting of 309 records and 16 attributes. A local Random Forest classifier was created at each university, and models with accuracy above 85% were documented in a simulated blockchain utilizing the SHA-256 hashing algorithm. This ensures an immutable, verifiable provenance of model contributions. This architecture illustrates decentralization learning with high accuracy while maintaining user data privacy and trust in federated nodes. The results indicated a great opportunity for practical applications, especially in public health systems and joint clinical studies.

Author: M, C. D.; R, S. M.; Kathavate, S.; S, A.

The study also examines new trends which have been occasioned by artificial intelligence in content moderation and the legal development aspect of it. As much as this survey focuses on current practices and asks questions in support of proactive measures, it seeks to enlighten policy makers on the best practices to engage in and create awareness to positive handling of user data in OSNs for the safety of users, as well as promoting ethical usage of the social networking systems.

Author: E, S.; C, R.; Faisal, M.; S, P.; S, S.; Palanivel, V.
Title: Privacy-Preserving Patient Consent Management Using Federated Learning and Cloud Technology in Digital Health
Publication Title: 2025 11th International Conference on Communication and Signal Processing (ICCSP)
Abstract Note: Protecting patients' personal information while keeping track of their permission is a major challenge in the constantly evolving world of digital health. This paper provides a new approach to patient consent management that uses cloud computing and federated learning (FL) to ensure patient privacy. Training machine learning models on decentralized data is made feasible by FL, which keeps patient information localized and safe. Scalability and reliable data storage are made possible using cloud technologies. To implement this technique, there is a safe system for managing permission, making it easy for patients to approve or reject using their health records. The system uses advanced cryptographic methods and decentralized IDs to safeguard confidentiality and integrity. Healthcare providers may work together to enhance patient care models using FL without gaining direct access to patient data, allowing them to comply with data protection rules like GDPR and HIPAA. This research uses the Patient Consent Management (PCM) database from the BHITS GitHub repository to establish a privacy-preserving FL model for safe and decentralised healthcare data analysis. The proposed methodology achieved a 98.7% accuracy in permission validation, reduced data exposure by 85%, and enhanced processing efficiency by 60%, enabling safe and scalable administration of patient consent in digital health.

Author: Sherin, A.; Reena, K.; Shebin, A.; Karthikeyan, B.
Title: AI-Enhanced Intrusion Detection with Blockchain for Securing Cyber-Physical Systems
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent Innovations in Engineering and Technology (ICIIET)
Abstract Note: Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) are essential to critical infrastructures such as smart grids, h ealth care, autonomous vehicles, and industrial automation. Their integration of computational and physical processes delivers efficiency but also introduces significant cybersecurity risks. Traditional intrusion detection systems (IDS) often lack scalability, adaptability, and robustness against advanced cyberattacks. This work proposes a hybrid framework combining an AI-driven Intrusion Detection System (AI-IDS) with blockchain technology. The AI-IDS uses deep learning for anomaly detection, enhanced with graph-based learning to capture complex CPS interactions and federated learning for distributed, privacy-preserving defense. Blockchain ensures data integrity, access control, and decentralized trust through smart contracts and consensus mechanisms.Evaluation on CPS datasets shows improved detection accuracy, reduced false alarms, and resilience against adversarial threats. By merging AI adaptability with blockchain trust guarantees, the approach provides a scalable, transparent, and real-time defense mechanism, strengthening CPS security in safety-critical applications.

Author: N, S.; Kumaresan, M.; Kumar, A. S.
Title: A Comprehensive Review of Blockchain-Enabled Federated Learning and Hybrid Deep Learning Models for Cybersecurity Threat Detection
Publication Title: 2025 7th International Conference on Innovative Data Communication Technologies and Application (ICIDCA)
Abstract Note: The amount of cyber threats in a distributed environment that is dynamically growing cannot be addressed anymore through mere detection and secure learning practices. Repeat neural networks that run via attention are presented since they are ideal at classifying threats due to their ability to diminish dimensions and federated models are provided that are trained to decrease reconstruction hyperparameters to accomplish triumph in attack detection. Author: Zhao, D.; Tian, C.; Ju, Z.; Rong, Y.; He, X.; Yang, W.
Title: A Blockchain-Enabled AIoT Framework for Secure Metaverse in Wireless Communication Networks
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 24th International Conference on Trust, Security and Privacy in Computing and Communications (TrustCom)
Abstract Note: The wireless communication network, comprising billions of cloud, edge, and end devices, enables emerging applications such as the metaverse—an immersive virtual environment where experiences and user interactions converge. However, user interactions in the metaverse generate substantial amounts of private data (e.g., identity, location), raising significant privacy concerns despite their utility in training machine learning models. Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) offers solutions to these challenges, with Federated Learning (FL) serving as a decentralized framework that enables collaborative model training without exposing local data. Nevertheless, deploying FL in large-scale environments like the metaverse increases vulnerability to malicious attacks. To address this issue, we propose a blockchain-based FL architecture that enhances trust and security. The architecture integrates a multi-task FL strategy with blockchain sharding to boost system throughput and reduce resource consumption. By partitioning the blockchain into smaller shards, we lower computational demands and enable concurrent training of multiple models, improving efficiency. We also design a shard creation algorithm based on bipartite matching and a bandwidth scheduling mechanism that prioritizes reliable devices with informative data. Experimental results show that our architecture outperforms existing baselines across multiple evaluation metrics.

Author: Rghioui, A.; Cherrabi, M.
Title: Enhancing Security and Anomaly Detection in IoMT Systems Using Autoencoders and Blockchain
Publication Title: 2025 12th International Conference on Wireless Networks and Mobile Communications (WINCOM)
Abstract Note: Health care is undergoing transformation with the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) interconnecting physiological sensors to keep track of patients around the clock. In decentralized, resource-challenged environments, maintaining data security, traceability and reliability is an ongoing effort. In this paper we put forward a hybrid architecture that combines neural autoencoders for anomaly detection and blockchain technology to ensure data integrity and make records auditable. This hybrid architecture ensures a unique combination of trust and reliability, rarely achieved in prior work. In a simulated experiment using the physiological features of heart rate, temperature, signal strength and battery level, our model achieves F1-Score 0.97 and AUC-ROC 0.999. With simulated data fallback under network degradation, robustness is maintained. This approach lays the groundwork for secure, transparent Internet of Medical Things. Unlike previous IDS approaches that mostly focus on networklevel anomalies, our contribution specifically targets device-level physiological signals, combined with blockchain-based anomaly logging.

Author: Arivalagan, D. K.; Srinivasan, S.

Author: Appavu, N.
Title: Examining Federated Learning Architecture's Capability to Protect Data Privacy During the Training of Collaborative Healthcare Models
Publication Title: 2025 9th International Conference on Inventive Systems and Control (ICISC)
Abstract Note: Working with artificial intelligence (AI) in the healthcare industry yields revolutionary results, especially when machine learning techniques are used to teamwork. Because patient data is sensitive and subject to stringent rules, central data aggregation is difficult. Federated Learning is a computer technique that allows for the decentralised deployment of artificial intelligence by training models at the source device while preserving the original data locally. By analysing healthcare collaborative systems that comprise EHR data, diagnostic imaging data, and wearable health data, researchers assess a variety of FL designs in terms of their ability to maintain privacy or their learning performance. Horizontal FL, Vertical FL, and Hybrid FL are compared based on their communication requirements, training efficiency, time to convergence, and vulnerability to data exposure. Using device simulations on a Raspberry Pi 4 and an NVIDIA Jetson Nano operating under real-world implementation constraints, the study team conducted experimental assessments. To assess real-world applications, the study uses privacy-protected methods such safe aggregation, homomorphic encryption, and differential privacy inside the FL structure. The optimal balance between superior performance as well as privacy protection in simulation operation is achieved by hybrid FL technology that combines adaptive compression with safe aggregation approaches. Our research offers useful insights into how Federalised Learning facilitates collaborative artificial brains that safeguard the privacy of medical data. By creating operational guidelines for healthcare professionals and AI developers who wish to establish large privacy-protecting smart systems, research that relies on real-world emulation acts as the study's basic novelty. In addition to explanatory model solutions for clinical deployment dependability, developers should concentrate on three primary future directions: using blockchain to enable reporting and customising models on device hardware.

Author: Leena, V. P.; Sudhir, K.; Harish, B.; Gautham, R.; Kishore, R.; Karthick, R.
Title: A Hybrid MySQL–Blockchain Architecture for Decentralized Data Integrity and Secure Healthcare Information Systems
Publication Title: 2025 9th International Conference on I-SMAC (IoT in Social, Mobile, Analytics and Cloud) (I-SMAC)
Abstract Note: The handling of healthcare data remains beset by long-standing problems such as data tampering, security breaches, and inefficient centralized storage. These are the problems tackled by the MBHA through offering a hybrid solution that MySQL's efficient handling of data with blockchain technology's decentralized and tamper-proof nature. The system is designed to accommodate real-time performance, secure access to data, and compliance. Empirical testing demonstrates strong performance: average user registration time is 1.54 seconds, login is 841 milliseconds, and database operations are below 1 millisecond. Furthermore, JWT tokens for authentication are provided in below 50 milliseconds. The goal is to create a secure, scalable, and regulation-compliant system that is friendly to healthcare data collaboration. The novelty is that blockchain is integrated with MySQL, offering decentralized data integrity without compromising fast and structured data handling abilities, ensuring both transparency and operational efficiency.

Author: Nelufule, N.

Author: Chittem, M. B.; Ghanta, S.; Cherukuri, V. A.; Lingincni, P. S.; Jalluri, R.; Pradhan, A. K.
Title: Blockchain Verified Federated Learning for Brain Tumour Classification using Colorized MRI Scans
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 4th International Conference on Data, Decision and Systems (ICDDS)
Abstract Note: Brain tumor classification via MRI scans poses challenges related to privacy, data decentralization, and model transparency. This work proposes a secure, decentralized pipeline combining Federated Learning (FL) with blockchain-based ver-ification for multi-class tumor detection. Using ResNet-SO with transfer learning, the model distinguishes glioma, meningioma, and pituitary tumors from colorized MRI images. Grayscale scans are enhanced using histogram equalization and edge sharpening to align with RGB-pretrained networks. Training is distributed across simulated hospital nodes via the Flower FL framework, leveraging Federated Batch Normalization (FedBN) to address non-IID data. A smart contract on Ethereum's Sepolia testnet records model hashes, accuracy, and timestamps for auditability. The approach achieves 97.98 % global accuracy, outperforming CNN baselines. This system offers a scalable, transparent, and privacy-preserving solution for AI-driven med-ical imaging.

Author: Negi, G.; Kumar, A.; Khan, S.; Gupta, S.; Ambikapathy, A.; Garg, S.

Publication Title: 2025 6th International Conference on Inventive Research in Computing Applications (ICIRCA)

This way of learning keeps user data private because artificial intelligence training happens on different devices instead of all together. In addition, the software relies on strong blockchain authentication and MQTT protocols that use quantum technology to guarantee trusted identity and secure communications as online dangers develop. Author: Shen, M.; Xiong, X.; Hu, D.; Xi, X.; Cao, W.; Wang, X.
Title: Privacy Preservation and Fair Payment Method Based on Blockchain and Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cloud Computing Technology and Science (CloudCom)
Abstract Note: Federated learning (FL) in Internet of Things (IoT) environments is impeded by model leakage, prohibitive computational overhead, and the lack of fair incentive mechanisms. To overcome these challenges,this paper proposes the PrivacyPreserving and Fair Payment framework based on Blockchain and Federated Learning (PPFP-BFL), a holistic architecture that synergistically integrates blockchain with federated learning. The framework's privacy is anchored by a novel Non-Interactive Functional Encryption (NIFE) scheme enhanced with SIMD technology, which secures model parameters with provable security and significantly reduced overhead. Concurrently, a novel incentive mechanism is established, transforming the blockchain from a passive ledger into an active arbitrator for fair exchange through automated, performance-based smart contracts. The framework's superiority and viability are validated by formal analysis and extensive experiments, which demonstrate a significant reduction in overhead against cryptographic-based solutions without sacrificing model accuracy.

Author: Alzahrani, A. I. A.
Title: Quantum-Enhanced Federated Learning With Zerotrust Blockchain for Secure 6G IoT Anomaly Detection
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Communication Networks (CICN)
Abstract Note: The rapid expansion of 6G-enabled Internet of Things (IoT) networks enables ultra-reliable, low-latency communication and massive device connectivity but simultaneously increases exposure to cyberattacks. Traditional centralized anomaly-detection schemes face limitations in latency, privacy, and computational cost. To address these challenges, this study proposes a Quantum-Enhanced Federated Learning (QEFL) framework integrated with a Zero-Trust Blockchain (ZTB) architecture for secure and lightweight anomaly detection. A simulated 6 G -IoT testbed comprising thirty heterogeneous devices was used to evaluate scalability and performance under diverse traffic classes. Each device trained a compact hybrid CNN-LSTM model using quantum-enhanced federated averaging, while a Proof-of-Authority (PoA) blockchain enforced secure aggregation and zero-trust validation. Baseline evaluation with the FedAvg algorithm achieved 92.7 % accuracy with low latency \(\textbackslash{}sim 0.8 \textbackslash{}mathrm{s}\ per round) but remained vulnerable to trust and privacy violations. The proposed QEFL-ZTB framework demonstrated improved auditability, privacy preservation, and communication efficiency, though quantum-simulation noise introduced convergence instability. These findings highlight the feasibility of integrating quantum-assisted optimization with zero-trust blockchain to establish privacy-preserving, verifiable anomaly detection for 6G-enabled IoT networks.

Author: Ar-Reyouchi, D.; Benali, H.; Jihane, B.; Ghoumid, K.; Ar-Reyouchi, E. M.
Title: Secure-by-Design IoMT Networks: A Quantum-Blockchain and AI Framework for 6G Healthcare
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Communication, Computing, Networking, and Control in Cyber-Physical Systems (CCNCPS)
Abstract Note: This paper proposes the Quantum-Blockchain Secured Framework (QBSF), a novel secure-by-design architecture for the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) in next-generation 6G healthcare systems. QBSF integrates Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) for post-quantum secure communication, blockchain technology for decentralized trust management and tamper-proof auditing, and Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) for real-time anomaly detection and adaptive security control. A federated artificial intelligence (AI) approach ensures privacy-preserving intelligence across distributed edge medical devices. Unlike existing approaches that address these components in isolation, QBSF provides an integrated, end-to-end security solution tailored to the dynamic and resource-constrained nature of medical cyber-physical systems (CPS). Simulation results demonstrate that QBSF significantly outperforms traditional 5 G-based healthcare security architectures, achieving a 137.5% improvement in overall security score, a 100% increase in blockchain trust index, and an 80% reduction in attack-related error rate. These findings underscore the potential of QBSF to support secure, scalable, and quantum-resilient medical infrastructures powered by AI.

Author: Tiwari, A.; Sinha, S.; Sah, A. K.; Mishra, R.; Narwaria, M.
Title: A Privacy-Centric Healthcare System: Integrating Blockchain, AI, and Federated Learning Design, Applications, and Future Directions
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 7th International Conference on Computing, Communication and Automation (ICCCA)
Abstract Note: The healthcare industry is massively and rapidly going digital, because the doctors are using dashboards despite of clipboards and video calls are replacing in-person visits. In fact this shift is exciting, this also raises complex questions about data ownership and interoperability. Our paper proposes a solution that combines Blockchain and AI to address these concerns. We propose lessons from crypto wallets and privacy-first machine learning to create a simple, trustworthy system. Our idea is to give each medical record a tamper-proof home on the blockchain, wrap it in smart contracts that dictate access rules, and use AI to handle the heavy computational lifting needed for security and speed. Our main aim is to build a system that people trust because they can clearly see where their information is stored and who has accessed it.

Author: Bououdina, S.
Title: Trustworthy Privacy-Preserving Federated Large Language Models for the Internet of Medical Things
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 36th International Symposium on Personal, Indoor and Mobile Radio Communications (PIMRC)
Abstract Note: The proliferation of Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) devices has led to an unprecedented volume of sensitive health data generated at the edge. Leveraging this data for intelligent healthcare solutions necessitates models that are both powerful and privacy-conscious. This paper introduces a federated learning framework employing Large Language Models (LLMs) tailored for IoMT environments. By decentralizing training across edge devices, our approach ensures data privacy while harnessing the contextual understanding capabilities of LLMs. We address challenges unique to IoMT, including heterogeneous data distributions, limited computational resources, and stringent latency requirements. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that our federated LLM approach achieves competitive performance compared to centralized models, with significant improvements in data privacy and communication efficiency. This work underscores the potential of integrating federated LLMs into IoMT ecosystems, paving the way for advanced, privacy-preserving healthcare applications at the edge.

Author: Wei, S.; Tong, Y.; Zhou, Z.; He, T.; Xu, Y.
Title: Efficient Data Valuation Approximation in Federated Learning: A Sampling-Based Approach
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 41st International Conference on Data Engineering (ICDE)
Abstract Note: Federated learning (FL) has emerged as a prominent distributed learning paradigm to utilize datasets across multiple data providers. In FL, cross-silo data providers often hesitate to share their high-quality dataset unless their data value can be fairly assessed. Shapley value (SV) has been advocated as the standard metric for data valuation in FL due to its desirable properties. However, the computational overhead of SV is prohibitive in practice, as it inherently requires training and evaluating an FL model across an exponential number of dataset combinations. Furthermore, existing solutions fail to achieve high accuracy and efficiency, making practical use of SV still out of reach, because they ignore choosing suitable computation scheme for approximation framework and overlook the property of utility function in FL. We first propose a unified stratified-sampling framework for two widely-used schemes. Then, we analyze and choose the more promising scheme under the FL linear regression assumption. After that, we identify a phenomenon termed key combinations, where only limited dataset combinations have a high-impact on final data value. Building on these insights, we propose a practical approximation algorithm, IPSS, which strategically selects high-impact dataset combinations rather than evaluating all possible combinations, thus substantially reducing time cost with minor approximation error. Furthermore, we conduct extensive evaluations on the FL benchmark datasets to demonstrate that our proposed algorithm outperforms a series of representative baselines in terms of efficiency and effectiveness.
Manual Tags: federated learning; shapley value; data valuation

Author: Turazza, F.; Pietri, M.; Picone, M.; Mamei, M.
Title: FedBGS: A Blockchain Approach to Segment Gossip Learning in Decentralized Systems
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 45th International Conference on Distributed Computing Systems Workshops (ICDCSW)
Abstract Note: Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning (PPFL) is a Decentralized machine learning paradigm that enables multiple participants to collaboratively train a global model without sharing their data with the integration of cryptographic and privacy-based techniques to enhance the security of the global system. This privacy-oriented approach makes PPFL a highly suitable solution for training shared models in sectors where data privacy is a critical concern. In traditional FL, local models are trained on edge devices, and only model updates are shared with a central server, which aggregates them to improve the global model. However, despite the presence of the aforementioned privacy techniques, in the classical Federated structure, the issue of the server as a single-point-of-failure remains, leading to limitations both in terms of security and scalability. This paper introduces FedBGS, a fully Decentralized Blockchain-based framework that leverages Segmented Gossip Learning through Federated Analytics. The proposed system aims to optimize blockchain usage while providing comprehensive protection against all types of attacks, ensuring both privacy, security and non-IID data handling in Federated environments.

Author: Bouchra, B.; Trichni, S.; Omary, F.
Title: Blockchain Meets Federated Learning: A Comprehensive Survey on Smart Contract-driven Optimization for Aggregation, Security, and Scalability
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 8th Congress on Information Science and Technology (CiSt)
Abstract Note: Blockchain enabled Federated Learning systems seek to unite the privacy guarantees of Federated Learning with the decentralized trust and auditability of blockchain networks. Although Federated Learning enables collaborative model training without sharing raw data, it remains exposed to malicious participants and lacks verifiable global coordination. The immutable ledger and consensus mechanisms of blockchain address these gaps while requiring programmable logic to orchestrate complex Federated Learning operations. In this comprehensive survey we demonstrate how smart contracts optimize blockchain enabled Federated Learning architectures by ensuring secure and transparent model aggregation, detecting and excluding malicious updates in real time, managing participant reputation dynamically, and distributing incentives to maintain honest participation. We present a taxonomy of smart contract designs and evaluate their impact on security, scalability, and gas cost tradeoffs. We compare practical implementations across diverse application domains. Finally, we highlight open challenges including gas cost optimization, privacy-preserving computation and cross silo interoperability and outline future directions for robust, scalable and autonomous blockchain enabled Federated Learning systems in trustless environments.

Author: Meenakshisundaram, N.; G, S.

Publication Title: 2025 10th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
Abstract Note: This study presented a verified federated edge AI architecture that is supported by blockchain technology. The framework successfully addresses federated learning (FL) issues like malicious updates, free-rider participation, and auditability gaps by incorporating zero-knowledge proofs (ZKPs) for secure model update verification, a lightweight blockchain consensus for efficient transaction recording, and an adaptive incentive mechanism to reward verified contributions. Author: Takkalapally, P.; Reddy, J. K.; Syed, W. Khadri; Jiwani, N.; Logeshwaran, J.

Abstract Note: To demonstrate that fraud detection needs fast processing of massive transactional data and several restrictions on customer privacy and regulatory compliance for banking systems. Federated Learning (FL) can provide a decentralized solution for collaborative model training across multiple banks without exposing their raw data. In this setting, while models are trained locally on data from each bank, only AGGREGATED updates (as opposed to raw updates) are shared, and no actual data is exposed. In this paper, we investigate the use of FL for cross-bank fraud detection and study some significant challenges like non-IID data, communication efficiency, and adversarial robustness. This work presents a privacy-secured FL framework consisting of DP and encryption as defenses against information leakage. Further, we assess performance with real-world banking transaction databases compared to the central approach, which can track the accuracy, scalability, and privacy of preservation. Our results show that FL is comparable in accuracy to centralization concerning fraud detection and maintains a strong privacy guarantee, enabling cross-bank collaboration using this solution. The study shows FL could be used to improve financial security but still ensure regulatory compliance, making FL technologies open to being widely used in banking.

Author: Rammoo, H. M.; Hamdi, M. Ahmed; Abdalwahid, R. S.; Hassan, R. Ali; Kadhum, M. M.; Alsharfa, R. Majid
Title: Energy Grid Trading Security-based Regulatory Policies Across Smart Supply Chains
Publication Title: 2025 3rd International Conference on Cyber Resilience (ICCR)
Abstract Note: The growing complexity of energy grid trading within smart supply chains necessitates robust security and regulatory compliance frameworks. Existing methods often suffer from centralized vulnerabilities, lack of data privacy, and limited adaptability to regulatory changes, which undermine the integrity and efficiency of energy trading systems. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Blockchain-Enabled Federated Learning (BEFL) framework that integrates decentralized machine learning with secure, immutable blockchain technologies. BEFL ensures data privacy by allowing local model training while leveraging blockchain to maintain tamper-proof, auditable energy trading records aligned with regulatory policies. This framework supports secure peer-to-peer (P2P) energy transactions, enabling dynamic pricing and decentralized decision-making while maintaining data integrity and confidentiality. The proposed method is implemented within a smart grid scenario involving distributed energy producers and consumers, where real-time compliance checks and secure trading are performed. Results demonstrate enhanced security, improved trading transparency, regulatory alignment, and reduced risks of data leakage compared to conventional systems. The proposed method gradually enhances the data privacy preservation rate by 98.43%, the transparency index by 97.64%, the regulatory compliance accuracy by 96.53%, and the security breach detection rate by 96.52%.

Author: Gao, W.; Zhan, Y.; Wang, X.
Title: SEBFL: A Secure and Efficient Blockchain-Assisted Federated Learning Framework
Publication Title: 2025 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Internet of Things and Cloud Computing Technology (AIoTC)
Abstract Note: The decentralized blockchain-assisted Federated Learning (BFL) scheme reduces excessive reliance on the FL central server, thereby lower the risks when the server is attacked, broken or induced to take malicious actions. However, it rarely considers the defense against malicious clients and the inefficiency problem of the consensus mechanism caused by multiple crossvalidations of models. To address these issues, this paper proposes a secure and efficient BFL framework (SEBFL). Firstly, we design a malicious client identification method in which a clean dataset is introduced as a trusted benchmark to evaluate the credibility of clients and reduce the impact of malicious clients. Secondly, we adopt the Verifiable Random Function (VRF) to establish an efficient committee election mechanism where a small number of trusted clients are selected to form a committee, and the consensus process performs restrictedly within the committee to enhance consensus efficiency. Moreover, since the selection process of committee nodes is unpredictable yet easily verifiable, it is impossible for attackers to corrupt them in advance. Finally, experiments based on real datasets demonstrate the robustness and effectiveness of the proposed framework.

Author: Sajiv, G.; Meenakshisundaram, N.

In this study, we propose a novel Federated Learning-Generative Adversarial Network (FL-GAN) framework, augmented with blockchain technology and 6 G edge connectivity, to address these pressing concerns. The proposed framework enables multiple medical edge devices to collaboratively train AI models without sharing raw patient data, thereby preserving privacy. Blockchain ensures auditability and traceability of federated updates, while GANs are employed to generate synthetic medical data to further reduce dependency on sensitive real-world datasets. We simulate the framework using genomic and medical imaging datasets partitioned across multiple nodes and evaluate its performance in terms of accuracy, privacy preservation, latency, and model interpretability. Abstract Note: With the rapid expansion of online social networks (OSNs), photo sharing has become increasingly prevalent, raising significant privacy and security concern. The method creates a distributed training simulation that allows GNN models operating on client devices to analyze local data and share collective knowledge independently from the original data. Author: Thenmozhi, P.; Ramathilagam, A.
Title: Privacy-Preserving Multimodal Diagnostic Framework for VSH-IoT Using Differential Privacy and LSTM-Gated GAN
Publication Title: 2025 1st International Conference on Advancement in Futuristic Technologies (ICAFT)
Abstract Note: The Visual Sensor Healthcare Internet of Things (VSH-IoT) enables intelligent, real-time medical analytics by integrating AI-driven image processing with distributed sensor networks. To protect sensitive clinical information, a Differential Privacy Noise Injection Model is applied, ensuring that individual patient details remain unidentifiable while retaining analytical value. Author: Ali, S. M.; Hadi, R. M.; Alansari, A.; Siddiqi, A.; Nashwan, O.; Alqudah, O. M.
Title: Anomaly Detection in Smart Grid Networks Using Federated Learning

Author: Siyal, F.; Alkhabbas, F.; Alawadi, S.; Guzzo, A.; Fortino, G.
Title: Towards a Blockchain-Based Federated Learning Framework for Sustainable Supply Chain
Publication Title: 2025 3rd International Conference on Federated Learning Technologies and Applications (FLTA)
Abstract Note: Federated learning (FL) is a distributed machine learning paradigm that enables multiple participants to collaboratively train a model without sharing raw data to preserve privacy. However, traditional FL frameworks remain vulnerable to integrity and accountability issues at both the global and local levels. Blockchain (BC), known for its decentralization, transparency, immutability, and cryptographic security, has been explored to enhance trust in FL. Yet, prior BC-integrated FL approaches often suffer from limitations such as resource-heavy consensus algorithms, on-chain storage of model weights, and unenforced incentive schemes in semi-decentralized settings. In this work, we propose a lightweight decentralized FL framework for supply chains. Our design features role-based governance, quorum-based model approval, stake-and-slash incentives, and off-chain model storage via the InterPlanetary File System (IPFS) to minimize gas costs. Author: Shambhavi, P.; V.Jyothi; Anusha, M.; K.A.Jyotsna; S.Kanakaprabha; Babu, G. C.

This paper introduces a 6G enabled Federated Learning (FL) model to large-scale smart agriculture applications to overcome these limits. This framework is based on the ultra-low latency, massive connectivity, and high reliability features of 6G networks that allow solving one of the major challenges of machine learning: the ability of distributed agricultural apparatus, including IoT sensors, drones, and autonomous machinery, to collaboratively learn machine learning without exchanging raw data. This methodology preserves the privacy of data, leads to reduced communications overhead, and real-time decision-making capabilities in precision agriculture. Author: Lakshmanan, M.; Londhe, G.; R, S.; Naik, M. N.; Dhanraj, J. Arockia; Jain, N.; Hole, S. R.
Title: Edge-Intelligent Blockchain Framework for Federated Privacy-Preserving Medical Diagnostics
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Recent Trends in Computing and Smart Mobility (RCSM)
Abstract Note: Rapid advancements in technology have had a significant impact on the world's health care system. Among these, the innovative devices of the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) and the first ever artificially intelligent diagnostic systems have made it easier to keep up with the healthcare industry, with data privacy, latency, and trust remaining as the most critical challenges. Then, once the user’s data has been protected and only the AI model has been passed on, smart contracts on the blockchain will validate the encrypted model updates kept on the immutably secured ledger. The framework will come up with a POA consensus mechanism optimized by energy consumption (A PBFT) that can agree on and execute messages in a timely, reliable, and fault-free way even at a fraction of the cost compared to other systems that are not energy-optimized. The final application outcome of the investigation using the MIMIC III and PhysioNet databases was that the edge-accelerated EIBF approach is at the 96.4% classification accuracy level and is able to offer a more reliable and faster model convergence time by 35% as well as a 40% renewable energy consumption than the conventional FL systems. Author: Zhang, Y.; Chen, X.; Cai, W.; Zhang, H.
Title: A Survey of Privacy Preservation Techniques for Large Language Models
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 11th International Conference on Edge Computing and Scalable Cloud (EdgeCom)
Abstract Note: Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable success across a wide range of applications, but their data-driven nature introduces significant privacy risks throughout the model lifecycle. This survey provides a comprehensive overview of privacy preservation techniques for LLMs, categorized by the stage at which they are applied: data preprocessing, model training, inference, deployment, and post-deployment. We examine classical and deep learning-based anonymization methods, training-time differential privacy including parameterefficient fine-tuning, inference-stage safeguards such as DP incontext learning and local-DP interfaces, as well as federated learning, machine unlearning, and cryptographic inference. For each technique, we analyze its mechanisms, privacy-utility tradeoffs, and deployment feasibility. We also discuss open challenges and future directions in corpus hygiene, differential privacy at scale, unlearning, and system-level integration. This survey aims to provide a structured foundation for developing trustworthy and privacy-preserving LLM systems.

Author: V, V. L.; Ramaswamy, Y.; Gudala, L.; MohamadAbbas, H.; Sushama, C.
Title: Privacy-Preserving Data Analysis using Decentralized Blockchain-Based Authentication with Zero-Knowledge Cloud Auditing
Publication Title: 2025 3rd International Conference on Data Science and Information System (ICDSIS)
Abstract Note: Nowadays, the increasing adoption of cloud computing has raised concerns about data privacy and security. However, the existing Homomorphic Encryption (HE) model has limited scalability which led to time-consuming in large-scale cloud computing environments. Hence, this research proposes Decentralized Blockchain-based Authentication with Zero-Knowledge Cloud Auditing (DBA-ZKCA) to improve data security and integrity in cloud computing environments. The proposed DBA-ZKCA consists of five key phases to ensure the privacy, authentication and secure data communication. The first phase initialization sets up cryptographic keys and identity verification parameters before cloud operations starts. These operations are executed by Cloud Service Providers (CSP) and Revocation Admin (RA) respectively. Then, cloud consumer registration phase allows only authorized users to access the cloud services. After that, authentication based on anonymous access phase utilizes DBA to store immutable authentication records. Next, the secure cloud communications phase with ZKCA where the Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKP) allow cloud users to verity data integrity without revealing actual data. Finally, revocation phase utilizes RA to revoke access for unauthorized users and updates authentication records for preventing future access. From the results, the proposed DBAZKCA achieved better results when compared to existing Federated Learning and Cryptography (FLC) in terms of accuracy (98.9%) respectively.

This work seeks to provide a path for academics and practitioners by synthesizing recent accomplishments and pinpointing existing problems in the development of safe, efficient, and ethical healthcare data management systems. The amalgamation of cloud storage with AI-driven analytics has significant promise to transform healthcare; yet, it necessitates a multidisciplinary strategy to mitigate related risks and establish trustworthiness within the digital health ecosystem.

Author: R, V.; Sharhrah, S.; Rajeswari, P.; K, J. P.; V, R. K.
Title: Artificital Intelligence-Assisted Blockchain-Software Defined Cloud-Based Secure Data Exchange in Industrial IoT Frameworks
Publication Title: 2025 3rd International Conference on Data Science and Network Security (ICDSNS)
Abstract Note: The rapid evolution of Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) systems has introduced complex challenges related to data security, trust management, and reliable cloud integration. However, the existing Distributed Block Software Defined Cloud (DistB-SDCloud) with centralized architectures and static rule-based security models are inadequate for the dynamic, large-scale, and heterogeneous environments of Industry 4.0. To address these limitations, this paper proposes an Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Blockchain-SDCloud (AI-BSDCloud) Framework that employs SDN, Federated AI, and Blockchain technologies to provide a secure, scalable, and intelligent IIoT-cloud infrastructure. The proposed framework is a multi-layered framework where SDN is used for programmable flow control and isolation of devices. Next, a BlockChain is used to guarantee decentralization and maintain immutable transaction history, and AI assistive trust model to dynamically learn device behaviors via federated learning with anomaly detection. Additionally, smart contracts are used to direct access control and check logging capabilities. The AI-enabled trust model includes attack detection transforming the threat detection from static to dynamic. The attack detection engine is based on deep-learning techniques that applies to detect and mitigate attacks while the IIoT system is running. The framework is validated in the IIoT environment simulation with integration of OpenFlow, Ethereum Proof-of-Authority (PoA) blockchain, and cloud based RESTful APIs. Experimental results show that AI-BSDCloud provided the throughput (19.5 KB/s) based on number of nodes for securing industrial data exchange to improve operational resiliency.

Author: Xia, Y.; Yin, R.; Feng, J.; Shang, B.; Lei, J.; Pei, Q.
Title: An Efficient Diffusion Model-Based Federated Learning with Non-IID Data for 6G Networks
Publication Title: IEEE INFOCOM 2025 - IEEE Conference on Computer Communications Workshops (INFOCOM WKSHPS)
Abstract Note: Non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data significantly impact the performance of federated learning (FL) for 6G networks. Existing external solutions cannot address the underlying distribution imbalances or data scarcity. In this paper, we propose, for the first time, a novel FL training framework based on diffusion models (DMs). Within this framework, the DM and FL models are trained simultaneously. The DM training process is specifically designed to adapt to the non-IID characteristics of the data distribution in FL, effectively achieving a more balanced data distribution. To account for the resource limitations of client devices, DM training is assigned to clients with data scarcity, while other clients focus on FL model training. Additionally, a subset of data-rich clients participates in DM training to guide the generation of higher-quality synthetic data. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed DM-based FL framework outperforms existing FL approaches by improving performance and achieving a more balanced data distribution.

Author: Asad, M.; Otoum, S.
Title: FLChain-LLM: A Blockchain-Enabled Framework for Training Large Language Models
Publication Title: 2025 7th International Conference on Blockchain Computing and Applications (BCCA)
Abstract Note: The training of large language models (LLMs) on decentralized and privacy-sensitive data poses significant challenges related to trust, coordination, and security. To address these issues, we propose FLChain-LLM, a blockchain-enabled federated learning (FL) framework designed for collaborative fine-tuning of pre-trained LLMs across distributed clients. Our framework integrates smart contracts to automate client participation, secure model update verification, and reward contribution, while ensuring transparency and immutability through blockchain records. We employ GPT-2 as a base model and fine-tune it using the StackOverflow dataset partitioned by user, simulating a realistic FL environment. Experimental results show a reduction in global model perplexity from 34.7 to 27.8 over 10 rounds. The token-based incentive mechanism fairly rewards clients based on local loss and participation quality. FLChain-LLM demonstrates strong resilience to nonIIID data and malicious clients while preserving model utility. Our work highlights the potential of blockchain as a trust infrastructure for scalable, privacy-preserving LLM adaptation in decentralized settings, such as edge computing or crossorganization collaborations.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; Federated Learning; Decentralized Training; GPT-2; Large Language Models

Author: Xiandong, Z.; Zhiwen, P.; Nan, L.
Title: A Blockchain and Federated Learning Based Cooperative Spectrum Sensing Model for Cognitive Radio Networks
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 101st Vehicular Technology Conference (VTC2025-Spring)
Abstract Note: To address the issues of single point of failure and malicious attacks faced by existing federated learning-based spec-trum sensing models in cognitive radio, a cooperative spectrum sensing model based on blockchain and federated learning is proposed. A novel consensus mechanism based on Proof of Rapid Aggregation (PoRA) is first introduced, which effectively avoids the block generation delay caused by the mining process. Additionally, an adaptive weight aggregation algorithm is proposed using smart contract to improve accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves efficient and accurate cooperative spectrum sensing while ensuring security.

Author: Nagarajan, H.; Alagarsundaram, P.; Sitaraman, S. R.; Gattupalli, K.; Gollavilli, V. S. Bhavana Harish; J, B.
Title: AI-Driven Cryptographic Framework for Smart Industrial Cloud Security
Publication Title: 2025 8th International Conference on Computing Methodologies and Communication (ICCMC)
Abstract Note: Industrial systems, nowadays, are rapidly advancing with Industry 4.0 to encompass IoT, automation, and cloud computing in Cloud-based Industrial Control Systems. However, such increased interconnectivity and reliance on data opens up vulnerabilities whereby unauthorized access and cyberattacks can exploit these systems with data breaches. This study aims at the creation of a robust security solution in order to address these vulnerabilities with the integration of multi-layered attribute-based authentication, advanced cryptographic techniques, and AI-powered threat detection. The primary objectives of enhancing privacy protection, increasing efficiency, and ensuring safe data sharing in dynamic industrial environments. The proposed framework makes use of attribute-based encryption for adaptable access management, uses multi-tier encryption design to have robust data safeguarding, and trains AI models for the detection of threats in real-time. It combines symmetric, asymmetric, and homomorphic encryption with AI-driven anomaly identification to counter the risks emerging from such new vulnerabilities. Performance analysis shows that the suggested AI-driven multi-layered encryption framework outperforms prior cloud-based ICS techniques in terms of scalability and resource optimisation, achieving 95.4% privacy preservation, 10.1 ms authentication speed, 520.7 operations/sec encryption throughput, and 93.8% threat detection accuracy. The results illustrate that the AI-assisted multi-layered framework will provide an integrated solution securing industrial control systems by ensuring data integrity, confidentiality, and operational efficiency.
Manual Tags: Industry 4.0; threat detection; cloud security; AI-driven security; advanced cryptography; attribute-based authentication; smart industrial control systems

Author: Anusha.C; Ambili.P.S; D, S. P.; Surendran, A.; T, M. M.
Title: The Role of AI Technologies in Data Privacy and Protection in the Metaverse Era: A detailed Review
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent Systems and Pioneering Innovations in Robotics and Electric Mobility (INSPIRE)
Abstract Note: The sudden convergence of Metaverse and Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies has transformed individuals' interactions, socialization, and online transactions within virtual ecosystems. With the increasing integration of AI into Metaverse platforms so that smart agents, emotion analysis, and live adaptation are feasible, there come immediate concerns for data privacy, digital identity, and secure authentication of users. This article provides an extensive overview of the existing state of data protection measures in AI-based Metaverse systems, with emphasis on issues like deep-fake-induced identity creation, biometric exposure, centralized control of identities, and the absence of standardized security protocols. To tackle these challenges, this study reviewed a variety of privacy-friendly methods such as biometric and behavior-based authentication, decentralized identity platforms based on blockchain, transparent AI for responsible transparency, and enhanced cryptographic solutions like quantum signatures. The authors also investigate the shortfalls of current methods, identify important research gaps, and suggest directions for scalable, interoperable, and ethically sound security frameworks. The results highlight the necessity of interdisciplinary collaboration and embracement of user-centric, adaptive protection approaches toward developing trusted, secure, and inclusive Metaverse ecosystems.

Author: Majigi, M. U.; Ikuesan, R. A.; Idris, I.; Abdulhamid, S. M.
Title: Blockchain-Based Enhanced Secure Data Storage Model: A Framework for the Internet of Vehicle Networks
Publication Title: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
Abstract Note: The Internet of Vehicles (IoV) has gained significant attention due to its capability to facilitate Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) and Vehicle-to-Infrastructure (V2I) communication. However, IoV networks are highly susceptible to security and privacy threats, including unauthorized tracking of vehicle locations and Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) attacks. To address these challenges, recent studies have explored blockchain technology as a potential solution for enhancing data security and privacy in IoV networks. This research proposes a blockchain-based enhanced secure data storage model for IoV networks, incorporating lightweight cryptography algorithms to ensure robust security. Additionally, the framework integrates statistical and machine learning models to analyze harvested vehicular data, providing predictive insights for threat detection and mitigation. The study presents a hypothetical V2V communication dataset comprising eleven attributes and four records representing a four-smart-vehicle scenario. Analysis of vehicular speed data reveals an average speed of 55 km/h, with maximum and minimum speeds of 100 km/h and 0 km/h, respectively. The total payload transmitted is 42 KB, with an average payload size of 10.5 KB. A key contribution of this study is the development of a Solana blockchain-based secure data storage model, where transactions are automated and validated through smart contracts. The model efficiently stores the large volume of data generated by smart vehicles and enables real-time data retrieval using embedded internet protocols. The proposed framework is expected to provide a highly secure IoV data storage system upon successful implementation while enhancing threat prediction accuracy and overall network security.
Manual Tags: blockchain; Security; machine learning; Internet of Vehicles; lightweight cryptography algorithm

Author: Lin, H.; Yu, Z.; Wang, G.; Dong, A.; Tian, X.
Title: BLDTS: Blockchain-based Lightweight Data Trusted Sharing Scheme for Internet of Vehicles
Publication Title: 2025 28th International Conference on Computer Supported Cooperative Work in Design (CSCWD)
Abstract Note: Ensuring safe and reliable data sharing is crucial for the development of Internet of Vehicles (IoV) technology. To provide a trusted data environment for IoV and enable traditional consensus algorithms to meet the high dynamic requirements of the IoV. In this article, we propose a blockchain-based data sharing scheme for IoV (BLDTS) to achieve secure and trusted sharing. First, we design a false information identification strategy that utilizes a bayesian inference model to determine the authenticity of shared data with the assistance of reputation value. Second, the Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) is used to construct a novel lightweight consensus mechanism based on vehicle reputation values and traffic environment factors, and the nodes with high scores were selected as participants in the consensus, which can reduce the computational overhead. Finally, experimental results show that our scheme has advantages in improving the accuracy of false message identification and consensus efficiency.

Author: Shi, Z.; Cao, Z.; Pan, X.; Zeng, J.; Yu, F.
Title: An Adaptive Weighting Approach to Enhance the Efficiency and Robustness of Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2025 28th International Conference on Computer Supported Cooperative Work in Design (CSCWD)
Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) is a distributed machine learning method that allows multiple devices to train models locally and aggregate updates at a central server to ensure data privacy. However, constructing a robust global model is challenging due to limited access to local data and heterogeneous client data. Furthermore, malicious clients and high communication and computation costs further complicate the design of FL algorithms. Existing methods for evaluating client contributions are computationally intensive, unsuitable for large-scale applications. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes an adaptive weighting FL framework based on the Banzhaf index, providing a more efficient mechanism for evaluating and allocating client contributions. The Banzhaf index simplifies the computation process compared to traditional methods, allowing for better scalability. Additionally, we introduce a Neyman allocation stratified sampling strategy to optimize client selection, which effectively reduces variance and ensures balanced client representation, further enhancing both model performance and computational efficiency. Experimental results show that the proposed method significantly improves training efficiency, model accuracy, and robustness across various datasets, while reducing computation costs, making it well-suited for large-scale FL.

Author: Arangasamy, R.; Kodela, V.; Soumya, G.; Srivastava, S.; Meghashree, A. C.
Title: Federated Attention-Encrypted Learning for Privacy-Preserving Medical Image Classification
Publication Title: 2025 5th International Conference on Mobile Networks and Wireless Communications (ICMNWC)
Abstract Note: In modern era, the progress made in artificial intelligence in medicine has changed the way medical images are analyzed, but the privacy and security issues due to centralized collection of patient-sensitive data are huge issues. Traditional deep learning operates on data centralization, violating confidentiality and disrupting collaborative work between medical institutions. This work presents a Federated AttentionEncrypted Federated Learning (FAE-FL) model for medicalimage classification which is privacy-preserving. In this study, the ChestX-ray14 dataset is utilized, distributed over multiple medical nodes, enabling decentralized learning without raw data transfer. The images are pre-processed with normalizing and Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) to suppress the effects of variation in image uniformity and contrast across the medical facilities. An Attention-based ResNet (ARFE) is used for deep feature extraction, which emphasizes parts of the image relevant to the disease, to improve diagnostic accuracy. The FAE-FL model utilizes Partial Homomorphic Encryption (PHE) and Differential Privacy (DP) to provide security of the model updates, combined with Federated Averaging (FedAvg) for the efficiency of global aggregation of the model with cooperation. Experimental results proved the proposed FAE-FL framework achieved better accuracy (98.90%), precision (98.98%), recall (99.67%), and \F 1\-score (98.76%) than exiting Federated Learning (FL) model with significantly reduced encryption overhead, ensuring both high diagnostic performance and strict patient data confidentiality in decentralized healthcare environments.

Author: Dattatreya, V.; Adudhodla, M.; Krishna, V. S. R.; Nimmala, S.; Prasad, C. G. V. N.; Manellore, P. K. R.
Title: Energy-Efficient Federated Learning Framework for Secure IoT Sensor Networks in Smart Cities
Publication Title: 2025 5th International Conference on Ubiquitous Computing and Intelligent Information Systems (ICUIS)
Abstract Note: The proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices in smart city environments has created unprecedented opportunities for data-driven urban management while simultaneously introducing significant challenges in energy efficiency, security, and scalability. This is a novel energy-efficient federated learning framework designed specifically for secure IoT sensor networks in smart city applications. The proposed system integrates edge computing capabilities with distributed machine learning to enable real-time data processing while preserving privacy and minimizing energy consumption. The framework employs a hierarchical architecture comprising sensor nodes, edge gateways, and cloud infrastructure, utilizing MQTT protocol for lightweight communication and blockchain-based security mechanisms. Experimental evaluation conducted over a 30-day deployment period with 120 sensor nodes demonstrated significant performance improvements, including a 34% reduction in energy consumption compared to centralized approaches, an average end-to-end latency of 185 ms, and a packet delivery ratio of 99.2%. The federated learning component achieved 92% accuracy in anomaly detection while reducing communication overhead by 67% through local model training. The security framework successfully mitigated 98.5% of simulated adversarial attacks while maintaining system responsiveness. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework effectively addresses the critical challenges of scalability, energy efficiency, and security in smart city IoT deployments, providing a foundation for sustainable urban sensing applications.

Author: Gundaboina, A.
Title: Secure and Compliant Cloud-based Healthcare Analytics using Federated Learning and Differential Privacy
Publication Title: 2025 3rd International Conference on Sustainable Computing and Smart Systems (ICSCSS)
Abstract Note: In the era of data-driven healthcare, ensuring the security, privacy, and regulatory compliance of cloud-based artificial intelligence (AI) systems has become critically significant. With sensitive patient data increasingly stored and processed in distributed cloud environments, safeguarding information while maintaining model performance is an initial requirement for ethical and legal AI deployment. Traditional machine learning (ML) models, though effective in terms of accuracy, require raw data transmission and centralized storage, exposing systems to increased risks of data breaches, unauthorized access, and privacy violations. Moreover, these existing systems often lack mechanisms for auditable compliance, adaptive privacy control, and scalable collaboration across multiple institutions. To address these limitations, this study presents a two-stage privacy-preserving AI framework for cloud and edge computing that integrates EfficientNetB0-based feature extraction, compressed variational autoencoders (CVAE) for anomaly detection, differential privacy (DP) transformation, federated learning (FL), and reinforcement learning (RL)-based adaptive privacy enforcement, enabled by blockchain-based compliance logging. Experimental evaluation on the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care III (MIMIC-III) dataset demonstrates a high prediction accuracy of 97.3%, an AUROC of 0.981, and robust performance across varying privacy budgets (∈) . The model also shows steady convergence across federated training rounds without sacrificing privacy or accuracy. This study provides valuable insights into designing secure, privacy-aware, and compliant AI architectures for healthcare, offering a practical foundation for future systems deployed in sensitive, multi-institutional environments.
Manual Tags: Federated Learning; Differential Privacy; Reinforcement Learning; Cloud Security; Predictive Analytics; Healthcare Compliance; Privacy-Preserving Artificial Intelligence

Author: More, N.; Vanjale, S. B.; Rao, G.; Mane, M.
Title: Design and Evaluation of a Blockchain–IPFS Framework for Secure Electronic Health Records in IoT-Enabled Healthcare
Publication Title: 2025 1st International Conference on Advancement in Futuristic Technologies (ICAFT)
Abstract Note: This study introduces a blockchain-based framework designed to strengthen the privacy, security, and verifiability of Electronic Health Records (EHRs) within Internet of Things (IoT)-driven healthcare environments. The proposed hybrid model combines blockchain for tamper-proof data logging, the InterPlanetary File System (IPFS) for scalable and efficient off-chain storage, and advanced cryptographic mechanisms such as smart contracts and Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs) to enable secure access management. Within this architecture, patients retain ownership and control of their encrypted medical data, while healthcare providers obtain permissioned access verified through ZKP-enabled smart contracts. Comparative evaluation reveals notable performance gains—92% enhancement in data integrity, 87% improvement in privacy protection, and a 30–35% reduction in unauthorized access—relative to conventional centralized EHR systems. Additionally, the framework demonstrates over 40% higher auditability and trust among healthcare entities. Remaining research challenges include achieving cross-platform interoperability, ensuring regulatory compliance, and integrating advanced privacy-preserving technologies such as federated learning and homomorphic encryption. Future work aims to optimize consensus mechanisms and align the framework with HL7 FHIR standards to facilitate scalability and real-world deployment.

Author: Jaiswal, V.; Shahi, A.; Kaushal, A.
Title: Integration of Blockchain with Artificial Intelligence for Financial Security: A Comprehensive Review
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 7th International Conference on Computing, Communication and Automation (ICCCA)
Abstract Note: The need of secure, efficient as well as transparent mechanisms to control transactions and data has raised due to the rapid changes in the existing and evolving financial system. In this regard, the integration of AI and Blockchain has played a major role towards considering as a secure defence mechanism. Due to its decentralized and tamper-proof nature, Blockchain ensures the integrity of financial data. On the other hand, AI in form of Intrusion Detection System can be used to predict and thus prevent from known as well as unknown attacks. These properties of both AI and Blockchain can be harnessed in order to build a strong defence mechanism in order to safeguard the financial data over the internet. Several traditional approaches have been developed in the past as security mechanism but have failed to safeguard the data. Thus there is a continuous need for developing efficient, more complex mechanism that can be used as security tool for the financial data. This review paper presents a comprehensive review of several research papers published in reputed journals with good citation that focuses on how the integration of Blockchain with Artificial Intelligence for can be used as security tool for financial data.

Author: Malothu, V.; D.Ramesh
Title: A Novel Intrusion Detection and Prevention Framework for Enhancing Robust Security in Cloud Computing Environments
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Communication Networks and Application (ICSCN)
Abstract Note: Advanced cyber-attacks like Distributed Denial-of-Service, Economic Denial of Sustainability, and insider threats have remained a constant menace to the cloud computing environment that affect service availability and data confidentiality badly. In place, intrusion detection and prevention methods are based on machine learning, deep learning, and hybrid ensembles, yet, there is a lot to be desired in terms of scalability, false positives, and real-time flexibility. The reported findings in previous studies demonstrate that optimized models could reach detection rates of over 97-98 % whereas ensemble-based models cause false positives to be almost 20 % lower than their single counterparts. Although these developments have been made, the latest networks with high-throughput still suffer latency, and cannot efficiently respond to zero-day attacks. In order to consider these gaps, this paper will suggest an adaptive intrusion detection and prevention framework which will incorporate federated deep reinforcement learners with blockchain based trust management. The federated methodology enables joint anomaly detection between cloud and edge layers and preserves the privacy of the data, whereas reinforcement learning guarantees adaptation to the changes in the traffic pattern. Smart contracts that are based on blockchain verify and protect the notification, and guarantee non-interference of distributed nodes. The initial examination reveals that this framework may potentially raise the detection rates up to more than 99%, the number of false positives will decrease to less than 3%, and the response time will be reduced by 25% in comparison with traditional systems. This contribution is a scalable, and resilient security system that can protect the next-generation cloud infrastructures against advanced cyber threats.

Author: S, N. Prajwalasimha; Saini, D. K. J. B.; Lakshmi, K.; Kolekar, S.; S, P. Joshe Raj; Monish, L.
Title: Federated Blockchain Intelligence: A Multi-Modal AI Framework for Cyber-Resilient Smart Cities
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on NexGen Networks and Cybernetics (IC2NC)
Abstract Note: The unprecedented growth of networked devices, diverse data streams, and cyber-physical infrastructure of contemporary smart cities has dramatically increased the attack surface of adversarial actions. Current mechanisms of security are frequently siloed, reactive, and limited in their capacity for delivering trustworthy, explainable, and real-time threat intelligence across diverse domains. This work introduces Blockchain-Enabled Multi-Modal Artificial Intelligence (BMAI), a converged framework using distributed ledger technologies and state-of-the-art Machine Learning (ML) to deliver assured, transparent, and adaptive smart city threat intelligence. The resulting architecture unifies multi-modal data sources such as network traffic, IoT sensor telemetry, video surveillance feeds, and citizen complaints into a scalable Deep Learning (DL) pipe capable of combining diverse heterogenous signals for high-fidelity detection of coordinated attack and anomalies. By integrating blockchain-based consensus and indelible audit logs, the system ensures data provenance and trustless collaborations of diverse stakeholders and immunity against data tampering and poisoning of the model. Finally, the work describes a self-optimizing control loop using federated and explainable AI that is used to continually optimize detection of smart city threats while guaranteeing regulatory compliance and preserving private information. Experimental characterization based on constrained smart city testbeds shows up to 35% detection accuracy improvement, 40% reduction of false positives and near real-time performance when matched with state-of-the-art alternatives. BMAI shows promise of being a foundation technology of sustainable, citizen-centric, and cyber-resilient smart cities.

Author: Mao, J.; Xiao, X.; Wang, S.; Gao, P.; Si, Y.
Title: Privacy Protection Strategy for Virtual Power Plant Users Based on Hierarchical Dynamic Differential Privacy
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 7th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
Abstract Note: Virtual Power Plants (VPPs) face risks of user privacy data leakage during the integration of distributed energy resources and user assets.Existing privacy protection technologies suffer from issues such as the lack of full-process protection and an imbalance between privacy preservation and efficiency.To address these challenges, this study proposes a Hierarchical Dynamic Privacy Protection Framework (HDPF) that integrates dynamic differential privacy, federated learning, and blockchain technology to construct a collaborative protection system across local, aggregation, and interaction layers.The local layer employs lightweight homomorphic encryption and dynamic noise injection mechanisms to encrypt and anonymize user electricity consumption data and market transaction information.The aggregation layer utilizes CKKS homomorphic encryption technology for resource aggregation under ciphertext conditions and records full-process operational logs through blockchain to ensure data traceability and tamper resistance.The interaction layer relies on smart contracts to design automated transaction clearing algorithms, completing privacy-preserving ranking and trusted settlement while verifying grid operational constraints through security validation contracts. Experimental results demonstrate that this strategy enhances privacy protection strength, computational efficiency, and data usability in VPPs.

Author: Mukisa, K. J.; Ahakonye, L. A. Chijioke; Kim, D.-S.; Lee, J. M.
Title: Enhancing IIoT Security Using Hybrid CNN-BiLSTM Models with Blockchain Integration
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Information and Communication (ICAIIC)
Abstract Note: In the rapidly evolving Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) landscape, ensuring robust security measures for detecting and mitigating cyber threats is paramount. This paper suggests a decentralized intrusion detection system (IDS) that uses Federated Learning (FL) integrated with a permissioned blockchain layer to secure IIoT networks. The system leverages a modified deep learning architecture, staking Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) with Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) layers to quickly detect the temporal and spatial sequences in data traffic over a network. Training the model in a federated environment ensures data privacy, and the blockchain layer guarantees that only authorized devices participate in the learning process, adding an extra layer of security. We evaluated our model using the Edge-IIoTset dataset, containing 14 cyber-attack types and one benign class. Our suggested model showed superior performance, achieving an accuracy of 95%, surpassing traditional models' accuracy in similar environments.
