Abstract Note: Real-time gathering of data and better patient outcomes are now possible because of the healthcare industry's quick adoption of IoT technologies, which have transformed medical diagnostics and patient monitoring. However, there are serious security and privacy threats due to the highly sensitive nature of clinical data and the widespread connectivity of IoT devices. A thorough analysis of the privacy and security issues of IoT-based healthcare systems is provided in this research. It examines current risks, major obstacles, approaches, and remedies documented in current studies (2020–2025). The report highlights the importance of energy-efficient designs, blockchain structures, AI/ML-driven security measures, and cryptographic techniques as key facilitators for robust healthcare IoT infrastructures.

Author: Li, Y.; Feng, J.; Liu, L.; Shang, B.; Lei, J.; Pei, Q.
Title: FedEXD: Self-Propelled Federated Learning with Extraction-Based Knowledge Distillation in Heterogeneous Environments
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 101st Vehicular Technology Conference (VTC2025-Spring)
Abstract Note: Federated learning (FL) is a pivotal paradigm for decentralized model training while preserving data privacy. However, data heterogeneity among clients significantly degrades model performance and convergence efficiency. In response, we introduce a federated knowledge distillation mechanism, FedEXD, that addresses robustness and convergence in diverse client environments through a self-propelled learning architecture. FedEXD employs a novel density ratio-based data extraction algorithm, leveraging KLIEP to select representative data, enhancing global knowledge synthesis and local model adaptability while preserving privacy. Extensive evaluations on benchmark datasets demonstrate FedEXD's substantial improvements in efficiency and accuracy, demonstrating a substantial 1.51% accuracy improvement over state-of-the-art methods under firm heterogeneity while reducing communication rounds by over 46.3%. These findings underscore FedEXD's potential to advance FL systems' generalizability across complex, non-IID data distributions, offering a scalable solution for privacy-conscious, high-performance distributed learning.

Author: T, K. C.; K, T. S. S.; M, V.
Title: Next-Gen AI-Driven Cybersecurity Framework for Flying Taxis with Intrusion Detection and Secure Command Validation
Publication Title: 2025 2nd International Conference on Recent Trends in Electrical, Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICRTEECT)
Abstract Note: The rapid development of autonomous flying taxis presents new opportunities for urban transportation, but also introduces significant cybersecurity risks. The proposed system integrates machine learning, deep learning, and reinforcement learning for real-time threat detection and autonomous response. It leverages blockchain for secure communication, federated learning for decentralized data protection, and digital twin simulations for vulnerability forecasting and resilience testing. This AI-enhanced framework ensures continuous surveillance, system adaptability, and proactive threat mitigation across critical components such as navigation, flight controls, and passenger interfaces. Author: Xu, S.; Li, D.; Wang, L.; Mihaljević, M. J.; Zhang, S.; Shao, W.; Wang, Q.
Title: Cross-Chain Identity Authentication Protocol based on Group Signature and Zero-Knowledge Proof
Publication Title: 2025 28th International Conference on Computer Supported Cooperative Work in Design (CSCWD)
Abstract Note: Cross-chain interaction plays a crucial role in enhancing asset circulation and data sharing across diverse blockchain systems. Cross-chain identity authentication is the primary pre-requisite of cross-chain security interaction. However, existing cross-chain identity authentication protocol generally has issues such as insufficient decentralization, poor universality, and low authentication efficiency. These issues compromise the reliability of cross-chain interactions. Based on group signature and zero-knowledge proof, this paper proposes a cross-chain identity authentication protocol to address these concerns. The protocol employs Decentralized Identifiers(DIDs) as the global identity identifier of users, utilizes zero-knowledge proof to provide privacy for the verification of users' identities when joining the group, and then constructs the users' transaction signatures through group signatures to hide the users' identities. This approach not only reduces the risk of users' privacy leakage but also facilitates mutual recognition of identities among cross-chain systems. Finally, the security analysis and experimental analysis shows the correctness and efficiency of the proposed scheme.

Author: Li, Q.; Han, Y.; Liu, Q.; Wang, G.; Yu, H.; Yu, J.
Title: BCPPAS : Blockchain-Based Cross-Domain Identity Authentication Scheme for IoT with Privacy Protection
Publication Title: 2025 28th International Conference on Computer Supported Cooperative Work in Design (CSCWD)
Abstract Note: In Internet of Things(IoT) systems, ensuring the secure exchange of information between devices from different domains is crucial. Current cross-domain authentication schemes based on a single blockchain struggle to meet the confidentiality requirements for data and information exchange in large-scale IoT systems. This paper proposes a blockchain-based identity authentication scheme (BCPPAS) for IoT, featuring dual-chain collaboration, and designs a novel certificateless aggregate signature algorithm to address complex certificate management and key escrow issues. The edge server is capable of aggregating different signatures to achieve batch authentication, markedly improving authentication efficiency and reducing computational and storage overhead. Also, BCPPAS is designed to avoid costly bilinear pairing operations, providing less computational overhead for IoT devices with limited resources. To protect the privacy of IoT devices, BCPPAS uses the pseudonym instead of the real identity. Finally, efficiency of BCPPAS are demonstrated through theoretical analysis and experiments.

Author: Pallela, S. P.; Banerjee, S.

Author: Kaithal, P. K.; Singh, R.; Kaithal, S.; Pandey, A.; Sengar, A. S.; Gangrade, S.
Title: A Federated Neuro-Symbolic Deep Learning Framework with Zero-Knowledge Blockchain for Electronic Health Data Security
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 5th International Conference on ICT in Business Industry & Government (ICTBIG)
Abstract Note: The need for strong cybersecurity frameworks in the healthcare industry has increased due to the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) devices and electronic health records (EHRs) exponential growth. This paper presents HealthSentinel-ZKP, a novel framework that leverages federated neuro-symbolic deep learning and zero-knowledge blockchain to secure electronic health data. In contrast to earlier models, HealthSentinel-ZKP combines CNNs, Transformers, and symbolic reasoning for multi-perspective intrusion detection. Federated learning and zero-knowledge proof mechanisms protect data privacy. Using an immutable ZKPenhanced blockchain, the system guarantees GDPR-compliant auditing and has a dual-stream anomaly detection architecture. HealthSentinel-ZKP is a next-generation healthcare cybersecurity paradigm, as demonstrated by experimental results on benchmark datasets that demonstrate superior performance in zero-day attack detection and privacy preservation.

Author: Mastoi, Q.-U.-A.; Ramadhani, U. A.; Lakhan, A.; Shah, S. I.; Yar, M. A. E.; Shah, S. Y.; Shah, S. A.
Title: Federated Learning-Enabled Adversarial Attack Detection Framework for Healthcare Laboratory Data
Publication Title: 2025 7th International Conference on Blockchain Computing and Applications (BCCA)
Abstract Note: An adversarial attack deliberately manipulates data or model inputs to deceive a machine learning model, causing it to make incorrect predictions or classifications. In machine learning and artificial intelligence, adversarial attacks exploit vulnerabilities in models by subtly altering the input data in ways that are often imperceptible to humans but cause the model to misbehave. These attacks can target various machine learning models and healthcare applications. This paper presents a federated learning-enabled framework that collects and trains healthcare data from different laboratories and hospitals and aggregates it in a centralized hospital for disease prediction. We present the AADFLS (Adversarial Attack Detection Federated Learning Scheme), which consists of different steps to identify attacks and securely process data between connected hospitals and laboratories. We aim to collect and train data securely and avoid adversarial attacks in the distributed healthcare environment. Simulation results show that our testbed results are based on AADFLS having higher accuracy and scores as compared to existing adversarial attack detection schemes (AADS) and adversarial attack federated learning schemes (AAFL) when shared and aggregated data for training predictions on the aggregate node.

Author: Latchupatula, P. K.; Alzubaidy, A.; V, S. A.; R, K. P.; Ramaswamy, Y.
Title: A Comprehensive Research on Privacy-Preserving in Health Data Analytics
Publication Title: 2025 Third International Conference on Networks, Multimedia and Information Technology (NMITCON)
Abstract Note: Digital healthcare systems have generated massive volumes of sensitive health data, allowing data-driven medical diagnostics, personalized treatment, and public health research. However, the use of such data increases serious privacy issues, owing to risk of data breaches, unauthorized access, and inappropriate use of personal health information. This has necessitated the improvement of privacy-preserving techniques to ensure secure and ethical use of health data. However, several privacy-preserving techniques, such as differential privacy, homomorphic encryption, secure multiparty computation, and secure sensitive health data, frequently reduce data utility, degrade model accuracy, and result in computational costs. However, this is a serious limitation in healthcare, in which both data accuracy and secure privacy guarantees are crucial for safe clinical decisions and meaningful insights. Additionally, there is a rising need to strike a balance between effective data analysis and strict privacy protection, as health data remain to fuel AI-driven innovations, and confirming their confidentiality without delaying analytic value is vital. Furthermore, existing privacy-preserving techniques often struggle to ensure high utility while confirming strong privacy guarantees, thereby highlighting the necessity for stronger, scalable, and adaptive solutions.

Author: Shobana, D.
Title: Performance Evaluation of a Blockchain-Oriented Secure Validation Mechanism for 5G-Integrated IoT Networks
Publication Title: 2025 10th International Conference on Smart Structures and Systems (ICSSS)
Abstract Note: With the billions of devices that are connected in 5G-enabled Internet of Things (IoT) networks, industries have been revolutionized, due to high-speed data transmission, ultra-low latency as well as large scale connectivity that 5g offers. Yet, the growing number of IoT devices also creates serious security and privacy issues like unauthorized access, data breaches, and cyber-attacks. Security frameworks are dependent, centralized, and they cannot establish trust, scalability, and resilience against attack. With its potential to offer decentralized validation, secure authentication, and tamper-proof data storage, blockchain technology has therefore emerged as a promising solution to these concerns. Through this work, we investigate the combination of blockchain-based validation mechanisms with \textbackslash{}mathbf{5 G}\ Internet of Things networks to allow more secure, private, and integritypreserving networks. This usually involves lightweight consensus mechanisms like Proof-of-Stake (PoS) and Byzantine Fault Tolerance (BFT) to enhance transaction efficiency while lowering energy consumption. Edge computing along with blockchain also helps in processing of data at the spot while waiting to be encoded which saves time and decrease latency of IoT applications. Beyond that, AI-driven security models provide higher accuracy in threat detection and anomaly identification in \textbackslash{}mathbf{5 G}\ IoT networks available in blockchain. However, notwithstanding the benefits, issues such as privacy, scalability, regulatory compliance, and computational overhead are still emergent areas of research. In contrast, on the other hand, enhancing the security frameworks of \textbackslash{}mathbf{5 G } \textbackslash{}mathbf{ I o T}\ ecosystems built on blockchain through post-quantum cryptography, federated learning, and self-sovereign identity management will lay a crucial role in the developments of computer-based solutions coming in the future. Upon learning the state-of-the-art blockchain validation methods and their contributions to the Internet of Things security, we analyze and evaluate the future works and threats on the secure 5G Internet of Things in this study.

Author: Jia, Z.; Zhao, Z.; Liu, C.; Wan, J.; Zhang, X.; Sun, P.; Zhou, C.
Title: Distributed Resource Allocation for Energy Minimization in Blockchain-Based MEC
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE International Symposium on Parallel and Distributed Processing with Applications (ISPA)
Abstract Note: The rapid growth of 5G has increased intelligent terminals, boosting mobile data and computational demands. Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) offloads compute-intensive tasks to nearby servers for fast responses and local decision-making, but its distributed nature and limited resources pose security and privacy risks like data tampering. Blockchain enhances security with immutability and traceability, though its consensus process is energy-intensive. This paper proposes a Federated Reinforcement Learning (FRL)-based joint optimization for blockchain-based MEC (B-MEC), formulated as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) to minimize energy consumption (task execution and consensus) while meeting latency constraints. A Federated Proximal Policy Optimization (F-PPO) algorithm with an attention-based aggregation mechanism improves policy learning and privacy. Simulations show F-PPO outperforms traditional federated learning and standalone methods in convergence, confirming its effectiveness in B-MEC systems.

Author: Mallick, S. R.; Rakesh, N.; Diwan, P.; Lenka, R. K.; Sahoo, S. R.
Title: End-to-End Trustless and Scalable Frame-Work for Smart Agro-Infrastructure Using Blockchain, IoT, and Distributed Storage Technologies
Publication Title: 2025 Artificial Intelligence and Smart Technologies for Sustainability Conference (AISTS)
Abstract Note: The next generation of smart agricultural frameworks must be robust, secure, and privacy-preserving to keep up with the growing volume of sensitive data generated by widely distributed IoT devices. Data integrity problems, scalability issues, and the possibility of single points of failure are making current centralised designs inappropriate. This article proposes an end-to-end secure and scalable privacy-preserving framework by integrating Blockchain with the IoT and IPFS distributed storage solutions. By using cryptographic approaches and lightweight authentication procedures, the proposed system guarantees efficient off-chain data storage, decentralised access control, and tamper-proof data logging while protecting the privacy of stakeholders and farmers. Additionally, smart contract integration streamlines supply chain operations, optimises resource allocation, and enforces transparent data sharing standards. Experimental evaluation and testing of the framework in real-world environments confirm its efficiency in reducing latency, increasing throughput, and energy consumption. Furthermore, it promotes reliability, transparency, and sustainability, establishing the groundwork for a robust and privacy-conscious agricultural ecosystem.

Author: Wang, P.; Liu, X.; Mi, Z.; Guo, B.; Yin, Z.; Shen, Z.
Title: FedIFPG. Personalized Federated Learning based on Information Fusion and Prototype Guidance
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics (SMC)
Abstract Note: Personalized Federated Learning (PFL) aims to tailor models for individual clients while leveraging shared knowledge across a decentralized system. However, PFL faces challenges such as global model drift and global-local knowledge discrepancy, particularly under heterogeneous data distributions and client dropouts. To address these challenges, we propose FedIFPG, which integrates an information fusion module, a dynamic temporal weighting mechanism, and a global class prototype guidance strategy. The information fusion module, incorporating a dynamic temporal weighting mechanism, effectively balances global and local information, mitigating the effects of client drift and global-local bias. Simultaneously, the global class prototype guidance strategy enhances semantic consistency for the same class across different client models. Experiments on four benchmark datasets demonstrate that FedIFPG consistently outperforms SOTA methods in both accuracy and robustness.

Author: Zhang, P.; Chen, Z.; Xu, F.; Zhu, H.
Title: Blockchain-Enhanced Trusted Social Manufacturing: A Perspective on Product Lifecycle Management
Publication Title: 2025 1st International Symposium on E-CARGO and Applications (E-CARGO)
Abstract Note: Social manufacturing (SM) is an emerging manufacturing paradigm relying on advanced information and communication technologies to socialize and network manufacturing resources. It aims to enhance social participation, innovation, efficiency, and sustainable development. However, improving trustworthiness in SM is crucial and challenging for promoting open, collaborative, and innovative cooperation. Blockchain, as a distributed ledger technology, has the characteristics of decentralization, transparency, immutability, security, and automation, which can promote the realization of Trusted social manufacturing (TSM). This work categorizes Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) into five stages: 1) design; 2) manufacturing; 3) distribution and sales; 4) usage and maintenance; and 5) remanufacturing and recycling. Based on a PLM perspective, this work surveys studies on Blockchain-based TSM (BTSM). Particularly, it investigates and summarizes trustworthy dimensions achievable through blockchains in these five PLM stages, including decentralization, collaboration, intelligence, traceability, and security. Author: Mohammadi, K.; Moradi, A.; Atani, R. E.
Title: FedRLEA: Federated Aggregation of Parallel SLMs with RL-Based Prompt Optimization for Smart Enterprise Architecture
Publication Title: 2025 9th Iranian Conference on Advances in Enterprise Architecture (ICAEA)
Abstract Note: The rapid adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in enterprise architectures has created new opportunities for intelligent automation and decision support while simultaneously raising concerns regarding data privacy, scalability, and adaptability. Traditional centralized training of large language models (LLMs) is impractical for many organizations due to high computational demands and privacy risks associated with data aggregation. This paper introduces a federated aggregation framework for parallel Small Language Models (SLMs) that applies Hashgraph-based decentralized learning to eliminate reliance on central servers. To further enhance adaptability and task-specific accuracy, the framework integrates a reinforcement learning (RL)-based prompt optimization mechanism, enabling continuous refinement of SLM prompts through interaction driven feedback. The proposed system supports cross organizational collaboration under privacy-preserving constraints and is designed for deployment within smart enterprise architectures. Our formal model analysis demonstrates efficient distributed model training, scalability across heterogeneous nodes, and reduced communication overhead compared to traditional federated learning approaches. The integration of RL-based prompt tuning yields measurable improvements in model relevance and responsiveness to evolving enterprise data. The results highlight the potential of federated SLM aggregation to provide a secure, adaptive, and resource-efficient foundation for next-generation AI-based enterprise architectures.

Author: Manne, V. T.
Title: AEP-M: AI-Enhanced Anonymous E-Payment for Mobile Devices using ARM Trust Zone and Divisible E-Cash
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain and Distributed Systems Security (ICBDS)
Abstract Note: E-Payment has become popular in mobile commerce, can provide consumers with a convenient way to make purchases electronically. Currently, however, all too many E-Payment systems are primarily focused on securing a consumer's financial information and do little to prevent privacy leaks and AI-generated scams. This paper defines AEP-M, a novel AI-enhanced anonymous e-payment scheme developed for mobile devices that uses TrustZone and divisible e-cash. Since mobile devices have very limited processing power and each transaction must be performed in real time, the proposed solution combines an efficient divisible e-cash system with AI-powered anomaly detection techniques to improve both the security, privacy and fraud detection in mobile payments. In addition to enabling users to divide a single withdrawal of an e-coin of a large amount into multiple transactions without disclosing their identity to either banks or merchants, AEP-M integrates AI-based risk assessment to identify suspicious spending behaviors to rapidly mitigate fraud and continuously monitor transactions. By employing a combination of bit decomposition and precomputation to minimize the computational overhead of the transaction process, AEP-M provides the optimal performance in terms of minimizing the max number of exponentiation operations required to perform the frequent online spending process on elliptic curves. Finally, AEP-M also incorporates an ARM TrustZone to protect a user's financial data and important private data; an SRAM PUF is used as a Root of Trust to derive AI-powered keys and manage sensitive data, thereby increasing both the security and reliability of the system. A prototype of AEP-M was implemented and evaluated using the BN curve at a 128-bit security level. The experimental results demonstrated that AEP-M is capable of improving the Security, Efficiency and Fraud Detection capabilities of Mobile Digital Payments while maintaining User Privacy and Anonymity.
Manual Tags: privacy; fraud detection; Anonymous electronic payment; ARM TrustZone; divisible e-cash; mobile payment; secure hardware

Author: Zhang, C.; Ling, L.
Title: Pro-ZkFL: Efficient Verifiable Federated Learning Based on Probabilistic Zero-Knowledge Auditing and Reputation Sharding
Publication Title: 2025 5th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) enables distributed model training while preserving data privacy; however, it remains vulnerable to poisoning attacks and lacks computational integrity. Recent solutions integrating Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs) and blockchain have successfully established process-level verifiability but suffer from prohibitive computational overhead due to the requirement of generating cryptographic proofs for every local update. To address this efficiency bottleneck, this paper proposes Pro-ZkFL, a reputation-aware probabilistic verification framework. Unlike deterministic approaches that verify every transaction, Pro-ZkFL utilizes Verifiable Random Functions (VRF) on-chain to dynamically select a subset of clients for auditing based on their historical reputation scores. We design a dual-commitment scheme where clients submit lightweight cryptographic commitments for every round but generate heavy ZKPs only when challenged. Experimental results on FashionMNIST and CIFAR-10 demonstrate that Pro-ZkFL reduces computational overhead by approximately 82 % and gas costs by 73 % compared to full-verification baselines while maintaining a 99 % detection rate against persistent adversaries, offering a scalable trade-off between security and efficiency.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; Federated Learning; Zero-Knowledge Proofs; Reputation Systems; Probabilistic Verification

Author: Kumar, T.; Alwaisi, Z.; Gupta, A. K.; Auluck, N.; Mähönen, P.
Title: Sustainable Security for Edge AI: Challenges and Solutions
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE Globecom Workshops (GC Wkshps)
Abstract Note: The ongoing transition from 5G to 6G wireless networks has already spotlighted the critical and centric role of secure and sustainable communication. The integration of Edge AI networks in the 6G network is expected to significantly widen the security threat landscape. Edge devices are usually resource-constrained, and thus managing overall security would require sustainable security solutions. Author: Ren, P.; Yan, T.
Title: Robust and Efficient Cross-silo Blockchained Federated Learning with Proof of Generalization
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
Abstract Note: Blockchain-based federated learning (BFL) enables decentralized model training across multiple data silos without exposing raw data. However, its deployment in cross-silo scenarios faces two key challenges. First, it is vulnerable to dual poisoning attacks on both local and global models. Second, massive communication and computation latency can lead to inefficiencies. To address these issues, we propose Proof of Generalization (PoG), a consensus mechanism integrated into the training process. PoG ensures model credibility through cross-validation while maintaining high efficiency. In addition, we develop a comprehensive latency model to evaluate convergence time and derive a closed-form solution for optimizing local training epochs. Experimental results on two benchmark datasets demonstrate that PoG outperforms three advanced verification methods and two classical consensus algorithms in both robustness and efficiency.

Author: Sathya, T.; Kumar, M. S.; Sarjun, M. M.; Monish, N.; Subramani, G.
Title: Denial of Service Detection for System Security Using Machine Learning
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain and Distributed Systems Security (ICBDS)

The algorithm receives a Python application framework which operates as a surveillance tool to monitor traffic activity until it detects compromised behavior. The implementation provides predictive and efficient protection that adapts well to growing networks and strengthens network protection by enabling quick detection and prevention of harmful network action for better digital infrastructure security.

Author: Thakre, G.; Raut, R.; Verma, P.
Title: A Review on AI - Enhanced Security in Blockchain and Cloud-Based Electronic Healthcare Records Systems
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
Abstract Note: The combination of Artificial Intelligence, Blockchain, and cloud computing have the potential to significantly improve the security and use of Electronic Healthcare Records (EHR) systems. This study looks into the future possibilities for AI-enhanced security and Predictive Analytics in Blockchain and Cloud-based EHR systems. Blockchain technology provides dependable solutions for data integrity, privacy, and safe sharing, whilst cloud platforms offer scalable and readily available infrastructure. AI improves these systems by providing improved threat identification, anomaly detection, and real-time automated responses, hence strengthening the security architecture. Furthermore, AI-powered Predictive Analytics in Cloud-based EHR systems enables early identification, personalized treatment, and improved patient outcomes. As the healthcare sector faces rising cyber dangers and data management challenges, merging these technologies is crucial to developing strong, efficient, and patient-centric EHR systems. However, combining AI with Blockchain presents ethical concerns, regulatory compliance hurdles, and the need for interoperable systems. This paper looks at current advancements and emerging developments in safe and predictive healthcare data management, such as quantum-resistant algorithms, federated learning, and AI-powered smart contracts. Author: Namazi, M.; Amirmozafarisabet, K.; Naserameri, M.; Arabzadeh, H.
Title: Strengthening Trust and Data Authenticity in AI and ML Through Blockchain-Based Mechanisms
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 15th International Conference on Electronics Information and Emergency Communication (ICEIEC)
Abstract Note: As we move towards greater penetration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) into numerous sectors, the authenticity of data used for training as well as inference is of paramount importance. Integrity, transparency, and robustness of such systems are key in avoiding manipulation and guaranteeing the trustworthiness of the outcome. In this paper, we introduce a new approach, Secure ML, which integrates Blockchain’s decentralized and immutable structure as a security measure to secure and ensure the reliability of the training data in the ML pipeline. We incorporate the Confidential Multi-Party Protocol (CMPP) to ensure the privacy of data and employ the Federated Consensus Protocol (FCP) as the consensus mechanism for secure cooperation. Every dataset is encrypted and validated by smart contracts and made available for verification by any system participants. These verified items are committed to a secure ledger and supported by cloud infrastructure with high redundancy and consistency levels. This architecture is intended to provide a solid basis for trustworthy AI. It addresses how data is shared securely, processed in a verifiable manner, and is less susceptible to adversarial tampering. The architecture considerations provide a relevant framework for real-world implementations and open an avenue for future work on scalable and secure AI deployment in sensitive domains.

Author: Marković, L.; Trpkov, A.; Sovtić, D.; Rodić, B.; Labus, A.
Title: Leveraging blockchain-based healthcare services with artificial intelligence
Publication Title: 2025 10th International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Technologies (SpliTech)
Abstract Note: Challenges in healthcare ecosystems related to data privacy and integrity, security, trust, optimization of processes, the need for more efficient logistics, etc., can be solved by integrating blockchain and artificial intelligence (AI) technologies. This paper analyses applications of blockchain and artificial intelligence in healthcare, with a focus on defining possible types and examples of integration of these technologies. The development of a model of a healthcare ecosystem based on blockchain and artificial intelligence technologies is presented. The proposed model outlines key healthcare stakeholders and their interactions within a secure, scalable, and efficient framework powered by emerging technologies. The focus is on the patients and the possibility of tracking all their medical data using a decentralized application as a personal healthcare record. The proposed model leverages blockchain to provide secure, transparent, and immutable transactions within a healthcare ecosystem, while AI-driven analytics improve operational efficiency, decision-making, and recommendations for healthcare services. Author: Manoj, N.; M, A.; Nandana, N.; Sankaran, S.
Title: Federated Learning-Based Secure Access Control and Anomaly Detection in IoMT Systems
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
Abstract Note: The rapid expansion of Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) systems has not only made healthcare delivery more efficient but has also introduced critical security and privacy threats. With IoMT devices communicating private data using APIs, traditional centralised security controls do not provide the requirements of privacy protection, regulatory needs, and alignment with new-generation threats. Thus, we propose a Federated Learning-based secure access control and anomaly detection framework for protecting IoMT APIs with Zero Trust principles and gradient boosting models in this paper. The framework works in two phases: an offline federated training phase across decentralised healthcare entities, and an online enforcement phase where the trained model is used in a Flask-based Zero Trust backend. Using the CIC-IoMT2024 dataset, our framework demonstrated strong results: XGBoost achieved 98% accuracy, 96% precision, 97% recall and 98% F1-score, outperforming CatBoost (95% accuracy, 96% precision, 94% recall, 93% F1-score) and LightGBM (87% accuracy, 85% precision, 87% recall, 86% F1-score). During deployment, the Flask backend handled API requests in real time with less than 300 ms average response time and 98% uptime, demonstrating scalability. Thus, the system not only assures robust anomaly detection but also imposes fine-grained access control while maintaining data authority and compliance with regulations.

Author: Shinde, S.; Virdee, B.; Khanna, A.; Dhakite, S.; Badlani, T.
Title: Intrusion Detection using Federated Learning with Application of Federated Dropout
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
Abstract Note: The massive proliferation of IoT devices in recent years creates new challenges in securing distributed systems, especially when it comes to intrusion detection and mitigation in real-time. Most traditional cloud-based intrusion detection approaches encounter issues ranging from increased latency to bandwidths and even centralized vulnerabilities. This paper introduces an innovative IDS framework based on federated learning (FL) combined with a novel federated dropout mechanism and edge computing. Federated dropout updates model parameters selectively during communication rounds, minimizing bandwidth usage considerably without compromising model performance. This work resolves key challenges such as communication overhead and encrypted traffic processing, opening the door to strong, real-time, and decentralized security solutions.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; IoT; Intrusion Detection; Edge Computing; Real-time Security

Author: Houichi, M.; Jaidi, F.; Bouhoula, A.
Title: Decentralized AI for Smart Cities: A Federated Learning Framework for Resilient Cybersecurity
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 9th Forum on Research and Technologies for Society and Industry (RTSI)
Abstract Note: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into cybersecurity has transformed the ability to detect, predict, and respond to cyber threats in real time. However, centralized AI systems often struggle with privacy concerns, data heterogeneity, and limited scalability—especially within smart city infrastructures that generate massive volumes of sensitive, distributed data. In this paper, we propose a federated learning-based cybersecurity framework tailored for smart cities, enabling collaborative anomaly detection across multiple urban nodes without sharing raw data. The framework leverages local AI models trained on edge devices to detect cyber-attacks while preserving data privacy. We simulate multiple attack scenarios using the CICIDS2017 dataset adapted for a smart city context and evaluate the system’s performance in terms of accuracy, communication cost, and robustness against adversarial perturbations. Results demonstrate that the proposed federated learning approach achieves comparable detection accuracy to centralized models while ensuring privacy preservation and improved scalability. This work highlights the potential of federated AI in creating resilient, ethical, and decentralized cybersecurity solutions for future smart cities.
Manual Tags: Federated Learning; Cybersecurity; Smart Cities; Edge Computing; Anomaly Detection; Privacy-Preserving AI

Author: Kumar, L.; Kumar, A.
Title: Securing Digital Twins in Autonomous Vehicles: Cyber Threats, Mitigation Strategies, and Innovative Security Solutions
Publication Title: 2025 Second International Conference on Cognitive Robotics and Intelligent Systems (ICC - ROBINS)
Abstract Note: Digital Twin (DT) technology in the Autonomous Vehicles (AVs) has revolutionized vehicle design, predictive maintenance, and real-time decision-making. For instance, by virtualizing physical assets, Digital Twins allow for optimization based on data, and learning in a simulation context. However, integration poses risks such as cyber-attacks in various forms: a data breach, sensor spoofing, adversarial attack, ransomware, and even model poisoning. These vulnerabilities would lead to the unauthorized access of systems, operational failure, and decision-making compromise, with a threat to the safety and reliability of the AV ecosystems. This review work provides a comprehensive analysis of the challenges in DT-enabled AVs from the cybersecurity standpoint, focusing on key attack surfaces such as cloud-based DT platforms, AI-driven analytics, and vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communications. In fact, it further advances cutting-edge mitigation strategies such as blockchain-based authentication, federated learning for secure model training, AI-driven intrusion detection, and quantumresistant cryptographic techniques.

Author: Reis, J. C. S. Manuel; Sousa, A.; Barbosa, A.; Reis, A.
Title: Security Challenges in IoT-enabled Green Mobility Systems
Publication Title: 2025 5th International Conference on Electrical, Computer, Communications and Mechatronics Engineering (ICECCME)
Abstract Note: The rise of green mobility solutions, such as electric vehicles (EVs), smart charging stations, and connected public transit systems, has been accompanied by increased reliance on Internet of Things (IoT) technologies. While these advancements support sustainable urban development, they also introduce cybersecurity risks. This paper explores key security challenges in IoT-enabled green mobility—such as attack vectors, vulnerabilities in vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication, and risks to EV charging infrastructure. We review existing frameworks and propose a multi-layered model integrating blockchain-based authentication, AI-driven intrusion detection, and lightweight cryptographic protocols for resource-constrained IoT devices. The framework ensures confidentiality, integrity, and availability while maintaining scalability and energy efficiency. Case studies and simulations demonstrate the feasibility of securing sustainable transportation systems.

Author: Anusiya, M.; Usha, A.
Title: A Hybrid Privacy-Aware Fuzzy Transportation Model for Analyzing Internet Addiction: Evidence of Instagram as the Most Addictive Platform
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent Computing, Information and Control Systems (ICOIICS)
Abstract Note: Internet addiction has become a growing concern in the digital era, with social media platforms intensifying compulsive online behavior. This study introduces a Hybrid Privacy-Aware Fuzzy Transportation Model (HPFTM) that integrates fuzzy set theory and federated learning to analyze Internet addiction while safeguarding user privacy. Using the Enhanced Advanced Vogel's Approximation Method (E-AVAM), the model achieves efficient, privacy-preserving optimization under uncertainty. Experimental results show that HPFTM improves detection accuracy, reduces computation time, and minimizes privacy leakage compared with traditional models. Across all analyses, Instagram consistently exhibits the highest addiction risk, surpassing Facebook and shortvideo platforms. The findings confirm that while Internet addiction spans multiple platforms, Instagram addiction emerges as its most severe and urgent form, offering valuable insights for policymakers, educators, and platform designers committed to digital well-being.

Author: Bhola, R.; Navaroj, G. I.; Gorkhe, M.; Sajiv, G.; Varimani, S. M.; Bala, B. K.
Title: SecureIoTGrid: A Blockchain-Enabled Cybersecurity Framework for Resilient IoT-Based Smart Energy Grids and E-Mobility Ecosystems
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
Abstract Note: The rapid digitalization of energy infrastructure through the integration of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has significantly improved the efficiency of smart energy grids and e-mobility systems. However, this advancement has also introduced complex cybersecurity challenges, as traditional intrusion detection systems (IDS) often suffer from limited scalability, delayed response, and inadequate data integrity mechanisms. Existing methods such as federated LSTM and hybrid CNN-RNN architectures exhibit moderate performance but fall short in real-time detection and secure incident handling. To address these limitations, this study proposes SecureIoTGrid a blockchain-enabled cybersecurity framework designed to detect and mitigate threats in IoT-based smart grid environments. The objective is to develop a decentralized, intelligent system capable of edge-level anomaly detection using LSTM autoencoders, combined with blockchain-based secure logging and smart contract-driven autonomous response. The novelty of this approach lies in its fusion of federated learning and distributed ledger technology to ensure data integrity, traceability, and rapid mitigation. Developed using Python, TensorFlow, Matplotlib, and Hyperledger Fabric, the framework was evaluated using a high-fidelity smart grid intrusion dataset. Experimental results demonstrate superior performance, achieving 97.4% accuracy, 95.2% precision, and \96.8 \textbackslash{}%\ recall, making SecureIoTGrid a reliable and scalable solution for securing future smart grids and e-mobility infrastructures.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; IoT Cybersecurity; Smart Grid Security; Anomaly Detection; LSTM Autoencoder

Author: Jegannathan, G. K.; Lalitha, P.; Thamaraiselvi, G.; Bachhav, M. Shivaji; Senniappan, V.; S, S.
Title: Retracted: Enhancing Cybersecurity in Healthcare Hybrid Cloud Systems with Federated Learning and Blockchain

Abstract Note: The incorporation of AI in healthcare has resulted in substantial progress in disease identification, treatment, and clinical decision-making. AI-driven solutions automate numerous operations and support healthcare workers; yet, their dependence on ML models has revealed significant cybersecurity weaknesses. This increasing reliance presents significant threats to patient safety and trust, rendering cybersecurity in healthcare an essential issue. This paper presents a Hybrid FL system aimed at improving cybersecurity in healthcare environments through secure, privacy-aware inference and learning. The methodology incorporates multiple preprocessing techniques, such as data purification, transformation, and normalisation, to enhance data quality, while ACO is utilised for effective feature extraction. Comprehensive empirical research assesses the suggested system’s capacity to maintain privacy and identify malicious behaviours in collaborative learning settings. The findings demonstrate that the Hybrid FL model surpasses conventional techniques, with an impressive accuracy of 98.52%, in addition to elevated recall and F-measure metrics. These results validate the model’s efficacy in safeguarding sensitive healthcare information. In summary, the suggested methodology enhances cybersecurity in healthcare, reinforces patient confidence in AI applications, and represents a substantial advancement in the creation of secure, privacy-preserving collaborative learning frameworks.

Author: Chaudhary, A. K.; Kurada, S. B.; Mogili, V. B.; Patel, R. B.; Nandan, D.
Title: Smart Healthcare Monitoring Through Federated IoT Networks and Privacy-Preserving Deep Learning
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICACT)
Abstract Note: This work describes a full federated learning-based smart healthcare monitoring concept using advanced deep learning, privacy-preserving methods, and distributed IoT data collecting. It addresses the demand for real-time, large-scale, secure health data processing employing wearable and ambient sensors. It uses a clear process that starts with strong data preparation and then extracts important features using convolutional and recurrent neural networks. Local embeddings are encrypted and transferred to a central server. The central server builds models using adaptive gradient descent, safe multiparty computation, and encryption. To be more versatile across data types and safeguard privacy through noise addition and gradient clipping, the method involves custom model improvements for each customer. We compared the suggested solution with centralized deep learning, ordinary federated learning, edge AI without encryption, and blockchain-enhanced learning. It had improved F 1 -score, precision, memory, specificity, and AUCROC. System-level tests indicated lower communication overhead, faster convergence, and higher energy efficiency. Privacy scores remained steady. These results indicate that the suggested framework can balance generalization, personalization, accuracy, efficiency, and real-time performance while maintaining strict privacy. This study prepares next-generation healthcare systems for privacy-sensitive and resource-constrained contexts using federated learning, edge AI, and secure computation. It also proposes expanding clinical and remote health tracking deployments.
Manual Tags: Federated learning; Blockchain; Secure aggregation; IoT devices; Deep learning; Privacy preservation; Smart healthcare; Edge AI; Healthcare monitoring; Personalized models

Author: Ali, S. M.; Tawdrous, M. Ibrahim; Alawadi, R.
Title: Anomaly Detection in Traffic Data Using Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Business Intelligence for Technology Innovation (ICBITI)
Abstract Note: As intelligent transportation systems become more prevalent, there is a growing need for reliable techniques for detecting anomalies in traffic data. This paper analyzes the utilization of federated learning (FL) for the purpose of detecting anomalies in traffic data with the distributed data of multiple edge devices while still securing privacy. The traditional ways of detecting anomalies have problems like the conservation of data privacy, high latency, and the savvy consumption of computation resources. However, federated learning solves these problems by letting models learn without the necessity for the data to switch hands. In this study, a new FL framework developed especially for traffic anomaly detection is reported, newest machine learning algorithms are incorporated to identify irregular patterns in traffic flow, congestion, and vehicle behavior. The experimental evaluations on established traffic datasets have shown the proposed method achieved high anomaly detection accuracy, data privacy was assured, and communication costs were cut. It has been demonstrated that federated learning can become a sustainable and secure technique for real-time traffic monitoring and management in smart cities.

Author: Raju, V. V. R.; I.Ranaveer; Alabdeli, H. M.; P.Selvaprasanth; Raghatate, K. S.; S, L. S.

Abstract Note: In low-resource settings, healthcare use and access are still very much limited by a lack of infrastructure, shortage of medical expertise, and medical connectivity. The proposed system consists of integrating lightweight CNN models best suited for mobile and edge devices for on-device medical image analysis which can decrease the dependency over the cloud-based processing. Through federated learning, improvement in the model is ensured without loss of privacy of patient data, and through a multi-modal diagnostic approach, which uses image, audio, and analysis based on symptoms, the accuracy is improved. The system is also based on efficient image compression and quantization techniques to enable real-time diagnosis in bandwidth-constrained environments. Also, for the safe and tamper-proof management of medical records, blockchain technology is added to the healthcare networks that can be decentralized regarding data integrity and compatibility with one another. It has been designed to work in off-grid environments powered by AI stations, solar powered enabling it to be sustainable to rural or underdeveloped regions. Diagnosis is also shown to be highly accurate, have low latency, and be adaptable for different medical conditions in experimental evaluation. Author: Gandhi, M. A.; Praveen, R.; Rambhatla, A. K.; Trakroo, K.; Kiran, V. L. S.; Bharathidasan, S.
Title: Blockchain—IoT—AI Model for Secure Supply Chain Management and Real-Time Agricultural Recommendations
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Emerging Trends in Computing and Communication (ETCOM)
Abstract Note: The developing richness of agricultural supply chains, together with issues in data quality, transparency, and predictive decision-making, demands substantial digital transformation. IoT devices collect soil, crop, and climatic data, which are pre-processed at the edge and verified by blockchain smart contracts to guarantee accuracy and reliability. AI models, enhanced by federated learning and feature extraction, produce accurate suggestions while safeguarding privacy. Author: Kavitha, R.; Rupa, M. S.; Gayathri, R.
Title: Federated Learning Based Explainable Hybrid Framework for Cyber Threat Analysis
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 7th International Conference on Computing, Communication and Automation (ICCCA)
Abstract Note: Traditional centralized security solutions are limited in their scalability, privacy, and responsiveness due to the increasing size and decentralization of contemporary networks. In order to combine supervised classification and unsupervised anomaly detection in a privacy-preserving federated learning (FL) environment, this paper suggests a Federated Explainable Hybrid Framework for Anomaly and Threat Detection. Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks are used to model temporal dependencies and changing attack patterns in network flows, while Variational Autoencoders (VAE) are used to capture richer latent representations of typical traffic behavior. XGBoost is used to classify anomalies. We use selective parameter sharing and compressed model updates to minimize communication overhead, which makes the method appropriate for IoT devices with limited resources. We use SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) to highlight the most important traffic features in anomaly decisions at the local and federated levels in order to increase transparency and analyst trust. The suggested framework achieves high detection accuracy, lowers false positives, and lowers communication costs, according to experimental evaluation on the CIC-IDS2018 and HIKARI2021 datasets across multiple virtual IoT clients. For IoT, healthcare, and smart infrastructure settings, this architecture provides a scalable, interpretable, and communication-efficient security solution.
Manual Tags: Federated Learning; Cybersecurity; Privacy Preservation; Explainable AI; Anomaly Detection; Intrusion Detection System; Threat Detection; Variational Autoencoders; Long Short-Term Memory

Abstract Note: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Blockchain have been game-changing technologies for the last few years in several industries. The decentralized nature and immutable ledger of blockchain could prove to be ideal solutions for many of these problems. In this context, this paper proposes a Blockchain-based method to facilitate secure, transparent, and efficient data sharing to optimize AI algorithms for precise Big Data analysis. The proposed approach improves data security by utilizing the unique features of Blockchain (immutability, transparency, and consensus mechanisms), thus maintaining the integrity and trust of AI-driven processes. In this paper, describes the integration framework, discuss the main advantages and compare the performance of AI with and without Blockchain integrated. When Blockchain technology is employed for data sharing and processing, the experimental results show better protection, more transparency, and superior performance of AI models. The analysis emphasizes on the most promising area of Blockchain-AI coupling impact from this study which is to help reshape domains with extreme necessities of data integrity and demand secure collaborative environments like healthcare, finance and supply chain management.

Author: Nourmohammadi, R.; Zhang, K.
Title: SoK: The Role of Zero-Knowledge Proofs in Building Confidential and Trustworthy AI
Publication Title: 2025 7th International Conference on Blockchain Computing and Applications (BCCA)
Abstract Note: The verifiability of machine learning models and the privacy of training data have become critical concerns due to their widespread deployment in sensitive applications. Ensuring that a model performs as claimed, without revealing private data or algorithms, is a significant challenge. Zero-Knowledge Proof systems (ZKPs) have emerged as a promising cryptographic solution, enabling the verification of statements without disclosing underlying information. Their integration with blockchain technology further enhances trust and decentralization, offering robust solutions for secure and transparent AI systems. This paper explores the use of ZKPs in machine learning, focusing on privacy-preservation techniques, model verifiability, and confidential AI. It compares the differences and challenges of employing ZKPs in machine learning versus blockchains, highlighting their unique requirements and overlapping benefits. We review the basic concepts of ZKPs, advances such as zkSNARKs and zk-STARKs, and their applications in blockchainbased AI frameworks to ensure data integrity, immutability, and scalability. Furthermore, the paper delves into the practical implications of using ZKPs in AI, providing case studies and analyzing their scalability, performance, and limitations. We conclude by identifying key challenges and presenting future research directions to extend the applicability of ZKPs in AI, particularly in federated learning, model fairness, and decentralized AI pipelines.
Manual Tags: Federated Learning; Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning; Zero-Knowledge Proofs; Trustworthy AI; Blockchain Technology; Confidential AI; Secure AI Systems; Transparent AI

Title: Privacy-by-design GEN-RWD Sandbox for Distributed Multicentric Data Analysis in Healthcare: The Proxy Module

Abstract Note: Modern data analysis techniques are transforming the healthcare landscape from both research and operational perspectives. Applying statistical analysis, machine learning, data science, and process mining to large databases enables data analysts and clinicians to enhance the quality and precision of their research and care efforts. Author: Mao, M.; Zhu, X.; Chen, J.; Zhang, L.; Liao, G.; Diao, Z.
Title: SCAMA: A Smart-Contract-Driven Asynchronous Model Aggregation Framework for Decentralized Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 11th International Conference on High Performance and Smart Computing (HPSC)
Abstract Note: Due to the absence of a trusted model parameter sharing mechanism, model tampering, malicious uploads, and data inconsistency pose significant risks within the Federated Learning (FL) architecture. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an automated Smart Contract-based Asynchronous Model Aggregation (SCAMA) method to enhance model security in decentralized FL frameworks. We design a trigger-based asynchronous model submission mechanism driven by smart contracts. These contracts incorporate a dynamic adjustment strategy that can initiate global aggregation in real time. Furthermore, a decentralized parameter validity verification rule is embedded within the smart contract to ensure that submitted model updates align with the global optimization objective, thereby mitigating risks such as malicious uploads and training drift. Building upon this, we introduce a trustless model parameter-sharing strategy based on on-chain storage. The global model update process is encoded into the smart contract and executed through multiparty verifiable storage on a distributed ledger. During model aggregation, the smart contract utilizes encrypted hashing to verify the consistency of submitted models, ensuring that the parameter versions received by each node are traceable, reliable, and tamper-proof. Experimental results demonstrate that our method offers significant improvements in computational efficiency and model convergence speed compared with traditional synchronous FL approaches and existing asynchronous strategies.
Manual Tags: blockchain; decentralized federated learning; smart contract; Asynchronous model aggregation; trustless model parameter-sharing

Author: Li, J.; Ma, W.; Zhao, C.; Zhao, K.; Chen, J.; Chen, Z.
Title: REDFL: Robust and Efficient Decentralized Federated Learning Based on Committee Consensus
Publication Title: ICC 2025 - IEEE International Conference on Communications
Abstract Note: Federated learning (FL) enables multiple clients to collaboratively train a global model without disclosing their original data. However, traditional FL is susceptible to attacks from malicious clients who can disrupt the training process by uploading poisoned models to the server. In this paper, we introduce REDFL, a robust and efficient decentralized federated learning framework that employs committee consensus to effectively defend against poisoning attacks. Our framework not only enhances security but also improves the performance of the global model. In REDFL, we propose a dual model validation algorithm based on mutual information for precise validation of model updates. To evaluate the contributions made by clients to the global model, we develop a contribution calculation method that accounts for the varying roles of clients. Our proof of contribution mechanism enables a more accurate selection of honest clients as committee members. The committee validates the model updates from trainers, reaches a consensus on these updates, and ultimately aggregates a high-quality global model. Experimental results demonstrate that REDFL outperforms other Byzantine-tolerant algorithms in terms of global model accuracy and convergence speed. On the Non-IID dataset under a poisoning attack scenario, REDFL achieves an accuracy of 80%, showcasing its robustness and effectiveness.

Author: Lu, X.; Cao, Y.
Title: Adaptive Neuron Honeypot: Trapping Malicious Backdoors in Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 24th International Conference on Trust, Security and Privacy in Computing and Communications (TrustCom)
Abstract Note: Federated learning allows multiple clients to locally train on private datasets, followed by the central server aggregating these parameters to form a global model. This process maintains the privacy of client data while enabling the global model to learn from diverse data distributions, thus enhancing its generalization capability. However, it cannot be ensured that all clients participating in the federated aggregation process are fully trustworthy. Some clients might maliciously alter the parameters they upload to the central server, embedding backdoors into the global model. This causes the model to behave in ways dictated by attackers for specific inputs. Existing backdoor defense mechanisms primarily operate on the central server side, attempting to eliminate malicious clients by analyzing parameter characteristics or behaviors, or by pruning or distilling the aggregated model. In this paper, we first reveal the impact of backdoor attacks on neural networks at the neuron level and analyze the parameter changes during backdoor training from the attacker’s perspective. Building on this analysis, we propose a neural network honeypot mechanism. This approach initially uses parameter perturbation and masking for adversarial training to identify fundamental malicious neurons. These neurons are then processed to lure attackers into traps, thereby enhancing the accuracy of malicious neuron identification. We conducted extensive experiments under different adversarial settings and assumptions, demonstrating that our backdoor defense approach consistently surpasses current state-of-the-art baseline methods.
Manual Tags: Federated Learning; Distributed Learning; Backdoor Attack; Neural Network honeypot

Author: Qureshi, M. A.; Aurangzaib; Asghar, A.; Hassan, T.
Title: Blockchain based Anomaly Detection System using CNN
Publication Title: 2025 6th International Conference on Innovative Computing (ICIC)
Abstract Note: The detection of anomalies is a foundational component of modern security and risk management systems. Traditional anomaly detection approaches lack built-in mechanisms for data privacy and accountability. This paper presents a privacy-protected anomaly detection system that combines Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) with blockchain technology to ensure secure and trustworthy surveillance monitoring. The system identifies unusual or suspicious activities in video frames, using data from the UCSD Pedestrian Dataset. To protect privacy, the video frames are encrypted using AES-128. The CNN is trained to accurately classify each encrypted frame as either normal or anomalous. After classification, the results, along with the hash of the encrypted frame and the timestamp, are stored on a private Ethereum blockchain using smart contracts. This step ensures that the results are not only secure but also cannot be altered which provides traceability and transparency. The proposed system achieved over 92% accuracy and an AUC score of 0.91. It also showed low latency and acceptable performance for real-time use. The blockchain component added minimal overhead while ensuring data security and auditability. Lastly, this research offering a solution that combines artificial intelligence with secure data handling. The system is especially useful for applications in smart surveillance, healthcare monitoring, and critical infrastructure, where both accuracy and data privacy are essential.

Author: Udurume, M.; Ahakonye, L. A. Chijioke; Lee, J. Min; Kim, D.-S.
Title: Scalable and Efficient PureChain-Based Federated Learning for Intelligent Transportation Systems
Publication Title: 2025 16th International Conference on Information and Communication Technology Convergence (ICTC)
Abstract Note: Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) increasingly leverage edge intelligence for real-time, privacy-preserving, and safety-critical decision-making. However, conventional Federated Learning (FL) frameworks face challenges such as unverifiable updates, central points of failure, and limited scalability. To overcome these issues, we propose PureChain, a scalable FL framework integrated with a permissioned blockchain to enable secure, auditable, and decentralized learning across connected vehicles and road infrastructure. Smart contracts and blockchain validation ensure traceability and integrity of model updates. We simulated the system using three benchmark datasets (BurST-ADMA, Veremi, CICIoV2024), analyzing how variations in client participation and training rounds influence training efficiency and convergence behavior. The results showed a strong linear relationship between the number of clients and sample volume. Extended training improves convergence stability, even in dynamic environments. These findings affirm PureChain’s suitability for Software-Defined ITS (SD-ITS), offering both architectural resilience and practical insights for optimizing training configurations in real-world vehicular networks.

Author: Suneetha, B.; Kesavan, R.

Abstract Note: The rising adoption of cloud computing has transformed data processing and storage, but it has also posed substantial cybersecurity threats as a result of changing attack patterns and issues of privacy. Conventional threat detection solutions are dependent on centralized architectures that sacrifice data privacy and are not effective in dealing with high false positive rates. The current federated learning and privacy-preserving approaches encounter issues with handling non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data distributions and adversarial attacks which hinders their performance in realistic cloud security deployments. Author: M, S.; P, S.

Abstract Note: Urban flood is a serious threat to facilities, life and economic development hence requires fast and efficient classification system for rescue missions. Author: Shreya, M.; Chitra, R.; Brindha, D.
Title: Enhancing Additive Manufacturing Security: A Novel Approach using Zero Trust, Blockchain, and AI-Powered Watermarking
Publication Title: 2025 6th International Conference on Smart Electronics and Communication (ICOSEC)
Abstract Note: Additive Manufacturing (AM), commonly referred to as 3D printing, is a groundbreaking technology revolutionizing industrial manufacturing by enabling instant prototyping, on-demand production, and intricate geometries. The increasing interconnectedness and application of digital instructions in AM systems, however, make them vulnerable to a myriad of cybersecurity attacks such as unauthorized access, data tampering, intellectual property (IP) theft, and sabotage. The existing security measures are unable to address these issues in an all-encompassing manner. This paper presents an innovative, multi-layered cybersecurity model for improving the security of the AM process end to end. The new approach employs Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA) for strict user authentication and access control, AI-driven G-code watermarking through deep-learning-based steganography for ensuring data integrity and protection against malicious tampering, Federated Learning (FL) to enable threat intelligence sharing across decentralized systems without compromising data privacy, and Blockchain technology for tamper-evident storage and enhanced authentication. Integrating these technologies, the proposed system offers a robust defense mechanism against advanced cyber-attacks for AM systems while ensuring security without compromising scalability, efficiency, or performance. This paper presents the proposed system's architecture and demonstrates its effectiveness through a simulated deployment.

Author: Queiroz, M. P. C. M.; Morales, A. S.; Berretta, L. de Oliveira; Filho, A. G.; Sene, I.
Title: Artificial Intelligence and Blockchain in the Metaverse
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE Latin Conference on IoT (LCIoT)
Abstract Note: The Metaverse emerges as a completely virtual reality offering diverse possibilities through the immersive use of technology. Author: Liu, X.; Li, L.; Liu, D.; Wang, R.; Su, B.; Xu, S.
Title: Federated Matching Learning for Privacy-Preserving and Robust Task Allocation in Industrial Control System Crowdsourced Testing
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
Abstract Note: Industrial Control Systems (ICS) security is of critical importance to modern infrastructure. This paper proposes a novel Federated Matching Learning (FML) framework for privacy-preserving task allocation in ICS crowdsourced testing. Our method consists of three key components: (1) a FML module that employs knowledge graph-enhanced representations to estimate tasktester affinity without centralizing sensitive data; (2) a hybrid metaheuristic scheduling algorithm that efficiently solves the multi-objective allocation problem on reduced candidate graphs; and (3) a dynamic reputation and adversary detection subsystem that ensures system robustness against malicious participants. The proposed framework provides a comprehensive solution for secure, efficient, and reliable crowdsourced testing in ICS.

Author: Ye, L.; Xiong, Z.; Luo, J.; Gao, L.
Title: LBFL: Lightweight Blockchain-Enabled Federated Learning via DPoS Consensus
Publication Title: ICC 2025 - IEEE International Conference on Communications
Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) is an innovative learning paradigm that allows multiple devices to collaboratively train a shared model without uploading the raw data to the cloud, thereby enhancing privacy and security. Leveraging Mobile Edge Computing (MEC), Hierarchical Federated Learning (HFL) can further reduce the communication overhead, thereby increasing the efficiency and scalability of FL systems by enabling model aggregation at the network edge. However, this framework often encounters security challenges, such as single points of failure and the risk of malicious model tampering. To address these challenges, researches have employed blockchain technology to enhance the security of FL systems, but most of these solutions incur significant resource burdens due to the intensive computation demands of blockchain consensus mechanisms, such as Proof-of-Work (PoW). In this work, we aim to explore a lightweight blockchain-enabled federated learning (LBFL) framework that utilizes the Delegated Proof-of-Stake (DPoS) consensus mechanism, which employs a simple voting process to elect a small number of candidate block producers (known as delegates) to aggregate the FL model and produce blocks. This framework significantly reduces the number of consensus nodes, thereby minimizing resource consumption during the consensus process. We study the joint optimization of mobile device association, bandwidth allocation, computing frequency management, and block producer selection, aiming to minimize the overall delay and energy consumption. To address the challenges posed by discrete and continuous decision variables, we decompose the problem into three sequential subproblems and solve them iteratively. Simulation results show that compared with the existing benchmarks, the proposed scheme can reduce overall delay and energy consumption by 15% to 22%.

Author: Swain, R. R.; Grace, J.; Chandna, M.; Sharma, D.; Mahato, N.; Venkadeshwaran, K.

It integrates ZTA and distributed fraud detection poly systems and principles of ZTA to optimally detect and prevent fraud. Using federated learning and encapsulated with reinforcement learning, AAD-FRL can conduct real-time, and lac data fraud detection and prevention across different financial systems without compromising user privacy. AADFRL, when operating within a ZTA paradigm, amplifies the Zero Trust principles of the banking security, strengthens proactive, real-time fraud detection and prevention systems, increases anomaly detection, and misclassification detection, and reframes the security architecture of the systems. The proposed AAD-FRL method accomplished a detection accuracy of 95%, a false positive rate of 3%, a false negative rate of 4%, and an average response time of 70 milliseconds, reflecting excellent real-time performance in fraud detection.

Author: Amari, H.; Houda, Z. A. El; Moudoud, H.; Khoukhi, L.; Belguith, L. H.
Title: Blockchain-Based Federated Learning for Enhanced Cyber-Threats Detection in Connected Vehicles
Publication Title: ICC 2025 - IEEE International Conference on Communications
Abstract Note: Over the past few years, there have been made significant strides in advancing the Internet of Vehicles (IoV), recognizing its strategic importance in Intelligent Transport Systems. The proliferation of connected and autonomous vehicles on the roads has propelled the IoV into the spotlight. However, addressing the specific demands of vehicular networks, such as low latency, high mobility, extensive connectivity of 5G/6G networks, and robust security, remains a substantial challenge. Therefore, there is a critical need for substantial progress in implementing a resilient Intrusion Detection System within the IoV ecosystem. This paper introduces VFed-IDS, a decentralized, secure, flexible, scalable, and robust Blockchain and Federated Learning-based intrusion detection system. VFed-IDS is designed to identify cyber threats in the IoV while preserving privacy in connected vehicles. The proposed architecture consists of three main layers: the central layer, the local layer, and the Blockchain layer. The central layer includes the SDN Controller, responsible for training and aggregating the global model. The local layer comprises vehicles training individual models based on their private local datasets. The Blockchain layer introduces the Smart Contract VFed-SC, which manages the list of authenticated and collaborating vehicles in the Federated Learning process. It also hashes trained local model updates before transmitting them as transactions between the central and local layers. Simulation results demonstrate that VFed-IDS achieves a high accuracy rate of 99%, effectively enhancing the autonomous behavior of connected vehicles against cyber threats.

Author: Nandhini, D.; Brindha, M.

This method matches test accuracy while lowering communication rounds by 40% and total communication volume by 45% when compared to a baseline FedAvg setup with 30 clients. The findings show that moderate cluster reduction is possible without sacrificing performance when algorithmic regularization and adaptive resource scaling are combined.

Author: Tran, T.-D.; Tran, N.-H.; Vu, H.-M.; Pham, V.-H.

Author: Gupta, S.; Sayeed, M. A.

Publication Title: 2025 3rd International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Blockchain, and Internet of Things (AIBThings)
Abstract Note: Epileptic seizures, triggered by irregular electrical activity in the brain, pose serious health challenges for millions worldwide. This work presents a secure, real-time seizure detection framework driven by artificial intelligence (AI) utilizing machine learning algorithms and homomorphic encryption (HE). Author: Parmar, P. K.; Prajapati, R. T.
Title: Federated and Homomorphic Encryption-Enabled Lightweight Cryptography for Secure IoT Environments
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Innovations and Emerging Technologies In AI & Communication Systems (IETACS)
Abstract Note: The rapid growth of Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystems in domains such as healthcare, transportation, industrial automation, and smart cities has created an urgent need for secure, efficient, and privacy-preserving communication methods. This paper presents a hybrid security framework that integrates Federated Learning (FL), Homomorphic Encryption (HE), and Lightweight Cryptography (LWC) into a unified pipeline for privacy-preserving IoT environments. Author: Anupkant, S.; Kanaparthi, S.; Cheruku, S.; Adudhodla, M.; Prasad, C. G. V. N.; Manellore, P. K. R.
Title: Design and Implementation of a Blockchain-Enabled Microgrid Monitoring System for Remote Energy Management
Publication Title: 2025 10th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
Abstract Note: The increasing demand for sustainable and decentralized energy solutions in remote and underserved areas has accelerated the adoption of microgrids. However, traditional monitoring systems often face challenges such as data integrity, security vulnerabilities, and restricted accessibility. This study presents the design and implementation of a blockchain-enabled microgrid monitoring system that overcomes these limitations through a secure, transparent, and decentralized framework. The proposed system integrates IoT-based sensors for real-time data acquisition, edge computing for localized analysis, and a private blockchain to ensure immutable data storage and trusted energy transactions. Smart contracts govern automated energy distribution and enforce operational policies among stakeholders. A prototype implementation highlights the system's capability to enhance monitoring reliability, reduce latency, and build trust in energy management. The results demonstrate the architecture's viability for deployment in rural communities, isolated industries, and post-disaster recovery environments.
