Author: Musam, V. S.; Musham, N. K.; Siva, C.; Basha, S. K.; Mekala, R.; Nagendran, R.
Title: Privacy-Preserving Healthcare Monitoring using Multi-Authority Attribute-based Encryption and Zero-Knowledge Proofs
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Communication Networks and Application (ICSCN)
Abstract Note: The field of healthcare monitoring has been revolutionized by a combination of cloud computing and IoT-enabled sensor networks that enable real-time data collection, storage and processing. However, because healthcare data is sensitive, strong security and privacy-preserving measures are required to stop unwanted access and preserve data integrity in multi-authority settings. To propose a collaborative and privacy-preserving sensor cloud architecture for safe, scalable, and fine-grained access control for healthcare monitoring systems by utilizing Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKP) and Multi-Authority Attribute-Based Encryption (MA-ABE). The proposed method combines ZKP for authentication and MA-ABE for attribute-based encryption to protect sensitive data. It uses gateways to securely aggregate and transmit data to the cloud, and elliptic curve cryptography to optimize performance. The framework decreased computational overhead by 40% while achieving notable gains in encryption (120 ms) and decryption (150 ms). Outperforming current approaches in healthcare data security and access management, classification accuracy reached 96.5% with improved privacy preservation (96%) and scalability (94%). The suggested system addresses privacy, scalability, and computational efficiency while incorporating cutting-edge cryptographic approaches to provide secure healthcare monitoring. Large-scale, real-time healthcare applications can benefit greatly from its strong solution.
Manual Tags: IoT; Privacy Preservation; Zero-Knowledge Proofs; Data Security; Cloud Computing; Healthcare monitoring; Multi-Authority Attribute-Based Encryption

Author: Sundaram, V. M. K.
Title: Distributed AI/ML Models (Detecting Network Attacks with Distributed AI using TriBoostFedHyFedX Model)
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain and Distributed Systems Security (ICBDS)
Abstract Note: Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) are vital for identifying and mitigating malicious activities within increasingly complex and distributed network environments. Conventional centralized IDS architectures often face limitations related to data privacy, high communication overhead, and susceptibility to single points of failure. To overcome these challenges, this paper introduces TriBoostFed-HyFedX, a privacy-preserving federated learning framework tailored for intrusion detection in decentralized systems. TriBoost-Fed employs an ensemble of three powerful classifiers XGBoost, LightGBM, and Random Forest (RF) executed locally at each client node. This local ensemble architecture enhances detection robustness and accuracy by leveraging classifier diversity. Complementing this, HyFedX is a hybrid aggregation mechanism that adaptively combines FedAvg and FedProx, utilizing Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence to assign dynamic weights to client updates based on model alignment. This ensures stable convergence and improved performance under non-IID data conditions. Experimental evaluation demonstrates that the proposed method outperforms baseline models across multiple metrics including accuracy, precision, recall, and ROC-AUC, while preserving data confidentiality. The proposed system offers a scalable, secure, and adaptive solution suitable for deployment in edge, IoT, and cloud-integrated infrastructures.
Manual Tags: Federated Learning; Privacy Preservation; Intrusion Detection System (IDS); Ensemble learning; LightGBM

Author: Kissiouer, I. Ben; Ouissem, S.-A.; Maissa, B.; Bouarfa, H.; Ouchani, S.
Title: Securing Digital Twin System Using Blockchain: Application on Smart Home
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent Computer Systems, Data Science and Applications (IC2SDA)
Abstract Note: Digital twins (DTs) offer a virtual representation of physical entities, enabling advanced monitoring, control, and predictive analysis, particularly in Internet of Things (IoT) environments. However, the integration of DTs in smart homes raises significant security and privacy concerns due to the volume of sensitive data generated and exchanged. This paper proposes a secure architecture for smart home DTs using blockchain technology and homomorphic encryption (HE). Blockchain ensures data integrity and access control through its decentralized and immutable nature, while HE enables computations on encrypted data without decryption, preserving confidentiality. This approach enhances the security and privacy of smart home DTs, contributing to safer and more resilient smart environments.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; Security; Privacy; Access Control; IoT; Homomorphic Encryption; Digital Twin; Smart Home

Author: Kasu, V. R.; Deepalakshmi, P.
Title: Equipment Security for Internet of Things: Defending IoT Devices in Exposure-Risk Edge Computing Settings using Artificial Intelligence and Cryptographic Protocols
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Smart & Sustainable Technology (INCSST)
Abstract Note: The Internet of Things (IoT) is expanding at an unprecedented rate, bringing new and serious security threats, especially in exposure-risk edge computing environments with devices working in spread and sometimes bad conditions. The resource-constrained nature of IoT devices and the growing complexity of cyber-attacks make it difficult for existing security mechanisms to offer effective protection. The proposed approach focuses on enhancing the security of equipment in IoT systems in edge computing environments through the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and cryptographic protocols. AI-based anomaly detection, machine learning-based intrusion prevention, and adaptive authentication mechanisms are utilized to identify and mitigate security threats in realtime. The combination of cryptographic methods such as lightweight encryption, secure key management, and blockchain-based authentication guarantees data integrity, confidentiality, and secure communication between IoT devices. This research shows that by integrating AI with cryptographic protocols, it provides a multi-layered approach to ensure security against threats like unauthorized access, man-in-the-middle attacks, data tampering, and DDoS (distributed denial-of-service) attacks. With continuously analyzing network traffic, device behavior, and historic attack patterns, AI algorithms improves threat detection accuracy and allows for pro-active measures against upcoming security threats. Post-quantum cryptographic algorithms implementation adds another layer of future-proofing against upcoming cryptographic attacks. Furthermore, decentralized, secure authentication is addressed by employing federated learning and edge-based AI solutions to mitigate latencies and computational overheads. The experimental results show that the introduced hybrid model: AI-cryptography for DDoS detection methods, has a better performance in terms of detection accuracy, false positive rate, data security and energy consumption for IoT devices. This research has made a notable contribution to the field of IoT security by the development of a scalable, intelligent and cryptographically secure defense mechanism for protecting the IoT devices in exposure risk edge computing environments. Overall, the results emphasize the promise of AI and cryptographic integration toward a robust IoT ecosystem, leading to the implementation of secure and smart IoT infrastructures.
Manual Tags: Federated Learning; Post-Quantum Cryptography; Anomaly Detection; Cryptographic Protocols; Cyber Threats; Intrusion Prevention; Lightweight Encryption; Secure Authentication

Author: Ding, W.; Liu, Y.; Wang, Z.; Chu, Z.
Title: MPFL: A Decentralised Federated Learning Framework Based on Multi-Population Genetic Algorithm
Publication Title: ICASSP 2025 - 2025 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP)
Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative training while protecting the privacy of participant data. However, typical centralized FL structures are vulnerable to malicious client attacks. To mitigate such vulnerabilities, blockchain technology has been used to develop a decentralized FL framework. Yet, this approach leads to significant transmission and computation overhead. In order to improve robustness as well as efficiency, we propose Multi-Population Federated Learning (MPFL), which optimizes blockchain-based federated learning by incorporating operators of multi-population genetic algorithm (MPGA), such as selection, crossover, mutation and migration. Moreover, we introduce a committee consensus mechanism tailored to MPFL, where honest clients are elected to govern each population, thereby facilitating intraspecific and interspecific competition. Our experiments demonstrate that MPFL outperforms various aggregation algorithms in achieving superior robustness, and it reduces the costs of transmission and computation compared to the blockchain-based FL framework.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; Federated Learning; Genetic Algorithm; Committee Mechanism

Author: Chinnaiah, M.; Gupta, A.; Srivastava, S.; Ghimire, A.
Title: Zero-Knowledge AI: Privacy-First ML Inference in Distributed Ecosystems
Publication Title: 2025 5th International Conference on Emerging Research in Electronics, Computer Science and Technology (ICERECT)
Abstract Note: At a time when data privacy laws and cyber-attacks are on the rise, Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) hold the potential of a transformational paradigm of safe (privacy-preserving) machine learning (ML) inferences. In this paper, we present a new architecture that facilitates Zero-Knowledge AI, in which sensitive data inputs and internal model parameters remain unknown during the model inference procedure across distributed ecosystems. The proposed framework can help preserve privacy standards like GDPR and HIPAA, inference accuracies, and scalability of these inferences by utilising mechanisms to observe cryptographic zero-knowledge protocols, as well as federated learning protocols. We describe the construction of ZK-friendly models to apply to neural inference pipelines, efficient zk-SNARK-based model validation, decentralized trusting schemes, and privacy-respecting model auditing. Testing over a variety of healthcare and financial datasets indicates that our Zero-Knowledge AI solution results in high privacy guarantees with limited throughput losses. The work provides a strong basis on how to implement trusted and privacy-first AI systems in the real life and distributed operating environment.
Manual Tags: Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning; Zero-Knowledge Proofs; zk-SNARKs; Distributed AI; Cryptographic AI Security; Federated Inference

Author: Devarajulu, V. S.
Title: LLM Deployment in Regulated Enterprise AI Systems: A Privacy-Preserving and Compliant Architectural Approach
Publication Title: 2025 3rd International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Blockchain, and Internet of Things (AIBThings)
Abstract Note: Large Language Models (LLMs) are being increasingly adopted by enterprises due to their impressive natural language processing capabilities. However, their deployment in regulated industries such as finance, healthcare, and legal systems raises critical concerns regarding data privacy, regulatory compliance, and security control. To ensure the safe and compliant integration of LLMs into enterprise AI workflows while maintaining regulatory adherence, this paper introduces a comprehensive privacy-preserving framework designed to meet HIPAA, GDPR, and PCI DSS requirements in enterprise environments. The proposed modular architecture incorporates input sanitization, compliance policy enforcement, role-based access controls, secure data flows, and comprehensive audit logging to ensure LLM deployment remains both compliant and secure. We evaluated the framework through a financial services chatbot case study using synthetic data and demonstrated significant risk reduction without compromising standard LLM functionality. The results show this architecture reduces data leakage by 85% while maintaining full regulatory compliance and auditability. The 85% data leakage reduction was measured through controlled testing with 10,000 synthetic prompts containing known PII patterns, comparing direct API calls versus our sanitized approach across SSN, credit card, phone number, and email detection scenarios.
Manual Tags: GDPR; HIPAA; Large Language Models; Privacy-Preserving AI; Regulatory Compliance; Enterprise Architecture; PCI-DSS

Author: Jasmin, M.; Vij, P.; Anjaneyulu, M.; Jasim, L. H.; Gopinath, S.; Zahraa, F. A. Abd Al; Alhayaly, O. U.
Title: Automated Theorem Proving Algorithm for Verifying Security Protocols in Communication Networks
Publication Title: 2025 3rd International Conference on Cyber Resilience (ICCR)
Abstract Note: Communication protocol security is becoming more important in today's interconnected society because of the increasing sophistication of hacking methods to compromise data privacy, authenticity, and integrity. Complex protocol systems are unsuitable for conventional verification methods due to their dependence on human judgment and scalability issues. Our paper presents PROTOSEC-ATP, a novel automated theorem-proving algorithm based on verifying communication network protocols. With symbolic model checking and first-order logic inference, PROTOSEC-ATP automates reasoning and extracts authentication and secrecy from protocol specifications. The method builds logical models of protocol operations and confirms that they meet security restrictions using resolution-based proving. PROTOSEC-ATP finds small logical mistakes in well-known, obscure protocols like Needham-Schroeder and Kerberos. Our approach verifies faster and more accurately than previous methods. Automation, scalability, and reliability underpin PROTOSEC-ATP's communication protocol security. Network protocol assurance is automated and reliable using this solution.
Manual Tags: Network Security; Automated Theorem Proving(ATP); First-Order Logic; Protocol Authentication; Security Protocol Verification

Author: Modi, T.; Jariwala, P. R.
Title: A Systematic Review of Automated Anti-Money Laundering (AML) Integration in Permissioned Blockchain Systems
Publication Title: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advances in Computation, Communication and Information Technology (ICAICCIT)
Abstract Note: Money laundering poses a persistent global threat, undermining both financial stability and the sound operation of economic systems. One of the central obstacles in advancing Anti-Money Laundering (AML) methods is balancing strict data confidentiality with the necessity of analyzing large, interconnected financial transaction networks. This paper introduces the first comparative assessment of centralized Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and privacypreserving Federated Learning (FL)-based GNNs for AML detection, evaluated on the SAML dataset. Our study contrasts the performance of federated GNNs with centralized counterparts and with traditional baselines, including rulebased models, random forests, and autoencoders. Results indicate that federated GNNs deliver strong detection accuracy while safeguarding sensitive information, though with tradeoffs involving efficiency, scalability, and regulatory alignment. These outcomes provide a foundation for designing future AML frameworks that balance predictive effectiveness with privacy preservation. Additionally, the study shows how collaborative analytics and immutable auditability can coexist with compliance constraints by integrating these architectures into permissioned blockchain environments like Hyperledger Fabric. The integration of AI-driven, privacy-conscious AML solutions into regulated financial ecosystems is made possible by this work, which bridges the gap between automation, interpretability, and practical implementation.

Author: Nazerath, P.; Uppoor, P.; Laxman, B. P.; Nayak, S. M.; Jagadeesha, S. G.
Title: Blockchain in Disaster Management: A Systematic Review of Emerging Frameworks, Applications, and Future Directions
Publication Title: 2025 4th International Conference on Innovative Mechanisms for Industry Applications (ICIMIA)
Abstract Note: Blockchain technology has been identified as a potential facilitator of increased transparency, trust, and coordination in different stages of disaster management. The current systematic review integrates latest developments on blockchain-based systems for disaster preparedness, response, recovery, and mitigation. Based on insights gleaned from ten peer-reviewed papers, this paper analyzes frameworks like UAV swarm coordination, vehicular forensics, intelligent public safety microservices, emergency service dispatch systems, and knowledge management models. These systems tap into the primary blockchain characteristics such as smart contracts, decentralized architectures, IoT integration, edge computing, and consensus protocols like DPoS-PBFT to secure data integrity, protected communication, and automatic decision-making. The review demonstrates how blockchain enhances stakeholder cooperation, auditability, and operational effectiveness during disasters considerably. This review also presents opportunities for leveraging blockchain with AI, augmented reality, and federated learning towards developing more robust and smart disaster relief systems.

Author: Mukisa, K. J.; Ahakonye, L. A. C.; Lee, J. M.; Kim, D.-S.
Title: Synergistic Smart Grid: Instability and Fault Detection Using Blockchain and Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2025 Sixteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
Abstract Note: Smart grids have revolutionized energy management by integrating IoT, allowing real-time monitoring and optimization. However, this connectivity also increases vulnerability to cyber threats. We propose an innovative solution that combines federated learning with a customized IoT-PureChain network to enhance fault detection and grid stability. Utilizing a hybrid model with LSTM and dense layers tailored for decentralized IoT data, our approach leverages two key datasets for fault simulation and stability analysis. We address non-IID data challenges by employing a trimmed mean aggregation, enhancing robustness and accuracy. Our blockchain, designed for IoT, uses a Proof-of-Authority with Association consensus and adaptive mining for high-efficiency, gas-free transactions. This research demonstrates a scalable, secure, privacy-focused system and paves the way for further exploration in IoT blockchain synergy and advanced federated learning.

Author: Abreu, R.; Sousa, A.; Correia, L.; Reis, A.; Serôdio, C.; Branco, F.; Reis, M. J. C. S.
Title: A Privacy-Preserving Cybersecurity Framework for AI-Driven Green Mobility Ecosystems
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
Abstract Note: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT), and Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) technologies in green mobility systems introduces new cybersecurity and privacy challenges. This paper proposes a lightweight cybersecurity framework that integrates compact convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for real-time anomaly detection at the edge, federated learning for decentralized model training, and blockchain-based decentralized identity management with zero-knowledge proofs. These mechanisms collectively ensure sub-100 ms threat detection latency, reduced communication overhead, and GDPR-compliant privacy preservation. Simulation results demonstrate a 60% reduction in latency, 45% lower communication costs, 30% energy savings at edge nodes, and a detection accuracy of 93.4% compared to traditional cloud-centric models.

Author: Kennedy, C. H.; Hilal, A.; Momeni, M.
Title: The Role of Federated Learning in Improving Financial Security: A Survey
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE Global Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things (GCAIoT)
Abstract Note: With the growth of digital financial systems, robust security and privacy have become a concern for financial institutions. Even though traditional machine learning models have shown to be effective in fraud detections, they often compromise user data by requiring centralized access to sensitive information. In IoT-enabled financial endpoints such as ATMs and POS Systems that regularly produce sensitive data that is sent over the network. Federated Learning (FL) offers a privacy-preserving, decentralized model training across institutions without sharing raw data. FL enables cross-silo collaboration among banks while also using cross-device learning on IoT endpoints. This survey explores the role of FL in enhancing financial security and introduces a novel classification of its applications based on regulatory and compliance exposure levels— ranging from low-exposure tasks such as collaborative portfolio optimization [16] to high-exposure tasks like real-time fraud detection [7], [8]. Unlike prior surveys, this work reviews FL’s practical use within financial systems, discussing its regulatory compliance and recent successes in fraud prevention and blockchainintegrated frameworks. However, FL’s deployment in finance is not without challenges. Data heterogeneity, adversarial attacks, and regulatory compliance make implementation far from easy. This survey reviews current defense mechanisms and discusses future directions, including blockchain integration, differential privacy, secure multi-party computation, and quantum-secure frameworks. Ultimately, this work aims to be a resource for researchers exploring FL’s potential to advance secure, privacycompliant financial systems.

Author: K, M.; R, Y. M.; B, J.; M, P.
Title: AI-Enhanced Cloud Security: A Dynamic Framework for Adaptive Threat Intelligence
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Computing Technologies (ICOCT)
Abstract Note: The rapidly evolving cyber threat landscape necessitates dynamic and intelligent approaches to cloud security. This research highlights the transformative role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in addressing the inadequacies of traditional static rule-based systems for threat detection. By integrating advanced techniques like Extended Detection and Response (XDR), Security Information and Event Management (SIEM), Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response (SOAR), and Network Detection and Response (NDR), AI-driven systems enhance real-time monitoring and network forensics, enabling faster and more accurate incident responses. The proposed framework combines supervised learning with Random Forest for identifying known threats and unsupervised learning with Isolation Forest for detecting novel anomalies. It utilizes AI- driven anomaly detection and machine learning (ML) techniques to adapt to emerging security challenges. Moreover, this research emphasizes the synergy between AI and cloud security operations, showcasing how AI accelerates incident response times while fortifying organizational defences against sophisticated attacks. By refining proactive measures and leveraging continuous data analysis from diverse cloud environments, this study offers a robust, scalable approach to safeguarding cloud infrastructures. The findings underline the necessity of adopting AI-powered strategies to maintain a flexible and resilient security posture in an era of increasingly complex cyber threats.

Author: Wang, T.
Title: Trustworthiness Verification for Federated Learning in Web3.0 Healthcare Communities
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Bioinformatics and Biomedicine (BIBM)
Abstract Note: The rapid development of Web3.0 infrastructure has provided new approaches for building wisdom healthcare communities. However, existing solutions of federated learning struggle to handle large volumes of multi-modal privacy data across healthcare organizations. This paper proposes a blockchain-based verification mechanism for the entire process of multi-modal federated learning. For the initial federated state among multiple organizations, feature extraction, cosine similarity, and oracles are used to ensure privacy and security, while establishing a traceable initial state. Then, we perform encrypted verification for each iteration, utilize similarity matrices to realize mutual verification between clients, and validate the effectiveness of dynamically expanding multi-modal datasets from different organizations. This reduces on-chain storage and computational costs while protecting the privacy of organizations. Experimental results demonstrate that this mechanism effectively supports the needs of communities. Compared with state-of-the-art works, our method saves up to 70 % of on-chain storage and 54 % of computational costs, and enables the performance of medical federated learning training to differ from conventional models by no more than 1.89 %.

Author: Rohith, B.; Kumar, N. R. S.; Srinivasine, P. A.; Babu, B. Y.; Prajwin, A. S.

Publication Title: 2025 4th International Conference on Advances in Computing, Communication, Embedded and Secure Systems (ACCESS)
Abstract Note: Modern online finance operations create difficult obstacles for detecting fraudulent activity. While deep learning (DL) models effectively identify fraudulent activities, their "black-box"" nature raises concerns about trust and interpretability. The research design recommends an XDL-Blockchain solution for fraud detection that enhances transparency and accuracy alongside enhanced security capabilities. SHAP and Grad-CAM methods supply interpretation features that enhance stakeholder confidence and blockchain technologies deliver permanent decentralized identity proofing systems which minimize fraudulent activity. Experimental assessments using genuine financial data show that the proposed model delivers superior outcomes compared to conventional detection systems regarding precision and network security. The framework unites artificial intelligence with blockchain technology to provide banks with a dependable system that delivers reliable detection of contemporary financial fraud."

Author: Bharath, E.; Reddy, G. D.; Kiran, K.
Title: A Hybrid Cloud–Blockchain Framework Enhanced by Deep Learning for Smart SME Digital Transformation
Publication Title: 2025 4th International Conference on Applied Artificial Intelligence and Computing (ICAAIC)
Abstract Note: Small enterprises experience extremely tough times while trying to adopt newest computer technology because of inadequate financial means, technical competencies and expansion opportunities. The system addresses prime concerns such as ensuring data security, establishing trust among actors, achieving scalability at low costs and enabling better decision making. With blockchain the system ensures proper tracking of information and automated transaction through smart contracts, while cloud computing ensures flexible access to computing and big data processing enables handling of large volumes of information. The system is designed in a way where smaller companies can add pieces as needed and expand gradually as they become larger. Testing indicates substantial improvements in data security, cost reduction and decision accuracy compared to traditional business practices. The blockchain element creates unalterable records of transactions and enforces obedience with defined rules, while the cloud based analytical software offers instantaneous monitoring and predictive analysis. Author: Reddy, B. L.; Jadhav, S.; Singh, S.; Mapari, N. B.; Gupta, S.; S, R.; Bhutani, M.
Title: Blockchain-Based Intrusion Detection and Response Framework for Secure Industrial IoT Networks
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Communication and Smart Devices (ICCoSD)
Abstract Note: As Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) networks expand, they face increasing challenges in detecting and mitigating cyber threats in real time. This paper proposes a novel Blockchain-Based Intrusion Detection and Response Framework (BIDRF) that combines the immutable nature of blockchain with the predictive power of a Random Forest classifier. BIDRF secures inter-node communication and detects anomalous network activities efficiently. Experimental evaluation using a benchmark IIoT dataset demonstrates that BIDRF achieves a classification accuracy of 94%, with precision and recall values exceeding 0.90 and an AUC of 0.94. By ensuring tamper-proof logging and automated response through smart contracts, the framework provides robust, real-time protection for IIoT networks, supporting the security demands of Industry 4.0 environments.

Author: Sandeep, C.; Martha, S.; Maram, B.
Title: Smart Travel Security Framework: AI-Driven Solutions for Threat Detection in IoT-Enabled Mobility Systems
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 7th International Conference on Computing, Communication and Automation (ICCCA)
Abstract Note: The rising amount of Internet of Things (IoT) devices in the contemporary mobility networks has posed significant risk to vehicular infrastructure and the safety of users. The paper introduces new enhanced AI-based security architecture with the purpose of heterogeneous and IoT-enabled travel environments, that is, in the real-time detection of threats. The framework ensures the provision of scalable and latency and resource-efficient privacy-preserving defense mechanisms and indeed achieves it without sacrificing system latency or resource efficiency by using a multi-layered architecture that involves the combination of federated learning, lightweight large language models (LLMs) and the use of a permissioned blockchain layer. The established vehicular ecosystem-specific taxonomy of threats is formalized and detection models are deployed over the perceived, edge, and application layers with an optimized amalgamation of dichotomies. The bench-mark datasets are evaluated through experiments with consistent results on three (open) bench-mark and two proprietary corpora (with over 10 million records) showing a reliable detection rate of over 96 percent with the latency being less than 100 milliseconds even on lower-power edge nodes. Furthermore, game-theoretic optimization approaches can decrease false positives by up to 18 percent whilst ensuring auditability by transmitting event paths on blockchains. Not only does the said framework allow outperforming the current baseline structures in both detection and scalability, but it also allows adherence to such popular standards as ISO/SAE 21434 and ETSI EN 303 645.
Manual Tags: Federated Learning; IoT Security; Threat detection; Large Language Models; Smart Mobility

Author: P, K.; Gohin; Al-Assaf, K. T.; Lakhanpal, S.; Dinesh, M.; Yuvabharathi, E.
Title: Employing the Synergies of Blockchain with AI: Enhance Trust, Efficiency, and Accuracy in the Execution of Smart Contracts
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICACT)
Abstract Note: The intersection of Blockchain and Artificial Intelligence (AI) holds the potential to revolutionize the way smart contracts are deployed and managed. Blockchain provides decentralization, immutability and transparency however its deterministic and inflexible characteristics make it challenging to adapt to dynamic and rapidly changing environments. On the other hand, AI can provide the ability to do things such as pattern recognition, predictive analytics, and intelligent decision-making, but lacks the trust and verifiability that a blockchain can provide. This article presents research on the incorporation of AI in blockchain-powered smart contracts to improve trust, operational efficacy, and execution precision. We propose a new type of architecture where AI agents run in or adjacent to smart contracts to optimally set the conditions, automatically resolve disputes, detect anomalous behavior, and validate external data using oracles and machine learning models in real-time. By illustrating AIenabled smart contracts in domains such as supply chain management and decentralized finance (DeFi), we show how the use of AI can improve the performance of smart contracts by lowering latency, eliminating fraudulent triggers of contracts and the ability for contracts to adapt based on context-aware inputs without having to sacrifice the integrity and auditability native in decentralized systems. These two aspects of performance, namely, gas cost reduction, error rate minimization, and contract adaptability, are studied across the domains, or environments, of public and permissioned blockchains. The paper further addresses hurdles considering AI interpretability, on-chain computational limits, and the necessity for uniform standards for AI-blockchain interfacing. By combining the trust layer of blockchain with the cognitive layer of AI, we unlock a new realm of smart contracts - those that are not only self-executing but also self-optimizing and contextually aware.
Manual Tags: Smart Contracts; Blockchain Technology; Decentralized Applications (dApps); Intelligent Contract Execution; Machine Learning Integration; Predictive Decision-Making; Trust Automation

Author: Reddy, B. Avinash; Reddy, N. Pavan; Reddy, G. Sharath; Balaji, M. Narendra; Chandra, K. Sharat; Reddy, A. Suresh
Title: Federated and Privacy-Preserving AI Architectures for Strengthening Data Governance Across Distributed and Multi-Cloud Environments
Publication Title: 2025 First International Conference of Advances in Engineering and Computing Technologies for Sustainable Development (AECTSD)
Abstract Note: The high rate of growth of distributed data resources through hybrid and multi-cloud environments has escalated the concerns of data privacy, compliance, and governance. The idea of traditional centralized AI architecture is becoming more and more unsuitable to meet modern data protection regulations like GDPR, HIPAA, and the DPDP Act in India because there is a threat of information disclosure and lack of compliance. This paper presented a Federated and Privacy-Preserving AI (FPPAI) architecture that could enhance data governance by enhancing federated learning, differential privacy and safe multiparty computation (SMC). The framework has been deployed on three simulated clouds including AWS, Azure and GCP and has been performance benchmarked, accuracy benchmarked and compliance efficiency benchmarked. The results of the experiment showed that FPPAI minimized data movement by 94.3 per cent, enhanced the governance auditability by 28.5 per cent, and ensured model accuracy with centralized baselines of 2.4 per cent. Besides advancing regulatory compliance, the experiment indicated that federated AI with built-in privacy controller facilitated cross-cloud AI interaction, which forms an extendable and authoritative paradigm of data management in remote digital communities.

Author: Wang, J.; Shi, Z.; Pan, X.; Zeng, J.
Title: Personalized Federated Learning with Dual Collaborative Information for Data Heterogeneity
Publication Title: 2025 28th International Conference on Computer Supported Cooperative Work in Design (CSCWD)
Abstract Note: Personalized federated learning has gained significant attention due to its effectiveness in addressing data heterogeneity and achieving personalization. To train a model that performs well on local datasets, the key is to enable more effective knowledge sharing between clients and servers without compromising data privacy. Most current approaches aggregate partial model on central server for collaborative learning. However, the information conveyed through model parameters is limited. In this work, we propose a dual-information guided personalized federated learning approach called FedDCI. To obtain more collaborative information, we capture information from both model Parameters and data features. By implementing prototypes similarity-based aggregation, we generate client-specific global models and prototypes, effectively mitigating the challenges posed by data heterogeneity in Federated Learning. We conduct extensive experiments in both label skew and feature skew settings using four benchmark datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that FedDCI achieve accuracy improvements over existing methods in complex heterogeneous scenarios.

Author: Rehyadd, R.; Kashiv, D. j
Title: A Blockchain-Enabled Deep Learning Framework for Securing IoT and Cloud Networks Through Collaborative Intrusion Detection

Abstract Note: Cloud computing and the Internet of Things (IoT) have significantly increased the complexity and vulnerability of digital infrastructures today. IoT and cloud networks can be protected through a collaborative intrusion detection framework based on deep learning and blockchain. To detect sophisticated cyber threats, the framework utilises deep learning, specifically BiLSTM networks, which leverage the decentralised nature of blockchain. Distributed architectures involving cloud servers, SDN controllers, and edge devices are crucial for efficiently detecting threats in vehicular and industrial Internet of Things (IoT) environments. The UNSW-NB15 and BOT - IoT datasets demonstrate the high accuracy of the system, which improves detection speed and accuracy using these datasets. Experimental results confirm that the proposed defence mechanism can provide resilient, scalable, and privacy-preserving protection against modern network security threats.

Author: Bendaouch, F.; Zaydi, H.; Merzouk, S.; Assoul, S.
Title: Securing IoT Architectures with Blockchain: Opportunities, Challenges, and Future Directions
Publication Title: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
Abstract Note: The rapid growth of the Internet of Things creates many challenges for security and scalability. These challenges result from device weaknesses and the complexity of large-scale data management. To shed light on these issues, this paper reviews recent studies from databases like Scopus, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore. We selected articles that clearly propose blockchain-based solutions addressing IoT security, trust, traceability, or scalability, while excluding those that do not focus on these aspects. The results reveal key obstacles related to blockchain integration into IoT architectures. These include limited scalability, difficulties with interoperability among different systems, and data privacy risks. The paper also proposes solutions and directions for future research. Author: Parameswari, S.; Latha, B.
Title: ChainFort: Hybrid Blockchain-Orchestrated Firmware Validation and Secure Update Delivery Using PQC and Federated Trust Consensus
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE Pune Section International Conference (PuneCon)
Abstract Note: IoT and embedded system firmware updates are becoming more susceptible to online assaults, hacking, and a new quantum threat. This study proposes ChainFort, which is a hybrid blockchain managed framework that incorporates post-quantum cryptography (PQC), federated trust consensus (FTC), and AI-assisted anomaly detection, to safeguard the validation and distribution of firmware. Metadata of the firmware is prehashed and metadata of the network traffic is stored on a permissioned blockchain to permit tamper-proof provenance verification. The PQC layer makes use of CRYSTALS-Dilithium to sign messages and Kyber512 to encrypt them, which is quantum-resistant. ftc is dynamically trusted to nodes by using Proof-of-Federated-Authenticity (PoFA) and swarm-efficient validator selection and balances between decentralization and efficiency. A Blockchain-LSTM Fusion Monitor (BLFM) is an LSTM-based anomaly detection method, which detects the presence of an anomalous firmware behavior to roll back to a verified snapshot. Experimental analysis with sets of IoT firmware and simulated network conditions illustrates 96.8 percent anomaly detection precision, 42 percent less update latency and well-balanced trust-weighted validation of the heterogeneous nodes. The framework proposed provides a holistic, scaleable, and forward-compatible secure firmware management solution, which fills the gap between the conventional blockchain solutions and quantum-resilient, decentralized, IoT-security.
Manual Tags: LSTM; IoT Security; Post-Quantum Cryptography; Firmware; ChainFort; Proof-of-Federated Authenticity

Author: Ajibade, S.-S. M.; Jasser, M. B.; Hoong, A. L. Siew; Oyebode, O. J.; Adediran, A. O.; Adetunla, A. O.
Title: A Literature Review of Federated Learning for Energy Load Prediction in Smart Grid
Publication Title: 2025 6th International Conference on Intelligent Communication Technologies and Virtual Mobile Networks (ICICV)
Abstract Note: Energy load prediction that incorporates federated learning has become a game-changing method for improving smart grid operations. There are issues with data privacy, computational efficiency, and scalability with traditional centralized machine learning models. This study examines the use of federated learning to forecast energy loads in smart grids, reviewing the existing literature and drawing conclusions about its benefits, drawbacks, and potential future applications. We take a look at how well different federated learning algorithms—like FLchain, FedAvg, FedSGD, and FedNorm—handle decentralized data while keeping model correctness in mind. Furthermore, the potential of deep learning methods like Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN), Gated Recurrent Units (GRU), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) to enhance predictive capabilities is investigated. The article also mentions how edge computing is being used to improve federated learning by minimizing latency and making the most of available resources. Still, problems like data heterogeneity, communication overhead, and model convergence are there, even with all the progress. Improving privacy-preserving methods, federated learning frameworks, and model flexibility to changing energy usage patterns should be the focus of future study. Smart grid energy management that is efficient, secure, and scalable can be achieved through the use of federated learning, which leverages decentralized intelligence and modern machine learning approaches.

Author: Vijayarangam, S.; Aleti, S.; Alleema, N. N.; Paul, P. M.; Sachdeva, M.; Deshpande, B. S.
Title: Blockchain-Federated Learning Framework for Secure and Privacy-Aware IoT-Enabled Wireless Sensor Networks in Smart Cities
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Computing and Communications (COMPUTINGCON)
Abstract Note: The ability to efficiently monitor, gather data from, and communicate across urban infrastructures is made possible by WSN, which are essential to Smart Cities. Problems with data quality, security, and decentralised learning arise from the vast amounts of sensor data. In response to these issues, it provides BlockFLA, a FL hybrid architecture that incorporates blockchain technology. Data cleansing, removal of unnecessary information, and normalisation are all part of the system's first data preparation procedure, which is designed to guarantee high-quality inputs. By eliminating the need to share raw data, FL enables distributed and decentralised model training among sensor nodes, protecting user privacy. Smart contracts on the blockchain can identify and punish bad actors automatically, making the network more trustworthy. Results from experiments demonstrate that BlockFLA improves resilience and dependability without sacrificing the communication efficiency that is typical of classic FL systems. Our experimental findings show that the suggested model outperforms similar frameworks, reaching an impressive accuracy rate of 97.53%. Finally, a safe, scalable, and effective way for smart data processing in Smart Cities is to combine FL with blockchain in WSNs. By improving distributed learning performance and fortifying urban sensor networks generally, BlockFLA is a game-changer.

Author: Chaudhari, S.; Jagdale, A. D.; Prabhat, S.; Najana, M.; Choudhary, S. K.; Ranjan, P.
Title: Enhancing Security in Event-Driven Architectures: Threat Detection and Mitigation Strategies
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Business Intelligence for Technology Innovation (ICBITI)
Abstract Note: Event-driven architectures (EDAs) provide high-level scalability and responsiveness in the modern wave of distributed systems. Dynamic nature in event propagation and event asynchronous communication, however, exposes the systems to many tough security challenges such as unauthorized event injection, data integrity breaches, or event-based denial-of-service (EDoS) attacks. This paper presents the Event-Driven Oncology Model for Security (EDOM) as a security model for aiding detection and mitigation of security threats in EDA environments. EDOM introduces real-time event monitoring, deep learning-based anomaly detection, and an adaptive response mechanism to protect critical event-driven systems. The system has a context-aware event filtering mechanism to guard against malicious event propagation and a blockchain-backed event validation to guarantee data integrity and non-repudiation. Finally, EDOM presents a hybrid cryptographic model to secure event channels against unauthorized access risks. Experimental evaluations show that EDOM achieves 97.1% threat detection accuracy, effectiveness against injecting events of 87.6%, and event integrity verification improvements of 92.3%. Total latency of the security response of EDOM is reduced by 23.5%, enabling real-time protection without compromising on system performance. Compared with the state-of-the-art security models, this model is specifically suitable for health care applications in which event integrity and real-time security are paramount since EDOM is most resilient and adaptive for event-driven environments.

Author: Rajendran, V.; Jayabal, S. R.; Patil, S. C.; Mandadi, D.
Title: B-FedGNN: Blockchain-Coordinated, Privacy-Preserving Federated Graph Neural Networks for Social-Commerce Recommendations
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Computer, Data Sciences and Applications (ACDSA)
Abstract Note: Social-commerce recommendations leverage user interactions and social relationships to enhance shopping experiences, yet existing centralized approaches raise significant privacy concerns and scalability limitations. We propose a novel privacy-preserving framework that combines Federated Graph Neural Networks (FedGNN) with blockchain technology to enable scalable social-commerce recommendations across retail networks. Our approach tackles three critical challenges: (1) preserving user privacy while utilizing social-graph structures; (2) enabling cross-retailer collaboration without exposing competitive data; and (3) achieving real-time performance at scale.We introduce a hierarchical federated-learning architecture in which Graph Neural Networks are trained locally on user devices and retail nodes, capturing social-influence patterns without exposing raw data. A purpose-built blockchain coordinates the learning process through smart contracts, ensuring transparent model aggregation and immutable audit trails. To address scalability, we implement novel graph-partitioning algorithms, asynchronous model-aggregation protocols, and an optimized consensus mechanism supporting up to 10000 transactionss−1.Our system employs differential-privacy techniques and secure multi-party computation to protect both individual user data and graph topology. Experiments on three large-scale data sets show that our approach retains 94.3% of centralized accuracy while processing more than one million recommendations per minute across 1000 retail nodes. Compared with existing solutions, we cut communication overhead by 73% and improve recommendation latency by 5×, while providing formal privacy guarantees (ε =0.1, δ =10−5).The framework enables retailers to collaboratively improve recommendation quality without compromising user privacy or leaking proprietary data, paving the way for truly decentralized social-commerce ecosystems.

Author: Nugrasyah, A.; Stiawan, D.; Afifah, N.; Mohruni, A. S.; Permana, D. R.; Ningrum, S. K.
Title: Songket MPN: A Decentralized Quality Ranking Architecture for Songket Based on Material Composition Using Federated Learning (Work in Progress)
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Informatics, Multimedia, Cyber and Information System (ICIMCIS)
Abstract Note: Songket is a valuable Indonesian cultural heritage, but its quality assessment is often subjective, and the data for objective ranking is sensitive and an asset to craftsmen. This study proposes an innovative framework that integrates Federated Learning (FL) with blockchain technology to create an objective and privacy-preserving Songket quality prediction system. The proposed architecture uses a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) model, where a central server distributes the initial model to a number of artisans (clients). Each client then trains the model on their local data, the integrity of which is guaranteed by the blockchain module, and only sends weight updates back to the server, without exposing the raw data. The initial evaluation stage presented in this paper focuses on model training performance on the client side. The results show excellent performance, with the model converging quickly within the first 20 epochs with very low error values (MSE 5.48, MAE 1.83, MAPE 3.54%). More importantly, the minimal gap between the training and test data error curves proves the model's strong generalization ability and lack of overfitting. The proposed approach is highly feasible, as each client is able to generate a robust, high-quality local model as the foundation for collaboratively and securely building an accurate global model.

Author: Perera, A.; Somasundaram, S.
Title: Decentralizing Machine Learning with Blockchain: A Review

Abstract Note: Since the dawn of AI (Artificial Intelligence), machine learning, as one of its subdomains, has held a preeminent position in its technological advancement. Machine learning inferences rely predominantly on its training data, which raises concerns about its integrity, transparency, and dependability. Decentralization presents a viable solution to tackle these difficulties. Decentralized systems improve data integrity and security by distributing data across multiple entities instead of relying on a centralized source. This approach mitigates data manipulation and unauthorized access by malicious actors, as no single party possesses control over the complete dataset. Moreover, decentralization enhances transparency, as all transactions and data interactions are recorded, offering an immutable audit trail that stakeholders can rely upon. Author: Bezzaoucha, F. S.; Aoul, F. Z. A.; Boukli-Hacene, S.
Title: Real-time damage detection and classification in wind turbine gearboxes using Ferderated learning
Publication Title: 2025 5th International Conference on Applied Automation and Industrial Diagnostics (ICAAID)
Abstract Note: Gearbox failures are a primary cause of wind turbine downtime, and while vibration-based monitoring is effective, centralising sensitive operational data for model training raises significant privacy and security concerns. This work proposes a federated learning (FL) framework to overcome this limitation, enabling collaborative training of a fault diagnosis model without the need to share raw vibration data from individual turbines. The selection of FL is critically justified by its unique ability to address data privacy mandates while leveraging distributed on-site data, a capability centralised learning models lack. Our methodology involves preprocessing sensor data, identifying in- formative sensors via outlier detection and ranking, and training a global neural network model across multiple client turbines using the Flower framework. The principal contribution of this paper is the development and comprehensive evaluation of an FL system under realistic, non-IID data distributions, demonstrating that such a privacy-preserving approach does not compromise diagnostic performance. Experimental findings demonstrate that the FL model successfully achieved stable convergence and high classification accuracy (92% to 99%) in distinguishing healthy operations from seven specific fault types. This work establishes FL as a robust alternative to conventional methods for building accurate, privacy-preserving predictive maintenance systems in the wind energy sector, offering a practical path to industry-wide collaboration without compromising data sovereignty.

Author: Linkalapalli, K.; Shah, H.; Guntupalli, B. K. Rao; Satyanarayanan, A.; Krishnan, P.
Title: Federated Big Data Processing in Multi-Cloud Architectures

Author: R, V.; Kamalin, D.; Vanaja, S.; Ramesh, C. H.; Karuna, G.; Sabarinathan, G.
Title: Enhanced Naïve Bayes Model for Intelligent and Secure Email Spam Detection Using Hybrid Feature Engineering and Blockchain-Based Verification
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Metaverse and Current Trends in Computing (ICMCTC)
Abstract Note: Cyber security threat posed by spam emails is phishing, data breach, and system vulnerability. Spam detection using traditional Naïve Bayes classifiers has been used since their simplicity and probabilistic reasoning. Although current models fail in case of evolving spam patterns and learning concept drift, or in the case of adversarial attacks. The type of email verification integrated with hybrid feature engineering and adaptive learning is proposed here and is named as the Enhanced Naïve Bayes (ENB) Model. To bring a better representation of the text, the model uses context-aware tokenization and semantic filtering, and URL and attachment analysis to find embedded phishing attempts. In addition, a learning framework is presented that takes advantage of learning new and more effective techniques incrementally, by adapting continuously to emerging spam techniques. To stave off spoofing of email, the sender metadata is recorded to a blockchain-based trust mechanism and a consensus-driven trust score is assigned to it. The development was evaluated on the SpamAssassin and Enron datasets, and it achieved 98.5% of spam detection accuracy, which outperforms conventional Naive Bayes models. This shows that there is a great decrease in false positives and resilience to adversarial spam techniques. The results presented in this research lay an important foundation for the next generation spam filtering systems that are both scalable and adaptive. We will go ahead to integrate federated learning and optimize real-time performance for large-scale email infrastructures.

Author: Stolz, C.; Zhang, J.
Title: Blockchain-Enabled Distributed Intrusion Detection System for Securing IoT Networks
Publication Title: MILCOM 2025 - 2025 IEEE Military Communications Conference (MILCOM)
Abstract Note: The proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has created a significant cybersecurity challenge. This has given rise to the need for Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) capable of operating at the network edge on resource-constrained devices. The IDS must be able to detect both known and unknown threats so combining detection methods provides an efficient and scalable way to enhance security. The centralized IDS is limited, it is a single point of failure and has data privacy issues. Often sharing data between devices is not efficient or desired. Collaborative methods, such as federated learning, provide an alternative but remain susceptible to adversarial attacks, including model poisoning. Trust establishment among distributed nodes remains a challenge, motivating our design of a lightweight, blockchainbacked distributed IDS for IoT networks. Our implementation combines anomaly-based federated learning with Snort-based signature detection. We use the blockchain for immutable logging of model updates and reputation-based trust scores. Experiments with the CICIDS2017 dataset demonstrate high detection accuracy and acceptable latency for our use case. All experiments were conducted on a real-world testbed, including on Raspberry Pi and ESP32 devices.

Author: Wang, J.; Wu, Z.; Wang, Z.; Dong, L.
Title: SBA: A Swift and Stealthy Backdoor Attack Framework for Federated Learning
Publication Title: ICASSP 2025 - 2025 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP)
Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative model training while protecting the privacy of individual participants. However, this decentralized framework is vulnerable to certain risks, particularly backdoor attacks. In such attacks, malicious actors embed triggers into the global model, causing incorrect classifications for inputs with specific features. Traditional backdoor attacks typically use uniform triggers, which makes them more likely to be detected. Furthermore, These methods tend to overlook the fact that poisoned samples may cause abnormal confidence levels in non-target classes. These methods also require an extended attack window to achieve the desired success rate, which reduces their efficiency and increases the chances of detection. This paper introduces a novel backdoor attack method called Swift Backdoor Attack (SBA), designed to overcome these challenges. SBA improves both the stealth and success rate of backdoor attacks by generating adaptive triggers tailored to specific inputs. It also incorporates Non-Target Class Suppression (NTCS) loss and an entropy gain mechanism to enhance the attack’s effectiveness. Our approach suppresses unnecessary activations in the neural network when encountering poisoned samples, making the attack harder to be detected. Experimental results demonstrate that this method significantly increases the success rate of backdoor attacks within a shorter attack window, while evading existing detection mechanisms. This provides a more efficient and covert strategy for executing backdoor attacks in FL. Our code is available at https://github.com/bigcheeses/SBA.
Manual Tags: federated learning; adversarial machine learning; Backdoor attack; attack stealthiness

Author: Manimegalai, R.; Poornima, G.; P, K.; Revathy, S.; Vedanarayanan, V.; Kumar, T. D.
Title: Blockchain-Enabled Incentive Mechanisms for Multi-Institutional Cervical Cancer Risk Prediction in 6G Networks
Publication Title: 2025 10th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
Abstract Note: Cervical cancer remains a leading cause of mortality among women worldwide, yet multiinstitutional collaborations for predictive modeling are hindered by privacy concerns, lack of trust, and limited incentives for data sharing. This work proposes a block chain-enabled incentive framework to encourage hospitals and research institutions to participate in federated learning (FL) for cervical cancer risk prediction under 6G-enabled healthcare environments. Using UCI Cervical Cancer Risk Factors dataset, heterogeneous data contributions from multiple institutions are simulated, and a smart contract-driven tokenomics mechanism is employed to ensure transparent and fair reward distribution based on data volume, quality, and model impact. Logistic Regression is used as a proof-of-concept classifier, achieving a stable accuracy improvement from 0.87 in Round 1 to 0.90 in Round 5. Reward allocation consistently reflected institutional contributions, with higher-performing nodes receiving proportionally greater tokens. Author: Kumar, S.; Hiremath, S.; Jha, P.; Narang, R.

Author: Ajznblasm, Z.; Deepika, A.; Parameswaran, M.; Satyanarayana, B.; Srinivas, T.; Ramesh, P. S.
Title: Exploring Zero Trust Artificial Intelligence-Based Frameworks in Large-scale Dynamic Networks for Enhancing Cybersecurity
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Computational Innovations and Engineering Sustainability (ICCIES)
Abstract Note: Zero Trust AI-based models play a pivotal role in providing security for large-scale dynamic networks by continuously authenticating and verifying every network entity. Such models banish implicit trust, lowering cyber threat and unapproved access chances. APTs and other complex attacks pose a major challenge, especially when utilizing models that primarily utilize fixed techniques such as signature based intrusion detection. In regards to these limitations, this paper proposes a model called RL-AD, or Reinforcement Learningbased Anomaly Detection, which autonomously modifies the behaviors of networks to detect outlier events in real time. Our proposed RL-AD model has been found to be beneficial in protecting high scale dynamic environments such as enterprise cloud infrastructure, IoT networks, and even 5G communication systems by embedding Zero Trust principles that AI powered policy enforcement systems evaluate access requests constantly. The experimental evidence clearly shows RL-AD strengthens the effectiveness of anomaly detection, reduces false positives, improves real-time threat mitigation, forming a truly effective cybersecurity approach. This study illustrates the efficacy of utilizing Zero Trust AI based models to secure essential infrastructure against modern cybersecurity threats.

Author: Chakraborty, A.; Roy, S.; Ahamed, S. F.; Bandara, E.; Singh, B. C.; Shetty, S.
Title: A Unified Blockchain-based Framework for Decentralized Collaborative Transfer Learning using Adaptive Incentivization
Publication Title: ICC 2025 - IEEE International Conference on Communications
Abstract Note: Transfer learning, a method that influences pretrained models to improve performance on new tasks, faces several data privacy, security, and scalability challenges when applied in decentralized environments. Recently, there have been few attempts to integrate blockchain technology with a transfer-learning approach. However, these classical blockchainbased non-collaborative transfer learning models face significant challenges, including poor scalability, security vulnerability, lack of data diversity, and inefficient incentive structures, thereby hindering the effectiveness and efficiency of the transfer learning process. This paper presents a unified framework that utilizes decentralized blockchain technology for collaborative transfer learning. The framework enables secure model sharing within a collaborative learning environment, supported by incentive mechanisms while maintaining model integrity and providing context protection. We perform extensive experimental studies with eight well-known large-scale and fine-grained image datasets. After initial transfer learning, incorporating collaborative learning via the decentralized blockchain network yielded promising results. The global model, after aggregating contributions from all entities, shows an impressive 6.8 % to 10.0 % accuracy improvement compared to individual baseline models. For blockchain implementation, we use the Rahasak blockchain as the ledger and its Aplos platform for a customized smart contract interface. Rahasak-CA, the certificate authority of the Rahasak blockchain, stores the digital certificates of peers in the transfer learning process. The system was deployed using Docker and Kubernetes, and evaluated on the proposed testbed.

Author: Pavuluri, V. K.; Borah, A.; Paranjothi, A.; Khan, M. S.
Title: Enhancing Security in VANETs using Distributed Computing: A Review
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 15th Annual Computing and Communication Workshop and Conference (CCWC)
Abstract Note: Vehicular Ad-Hoc Networks (VANETs) are a cornerstone of intelligent transportation systems, enabling vehicles to communicate with each other and roadside infrastructure to enhance traffic safety and efficiency. This paper reviews and analyzes various distributed technologies-blockchain, fog computing, and federated learning-deployed for enhancing VANET security. Author: Alijoyo, F. A.; Alazzam, M. B.; Muhammad, A. H. Hassan; Mutlag, A. H.; Al-Dabagh, M. Z. Nayef; Bala, B. Kiran
Title: Ethical Implications of Data Sharing and Patient Privacy in Medical Informatics Systems

Abstract Note: The healthcare industry is being driven by data variants that have aided clinical decision making, operational workflow optimization, and medical research progression at an unprecedented pace as medical informatics systems evolve. EHR’s integration has become widespread, advanced analytics along with AI-powered enabling has changed the way health delivering is done traditionally in a highly connected ecosystem. Simultaneously, however, these technological advances present difficult moral questions regarding patient privacy, informed consent, and secure sharing of sensitive health data. A core difficulty of medical informatics is to strike a synchrony between privacy of individuals and maximizing data utility for research. This study addresses these concerns by introducing a dual methodological framework that is coupled to use of Descriptive Analysis and Critical Discourse Analysis. To understand the types, patterns, regulatory responses and recurring issues to PHI violations in the presence of breach data reported by U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, January 2009-December 2017; the descriptive analysis is used. CDA is also used to reveal the greater sociopolitical, cultural, and institutional power relations which influence ethical narratives about privacy and data governance, taken up as well. Mentioned emerging technologies like federated learning and blockchain are probably designed in order to strengthen privacy benefits, however, leave unresolved ethical dilemmas. Author: Gore, S.; Shaikh, N.; Sandeep, K. S.; Jagadish, S.; Priya, L.; Priyanka, T. P.
Title: Next-Gen Biometric Security: AI for Identity Authentication
Publication Title: 2025 6th International Conference on Electronics and Sustainable Communication Systems (ICESC)
Abstract Note: Biometric verification is an essential aspect of secure identity verification; nonetheless, unimodal systems are plagued by security flaws, uneven accuracy, and susceptibility to spoof attacks. To mitigate such weaknesses, this research suggests an AI-based multimodal biometric verification system that combines facial recognition, dynamic signature, EEG signals, and keystroke dynamics. The system harnesses deep learning-based feature extraction and late feature-level fusion to build stronger robustness and decrease error rates. Experimental results show that the proposed model performs better, yielding an accuracy of 97.8%, a precision of 96.5%, and a recall of 98.2%, while reducing the False Acceptance Rate (FAR) by a large margin to 1.3% and the False Rejection Rate (FRR) to 2.0%. In comparison to current unimodal and multimodal systems, the proposed framework proves to be more secure, reliable, and efficient in identity verification. The results prove the strength of combining heterogeneous modalities for the next generation of authentication systems. Subsequent research will target optimization of computational effectiveness for real-time use, including federated learning for privacy protection, and expansion of the system to more biometric modalities.

Author: Ajakwe, S. O.; Kim, D.-S.
Title: Federated Learning and Lightweight Blockchain for Resilient UAV Communication Against PNT and Model Poisoning Attacks
Publication Title: 2025 16th International Conference on Information and Communication Technology Convergence (ICTC)
Abstract Note: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) swarms are increasingly deployed in Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) applications, but remain vulnerable to Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) spoofing and federated model poisoning, which threaten safety and mission reliability. Traditional cloud-centric or heavyweight blockchain solutions suffer from latency and scalability limits in UAV-class hardware. This paper proposes a hybrid framework that integrates Horizontal Federated Learning (HFL) with a lightweight DAG-based blockchain. The HFL layer enables privacy-preserving anomaly detection with Byzantinerobust aggregation, while the DAG blockchain ensures low-latency consensus, tamper-proof anomaly logging, and update reputation tracking. Experimental validation on a GNSS spoofing dataset shows 81.5% detection accuracy under non-IID data (vs. 52.5% FedAvg), 62% lower testing loss, and sub-second transaction latency (0.85s) with 25 MB lower communication cost per round. The proposed design establishes a unified, auditable, and scalable defense pipeline, advancing resilient UAV swarm communication infrastructures for IIoT logistics, inspection, and surveillance.

Author: Satheesh, P.; K, S. C.; Sathiya, K. G.; S, S. S.; Sujitha, R.; Rathika, S.
Title: Hybrid Trust-Enhanced Blockchain Scaling: A Cloud-Driven Dual-Layer Signature Verification Framework
Publication Title: 2025 3rd International Conference on Sustainable Computing and Smart Systems (ICSCSS)
Abstract Note: Recently, the scalability issue of blockchain is a major obstacle to the wide adoption of the blockchain technology to several high-throughput and trust-intensive use cases. To overcome these constraints of scalability, this paper suggests a new trust-aware architecture which uses a cloud computing and a multi-layered digital signature verification system that can support scalability, maintain security and transparency. The point is to outsource the heavy-computation tasks (cryptographic signature verifications and transaction pre-processing) to a specialized layer of clouds, which decreases computation capacity on the chain and increases the throughput. The framework proposed will have a dual-layer trust design where the first layer will be rapid cloud-based signature validation based on the dynamic key management protocol and the second layer will be consensus-aligned verification on-chain to provide integrity and fault tolerance. Experimental data show that our model has a much higher transaction throughput and lower latency in comparison with conventional blockchain systems, and barely compromises on decentralization. Also, fault tolerance is maintained by using a fallback feature, which shifts operations to the on-chain layer in the case of cloud service failure. This mixed model provides a feasible route to scalable, reliable and efficient blockchain infrastructures that can be deployed at an enterprise level and run in real-time decentralized applications.

Author: S, D.; Neelaveni, P.; Sankar, R.; Mythily, V.; Lakshmi, C. S.; Vani, N.
Title: A Secured Artificial Intelligence (AI) Assisted Personal Data Prediction and Leakage Prevention System Using Deep Learning Logic
Publication Title: 2025 2nd International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Knowledge Discovery in Concurrent Engineering (ICECONF)
Abstract Note: Securing personal data against prediction misuse and leakage threats has emerged as a pressing concern in the era of artificial intelligence. The paper suggests an AI-Assisted Secured Personal Data Prediction and Leakage Prevention System, which combines a hybrid CapsuleNetxGBoost-based system with federated privacy/differentiated privacy models. Data preprocessing includes sanitization, anonymization and synthetic data generation to make sure privacy is preserved. The CapsuleNet extracts hierarchical relationships in sensitive attributes, whereas XGBoost narrows down predictive decision-making. In order to protect against attacks further, adversarial training and immutable logging based on blockchain is added, and homomorphic encryption is also used to process queries securely. The experimental results indicate that the given method is notably superior to traditional deep learning models. In particular, it had a prediction accuracy of 98.6 (a higher score than CNN, 93.5), a precision of 98.3, a recall of 98.8, and F1-score of 98.5. Strongness against adversarial examples and leakage probability were higher than 94 and 2.1 respectively under a rigorous privacy constraint \(\textbackslash{}varepsilon=1.2)\. The Data Leakage Risk Index (DLRI), which was assisted by AI, also allowed identifying insider threats and abnormal access patterns in a dynamic way. Finally, the proposed model is not only more predictive accurate, but also resists leakage and adversarial exploitation. It has had wide applications in sensitive areas like health care, financial services and e-governance. Future studies will be aimed at extending the architecture by adding quantum-resistant-based encryption, reinforcement-based adaptive access control, as well as extending the DLRI architecture to multi-cloud and IoT-based settings. This paper takes the secure AI frameworks a step further to predictive intelligence and privacy protection.

Author: Patjoshi, P. K.; Thayumanavan, K.; Manikandan, G.; R, S.; Sundharesalingam, P.; Kaliappan, S.
Title: AI-Blockchain Integrated Solution for Intelligent Procurement and Logistics Optimization in Public Sector Enterprises

Abstract Note: The objective of this paper is to present a new version of a solution for supply chain optimization in relation to integrating blockchains and AI toward better operational efficiency in the PSE sector of India. Author: Li, R.; Sun, A.; Du, J.; Wang, C.; Hu, B.; Xu, J.; Miao, X.

Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 101st Vehicular Technology Conference (VTC2025-Spring)

Author: Zhang, F.; Jia, W.; Tan, Y.; Liu, T.; Jiang, Z.; Fan, Y.

Publication Title: 2025 18th International Conference on Advanced Computer Theory and Engineering (ICACTE)
Abstract Note: Aiming at the problem of illegal construction supervision in the real estate industry, this study proposes an intelligent supervision framework that integrates federated learning (FedUAV-FL), blockchain and edge computing, and breaks through the time-space constraints and data security bottlenecks of the traditional UAV supervision mode. By constructing a distributed collaboration model and combining multi-source data encryption aggregation with the tamper proof characteristics of blockchain, dynamic monitoring and trustworthy governance of illegal buildings can be achieved. The experiment was based on a high-resolution remote sensing dataset of the reconstructed area after the New Zealand earthquake, and the model performance was validated under a 5-party federated learning architecture. The results showed that the FedUAV-FL framework improved the detection accuracy by 4.3% (82.50%) compared to the YOLOv8 benchmark model. Empirical evidence shows that this framework performs outstandingly in complex building color recognition (such as red roofed buildings) and small-scale illegal building detection, providing an intelligent, collaborative, and trustworthy technological path for smart city governance.

Author: Jha, A. C.; Gannavarapu, P.; Durgam, S.
Title: Machine Learning-Driven Security System for Next-Generation Ultra-Low-Latency Financial Network Governance
Publication Title: 2025 Tenth International Conference on Science Technology Engineering and Mathematics (ICONSTEM)
Abstract Note: This paper suggests applying to the construction of an adaptive security system in ultra-low-latency financial networks the use of the Reinforcement Learning (RL). The suggested system takes advantage of the state-of-the-art RL algorithm, Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), to learn optimal security policies dynamically given a real-time feedback of the network. PPO modifies security measures automatically and reduces threats like fraud or unauthorized access without affecting the low-latency requirements of financial systems. The system is self adapting to the new threats which it constantly interacts with, and improves its defence mechanisms as time goes by. The results of the simulation have shown that the method can enhance the resilience of security in high-frequency trading systems and show a significant decrease in response time and an increase in detection efficiency. The RL into financial governance forms a new template of self-optimizing proactive security systems in the next generation financial networks.

Author: Luo, Z.; Lu, Q.; Li, Z.; Shu, Y.; Peng, J.; Jiang, W.
Title: Privacy-Preserving Traffic Flow Prediction Based on a Spatiotemporal Hybrid Attention Network
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
Abstract Note: With rapid urbanization, traffic flow prediction has become a crucial technology in intelligent transportation systems, alleviating congestion, enhancing traffic efficiency, and supporting decision-making in traffic management and scheduling. However, traffic data often contain sensitive personal mobility information, posing critical challenges for privacy protection and data security. Traditional models (e.g., ARIMA, SVR, LSTM, GRU) not only struggle to capture long-range temporal dependencies but also lack mechanisms to protect sensitive information in large-scale deployments. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a privacy-aware Spatiotemporal Hybrid Attention Network (STHAN), which integrates graph neural networks, Transformer, and LSTM architectures to jointly capture complex spatiotemporal dependencies. Meanwhile, the proposed framework can be extended to federated learning or secure multi-party computation settings, enabling collaborative model training while ensuring that raw traffic data remain locally stored. Experiments conducted on two public datasets demonstrate that STHAN achieves superior short- and long-term forecasting accuracy and robustness, while maintaining a security-preserving design that reduces risks of privacy breaches in intelligent transportation systems.
