Author: Day, A.; Smith, J.; Dagher, G. G.; Andersen, T.
Title: ASPARaGUS: Blockchain-Based Efficient Framework for Neural Network Poisoning Mitigation
Publication Title: 2025 7th International Conference on Blockchain Computing and Applications (BCCA)
Abstract Note: Training neural networks in outsourced or untrusted environments, such as third-party providers or cloud services, raises significant concerns about the integrity of the resulting models. Poisoning attacks may go undetected if validation only occurs post-training. We propose ASPARaGUS, a blockchain-integrated system that performs mid-training validation to detect and isolate poisoned intervals. ASPARaGUS combines dynamic weight analysis with Merkle tree-based verification to preserve uncontaminated training data. ASPARaGUS uses a two-part consensus process. First, we perform real-time anomaly detection using a weight analysis algorithm. Second, if anomalies are detected, we apply Merkle tree-based verification and selective retraining to recover uncontaminated intervals. This approach enables secure, verifiable training with an efficient audit trail.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; Poisoning Attacks; Neural Network; Model Integrity; Secure Training

Author: Sankaran, M.; Chaudhary, A.; Kumar, B. D.; N, R.; R, S. K.
Title: Federated Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Secure and Scalable Blockchain Consensus
Publication Title: 2025 2nd International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
Abstract Note: Blockchain technology has become a cornerstone of decentralized and secure applications. However, traditional consensus methods, such as the Proof of Work (PoW) and Proof of Stake (PoS), struggle with scalability, efficiency, and adaptability in changing network dynamics. Recent research has shown that using machine learning to optimize blockchains is feasible; however, much of the work to date has depended on centralized training or single-agent reinforcement learning, which limits robustness, security, and generalization. To address the challenge posed by the Federated Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (FMARL) framework as the method of choice. Initially, the Bitcoin researchers' transaction graph dataset (BRTGD) performs data extraction, cleansing, and normalization to run different graph-based feature extractions to extract relevant temporal and structural features. These features then become the input state for distributed reinforcement learning agents, each optimizing their own consensus parameters. A federated learning protocol ensures a secure aggregate of their model updates, leading to a global consensus policy. Therefore, the resulting framework of FMARL is a self-optimizing blockchain consensus system that preserves privacy and scales effortlessly. The FMARL framework achieved better accuracy \(98.67 \textbackslash{}%)\, precision \(97.55 \textbackslash{}%)\, recall \(98.64 \textbackslash{}%)\, and F1-score \(98.77 \textbackslash{}%)\ than the existing model Random Forest (RF).

Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Computing Technologies (ICOCT)
Abstract Note: The unified system that brings together federated learning (FL) with cluster/grid computing creates new possibilities to overcome scalability and resilience and privacy problems in advanced machine learning approaches. The proposed system achieves resilient model aggregation through its capability to adapt workload balancing and fault-tolerant node coordination which also reduces network congestion and energy usage. The FACC framework enables its users to provision resources dynamically while performing heterogeneity-aware scheduling to achieve optimal latency and guarantee smooth convergence across distributed platforms. The experimental tests using benchmark datasets showed that the proposed system offers enhanced training efficiency together with improved fault tolerance and scalability compared to standard FL methods. The work showcases opportunities to combine FL with clustered computation for building resilient scalable AI systems which protect user privacy at scale in real-world large-scale deployments.

Title: Latency Analysis of DAG-Driven Blockchain System for IoV Through the Lens of IOTA
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 31th International Conference on Parallel and Distributed Systems (ICPADS)
Abstract Note: The Internet of Vehicles (IoV) has emerged as a key enabler of Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS), IoV faces significant challenges in scalability and security. The growing volume of real-time vehicular data strains network resources, and traditional centralized architectures introduce single points of failure that compromise reliability and data integrity. This paper investigates the integration of IOTA-a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) based distributed ledger designed for feeless and scalable transactions-into the IoV system. In the proposed architecture, vehicles operate as lightweight nodes and roadside units function as full nodes, yielding a resource-efficient architecture for secure, tamper-resistant data interaction across vehicular networks. We formally model the latency of transaction propagation and consensus confirmation phases to gain insight into its performance characteristics under high concurrency. We conducted extensive simulations under diverse traffic conditions on a private IOTAenabled vehicular network. Experimental results demonstrate that the IOTA-based IoV system achieves low latency on the order of a few milliseconds and high throughput of hundreds of transactions per second even as vehicle density increases. The system exhibits strong scalability and operational stability, indicating considerable potential for deployment in real-world ITS environments.

Author: Arioua, I.; Bouardi, H.; Hraoui, S.; Fadili, H.
Title: Artificial intelligence Enhanced Chaotic Encryption vs Blockchain Frameworks for Embedded Medical Imaging Security
Publication Title: 2025 4th International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
Abstract Note: Advances in telemedicine and the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) have led to the decentralization of medical imaging systems, exposing sensitive patient data to increasing security risks, while also considering the hardware constraints of embedded devices and a strict regulatory framework. This work is a systematic comparative study of two emerging security paradigms: chaotic encryption enhanced by artificial intelligence and blockchain-based access control mechanisms, deployed in embedded healthcare environments. Four evaluation criteria were used: cryptographic robustness, computational load, scalability, and compliance with current standards. The results, obtained from real medical imaging datasets, reveal significant trade-offs. AI-assisted chaotic encryption hybrid approaches demonstrate remarkable real-time privacy efficiency, with informational entropy exceeding 7.997, correlation coefficients close to 0.001, and an average encryption time of 0.1 seconds for standardsized images. Simultaneously, blockchain ensures decentralized trust and irrefutable traceability, with a throughput of up to 109,248 transactions per second and an access latency of less than 500 ms. In-depth statistical analysis validates blockchain’s superiority for auditing and regulatory compliance, thanks to its immutable ledgers, while chaotic methods guarantee robust pixel protection, with alteration rates exceeding \99.6 \textbackslash{}%\. Ultimately, this study identifies optimal hybrid architectures that reconcile these conflicting imperatives, paving the way for secure, efficient, and compliant distributed medical imaging systems.

Author: Liu, X.; Liu, J.; Wei, X.; Wang, Y.
Title: Incentive Mechanism for Blockchain-Enabled Coded Federated Learning in Edge Clouds
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 31th International Conference on Parallel and Distributed Systems (ICPADS)
Abstract Note: Incentivizing participation and coordinating decisions across hierarchical agents remain critical challenges in blockchain-enabled federated learning (FL) over edge clouds, especially when a coded FL is performed over a client-edge-cloud hierarchical system. This paper proposes a novel hybrid incentive framework that integrates multidimensional contract theory with reinforcement learning (RL)-based Stackelberg game modeling for such a system. Specifically, we design personalized contracts between edge servers and clients, addressing their heterogeneous data volume, privacy sensitivity, and computational capacity under incomplete information. Simultaneously, we model the task publisher's reward allocation to edge servers as a one-leader multi-follower Stackelberg game, where each follower acts based on local observations. A decentralized RL algorithm is proposed to learn optimal reward strategies without revealing other agents' private information, such as local data volume/quality. Simulations demonstrate that our method can converge to equilibrium and achieve effectiveness under incomplete information compared to baseline incentive schemes.

Author: Pisupati, S.
Title: Towards Enhancing Smart Grid Security With TPM Enabled Systems
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
Abstract Note: The smart grid has become a critical cyber-physical infrastructure where synchronized measurements and authenticated device data are essential for reliable operation. Existing approaches treat time synchronization and identity management separately: GPS or network protocols provide weak temporal guarantees, while certificate-based identities risk privacy leak-age. This paper proposes a Trusted Platform Module (TPM)-anchored framework that unifies secure time attestation with privacy-preserving identity. Each device generates tokens com-bining TPM-signed timestamps with pseudonymous credentials, ensuring data freshness while preventing permanent identity linkage. At the control center, tokens are validated before data is admitted into operational workflows. A Raspberry Pi testbed with Infineon SLB 9670 TPM 2.0 modules demonstrates feasibility. Evaluation on up to five concurrent devices provides proof-of-concept scalability under realistic conditions. Results show low-latency operation, linear throughput growth, and resilience against replay, spoofing, and timing attacks. The proposed architecture establishes a unified, privacy-aware trust layer for next-generation smart grid communications.

Abstract Note: As blockchain technology continues to gain significance in various sectors, protecting its infrastructure from potential future cyberattacks is an inherent problem. Local machine learning models are trained on distributed private datasets across different stations of the grid and only the model parameters are communicated to a central server to create an aggregated global model for load forecasting, without exchanging any raw private data. Several experiments conducted on electricity consumption data validate the effectiveness of proposed approach in handling complex spatiotemporal load changes and generating station-specific adaptive forecasts. Author: Su, B.; Wang, R.; Zhang, H.; Fu, M.; Zhang, C.; Zhu, L.
Title: Towards Intelligent Power Monitoring via Personalized Federated Learning

Abstract Note: Electric power monitoring systems produce continuous, high-volume data streams from substations and grid devices, demanding real-time intelligence while preserving data privacy. In this paper, we propose PFL-EPM, a privacy-preserving personalized federated learning framework tailored for intelligent monitoring of electric power data streams. PFL-EPM incorporates (1) an energy-aware local training scheduler that adapts to device heterogeneity and grid dynamics, (2) a robust aggregation mechanism based on layer-normalized similarity and decentralized blockchain committees, and (3) a feedback-driven fine-tuning loop optimized via operational KPIs. Author: Shilpi, S.; Sait, R. A. M.; Harshitha, G. M.; Mapari, N. B.; Rani, A.
Title: Secure IoT Data Aggregation using Lightweight Homomorphic Encryption and Trust Modeling with Fingerprint Verification
Publication Title: 2025 5th International Conference on Mobile Networks and Wireless Communications (ICMNWC)
Abstract Note: In current era, secure data aggregation has gained significant attention in large scale Internet of Things (IoT) environments, where large distributed sensing systems continuously generate heterogeneous and sensitive data. However, the existing approach Sub Message Authentication Code (SubMAC) based secure aggregation framework struggles with vulnerability to false positives, limited trust evaluation capability and high computation due to repeated MAC verification. These challenges restricted the accuracy in detection of abnormal contributions and affect overall aggregation reliability. To address these challenges, this research proposed a Lightweight Homomorphic Encryption Sparse Random Projection based Coefficient Estimation with Verifiable Homomorphic Fingerprinting (LHE-SRPC-VHF) based secure aggregation framework. This research begins with the system modelling and data collection, followed by preprocessing where Min Max Interquartile (MMIQ), Entropy Stabilized Noise Reduction (ES-NR) and Outlier Aware Clipped Normalization (OACN) to refine sensor inputs and suppress distortions. Then, Lightweight Homomorphic Encryption (LHE) is applied to ensure privacy preserving on encrypted values. Further, Sparse Random Projection Coefficient (SRPC) evaluates node trust by analyzing statistical deviations to enable selective filtering of unreliable readings. Finally, Verifiable Homomorphic Fingerprinting (VHF) is employed to ensure end to end integrity of encrypted contributions during aggregation. Experimental results demonstrates that the proposed LHE-SRPC-VHF achieved higher sensitivity (79.3%), AA (98.7%) and lower energy dissipation (\textbackslash{}mathbf{2. 8 7 m J}\) compared to the existing approach.

Abstract Note: With the rapid development of the Internet of Vehicles (IoVs), Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as a promising distributed training paradigm. Author: A, A. S. Jeena; M, G. J.
Title: A Comprehensive Survey of Blockchain and Reinforcement Learning in IoMT

Abstract Note: The Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) integrates interconnected medical devices and sensors to enable continuous patient monitoring and real-time healthcare delivery. Blockchain technology, with its decentralized ledger, cryptographic integrity, and smart contracts, has emerged as a promising solution to secure sensitive medical data while ensuring transparency and compliance with regulations such as HIPAA and GDPR. Concurrently, reinforcement learning (RL) techniques, especially advanced deep RL algorithms, facilitate intelligent, adaptive task offloading in fog-cloud computing environments to optimize latency, energy consumption, and resource allocation. This survey synthesizes twenty recent studies addressing blockchain-enabled privacy-preserving frameworks and RL-based task offloading mechanisms in IoMT. It critically evaluates architectural designs, cryptographic innovations including zero-knowledge proofs and quantum-resistant signatures, and RL methodologies for dynamic resource management. Key research challenges identified include the lack of standardized interoperability protocols across heterogeneous IoMT devices and blockchain platforms, the computational overhead of quantum-resistant cryptography on resource-constrained devices, and the opaque nature of RL models hindering clinical trust. Future research directions emphasize developing unified communication standards, lightweight post-quantum cryptographic schemes tailored for IoMT edge devices, and explainable RL frameworks to foster clinical adoption. Author: Bemrah, F. Z.; Chikh, A.; Ouchani, S.

This review systematically analyzes existing IoT service management approaches, categorizing them into five core methodologies: (1) rule-based and model-driven control, (2) AI-driven learning techniques, (3) optimization-based strategies, (4) decentralized blockchain systems, and (5) edge-centric federated intelligence. Author: Herath, K.; Mahangade, S.; Bagchi, S.
Title: A Lightweight Reputation-Based Mechanism for Incentivizing Cooperation in Decentralized Federated Learning

Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative model training without centralizing data, but traditional server-assisted FL faces challenges such as single points of failure, communication bottlenecks, and trust dependency. However, DFL introduces new vulnerabilities, including exposure to adversarial attacks and the risk of free-riding behavior. To ensure sustainable and secure participation, effective incentive and reputation mechanisms are essential. In this work, we propose a lightweight, reputation-based algorithm tailored for resource-constrained edge devices in decentralized settings. Our approach prioritizes model sharing based on peer-evaluated contributions, discourages selfish behavior, and mitigates the impact of malicious clients through adaptive reputation adjustments. Unlike prior methods, our scheme explicitly accounts for clients' limited sending and receiving capacities, promoting fairness and practical applicability. Experimental results demonstrate that our method incentivizes meaningful participation and enhances the robustness of decentralized learning systems against both selfish and adversarial threats.

To address these threats, we propose new techniques using model diversity and progressive training. These methods allow different network nodes to train slightly different models, making the system more resilient to attacks. Our experimental results on realworld datasets show that model diversity can improve accuracy by up to 25% under attack scenarios. Author: Lin, J.
Title: BFTChain-Net: A Blockchain-based Federated Transformer Network for Cross-Organization Accounting Fraud Detection

Abstract Note: With the accelerating digitalization and automation of cross-institutional financial transactions, accounting fraud is exhibiting typical and widespread characteristics of concealment, intelligence, and cross-domain correlation. To address these issues, this paper proposes a blockchain-based federated Transformer cross-institutional fraud detection system, named BFTChain-Net. This system integrates the Byzantine Fault-Tolerant Blockchain (BFT) consensus mechanism, federated learning (FL), and Transformer coding networks for joint modeling. This algorithm achieves high-precision, traceable, and interpretable fraud detection while protecting the data sovereignty of each institution. In terms of model design, BFTChain-Net establishes a trusted parameter synchronization and anti-counterfeiting verification mechanism through an improved iPBFT consensus protocol. This mechanism ensures the integrity and robustness of the cross-institutional model aggregation process. The federated Transformer sub-network is deployed locally by each participant, using a multi-head self-attention mechanism to model time-series transaction features. This operation achieves global semantic association of heterogeneous features across organizations. Furthermore, the model introduces a graph contrastive learning module. This module combines node attention clustering and anomaly relationship prediction. The experimental section uses data subsets from three independent institutions, and conducts joint validation using the European credit card fraud dataset and the IEEE-CIS fraud detection dataset. Results show that BFTChain-Net achieves an average improvement of 3.4%–6.8% in F1-score and AUC compared to the comparison models. Simultaneously, it reduces the parameter convergence error to 0.014 in cross-institutional consistency detection. Through t-SNE visualization analysis, the model can significantly distinguish between normal transactions and anomalous samples. The detection performance of independent institutions is improved by 1.5%, 2.2%, and 3.7%, respectively. Author: Yang, H.; Wang, M.; Dai, L.; Wu, Y.; Du, J.
Title: Federated Graph Neural Networks for Heterogeneous Graphs with Data Privacy and Structural Consistency
Publication Title: 2025 5th International Conference on Computer Science and Blockchain (CCSB)
Abstract Note: This paper addresses the problem of joint modeling for multi-source heterogeneous graph data in distributed environments by proposing a federated graph neural network classification framework driven by structural alignment and consistency regularization. The method preserves data locality by enabling each participant to learn node features and topological information through a local graph neural network encoder. A cross-source structural alignment module maps embeddings from different graphs into a shared representation space, mitigating semantic inconsistencies caused by structural differences. Additionally, a consistency regularization mechanism is introduced to enhance the robustness of node representations through multi-view perturbations, improving the model's generalization ability during training. At the global level, a federated averaging strategy is adopted to periodically aggregate local models, enabling collaborative optimization and enhancing the consistency and discriminative capacity of the global representation. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, experiments are conducted in a multi-source heterogeneous graph environment using various node distribution strategies. The results show that the method outperforms existing federated graph learning models in terms of accuracy, clustering consistency, and structural expressiveness, achieving efficient multi-source graph classification while preserving data privacy.

Author: Sravanthi, G.; Karuna, G.; S.Selvi; Mohamed, H.; Jenifer, S.; V, K.

Author: Wang, Y.; Li, N.
Title: Lightweight Homomorphic Encryption Transmission Protocol for Multimodal Physiological Sensor Data

Abstract Note: This paper proposes a lightweight, homomorphically encrypted transmission protocol for multimodal physiological sensor data (LHE-TPMPSD) to support privacy protection and cloud-based secure analysis of multi-source data, including electrocardiogram (ECG), electroencephalogram (EEG), and skin conduction data, in music neurotherapy scenarios. Author: Xu, X.; Chen, X.; Lou, X.; Liu, Z.; Zhang, Y.; Zhang, H.
Title: Real-Time Self-Adaptive SMPC for Non-IID Vehicular Data in Intelligent Transportation Systems

Abstract Note: Real-time traffic analytics require joint processing of privacy-sensitive vehicular data that are inherently non-IID, yet current secure multi-party computation (SMPC) pipelines either ignore data skew or exceed the sub- 200 ms latency budget of V2X links. We present RT-AW-SMPC, a self-adaptive framework that combines (i) an entropy-volume-based local weighting estimator to debias aggregation under skewed sample distributions, and (ii) an edge-optimized private set intersection protocol that aligns feature keys in only two network rounds. The entire workflow executes within a two-party additive SMPC circuit, protecting inputs from honest-but-curious roadside units and cloud servers. Experiments on the public PEMS-D7 freeway dataset show that RT-AW-SMPC reduces aggregation error by \6.3 \textbackslash{}times\ compared with a uniform-weight SMPC baseline, completes each computation round in 25 ms-well below the V2X hard limit-and caps per-vehicle uplink traffic at 2.3 KB. Author: Garro, R. J.; Wilson, C. S.; Pordomingo, A. J.; Wibowo, S.
Title: An Integrated Federated Learning and Blockchain Architecture for Model Adoption in Precision Livestock Systems

Abstract Note: Federated learning (FL) deployments in agricultural environments face two critical challenges, such as intermittent connectivity in rural areas and the lack of transparent governance of shared models. In this system, IoT-enabled smart feeders equipped with RFID readers and load cells collect individual feed intake and weight data, which are transmitted to Raspberry Pi edge nodes for local processing and model updating. These edge nodes generate daily local models to correct measurement errors in feed intake estimations, and the resulting updates are aggregated at a gateway node using weighted FedAvg, even when one or more clients are temporarily offline. To ensure verifiability and trust, the aggregated models and metadata are recorded in a permissioned blockchain. Experimental simulations with three Raspberry Pi edge nodes, utilizing synthetic vectors to represent model parameters, confirmed that the architecture maintains operational continuity in the presence of client dropouts. At the same time, blockchain storage guarantees immutable traceability of model artifacts. Compared to conventional FL approaches, the proposed architecture achieves resilient performance in the presence of connectivity losses and provides robust end-to-end model governance. Blockchain integration further enhances the system by enabling verifiable and tamper-proof model storage with minimal latency remaining under 3.5 seconds per round, well within the operational needs of livestock data collection. This integration represents a novel contribution toward scalable, transparent, and resilient digital infrastructures for precision livestock farming.

Author: Canady, R.; Bhowmick, C.; Koutsoukos, X.
Title: Decentralized Learning using Hashgraph Consensus
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 49th Annual Computers, Software, and Applications Conference (COMPSAC)
Abstract Note: Federated learning has become increasingly popular for its ability to process large, distributed datasets and speed up learning while protecting data privacy. However, it typically relies on a central server for coordination, which can be a bottleneck and a single point of failure. To address these limitations, we developed a novel distributed learning architecture that eliminates the need for a central server. The architecture utilizes the hashgraph consensus algorithm (HCA), a distributed ledger technology, which enables the computing nodes to train machine learning models using local data and aggregation with models received from their neighbors. Our work demonstrates that distributed learning using hashgraph consensus can be performed efficiently and is a valid alternative to traditional federated learning. To strengthen this claim, we analyze resilient federated learning in a decentralized setting. Our analysis includes scenarios with denial-of-service and model poisoning attacks. We introduce trimmed soft-medoid (TSM), a resilient aggregation method that has proven resilience to model poisoning attacks. It can be performed at every node using the information available from the hashgraph. An extensive evaluation is conducted using two multimodal machine learning tasks, human emotion recognition and activity recognition. The results confirm that decentralized learning using hashgraph consensus maintains performance parity with traditional federated learning using a central server. This is shown in both normal and adversarial scenarios. We also evaluate the latency and memory overhead of the proposed approach. These are reported to be under an acceptable range, latency of 1s and memory overhead of 8.8-13 GB, for decentralized machine learning.

Abstract Note: Decentralized and Connected Autonomous Vehicle (CAV) networks offer promising advances in safety, efficiency, and real-time decision-making. Author: Hao, Z.; He, Q.; Chang, C.; Xu, Z.; Li, H.; Guo, J.; Du, J.

We address key challenges in universal healthcare standardization and propose actionable solutions to strengthen data integrity, safeguard patient privacy, and ensure interoperability. Author: Sahana, S.; R, S. U.; B, P. S.
Title: A Web-Orchestrated WSN Security Framework with Dual-Layer Anomaly Detection and Blockchain-Backed Integrity for IoT Environments

Abstract Note: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are fundamental to Internet of Things (IoT) systems but are increasingly vulnerable to adversarial attacks, data anomalies, and the absence of reliable forensic mechanisms. The system includes a web-based dashboard for simulating sensor behavior, launching targeted cyberat-tacks, tracking anomalies, and generating PDF reports for audit trails. Experimental evaluations demonstrate high detection accuracy (> 90%), low transaction latency (<300 ms), and resilience against attacks such as Replay, Sybil, and Constant Value injection. This research lays the groundwork for scalable, secure, and autonomous IoT deployments in domains such as smart infrastructure, industrial monitoring, and environmental sensing.

Author: Tahir, M.; Kumar, M.; Sajid, Z.; Zheng, X.
Title: SIoT-Based Classification of Trustworthy Nodes by Using Machine Learning Techniques
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
Abstract Note: The “Social Internet of Things” (SIoT) idea is rapidly evolving, bringing objects and Social Networking together to facilitate communication and collaboration. Nonetheless, there are challenges in making sure the security and reliability of the SIoT system given the attributes and vulnerabilities associated with the nodes. Though there has been extensive exploration in different Machine Learning techniques for trustworthy node classification in SIoT systems, there still exists an enormous gap in conducting in-depth and multi-dimensional comparisons exploiting more than one clustering algorithm in combination with ensemble learning techniques for implementing the assessment task. The aim of the task is strengthening security systems and decision-making techniques. Author: Surya, S.; Narayana, D.; S, S.; Gopalan, K. R.; Pathak, K. R.; Arunkumar, J. R.
Title: Retracted: Blockchain-Driven Access Control in Edge-Based Learning Environments

Abstract Note: The learning environments based on edges are gaining popularity because edge-aware learning can deliver low latency and distributed intelligence on edu-arrayed use cases like smart classroom, mobile learning, and federated training of AI. Nevertheless, edge computing is decentralized, which creates an especially high level of complexity during secure, reliable inputs in access control among a variety of devices and users. The centralized access control mechanism used in the past is not scalable, not trustworthy and does not have resilience. To provide solutions to these problems, this paper proposes blockchain-based access control framework that is suitable to edge-based learning environments. The framework uses smart contracts to automatically deal with role- and attribute-based controls of access control, which are transparent, non-modifiable, and resistant to tampering. We use smart contracts on the Ethereum blockchain to deploy a prototype and make a simulation of the settings of an edge-learning scenario to measure performance facets like latency and gas cost and access decision time. It also discusses cases of practical application and describes the challenges and prospects of scalable, blockchain secured learning infrastructures.

Author: Manikandan, S.; Kaur, A.; Suri, S.; M, D.; A, S.; Badiger, V. S.

Abstract Note: The immersive and dynamic evolution of the Metaverse and Internet of Everything IoE architectures have presented a novel magnitude of interconnective immersion, experience and immediate data interactions amid heterogeneous devices and platforms. Though such dynamic environments accommodate a rich interaction with users and digital economies, they are also prone to emerging cybersecurity threats that cannot be tackled by the standard traditional approaches to cyber defense that deploy a model based on static environments. In this study, the author outlines a high level AI driven adaptive cyber security framework, AICAS F2M AI Driven Context Aware Security Framework for Future Metaverse, with the aim of securing future metaverse environments in a proactive fashion. The framework is based on a combination of deep learning to anomaly detection, the solution of federated learning based privacy preserving threat intelligence sharing, blockchain, and decentralized trust and identity, and a zero trust architecture to continuously verify users and devices. Author: Liao, T.; Yan, H.; Lin, J.; Cheng, Y.; Chen, F.
Title: FedANC: Towards Accurate and Learnable Knowledge-Aware Neighbor Collaboration in Personalized Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 31th International Conference on Parallel and Distributed Systems (ICPADS)
Abstract Note: In non-identically and independently distributed (non-IID) data scenarios, traditional federated learning struggles to meet diverse client needs due to the limitations of the global model aggregation. Personalized Federated Learning (PFL) tackles this challenge by improving model personalization for individual clients while preserving the benefits of collaboration. However, existing approaches are hindered by direct aggregation strategies, which lead to gradient conflicts and overly rely on parameter similarity for collaboration evaluation, resulting in unstable generalization. In this paper, we propose FedANC, a PFL framework that learns structured and stable collaborative relationships through three key components: (1) a trusted collaboration graph construction to identify reliable neighbors and filter low-quality paths; (2) a trainable cooperative weight matrix W to adaptively adjust aggregation intensity; and (3) an intermediate parameter mechanism that guides local model alignment using weighted neighbor models, alleviating gradient conflicts. Experiments on image classification tasks under various non-IID distributions show that FedANC achieves higher test accuracy, more stable convergence compared to existing PFL approaches, and demonstrating the effectiveness of learnable and structured cooperation mechanisms.
Manual Tags: Personalized Federated Learning; Knowledge Collaboration; Learnable

Author: Dimlo, U. M. Fernandes; Yadav, G. G.; Reddy, E. A.; Naik, S. Rahul; Arjumand, A.; Shruthi, M.
Title: Energy Demand Forecasting for EVs using Block Chain based Data Integrity
Publication Title: 2025 3rd International Conference on Sustainable Computing and Data Communication Systems (ICSCDS)
Abstract Note: Electric Vehicles (EV) energy demand forecasting plays a pivotal role in ensuring efficient allocation and utilization of smart grid resources. The blockchain component enables decentralized, tamper-evident recording of EV energy consumption data, thereby ensuring data provenance, authenticity, and integrity across the system. This integration of secure data logging with predictive analytics not only enhances the trustworthiness of the forecasting process but also reinforces the reliability and consistency of model outputs. Author: Pramudito, D. K.; Na'am, J.; Ernawan, F.
Title: Trustworthy Multimodal Fraud Detection with Federated Learning and Computer Vision
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Blockchain, Cloud Computing, and Data Analytics (ICoABCD)
Abstract Note: Fraud detection in financial systems is still very difficult to do due to a vast class imbalance, how quickly fraudsters change their tactics and stringent privacy laws. This study interprets the XClever framework which is based on gradient fatigue and that embraces multi-modality and interpret-ability. These modifications include gradient boosting (XGBoost), attention-based gated recursive unit (GRU—Attention), cost sensitive thresholding, federated learning (FL) as well as computer vision (CV) extensions. This study employed a benchmark credit card dataset in this experiment. While GRU-Attention had a higher recall and better accuracy, XGBoost had the best precision and ROC—AUC (0.985). A late-fusion strategy can find a middle ground between these trade-offs, which could lead to the lowest predicted loss in costly calibration. The use of federate simulations shows that decentralized training with FedAvg preserves recall with only a slight decrease in ROC—AUC (0.010.02), while differential privacy further protects sensitive data. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) trained on feature grids and recurrence plots attain a ROC—AUC of approximately 0.96, with visual representations elucidating supplementary structural anomalies. SHAP explanations identify V14, V12, and V4 as primary predictors, ensuring transparency and compliance with regulatory standards. The results indicate that an effective fraud detection system necessitates a comprehensive workflow that includes imbalance-aware learning, multimodal representation, privacy preserving collaboration, and explainability to ensure a reliable and scalable implementation within the financial services ecosystem.

Author: Shishodia, A.; Sharma, A.; Chaudhary, G.; Saraswat, B. K.; Vashist, P. C.; Singh, N.
Title: AI-Driven Anomaly Detection in IoT Networks: A Blockchain-Based Approach for Tamper-Proof Security
Publication Title: 2025 1st IEEE Uttar Pradesh Section Women in Engineering International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computer Engineering (UPWIECON)
Abstract Note: The growth of IoT networks at a fast pace has posed huge security challenges, especially regarding detecting anomalies and mitigating them, and guaranteeing the integrity of data. This contribution develops an AI-based anomaly detection framework incorporated with blockchain, offering tamper-proof security in IoT environments. By utilizing deep learning techniques (such as Auto-Encoders and LSTM networks), the system can detect outliers in real-time and act to mitigate threats as they happen. The AI module processes high-dimensional data streams from the IoT to learn intricate patterns for detecting anomalies. It can enable IT personnel to identify intrusions, device failures, and cyberattacks at a very granular level. To log and trace detected anomalies immutably, anomalies BELs are saved into a permissioned blockchain so that non-authorized parties cannot change them and that an auditable trace is available for forensic analysis. When used in combination with smart contracts, responses to threats can be done automatically, which is helpful in terms of accelerating incident response times, like isolating infected nodes or alerting system administrators. This hybrid methodology offers the agility of AI and the distributed security of the blockchain, which solves core weaknesses of the conventional centralized anomaly detection systems, such as single point of failure, data tampering vulnerabilities, among others. Experimental results on benchmark IQT datasets show that the proposed method can achieve better detection accuracy (>98%) and is robust against adversarial attacks, compared with the state of the art. This architecture, scalable, transparent, and strong, provides for secure, critical IoT infrastructure, including smart cities and industrial IoT, where data authenticity and real-time threat response are indispensable.

Author: N, L.; Kaliappan, S.; Muthukannan, M.; Priyadharshini, R.; M, R.
Title: Soft Actor Critic Reinforcement Learning for Decentralized Secured Drone System
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 5th International Conference on ICT in Business Industry & Government (ICTBIG)
Abstract Note: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are gaining more interest in the latest technologies based on their growing features. It is primarily used in emergency response systems, including disaster management, surveillance, and cybersecurity. As the drones operate autonomously, there is a high risk to the security of the data collected by the drones, which can be misused or subject to data spoofing. This occurs when the centralised system is opted for, where the sensed information is transmitted to it. It is also seen that the intrusion detection in the drone system needs to be communicated to the drones to avoid further loss of information. Based on this objective, this paper proposes the Federated Learning approach for the drone system, which uses only the gradients for data transmission. Soft Actor Critic Reinforcement Learning helps in detecting anomalies and determining necessary actions based on the critic's reward update. Thus, the proposed system functions dynamically by detecting intrusion activity and mitigating it by communicating the information to both the onboard and offboard systems of drone control. The proposed work was evaluated using the AIDER dataset from GitHub, which showed 92% trajectory accuracy with 3% collision loss.

Author: Sowan, B. I.; Zighan, S.; Altarawneh, A.

Author: Athamena, M. R.; Houhamdi, Z.; Athamena, B.
Title: Edge—Based Lightweight AI for Real—Time Intrusion Detection in IoT Networks
Publication Title: 2025 12th International Conference on Internet of Things: Systems, Management and Security (IOTSMS)
Abstract Note: The explosive growth of Internet of Things (IoT) deployments has introduced critical security challenges, as resource-constrained devices often lack the computer and energy to support traditional defenses. Signature-based IDS techniques cannot catch novel attacks, while heavyweight anomaly detectors (e.g., deep neural networks or SVMs) incur unacceptable latency and resource use. To address this, we propose an edge-centric intrusion detection framework that integrates lightweight AI models with edge computing. In our design, IoT devices send network data to a local edge gateway, which performs realtime anomaly detection using a pruned machine learning model (e.g., a small LSTM or decision-tree ensemble) optimized for limited hardware. This on-device approach reduces communication overhead and latency compared to cloud-based IDS (Intrusion Detection System). Key features are selected and optimized to keep the model compact (using techniques like tree-based feature importance) while retaining high detection capability. The expected impact is a low-power, real-time IDS that can promptly identify threats (e.g., IoT DDoS, spoofing, or data injection) with minimal false alarms, improving the robustness of smart homes, healthcare, and industrial IoT systems. Future work may extend this framework with adaptive learning at the edge and decentralized coordination for large-scale IoT security.

Author: SN, P.; Shelke, N.; Saini, D. K. J. B.; Pimpalkar, A.; Kumar, G. H.; D, S.

Abstract Note: Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs) are a formidable and ever-evolving threat to global cyber security, particularly against critical infrastructure, government networks, and cyber-physical systems. Recent advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI), such as deep learning, federated learning, graph neural networks, reinforcement learning, and adversarial learning, have introduced novel paradigms for real-time threat detection and proactive defense strategies. This paper presents a comprehensive and organized overview of state-of-the-art AI-based solutions for the detection, attribution, deception, and response to APTs. Illustrative case studies from sectors like financial networks, healthcare networks, cloud infrastructures, and national critical assets are discussed, highlighting realistic challenges, performance metrics, and optimal implementation practices. Emerging challenges are also explored, such as data availability constraints, labeling inconsistencies, risks of model compromise, vulnerability to adversarial attacks, and scalability constraints in real-time. The findings emphasize the supreme necessity of interdisciplinary research, as well as collaborative activities by academia, industry, and government, to create scalable, explainable, and anticipatory cyber security solutions that can effectively address APTs in future digital ecosystems.

Author: Kumari, A.; Raval, N.; Shah, R.; Assaad, M.

The deployment utilizes a simulated metaverse environment, with avatars created through Blender. Author: Reddy, P. V.; Enugala, V. K.; Prasad, S.; Tiwari, M. G. D.; Akarapu, S.; Siripuri, K.

Author: Hong, Y.; Hao, G.; Wu, J.

This work proposes an adaptive multi-party secure information-sharing framework based on digital twins (DT). Specifically, we introduce virtual representations of vehicles operating within an edge-centric DT architecture, thereby overcoming the limitations imposed by unstable physical links. Author: Meenakshi, M.; Vijayakumar, L.; Baliyan, M.; Ramana, V. V.; Reddy, B. A.; Srivastava, M.

Author: Pachorkar, P. R.; Ponnusamy, S.; Karale, A.
Title: A Secure and Intelligent Blockchain-Based E-Voting System Using Multimodal Voter Authentication and Smart Contract Optimization
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Future Technologies (ICFT)
Abstract Note: This paper proposes a secure and intelligent blockchain-based e-voting framework that integrates advanced artificial intelligence (AI) techniques to enhance the integrity, efficiency, and transparency of digital elections. The system is designed to overcome major limitations of existing e-voting models, including weak identity verification, high gas costs, and limited anomaly detection. Abstract Note: Recently, federated learning (FL) has been considered a promising and well-suited technique for edge computing applications, such as intelligent traffic control, autonomous driving, and mobile crowdsensing. Personalized FL (PFL) has then received considerable attention to tackle this problem. Many existing PFL works often employ knowledge distillation to mitigate the negative effects of data heterogeneity. In this work, we leverage the knowledge contained in global features to explore the potential of global models and propose a novel uncertainty-driven feature distillation framework called FedUFD. Specifically, we design an uncertainty estimation module in local models, by estimating the uncertainty of the personalized feature distribution, FedUFD can measure the difficulty of learning different personalized features, and then combine the global features to distill the corresponding personalized features. Abstract Note: Cancer prediction using machine learning is pivotal in advancing early diagnosis and treatment. This study introduces a hybrid SVM-XGBoost model that leverages SVM for feature extraction and XGBoost for classification, combining their strengths for enhanced predictive performance. Author: S, L.; Jaleel, D. A.; T.Nandhakumar; S, D.; Poornima, G.; Abdulkalamazad, G.
Title: Self-learning Cognitive Digital Twin Network of Autonomous Risk Intelligence and Predictive Fraud Protection in Next-Gen Banking
Publication Title: 2025 5th International Conference on Evolutionary Computing and Mobile Sustainable Networks (ICECMSN)
Abstract Note: This paper presents the GenFedNet, a Self-Learning Cognitive Digital Twin architecture for autonomous risk intelligence and predictive fraud detection in the next-generation digital banking systems. Traditional fraud detection has been based on static rules or static machine learning models that are losing the war against fast-changing cyberfraud vectors. The proposed GenFedNet proposes cognitive digital twin, which can learn and adapt to the individual customers' behavior, transaction patterns, and contextual variations continuously via neuro-symbolic reasoning and federated optimization. Each twin simulates dynamic behavioral characteristics including spending rhythm, device usage, geo-location mobility and temporal variation to develop a unique behavioral fingerprint. Experimental results report performance of GenFedNet with 97% accuracy, 96% precision, 98% recall, and 97% F1-score by beating the experimental results of baseline models (SVM, Random Forest, CNN, FedCNN) with 12 to18% improvements. It also proves to be up to 40% less inference latency while retaining 95% security accuracy, which means faster decision making while dealing in real-time transactions. Both the stable anomaly and the consistent self-learning behavior of the model are represented by the trend of anomaly stability and fraud probability confidence, which validates the good prediction ability of the model. The system is scalable, privacy-preserving and interpretable, and fills the gap in today's banking ecosystem between operational intelligence and proactive security. This research will be extended with research on multi-modal behavioral fusion, blockchain-enabled model governance, and cross-institutional federated collaboration towards achieving advanced levels of transparency, fairness, and resilience in the defense against financial fraud.

Author: E, V. R.; Rajasekhar, A.; Azib, L. M.; Reddy, M. P. S.; Reddy, B. J.; Amala, K.
Title: Federated and Explainable Verifiable Accountable Keyword Searchable Encryption for Multi-Tenant Cloud Environments
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent Computing, Information and Control Systems (ICOIICS)
Abstract Note: As federated and multi-cloud ecosystems grow at a very high rate, ensuring secure and verifiable keyword search in data silos that are independently operated is a critical issue. This research is based on the Privacy-Preserving and Trusted Keyword Search for Multi-Tenancy Cloud (VAKSE and PVAKSE) framework and presents an Enhanced Federated and Explainable VAKSE (F-EVAKSE) one. The suggested framework combines a blockchain-based accountability layer with a quantum-resistant lattice encryption module to provide verifiable, auditable, and privacy that will last into the future. In addition, explainable verification metrics are also built in to identify abnormal or malicious query behaviors based on interpretable attention-weighted learning. Experiments performed on the Enron and Wikipedia datasets (517K and 9.2M documents, respectively) show that, on average (compared to PVAKSE), the encryption time has decreased by 37.8 % and parallel search efficiency has increased by 42.5 %, and the average latency to verify a token is 0.01 s. The suggested F EVAKSE model has a verification accuracy of 99.3 percent, an accountability accuracy of 96.5 percent, and compensates less than 3.1 percent of computation costs in federated clouds. The findings show that F-EVAKSE offers scalable, transparent, quantum-resilient, and keyword search with high privacy guarantees that make it suitable for cross-tenant and crosscloud deployment.

Author: Rajendran, S. S. Punyam; Gebremedhin, A.
Title: A Distributed Hierarchical Framework for Self-Sustaining and Autonomous Multi-Energy Microgrid Communities
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
Abstract Note: Environmental issues and ever-increasing energy demands have increased the need for cleaner, sustainable, and advanced energy systems. Multi-energy microgrids that integrate the electrical, heating, and transportation sectors are a promising solution for reducing emissions and improving efficiency through network synergies. However, the future of energy systems lies in peer-to-peer (P2P) energy-trading frameworks that enable end-users to participate in the local energy market for profit, thereby reducing grid dependency. Despite recent advances, existing approaches lack integrated frameworks that combine rapid adaptation, scalable coordination, and robust market mechanisms while addressing practical deployment challenges. This study proposes a conceptual framework for a distributed hierarchical meta-reinforcement learning (meta-RL)-based P2P energy-trading framework for the coordination of multiple residential multi-energy microgrids, establishing a theoretical foundation for self-sustaining and autonomous communities. The proposed architecture employs a three-tier approach: (1) a metaRL module using the Reptile algorithm for a generalizable policies that can rapidly adapt to specific microgrids, (2) a P2P module utilizing a multi-agent soft actor-critic (MASAC) to coordinate between multiple microgrids and identify trading opportunities, and (3) a Stackelberg-Continuous Double Auction (CDA) hybrid market mechanism to ensure optimal price and market stability. The possibility of integrating cloud-fog-edge computing, federated learning, and blockchain to address wide-scale adoption challenges, such as cybersecurity considerations and computational constraints, was also discussed.
Manual Tags: distributed computing; microgrids; distributed framework; cyber-security; meta-reinforcement learning; multi-energy systems; peer-to-peer energy trading

Author: Putteti, S.; Santhi, G.; Mittoor, G. R.; Nagamani, C.; Udayaraju, P.
Title: Intelligent Industrial IoT: A Data-Driven Approach for Smart Manufacturing and Predictive Maintenance
Publication Title: 2025 Third International Conference on Augmented Intelligence and Sustainable Systems (ICAISS)
Abstract Note: The fast growth of the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) has changed modern manufacturing by allowing real-time data collection, smart automation, and predictive analysis. This study introduces an Intelligent Industrial IoT (I-IIoT) system that combines edge computing, artificial intelligence (AI), and big data analysis to support smart manufacturing and predictive maintenance. The proposed model uses machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) to identify equipment issues, predict failures, and improve production. A cloud-edge hybrid setup processes data in real time, reducing delays and making the system more responsive. A blockchain-based data-sharing method ensures data security, privacy, and smooth communication between IIoT systems. Comparisons with traditional maintenance methods reveal significant improvements, such as over 95% accuracy in predictions, a 30% reduction in downtime, and 25% better use of resources. These results suggest that data-driven IIoT solutions can transform industrial operations by improving automation, security, and decision-making, leading to the next level of smart factories.

Author: Ramya, S.; Pooja, V.; Preethi, K.; Priyanka, P.

Author: Zhao, F.
Title: Application and Performance Improvement of K-Means Algorithm in Collaborative
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent Systems and Computational Networks (ICISCN)
Abstract Note: With the popularity of Internet of Things (IoT) devices (IDs), blockchain networks provide computing, communication and caching functions for IDs by sinking cloud services to fog nodes (FNs) near users, promoting the development of edge computing, reducing the delay of user requests and easing network congestion. However, the cache resources of FNs are limited, and the network environment and user needs are constantly changing. Therefore, device concepts need to be optimized to improve resource efficiency and system-wide network performance. In addition, the distribution of FN also represents cybersecurity and data security. To avoid these problems, this paper creates a Group User Preference (CUPE) algorithm based on K-means algorithm. This algorithm integrates local and global content popularity, which can improve cache hit rates and reduce content retrieval latency. Through the cloud based collaborative architecture, IDs and FNs collaborate to cache popular content. The CUPE algorithm is based on user characteristics, uses K-means algorithm to cluster IDs, and uses deep neural network to predict content trends. Fn algorithm converges the local model parameters to the global model and further optimizes the cache performance. This paper proposes a cluster Federated Learning (BCFL) algorithm that combines blockchain technology and federated learning to address cybersecurity risks. This algorithm ensures the security and trustworthiness of FL through blockchain, improves model training efficiency through personalized learning, and optimizes edge caching. The simulation results show that the BCFL algorithm performs excellently in terms of security assurance, cache hit efficiency, and content retrieval latency.

Author: Wang, L.; Huang, X.; Li, Q.
Title: Application of Sharing Mechanism Based on Big Data and Cloud Computing in Smart Grid
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 8th International Conference on Information Systems and Computer Aided Education (ICISCAE)
Abstract Note: With the exponential growth of multi-source heterogeneous data in smart grids, data sharing models face bottlenecks such as low cross-system integration efficiency and high risk of privacy leakage. To this end, this study proposes a sharing mechanism based on big data and cloud computing. First, this paper constructs a multi-source data standardization processing framework based on knowledge graph. Secondly, an access control model based on dynamic Bayesian network is designed to realize hierarchical dynamic permission management; finally, this paper proposes a hybrid architecture of “blockchain + federated learning” to realize distributed computing under privacy protection. Experimental results show that the knowledge graph-based framework reduces the integration time by about 20% under large data volume; in the real-time data sharing delay test, the proposed method significantly reduces the data sharing delay; in the abnormal access identification accuracy test, the model based on dynamic Bayesian network has an accuracy of 95.4% in abnormal access identification, which is significantly better than the RBAC (Role-Based Access Control) model. These results verify the effectiveness of the proposed sharing mechanism in improving the efficiency of smart grid data processing, reducing latency and enhancing security.

Author: Singh, R.; Khan, A.; Purohit, N.; Lokulwar, P.
Title: Adaptive Multi-Layered Authentication Framework for Secure and Individualized Access to Health Data Sets
Publication Title: 2025 3rd International Conference on Sustainable Computing and Data Communication Systems (ICSCDS)
Abstract Note: Because the magnitude of health data is increasing exponentially, it mandates a comprehensive mechanism to authenticate, secure, and trace accesses to sensitive patient data samples. Current authentication systems for data in the healthcare sector are bound by the static nature of their cryptographic protocols, centralized access control processes, and the very limited provenance analyses associated with access. The aforementioned gaps in patient-specific authentication, behavioral validation, and future-proofing against quantum threats leave such systems exposed to threats for data tampering, replay attacks, and unauthorized access, thereby affecting data integrity and non-repudiation guarantees. This document contains a detailed and original multi-layered framework for patient-specific data authentication, using five analytically grounded mechanisms to accompany it in process. The PHT-AEE enhances the integrity of and resistance to replay commands for dynamic hash trees tagged with entropy for the securing of the data chunks through a patient-centric hash tree with adaptive entropy encoding. Identity-bound homomorphic encryption includes patient biometric identity with a session timestamp to eliminate impersonation and ensure temporal validity within the process. The federated zero-trust proof with behavioural access drift uses federated learning integrated with an LSTM-based model of behavioural drift to enable zero-trust, behaviourally aware access control. The graph neural network for provenance integrity tracing builds and analyses data transformation paths that may have been tainted through contextual graph reasoning. Finally, the Quantum-Ledger Integrated Access Resolver consolidates future-resilient access authorization in post-quantum keys integrated with immutable blockchain records. Such integrated approach leads to tremendous advancements in access security, provenance accuracy, and cryptographic resilience. Collectively, the proposed methods enhance the integration of data integrity, non-repudiation, session trust, and legal auditability, establishing a future-ready authentication model tailored for scalable, secure, and personalized healthcare systems.
Manual Tags: Homomorphic Encryption; Data Integrity; Quantum-Resistant Security; Applications; Patient Authentication; Provenance Tracking

Author: Kandelkar, A.; Kshirsagar, V.; Maral, S.; Chougule, S.; Rasekar, S.; Varade, A.
Title: Multimodal Biometric Authentication System
Publication Title: 2025 9th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control and Automation (ICCCBEA)
Abstract Note: Multimodal biometric authentication integrates facial, voice, fingerprint, and physiological signals to enhance security and accuracy, addressing limitations of unimodal systems such as spoofing, data variability, and low accuracy in complex environments. With the advent of Vision Transformers (ViTs), these systems have made significant strides in feature extraction, multimodal fusion, and real-time authentication. The Vision Transformer (ViT) processes images as sequences of patches instead of using convolutional filters. It splits an image into fixed-size patches, flattens them into vectors, and applies positional encoding to retain spatial information. The proposed method provides a comprehensive review of transformer based multimodal biometric authentication, analysing key challenges, fusion techniques, and security concerns. Additionally, it explores privacy-preserving approaches, including block chain based biometric security, federated learning, and cryptographic methods, to safeguard sensitive data. The review also discusses future research directions, focusing on lightweight architectures, quantum-secure authentication, and Edge AI integration for scalable and efficient biometric authentication systems. Facial expression recognition using Efficient LBP and CNN achieves 90 % accuracy on the CK+ dataset by leveraging LBP for feature extraction and CNN for classification. Efficiency, scalability, and privacy protection will be addressed in future studies, utilizing blockchain and edge computing for tamper-proof authentication. ViTs' capacity to model global dependencies and withstand spoofing attacks positions them as the perfect choice for nextgeneration biometric systems.

Author: Gao, T.; Wang, S.; Geng, X.; Zhang, L.; Jing, M.; Yu, T.; Yu, J.
Title: A Stackelberg Game Pricing for Blockchain-Based Industrial Internet of Things Data Market
Publication Title: 2025 28th International Conference on Computer Supported Cooperative Work in Design (CSCWD)
Abstract Note: The vigorous development of the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) has brought massive amounts of data. In order to serve users more extensively and fully utilize the potential of data, it is particularly important to establish a fair and open IIoT data market. In order to enhance trust between data owners and consumers and facilitate transactions between the two parties, this article proposes a blockchain-based IIoT data market framework. To address another important issue in the IIoT data market: data pricing, we formulate the problem of maximizing the interests of the data platform, data providers, and consumers as a Stackelberg game pricing model. In this model, the data platform charges the data provider for data transmission, the data provider sells data to the consumer, and the consumer can determine the amount of data to purchase. The existence of Stackelberg equilibrium is proved by backward induction. Finally, the performance of the model was evaluated through numerical simulations.

Author: Thorushe, K.; Desai, K. R.

Abstract Note: The rapid expansion of Internet of Things (IoT) network based devices has increased the vulnerability to Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks, creating a need for fast and intelligent detection frameworks. Author: V, M. T.; C, M.; A, G. M.
Title: Machine Learning in Environmental Sustainability for Accurate Carbon Emission Analysis

Abstract Note: Urban sustainability increasingly relies on accurate and privacy-preserving carbon emissions forecasting, yet traditional centralised learning systems present significant risks of data exposure, high energy consumption, and delays in processing. This study introduces FLARC, a novel federated learning framework that leverages smart meters, traffic infrastructure, and vehicle nodes as decentralised data sources for real-time, multi-domain carbon prediction within urban environments. FLARC incorporates a carbon-intensity-aware scheduling strategy, which ensures that model training occurs preferentially during periods of high renewable energy availability by integrating real-time carbon intensity signals from the power grid. The methodology emphasises privacy, scalability, and environmental responsibility by minimising sensitive data transfer and adapting to varying urban conditions. Author: Nalluri, S.; Malyala, M. M.; Kandagiri, H.; Kandagiri, K. K.
Title: NSCTI: A Hybrid Neuro-Symbolic Framework for AI-Driven Predictive Cyber Threat Intelligence
Publication Title: 2025 4th International Conference on Computational Modelling, Simulation and Optimization (ICCMSO)
Abstract Note: With the rapid evolution of cyber threats, traditional Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven security models often fail to provide real-time, interpretable, and adaptive threat intelligence. This paper proposes Neuro-Symbolic Cyber Threat Intelligence (NSCTI), a novel hybrid framework that integrates Deep NeuroSymbolic Learning (DNSL) with Graph-Based Threat Reasoning (GBTR) to enhance predictive cybersecurity analytics. The NSCTI framework comprises three core components: Hybrid Deep Learning-Based Threat Detection (HDL-TD), which leverages Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) for dynamic attack pattern recognition; Neuro-Symbolic Adversarial Defense (NSAD), which employs reinforcement learning-driven adversarial resilience mechanisms to mitigate evolving cyber threats; and Trust-Aware Federated Cyber Intelligence (TFCI), which utilizes federated learning (FL) and blockchain-based threat sharing to ensure secure, decentralized CTI. Experimental evaluations on benchmark datasets (CICIDS2017, UNSW-NB15, and N-BaIoT) demonstrate that NSCTI achieves 99.7% attack detection accuracy, a 0.5 % false positive rate (FPR), and a 35% reduction in computational overhead compared to existing cybersecurity frameworks. Security analysis confirms NSCTI's robustness against Man-in-the-Middle (MITM), replay attacks, and adversarial perturbations, making it a scalable and proactive cyber defense solution. Future research will explore quantumenhanced neuro-symbolic learning and self-adaptive reinforcement learning to further strengthen autonomous cybersecurity in large-scale IoT networks.
Manual Tags: Reinforcement Learning; GNN; Neuro-Symbolic AI; Federated Cyber Intelligence; Hybrid Threat Detection

In order to validate the performance of machine learning over anomaly detection on cloud, ten different machine learning algorithms are applied on three datasets. In dataset 3 AdaboostM1, NaiveBayes and VotedPerceptron performed best in terms of recall, F1-score, and accuracy with values 0.831081, 0.754413 and 0.831081 respectively, while in terms of precision decision tree, hoeffeding tree and J48 performed best with same value of 0.711735. Author: Wang, F.; Shen, T.; Zhu, K.; Zhang, L.
Title: Toward Online Sharding in One-Sided Feedback Scenario
Publication Title: 2025 28th International Conference on Computer Supported Cooperative Work in Design (CSCWD)
Abstract Note: Sharding is a promising solution for improving blockchain scalability by distributing the workload across smaller groups of nodes called shards. However, it presents significant challenges, such as balancing tradeoffs between transactions per second (TPS), cross-shard transactions (CSTx), and confirmation latency in dynamic, online environments. While increasing the number of shards enhances TPS within individual shards, it also raises CSTx frequency, leading to higher failure probabilities, increased communication overhead, and prolonged confirmation times. Moreover, managing the number of shards and their configurations under one-sided feedback scenarios adds further complexity. To address these challenges, we model sharding as an online one-sided feedback optimization problem, focusing on maximizing long-term utilities. We introduce a polynomial-time online algorithm that adapts selection probabilities based on feedback information to address this NP-hard problem. Through rigorous analysis, we demonstrate that our approach achieves dynamic regret that grows sub-linearly over time. Extensive evaluations on real-world datasets confirm that our method outperforms existing baseline algorithms in terms of practical performance.

Title: Lightweight Device Fingerprint Construction and Edge-Side Real-Time Identification Technology for Dynamic Power Communication Networks
Publication Title: 2025 4th International Conference on Networks, Communications and Information Technology (CNCIT)
Abstract Note: With the rapid expansion of smart grids and Industrial IoT, the dynamic and heterogeneous nature of power communication networks poses significant challenges for terminal device identification, including IP spoofing, resource constraints, and real-time requirements. Existing solutions, such as cryptographic authentication and static fingerprinting, struggle to balance security, efficiency, and adaptability. This paper proposes a lightweight device fingerprinting framework leveraging edge computing and federated learning to address these challenges. First, we design a multi-domain dynamic feature extraction method that integrates protocol semantics (e.g., Modbus function codes), traffic periodicity, and physical layer characteristics (e.g., channel-state fingerprints) to enhance robustness against IP/MAC spoofing. Second, a compressed hybrid neural network (CNN-LSTM) is developed using knowledge distillation and feature hashing, reducing computational overhead by 58% compared to centralized models. Third, an edge-cloud collaborative architecture deploys lightweight models on edge gateways, achieving real-time identification with latency below 30ms while preserving data privacy through federated updates. Evaluations on real-world power IoT datasets (5,000+ devices) demonstrate 98.6% accuracy in dynamic environments, outperforming traditional SVM and blockchain-based schemes. Additionally, the framework detects silent intrusion devices in Fieldbus networks with 96.3% precision by analyzing channel-state group fingerprints. This work bridges the gap between resource efficiency and security in large-scale power communication systems.
Manual Tags: Federated learning; Edge computing; Dynamic feature extraction; Lightweight device fingerprint; Power communication network

Author: Rajasekaran, R. T.; Selvam, M.
Title: Enhancing User Interaction in Digital Financial Systems Using AI-Driven Front-End Technologies: A Personalised Response Approach
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
Abstract Note: This study highlights the rapid advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML), which have transformed the financial sector by enhancing personalised user interactions and customer engagement. An innovative AI-driven framework was proposed to deliver real-time, context-aware, and highly personalised responses for Digital Banking users. The system architecture employs advanced ML models, natural language processing (NLP) techniques, and modern front-end technologies such as React and GraphQL to address the challenges related to data silos, computational demand, and data privacy. ML models such as user segmentation, recommendation, and NLP models work together to analyse user behaviour, predict needs, and generate human-like responses. Utilising React, GraphQL subscriptions, and Edge AI, the front-end layer ensures a seamless and responsive user experience. The experimental results showed a 120% increase in click-through rates, a 180% increase in follow-up actions, and a 70% reduction in average response time, demonstrating significant improvements in user engagement. User satisfaction, measured by the Net Promoter Score, was significantly higher for the personalised system (8.5) than for the traditional system (5.2). The proposed methodology lays the foundation for an agile trust-based financial environment. Future enhancements will focus on explainable AI, multimodal interactions, and blockchain integration to boost transparency, engagement, and data privacy.

Author: Fan, J.; Zhang, C.; Cai, X.; Jiang, Z. L.; Au, M. H.; Yiu, S. M.
Title: Centralized Multi-Key Fully Homomorphic Encryption from CKKS
Publication Title: 2025 5th International Conference on Computer Science and Blockchain (CCSB)
Abstract Note: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) enables computation over encrypted data without revealing its content. However, most existing FHE schemes are designed for singlekey settings, limiting their use in collaborative applications involving multiple data owners. Multi-Key FHE (MKFHE) extends support to such scenarios but often incurs ciphertext expansion proportional to the number of participants and relies on complex, multi-round decryption. We propose a Centralized Multi-key Fully Homomorphic Encryption (CMKFHE) scheme that enables efficient and scalable multiuser computation. Each child node holds a distinct FHE key derived from public parameters generated by the parent, and functions as a standard FHE system. Ciphertexts produced by different children also support homomorphic evaluation, with the result decryptable only by a parent node possessing a master key. Computations within a child domain remain decryptable by that child, while sibling nodes cannot access each other's ciphertexts. We present a construction based on the CKKS framework that supports approximate arithmetic and ciphertext packing while maintaining constant ciphertext size, making it suitable for applications such as federated learning and privacy-preserving analytics.
Manual Tags: CKKS; Fully Homomorphic Encryption; Multi-key Fully Homomorphic Encryption

Author: Gharami, K.; Parrilla, M.; Bhullar, H. K.; Davis, W. A.; Moni, S. S.
Title: Intrusion Detection in IoT: A Comprehensive Review of Techniques, Challenges, and Future Directions
Publication Title: 2025 1st International Conference on Secure IoT, Assured and Trusted Computing (SATC)
Abstract Note: The Internet of Things (IoT) has rapidly evolved, creating a vast network of interconnected devices that increasingly impact everyday life. However, this widespread adoption has also attracted the attention of cybercriminals, exposing IoT devices to a wide range of malicious attacks. Various IoT Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) have been developed to combat these threats, utilizing machine learning techniques, algorithms, and customized solutions to effectively address the unique challenges encountered by highly collaborative IoT environments. This paper offers a comprehensive review of the evolving landscape of IoT IDS, exploring various detection techniques, deployment strategies, validation approaches, and key datasets used for developing and training IDS. We also explore common IoT network attack types, propose a detailed IDS taxonomy, and analyze existing datasets for training IDS. Finally, we highlight ongoing research challenges and future directions in securing the IoT ecosystem. The insights offered aim to unify diverse research efforts and provide a holistic view to advance the security of IoT systems.
Manual Tags: Internet of Things (IoT); Cybersecurity; IoT Security; Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS); IDS Taxonomy; IoT Network Attacks

Author: George, C. J.; Rajkumar, J. S.; Babu, N. V.
Title: Explainable Digital Twin Framework for Aircraft Engine Maintenance
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on NexGen Networks and Cybernetics (IC2NC)
Abstract Note: Growing dependence of modern aviation on aircraft engines underscores persistent challenges in balancing safety, reliability, and operational costs. Conventional maintenance practices, whether preventive or reactive, often prove inadequate, leading to premature component replacement, unscheduled downtime, and limited diagnostic transparency. To address these gaps, this study proposes an AI-driven digital twin framework that integrates predictive modeling, explainability, immersive visualization, and secure data management for aircraft engine maintenance. A Python-based simulator generates realistic IoT sensor streams replicating operational stresses, gradual degradation, and subtle anomalies, which are then analyzed using complementary machine learning models: an Isolation Forest for anomaly detection and a Random Forest Regressor for Remaining Useful Life (RUL) estimation. SHAP-based interpretability ensures that predictions remain transparent and traceable, a critical requirement for aviation applications. The framework further incorporates Unity 3D for interactive engine visualization and a Flutter mobile application for field-level accessibility, while blockchain-backed IoT logging and federated learning strengthen data integrity and collaborative scalability. Validation on synthetic datasets and the NASA C-MAPSS benchmark confirms improved robustness, with the Random Forest reducing RUL prediction error by over \30 \textbackslash{}%\ and the Isolation Forest achieving an F1-score of 0.89 for anomaly detection. These results specify the framework’s potential as a transparent, scalable, and industry-ready solution for predictive maintenance in aviation, with adaptability to other safety-critical domains such as manufacturing and energy.
Manual Tags: Digital Twin; Explainable AI; SHAP; Anomaly Detection; Predictive Maintenance; Aircraft Engines

Author: Koribilli, N.; Antara, F.; Ugli, Y. J. E.; Rajabov, R.; Ugli, I. T. K.
Title: Automating Compliance in Clinical Data Pipelines Using Policy-as-Code, NLP, and Blockchain-Inspired Auditing
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Sustainability, Innovation & Technology (ICSIT)
Abstract Note: Rapidly growing clinical data, augmented by digitization of health records and multi-site studies, is of tremendous potential but also an emerging regulatory challenge. Maintaining pace with new healthcare regulations such as HIPAA, GDPR, and 21 CFR Part 11 remains a top inhibitor to scaling clinical data pipelines. Traditional manual compliance checks take time, are error-prone, and are not well-suited for high-throughput data pipelines designed for today. In this paper, we outline a layered, automated compliance framework using policy-as-code, real time auditing, metadata tagging, and user-facing dashboards as part of clinical data infrastructure. We discuss the state of the art, define best practices in architectural design and discuss the primary challenges in developing automation at scale. The paper aims to offer health professionals, researchers, and technologists hands-on information to transform compliance into a bottleneck into a strategic enabler for secure and compliant innovation.
