Author: K, K.; Krishna, V.; Pragada, S. R. Rao Thirumala; Kantamani, R.; Nath, J. C.; Singh, S.
Title: Next Generation AI Powered Framework for Autonomous Energy Optimization and Real Time Anomaly Detection in IoT Driven Wireless Sensor Networks
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent Computing, Information and Control Systems (ICOIICS)
Abstract Note: The exponential growth of Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystems and Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) has created unprecedented challenges in energy efficiency, real-time reliability, and anomaly detection. LEACH, HEED, and Support Vector Machines (SVMs) are traditional routing and fault detection systems which provide partial solutions, but cannot be scaled to larger networks, nor adapted to changing conditions, nor consume less energy. To cover such problems, we suggest Next-Generation AI-Powered Framework of Autonomous Energy Optimization and Real-Time Anomaly Detection in IoT-Based WSNs. The design uses a layered architecture (sensor-edge-fog-cloud) to give it modularity and scalability. Preprocessing of data is done by the methods of normalization and imputation to assure high quality input. An Energy-Aware Graph Neural Network (GNN) is used to achieve energy optimization which is combined with dynamic duty cycling, adaptive power control, and clustering. To detect anomalies, a hybrid model of LSTM Autoencoder-Bayesian Network model is used, which involves the use of both the temporal pattern recognition and probabilistic reasoning. It is shown that the network lifetime is increased by 45 - 50 % and the anomaly detection engine has a 97.8 % accuracy, 97.2 % precision, and 97.0 % F1-score, which is far superior to base methods. Medium-scale deployments have latency that is maintained to less than 120 ms to be responsive. The trade-off optimization engine strikes a balance between the energy use and the detection performance by means of Pareto-front strategies. Moreover, Federated Learning using Blockchain ensures privacy-preservation, safe updates of the model and attains accuracy of 97.6 % with a 99 % trust validation. The suggested framework provides a scalable, energy-saving, and secure platform in mission-critical IoT applications, such as smart grids, medical, and industrial automation.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; Federated Learning; IoT; Anomaly Detection; Edge Intelligence; Energy Optimization; Wireless Sensor Networks

Author: Brahmandam, B. A.; Samanvita, N.; Aich, M.; Sengupta, D.; Tandon, N.
Title: A Hybrid Blockchain and Deep Learning Approach for Credit Card Fraud Detection using Slice Recurrent Neural Networks
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent and Cloud Computing (ICoICC)
Abstract Note: In this paper, we propose a hybrid blockchain and deep learning approach for credit card fraud detection, leveraging Slice recurrent neural networks (Slice-RNN) and blockchain technology. The study addresses the challenges posed by highly imbalanced datasets in fraud detection, exemplified by the ECC dataset, which contains only 0.172% fraudulent transactions. We introduce a two-pronged solution: first, employing advanced resampling techniques like SMOTE to tackle class imbalance, and second, utilizing the Slice-RNN architecture to efficiently process temporal data and enhance model convergence through parallelization. To further improve performance, we incorporate multi-head self-attention (MSA) and Bi-SGRU for bidirectional sequence modeling, which significantly boosts classification accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. The blockchain integration ensures secure, transparent, and real-time monitoring of credit card transactions, with smart contracts enabling automatic fraud detection and alerting. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms existing machine learning techniques, achieving a remarkable 97% accuracy, with enhanced fraud detection capabilities and reduced computational complexity. The hybrid approach presents a robust, scalable solution for detection of fraud in financial systems, offering higher reliability, efficiency, and security compared to traditional methods.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; Cyberattacks; Credit card fraud detection; Flag questionable transactions; Slice Recurrent Neural Network

Author: Duc, D. T. Anh; Le, H.-G.; Chu-Nguyen, H.-P.; Pham, V.-H.; Duy, P. T.
Title: Smart Contract Vulnerability Detection using Prompt Engineering with Reasoning Models
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Multimedia Analysis and Pattern Recognition (MAPR)
Abstract Note: The increasing deployment of smart contracts has drawn significant attention to the urgent need for robust and scalable vulnerability detection techniques to mitigate substantial financial risks associated with their immutable nature on blockchain platforms. This paper introduces structured reasoning prompts using agent-role chaining for vulnerability detection that utilizes model capacity to enhance smart contract security through zero-shot and structured prompt engineering without fine-tuning. By carefully defining agent roles and embedding explicit reasoning steps within structured prompts for large language models (LLMs), the proposed method exploits the inherent reasoning capabilities of LLMs to identify security flaws in smart contracts without extensive model retraining. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the system in achieving competitive performance compared to existing vulnerability detection techniques, highlighting the potential of prompt engineering as an efficient and adaptable strategy for enhancing smart contract security.

Author: Kariyappagowda, Y. B.; G, M.; Mahjabeen; T, S. T.; Pramod; K, P.
Title: Edge AI-Driven Vision Systems for Zero-Defect Manufacturing in 6G-Enabled Industry 5.0: The Factory of the Future
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Sustainability, Innovation & Technology (ICSIT)
Abstract Note: In the era of Industry 5.0, achieving zero-defect manufacturing is essential for enhancing production quality, minimizing waste, and ensuring operational efficiency. Traditional quality control systems—whether manual or cloud-based—face challenges such as high latency, limited scalability, and data security risks. This paper presents a novel Edge AIdriven vision system that leverages 6G connectivity to enable real-time defect detection on the manufacturing floor. The proposed solution integrates lightweight deep learning models and high-speed edge inference to eliminate the need for centralized processing, thereby reducing response times and energy consumption. Experimental validation using NVIDIA Jetson AGX Xavier demonstrates significant performance gains, including 99.2% defect detection accuracy, a 70% reduction in latency, and 40% lower energy consumption compared to conventional cloud-based approaches. These results underscore the system's potential to facilitate predictive maintenance, seamless human-AI collaboration, and real-time defect elimination—core principles of Industry 5.0. Despite these advancements, challenges such as model optimization for edge hardware, secure federated learning, and widespread 6G infrastructure adoption remain open research problems. Future work will focus on integrating neuromorphic computing and blockchain-enhanced AI for improved adaptability, security, and scalability. This research lays a strong foundation for intelligent, autonomous, and defect-free manufacturing in nextgeneration smart factories.

Author: Panizales, W.; Cortez, D. M.; Lagunzad, H.; Samonteza, C. M.
Title: iSecure: AI-Enhanced Blockchain-Based Network Intrusion Detection for Academic Institutions in the Philippines
Publication Title: 2025 6th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
Abstract Note: Academic institutions in the Philippines are rapidly adopting digital platforms for learning, research, and administration, but this shift has also made them more vulnerable to cyberattacks. Traditional intrusion detection systems (IDS) often face challenges in handling large traffic, detecting advanced threats, and providing timely responses. To address these issues, emerging approaches combine Artificial Intelligence (AI) and blockchain to build more secure and reliable security frameworks. AI-based IDS models, such as deep learning, federated learning, and anomaly detection, have shown improved accuracy in identifying cyber threats and reducing false alarms. However, AI alone may lack transparency and trust in multi-user environments. Blockchain technology offers immutability, decentralized trust, and tamper-proof logging, making it a strong complement to IDS. This paper proposes iSecure, an AI-enhanced blockchain-based IDS framework designed for Philippine academic institutions. By combining the smart detection capabilities of AI with the trusted record-keeping of blockchain, iSecure aims to strengthen cybersecurity resilience, protect sensitive academic data, and ensure safe digital learning and research.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; Cybersecurity; Intrusion Detection; Artificial Intelligence; Academic Institutions

Author: Verma, S.; Harshavardhan, K. P.; Ghumman, S.; Kavipriya, P.; Lakkangoudr, S.; Parivara, S. A.
Title: Advanced Deep Learning Architectures for Enhanced Predictive Accuracy in Decentralized Blockchain-Based Risk Mitigation
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 5th International Conference on ICT in Business Industry & Government (ICTBIG)
Abstract Note: In an age characterized by intelligent distributed systems, achieving proactive risk reduction by precise predictive modeling is a significant problem. This study introduces a unique methodology—Blockchain-Integrated Transformer Ensemble Framework (BiTE-F)—that combines sophisticated deep learning algorithms with decentralised blockchain systems to improve forecast accuracy and reliability in dynamic contexts. The proposed architecture utilizes an ensemble of Transformer-based models, trained local on node-specific data using federated learning methodologies, permit situational and domain-aware prediction avoiding the need for central data aggregating. To ensure data integrity, facilitate model transparency and provide tampering obstruction, BiTE-F incorporates an encrypted blockchain layer that documents hashing snapshot of training datasets, model revisions, and predictions records. A decentralized agreement technique, Proof-of-Model-Integrity (PoMI), guarantees the acceptance of only correct and reliable modeling their contributions into the global ensembles. Moreover, smart contracts are used for automating the creation of risk alerts and the corresponding mitigation solutions in real time. This collaborative integration enhances distributed systems with safe, transparent, and precise risk modeling capacities. The suggested approach is especially appropriate for sectors such as healthcare, financial services, industrial IoT, and cyber-physical systems, where trust, precision, and real-time insights are critical. The suggested BiTE-F framework had an overall accuracy of 98.6% in predicting performance.
Manual Tags: BAIH; BiTE-F; DRM; FDL; PoMI; TOC

Author: Sundarrajan, M.; Krishnan, S. B.; V, S. M.; Chakrabarti, P.
Title: Adaptive AI-Driven Intrusion Detection Systems for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles Networks
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Trends in Networks and Computer Communications (ETNCC)
Abstract Note: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are now used more widely in surveillance, farming, disaster management and industry, their safety and dependability are very important. Cyber-physical attacks are common for UAVs because they operate in hectic, diffuse and sometimes competitive settings. Currently, creating reliable IDS for UAVs requires setting up rules and thresholds that do not adapt to unexpected changes, resource tightness and urgent response needs. Despite recent IDS models using deep learning being more accurate, they are often complex to use, fail to detect actions promptly and have a hard time coping with emerging attacks in running environments. A trust metric for every node is managed to show its past reliability and important choices are made through voting that responds to trust values. The system is able to learn from delayed mission results, using online training to slowly perfect its detection boundaries and stay current with changes in its operations. Experiments with this system consistently show that it detects threats with accuracy reaching 94 %, reducing the inference time to \textbackslash{}mathbf{1 0. 1} \textbackslash{}text{ms}\-greater results than those seen in static IDS, heuristic solutions and typical conventional Deep Learning systems for various types of threats.

Author: Singh, A.; Birudugadda, R. B.; Singh, N.; Rao, M. N.; Reddy, P. Vamshi Vardhan
Title: Comparative Analysis of Supervised Algorithms for Machine Learning-Based Detection of Phishing Websites
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent and Secure Engineering Solutions (CISES)
Abstract Note: A large number of false alerts, slow reactions to zero-day threats and holes in their defense limit the ability of standard security systems to detect advanced phishing attacks. Both Decision Trees and Random Forest classifiers help with phishing detection; however, they have issues with fresh phishing URLs and especially when faced with adversarial attacks. We therefore introduce a Hybrid CNN-Based Approach for Spotting Phishing URLs that relies on spatial- temporal features and insights from Internet of Things data. CNNs check URL patterns for this system and combined with smart device access logs and uncommon network issues in IoT, it provides full phishing detection in real time. With temporal trend analysis, the model is able to deal with changing phishing styles and reduce the effect of new attacks. CNN-based classifiers have a 92.4% accuracy finding URLs in a set of 1.5 million, better than Random Forest (87.0%) and Decision Tree (82.4%). In addition, the model is able to protect against 89.3% of adversarial phishing attacks. Using automated phishing feature restoration and IoT network surveillance makes it much harder for threat actors to evade security. The model is built to be effective in IoT and edge systems using few resources, making it easy to detect threats quickly and with high performance. The deployment of the CNN-LSTM model together with the IoT -contextual intelligence and the FGSM-based anti-attack capability provides a new, extendable, and edge-compatible solution phishing detection.

Author: Sennan, S.; Beevi, S. Z.; Anuradha, K.; E, D.; Roopa, R.; V, D. G.
Title: Adaptive Routing in Urban Wireless Ad Hoc Networks Using AI-Assisted Algorithms
Publication Title: 2025 9th International Conference on Inventive Systems and Control (ICISC)
Abstract Note: Modern smart city applications as well as vehicular communication and emergency response systems heavily depend on Urban Wireless Ad Hoc Networks (UWAHNs). Conventional network routing procedures face multiple challenges in handling abrupt route topology changes and delayed performance and consume excessive energy while operating in unsecure environments. A proposed routing procedure incorporates artificial intelligence through reinforcement learning predictive models and hybrid optimization with PSO-GA to improve network performance characteristics. Real-time network condition analysis allows the algorithm to dynamically choose the best routing paths which enhances packet delivery and maximizes transmission effectiveness. The proposed routing design supported by AI assistance exceeds traditional methods according to extensive simulation results. Experimental results demonstrate the algorithm's delivery of 94.7% packet success rates while decreasing end-to-end delay by 40% with 30% reduced energy usage to extend the network's operational lifespan. The anomaly detection module powered by AI defends networks from black hole and wormhole and Sybil attacks while protecting users from cyber security threats. The convergence of edge computing and federated learning results in enhanced decision-making capabilities as well as adaptable network system features. Study data shows AI-driven adaptive routing constitutes an adaptable efficient and protected technical solution for UWAHNs. Future investigation includes blockchain security research along with artificial intelligence model enhancements and real-world network installation to boost large urban systems' efficiency.

Author: Sethi, M.; Kasu, V. R.; Malamuthu, B. K.; Al-Assaf, K. T.; Dutt, A.; Karthikeyan, G.
Title: Enhanced Cybersecurity in Enterprise Circumstances: A Behavior-Based Procedure to ML-Based Insider Threat Detection
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain and Distributed Systems Security (ICBDS)
Abstract Note: Insider threats have become one of the most challenging cybersecurity problems for enterprises, since it causes a tremendous impact on the financial, reputation, and operation. Legacy security tools, largely designed with external threats in mind, have failed to detect subtle, contextually-complex insider-induced security infractions. This study introduces a behavior-based ML-based solution that can be used to both reduce and identify the threats posed by legitimate users by analyzing usage patterns, access behaviors, and anomalous patterns from the established normal scheme of activities in enterprise systems. By using supervised and unsupervised ML techniques, we model user's behavior on several dimensions, such as login frequency, file access, email usage and system navigation pattern. These models are used for training in large-scale datasets with benign and malicious behaviors, to learn the system to detect in real-time the anomalies of the behavior referring for insider threats. The approach advocated derives from the two concepts of sensitivity to context of user intent and activity; in this way, it can differentiate between legitimate albeit anomalous behavior and truly malicious activity. Feature engineering is vital for transforming raw logs to meaningful indicators that improve model accuracy and minimize false positives. In addition, the system includes adaptive learning capabilities to adapt to new threats vectors and patterns of behaviors, so it remains current and robust. The proposed model is evaluated on real datasets in comparison with conventional rule-based and signature-based systems, resulting in better detection of mild insider threats with high precision, and recall. This research highlights the promise of behavior-oriented, ML-enabled approaches to transform the paradigms and patterns of enterprise cybersecurity, triggering more proactive threat defense and enabling organizations to remain relevant and resilient in the face of the constantly growing digital complexity.
Manual Tags: Anomaly Detection; Supervised Learning; Behavioral Analytics; Enterprise Cybersecurity; Insider Threat Detection; Unsupervised Learning; User Activity Monitoring

Author: G, A.; S, J.; D, S.; S.P, S.
Title: PawSense: AI-IoT Enabled Smart Pet Care for Real-Time Health Monitoring
Publication Title: 2025 Third International Conference on Augmented Intelligence and Sustainable Systems (ICAISS)
Abstract Note: Next generation AI systems required for intelligent pet care would have to be capable of real time health monitoring, prevent diagnostics and automated well-being management to meet the rising need for health management of pets. In this article, I am going to describe a mobile app based on Flutter which integrates with AI driven IoT data for reimagining pet monitoring by means of real time anomaly detection, adaptive behaviour tracking, as well as automated care suggestions. The pet health data is collected from multi sensor IoT wearables and such collected data is then analyzed with the help of deep learning algorithm to check and predict early illness and to provide the predictive wellness insights. Hybrid cloudedge architecture effectively processes the data at reduced latency with a preserved scalability and fault tolerance of the underlaying clouds. The Flutter app has smooth communication between pet owners and healthcare professionals with an interactive dashboard, live health data, teleconsultation with a veterinarian and emergency alarms. The use blockchain data integrity mechanisms gives extra security by preventing manipulation and unauthorized access. The suggestion engine is AI-driven and customises to pets based on their lifestyle, their breed and their environmental factors. Results of comparative performance research indicate that real-time monitoring combined with AI driven prediction provide more and higher quality of information in terms of data security and accuracy of prediction than traditional pet care solutions. This ecosystem will improve in the future, by the means of context aware AI model, autonomous robotic pet assistance, cross platform interoperability etc. This technology makes use of AI, IoT, blockchain security and mobile app intelligence to offer pet owners a brand new paradigm in pet care experience enabled through scalable solutions, secure access, and a user centric and personalized pet health monitoring solution for the pets around the world.

Author: Chahar, S.; Gaba, P.; Kaswan, K. S.; Dhatterwal, J. S.; Baliyan, A.

Publication Title: 2025 Artificial Intelligence and Smart Technologies for Sustainability Conference (AISTS)
Abstract Note: In this work, we offer a broad survey, and an original hybrid model for Agentic AI intelligent systems that reason, plan, and act with little human guidance. It investigates the intersection between reinforcement learning, symbolic reasoning, long term memory architectures and explainable AI to build scaled out intelligent systems that are transparent and adaptive. Author: Rani, S. P. Sophia; Samhan, A. Abdelhafiz Ali; Rao, R. V.; Bayyapureddy, S.; Reddy, A. K. Kumar; G, K.
Title: Development of an Optimized QuantumTechniques for Secure Remote Medical Image Sharing
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Recent Innovation in Science Engineering and Technology (ICRISET)
Abstract Note: Secure remote sharing of medical images is essential for advancing telemedicine, accurate diagnostics, and collaborative healthcare delivery. The traditional cryptography techniques are fast turning to be susceptible to quantum computing risks and generally are less efficient in high throughput medical settings. To counter such a shortcoming, we present an innovative quantum-oriented solution that utilizes optimized methods of secure and real-time medical image transmission over a long-distance network. In this method, Quantum Key Distribution (BB84 protocol), hybrid cryptography, quantum informed optimization, and quantum steganography are used to provide efficient high-fidelity and low latency transmission of images. The QKD is used to securely create symmetric keys that are to be used in the AES 256 encryption of the image and Elliptic Curve Cryptography is applied so that the metadata can be kept confidential. Immutable and transparent access logs are kept by using the blockchain technology. In order to even improve the performance, a dynamically tuning encryption parameters using a Quantum Genetic Algorithm can be applied to eliminate the computing overhead. Experimental testing with NIH Chest X-ray dataset shows an average encryption and decryption speed of 38.1 milliseconds, with a success rate of more than 25% relative to the conventional post-quantum cryptographic system. The results of a secure transmission show a decrease in latency of 12.5% over the TLS-enhanced QKD. The system keeps the Quantum Bit Error Rate at less than 5% under realistic noise levels and retains more than 75% of the key material obtained. In quantum steganography, the level of accuracy to detect tampering is 98.6%, hence data integrity. The solution has shown the capability to integrate quantum-level security, computing performance, and regulatory durability to become a trusted and long-term process of safe sharing of medical images in modern healthcare systems.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; ECC; Hybrid Encryption; Quantum Key Distribution; Medical Image Sharing; Quantum Genetic Algorithm; Steganography; Telemedicine Security

Author: RiadHwsein, R.; Nagar, M.; Siri, D.; Kewte, S.; Kuppuraj, T.; Khudayberganov, S.
Title: AI for Sustainability: Real-Time Computer Vision for Environmental Monitoring and Conservation
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Metaverse and Current Trends in Computing (ICMCTC)

The system additionally combines multi-modal detection of RGB imaging, infrared, LiDAR and hyperspectral data, raising the detection accuracy. Along with providing a bio-inspired swarm AI drones and ground-based robotic units for real-time ecological parameter assessment of real-time illegalities, their eyes and ears are the swarm AI drones and ground-based robotic units. The adaptive AI models, armed with reinforcement learning, undergo continuous improvement in terms of the detection accuracy owing to the variations in the environment. The framework of the secure, transparent, immutable data storage for conservation data is based on the blockchain technology. The experimental results reveal that automation achieved 95% reduction of manual surveillance, 80% decrease in the response time to illegal activities, 50% energy saving as compared to traditional AI models. This work furthers sustainability of environmental monitoring by producing a more efficient, scalable, and applicable means of using AI. Author: Sani, S. D.; Salman, T.
Title: iDLG-IG: an Explainability Guided Model Inversion Attack
Publication Title: 2025 3rd International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Blockchain, and Internet of Things (AIBThings)
Abstract Note: Federated learning (FL) trains a shared model without centralizing raw data, which reduces the exposure of user information. Nevertheless, these approaches have demonstrated susceptibility to model inversion attacks, which are capable of reconstructing confidential training data from shared gradients. Optimization-based attacks, such as the deep leakage gradient (DLG) and its improved variant (iDLG), have demonstrated effectiveness in reconstructing ground-truth samples. However, they often struggle with slow convergence and limited reconstruction quality, particularly when dealing with complex images or multiple classes. Building on iDLG, we introduce iDLG-IG, a faster attribution-guided iDLG attack that augments the standard gradient-matching objective with an integrated gradients (IG) attribution map into the attack pipeline. By decomposing the IG attribution map into its positive and negative components, we design a novel loss function that extends the standard gradient matching loss with additional terms guided by the separated IG information. Experiments on CIFAR-10 and SVHN datasets demonstrate that iDLG-IG consistently outperforms iDLG by reducing the mean squared error (MSE), L2 norms of gradients, and faster convergence.

Abstract Note: The rapid digitization of healthcare has transformed how patient data is collected, stored, and utilized, bringing both opportunities and challenges for modern medical systems. Yet, deploying EHRs in shared environments raises serious challenges of privacy, regulatory compliance, and secure management of sensitive patient information. This study introduces a HIPAA (Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act)-compliant hybrid cloud framework that integrates homomorphic encryption with logistic regression for privacy-preserving EHR analysis. The architecture employs the Cheon–Kim–Kim–Song (CKKS) scheme, enabling computations to be performed directly on encrypted data without decryption. Sensitive patient records remain encrypted within the private cloud, while encrypted computations are securely carried out in the public cloud. Logistic regression functions as the predictive model in the public cloud, delivering outcomes on mortality and readmission risk. Once decrypted in the private cloud, predictions are mapped back to patients, and clinicians are alerted through secure hospital systems. Experimental evaluation demonstrates the robustness of the framework, achieving an accuracy of 98.7% for mortality prediction and 98.3% for readmission risk, with precision, recall, and F1-scores consistently above 96%. Title: HDFG: Ethereum Smart Contract Honeypot Detection Based on Pre-Training Techniques

Abstract Note: In recent years, a new fraud method, namely smart contract honeypots, has emerged on the famous blockchain platform Ethereum. Deep learning algorithms are preferred among current contract honeypot detection methods because they can learn more general characteristics and do not rely on expert experience. Most previous works use natural language models to learn the opcodes of contract honeypots but overlook the relevant structural features of the source code. We propose a novel method called the Smart Contract Honey-pot Data Flow Graph, which utilizes a data flow graph to extract the calling relationships of critical source code within contract honeypots and employs a pre-trained model for representation learning. First, contract honeypots generally have a code that transfers money to the calling address, which is critical information for constructing a source code data flow graph. Then, the pre-trained model is used to learn the source code representation and perform downstream classification tasks. The F1-score of our model significantly outperforms the state-of-the-art approaches in the contract honeypot classification task and is close to the highest performance in the detection task. In addition, this model is an end-to-end model that can detect unknown-type contract honeypots.

Abstract Note: This paper reviews the benefits accrued by cloud computing namely scalable, on-demand resources that could be implemented in various fields. The Enhanced Earthworm Optimization (EEO) algorithm is then used in feature selection and thus the algorithm decreases the dimensions of the data whilst maintaining the accuracy of the classification. The Graph Neural Network (GNN) is used to analyze the threat pattern and provides effective detection of complex patterns of cyber-attacks in cloud environments. The model is tested on the two benchmark datasets, CIC-IDS2017 and CSE-CIC-IDS2018 and it is evaluated with several measures. The comparative analysis indicates that the proposed model outperforms existing models by up to 3.89 %, 3.72 % and 2.87 % in detection accuracy and with significantly lower false positive rates respectively. While blockchain was not a central focus in most studies, its use for data provenance and tamper resistance showed promise in enhancing detection credibility. Despite encouraging results, the review highlights the need for further research to validate these approaches under real-time conditions and to address challenges related to scalability, integration, and standardized benchmarking. Author: Shrivastava, A.; Kholmatovna, U. N.; Kannimuthu, S.; MohamadAbbas, H.; Thakur, D.; Priyanka, T. P.

Abstract Note: In the age of intelligent healthcare, fast multisensory information fusion at rates beyond real-time is crucial to perform accurate diagnosis, patient monitoring, and emergency response. Moreover, to embed the privacy of medical data in the training algorithms, the model applies multi-agent reinforcement learning for dynamic decisions in general and blockchain integrated federated learning for private, decentralized training across multiple healthcare institutions. Deployment of the Edge AI on the 5G enabled devices achieves real-time processing as it decreases the latency and the resource consumption in the wearable devices. The proposal results experimentally prove its superiority as a diagnostic approach in terms of accuracy, and speed of computations, as well as its security. With growing threats in the cyber world, the security of smart city systems has become a key challenge. Our article presents an extensive overview of recent work on detection and cyberattack mitigation using machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and hybrid approaches in smart cities. The reviewed methods are classified into three families: ML-based models, DL architectures, and hybrid frameworks that include other technologies such as optimization methods, federated learning (FL), or blockchain to enhance the robustness, scalability, and privacy-preserving nature of the detection. Comparative examination highlights trade-offs among detection quality, processing efficiency, and architectural complexity. The literature review also suggests a growing preference for decentralized, adaptive, and privacy-preserving systems, specifically from federated and distributed learning. Author: Adnan, M. T.; Noor, S. Bin; Ghosh, S. K.; Lee, J.-M.; Kim, D.-S.
Title: CoLLAID: Collaborative Lightweight Language Model for Adaptive Intrusion Detection in Maritime IoT

Abstract Note: Maritime IoT environments face growing cybersecurity threats, yet traditional intrusion detection systems remain illsuited for dynamic, decentralized, and resource-limited settings. We propose CoLLAID, a Collaborative Lightweight Language Model framework for adaptive intrusion detection across distributed maritime nodes. CoLLAID converts structured network traffic into natural language sentences using a feature-templated encoding scheme and processes them with a compact TinyBERT model for efficient classification. To address unknown attacks, the system applies a confidence-aware rejection mechanism followed by Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) clustering for dynamic threat discovery. Federated learning enables decentralized model refinement without raw data exchange, while PureChain, a permissioned blockchain, ensures verifiable synchronization and tamper-resistant update tracking. Evaluations on NSL-KDD and CICIDS2017 demonstrate that CoLLAID outperforms classical baselines, achieving high accuracy (up to 94.72%), strong generalization, and low-latency performance suitable for real-time edge deployment in maritime environments.

Author: Jain, R.; Mamodiya, U.; Sheikh, F.; Avasthi, A.; Kanwer, B.
Title: Artificial Intelligence and Edge-IoT Security in a Smart City Infrequent
Publication Title: 2025 8th International Conference on Emerging Technologies in Computer Engineering: Advances in Computing, Healthcare and Smart Systems (ICETCE)
Abstract Note: Smart cities are increasingly reliant on the Internet of Things (IoT) in the form of interconnected devices that enable intelligent services across all aspects of the smart city, from traffic management to energy distribution. By their very nature, IoT networks are challenging to secure because IoT devices are heterogeneous devices with a distributed network architecture, and they often operate in energy-saving mode, where they undertake infrequent or sporadic communication due to the nature of their intermittent connection or because of event-driven triggers. Smart cities leverage advanced high-speed communication networks (e.g., C-ITS, 5G, etc.), but traditional, centralized security approaches cannot provide trust, data integrity, and resilience in these situations. Thus, this paper discusses how we may apply blockchain to the area of edge-based IoT frameworks to create a more trustworthy and secure smart city based on infrequent IoT interaction. As smart cities explore the possible uses of IoT devices, there is the notion we need to overcome, in fact, the unique area of infrequent, yet catastrophic, security threats that could manifest in a smart city by compromising health services, transport systems, and electrical grids.. This study investigates the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in addressing vulnerabilities in a decentralized smart city using Edge-IoT architecture. Using different benchmarking datasets such as NSL-KDD, CICIDS-2017 and IoT-23, we examine anomaly detection approaches, intrusion prevention mechanisms, and resiliency against sparse attacks. Blockchain provides a public, tamper-proof recorded ledger of infrequent device events and transactions, while edge computing makes both the real-time, on-site processing and access control much closer to data source of origin, while reducing latency and vendor dependency on cloud-based infrastructures. We detail the architecture issues, such as lightweight consensus mechanisms with resource-constrained nodes, and present a hybrid edge-blockchain diagram with a design for infrequent data exchanges. We also consider security issues, including authentication, data provenance, and resiliency in the context of attacks under specific sparse and critical, IoT communications such as emergency alerts, monitoring unique anomalies in infrastructure, etc. The proposed architecture identifies opportunities for scalability, specifying secure, smart city innovation with reliability and integrity as foundational components, even if just through a low frequency of communication.

Author: Ramkumar, G.

Author: Gangavarapu, R. B.; Sharma, V. K.
Title: Design of an Improved Model for IoT Forensic Analysis Using Federated Swarm Learning and Evolutionary Graph Compressions
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Trends in Networks and Computer Communications (ETNCC)
Abstract Note: Low-latency, high-power, high-bandwidth, and heterogeneous datasets have recently emerged due to the rapid proliferation of IoT devices & amp; deployments. Therefore, considerable challenges in carrying out timely and scalable forensic analysis exist. Forensic investigations based on traditional investigation techniques rely mainly on centralized data collection, incurring huge amounts in communication, infringing upon confidentiality, and unable to be fully operational in dynamic and resource-constraint settings typical of IoT environments. In addition, traditional models are more rigid in countering concept drift, ensuring data integrity at the edge level, and efficiently processing graph-based forensic evidence during runtime. To circumvent these challenges presented above, our work proposes an all-inclusive and incremental learning framework for IoT forensic analysis, which embeds five novel bioinspired optimization methods to enhance scalability, efficiency, and adaptability. The first method, Federated Swarm Initiated Forensic Learning (FSIFL), leverages federated intelligence and swarm intelligence to allow decentralized model training while safeguarding data privacy and conserving resources. The second method, Multi-Objective Evolutionary Graph Compression for Forensics (MoEGCF), incorporates an evolutionary pruning mechanism on forensic graphs, retaining evidence relevant to the case while significantly decreasing graph size and traversal complexity. The third, Reinforcement-Guided Adaptive Forensic Policy Engine (RG-AFPE), uses neuroevolution- augmented reinforcement learning for real-time forensic policy selection from dynamic environmental states. The fourth, Edge-Evolved Compression with Forensic Integrity Assurance (EECFIA) is based on genetic algorithms to perform edge-side data compression combined with evolved checksum validation to ensure forensic integrity sets. Finally, DriftAdaptive Contextual Forensic Learner (DACFL) integrates contextual windowing and drift-aware mutations to preserve model applicability in the face of the ever-evolving behaviour of IoT agents. Experimental evaluations result in a massive gain in several metrics, such as convergence time, accuracy, resource utilization, and adaptability. The proposed integrated model constitutes a significant advancement towards the highly competitive state of scalable IoT forensics, which strives for an unbiased, effective, and privacy-preserving forensic intelligence in fast-paced and large-scale environments.

Title: A Real-Time Anomaly Detection Framework for Ethereum Using Rule-Based Logic, GraphSAGE and Consensus-Driven Event Processing

Abstract Note: Ethereum is one of the key platforms in public blockchain networks. Ethereum used for various critical applications like decentralized finance (DeFi), smart contract based and supply chain operations etc., Because of its growing popularity along with its open and anonymous nature, network can contribute fraudulent or abnormal transactions. The existing anomaly detection methods suffer from real time detection as they use rule based or statistical methods. These methods are failed to identify dynamic or structural transactional anomalies and has no consensus verification. To address these challenges, in this study we designed an anomaly detection model that features rule based logic, Graph Neural Networks with GraphSAGE and Consensus-driven Complex Event Processing (CEP). We developed this model by combining three key procedures primarily the transactions are fetched from live Ethereum network and presented to rule based filtering. Author: Verma, B. K.; Runthala, A.; Sharma, P. K.; Singh, S.; Garg, D. K.; Kumar, H.
Title: Enhancing Cybersecurity in Connected and Autonomous Vehicles: A CatBoost-Based Ensemble Framework for Multi-Class Threat Detection
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE DELCON - International Conference on Recent Smart Technologies in Engineering for Sustainable Development
Abstract Note: The deployment of Connected and Autonomous Vehicles [CAVs] in intelligent transportation systems has increased the demand for real-time, robust cybersecurity solutions. Here, we present a CatBoost-based threat detection framework specifically designed for multi-class classification of vehicular cyberattacks without an accompanying dataset, such as the VEREMI Extension Simple. The dataset, comprising benign and malicious vehicle communications in the context of a variety of attacks, experiences exhaustive preprocessing that involves null value processing, feature discretization, feature encoding and normalization. The developed model of CatBoost Classifier using the multi-class loss function (averaged over all observations) that uses ordered boosting is utilized to efficiently deal with categorical features and minimize prediction bias. Producing an explanation for a prediction given by anba model allows it to enhance the interpretability of marketing campaigns based on communication characteristics in long-range dependent networks. Hyperparameters such as number of rounds, learning rate and depth are optimized to trade the generalization performance and training speed. The model is learned using the stratified \textbackslash{}mathbf{k}\-fold cross-validation scheme to improve robustness over multiple data splits. From experimental evaluation, we find the proposed method provides high accuracy, macro averaged F1-score and balanced recall on all attack categories compared to the baseline ensemble learning technique such as Random Forest. These findings illustrate that CatBoost is capable of handling heterogeneous vehicular data, and thus a strong candidate for implementation in vehicle intrusion detection systems and wider intelligent transport security solutions. The proposed method does not only enhance detection accuracy in terms of precision, but also reduces false alarm rate so that the trust can be taken into account when constructing autonomous vehicular communication networks.

Author: Tomar, K.; Thada, V.; Garg, U.

Author: Sivasubramanian, S.; Sobirovich, N. B.; Salami, Z. A.; Soni, S.; Balambigai, S.; Pirnazarova, M.; J, Y.; Pallavi, M. O.

Thanks to a blockchain-inspired decentralized protocol, all messages are authenticated and remain reliable without requiring central servers, thus increasing security. An AI-based collision forecasting system checks the collected sensor signals to predict collisions fast and take quick preemptive actions. It prioritizes the delivery of important messages and manages the device’s bandwidth by sending the signals only when needed. It also helps by switching available channels cleverly to prevent communication interruptions and overcrowding. Working together, models updates make the network better, and all data is kept confidential during this process. The results of the simulation explain that collision rates, time between messages, and network delays are reduced more than in current V2V systems. This approach makes it easy to avoid collisions in real time and offers good security, which also makes it simple for AVs to communicate with other vehicles on the roads. Author: Bharathi, P. S.; Tejaswi, R.
Title: DL-SecureNet: A Transformer-based Cybersecurity Framework for Threat Detection in 5G and Beyond
Publication Title: 2025 6th International Conference on Intelligent Communication Technologies and Virtual Mobile Networks (ICICV)
Abstract Note: The development of the 5G networks has given a new direction for the faster communication but it has brought new security threats related to its efficacy. Author: M, P. C.; Pandiyarajan, P.

Abstract Note: Cotton production is extremely susceptible to pests, disease, and irrigation mismanagement, resulting in considerable yield loss and environmental degradation. The intersection of Artificial Intelligence (AI), the Internet of Things (IoT), and smart water management offers a revolutionary chance towards sustainable agriculture. This paper discusses the cooperative function of IoT and AI in cotton cultivation, particularly real-time pest identification, disease classification, and dynamic irrigation management. Deep learning techniques precisely detect pests at all stages of development, whereas IoT sensors track environmental data like soil moisture, temperature, and humidity. Furthermore, adaptive learning methods such as federated and incremental learning optimize system performance through time, allowing for ongoing improvement without violating data privacy. Author: Balogun, V.; Rahman, S. S.; Watt, W. Kai

Author: NiranjanReddy, K.; MohamadAbbas, H.; Kumar, Y. J. N.; Ram, R. B.; Atheeswari, S.; Kumar, V. S.

Abstract Note: With Deep learning and quantum computing are emerging technologies with transformative potential in financial risk assessment, optimization, and fraud detection. To address these issues, we propose the Quantum-Inspired Neural Networks for Fraud Detection (Q-INN-FD) framework, which leverages quantum-inspired computing principles to enhance neural network architectures. Author: Li, J.; Lu, Z.
Title: Intelligent Perception and Early Warning Framework for Agricultural Product Supply Chain Risks Based on Large Language Model and Knowledge Graph
Publication Title: 2025 3rd International Conference on Logistics Engineering, Supply Chain and Digital Transformation (LESCDT)
Abstract Note: In the context of globalization and climate uncertainty, agricultural supply chains face increasingly complex, dynamic, and multi-source risks that threaten food security and system resilience. Traditional early-warning systems, primarily based on structured data and predefined rules, fail to capture latent dependencies and high-frequency unstructured information, resulting in poor timeliness, accuracy, and interpretability. To address these challenges, this study proposes an intelligent risk perception and early-warning framework that deeply integrates Large Language Models (LLMs) with Knowledge Graphs (KGs) for agricultural supply chain management. The framework is designed to (1) automatically extract risk entities and relations from heterogeneous textual streams, (2) construct a dynamically evolving knowledge graph that encodes causal dependencies, and (3) reason about risk propagation paths using a hybrid mechanism that couples graph-based structural inference with LLM-driven semantic reasoning. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves entity and relation extraction F1-scores of 0.87 and 0.83, respectively. In forecasting risk levels over \1-7\ day horizons, the system outperforms traditional rule-based, KG-only, and LLM-only baselines, achieving MAE \=0.042\, AUC \=0.91\, and \textbackslash{}mathbf{E C E}=\ 0.028, indicating both superior predictive accuracy and probabilistic calibration. The proposed framework contributes a novel paradigm that systematically fuses the semantic reasoning capacity of LLMs with the structural interpretability of KGs, advancing from “risk perception” to “risk cognition”. Beyond methodological innovation, it provides a deployable technical pathway for enhancing early warning, resilience, and sustainability in agricultural supply chains.

Author: Legheraba, M. A.; Rachdi, N.; Potop-Butucaru, M.; Tixeuil, S.
Title: LIFT: Byzantine Resilient Hub-Sampling
Publication Title: 2025 Thirteenth International Symposium on Computing and Networking (CANDAR)
Abstract Note: Recently, a novel peer sampling protocol, Elevator, was introduced to construct network topologies tailored for emerging decentralized applications such as federated learning and blockchain. Elevator builds hub-based topologies in a fully decentralized manner, randomly selecting hubs among participating nodes. These hubs, acting as central nodes connected to the entire network, can be leveraged to accelerate message dissemination. Simulation results have shown that Elevator converges rapidly (within 3–4 cycles) and exhibits robustness against crash failures and churn. However, its resilience to Byzantine adversaries has not been investigated.In this work, we provide the first evaluation of Elevator under Byzantine adversaries and show that even a small fraction (2%) of Byzantine nodes is sufficient to subvert the network. As a result, we introduce LIFT, a new protocol that extends Elevator by employing a cryptographically secure pseudo-random number generator (PRNG) for hub selection, thereby mitigating Byzantine manipulation. In contrast, LIFT withstands adversarial infiltration and remains robust with up to 10% Byzantine nodes. These results highlight the necessity of secure randomness in decentralized hub formation and position LIFT as a more reliable building block for Byzantine-resilient decentralized systems.

Author: Hinov, N.; Stanchev, P.
Title: AI-Enhanced Virtual Power Plants: Comparative Approaches, Future Architectures, and Policy Implications
Publication Title: 2025 10th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
Abstract Note: The large-scale integration of renewable energy sources (RES) introduces challenges of volatility, flexibility, and cybersecurity in modern power systems. While numerous studies have reviewed VPP operations, most remain descriptive and lack comparative, architectural, and practical insights. This paper contributes in four main directions. First, we provide a comparative analysis between classical optimization methods (e.g., MILP, MINLP, stochastic programming) and emerging AI-based approaches (e.g., machine learning, reinforcement learning, federated learning). A structured comparison highlights strengths, weaknesses, and applicability under different operational conditions. Second, we propose a future AI-based VPP architecture, structured in layered form to integrate DERs, communication protocols, advanced optimization intelligence, and market interfaces. Third, a minisimulation case study is presented, contrasting classical MILP scheduling with reinforcement learning under forecast uncertainty. Results demonstrate that AI-based control achieves up to 8 % cost reduction while maintaining flexibility, though at the expense of transparency and computational complexity. Finally, we offer policy and industry recommendations, emphasizing hybrid frameworks, standardization, explainability, and cybersecurity. The findings suggest that hybrid VPP control, combining mathematical rigor with adaptive AI, will be essential for next-generation power systems. This work provides both researchers and practitioners with a roadmap toward resilient, scalable, and trustworthy VPP operations.

Author: Bandopadhyay, N.; Swain, S.; Mohapatra, S.; Chakravarty, K.; Saha, D.; Bandyopadhyay, A.
Title: Spectrum Based Resource Allocation Using Auction Based Game Theoretic Approach
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Engineering Innovations and Technologies (ICoEIT)
Abstract Note: Efficient spectrum allocation is a crucial challenge in edge computing, where limited wireless resources must support diverse applications with strict latency constraints. As edge computing relies on real-time data processing close to users, optimizing spectrum usage is essential for maintaining performance. Auction-based models have emerged as a promising solution, enabling fair, efficient, and incentive-compatible spectrum allocation by allowing participants to bid dynamically based on demand. In this paper, we propose a novel auction-based spectrum allocation model tailored to the unique characteristics of edge networks, considering factors such as low latency requirements, dynamic resource demands, and heterogeneous edge devices. Our model incorporates advanced auction mechanisms, including combinatorial auctions, which allow bidding on multiple spectrum blocks simultaneously for improved efficiency, and double auctions, which match spectrum buyers and sellers while maximizing utilization and fairness. Through simulations, we demonstrate that our approach significantly enhances spectrum efficiency, fairness, and computational scalability compared to traditional allocation methods. The findings highlight the potential of auction-based spectrum allocation models as a key enabler for future edge computing systems, ensuring optimal resource utilization and improved network performance.

Title: Cloud-enabled NLP for Automated Medical Record Summarization and Decision Support
Publication Title: 2025 2nd International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
Abstract Note: The rapid expansion of electronic health records (EHRs) has posed difficulties retrieving essential patient information for clinical decision-making. This research presents a cloud-based Natural Language Processing (NLP) system for automating medical record summarization and decision assistance. The system utilizes sophisticated NLP methodologies, such as Named Entity Recognition (NER) and Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT), to derive essential clinical insights from unstructured medical material. The decision assistance module enhanced diagnostic prediction accuracy by 14.7% and decreased manual review time by an average of 37%. Cloud integration improved processing speed, with an average response time of 1.8 seconds per document, demonstrating scalability for real-time applications. The findings demonstrate that cloud-based NLP may substantially improve medical record summarization, optimize clinical processes, and improve decision-making precision. The research highlights the possibility of combining NLP with cloud computing to provide prompt and accurate patient care for healthcare workers.

Author: Narsimhulu, B.; Kumar, T. S.
Title: Review on Optimizing Cloud Computing: Resource Allocation, Task Scheduling, and AI-Driven Enhancements
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
Abstract Note: With flexible access to computing power provided via the cloud computing, the traditional way of working with IT infrastructure has been changed. The article discusses to optimize the cloud systems from Resource Distribution, Optimization techniques and Task scheduling. Researchers have explored heuristic, metaheuristic, and AI-based approaches to reduce delays and costs.. It shows that AI driven methods can achieve \37.8 \textbackslash{}%\ saving on energy consumption, \22 \textbackslash{}%\ increase on SLA compliance, \30.4 \textbackslash{}%\ on workload distribution efficiency. The deep reinforcement learning models reduce the task execution time by \31.5 \textbackslash{}%\ and increase the CPU usage by \17 \textbackslash{}%\. Blockchain has also been considered for multi cloud management of workload and it has resulted in a \62 \textbackslash{}%\ decrease in unauthorized access efforts, and \57 \textbackslash{}%\ decrease in data breach. The only troubles in introducing these capabilities are the high computational demands, security efficiency tradeoffs, and real time adaptation flaws. While the authors provide a way to improve AI heuristic models, energy aware scheduling and scalable security, this study also shows where current methods fail and how they may be strengthened. The study’s results indicate that by combining the AI and blockchain, we can build the cloud systems to be more efficient, secured and less expensive for the future

Author: Liu, W.; Jiang, Y.; Cao, S.; Zhang, Y.; Leng, K.
Title: Carbon Emission Accounting System of Power Grid Supply Chain Based on Artificial Intelligence
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart Innovations in Systems, Infrastructure, Mechanical, Power, AI and Computing Technologies (SISIMPACT)
Abstract Note: With the advancement of the “dual carbon” goals, the carbon emission accounting of the power grid supply chain faces challenges such as insufficient dynamics and blurred boundaries. This study proposes an artificial intelligence-based carbon emission accounting system for the power grid supply chain, builds a multi-level accounting system covering the entire life cycle of planning and design, production and manufacturing, logistics and transportation, and designs a fourlayer architecture of “data collection-intelligent processingaccounting model-application service”. The system integrates IoT terminals, federated learning and blockchain technology to achieve real-time collection of multi-source data and joint modeling under privacy protection; LSTM neural network is used to dynamically predict emission trends, and the benchmark model (LCA framework) is combined to improve the accounting accuracy. Experiments show that the system accounting accuracy is improved to 85.2%-98.4%, and the task processing time is shortened. This paper provides an efficient tool for accurate tracking of carbon footprint and emission reduction decision-making in the power grid supply chain.

Author: Indu, V. T.; Sathish.P; R.Saranya; Banu, N. S.; S.Gayathri; Pajila, P. J. B.
Title: Enhancing Malware Detection with Machine Learning
Publication Title: 2025 7th International Conference on Innovative Data Communication Technologies and Application (ICIDCA)
Abstract Note: The constant development of new forms of malware has made it difficult to detect them using conventional approaches, but with the help of such sophisticated approaches as machine learning (ML). In this paper, the author aims at discussing the application of ML in improving malware detection and classification using supervised, unsupervised, and deep learning techniques. The survey focuses on important aspects of ML application such as feature selection and construction, and static and dynamic analysis of the application, as well as the interaction between ML and other cutting-edge technologies including edge computing and blockchain. The study shows how ML helps to mitigate zero-day threats and the advanced malware types namely polymorphic and metamorphic. It also provides information about drawbacks of ML which are adversarial attacks, data deficiency, problems related to scalability, and last one is regarding the model’s interpretation. In the last section of the paper, the author discusses the directions for future work, pointing out that the formation of datasets, evaluation procedures, and open-source platforms for reliable and effective anti-malware systems should involve joint work of researchers, businesses, and regulatory agencies.

Author: Saravanan, S.; Thanigasalam, T.
Title: The Role of MEC in Enhancing 5G RAN: Cloudification and Edge Computing Synergy
Publication Title: 2025 5th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
Abstract Note: The rapid evolution of 5G mobile networks has introduced stringent requirements for ultra-low latency, high reliability, and dynamic scalability, particularly in Radio Access Networks (RAN). The combination of cloudified 5G RAN designs like Cloud-RAN (C-RAN) and Open RAN (O-RAN) with Multi-access Edge Computing (MEC) has become a paradigm shift in response to these needs.This paper explores the synergy between MEC and 5G RAN cloudification, highlighting how edge intelligence enables localized processing, reduces backhaul congestion, and enhances service responsiveness. Using a layered architectural approach that combines virtualized RAN operations with MEC nodes, we provide network slicing, real-time analytics, and support for ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC). Through analysis of relevant use cases—such as AR/VR streaming, autonomous driving, and industrial IoT—we demonstrate the performance benefits of this integration. Furthermore, the paper discusses current challenges in orchestration, security, and standardization. This study contributes to understanding MEC’s pivotal role in optimizing RAN performance and driving future 6G-ready network deployments.

Author: Krushnasamy, V. S.; Farooq, M.; Al-Muraad, N. H.; Hussein, O. M.; Ali, A. T. H.; Selvakumarasamy, K.
Title: Adaptive Cognitive Digital Twin Framework for Efficient Smart City Operations
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on NexGen Networks and Cybernetics (IC2NC)
Abstract Note: The rapid evolution of cyber-physical smart cities necessitates intelligent, adaptive systems capable of handling vast urban complexities. Therefore, a Cognitive Digital Twin (CDT) framework built on real time sensor data, deep learning, anomaly detection and blockchain based security to enhance urban operation like traffic control, energy management and public safety has been presented in this research. The target is to construct a scalable self-learning AI model that assists the prediction analytics and thereby the decision making for the smart cities. In contrast to methodical digital twins, the proposed CDT combines both the advanced AI and distributed cloud-edge computing to both speed up data processing and to create more accurate forecasting. The contribution of this work is in its holistic approach by integrating time series forecasting, anomaly detection, and energy consumption prediction in a single AI Driven system and has been verified for both simulation environments as well as real world setup. RMSE and MAPE metrics are used to assess the system performance in terms of processing latency values of around 50 milliseconds for one thousand IoT devices and MAPE values below industry thresholds. Robustness, scalability and precision of urban data management is demonstrated with CDT through optimization of resource allocation, improvement of public safety responsiveness and sustainability of urban development. These results confirm the proposed model’s ability to improve the urban management efficiency to a great extent while ensuring the stringent data security and system resilience.
Manual Tags: Smart Cities; Predictive Analytics; Cognitive Digital Twin; IoT Data Processing; Urban Sustainability

Author: Torres, V. M.; Diaz, J. Roman; Portugal, E. S.; Cornejo, J.
Title: Prediction of Cyberattacks using Machine Learning in the Financial Sector: Technical Review
Publication Title: 2025 9th International Symposium on Multidisciplinary Studies and Innovative Technologies (ISMSIT)
Abstract Note: This systematic literature review (SLR) tests the use of Machine Learning and Deep Learning algorithms to predict cyberattacks and fraud on business portals in the financial industry. The most effective techniques are tested to identify abnormal patterns in digital transactions, achieving accuracies up to 99% and reducing false positives by 31%, as well as current approaches to money laundering, fraud, terrorist financing, and systemic risks on financial platforms. The report identifies the use of hybrid models, deep neural networks, graph neural network (GNN)-based architecture, harvesting techniques, compensation methods, and active learning, such as how to improve the most obvious strategy for threatening predictions. Through the use of transactional data, user profiles, and behavioral metrics, it is possible to create robust and adaptable models ideal for the protection of financial systems. In addition, the increase in the incorporation of emerging technologies such as blockchain and differential privacy in anti-fraud systems is observed. This RSL concludes that applying intelligent models to financial portals improves early detection of cyberattacks; however, it is recommended to continue researching these models in real-time, data-driven environments, as well as promoting the practical implementation of these models in financial institutions.

Author: Singh, N.; Prakash, J.; Srivastava, A.
Title: Advancements in Accident Detection for Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks: Techniques, Challenges, and Future Directions
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE 4th International Conference on Technology, Engineering, Management for Societal impact using Marketing, Entrepreneurship and Talent (TEMSMET)
Abstract Note: Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (VANETs) have recently attracted a lot of interest in accident detection because of their essential service in road safety to ensure traffic flows smoothly. These networks used to support real time communications between vehicles (V2V) and infrastructure (V2I) serve as a base to intelligent transportation systems that can detect accident in a timely and precise manner. Recent improvements in the sphere of communication technologies, artificial intelligence as well as Internet of Things (IoT) have led to the creation of more efficient and stable mechanisms of accident detection. The given paper will provide a coherent overview of the latest methods being used in the detection of accidents, such as rule-based schemes, machine learning systems, IoT-driven frameworks, and identification systems that use a mix of different procedures to increase precision and stability. It also examines how edge computing can be incorporated into real-time computing of data, and how important communication protocols, including 5G and Dedicated Short-Range Communications (DSRC), will be to low-latency reporting in accidents. Moreover, the paper provides the information on the current difficulties, such as the problem of data privacy, scalability in an urban context, and absence of uniformity in VANET architectures. Suggestions are made on future research directions that should take advantage of improved technologies to solve these problems and make the VANETs capable of developing scalable, reliable, and real-time accident detection systems by exploiting 6G networks, hybrid AI models and blockchain to securely share its data. This research aligns with SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being).
Manual Tags: Deep Learning; Machine Learning; Accident Detection; Road Safety; SDG 3; Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (VANETs)

Author: Acquah, T.; Freeman, E.; Brown-Acquaye, W. L.; Acheampong, P.; Agbehadji, I. E.; Millham, R. C.
Title: Assessing E-Government Systems on Public Service Delivery in Ghana: A Bibliometric Analysis
Publication Title: 2025 IST-Africa Conference (IST-Africa)
Abstract Note: This research undertakes a bibliometric analysis of e-government studies services from 2020 to 2024. Significant research trends, impactful publications, and collaborative networks are delineated, with notable subjects encompassing egovernance and public administration. A total of 2,717 documents from 2020 to 2024 were analysed. The analysis indicates that well-established themes, such as decisionmaking, coexist alongside emerging domains, including blockchain and network security. Collaboration networks illustrate notable contributions from nations such as China, India, and the United States. The results provide a comprehensive understanding of the integration of digital technologies aimed at improving governmental services, thereby enhancing both efficiency and transparency. Notwithstanding the constraints imposed by the exclusion of non-scholarly sources, the study proposes avenues for future inquiry, especially in tackling the distinct challenges encountered by developing countries such as Ghana. This study enhances comprehension of the development of e-government systems and their capacity to transform public service delivery.

Author: Joseph, A. S. K.; Srinivasan, S.
Title: Anti-Phishing Adaptive AI Systems: Efficiently Countering Social Engineering Attacks by Real-Time Analysis of Email Content
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Computational Innovations and Engineering Sustainability (ICCIES)
Abstract Note: Attacks using phishing, the most common kind of social engineering, are getting smarter all the time; they target human weaknesses to steal personal data. The most common vector for these types of assaults is phishing emails that appear to come from trusted sources in an effort to deceive recipients into giving up sensitive information or installing harmful programs. Because they are built on static rule-based detection systems and signature-based methodologies, traditional anti-phishing solutions can't keep up with the ever-changing tactics used by attackers. In order to effectively combat phishing assaults, this study presents adaptive AI systems that use real-time email content analysis. These AI systems are able to detect tiny indications of harmful behaviour by seamlessly analysing the context, content, and intent of email messages using advanced machine learning (ML) algorithms and natural language processing (NLP) techniques. Metadata, links, attachments, and the message's semantic structure are all parts of structured and unstructured email content that the system examines for phishing signs. Adaptive AI systems may continually enhance their detection skills over time, unlike traditional models that depend on predetermined criteria. This is because they can learn from evolving phishing techniques. In addition, these systems can detect zero-day phishing assaults and other types of phishing that haven't been seen before, making them a more effective and agile defence. Improving detection accuracy while lowering false positives, which generally plague anti-phishing efforts, is the subject of this research, which further explores the use of real-time analysis. Finding a happy medium between system openness and user privacy and incorporating AI systems into preexisting email infrastructure are other issues covered in the research. Improved detection of complex phishing attempts and subsequent faster and more effective incident responses are achieved by the suggested adaptive AI systems through a mix of supervised and unsupervised learning models. In its last section, the article delves into the possible future applications of anti-phishing technologies powered by artificial intelligence and how they could improve cybersecurity for a wider variety of online communication channels.
Manual Tags: Natural Language Processing (NLP); Email Content Analysis; Phishing Attack Prevention; Phishing Detection Algorithms; Phishing Email Classification; Real-Time Phishing Detection; Social Engineering Attacks

Author: Thallapalli, R.; Yadav, B. P.; Srinivasulu, B.; Venkateshwarlu, P.; M.Srinivas; Kumar, E. K.
Title: AI-Driven Cyber-Physical Systems and IoT for Enabling Intelligent, Secure, and Adaptive Ecosystems
Publication Title: 2025 2nd International Conference on Recent Trends in Electrical, Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICRTEECT)
Abstract Note: The Internet of Things (IoT) and Cyber-Physical Systems (CPSs) are pacesetters to advance intelligent and connected environments, and their ubiquitous adoption will bring radical impact to critical domains including smart cities, healthcare, and autonomous systems. The transformative impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) on the CPS-IoT ecosystems is investigated in this paper. With AI, real time decision making, predictive maintenance, and even system optimisation is possible — all possible while solving the problem of scalability, latency, adaptability in highly dynamic environments. This paper provides unique insights into the convergence of AI, CPSs and IoT by presenting novel technologies like edge computing, digital twins, and AI-based cybersecurity. Overall, these advances illustrate the potential of AI-driven CPSs to realize next generation smarter, safer and more efficient systems. Finally, the paper also discusses critical challenges, primarily related to data privacy, ethical considerations as well as interoperability and suggests possible ways to overcome these barriers. The main findings underscore AI’s central importance to next generation CPS-IoT systems and suggest a pathway for building secure, adaptive, and sustainable infrastructures.

Author: Wen, H.; Huang, G.; Liu, Y.; Chen, W.; Xu, G.; Lei, B.
Title: Toward Seamless IoT Interoperability for Energy and Mobility Integration: A Systemic Perspective
Publication Title: 2025 25th Conference of the Electric Power Supply Industry (CEPSI)
Abstract Note: The convergence of energy and mobility systems, accelerated by electric vehicle adoption and the rise of smart grids, presents significant challenges and opportunities for system interoperability. This paper investigates how Internet of Things (IoT) technologies can enable seamless integration across these domains by addressing technical, semantic, and regulatory barriers. We identify key challenges such as legacy infrastructure, protocol fragmentation, data heterogeneity, and institutional misalignment. To address these, we review enabling solutions including IoT middleware platforms, ontology-driven data models, standardized communication protocols, and privacy-preserving frameworks. A layered architecture is presented to illustrate how modular and scalable integration can be achieved in real-world systems. Additionally, we highlight emerging research opportunities in adaptive architectures, decentralized data governance, semantic automation, and secure edge intelligence. By synthesizing multidisciplinary insights, this work provides a foundation for developing resilient and interoperable energy-mobility ecosystems, supporting the broader goals of sustainability, decarbonization, and digital transformation.

Author: Supraja, B.; V, K. K.; N, K. Kumar
Title: Optimized Energy-Efficient IoT Healthcare Systems Using Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Advances in Computing Research On Science Engineering and Technology (ACROSET)
Abstract Note: We present a new energy focused IoT healthcare structure in this paper with Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning (HDRL) to optimise performance of an IoT healthcare structure on various levels of systems decision-making. In contrast to conventional architectures, the suggested model includes two-level reinforcement learning framework, namely Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) at the cloud tier and Deep Q-Network (DQN) at the edge. This integration has enabled the system to be quicker in a real-time manner although it has the long-term strategic planning. Due to the extensive simulation with Python, TensorFlow and OpenAI Gym, a 40 percent decrease in energy usage and a 7 percent better patient outcomes are identified. The given system is robust, scalable, and can be possibly introduced into reality to implement intelligent IoT in healthcare. Future extensions could think of validation with the real-world, and privacy-preserving mechanisms.

Author: Mamatjan, Y.
Title: Intelligent Systems in Health: Historical Evolution, Current Development and Future Perspectives
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE Canadian Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (CCECE)
Abstract Note: Digital technologies are rapidly transforming healthcare by integrating networked devices, advanced analytics, telemedicine, and electronic health records. Intelligent systems have evolved from early rule-based medical expert systems to modern AI-driven Intelligent agent-based systems (software systems that autonomously reason, learn, and interact). These systems not only enhance operational efficiency and diagnostic accuracy but also support personalized and proactive patient care. This paper presents a historical overview of intelligent systems in healthcare, compares past and present systems through two detailed tables, and introduces current research and development that focuses on clinical decision making (CDM) in the age of AI. The evolution of intelligent systems in digital health from early medical expert systems like MYCIN to modern data-driven platforms illustrates significant technological progress. Contemporary intelligent systems demonstrate increased adaptability, scalability, and integration with clinical workflows. The introduction of advanced AI frameworks and the application of Explainable AI (XAI) techniques have further enhanced transparency and clinician trust. In particular, we discuss an AI-agent framework that integrates machine learning models with XAI techniques and human feedback to automate medical data analysis and report generation. We conclude with a discussion of the advantages, challenges, and future promise of these systems, emphasizing the importance of ethical leadership, effective security mechanisms and stronger cross-disciplinary collaboration.
