Author: Yoo, S.; Kim, D.-Y.; Kim, D.-Y.
Title: A Procedural Architecture for Agent Trust and Credibility Verification in Distributed Ledger-Based Federated Learning
Publication Title: IEEE Access
Abstract Note: Agent-based federated learning (FL) enables multiple nodes to collaboratively train a global model without sharing raw data, thereby mitigating privacy and security concerns. However, FL inherently relies on the credibility of participating agents, making trust assurance critical in environments susceptible to malicious attacks and operational faults. This paper proposes a procedural architecture for evaluating and enhancing agent credibility in distributed ledger-based FL (DLFL) systems. The proposed architecture spans the agent life cycle, consisting of the pre-training, in-training, and post-training stages, and integrates three verification domains: data-based, behavior-based, and technology-based verification. In the pre-training stage, data-based verification assesses data integrity and quality through reference distribution analysis and entropy reduction to improve learning stability. During the in-training stage, behavior-based verification establishes a dual mechanism that monitors and analyzes agents’ learning processes and outcomes and detects anomalies in updates and performance. In the post-training stage, technology-based verification ensures record immutability and accountability through blockchain, cryptographic validation, and auditing mechanisms. By combining these multi-layered procedures, the proposed architecture enables systematic and continuous evaluation of agent credibility, fostering a trustworthy FL ecosystem and enabling future applications in autonomous agent collaboration and trust-oriented AI governance.

Author: Rahman, A.; Walee, N. A.; Mahir, S. H.; Tashrif, M. T. A.; Rana, M. S.
Title: BIoMT-VFL: Ensuring Blockchain-based Security and Privacy in Internet of Medical Things through Vertical Federated Learning

Abstract Note: Blockchain is an emerging leading technology for decentralized and transaction-based sharing of data. However, the data of the patients needs to be available publicly, while the information should be secure and private through the Vertical Federated Learning (VFL) platform. To overcome this problem, Blockchain will utilize smart contracts to update the data-sharing methods on the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT). The control of the data availability will be handled by the owner of the data (the patients), such as the patient, who will allow the researchers to use their data along with their personal information using the VFL environment. The publicly available data will be stored in the public ledger, which no unauthentic user can access and tamper. People can share their medical reports remotely in the proposed system “BIoMT-VFL” efficiently, and motivation will be given to them to do this. In this way, medical service providers can easily improve the lack of care, and the general public can get more suitable care from hospitals. Author: Nelufule, N.; Mudau, C.; Senamela, P.; Siphambili, N.
Title: From 5G to 6G: A Systematic Review and Quantum-Resilient Blockchain-Augmented Federated Learning Framework for Privacy-by-Design in IoT Ecosystems
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Cyber Security and Resilience (CSR)
Abstract Note: The evolution from 5G to 6G networks is promising hyper-competitivity. This is enhanced by the AI-native systems which support massive IoT deployments particularly in industries such as smart cities, smart healthcare, and smart transportation. However, this advancement heightens the privacy risks such as quantum-vulnerable cryptography, model inversion in federated learning (FL), and centralized trust bottlenecks. In this work a systematic literature review was conducted on peer-reviewed research articles and conference papers on 6G security and privacy. The main aim was to identify the discrepancies in the integration of FL, Blockchain, and Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC). Furthermore, Quantum-Resilient Blockchain-Augmented Federated Learning (QR-BAFL) framework was proposed. This framework embeds the Privacy-by-Design (PbD) principles with a verifiable smart contracts, PQC primitives, and edge-optimized FL. Simulations on ESP32 microcontrollers were conducted and the results demonstrated the feasibility of QR-BAFL particularly in resource-constrained IoT, with reduced privacy leakage and sub-millisecond latencies under 6G models. Comparisons with Raspberry Pi highlight trade-offs in performance and energy. This work advances trustworthy 6G IoT, offering standardization recommendations for 3GPP and ITU-R.

Author: Kumar, R.; Dutta, J.; Vamsi, N.; Varri, U. Sankararao; Puthal, D.
Title: Next-Generation Security in the 6G Era: The Role of AI in Safeguarding Future Networks
Publication Title: IEEE Access
Abstract Note: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into sixth-generation (6G) networks is a foundational requirement for achieving unprecedented performance, but it also introduces a sophisticated threat landscape that legacy security frameworks cannot address. This paper presents a comprehensive review of this dual role of AI, analyzing its potential to both compromise and safeguard future networks. Since AI has the ability to both protect and compromise security and privacy, its implementation with 6G technology may sometimes be a double-edged sword. The primary objective of this survey is to systematically analyze existing research that integrates AI techniques into 6G architectures, focusing on their implications for security and privacy. Among the concerns being investigated is the fundamental privacy and security risk associated with 6G technologies. Therefore, in order to incorporate and confirm this foundational research as a platform for future research, we have developed a review on the specifics of 6G security and privacy. The methodology involves reviewing recent academic and industrial studies related to AI-enabled 6G frameworks, threat models, and defense mechanisms, with an emphasis on how AI contributes to intrusion detection, authentication, and privacy preservation. This paper begins with a historical analysis of previous networking technologies and how they impacted contemporary 6G networking improvements. Therefore, this article discusses extensively the aspects that have rendered 6G technology relevant as well as the ongoing 6G-based projects. In addition, it identifies and critically evaluates key enabling technologies, including distributed ledger technology (DLT/blockchain), physical layer security (PLS), terahertz (THz) communication, quantum computing, visible light communication (VLC), and distributed AI/ML, that underpin secure 6G environments. The paper concludes by summarizing open challenges, future research opportunities, and potential pathways for building trustworthy AI-driven 6G systems.

Author: S, S.; H, A. R.; V, S. K.; R, W. B. N.
Title: Sustainable and Privacy-Aware Federated Learning Framework for Cross-Organizational Cyber Threat and Fraud Intelligence
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Computer Networks and Inventive Communication Technologies (ICCNCT)
Abstract Note: This paper presents a novel federated learning framework for privacy-preserving cybersecurity across organizational boundaries. The methodology employs a hybrid CNN-GRU architecture trained via federated learning across five organizational nodes, with secure aggregation weighted by dataset sizes. Key findings demonstrate 95.8% detection accuracy—a 4.6% improvement over centralized approaches—while reducing latency to 110ms and ensuring complete data locality. The framework successfully detects network intrusions, fraudulent transactions, and malware patterns across banking, healthcare, e-commerce, energy, and education sectors, establishing a scalable foundation for privacy-compliant collaborative cybersecurity.

Author: Zhou, B.
Title: Security and Privacy Protection Methods for Federated Learning for Big Data
Publication Title: Journal of Cyber Security and Mobility
Abstract Note: In the big data environment, federated learning faces multiple challenges such as privacy leakage, poisoning attacks, and communication overload. Existing methods, mostly functioning as point defenses, struggle to simultaneously balance security, efficiency, and utility. This research aims to construct a multi-layered federated learning security system encompassing “source protection, process defense, and global optimization”. The study builds a cloud-edge-end collaborative architecture, integrating differential privacy with Shamir's secret sharing to achieve data source perturbation and gradient share transmission. Through Mixup data augmentation combined with gradient clustering, it proactively detects poisoning attacks and introduces federated unlearning to remediate malicious impacts post factum. Based on static Bayesian games, it dynamically allocates privacy budgets to achieve a Nash equilibrium between personalized privacy and model utility. Experiments conducted on the CIFAR-10 and FEMNIST datasets, using a convolutional neural network as the base model and comparing it with the Vanilla FL model and module ablation versions, demonstrate the following: the FAA achieves a communication overhead of only 91.9 MB with 75 clients. Mixup combined with gradient clustering maintains an accuracy of 69.7% under 24% poisoning attacks. The game-theoretic framework attains a privacy-utility balance coefficient of up to 0.91. In complex dynamic scenarios, the multi-layered framework achieves an accuracy of 76.9%. This system exhibits robust security and adaptability under various attacks, providing a systematic solution for the practical deployment of federated learning.

Author: Priya, A.; Mohanty, S.; J.Balaji; Sekhar, A. V. N. Chandra; Narendran, T.; Kari, V. N. R. Sai Krishna
Title: Causal Blockchain-Governed Explainable Federated Learning for Trust-Calibrated and Privacy-Preserving Smart Healthcare Ecosystems
Publication Title: 2026 6th International Conference on Inventive Computation and Information Technologies (ICICIT)
Abstract Note: The quick expansion of IoT-related medical technologies and AI-based diagnostics has boosted the creation of smart healthcare systems, and even with centralized learning, sensitive patient data remains vulnerable to privacy concerns, lack of transparency, and adversarial risks. In order to address these issues, this paper will suggest a Causal Blockchain-Governed Explainable Federated learning (CBGEFL) framework of trust-calibrated and privacy-preserving healthcare intelligence. Author: Du, M.; Liu, Y.; Liu, G.; Kou, Z.; Han, Z.
Title: FedPoison: A Dual-Strategy Poisoning Attack on Multi-Agent Federated Learning With Local Differential Privacy
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking
Abstract Note: Federated learning (FL) is increasingly adopted in multi-agent healthcare systems where agents collaboratively train models without sharing sensitive data. While integrating FL with local differential privacy (LDP) offers robust protection against many privacy concerns, these models are still vulnerable to advanced adversarial attacks. A significant challenge is that even with LDP safeguards, FL models can be compromised by malicious attackers who inject poisoned data. In this paper, we introduce FedPoison, an advanced poisoning attack scheme designed to target both the mean and variance of datasets. Our method employs a dual strategy, integrating both input and output poisoning to effectively disrupt the FL process. Specifically, attackers can estimate the mean and variance of training data under LDP protection and inject poisoned data to carry out input poisoning attacks (IPA). The manipulated data in IPA is trained alongside the FL model, ultimately skewing the FL model’s output. Additionally, the attackers can bypass the LDP perturbation mechanism to launch output poisoning attacks (OPA) by uploading carefully altered mean and variance values, thus leading to biases in the aggregation of local model updates. Through the rigorous mathematical analyses, we demonstrate that the proposed scheme can successfully execute poisoning attacks on LDP-protected FL models. Extensive experiments conducted on four different datasets using PyTorch validate the effectiveness of our scheme, revealing that it significantly undermines the performance of FL models, even when LDP mechanisms are employed, highlighting its considerable threat to multi-agent collaborative decision-making systems in healthcare.

For malicious requesters providing inaccurate assessments, we adopt Pedersen Commitment to generate evidence, recorded on-chain for public scrutiny. Comprehensive security analysis demonstrates that UNITE^+\ achieves \(\textbackslash{}varepsilon,\textbackslash{}delta)\-local differential privacy. Finally, we conduct extensive experiments over Hyperledger Fabric on two real-world datasets, demonstrating satisfactory accuracy, robustness, and on-chain and off-chain performance.

Abstract Note: The rapid growth of Internet of Things (IoT) devices in fields like healthcare, industrial systems, and smart cities has created significant challenges in protecting sensitive data while ensuring real-time anomaly detection. Author: K, G. P. R.; Saranya, R.; M, S.; Thanikachalam, R.; M, S. K.; Aishwarya, B.
Title: Privacy-Preserving Collaborative Threat Intelligence for Predictive Cyber Defense
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Air Defense and Security (ICADS)
Abstract Note: The rapid increase in coordinated cyberattacks has exposed the limitations of isolated security monitoring. Author: Kumar, N.; Devi, P. G.; Upadhyaya, M.; K.Roopatharshini; Singh, J.; P, S.
Title: Reinforcement Learning–Driven Adaptive Differential Privacy for Personalized and Secure Federated Mobile Banking Intelligence

Abstract Note: The recent accelerated development of mobile banking applications has escalated the need to adopt smart recommendation systems that would not only be highly personalized but possess high data privacy as well. Older centralized learning models reveal delicate financial information, whereas current federated learning (FL) strategies use predetermined differential privacy (DP) budgets, and thus cause inefficient privacy-utility tradeoffs. To counter these issues, the current paper suggests a Reinforcement Learning-based Adaptive Differential Privacy (RL-ADP) system of secure and customized mobile banking intelligence. The suggested solution allows decentralization of model training at user devices without exchanging raw transaction data. A deep reinforcement learning agent actively tunes the privacy budget ( ε ) at each communication round based on the goal of optimizing a reward function that balances accuracy, privacy leakage and the cost of communication. Neural collaborative filtering is used to train local models to reflect user-specific financial behavior. Privacy-preserving updates are produced by the addition of Gaussian noise that is tuned by the RL-controlled ε. The federated averaging (FedAvg) is used to aggregate these updates and makes the global model better. It is implemented in Python 3.10, PyTorch, Flower, and OpenAI gym environments. Real-world financial datasets are experimentally evaluated and show the great improvement in performance compared to fixed-ε baselines. The model proposed has a Recall at 10 and AUC gain of about 10-15 % and 7-10% respectively. It also minimizes privacy loss by approximately 40-50 % , and overheads on communication by approximately 20-25%. The findings verify that adaptive privacy budgeting improves the accuracy of the model and data security. On the whole, the RL-ADP framework offers a privacy-preserving, efficient and scalable solution to next-generation mobile banking systems.

Subsequently, we present a personalized differential privacy (PDP) mechanism, which achieves comprehensive privacy protection with lower noise levels. Furthermore, the integration of the blockchain with the proposed reward mechanism overcomes SPOF and fosters constructive participation through transparent processes. Author: Bai, Y.; Liu, H.

Author: Jin, Z.; Li, D.; Liu, J.; Peng, H.; Wu, Q.; Guan, Z.; Susilo, W.; Deng, R. H.; Liu, Y.
Title: SharBipole: Secure and Scalable Sharding Blockchain-Based Federated Learning Against Poisoning Attacks
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security
Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative model training across distributed devices while preserving data privacy. However, it faces critical security challenges, including centralization risks and poisoning attacks, which degrade robustness and scalability. Existing schemes struggle to simultaneously mitigate targeted and untargeted poisoning attacks, impose restrictive adversary ratio assumptions (poison ratio <50%), and suffer from privacy-performance trade-offs. To address these limitations, we propose SharBipole, a decentralized FL scheme integrating sharding blockchain with a novel dual-metric defense mechanism, Bipole. SharBipole employs a Byzantine Fault Tolerant-enabled sharding architecture to eliminate single points of failure, reduce communication overhead, and enable parallel model aggregation. Meanwhile, the Bipole module defends against poisoning attacks using two adaptive similarity metrics to filter malicious updates dynamically. Reinforcement learning optimizes threshold adjustments, while noise-aware adaptive clipping balances privacy and model utility. Further, we give convergence analysis to prove the theoretical soundness and scalability of SharBipole. Lastly, extensive experimental evaluations demonstrate that SharBipole supports poison ratios exceeding 50% and improves throughput and latency. The model replacement attack with 60% adversaries is entirely ineffective against SharBipole, and the label-flipping attack achieves an attack success rate of only 2.344%. SharBipole establishes a scalable, secure, and privacy-preserving solution for distributed learning in massive environments.

Author: Ponsangeetha, A.; Chitra, R. J.; Sindhu, P. S.; Babu, V. D.; Vinayakaswami, N.; U, S. R.

Author: Denisha, J. J.; Jemina, J.; Ajibah, A. S. H.

Author: Dan, Y.; Yin, P.; Yang, Y.; He, Y.; Yang, Y.; Yang, D.; Li, X.

Author: Yang, W.; Chen, L.; Zhang, Z.; Shao, S.; Cao, X.
Title: AnonymTracker: Anonymously Traceable Copyright Protection for Federated Learning Model
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology
Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative model training with data privacy but risks malicious Clients, namely model leakers, compromising group intellectual property by secretly distributing or selling the valuable trained models. However, these works often achieve traceability by compromising the identity privacy of legitimate Clients. In this paper, we propose AnonymTracker, an anonymous FL model leaker tracing scheme. To protect the anonymity of legitimate Clients, we design a group signature-based fingerprint embedding mechanism, combining group signatures with model watermarking for effective and undeniable leaker identification. We further embed unique fingerprints in each Client’s model during training and use a cosine-similarity-based metric to compare extracted and embed fingerprints in the tracing phase, enhancing leak identification accuracy. The security analysis demonstrates AnonymTracker’s protection of legitimate Clients’ identity anonymity. Experiments on benchmark datasets and models confirm its good effectiveness, fidelity, and robustness against various watermark removal attacks.

Author: Sanku, R.; Recharla, M.; G, M. B. B.; Chikop, S. A.; K, M.
Title: Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning Framework with Adaptive Aggregated Gradient Perturbation for IoT Healthcare Systems
Publication Title: 2026 3rd International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
Abstract Note: In recent years, widespread adoption of Internet of Things (IoT) devices in healthcare has enabled continuous patient monitoring and intelligent clinical decision-making. However, the sensitive nature of medical data and strict privacy regulations had faced challenges to centralized data-driven learning approaches. Although federated learning (FL) improves data-sharing concerns by enabling decentralized model training, traditional FL frameworks remained vulnerable to gradient leakage and suffer from performance degradation because of static privacy mechanisms. To overcome these challenges, privacy-preserving federated learning framework based on Adaptive Aggregated Gradient Perturbation (A-AGP) is proposed for secure IoT healthcare analytics. Initially, healthcare institutions locally train models on private IoT-generated data without exposing raw information. Subsequently, clipped local gradients are securely aggregated at server, where an adaptive noise calibration strategy dynamically adjusts perturbation magnitude based on global gradient sensitivity and training dynamics. This adaptive perturbation mechanism significantly reduces unnecessary noise injection when compared to the static differential privacy approaches which effectively improved the model convergence and accuracy. Furthermore, secure aggregation ensures that individual client contributions remain indistinguishable, while privacy budget allocation across training rounds guarantees formal differential privacy protection.

Author: Laidi, R.; Merabtine, N.; Djenouri, D.; Latif, S.; Qadir, H. A.; Djenouri, Y.; Balasingham, I.
Title: Federated Learning in IoT Environments: Examining the Three-Way See-Saw for Privacy, Model-Performance, and Network-Efficiency

Abstract Note: This survey paper provides an in-depth exploration of Federated Learning (FL) in Internet of Things (IoT) environments, focusing on privacy-preserving techniques and their influence on model performance and network efficiency. Author: Ma, Y.
Title: PDS-FL: Privacy-Preserving Data Sharing in Blockchain Networks through Adaptive Differential Privacy and Trust-Aware Edge Filtering
Publication Title: 2026 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Communication Systems (ICICACS)
Abstract Note: Blockchain networks generate large volumes of sensitive transaction and node data that can improve consensus efficiency, anomaly detection, and network security through effective data sharing. However, centralized approaches raise privacy risks, while traditional Federated Learning (FL) suffers from model poisoning attacks, Non-Independent and Identically Distributed (Non-IID) data, high communication overhead, and single points of failure. This paper proposes Privacy-Preserving Data Sharing in Blockchain Networks (PDS-FL) through Adaptive Differential Privacy and Trust-Aware Edge Filtering, a four-tier hierarchical framework for secure data sharing in blockchain networks. This PDS-FL framework integrates Neural Factorization Machine for local training, Context-Aware Adaptive Differential Privacy (CAADP) guided by a Data Protection Score. The framework further employs a subjective logic-based reputation mechanism and Trust-Aware Multi-Krum Filtering at Road Side Units (RSUs). It subsequently applies a Verifiable Random Function (VRF)-based Sharded Consortium Blockchain and cloud-level knowledge distillation. Simulation experiments conducted on blockchain node telemetry and transaction logs show that the proposed PDS-FL framework achieves 95.8% final accuracy, reaches 92% accuracy in 61 rounds, reduces communication overhead to 92 MB per round for 100 vehicles, and limits attack success rates to 0.8-2.1%.

Author: Sathiyamoorthy, M.
Title: Blockchain-Enabled Federated Learning Framework for Secure Smart Healthcare Data Analytics

Abstract Note: In a smart healthcare environment, these devices produce a tremendous amount of health-related data that is extremely sensitive for patients, including data generated by wearable, electronic health records (EHRs), medical imaging systems and healthcare IoT sensors. Although federated learning allows for model training across different locations without exchanging patient information, traditional federated learning systems are still susceptible to attacks on model updates, data integrity problems and lack of visibility in the model aggregation process. Further, centralized health care analytics systems have privacy and security issues, as well as concerns about single points of failure and regulatory compliance. Based on the above analysis, this paper presents a Blockchain-Enabled Federated Learning Framework for Secure Smart Healthcare Data Analytics (BCFL-HC) to overcome these limitations. The framework proposed brings together permissioned blockchain and federated learning to create a secure, transparent and decentralized healthcare analytics ecosystem. The smart contracts are used to validate the updates to the local model before aggregation and differential privacy mechanisms are used to safeguard sensitive patient information against inference attacks. A PoS consensus protocol helps to reduce model poisoning attempts and ensures trustworthy participation. Also, the immutable ledgers, built using blockchain, offer the auditability and traceability of all learning transactions. The framework is tested on several healthcare applications like prediction of diabetes, diagnoses of heart disease, classification of medical images, and medical record for patient readmission risk assessment. Experimental results show that it has good performance, with a diagnostic accuracy rate of 97.86%, privacy preservation rate of 99.21%, attack detection rate of 96.74%, auditability confidence rate of 98.53%, and communication efficiency rate of 91.68%. The proposed BCFL-HC framework is compared to conventional federated learning and centralized healthcare analytics approaches and it is revealed that the proposed framework provides significant improvements in terms of security, transparency, reliability and predictive performance.

Author: Jedne, N. J.; Sheikh, S.; Ali, I.
Title: Privacy-Preserving Anomaly Detection in Federated Network Environments Using Differentially Private Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Blockchain, and Internet of Things (AIBThings)
Abstract Note: Machine-learning intrusion detection systems (IDS) achieve high accuracy but usually require raw network traffic to be centralized, which raises confidentiality, compliance, and scalability concerns in distributed deployments. This paper presents a privacy-preserving IDS that combines Federated Learning (FL) with Differential Privacy (DP). Using the NF-UQ-NIDS-v2 flow dataset, we establish centralized baselines (Random Forest, SVM, and a feed-forward neural network) and then train a federated model with the FedAvg algorithm across five clients that never share raw data. To protect the exchanged model updates against gradient-based leakage, DP is enforced locally through per-sample gradient clipping and Gaussian noise injection (DP-SGD) using the Opacus library. The federated model reaches 99.94% test accuracy, matching the centralized neural baseline, while the differentially private variant attains 98.95% at a per-client privacy budget of approximately 5 to 8. The roughly one-percent reduction quantifies a favourable privacy-utility trade-off and supports the feasibility of scalable, privacy-aware IDS for distributed networks.

Author: Wang, D.; Pang, X.; Hu, J.; Yue, S.; Ren, J.
Title: Two-Dimensional Stackelberg Game-Based Incentive Mechanism for Differential Private Federated Learning With Non-IID Data
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing
Abstract Note: Incentive mechanisms are essential for boosting client engagement in differential private federated learning (DP-FL). However, existing Stakelberg games-based incentive mechanisms typically assume that client decisions are one-dimension and that data is independent and identically distributed (IID) across clients. In reality, data distributions are often non-IID and clients have two-dimensional resources decisions, including data quantity and privacy. Therefore, in this paper, we present a novel two-dimensional Stackelberg game-based incentive mechanism for DP-FL with non-IID data, aiming to maximize the total utility of clients and server by seeking a balance between the clients’ two-dimensional decisions and the server’s payment. Specifically, we first formulate the utility functions of both server and clients under two-dimensional decisions and then model the interactions between server and clients as a single-leader-multiple-followers Stackelberg game. To derive the optimal decisions that maximize their utilities, we theoretically prove the existence of a Stackelberg equilibrium between server and clients. Due to the difficulty to directly calculate the Stackelberg equilibrium, we propose a bi-level multi-agent reinforment learning algorithm to learn the optimal decisions for both server and clients by trial and error. Extensive simulation results demonstrate that our proposed method outperforms the baselines in terms of total utility.
Manual Tags: Federated learning; Differential privacy; Incentive mechanism; Non-IID data; Reinforcement learning

Author: Lahoti, V.; Pai, V.; Hande, S.; Nashipudimath, M.; Chavan, S.
Title: Text Message Filtering System Using Transformer-Based Deep Learning and Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2026 1st International Conference on Innovation & Growth in Next-Gen Intelligent Technology & Engineering (IGNITE)

Author: Saranya, S.; S, M.; R, S.; Balachandren, G.; O, D. M.; Suguna, S.
Title: Federated Edge Intelligence for Secure and Scalable IoT Enabled Smart Systems
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Modern Sustainable Systems (CMSS)
Abstract Note: This paper proposes a federated edge intelligence framework to effectively tackle some of the important issues of privacy, security and scalability in Internet of Things enabled smart systems. The evaluation is done on heterogeneous IoT datasets, experimental network environments and performance metrics are calculated to measure accuracy, latency, communication overhead along with the security effectiveness. Author: Kalyani, N.; Jemin, V. M.; Glory, J. S.; Saravanan, K.; K, S.; Ramshankar, N.
Title: Secure and Intelligent Blockchain-Based Federated Directed Acyclic Graph Neural Network for Privacy-Preserving Brain Tumor Detection
Publication Title: 2026 6th International Conference on Soft Computing for Security Applications (ICSCSA)
Abstract Note: The convergence of healthcare has accelerated the adoption of federated learning for the group analysis of sensitive health information. On the other hand, deep learning has significantly enhanced medical image processing, enabling more accurate diagnoses and offering better treatment options in the era of the Internet of Things (IoT). Still, maintaining both high diagnostic quality and patient data privacy is a key problem because traditional techniques usually compromise either security or performance. To address these challenges, the current research proposes a Blockchain-Based Directed Acyclic Graph Neural Network with a Meerkat Optimization Algorithm (DAGNNet-MAO) for brain tumor detection. A set of high-resolution brain MRI images from the Brain Tumor Dataset is initially preprocessed using Robust Double-Weighted Guided Image Filtering (RDWGIF) to remove noise and improve image quality. The One Single Transformer (OST) is then used to extract features and enable local and global representations. The features are classified using DAGNNet with Meerkat Optimization Algorithm (MAO)-optimized model parameters, and prediction is secured through Blockchain-based Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning (BPPFL). The proposed model brings out impressive performance with 99.8% accuracy, 99.0% F1-score, 99.1% precision, 99.3% recall, 99.1% specificity, a low error rate of 0.8%, high throughput of 59.4 Mbps, low latency of 8.6 ms, and security level of 99%, showing that it is highly effective for fast, accurate, and privacy-protecting brain tumor detection in intelligent healthcare systems.

Author: Liu, L.; Chen, J.; Fan, H.; Xu, K.; Zhang, P.; Li, X.; Xiang, T.
Title: BRFL: A Blockchain-Based and Ring Signature-Empowered Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning Scheme for Low-Altitude Networks
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking
Abstract Note: In low-altitude networks, federated learning (FL) with uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) faces significant privacy threats—notably membership inference attacks (MIAs) that correlate multi-round gradients to infer client participation. To cope with the stringent latency, mobility, and energy budgets of UAV swarms, this work proposes Blockchain- and Ring-signature-empowered Federated Learning (BRFL), a privacy-preserving framework tailored to aerial networks. BRFL uses a decentralized ledger for auditing and storage, and a no-pairing elliptic curve ring signature to anonymize client uploads by forming a random UAV ring each round. Smart contracts further verify the signatures and invoke a lightweight ring-internal supervision voting mechanism to filter malicious updates. Experiments on MNIST and CIFAR-10 demonstrate that BRFL converges stably on non-IID data even when 40% of UAVs behave Byzantinely. Theoretical analysis further bounds the adversary’s cross-round-linking probability by \(1/n)^{T}\ . Overall, BRFL preserves UAV anonymity with negligible overhead, offering a practical solution for privacy-aware and scalable FL in large-scale aerial networks.

Author: Wu, M.; Guo, K.; Wang, Z.; Dong, C.; Liu, Y.; Wu, Q.; Zheng, Z.
Title: Federated Learning-Driven Covert Communication in Satellite–Terrestrial Integrated Networks: A Privacy-Preserving Framework
Publication Title: IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Communications
Abstract Note: Due to the broadcasting characteristics of satellite-terrestrial integrated networks (STINs), security vulnerabilities have emerged as a critical concern requiring urgent mitigation strategies. Unlike traditional security methods, federated learning (FL) enables a large number of participants to collaborate without disclosing actual privacy data. Its potential as a framework that combines collaborative model training and covert payload transmission in STINs represents a significant research gap. This paper proposes FedSAT, a novel FL-based covert communication scheme for STINs, in which each participant in the FL process can utilize the shared learning protocol as a covert medium for transmitting arbitrary information in privacy-preserving framework. Our framework leverages the dual capabilities of FL for collaborative model training and covert payload embedding, utilizing Geostationary Earth Orbit (GEO) satellites and distributed terrestrial nodes to embed sensitive data within FL parameter updates. The system maintains model convergence accuracy while implementing strategic encryption to achieve robust sharing and transmission of payloads within the FL framework. Comprehensive simulation tests demonstrate the framework significant efficacy, achieving a 98.7% communication coverage for covert payload transmission under monitoring by low Earth orbit (LEO) surveillance satellites, with only a 0.8% decrease in model accuracy. Author: Vashisth, A.; Kaur, G.; Jain, R.; Pathania, N.

Author: Singh, A. R.; Ashraf, M. W. A.; Rathore, R. S.; Bhatt, M. W.; Bajaj, M.; Atrekar, V.
Title: Enhanced Quantum-Inspired Metaheuristic Framework for Federated Trust Management and Blockchain-Enabled Privacy in Large-Scale Internet of Vehicles
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Consumer Electronics
Abstract Note: The dynamic nature and large scale of the Internet of Vehicles (IoV) pose challenges in managing scalable, trust, and privacy-preserving trust management systems. These limitations are overcome by introducing the Enhanced Quantum-Inspired Metaheuristic Framework for Federated Learning (EQIMFFL) to ensure a secure and trusted IoV communication environment. Initially, quantum-inspired networks are applied to a trust model that utilizes quantum-inspired activation and superposition-related neurons to enhance feature exploration for trust inference. A particle optimization-related federated aggregation process is incorporated to train the vehicle features and update them to the roadside units and central servers. The hybrid optimization process implemented at the RSU level enhances the aggregation, which updates the model and directly improves the global model accuracy. Finally, a blockchain ledger is incorporated to maintain the cloud server and RSU, in which the hash function is integrated to manage records that directly impact trust decisions, confirming the resilience against unwanted activities, auditability, and integrity. In addition, the Shapley value is incorporated to reward the vehicle for maintaining the data quality while ensuring secure transmission. Then, the complex urban IoV scenario is implemented to evaluate the system’s performance, in which the framework achieves a 33.1% improvement in communication overhead, 18.5% faster convergence, and 96.83% trust prediction accuracy compared to the baseline methods.

Author: Chen, X.; Li, S.
Title: Semantic-Aware Differentially Private and Trust-Driven Robust Federated Optimization for Multi-Center Medical Image Analysis
Publication Title: 2026 6th International Conference on Computer Science and Blockchain (CCSB)
Abstract Note: Federated learning enables hospitals to jointly train diagnostic models without sharing raw medical images, yet multi-center deployment remains vulnerable to site-dependent semantic shifts, privacy leakage, and unreliable model updates. This paper presents a two-level optimization framework. At the client level, SemaDiffPriv disentangles shared diagnostic representations from institution-specific features and perturbs only clipped shared updates, retaining private semantics locally under differential privacy. At the server level, FedTrustOpt estimates client reliability from update stability, historical consistency, and directional agreement, producing trust scores that control both robust aggregation weight and the next-round privacy budget. A result-free evaluation protocol is specified for multi-center brain-tumor segmentation under non-IID data and anomalous-client settings, with formal definitions of convergence variance, angular update dispersion, and robustness degradation. The framework establishes a unified basis for studying utility, privacy, and aggregation robustness without centralized medical data.

Author: Druba, R. A.; Shihab, A. H.; Mussa, A.; Mansurova, M.
Title: Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning for Post-Flood Security and Resource Planning in Bangladesh: A Review and Conceptual Framework
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Quantum Photonics, Artificial Intelligence & Networking (QPAIN)
Abstract Note: Bangladesh is highly vulnerable to floods, with around 70 million people living in flood prone areas and a large share of the population exposed to high flood risk. Disaster response increasingly depends on detailed household data for forecasting, evacuation, and aid distribution. When this data is collected and stored centrally, it exposes vulnerable groups, especially women, children, and displaced families, to theft, harassment, trafficking, and gender based violence through misuse or data breaches. We review federated learning applications in disaster management and propose a simple conceptual framework for privacy preserving post flood security and resource planning in Bangladesh. The framework model is structured into 04 layers, namely, local data collection, federated training, secure aggregation, and personalized deployment. A structured review of 45 studies covering federated learning algorithms, privacy mechanisms such as secure aggregation and differential privacy, and disaster related applications shows that existing work performs well technically in flood forecasting, disaster detection, and infrastructure monitoring while keeping data local. However, most studies still focus on accuracy and efficiency without addressing human security risks during aid operations. The suggested conceptual framework combines the ideas of federated optimization, Byzantine robust aggregation, fairness systems, personalized learning, and multi stakeholder governance to safeguard the vulnerable groups in post flood response. It considers system heterogeneity, the communication constraints, and the organizational capacity variation. The framework extends evaluation criteria to include human-centered indicators such as reduction of security incidents and fair distribution of aid. This work outlines future directions for deploying federated learning in disaster settings where beneficiary data collection creates direct protection risks.

Author: Acharya, K. P.; Sonowal, G.; Poudel, R.; Mandal, S. P.; Gautam, S. C.; Khati, A. K.
Title: Implementing Blockchain Technology for Enhanced Privacy and Security in Federated Learning Health
Publication Title: 2026 1st International Conference on Sustainable Solutions in Engineering Technologies and Earth Science (ICSSETES)
Abstract Note: Healthcare data represents the most sensitive category of personal information and the most aggressively targeted dataset in the global economy: the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Office for Civil Rights recorded 725 data breaches affecting 500 or more individuals in 2024 alone, collectively exposing over 186 million patient records. Federated learning (FL) offers a theoretically compelling solution by enabling collaborative model training across decentralised clinical datasets without raw data leaving institutional boundaries. However, FL in isolation remains vulnerable to gradient inversion attacks, model poisoning, and Byzantine client failures, which reconstruct patient-level sensitive information from shared model updates with documented attack success rates exceeding 84% under standard FL configurations. Compared with standard FedAvg without security augmentation, BC-FedHealth reduces gradient inversion attack success rate from 84.3% to 3.1%, model poisoning accuracy degradation from 18.7 percentage points to 0.9 percentage points, and achieves audit trail completeness of 99.97% across 4.2 million model update transactions. By systematically categorizing and analyzing state-of-the-art techniques, this work offers valuable insights for researchers and practitioners aiming to achieve an optimal balance between privacy preservation and the computational as well as communication efficiency in PPFL systems.

Author: Nair, A. S. V.; Achary, R.
Title: Security and Privacy Challenges in Web 3.0: A Survey of Threats, Authentication Mechanisms, and Open Problems
Publication Title: 2026 6th International Conference on Soft Computing for Security Applications (ICSCSA)
Abstract Note: Web 3.0 is a paradigm shift in the design of the Internet, from centralized platform custodians to decentralized blockchain-based infrastructures and user empowered data models. This results in a new and dynamic threat landscape including social engineering, smart-contract exploitation, cryptojacking, identity abuse and data-reliability failures, which existing security frameworks only address in part. This paper provides a comprehensive survey on the security and privacy issues of Web 3.0. We systematically review the dominant attack classes. We review the current state of decentralized authentication mechanisms including publicprivate key schemes, Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs) and Verifiable Credentials. We synthesize findings from ten recent studies to identify recurring gaps. In particular, the unresolved tension between user anonymity and network accountability has repeatedly been identified as an open problem in the literature. We characterize this gap, classify proposed mitigations, and identify areas for future research. The objective of this survey is to offer a structured reference for researchers and practitioners who are developing security-aware decentralized applications.

Author: Feng, L.; Guo, J.; Fang, F.; He, Z.; Yu, Y.; Yao, S.; Peng, X.
Title: SEPP-FLBC: A Secure and Efficient Privacy Protection Scheme Using Federate Learning and Blockchain for Edge-End-Cloud Devices
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Services Computing
Abstract Note: The convergence of federated learning (FL) and blockchain in edge-end-cloud systems offers promising opportunities for privacy-preserving collaborative intelligence. However, existing blockchain-enhanced FL (BFL) approaches remain vulnerable to malicious participants and lack robust protection for model updates. To address these issues, we propose SEPP-FLBC, a Secure and Efficient Privacy Protection framework based on Federated Learning and Blockchain Committees. SEPP-FLBC introduces a novel blockchain committee consensus mechanism to validate model updates and defend against unreliable nodes. It further employs a refined multi-party communication paradigm to facilitate indirect and secure data interactions, reducing the risk of information leakage. Additionally, differential privacy noise is applied to model updates to enhance resistance to inference attacks. A formal convergence analysis is conducted to ensure model stability and minimize overhead. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that SEPP-FLBC achieves superior accuracy while maintaining strong privacy guarantees and communication efficiency, outperforming state-of-the-art BFL methods in both security and performance.

Author: Kumar, R.; Gupta, S.; Ali, A.

Author: Duggegowda, D.; S, A. G.; Monga, S.; Jose, T.; Presannakumar, K.
Title: A Blockchain-Enabled Federated Learning Framework for Secure and Intelligent Maritime Communication Networks
Publication Title: 2026 Forth International Conference on Networks, Multimedia and Information Technology (NMITCON)
Abstract Note: The existing conventional centralized maritime communication network is very vulnerable to cyber-attacks such as spoofing, jamming, and stealing the data due to its heterogeneous nature and distributed structure. In this research work, a blockchain-based federated learning approach is proposed for maritime communication networks. This architecture applies a blockchain-based approach in a light form for secure data authentication and data integrity with the federated learning approach where collaborative learning is performed without data sharing. With smart contracts, the access control of the ship is managed and nodes can learn their own anomaly detection models while the global model is aggregated by edge servers. In this paper, a novel blockchain-based federated learning approach is introduced that provides solutions for various issues in terms of privacy, trust management, secure aggregation, and reliable communication in the marine environment. This model is tested by simulating maritime communications and the results indicate superior attack detection, low latency, and high data security of the proposed model compared to existing methods. Author: Babar, M.; Kaleem, S.; Qureshi, B.; Boulila, W.
Title: TrustChain-FL: Lightweight Blockchain-Assisted Trust Aggregation for IoT-Enabled Decentralized Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE 103rd Vehicular Technology Conference (VTC2026-Spring)
Abstract Note: Federated learning (FL) is well suited to IoT settings because it lets devices train a common model without sharing their raw data. Even so, the training process can become unreliable when some clients send noisy or malicious updates. This becomes harder under non-IID data and irregular client participation. In this paper, we propose TrustChain-FL, a lightweight blockchain-assisted trust aggregation framework for this setting. The training process remains off-chain, while a small validator committee checks whether client updates look plausible. To keep the system auditable, only compact signed validation results are written to a permissioned ledger. The server then uses these results in a rolling trust-weighted FedAvg scheme. We evaluate the method on the UCI HAR dataset using non-IID Dirichlet partitioning with ρ = 20% label-flip attackers. TrustChain-FL achieves the best macro-F1 score of 93.3%, while FedAvg, trimmed mean, and median reach 92.2%, 89.6%, and 87.2%, respectively. It also shows a more stable training trend across rounds. Overall, the results show that lightweight validation and trust-aware aggregation can make IoT-FL more robust without relying on heavy on-chain computation.

Author: Akpan, E. E.; Ojaide, E.; Rosa, R. L.; Adedokun, M. T.; Matthew, U. O.; Adenike, O. O.; Okafor, N. U.; Adasme, P.; Rodriguez, D. Z.
Title: SAFHA: An IoT Predictive Analytics for Security and Privacy Protection in Distributed Health System
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Connected Intelligence for Industrial Applications (CI2A)
Abstract Note: Federated learning (FL) is transforming distributed health information system through cognitive intelligence across Internet of Things (IoT)-driven platforms. Secure Adaptive Federated Health Analytics (SAFHA), a unique framework is presented in this study with a goal of improving security, privacy, and predictive analytics in healthcare settings that uses artificial intelligence(AI). The SAFHA framework addresses several issues in FL healthcare, such as limited interoperability across IoT medical devices, model security flaws, and data privacy threats. In addition to maximizing collaborative AI training across various healthcare institutions, SAFHA enhances patient data protection by utilizing secure aggregation, differential privacy, and blockchain-based authentication. SAFHA enabled IoT predictive analytics by enabling real-time compliance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) on digital data security, that addresses legal concerns surrounding electronic healthcare systems. SAFHA demonstrates substantial advancements across four critical blockchain-based identity security dimensions when benchmarked against conventional centralized architectures. Specifically, the computing framework improved data authentication precision by 38 %, while smart contract enforcement enhances authorization efficiency by 42 %. The integration of tamper-resistant transaction logs further strengthens auditability and reliability by 47 %. The combined application of zero-knowledge proofs and differential privacy techniques fortifies anonymity safeguards by 51 %, contributing to an overall security improvement of \textbackslash{}mathbf{5 1 \textbackslash{}%}\. Collectively, these outcomes underscore SAFHA's transformative potential in healthcare data management and analytics, fostering robust digital health ecosystems, ensuring ethical AI utilization, and reinforcing regulatory compliance across the broader digital health landscape.

Author: Xue, Y.; Zhai, Y.; Qiao, Y.; Zhang, D.; Ghoneim, A.
Title: Blockchain-Based Secure and Efficient Federated Learning Scheme for IoMT Consumer Electronics Devices
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Consumer Electronics
Abstract Note: The Internet of Medical Things consumer electronics (IoMT-CE) devices integrated with deep learning (DL) model have achieved remarkable success in the medical field, which provides intelligent diagnostic assistance. However, as DL technologies evolve rapidly, a key challenge lies in how to continuously enhance the intelligent assisted diagnostic capabilities of IoMT-CE devices. Federated learning (FL), an effective distributed learning framework, holds great potential to address this issue. In this article, we propose a novel secure and efficient FL scheme for IoMT-CE devices based on consortium blockchain. In this scheme, all participating hospitals, the aggregation server (AS), and the noise parameter server (NPS) establish a consortium blockchain, where hash values and signature data are stored. Paillier homomorphic encryption (HE) and noise mechanisms are employed to protect patient privacy, while an elliptic curve cryptography-based proxy re-encryption (ECC-PRE) strategy is adopted to ensure model security between the AS and IoMT-CE devices. Furthermore, this scheme guarantees that model updates are applied correctly, even when local models cannot be uploaded to hospitals. Finally, the performance of our proposed scheme is verified. The results demonstrate that the encryption mechanisms have almost no impact on model accuracy, and the proposed scheme proves to be robust and fault-tolerant in cases of disconnection.

Author: Kothavle, S.; Chandre, P.
Title: Federated Learning with Homomorphic Encryption: Balancing Data Privacy and Defense Against Adversarial Attacks
Publication Title: 2026 1st International Conference on Computer, Mechatronics, Robotics & Artificial Intelligence (ICCMRAI)
Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) facilitates the distributed training without revealing raw data but still suffers from privacy leakage and adversarial attack. In order to tackle these issues, we present a secure and resilient FL framework, which integrates homomorphic encryption (HE) and Median-of-Means (MoM) aggregator. To maintain client confidentiality, we encrypt client updates using the CKKS scheme and the MoM aggregated deltas on encrypted values also prevent label-flip and sign-flip attacks against MoM aggregation. In particular, we present trade-offs for privacy, robust-ness, and efficiency via experiments in the MNIST data set with five variants: baseline FL, FL + HE, FL under attack, FL + HE under attack, and FL + HE + MoM. The results demonstrate that FedAvg is both efficient and very vulnerable, and that encryption alone incurs high overhead and fails to provide strong protection while the proposed FL + HE + MoM achieves 0% attack success rate and transmit baseline level accuracy whilst avoiding additional communication cost with only moderate increase in run time.

Author: Shajahan, S.; Swetha, S.; Elavarasi, J.; B, Y.; Hashini, S.; N, A. S.
Title: Protecting Intelligent Information Systems: Security Threats, Privacy Risks, and Defense Mechanisms
Publication Title: 2026 2nd International Conference on Smart Technologies for Sustainable Development Goals (ICSTSDG)
Abstract Note: Intelligent Information Systems (IIS) have taken center stage in the modern digital infrastructures and have allowed sophisticated decision-making in healthcare, finance, transportation, smart cities, and in cyber-physical systems. Their increasing reliance on big data, machine learning models, and distributed systems, however, leads to a major security and privacy concerns. This survey provides a comprehensive analysis of emerging security vulnerabilities and privacy risks in IIS, such as adversarial ML attacks, data breach, model poisoning, re-identification threat, and privacy leakage in AI pipelines. It also discusses models of security and privacy protection like the cryptographic methods, privacy preserving ML, differential privacy, federated learning, zero-trust architectures, blockchain security, and secure semantic models. The paper examines the recent trends, such as quantumresistant AI security, cognitive security, and AI-assisted privacy surveillance as well as the legal and ethical implications associated with regulatory frameworks. Nevertheless, issues related to scalability, trustworthy AI, interoperability, and realtime threat detection remain problematic. Future research has been directed toward integrated security-by-design and privacy-by-design as approaches for developing robust, transparent, and ethically consistent intelligent systems. In general, this survey indicates that there is a critical need for effective security and privacy models to guarantee the safe and reliable functioning of next generation intelligent information systems.

Author: Udurume, M.; Ahakonye, L. A. C.; Lee, J. M.; Kim, D.-S.
Title: Trust-Aware Federated Learning with Round-Level Blockchain Logging for Software-Defined Vehicles
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE Vehicular Networking Conference (VNC)
Abstract Note: Software-Defined Vehicles (SDVs) require continuous and collaborative learning to support adaptive decisionmaking and security in dynamic Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS). Federated Learning (FL) enables such collaboration while preserving data locality, but SDV-oriented FL remains vulnerable to adversarial participants due to mobility-induced non-Independent and Identically Distributed (non-IID) data, intermittent participation, and limited update accountability. Existing blockchain-assisted FL approaches also incur excessive overhead when validation is performed per client update. This paper proposes a trust-aware blockchain-assisted FL framework tailored for SDV environments. A dynamic trust-scoring mechanism evaluates participating vehicles in FL rounds based on update consistency, anomaly deviation, and historical behavior, allowing selective isolation of persistently low-trust clients. To provide tamper-resistant auditability with bounded overhead, aggregated trust metadata is recorded using PureChain, a permissioned blockchain that employs Proof-of-Authority and Association (PoA { }^{2})\ consensus and enforces a single authenticated blockchain commit per FL round. The framework is evaluated on the VeReMi dataset under targeted and mobility-aware poisoning attacks over 30 FL rounds. The results demonstrate that the trust-aware aggregation strategy achieves more stable accuracy and improved Macro-F1 performance compared to FedAvg and Trimmed Mean, while effectively isolating malicious SDVs with controlled false positives. In general, the proposed approach enables robust, auditable, and scalable FL suitable for adversarial and time-sensitive SDV deployments.

Author: Bobade, V.; Ladwan, S.; Waghmare, P.; Ghai, L.; Chaudhari, P.; Puri, C.
Title: A Paradigm Shift in Digital Trust: A Cybersecurity Analysis of Zero-Knowledge Proofs
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Modern Sustainable Systems (CMSS)
Abstract Note: The digitalization of the technologies has vastly enhanced the risk of cyber-attacks to the financial institutions, government, and users. Author: Thaalbi, M.; Tabbane, N.
Title: An FL-Blockchain Urbanization Approach for Trust and Intelligent Collaboration Platform in Smart Cities
Publication Title: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
Abstract Note: A smart city offers different services such as transportation, waste management, public safety, healthcare, energy management, and governance that continuously exchange massive volumes of sensitive data across highly connected 6G-enabled environments. Existing blockchain-enabled federated learning (FL) frameworks for smart cities generally rely on monolithic architectures that suffer from scalability limitations, excessive consensus overhead, and limited support for autonomous interservice coordination. Furthermore, current approaches rarely address hierarchical trust management and secure collaboration across heterogeneous urban domains. This article introduces a hierarchical service-oriented orchestration architecture enabling scalable and autonomous collaboration between heterogeneous smart city domains. More specifically, this article proposes a hierarchical nested blockchain framework integrating FL, homomorphic encryption, smart-contract-driven governance, and Hashgraph-based asynchronous Byzantine fault-tolerant (aBFT) consensus for scalable and privacy-preserving intersmart-city services collaboration. Experimental results based on a prototype implementation using the Hedera Hashgraph platform and a traffic-flow prediction use case demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed framework. The evaluation confirms that the hierarchical service-oriented architecture reduces communication overhead associated with encrypted federated-learning aggregation while preserving data privacy and secure cross-service collaboration.

Author: Taherpour, A.; Wang, X.
Title: ZK-HybridFL: Zero-Knowledge Proof-Enhanced Hybrid Ledger for Federated Learning
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems
Abstract Note: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training while preserving data privacy, yet both centralized and decentralized approaches face challenges in scalability, security, and update validation. We propose ZK-HybridFL, a secure decentralized FL framework that integrates a directed acyclic graph (DAG) ledger with dedicated sidechains and zero-knowledge proofs (ZKPs) for privacy-preserving model validation. The framework uses event-driven smart contracts (EDSCs) and an oracle-assisted sidechain to verify local model updates without exposing sensitive data. A built-in challenge mechanism efficiently detects adversarial behavior. In experiments on image classification and language modeling tasks, ZK-HybridFL achieves faster convergence, higher accuracy, lower perplexity, and reduced latency compared to Blade-FL and ChainFL. It remains robust against substantial fractions of adversarial and idle nodes, supports sub-second on-chain verification with efficient gas usage, and prevents invalid updates and orphanage-style attacks. This makes ZK-HybridFL a scalable and secure solution for decentralized FL across diverse environments.

Author: Mishra, S.; Prajapati, Y.; Aggarwal, K.; Pal, S.
Title: BloBS-FL: A Robust Architecture of Blockchain Based Decentralized Split Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2026 18th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
Abstract Note: Modern distributed machine learning paradigms face critical challenges in balancing privacy preservation, communication efficiency, and Byzantine resilience. This paper introduces BloBS-FL, a hybrid architecture that integrates split learning with blockchain-based decentralized federated learning. Our architecture partitions model training between client-side feature extractors and server-side classifiers. BloBS-FL employs Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance (PBFT)-based consensus for poison attack resistance. Experimental results on network intrusion detection datasets demonstrate 93.5%, and 90% accuracy with MNIST and CICIDS-2017 datasets. BloBS-FL reduces communication overhead and resolves the problem of privacy via split learning making the architecture suitable for secure applications.

Author: Tang, M.; Wang, W.; Yu, S.
Title: Privacy Pricing: A Survey from the Perspective of Privacy Business
Publication Title: Big Data Mining and Analytics
Abstract Note: Privacy is valuable, especially in the current digital economy with its thriving online services. The value and price of the private data perform a critical role in most of economic activities like trading and sharing, and even in the security protection process. The price also embodies the value of privacy itself, which raises people's awareness of their privacy. Existing work on pricing varies with different purposes and methods, and accordingly the term “price of privacy” has not found a consistent and consensus definition, which poses difficulties for the future research in this domain. To address this and offer a clear map for the work in pricing private data, we summarise the existing work on privacy pricing into two major business on the market including trading and protection, and further classify them in terms of different pricing methods. We also evaluate the contribution for each pricing model, and we find that there is work to do to improve the pricing model themselves, and address privacy security problems with privacy pricing, especially in the new era of generative artificial intelligence.

Author: Kumar, A.; Aparcana-Tasayco, A. J.; Kim, M.; Camacho, D.; Park, J. H.
Title: Blockchain-Assisted Federated Learning to Secure Critical IoT Infrastructure
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Consumer Electronics
Abstract Note: The expansion of Internet of Things (IoT) devices brings challenges of data security and privacy preservation in critical infrastructure. The proposed system combines blockchain technology with federated learning (FL) to secure IoT communications. It ensures decentralized model training with immutable and verifiable blockchain records. The study incorporates a lightweight FL model with a two-stage multitask head for binary and multiclass attack detection, enabling efficient deployment in constrained IoT. Federated learning effectively resolves privacy issues by facilitating cooperative model training across dispersed IoT nodes without revealing raw data. It guarantees collaboration based on a trust-aware mechanism that evaluates the reliability of clients and guides the robust aggregation. Blockchain ensures tamper-evident auditing of model updates and supports Byzantine-fault-tolerant (BFT) and Delegated proof-of-stake (DPoS) trust guarantees. Blockchain records cryptographic hashes of model modifications in a tamper-proof ledger, ensuring the legitimacy of the training process. Smart contracts enable the tamper-evident logging of model hashes, and global model convergence is ensured by federated averaging. Experimental tests demonstrate a secure and verifiable collaborative learning enabling model integrity in IoT networks. The study achieved a fast block generation time of 77.3ms, satisfactory model performance with 98% of training accuracy, and 0.992 F1-score alongside meaningful evolution of client trust values. The final testing accuracy of the FL model for the binary class detection is 98.1%. In a multi-class attack scenario, the FL model achieves a strong multi-class attack detection rate for dominant attack types.

Author: S, P. M. K.; Prakash, S. P. Shiva; Krinkin, K.
Title: Federated Multi-Faceted Trust Framework for Social Internet of Things
Publication Title: 2026 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Communication Systems (ICICACS)
Abstract Note: The rapid growth of Social Internet of Things (SIoT) has created new challenges for establishing reliable trust among IoT devices due to dynamic interactions and heterogeneous environments. The traditional trust models are based on limited features and a centralized approach. This has limited the possibility of establishing complex trust relationships. This paper proposes a novel federated multifaceted trust model for social internet of things, termed FMFT-SIoT. The proposed trust model is based on a federated approach for calculating trust scores for IoT devices. The proposed trust model is based on a comprehensive system model for calculating trust scores for IoT devices. The proposed trust model is validated using various ratios for training and testing. The proposed trust model is compared with traditional trust models using various performance metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, mean squared error, and mean absolute error. The performance of the proposed trust model is found to be superior compared to traditional trust models, and it provides higher accuracy and lower error rates.

Author: Kang, S.; Sun, Y.; Wu, Y.; Wang, Y.; Wang, Q.; Liang, X.
Title: Privacy-Enhanced Federated Learning Algorithm Empowered by Blockchain and Game Theory
Publication Title: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
Abstract Note: Federated learning (FL) enables participants to collaboratively train a global model through distributed training without sharing raw data. However, this distributed training is vulnerable to single-point failures, privacy leakage, and Byzantine attacks. To address these challenges simultaneously, we propose a privacy-enhanced FL algorithm empowered by blockchain and game theory (BGFL). First, we integrate blockchain technology into FL and establish a decentralized training paradigm, which effectively avoids the threat of single-point failures in centralized training. Second, we propose a privacy protection method that combines Chinese remainder theorem and Shamir’s secret sharing, providing dual privacy protection for participants in decentralized FL scenarios. Furthermore, leveraging the homomorphic properties of the proposed privacy-enhanced approach, a Byzantine attack defense mechanism is designed. Finally, a game-theoretic incentive mechanism is proposed to mitigate malicious behaviors during collaborative training, ensuring secure cooperation among all parties. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared to baseline methods, BGFL improves test accuracy by 0.93%–22.75%. Compared to other secret sharing-based FL schemes, BGFL requires only 5.91% of the computational overhead and 4.01% of the communication overhead at the same dataset scale. This enables efficient achievement of security and robustness objectives.

Author: Ahmed, R. H.; Khan, M. S.; Delshadi, A.; Ahmad, N.; Hussain, M.
Title: Edge-Intelligent Blockchain Framework for Ultra-Secure and Energy-Efficient Real-Time Patient Monitoring in IoMT Using Hierarchical Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Data Science, Machine Learning, and Intelligence (DataSciMI)
Abstract Note: Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) provides the possibility to conduct continuous monitoring of health, perform intelligent diagnostics, and make a clinical decision based on data. Nonetheless, there are security, privacy, scalability, latency, and energy issues with large-scale deployment. Although Federated learning (FL) provides less exposure to data, and blockchain provides trust, current solutions that combine both blockchain and FL have high consensus overhead, fixed privacy, and adversarial resilience. To handle them, we present an Edge-Intelligent Hierarchical Blockchain-IoMT framework that integrates Hierarchical FL (HFL), Adaptive Differential Privacy (ADP), Lightweight Homomorphic Encryption (LHE), Zero-Knowledge Proof (ZKP) authentication, and an Energy-Aware PoS with Edge Learning (PoS-EL) consensus. Hierarchical aggregation minimizes bottlenecks in communication. ADP minimizes security vs utility. ZKP achieves authentication and PoS-EL minimizes energy consumption. Experiments on real-world data demonstrate 99.21% accuracy of detecting anomalies, 34% decreased latency, 41% decreased energy usage, 52 percent lower blockchain overhead and 97 percent resistance to adversarial attacks, which justifies the framework in real-time, mission-critical IoMT systems.

Author: Khatri, H.; R, V. K.; R, R. K.
Title: FederoChain: A Lightweight Federated Learning and Blockchain Framework for Secure and Transparent Medical Diagnostics
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Trends in Quantum Computing and Emerging Business Technologies (TQCEBT)
Abstract Note: Medical institutions leverage machine learning across multiple domains of disease to improve accuracy, efficiency, and decision support. Systems that provide secure training of models exist, but so do technical gaps in them, such as complexity and high communication cost. Federated learning enables collaborative training without moving raw data, but introduces concerns of trust, as institutions must rely on correct aggregation and honest participation. Blockchain technology provides an immutable and verifiable ledger that addresses this challenge by recording model updates, proofs, and participant information in a transparent manner. The design provides secure aggregation of updates to ensure individual privacy, norm-based defenses to mitigate malicious contributions, and blockchain auditability to guarantee transparency. Using this paper, we aim to improve trust and feasibility in collaboration between multiple medical institutions.

Author: Manavadaria, M. S.; Sugin, S. V.; Gupta, M.; P, D.; Abhang, S.; Kumar, S.
Title: Intelligent Hybrid 6G Communication Framework with Cloud-Based Intrusion Detection and Privacy Preservation

Abstract Note: The future 6G communication network will provide ultimate connection and ultra data-rates with ultra-low latency but at the same time, it faces potential cyber-attacks on very-diffused infrastructures along with big concerns in privacy. Old style intrusion detection systems suffer from centralized information processing, slow in responding to threat and not having privacy guarantees. Here, the objective was to design advanced hybrid 6G communication system with cloud-based intrusion detection and unified privacy preservation techniques which is proposed in this study. The proposed framework makes use of edge-level traffic analysis, federated learning and differential privacy to enable collaborative real-time threat investigation while protecting raw data from direct exposure. A hybrid deep learning Architecture, analyses multi-dimensional traffic features while cloud intelligence performs global correlation and adaptive model optimization. The extensive experimentation on a large synthetic dataset indicates better performance than classical machine learning and deep learning baselines, achieving a detection accuracy of 99.21%, precision of 98.95%, recall of 99.10% and less false positive rate (0.42%). Author: You, Z.; Dong, X.; Cheng, K.; Mu, X.; Fu, J.; Ma, S.; Qu, Q.; Shen, Y.
Title: PriFFT: Privacy-Preserving Federated Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models via Hybrid Secret Sharing
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing
Abstract Note: Fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) raises privacy concerns due to the risk of exposing sensitive training data. Federated learning (FL) mitigates this risk by keeping training samples on local devices, while facing the following privacy problems. (i) Recent studies show that adversaries can still infer private information in FL. (ii) LLM parameters are shared publicly during federated fine-tuning, while developers are often reluctant to disclose these parameters. (iii) Existing works focus on secure inference but neglects privacy-preserving fine-tuning. Inspired by above problems, we propose PriFFT, a privacy-preserving federated fine-tuning mechanism, to protect both model parameters and users’ privacy. Due to considerable LLM parameters, we present hybrid secret sharing combining arithmetic secret sharing (ASS) and function secret sharing (FSS) to build secure operations and implement secure neural network layers and activation functions for fine-tuning. We optimize several secure protocols based on FSS, including reciprocal calculation, tensor products, natural exponentiation, softmax, sigmoid, hyperbolic tangent, and dropout. The hybrid secret sharing enables PriFFT to apply our optimized FSS protocols while combining ASS protocols to support complex computation without extra communication. PriFFT reduces execution time and communication overhead in privacy-preserving fine-tuning up to 59.1% and 77.0% without accuracy drop compared to the existing secret sharing methods.

Author: A.Mallika; Christy, A. A.; Krishnamoorthy, P.; Priya, A.; Ebenezer, D. D.; Shroff, A.

Abstract Note: Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) systems require dynamical, safe, and competent control to address the dynamic industrial processes. Abstract Note: Personalized federated learning (PFL) is a practical solution to provide personalized services for Internet of Things (IoT) devices while protecting their privacy. Title: Privacy-Preserving Services for Internet of Medical Things: Architecture, Techniques, and Challenges
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Services Computing
Abstract Note: The Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) has attracted the attention of many scholars because of its revolutionary impact on healthcare services. This survey offers a comprehensive and novel investigation and classification of privacy and security issues in IoMT. We explore the issue from four distinct angles: privacy protection technologies, IoMT architecture, data type variations, and emerging technologies, with each section delving into more detailed analysis. Author: Shen, X.; Xu, C.; Zhu, L.; Liu, H.; Sun, L.; Sharif, K.
Title: Blockchain-Assisted Privacy-Preserving and Robust Federated Learning in Edge Computing
Publication Title: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
Abstract Note: Federated learning (FL) enables distributed clients to collaboratively train machine learning models without sharing raw data, making it well-suited for edge computing environments. However, deploying FL at the edge introduces critical challenges, including potential model poisoning by malicious clients or edge servers, increased privacy risks, and communication bottlenecks. To address these issues, we propose a two-layer blockchain-assisted FL framework that ensures privacy, robustness, and efficiency. In our design, each client uploads an encrypted local update to an edge server for privacy-preserving validation, while a lightweight, sparse upload strategy is adopted to reduce communication overhead. We design a two-layer defense strategy that employs the secure cosine similarity technique and a truth discovery algorithm to resist Byzantine attacks from both malicious clients and edge servers, while a consortium blockchain maintained by edge servers guarantees decentralized and tamper-resistant global model updates. Theoretical analysis and extensive experiments under both IID and non-IID data partitions demonstrate that the proposed scheme effectively defends against targeted and untargeted poisoning attacks and preserves the privacy of local model updates. It also substantially reduces communication overhead. These results indicate that our framework provides a practical and scalable solution for privacy-preserving and robust FL in edge environments.

Author: Hadi, A.; Mula, K.; Bacha, A.; Muktevi, S.; Gudipati, R. R.; Gutha, P.
Title: Zero-Knowledge Federated Learning for Privacy-Preserving Cyber Threat Detection
