Abstract Note: The growing nature and complexity of the cyber threats within the distributed digital infrastructures require collective intelligence without jeopardizing the privacy of data. Federated Learning (FL) is an up-and-coming model that holds potential in training models in a decentralized way; nonetheless, the existing FL models are susceptible to information leakage as a result of model updates and adversarial inference attacks. To overcome these shortcomings, this paper introduces a Zero-Knowledge Federated Learning (ZK-FL) system to detect cyber threats in a privacy-preserving way so that collaboration in the learning process can be secured without sensitive information about the intermediate models and without exposing sensitive data. In the suggested solution, the zero-knowledge proof (ZKP) mechanisms along with federated optimization are combined to make sure that the participating clients can prove the accuracy of their local model updates, revealing no data features. This cryptographic integrity check deters malicious model poisoning, gradient inversion and unauthorized inference of data, improving the confidence of heterogeneous and untrusted parties. Another approach used is a secure aggregation protocol which protects model parameters in the transmission process to guarantee end-to-end confidentiality and integrity. The framework is tested with actual datasets of cyber threat in a distributed environment and adversarial environment. Empirical studies show that the suggested ZK-FL model can be used to obtain a high detection accuracy and robustness on par with centralized learning, and substantially increase privacy guarantees and anti-inference attack. Furthermore, the communication and computation cost that is entailed by zero-knowledge verification is within manageable limits, and thus the solution is feasible to large-scale cyber defence systems. The suggested ZK-FL architecture provides a secure and trusted platform to cooperative cyber threat intelligence, which is a scalable service in privacy-sensitive environments like enterprise networks, critical infrastructures, and edge-cloud security systems.

Abstract Note: The use of Federated Learning (FL) in sensitive, multi-party settings has made it even more important to have trust, accountability and safe systems of governance have become increasingly critical in the context of Federated Learning (FL) being utilized in sensitive multi-party environments. Abstract Note: As global demand for efficient network services increases, the limitations of traditional terrestrial wireless networks are becoming more apparent. Author: K, N.; Sathya, S.
Title: FedChain-HyperVision: Trust-Aware Federated Blockchain Learning with Hypergraph-Guided Attention for Robust Rumor Detection
Publication Title: 2026 3rd International Conference on Electronic Circuits and Signaling Technologies (ICECST)
Abstract Note: Federated learning promises privacy-preserving multimodal rumor detection across distributed social-media clients, but two of its core claims are rarely tested end to end: that trust-based aggregation resists malicious clients, and that a hypergraph-structured encoder actually helps. This paper reports a from-scratch, fully instrumented reference implementation of FedChain-HyperVision, combining a hypergraph neural network (HGNN), a vision transformer (ViT), hypergraph-guided vision attention (HGVA) fusion, a blockchain-style validation ledger, and differential privacy, then subjects every claimed component to evaluation on real Twitter15, Twitter16, and Weibo data. Separately, an ablation study shows the hypergraph encoder degrades accuracy by roughly half on all three datasets, traced to batch-local k-nearest-neighbor graphs causing representation over-smoothing; this paper's contribution on that front is the evaluation itself, not a validated architectural benefit, and the finding should be read as a caution against the encoder's title role rather than an endorsement of it. Measured by the direction-agnostic leakage statistic| AUC-0.5| rather than signed AUC, differential privacy reduces apparent membership-inference leakage on Twitter15 and Twitter16, but increases it on Weibo; a formal \(\textbackslash{}boldsymbol{\textbackslash{}varepsilon}, \textbackslash{}boldsymbol{\textbackslash{}delta})\ accounting of the same mechanism, added in this revision using its actual clip-norm and noise-multiplier settings, shows the configured noise level currently yields an extremely large, practically meaningless privacy budget, so the empirical AUC reduction should not be read as evidence of a strong formal guarantee. A companion micro-benchmark shows the blockchain ledger's own compute and storage overhead is negligible relative to local training. Together these results argue for validating, rather than assuming, every architectural and defensive claim made in a federated multimodal pipeline.

Title: A Comprehensive Survey of Federated Learning: Privacy, Personalization, and Future Horizons
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Emerging Trends and Innovations in ICT (ICEI)
Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) is a decentralized machine learning method that enables collaborative model training on various devices or entities without the need to share raw data, thus addressing privacy, security, and regulatory hurdles imposed by industries care, finance and Internet of Things, etc. FL was initially conceived as a system for distributed training and later generalized by the FedAvg algorithm, it has become one of the core technologies of privacy, preserving AI. Research in this field can be roughly divided into five themes: optimization techniques, privacy, preserving strategies, data heterogeneity management, personalization approaches and adversarial attacks resistance. The major achievements are the algorithms for improved convergence in heterogeneous environments as well as the techniques for overcoming the problems caused by non, independent and non, identically distributed data. The publications now focus on real, world issues, methodological trade, offs, and problems such as communication overheads and attack robustness that remain unsolved. Popular research themes explore the integration of FL with blockchain, edge computing and quantum technologies to enhance security, scalability and efficiency.
Manual Tags: Federated learning; Privacy preservation; Non-IID data; Personalized federated learning

Author: Joshi, K.; Kaur, D. P.; Dewangan, G. S.; Nune, B.; Raja, C.; Nagpal, A.
Title: Secure and Privacy-Preserving Healthcare Data Management Using AI-Based Intrusion Detection Models
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Multidisciplinary Innovations For Smart & Sustainable Future (MISSF)
Abstract Note: The employment of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in healthcare data management gains clinical efficiency, yet it also increases the level of privacy and security risks. In this study, a new AI-powered intrusion detection model is proposed to support safe and privacy-sensitive management of healthcare data in distributed clouds. The suggested model integrates federated deep learning with difference privacy to demonstrate abnormal access patterns without revealing sensitive details of patients. However, in contrast with the traditional centralized intrusion detection systems, the architecture can leverage decentralized training on encrypted datasets, which ensures scalability and adherence to the healthcare regulations. Experimental assessment of benchmark medical data shows that it has detection accuracy of 98.3 % and a reduction in false alarm of 3.7 percent over that of the existing models. The result underscores the ability of the framework in realizing real-time threats detection with a sense of maintained confidentiality, integrity and regulatory complacency and sport trustworthy smart healthcare ecosystems.
Manual Tags: Differential privacy; Intrusion detection; Cloud computing; Privacy preservation; Federated deep learning; Healthcare data security; Secure data management

Author: Mathpati, S. S.; Chirputkar, A.
Title: Explainable AI and Federated Learning for Privacy-Preserving Loan Default Prediction in Cooperative Banking Networks
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE International Conference for Convergence in Computing Technology (I3CTCON)
Abstract Note: Co-operative banking networks in emerging economies, like India, have to perform the increasingly arduous task of manage loan defaults with ever increasing needs for data Privacy and demands for transparency in decision making. Centralized machine learning models have been widely used for The task of loan default prediction typically require data centralization that exposes sensitive customer information to data breaches, among other similar incidents, thus breaking laws. such as the DPDP Act 2023 of India. Further, complex models, are usually such that is based on deep neural networks. Not transparent, therefore able to undermine regulatory compliance. and may further erode stakeholder trust. This work proposes a robust framework that synergistically integrates Federated Few-shot learning with explainable AI to enable privacy preserving by: and interpretable loan default predictions within cooperative banking networks. In this work, a synthetically generated dataset of 30,000 instances is used, similar to the UCI Credit Card Default dataset, in emulating a federated setup across three cooperative banks with non IID data distributions. Here, the core model is a Random Forest classifier trained via FedAvg aggregation, augmented with SHAP for both global and local explanations. Extensive experiments show that the federated model achieves an accuracy of 81.98%, precision of 64.87%, recall of 44.89%, and F1-score of 52.84%, close to the centralized baseline of 82.34% accuracy, with no data sharing. The feature attribution analysis underlines repayment status as the most important predictor, namely PAY 0, which contributes as much as 25% to the default risk scores. Ablation studies confirm the efficacy of XAI in explaining model decisions, with SHAP values permitting counterfactual explanations at the level of individual predictions. Further assessments of adding differential privacy noise provide additional protection against inference attacks. The contribution of the proposed architecture will be to towards a decrease in NPA, improved regulatory compliance and ethics in AI deployments. Our approach links the strong privacy guarantees of FL with the transparency afforded by XAI and provides a scalable paradigm for cooperative banks; It would probably help lower the default rates by 5–10% with proactive interventions. Extensions of this work may be done Using Blockchain for Secure Aggregations and Temporal Dynamics in credit histories.

Author: Sultana, S.; Banu, W. A.
Title: Secure Federated Ensemble Intrusion Detection Framework with Smart Contract Validation for Online Banking Platforms
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Applied Intelligence Devices, Machine Learning, and Data Science (AIDML)
Abstract Note: The Online banking has become popular, but relaxation of security has caused issues. Security measures for online banking, such as privacy awareness and defense against sophisticated intrusion detection systems, must be improved to counter the growth of online banking. The Secure Federated Ensemble Intrusion Detection Framework with Smart Contract Validation is presented in this paper to address online banking security concerns. The framework leverages Lorentz Machine Learning (federated learning) and SMOTE to train models across all clients of a system to tackle class imbalance. To account for individual transaction privacy, Laplace noise is introduced to the framework and used within the context of differential privacy. A global prediction is made through the aggregation of numerous local predictions made after training an ensemble of CatBoost, XGBoost, and LightGBM. Further, a smart contract validation model with a threshold for high model accuracy is simulated. Performance metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1, and AUC score were used to evaluate the framework and achieved over 98% accuracy. SHAP is used for framework Explainability. This approach provides a strong tool for fraud detection in a secure decentralized finance ecosystem.

Author: Kumar, L.; Baghel, A. S.; Singh, R. B.
Title: Federated Reinforced Trust Platform: A Next-Generation Trust Model for Secure and Resource-Efficient Wireless Sensor Networks
Publication Title: 2026 3rd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
Abstract Note: Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) are prone to various internal and external attacks, and trust management plays a vital role in sound security and resource optimization. Current models have improved trust measures, optimization, machine learning, and blockchain for detection and prevention but lack adaptability, scalability, transparency, and computational expense. This paper introduces the Federated Reinforced Trust Platform (FRTP), which is a federated learning and deep reinforcement learning-enabled system, incorporating dynamic multifeature trust, adversarial machine learning, anomaly detection, and blockchain-secured trust auditing. Extensive comparative analysis and simulation scenarios show that FRTP outperforms in terms of malicious node detection accuracy, network lifetime, adaptability, and auditability.

Author: N, T. P.; Kumari, V. S.
Title: A Decentralized Security Architecture for Privacy-Aware Data Mining in Cloud Systems
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Signal, Systems, and Computing for Next-Gen Automation (ICSSCNA)
Abstract Note: Cloud computing has emerged as a leading platform used to store and process large scale data which have been generated by different sectors e.g. healthcare, finance and smart environments. Nevertheless, there are strong concerns of data privacy, security and trust in cloud systems when carrying out data mining tasks with regard to sensitive information being exchanged across distributed infrastructures. The conventional centralized security measures usually have drawbacks in safeguarding transparency, resistance to interference and dependable access control. As a way of dealing with these issues, this paper presents a decentralized security architecture that will facilitate privacy-sensitive data mining in cloud computing. The framework proposed combines the blockchain technology with secure access control and privacy-protective data processing methods that guarantee trustworthy and immutable data processing. Blockchain is applied in architecture to store an immutable record of transactions and to impose decentralized access control by smart contracts. Ensuring the safety of the data is done by encryption and secure preprocessing and then mining is done in the cloud environment. Inclusion of smart monitoring systems in the framework is also done to identify abnormal access patterns and to improve reliability in the system. The analysis of experiments proves that the suggested decentralized architecture is more effective in enhancing the privacy of data and transparency in access as well as system security, and yet the data mining performance is not impacted. The findings show that the framework has the potential to support secure and privacy-conscious data mining of large-scale cloud systems.
Manual Tags: Smart Contracts; Blockchain Security; Cloud Computing; Decentralized Architecture; Secure Data Processing; Data Privacy Protection; Privacy-Aware Data Mining

Author: Jerbi, W.; Mechti, S.; Sassi, S.; Chbeir, R.
Title: Secure Medical Diagnostics Through Federated Learning on the Blockchain
Publication Title: 2026 International Wireless Communications and Mobile Computing (IWCMC)
Abstract Note: Medical healthcare centers are increasingly adopting advanced technologies to manage the vast volumes of data necessary for AI-driven disease diagnosis. Traditional machine learning (ML) methods, however, often require centralized data processing, which poses significant privacy risks for patients' sensitive medical information. To overcome these challenges, collaborative data training through federated learning (FL) has gained momentum. In this paradigm, multiple hospitals—treated as decentralized nodes—collaboratively train and share encrypted models without exposing raw data, thereby reducing the risk of data breaches. This approach also promotes resource sharing between healthcare institutions of varying sizes and locations. This study presents a novel framework that integrates blockchain technology with federated learning to enhance both diagnostic accuracy and data security. The proposed system was trained, tested, and evaluated on a large-scale radiology dataset, achieving a test accuracy of 94.93%, a data throughput of 12,062 bytes/s, and a latency of 48.6225 ms. Moreover, the blockchain layer underwent rigorous empirical evaluation under major cyber-attack scenarios. With resilience scores consistently approaching 90% across three key attack vectors, the system exhibits strong robustness and considerable promise for real-world deployment in healthcare environments.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; federated learning; data sharing; cybersecurity; healthcare; Adversarial attacks

Author: Liu, Z.; Yang, H.; Shen, J.; Vijayakumar, P.; Arya, V.; Gupta, B. B.
Title: An Efficient and Threshold Private Set Intersection for Privacy-Enhanced Vertical Federated Learning in Consumer Systems
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Consumer Electronics
Abstract Note: The industrial consumer field integrates industrial production with financial consumption, aiming to focus on the entire process of the consumption system, with comprehensive data analysis conducted across multiple institutions. Vertical federated learning is a vital component for distributed collaborative data analysis. It allows parties to integrate sample features from all parties while maintaining privacy and conduct comprehensive model training. This paper focuses on vertical federated learning in the industrial consumer field and proposes a vertical federated learning framework for factory economic prediction. In this framework, a factory institution collaborates with multiple consumer institutions to perform vertical federated learning, train a predictive model, and determine whether a factory institution is operating normally. We design a privacy-preserving (t,n)-threshold private set intersection protocol to achieve sample alignment for this framework. This protocol aligns sample data from all parties while protecting their privacy. It also introduces a weighting mechanism to accommodate missing sample data for some non-critical parties. We implement the proposed vertical federated learning framework and conduct a comprehensive security analysis. Evaluation results demonstrate that our private sample alignment protocol performs well, and the predictive model derived from vertical federated learning is highly accurate and practical.
Manual Tags: privacy-preserving; vertical federated learning; consumer systems; Threshold private set intersection

Author: Nakayiza, H. L.; Ahakonye, L. A. C.; Kim, D.-S.; Lee, J. M.
Title: PureFL: Trust-Weighted Federated Learning With Noise-Resilient Homomorphic Encryption for Blockchain-Based IoV Networks
Publication Title: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
Abstract Note: Federated learning (FL) in the Internet of Vehicles (IoV) networks is challenged by privacy vulnerabilities, model poisoning attacks, and the limitations of centralized aggregation, which threaten security and scalability. While homomorphic encryption (HE) provides an additional layer of privacy, existing schemes often suffer from cumulative noise growth, resulting in degraded model accuracy and increased inference latency, critical factors for real-time vehicular safety applications. This article presents PureFL, a novel FL framework that combines adaptive Cheon-Kim-Kim-Song (CKKS) HE with a custom permissioned blockchain (PureChain), utilizing a proof of authority and association (PoA2) consensus mechanism. PureFL incorporates dynamic precision scaling to manage noise accumulation, ensuring computational efficiency without sacrificing privacy or accuracy. The framework also implements a trust-based aggregation mechanism based on cosine-similarity trust scoring, which dynamically weights client contributions according to historical reliability and anomaly detection, thereby enhancing resilience against model poisoning. Experimentation results on the CICIOV2024 and 5G-NIDD datasets demonstrate that PureFL achieves superior anomaly detection accuracy of 99.9%, reduces CKKS HE overhead via precision scaling, and the proposed PoA2 consensus outperforms other consensus mechanisms in terms of throughput and latency, making it suitable for real-time IoV operations.
Manual Tags: blockchain; federated learning (FL); privacy preservation; Anomaly detection; Cheon-Kim-Kim-Song (CKKS); homomorphic encryption (HE); Internet of Vehicles (IoV)

Author: Awan, K. A.; Uddin, M.; Althobaiti, M. M.; Alaidaros, H.; Alsalman, D.; Farouk, A.
Title: TUB-IoT: Quantum Trust-Based Big Data UAV Architecture for Security-Centric Internet of Things
Publication Title: IEEE Open Journal of the Communications Society
Abstract Note: UAV-assisted sensing in dense smart-city IoT deployments requires trust-aware coordination under post-quantum adversarial models, fluctuating node behavior, and high-rate heterogeneous telemetry. This study introduces a quantum resilience trust architecture that couples probabilistic trust dynamics with hybrid post-quantum cryptography for real-time UAV–IoT coordination. At the edge, UAVs act as mobile trust agents that compute QRNG-driven interaction states and behavior vectors, combining task fidelity, entropy, and interaction history into structured descriptors that parameterize local trust. These descriptors are transformed at the fog layer by a Quantum Probabilistic Trust Model, which encodes trust as density matrices with non-commutative evidence operators, enabling order-sensitive updates and interference between heterogeneous trust cues. A Secure Trust Flow Algorithm then maps trust-state gradients and control signals to tri-level admission decisions (allow, defer, block) and feeds reinforcement updates back into the trust dynamics. A hybrid cryptographic engine integrates Kyber-based key encapsulation and Dilithium signatures with conditionally activated QKD, producing trust-aware session keys, adaptive rekeying, and post-quantum-secure channel authentication. A cloud-level ledger records PQC-protected trust trajectories and synthesizes time-varying trust maps that guide application governance, including flow prioritization, anomaly isolation, and cooperative route reconfiguration. Simulation in the inD traffic dataset under multiple attack classes achieves 95.1% accuracy in trust classification, 2.33% false positive rate, 2.65s mean trust response delay and 451 ops/s throughput with 200 UAV nodes.
Manual Tags: Internet of Things; security; big data; unmanned aerial vehicles; smart cities; Quantum computing; trust management; context-aware trust management

Author: Huang, R.; Ren, J.
Title: Distributed Anomaly Detection and Protection Mechanism Integrating Blockchain and Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2026 9th International Symposium on Big Data and Applied Statistics (ISBDAS)
Abstract Note: Distributed systems such as industrial IoT, cyber-physical production lines, and edge clouds increasingly suffer from data silos, privacy leakage, weak generalization to unseen anomalies, and model tampering during collaborative analytics. This paper proposes a blockchain-enhanced federated learning (BC-FL) mechanism for distributed anomaly detection and protection. Without sharing raw data, each node trains a local anomaly model and uploads encrypted and signed updates. Smart contracts enforce format validation, rate limiting, and provenance logging, while an auditable aggregation pipeline securely iterates the global model. To strengthen robustness against unknown anomalies and adversarial participants, we combine adaptive thresholding with robust aggregation and a lightweight reputation mechanism, and accelerate response through parallel edge execution. A prototype evaluation shows that the proposed design improves detection robustness while preserving data privacy and providing tamper-evident model lifecycle management, which is suitable for IoT and industrial interconnection scenarios and can be extended to smart city and medical IoT deployments.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; federated learning; anomaly detection; intrusion detection; IoT security; secure aggregation; model integrity

Author: Ammal, S. G.; Sumathi, R.
Title: Privacy-Preserving Healthcare Data Science: A Review of Federated Learning Approaches
Publication Title: 2026 8th International Conference on Intelligent Sustainable Systems (ICISS)
Abstract Note: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare has revolutionized clinical diagnostics, patient monitoring and decision support. However, the widespread deployment of centralized AI systems remains constrained by growing concerns over data privacy, security risks and regulatory compliance. In this context, federated learning (FL) has emerged as a promising solution that enables decentralized model training across multiple institutions without sharing sensitive patient data. This review critically analyzes recent studies that employ FL in diverse healthcare domains, categorizing them into three major groups: encryption and secure aggregation-based methods, blockchain-enhanced frameworks and standard or lightweight FL architectures. The studies employ a wide range of federated mechanisms, such as FedAvg, FedProx, PerFedAvg and split learning, combined with privacy-preserving strategies including homomorphic encryption (HE), differential privacy (DP) and blockchain protocols. These frameworks demonstrate comparable performance and regulatory alignment while addressing key challenges in collaborative model development. Nonetheless, limitations such as computational overhead, synchronization delays and scalability issues persist. By synthesizing methodological innovations and practical constraints, this review offers a comprehensive perspective on the current landscape of privacy-preserving FL in healthcare and provides insights for future research and clinical translation.
Manual Tags: Federated Learning; Healthcare Data Security; Privacy-Preserving AI; Medical Data Sharing; Clinical AI Systems

Author: Babar, M.; Khan, Z.; Kaleem, S.; Qureshi, B.; Boulila, W.
Title: TAWB-SFL: Trust-Aware Blockchain-Orchestrated Split Federated Learning for Intrusion Detection in 6G Healthcare IoT
Publication Title: IEEE Open Journal of the Communications Society
Abstract Note: The ongoing shift toward 6G-enabled healthcare IoT is making privacy-preserving collaborative intelligence a practical requirement rather than a research luxury. Federated Learning (FL) is a natural fit for this setting, yet it remains vulnerable when untrusted devices participate in training, as attackers can inject poisoned updates, distort aggregation, or increase the risk of sensitive information leakage. In this paper, we present TAWB-SFL, a trust-aware framework that combines Split Federated Learning (SFL), blockchain, and edge intelligence to build a secure intrusion detection pipeline for healthcare IoT. The proposed design splits the deep model across the device and edge: lightweight CNN layers on IoT nodes extract spatial patterns from patient-related data, while an edge-side BiLSTM models temporal behavior to identify attacks. SFL keeps raw data on devices, blockchain smart contracts handle device registration/authentication and provide auditable logging of update transactions, and trust scores are used to weight client contributions during aggregation. To support frequent and timely update commitments, we further adopt the TAWB-SFL consensus design to reduce latency and improve scalability. Experimental results on the ToN-IoT and IoT-Healthcare datasets achieve 99.9% detection accuracy with a consensus time of 250 ms, indicating that the proposed approach can deliver accurate threat detection while enabling low-latency, accountable model updates in 6G healthcare IoT environments.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; security; 6G-based consumer electronics; decentralized trust management; split federated learning

Author: Ilangovan, K.; C, D.; Valluri, J. Y.; Chitradevi, S.
Title: Blockchain-Enabled Secure Supply Chain Finance Using Federated Learning and Smart Contract-Based Trust Verification
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
Abstract Note: Federated learning based on blockchain-powered smart contracts transforms supply chain finance, with decentralized risk analysis, data privacy, and automatic transaction approval. The presented framework offers the operations of five strategic steps including data preprocessing, federated model training, risk forecasting, smart contract deployment, and system integration. In Federated Averaging (FedAvg), supply chain actors train models with their local information not being disclosed globally and use it to tweak global models, which in turn are trained by them. Blockchain provides verifiability which is not tamperable resulting into fraud and financial transparency. The classification of risks based on the patterns of the transactions and the operational parameters applies safe decision making in the decentralized networks. The platform enhances compliance, efficiency, and trust and provides an affordable system of autonomous financial validation at scale. The metrics like Transaction Throughput, Latency, Auditability Score, Trust Score demonstrate the performance of the framework in the real-life environment of the supply chain finance.

Author: Reguieg, H.; Sabir, E.; Kamili, M. E.
Title: Privacy and Security in Knowledge Distillation for Federated Learning: A Survey
Publication Title: IEEE Access
Abstract Note: Knowledge distillation (KD) is increasingly used in federated learning (FL) because it enables clients to exchange predictions, features, prototypes, or synthetic knowledge rather than full model parameters. This change can reduce communication and support heterogeneous models, but it also changes the privacy and security threat surface rather than eliminating it. This survey examines KD-based FL through a privacy and security lens. We distinguish formal differential-privacy guarantees, protocol-level cryptographic mechanisms, structural reductions of the attack surface, and empirical attack-specific defenses, and we map these notions to transfer direction, shared representation, and data-availability assumptions. We review attacks against released distilled knowledge, privacy-preserving distillation mechanisms, secure aggregation and encrypted-domain approaches, adversarial defenses, application domains, and open challenges for formal assurance and standardized benchmarking. The goal is to provide a precise framework for evaluating what KD-FL methods actually guarantee and what they only make harder for an adversary.
Manual Tags: federated learning; security; privacy; secure aggregation; distributed learning; knowledge distillation; differential privacy; Backdoor attacks; membership inference

Author: Aruna, C.; Merugu, P.; Anitha, M. R.; Gupta, J. N.; Sreedhar, V.; R, R. E.
Title: Blockchain-Based Secure Data Sharing Framework for Sustainable Healthcare Systems
Publication Title: 2026 1st International Conference on Sustainable Solutions in Engineering Technologies and Earth Science (ICSSETES)
Abstract Note: One of the challenges that hinder secure data sharing in healthcare systems is lack of security regarding privacy, data breaches, and interoperability between medical systems. Centralized data systems can be subject to security threats and are not transparent and trustworthy for users. This impacts on patient data management and delivery of health care. This paper introduces a Blockchain-Based Secure Data Sharing Framework (BBSDSF) using IoT and artificial intelligence for decentralized, transparent and secure healthcare data sharing. The framework leverages smart contracts, encryption techniques, and distributed ledger technology to ensure proper data access, communication security, and data integrity and transparency. The proposed system achieves accuracy of 96.8% for secure data access and the data retrieval time is improved by 35% along with risk reduction of data breach 40% as compared to the existing system. It also provides low latency and scalability in real-time healthcare situations. The proposed system helps by offering a secure, efficient, and transparent framework for sustainable healthcare systems that allows secure data sharing, enhances patient health outcomes and increases trust between healthcare providers.

Author: Singh, A.; Raman, M.; Singh, N.
Title: Blockchain-Integrated Framework for Security Over IoT Network
Publication Title: 2026 13th International Conference on Computing for Sustainable Global Development (INDIACom)
Abstract Note: In the current age of the intensive growth of the IoT Network, there are severe issues of insecurity, such as, unauthorized access, tampering of data, denial-of-service attacks, and a single-point failure. The current paper is a review article on Blockchain-Integrated IoT framework to provide data integrity, authentication and trust management using decentralized architecture and lightweight cryptography. The IoT framework proposed is the Blockchain-Integrated IoT framework, which incorporates AES-128 encryption, SHA-256 hashing and an energy-efficient lightweight consensus system to provide secure and scalable communication between resource-constrained IoT devices. This framework was tested by simulating over a 500 device IoT setup and used performance metrics including latency, throughput, packet delivery ratio, energy and security breach detection rate. The findings indicate that, the level of security has greatly improved up to 40 percent, network efficiency has been increased by about 20 percent, and blockchain overhead has been reduced to less than 5 percent as compared to traditional IoT systems. The results confirm the practical and scalable solution based on blockchain and lightweight cryptography to secure IoT ecosystems is feasible.

Author: Deng, R.; Wang, J.; Li, Q.; Li, J.; Liu, P.; Li, X.
Title: FedHeGA: A Federated Learning Framework for Enhanced Node Classification on Heterogeneous Graphs
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Computational Social Systems
Abstract Note: Heterogeneous graph neural networks (HGNNs) have proven effective at capturing complex relationships in graphs with diverse node and edge types. However, centralized training in HGNNs raises privacy concerns, as sensitive data can be exposed during model training. This risk is further exacerbated when the data is distributed across multiple clients. Federated learning (FL) offers a potential solution by enabling collaborative training without sharing local data. However, existing FL methods for heterogeneous graphs fail to effectively address challenges such as data imbalance and the handling of private edge types. Moreover, existing methods designed for homogeneous graphs are ineffective at addressing the data sparsity issue in heterogeneous graphs. In this article, we propose FedHeGA, a FL framework for heterogeneous graphs that enhances node classification performance while preserving privacy. We tackle data imbalance by integrating heterogeneous graph reconstruction with differential autoencoders to generate semantically coherent node features, improving feature propagation in sparse or imbalanced data. To preserve privacy, we propose a parameter decomposition mechanism that uploads only edge-type-independent global parameters, protecting sensitive local data. Additionally, we address dataset skewness by employing a contrastive learning strategy to align local and global model parameters, which enhances convergence. Experimental results demonstrate that FedHeGA significantly outperforms existing methods on node classification benchmarks, offering an effective solution for federated heterogeneous graph learning.
Manual Tags: federated learning (FL); Data imbalance; heterogeneous graph neural networks (HGNNs); node classification

Author: Al-Balasmeh, H.
Title: Federated Learning and Blockchain for Decentralized Cyber Threat Intelligence Sharing
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Blockchain, and Internet of Things (AIBThings)
Abstract Note: Cyber-threat-intelligence (CTI) sharing can improve detection of distributed attacks, but central collection exposes sensitive telemetry and creates governance risk. This paper specifies a blockchain-coordinated federated-learning (B-FL) framework in which organizations retain raw logs, train locally, commit signed update hashes to a permissioned ledger, and admit updates through bounded anomaly and reputation checks before robust aggregation. The framework makes the threat model, metrics, weighting rule, experimental protocol, and limitations explicit and contrasts the design with Byzantine-robust aggregation. In the reported simulation, B-FL reached 98.4% accuracy and 98.0% F1 while preserving an auditable contribution trail. These values are point estimates from a synthetic, simulation-only benchmark; they do not establish real-world superiority. The main contribution is an auditable governance layer that can wrap robust aggregation, not a claim that blockchain replaces poisoning defenses.
Manual Tags: blockchain; federated learning; auditability; CTI; poisoning resilience

Author: Singh, G.; Bhardwaj, K.; Kaur, G.; Pandey, C.; Sharma, B.; Kaur, B. P.
Title: Smart and Decentralized Security: AI and Blockchain Have a Synergistic to Future IoT
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE International Conference for Convergence in Computing Technology (I3CTCON)
Abstract Note: The convergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI), blockchain, and the Internet of Things (IoT) promises a robust, decentralized security paradigm that addresses pressing concerns over data integrity, authentication, privacy. This paper first surveys Security Challenges in AI, IoT, and Blockchain, highlighting the vulnerabilities that arise from distributed sensor networks, model drift, and ledger tampering, then explore AI Technologies in IoT Cybersecurity, detailing anomaly detection, predictive maintenance, and autonomous threat mitigation, while underscoring the need for transparent, explainable models. Next, the role of Blockchain in IoT Security is examined: immutable ledgers, smart contracts, and consensus protocols enhance data integrity and provide auditable audit trails, yet they introduce latency and scalability concerns. In final section discusses challenges and limitations, including computational overhead, energy consumption, regulatory compliance, and the difficulty of integrating heterogeneous devices. By synthesizing these insights, the study demonstrates that a synergistic combination of AI and blockchain can create a self-healing, trust-based IoT ecosystem, but achieving this vision requires overcoming technical, economic, and policy barriers.

Author: Jebamoni, T.; Agoramoorthy, M.
Title: A Sustainable Blockchain-Based Security Optimization Model for Resilient Smart Grid Energy Information Systems
Publication Title: 2026 7th International Conference on Smart Electronics and Communication (ICOSEC)
Abstract Note: Smart grid energy information systems (EIS) handle huge quantities of operational information that is sensitive, such as real-time generation data, consumption data, pricing data, and indicators of grid stability. The consequences of data integrity, availability and confidentiality breaches and failures in the context of cyberattacks can be widespread and span financial losses, privacy breaches and cascading failures. Traditional security systems, like firewalls, intrusion detection systems and central authentication systems, have high false-positive rates and are not adaptable; they are also prone to single points of failure. While blockchain technology provides decentralized and tamper-proof security, current blockchain-based solutions are energy-intensive, do not scale well, and have yet to be optimized for smart grid operations. To overcome these disadvantages, a Sustainable Blockchain-Based Security Optimization Model (SBSO-SG) for resilient smart grid energy information systems is proposed here. The framework has three components: an energy-efficient proof-of-authority and reputation-based consensus mechanism; a deep reinforcement learning agent to optimize security policies adaptively (such as threshold changes, anomaly detection rules); and a lightweight data integrity verification module based on a Merkle tree hashing method. A threat intelligence sharing mechanism allows coordinated defense at each substation without revealing any grid topology details. Using real-world attack data from 9,800 smart grid nodes over 24 months, experimental results show reduction in security incidents by 67.43%, false positive reduction by 72.58%, reduction in energy consumption by 94.28% compared to the PoW blockchain, transaction throughput of 1850 tps, and attack resilience of 96.37% in three smart grid scenarios: transmission substations, distribution feeders, and microgrid clusters. The proposed framework outperforms the state-of-the-art IDS, proof-of-work blockchain, and non-optimized security approaches in terms of detection accuracy, energy efficiency, and adaptive resilience in the next-generation smart grid cybersecurity.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; Smart Grid Security; Cyber-Physical Systems; Deep Reinforcement Learning; Threat Intelligence; Energy Information Systems; Proof-of-Authority; Resilient Optimization

Author: Zhang, X.; Lu, W.; Chen, H.; Lin, Y.; Zou, Y.
Title: A Secure and Efficient Data Sharing Mechanism for Trusted Data Spaces Based on Federated Learning and Blockchain
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Big Data Science and Engineering (ICBDSE)
Abstract Note: In cross-organization data circulation, data providers usually face a conflict between data value release and data security protection. Direct data sharing may expose private information, while isolated local analysis limits the use value of distributed data. Trusted data spaces provide a controlled environment for data sharing, but practical applications still require mechanisms that can support privacy protection, process traceability, and acceptable circulation efficiency. To address this problem, this paper proposes a secure and efficient data sharing mechanism based on federated learning and blockchain. In the proposed mechanism, each participant keeps raw data in the local domain and joins collaborative model training through federated learning. Blockchain is used to record data registration, access authorization, model update evidence, model version information, and service invocation logs. Secure aggregation and differential privacy are further introduced to reduce the risk of sensitive information leakage from model parameters. A cross-institutional financial risk control scenario is used to evaluate the mechanism. Experimental results show that the proposed method improves model performance compared with local training, avoids direct raw data collection compared with centralized learning, and provides better traceability than conventional federated learning. The results indicate that the proposed mechanism can support secure, traceable, and efficient data sharing in trusted data spaces.
Manual Tags: blockchain; federated learning; data sharing; secure aggregation; privacy computing; data circulation; trusted data space

Author: Yu, X.; Shen, M.; Li, Q.; Dong, J.; Tang, X.; Wang, G.; Xu, K.; Zhu, L.
Title: Ripple: Private Collaborative Learning Against Model Poisoning via Zero-Knowledge Proofs for Non-Linear Functions
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing
Abstract Note: Private collaborative learning allows a model owner to train neural networks using data from distributed data owners, while preserving both data and model privacy. Recent frameworks achieve this by leveraging secure multiparty computation (MPC) to enable private training across multiple parties. However, existing approaches assume semi-honest data owners and fail to defend against model poisoning attacks, where malicious data owners can inject forged updates to degrade model performance. In this paper, we propose \textbackslash{}mathsf{Ripple}\Ripple, a private collaborative learning framework that defends against model poisoning attacks via zero-knowledge proofs for non-linear functions. We reduce multi-party collaborative learning to a two-party computation paradigm between the model owner and each data owner. To ensure both the verifiability and privacy of inputs to non-linear functions, we design secure protocols that integrate removable noise mechanisms with Paillier-based zero-knowledge proofs. These protocols allow the model owner to verify the correctness of data owners’ computations without gaining access to their private inputs. Our theoretical analysis provides the security guarantees of {\textbackslash{}mathsf{Ripple}}\Ripple, and empirical evaluations demonstrate its ability to defend against model poisoning attacks. Specifically, under the Min-Max attack with non-IID data, existing methods suffer from accuracy degradation of up to 59%, whereas \textbackslash{}mathsf{Ripple}\Ripple consistently limits the degradation to within 4%. Moreover, the accuracy of the model is not affected by the data distribution or the proportion of malicious data owners.

Title: Privacy-Preserving for Low-Altitude Networks With Blockchain and Certificateless Undeniable Signature

Abstract Note: The rapid growth of UAV-enabled low-altitude networks (LANs) increases the demand for secure data sharing to support mission-critical applications, yet existing solutions struggle with LANs dynamics, quantum vulnerabilities of traditional cryptography, and unbalanced accountability-privacy. Abstract Note: Federated learning (FL) allows training of machine learning (ML) models across distributed data sources without moving private information. Blockchain offers a decentralized and tamper-resistant ledger that records all model updates in a transparent and verifiable manner. Author: Zuo, X.; Wang, M.; Zhu, T.; Zhang, L.; Ye, D.; Yu, S.; Zhou, W.

Author: Shetty, H.; Shetty, M. P.; D, P. S.; Rahman, H.; U, H.; Shetty, S. B.
Title: Blockchain-Based Edge Computing for Low-Latency Federated Learning: Architectures, Advances, and Open Challenges
Publication Title: 2026 2nd International Conference on Distributed Systems, Computer Networks and Cybersecurity (ICDSCNC)
Abstract Note: Federated learning (FL) enables privacy-preserving distributed training at the network edge, but conventional FL retains a trusted aggregator that is a single point of failure and an attack surface for model poisoning. A distributed ledger removes that assumption at the cost of consensus latency, and that tension decides whether blockchain-secured FL can meet 5G/6G deadlines. This paper develops an analytical treatment of that tension over a corpus of 37 studies published between 2017 and 2024, drawn from a 2017-2025 search window under an explicitly stated selection protocol. The contributions are an operational, testable definition of low latency; a taxonomy grounded in three binary criteria with a decision procedure that makes class membership reproducible; a four-component latency decomposition extended with closed-form component models and a normalized blockchain-overhead ratio, placing heterogeneously reported results on one comparable dimension; a model-based evaluation and sensitivity analysis over four canonical design patterns; and a mechanism-level separation of privacy techniques with individually attributed costs. The evaluation shows committee-based permissioned designs holding the overhead ratio below 0.02 while public proof-of-work exceeds 0.99, and predicts that BFT-style full-replica consensus stays sub-dominant only up to roughly 120-400 validators, a bound that tightens as radio links improve. Millisecond-class URLLC deadlines remain unreachable with consensus on the critical path in every framework examined.

Author: Rashid, M. M.; Uddin, M. P.; Xiang, Y.; Sood, K.; Zhang, Y.; Gao, L.
Title: TAFL: Trust-Aware Federated Learning for Anomalous Client Detection, Isolation, and Recovery
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security
Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) systems remain vulnerable to anomalous clients, including unreliable participants and malicious adversaries. Such clients can manipulate updates, poison data, exhibit non-IID drift, or participate intermittently, degrading model integrity, convergence, and trust. To address this, we propose Trust-Aware Federated Learning (TAFL), a unified framework for anomalous-client detection, probationary isolation, and controlled reintegration. TAFL combines Subjective Logic (SL) and Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) to provide uncertainty-aware trust estimation and peer-informed stabilization under dynamic participation. Targeting adaptive adversaries under bounded compromise capabilities, TAFL applies multi-signal consistency screening, including behavioral consistency and attribution drift, to detect subtle deviations beyond obvious outliers. Low-trust clients enter probationary isolation and are reintegrated only after sustained behavioral recovery. To promote fairness and deter malicious participation, TAFL enforces trust- and quality-aligned incentives with auditable smart-contract enforcement and provides theoretical analysis supporting convergence, trust recovery, and bounded adversarial influence. Experiments on MNIST and CIFAR10 show 2–4% higher anomalous-client detection and 20–25% lower convergence latency under 10–30% anomalous-client ratios. FEMNIST results further confirm robustness under stronger user-level heterogeneity, while stress tests on CIFAR10 show 94.6–97.1% mean detection and reduce semantic-backdoor attack success rate (ASR) to 2.9%.

Author: Magdum, S.; Patil, S.; Raut, A.
Title: Trust and Accountability in Federated Healthcare AI: A Blockchain-Governed Systematic Review
Publication Title: 2026 10th International Conference on Computing, Communication, Control & Automation (ICCUBEA)
Abstract Note: Although federated learning finds wide application in healthcare, the development of effective governance frameworks that incorporate strong privacy protections and regulatory compliance remains behind schedule, especially for sensitive areas like mental health. In this systematic review, we analyze blockchain-enabled governance in healthcare federated learning, paying particular attention to consent management, auditability, privacy budget monitoring, and regulatory compliance. Following the PRISMA 2020 methodology, we performed a search of seven bibliographic databases for peer-reviewed literature published between January 2020 and March 2026, identifying 3,847 sources, of which 67 papers were included. We find significant heterogeneity in governance solutions: on-chain privacy budget tracking is available in only 23%, dynamic consent with revocation in 31%, and security analysis in 42%. Ethereum dominates the implementation landscape, and mental health applications are underutilized despite increased privacy considerations. Performance overheads are large, with the median latency increase of 340% compared to conventional federated learning. Moreover, we provide an industry-ready implementation of an Ethereum-based governance framework for mental health depression detection, providing efficient consent validation and audit trail generation, and protecting user privacy without sacrificing model accuracy.

Title: B-DMTFL: A Practical and Efficient Framework of Dynamic Multi-Tier Federated Learning Based on Blockchain

Abstract Note: The emergence of federated learning as a novel distributed machine learning paradigm has found widespread applications in the field of data security. Author: Vijayalakshmi, S. C.; Vardhan, C. Mukesh Mun; Harshith, K. K.
Title: Privacy Enhanced PQBFL for Healthcare Applications
Publication Title: 2026 7th International Conference on Inventive Research in Computing Applications (ICIRCA)
Abstract Note: The idea of Federated Learning (FL) allows training models in collaboration between multiple institutions and keeps sensitive information local, which makes it especially applicable to privacy-sensitive areas of activity, including healthcare. Nevertheless, traditional FL systems have a number of issues such as insecure communication between models, the absence of transparent audit processes and mechanisms, susceptibility to bad actors, and using classical cryptographic algorithms which might be compromised in the age of quantum computation. Author: Prathapchandran, K.; Prasath, S. T.; Radhika, K.; Devi, K. N.; Saravanan, T.; Sathya, P.

Abstract Note: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSN) consist of densely deployed sensor nodes that collaboratively collect, process, and exchange data in dynamic and resource-constrained environments. Author: Khoder, R.; Samrouth, K.; Prasad, P.; Ali, S. A.; Bakir, N.

Abstract Note: Deep learning algorithms typically require access to large volumes of raw data. However, in the medical field, such data cannot be shared due to privacy constraints. Author: Melhem, A.; Aleroud, A.; Al-Mamun, A.; Ibrahem, M. I.
Title: Clustered Federated Learning for Healthcare Analytics: A Dual Blockchain-Functional Encryption Method for Fortified Aggregation

Abstract Note: The use of healthcare data for collaborative machine learning training amplifies the demand for strong privacy and security protection. To overcome these limitations, we propose C2SecFL, a cross-clustered secure FL framework that combines adaptive, model-aware clustering with an inner-product functional encryption (IPFE) scheme enabling encrypted aggregation without a key distribution center (KDC). Under adversarial settings with compromised participants, C2SecFL reduces the average attack success rate (ASR) by about 80% relative to a FedAvg baseline. Our extensive experiments on a heart attack dataset demonstrate that C2SecFL provides a practical, auditable, and resilient approach to secure healthcare FL.

Author: Ala’anzy, M. A.; Dumankyzy, A.; Saeed, N.
Title: Privacy Leakage in Blockchain-Based Healthcare Systems: A Layered Taxonomy and Systematic Review
Publication Title: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
Abstract Note: Blockchain technology has emerged as a compelling architecture for electronic health record (EHR) management, offering decentralization, immutability, and cryptographic auditability to address longstanding vulnerabilities in centralized healthcare data systems. Yet these same architectural properties introduce privacy leakage risks that existing surveys have not systematically examined: transparency enables transaction pattern analysis and patient reidentification; immutability conflicts with regulatory erasure obligations; and consensus operations expose institutional identities. This systematic review, following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines and analyzing 47 peer-reviewed original articles published between 2023 and 2026, develops what is, to the best of our knowledge, one of the first layered taxonomies of privacy leakage risks in blockchain-based healthcare systems, organized across the data, network, consensus, and application layers. The taxonomy maps 15 distinct attack vectors to their architectural origins and available countermeasures. Findings reveal that advanced techniques, including attribute-based encryption (ABE) with policy hiding, post-quantum lattice-based signatures, zero-knowledge proofs, and federated learning (FL) with differential privacy, provide significant but incomplete protection; critical vulnerabilities persist in metadata handling, peer-to-peer communication patterns, and consensus operations. Four concrete research priorities are identified: privacy-aware consensus protocols, standardized reidentification risk metrics, lightweight post-quantum primitives for resource-constrained IoT medical devices, and regulatory-compliant data erasure mechanisms compatible with General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA).

Author: Ma, X.; Fang, F.; Liu, T.; Wang, X.
Title: Dynamic Authentication and Granularized Authorization With a Cross-Domain Zero Trust Architecture in Large-Scale IoT Networks
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering
Abstract Note: With the increasing number of connected devices and complex networks involved, current domain-specific authentication mechanisms become inadequate for the dynamic access demands of large-scale Internet of Things (IoT) systems. However, they face new challenges including increased authentication latency, non-transferable trust, and excessive authorization computational overhead. To address these issues, in this paper, we propose Dynamic Authentication and Granularized Authorization (DAGA), a cross-domain Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA)-based framework that enables efficient, adaptive, and scalable authentication and authorization for large-scale IoT systems. At the same time, DAGA employs multi-level and cached fast authorization to achieve adaptive granularized access control, enhancing the accuracy and efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate that DAGA achieves notable reductions in communication and computation overhead compared to ZTA, blockchain-based, and lightweight mechanisms, significantly reducing authentication latency. Title: Privacy-Preserving Learning Approaches in 6G Networks: Benefits and Challenges

Author: Kavinda, L. H. D.; Wickramasinghe, B. M. G. S. T. S. K.
Title: A Blockchain-Enabled Federated Learning Framework for Secure and Interoperable Electronic Health Records in Sri Lanka

Abstract Note: Sri Lanka's public healthcare system has achieved strong population health outcomes despite operating under constrained resources; however, it continues to face persistent challenges related to fragmented health information systems, limited interoperability, and increasing concerns over patient data privacy. Existing digital initiatives such as the Hospital Health Information Management System (HHIMS) have improved operational efficiency within individual hospitals, yet the absence of secure inter-hospital data sharing mechanisms has resulted in isolated data silos, repeated diagnostic procedures, and delayed clinical decision-making. Simultaneously, the enforcement of the Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA) No. 9 of 2022 has introduced strict regulatory requirements that further complicate centralized health data aggregation for analytics and disease surveillance. This study presents a structured review and a conceptual framework for a secure, interoperable Electronic Health Record (EHR) ecosystem tailored to the Sri Lankan healthcare context. The proposed framework integrates a consortium blockchain platform with federated learning-based artificial intelligence to address trust, privacy, and scalability challenges. Blockchain technology is employed to establish an immutable audit trail for patient consent management, access control, and crossinstitutional trust, while off-chain encrypted storage ensures scalability and compliance with data minimization principles. The study synthesizes findings from prior literature, national digital health policies, and a stakeholder survey involving healthcare professionals and patients. Based on this synthesis, a three-layer conceptual model comprising trust, storage, and intelligence layers is proposed. Author: Tian, L.; Lin, F.; Gan, J.; Qi, J.; Jia, R.; Zheng, Z.; Li, M.; Shen, X.

Abstract Note: The Internet of Vehicles (IoV) has experienced rapid growth, generating extensive data that can be leveraged for intelligentapplications. Federated learning provides a privacy-preserving approach to utilize this data but faces challenges in performing multi-task learning and ensuring security. To address these issues, we propose a secure Federated Learning framework with Sharded Blockchain (FLSB), where the blockchain design aligns with FL requirements to enhance security, robustness, and scalability. FLSB partitions the blockchain into sharded chains to support parallel FL tasks, while a main chain governs task management and security enforcement. To prevent malicious behaviors such as creating fake identities or disrupting consensus, we develop the Proof of List Update (PoLU) consensus on the main chain. For secure FL, we design a committee-based adaptive weighted aggregation algorithm, whcih dynamically adjusts the model weights during aggregation to defend against poisoning attacks. In addition, we introduce the Proof of Task Participation (PoTP) consensus on sharded chains to ensure trustworthy model aggregation and defend against adversarial manipulations. Author: Kubba, A.; Sindhu, N. S.
Title: Blockchain and Data Mining: A Comprehensive Survey of Integration Frameworks, Applications, and Future Directions

Abstract Note: The combination of blockchain applications with data mining is one of the most profound trends existing in distributed computing today. In its turn, data mining offers some potent algorithms and statistical methods of retrieving useful patterns, relationships, and knowledge out of huge-sized data volumes. The following paper is an overview of the interaction and reinforcement of the two areas as well as their co-evolution. We thoroughly review the fundamental principles of both technologies, discuss their architectures of integration in three main dimensions including mining blockchain data, blockchain enhanced mining pipelines, and federated collaborative learning and evaluate their use in practice in the areas of healthcare, financial fraud detection, and supply chain management. We also explore such burning issues as scalability bottlenecks, privacy paradox that transparent ledgers represent, data heterogeneity across blockchain platforms, and smart contract vulnerabilities. A systematic overview of the future research directions such as the use of a graph neural network to analyze transactions, privacy-preserving computation, and cross-chain analytics are offered. Author: Ramasamy, A.; Lakshminarayanan, A. R.; Krishanmoorthy, M.; Rohith, M.

Abstract Note: Internet of Things (IoT) has been increased faster by the rapid development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the emergence of the next-generation communication technologies. Author: Ghanta, S.; Pradhan, A. K.; Boyapati, P.; Biswas, S.; Mohanty, S. P.
Title: Security and Verifiability in Federated Learning: A Zero-Knowledge Reputation-Based Blockchain Framework
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering
Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative training without centralizing sensitive data but faces challenges, including client authenticity, verifiable training participation, and secure aggregation. To overcome these challenges, we propose a novel framework, Zero-Knowledge Reputation-aware Blockchain Federated Learning (ZK-RBFL), which integrates blockchain, FL, Homomorphic Encryption (HE), and zero-knowledge proofs (ZKP). In the proposed ZK-RBFL framework, initially the clients undergo lightweight token-based authentication and then generate ZKP to provide cryptographic evidence of honest local training participation and reported inference accuracy before contributing their model updates. The model updates are encrypted using the CKKS HE mechanism to prevent any potential model inversion attacks. These encrypted model updates are stored on IPFS, with their corresponding CIDs recorded on the blockchain to ensure immutability. Further, ZK-RBFL enables mutual client verification of ZKPs to reduce server bottlenecks and enhance accountability. To ensure fairness and robustness in a distributed environment, we introduce a democratic blockchain consensus mechanism named Proof of Reputation-Weighted Voting (PoRWV) for block acceptance. Once consensus is reached, the encrypted model updates are aggregated using reputation-weighted averaging. We demonstrate the effectiveness of ZK-RBFL for brain tumor classification using a ZKP-compatible LeNet model for proof generation. Despite model simplicity, the global model achieves 94.22% accuracy. In addition, experiments with malicious clients and formal Scyther security analysis demonstrate that ZK-RBFL ensures both security and performance.

Author: Jyothi, V.; Divya, S.; Rajeswari, R.; Reddy, A. L. S.; VenkataRamana, J.

Author: Guan, Z.; Song, Y.; Li, R.; Ouyang, X.; Sun, S.; Qu, D.
Title: Trust Model and Privacy Protection in Edge Computing Environment
Publication Title: Intelligent and Converged Networks
Abstract Note: With the rapid increase in the number of terminals accessing Internet and the corresponding generated data, edge computing decreases the data sent to cloud center and reduces the pressure to bandwidth by processing data at the “edge” of network, either by the device or a local server. Meanwhile, the continuous evolution of Internet applications makes the content-centric mode be the trend of future Internet. Although the “content-centric” mode and innetwork caching make content-centric model more appropriate for solving the issues of resource discovery, compute reuse, and mobility management than the current IP address centric mode, some important security and privacy problems are still needed to be solved. Therefore, a hierarchical generalized trust model and corresponding privacy protection strategy are proposed for the edge computing environment. In the trust model, the direct trust between nodes for different interaction relationships within the intra-layers and across different layers are calculated, the indirect trust of the non-direct interaction node is obtained by the recommendation trust from the direct interaction nodes, and then the comprehensive trust is acquired by combining direct trust and indirect trust. Based on the proposed trust model, privacy is protected by encrypting transmission content between trusted interaction nodes. A symmetric encryption algorithm is applied between the interaction nodes in the intra-layer. For both of interaction nodes in cloud/edge layers, the key length is set based on their environment trust. Meanwhile, for terminals, the key length is set based on their environment trust and available resource. An asymmetric encryption is applied between the inter-layer interaction nodes. For an interaction from one node in higher layer to the other in lower layer, the key is calculated based on the environment trust of the node in lower layer and the similarity of the request content from nodes in lower layer. For the opposite interaction, the key is calculated based on the environment trust of the node in higher layer and the available resource of the node in lower layer. While the consideration of environment trust improves the interaction security and helps prevent privacy leakage, the consideration of available resource adjusts the key length adaptively, which reduces overhead and improves calculation efficiency. Experimental results show that the trust model has superior performance, in terms of interaction success rate, accuracy rate, recall rate, etc., than other trust models and the privacy protection policy has less overhead than fixed key length settings.

An AI-Extended Blockchain Framework that combines Federated Learning, Transformer-based deep learning, SHAP-based Explainable AI, and Hyperledger Fabric permissioned blockchain to build predictive financial analytics. The federated learning engine employs weighted FedAvg aggregation across five non-IID institutional nodes, whereas the Transformer encoder facilitates intricate temporal transaction reliance through multi-head self-attention. SHAP attribution scores are intended to support transparent decision-making aligned with regulatory accountability expectations The proposed framework, when tested on the IEEE-CIS Fraud Detection Dataset, consisting of 590,540 transactions, has an F1-score of 95.75%, ROC-AUC of 0.9713, precision of 96.38%, and recall of 95.14% at federated round 15, showing competitive results with broader architectural coverage in privacy preservation, explainability, and blockchain-based auditability compared to current state-of-the-art baselines

Author: C, R. D.; Mondeddula, S. R.; Vakkalagadda, T.; G, I.; Naveenkumar, R.
Title: BECTM-Net: Blockchain-Enabled Behavioral Credibility Equilibrium Trust Management Network for Decentralized Distributed Systems
Publication Title: 2026 2nd International Conference on Distributed Systems, Computer Networks and Cybersecurity (ICDSCNC)
Abstract Note: Over the years, decentralized distributed systems require reliable trust management mechanisms to support secure interactions among heterogeneous and potentially unreliable entities without depending on centralized authorities. Existing trust-management approaches often rely on static reputation models or individual behavioral indicators, which may fail to capture temporal behavior, neighborhood relationships, and contradictory transaction evidence. To address these limitations, this research proposes Blockchain-Enabled Behavioral Credibility Equilibrium Trust Management Network (BECTM-Net) for decentralized distributed systems. Initially, the elliptic bitcoin transaction dataset is employed to represent real-world blockchain transaction behavior and relational interactions. Then, transaction-behavior preprocessing mechanism normalizes heterogeneous transaction attributes and constructs structured behavioral representations while preserving temporal and neighborhood information. Subsequently, multi-relational graph convolutional feature extractor captures direct transaction connectivity, behavioral similarity and temporal dependencies to generate discriminative entity representations. Finally, proposed Behavioral Credibility Equilibrium Principle (BCEP) integrates behavioral reliability, neighborhood consistency, historical stability and contradictory evidence to estimate transaction-node credibility. The blockchain-based trust recording further ensures transparency, traceability and tamper resistance. The proposed framework is designed to improve trust evaluation, identify unreliable entities, strengthen accountability and supports transaction-level trust evaluation under the evaluated blockchain workload.

Author: Putchakayala, R.; Yallavula, R.; Jegajothi, B.
Title: Smart Data Governance: A Hybrid Deep-Machine Learning Model for Real-Time Privacy and Compliance Automation
Publication Title: 2026 Second International Conference on Intelligent Systems for Communication, IoT and Security (ICISCoIS)
Abstract Note: The emergence of IoT, IIoMT and smart-city infrastructures has resulted in data streams which are enormous, heterogeneous and need real-time control yet maintain privacy, security and regulatory compliance. Traditional centralized analytics solutions have high predictive performance, but are finding it harder and harder to remain relevant over time as data-sovereignty limits, high-privacy concerns, and lack of transparent auditability emerge. To overcome these shortcomings, this paper presents BC-FedHVAE-GRU, a blockchain-based federated hybrid deeplearning architecture that can be used to enable privacyconscious, compliant smart-data governance automation. The suggested system combines Hierarchical Variational Autoencoder (HVAE) to abstract privacy-sensitive features, a sequence modelling module that is based on GRU and that allows the representation of dynamic behavior and characterizing anomalies, and a federated learning (FL) architecture that allows learning without transferring raw data across different nodes. It includes a lightweight blockchain layer, which stores model changes immutably and enforces access permissions and offers audit traces that are complianceready based on smart contracts. Extensive experiments with IoT-like sensor datasets prove that BC-FedHVAE-GRU provides competitive methods of detection and has important privacy and governance benefits. The F1-scores of the centralized baselines were \0.942,0.859\ and 0.707 with MLP, GRU, and CNN+GRU, respectively. The proposed model achieved 0.889 accuracy and 0.864 F1-score under the federated conditions exceeding all the sequence based baselines and close to centralized performance regardless of decentralized training restrictions. Moreover, BC-FedHVAE-GRU reached ROCAUC 0.957 and PR-AUC 0.943 but federated optimization increased F1 -score to 0.856 after ten rounds. The interpretability of the framework, provided by SHAP and an autonomous policy of governance implemented by a DQN, support the transparency of the framework and its independent compliance. In general, BC-FedHVAE-GRU will provide a unified, privacy-sensitive and audit-capable framework of efficient smart-data management in real-time, which is suitable to the regulatory and operational demands of next-generation distributed settings.

Author: Feng, Y.; Zheng, B.; Li, T.; Wu, C.; Ma, Z.; Shen, Y.; Ma, J.
Title: AdaptiveShield: Dynamic Defense Against Decentralized Federated Learning Poisoning Attacks
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing
Abstract Note: Federated learning allows decentralized devices to collaboratively train a shared model while keeping datalocal, enhancing the privacy and security of the training process. However, it is vulnerable to poisoning attacks, where malicious participants inject false data to corrupt the global model. To address this, we propose AdaptiveShield, a dynamic hybrid defense approach designed to protect decentralized federated learning against such attacks. AdaptiveShield employs dynamic detection strategies that consider multiple risk factors to assess the maliciousness index and dynamically adjust the detection thresholds, which is able to adapt to various attack scenarios. In addition to attack detections, AdaptiveShield minimizes the negative impact on the global model from missed attackers by dynamically adjusting hyperparameters, thereby enhancing the robustness of the defense. It also dissociates user identities from their uploaded local models through a hierarchical shuffle mechanism, providing an extra layer of privacy protection for both the users and their local models. We evaluate AdaptiveShield across various experimental environments, attack settings, and datasets, demonstrating that it outperforms state-of-the-art approaches by achieving over 0.1 improvement in training accuracy while incurring negligible time overhead.

Author: Chintalacheruvu, N. K.; Kumar, D.; Prakash, A.

FL facilitates the training of machine learning models across institutions without the necessity of centralized patient data, hence safeguarding privacy. Blockchain facilitates a transparent and auditable digital ledger for managing data access and executing smart contracts. This survey offers an analysis of the existing literature on the frameworks that integrate FL and Blockchain in the healthcare domain. The works across different healthcare applications were summarized and discussed along with a few future directions.

Author: Lamani, L.; Leka, E.; Rexha, G.; Aliti, A.
Title: A Secure and Resilient Framework for Wildfire Management via UAVs and Blockchain Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2026 49th MIPRO ICT and Electronics Convention (MIPRO)
Abstract Note: The increasing frequency and severity of wildfires necessitate intelligent and robust airborne surveillance systems capable of functioning in dynamic, low-infrastructure areas. Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) have become critical for wildfire detection, monitoring, and damage assessment; yet, centralized coordination methods suffer from scalability challenges, sluggish decision-making, and vulnerability to cyber threats. This study presents a federated learning architecture combined with blockchain technology to improve UAV-assisted wildfire management. Federated learning allows UAVs to collectively train models for wildfire detection and severity assessment without sharing raw sensor data, protecting privacy and data location. Blockchain creates a decentralized foundation for trust by utilizing smart contracts to monitor UAV IDs, record model revisions, and enforce collaborative standards. Time-stamped ledger entries and consensus-driven validation help mitigate identity-based attacks such as spoofing and replay attempts, but they do not inherently prevent adversarial model poisoning, which requires additional defenses such as robust aggregation and anomaly detection. The system is designed for high-mobility aerial networks operating in beyond-5G/6G environments and supporting near-real-time wildfire monitoring. The suggested architecture combines federated learning with blockchain to enhance resilience, dependability, and scalability, providing a secure and scalable reference architecture for decentralized, mission-critical wildfire management.

Author: Gupta, G.; Verma, R. K.
Title: A Zero-Knowledge Proof and Differential Privacy-Enhanced Blockchain Framework for Secure Multi-Institutional Electronic Health Record Sharing
Publication Title: 2026 6th International Conference on Multimedia, Signal Processing and Communication Technologies (IMPACT)
Abstract Note: Secure and private sharing of electronic health records (EHRs) among multiple parties remains a significant challenge in digital healthcare. Although Blockchain technology can ensure data integrity through security and transparency, protecting patient privacy and enabling secure collaborative analysis continue to be difficult problems. To address these challenges, differential privacy (DP) and Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs) are integrated into a Blockchain-based solution in the innovative design of this multi-institutional EHR-sharing system architecture. ZKPs enable the verification of user identities and access requests without revealing sensitive information, while DP ensures that analytical results are statistically valid and that underlying data are protected against re-identification attacks. A permissioned Blockchain system is developed to support verifiable and privacy-preserving federated analytics over distributed data.
