Author: Vardhan, B. V.; Reethika, P.; Karuppasamy, S. G.; Arumugam, S. R.; V, S. M.; S, G.
Title: Secure Convergence Model for Distributed Interactions
Publication Title: 2026 7th International Conference on Mobile Computing and Sustainable Informatics (ICMCSI)
Abstract Note: In modern digital ecosystems, distributed architectures such as cloud computing, multi-agent systems, and the Internet of Things (IoT) are facing challenges in ensuring a secure and reliable coordination of heterogeneous nodes in the modern digital ecosystem. The current solutions typically cover only one aspect of security, e.g., encryption, trust management, or anomaly detection, without being able to cover the whole spectrum of dynamic networks. This study introduces SCMDI to overcome such drawbacks and it is a secure convergence model for distributed interactions. SCMDI combines hybrid encryption, situational risk assessment, adaptive anomaly detection and policy based access control. It compares the reliability of the nodes with respect to past data and the actual behavior through machine learning models that observe network activity in real time. The framework guarantees confidentiality and integrity by using a combination of symmetric and asymmetric cryptography as well as automatically changing access policies based on the evolving network situations. As well as it is a low weight audit logging system offers tamper free traceability without adding excessive weight to computation. Simulation environment experiments with distributed environments show that SCMDI is effective in terms of detecting malicious activities, imposing trust ratings, and enforcing security policies. Author: Liu, S.; Cao, Y.; Murakami, T.; Liu, W.; Liew, S. P.; Takahashi, T.; Liu, J.; Yoshikawa, M.
Title: Federated Graph Analytics With Differential Privacy
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing
Abstract Note: Collaborative graph analysis across multiple institutions is becoming increasingly popular. Realistic examples include social network analysis across various social platforms, financial transaction analysis across multiple banks, and analyzing the transmission of infectious diseases across multiple hospitals. We define the federated graph analytics, a new problem for collaborative graph analytics under differential privacy. Although differentially private graph analysis has been widely studied, it fails to achieve a good tradeoff between utility and privacy in federated scenarios, due to the limited view of local clients and overlapping information across multiple subgraphs. Motivated by this, we first propose a federated graph analytic framework, named \textbackslash{}mathsf {FEAT}\FEAT, which enables arbitrary downstream common graph statistics while preserving individual privacy. Furthermore, we introduce an optimized framework based on our proposed degree-based partition algorithm, called \textbackslash{}mathsf {FEAT}\FEAT+, which improves the overall utility by leveraging the true local subgraphs. Finally, extensive experiments demonstrate that our \textbackslash{}mathsf {FEAT}\FEAT and \textbackslash{}mathsf {FEAT+}\FEAT+ significantly outperform the baseline approach by approximately four and five orders of magnitude, respectively.

Author: Reddy, R. A.; Pasha, S. N.; Kumari, D. S.
Title: Scientometric Analysis of Data Privacy and Cloud Security: Research Trends in Access Control and Encryption Techniques
Publication Title: 2026 Sixth International Conference on Advances in Electrical, Computing, Communications and Sustainable Technologies (ICAECT)
Abstract Note: Data Privacy and Cloud Security are two inseparable components of contemporary digital infrastructure that allow sensitive data stored or processed in a cloud-based environment to be protected against unauthorized access, abuse, or loss. The purpose of the paper is to synthetically examine the research trends, collaboration networks, and thematic developments in the world in terms of access control and encryption methods through the method of scientometrics. Although there is a lot of literature on cryptography and secure cloud frameworks, the existing literature is still divided among various fields, with no coherent knowledge of the latest trends, interdisciplinary connections, and new security models. To fill this gap, bibliometric data from the Scopus database (20202025) were examined using VOSviewer, CiteSpace, Excel, and OriginPro. The analysis demonstrates that 694 publications are in 165 sources with an annual growth rate of 36.26, highlighting the fact that cloud security research is increasing rapidly. India and China became the most productive participants, and major topics such as blockchain-powered access control, hybrid encryption, and AI-powered privacy frameworks were introduced. The analysis of keywords and citations revealed research clusters in federated learning, post-quantum cryptography, and decentralized security models. The findings provide a thorough mapping of the intellectual organization of research on cloud security and point to further directions of explainable, energy-efficient, and regulation-consistent encryption systems for reliable cloud ecosystems.

Author: T.Muthumanickam; Jayalakshmi, D.; M, S.; Kumar, S. S.; S, L.; Agoramoorthy, M.

Abstract Note: The intersection of sixth-generation (6G) communication networks, edge computing, and federated learning offers a novel occasion regarding empowering trustful and scalable collaboration throughout distributed Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystems. The framework has high-uniform performance in adversarial environments where 99.6 percent of malicious model updates are identified with a small false positive. The results define the 6G-integrated federated learning as a framework of reliable and scalable edge-IoT cooperation.

Author: Agrahari, P.; Rai, M.; Saxena, A. K.; Rasheed, J.; Elkiran, H.

Author: Dhanraj, J. A.; Dhongle, P.; R.Tamilamuthan; M.Lakshmanan; Ashtankar, N.; Hole, S. R.

Author: Sereti, Z.; Mavrikos, E.; Chatzistamatis, S.; Tsekouras, G. E.

Author: Zhang, Y.; Zhang, M.; Zhang, H.; Tong, S.
Title: DeFi-GAT: A Blockchain-Enabled Federated Learning Framework With Hierarchical Attention for Privacy-Preserving RGB-D Human Motion Recognition
Publication Title: IEEE Access
Abstract Note: RGB-D human motion recognition is an important task in intelligent sensing, human-computer interaction, and assistive systems. However, real-world deployment is often hindered by distributed data silos, heterogeneous sensing environments, and strict privacy constraints. This paper presents DeFi-GAT, a blockchain-enabled federated learning framework that integrates hierarchical attention mechanisms for privacy-preserving multimodal human motion recognition. The framework introduces two key innovations: 1). a threshold signature-based authentication mechanism that enables auditable aggregation authorization for federated multi-institutional collaboration without relying on a single centralized authentication authority, and 2). a spatial-modality-feature attention-enhanced CNN-GAT hybrid architecture that dynamically focuses on discriminative visual regions and structurally important skeletal joints while suppressing background noise. Author: Kiruba, S. K.; Anand, R.

Author: Wang, Z.; Chen, T.; Yu, Y.; Wu, S.
Title: A Blockchain-Assisted Verifiable and Privacy-Preserving Heterogeneous Federated Learning Framework for Women-Centric Consumer Electronics
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Consumer Electronics
Abstract Note: The rapid evolution of women-centric consumer electronics has promoted the adoption of federated learning (FL) for privacy-preserving health monitoring over distributed user data. In real-world deployments, clients often require heterogeneous private model architectures tailored to different sensing modalities, device capabilities, and application-specific health tasks. HFL addresses model heterogeneity by enabling proxy-based knowledge sharing, but existing frameworks still lack efficient zero-knowledge verification of submitted updates and auditable admission control for trusted cross-device and cross-institution collaboration. We therefore propose BVPHFL: A Blockchain-Assisted Verifiable and Privacy-Preserving Heterogeneous Federated Learning Framework for Women-Centric Consumer Electronics. In BVPHFL, each client locally trains a private model and a proxy model through a prescribed private–proxy learning process, and submits only the resulting proxy update for global collaboration. Zero-knowledge proofs verify the provenance of submitted proxy updates and their correspondence to the training round, and certify the correctness of aggregation over the admitted update set, while preserving the confidentiality of raw data and private training states against the coordinator, verifier contract, and other participants. The blockchain provides an auditable record of admitted updates before global aggregation. Experiments on benchmark screening workloads show comparable utility in most evaluated tasks and characterize the efficiency of update validation and aggregation.

Author: Bhutta, M. A.; Harrath, Y.
Title: Fed-SMOTE: Differentially Private Federated Learning for Imbalanced Supply Chain Fraud Detection
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Blockchain, and Internet of Things (AIBThings)
Abstract Note: Due to the low frequency of fraudulent transactions in the supply chain, the inherently imbalanced nature of these datasets, and the privacy-sensitive data of the supply chain organizations, it is challenging to implement fraud detection systems using the centralized method or standard federated learning approaches. In this paper, we present a novel federated learning framework that leverages the advantages of both federated and SMOTE methods, called Federated Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (Fed-SMOTE). Each client calculates the statistics of the minority class of the supply chain transactions, applies the Laplacian mechanism to ensure the differential privacy of these statistics, and uses the statistics of the majority class calculated globally to generate synthetic transactions using the Borderline-SMOTE algorithm. These synthetic transactions are combined with the original transactions of each supply chain client to train an XGBoost classifier. The XGBoost classifiers from each client are combined using a performance-weighted aggregation algorithm to create a final fraud detection model. Experiments on the DataCo Smart Supply Chain dataset with 180,519 transactions and 2.25% fraudulent transactions show that the Fed-SMOTE framework achieves an F1-score of 0.686 ± 0.004 and 99.5% recall with 10 random seeds. These results are comparable with the centralized SMOTE-based methods but maintain the benefits of data locality, differential privacy with ε=1.0, and perform well with non-IID datasets over a range of 2 to 20 clients with 86.7% communication cost reduction compared to the centralized method of sharing supply chain data. Thus, the results of this experiment demonstrate that SMOTE-based federated learning with differential privacy can provide a privacy-preserving, communication-efficient, and decision-oriented solution for fraud detection in supply chain environments.
Manual Tags: Federated learning; privacy-preserving machine learning; differential privacy; XGBoost; SMOTE; imbalanced classification; supply chain fraud detection

Author: Ramadevi, R.; Suganya, B.; Babu, K.; Lakshmi, M. A.; Rajmohan, M.; K, A.

Communication latency is kept at 130 to 170 milliseconds, which helps establish an effective setting of data transfer via wireless networks. Its size is 10-14 MB, which means that the bandwidth is economically used. The security evaluation confirms that there is a low threat of information leakage that can be attributed to encryption and secure aggregation measures.

Author: Yin, J.; Yang, Q.; Sun, R.; Liu, J.; Du, X.; Aitsaadi, N.
Title: LPPFS: A Lightweight and Privacy-Preserving Feature Selection for Vertical Federated Learning
Publication Title: ICC 2026 - IEEE International Conference on Communications
Abstract Note: Vertical Federated Learning (VFL) is a distributed machine learning paradigm that preserves the privacy of participants’ raw data while enabling entities with fully overlapping sample spaces to collaboratively train a shared model. Feature selection plays a pivotal role in the data preprocessing phase of VFL. However, existing works often suffer from inefficiency and excessive interactions, which hinder their practical deployment. To address these deficiencies, we propose a lightweight and privacy-preserving feature selection scheme. Our scheme adopts a filter-based method and, for the first time in the VFL setting, employs the Fisher criterion as the scoring metric. Feature selection can be completed in only three rounds of interaction between the label holder and other participants, with communication costs kept within a practical range. Privacy preservation is ensured through the integration of Fully Homomorphic Encryption and a random masking mechanism, thereby removing the need for a trusted third party. We evaluate the proposed scheme on three real-world datasets, and the results demonstrate notable accuracy improvements and superior efficiency compared to existing filter-based secure feature selection methods for VFL.

Author: L, M. K.; Dhevi, B. Lakshmi
Title: An In-Depth Control of Blockchain Enabled and AI based Security Mechanisms in Distributed WSN-IoT Environments
Publication Title: 2026 9th International Conference on Computing Methodologies and Communication (ICCMC)
Abstract Note: This WSNs coupled with the Internet of Things (IoT) is very much needed in facilitating smart environment like smart cities, industrial automation, healthcare monitoring and environmental monitoring. Nevertheless, WSN-IoT systems are extremely susceptible to security risks such as denial-of-service attacks, malicious node behaviors, manipulation of routing, data manipulation, and privacy breaches due to their distributed, heterogeneous, and resource-constrained nature. Conventional centralized security models are usually insufficient to deal with these dynamic and scale cyber threats. The paper describes a detailed overview of blockchain-based and artificial intelligence (AI)-based security solutions to the distributed WSN-IoT scenarios. Author: Sultana, T.; Sunna, A. A.; Uddin, M. M.; Kshetri, N.
Title: ppAIsec: Privacy-Preserving AI Models in Healthcare Security - AI Frameworks Synthesis
Publication Title: 2026 14th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
Abstract Note: As artificial intelligence (AI) technologies, particularly generative and collaborative learning models—are increasingly integrated into healthcare and other sensitive domains, data privacy, security, and fairness concerns have grown significantly. Author: Li, L.; Guo, C.; Tang, X.; Choo, K.-K. R.; Liu, Y.

Abstract Note: Decentralized federated learning (DFL) has been widely used in edge computing and Internet of Things (IoT) settings with many devices. An implementation on Hyperledger Fabric demonstrates that ZKPoFL achieves high efficiency. Author: Althabahi, M.; Abbas, S.

Abstract Note: Privacy and cybersecurity systems in smart cities are critically reviewed and assessed in the present paper by synthesizing 21 peer-reviewed publications, published between 2018 and 2024, but the works on the topic published prior to 2018 are also acknowledged to provide background information. The systematic literature review was conducted based on the five-phase protocol presented by Kitchenham with the assistance of a PRISMAlike quality assessment of the studies included. These mechanisms were categorized into five themes that comprise blockchain-based architectures, intrusion detection and machine learning models, privacy-preserving learning systems, legal and governance frameworks and hybrid trust-based architectures. An evaluation lens Technology, Governance, and Resilience (TGR) triad was used to make comparative synthesis and prioritize both performance and limitation and applicability at the city level. As determined in the review, blockchain-enabled schemes dominate in the recent researches and offer immutability, auditability, but have a limitation of latency, interoperability and high power-consumption. These regulations such as GDPR are enforced but not dynamic and thus, they lag behind the evolving technologies. Hybrid trust based models are promising to be integrated yet they are computationally expensive. The results indicate that scalable, modular, and legally entrenched structures are immediately required in order to balance privacy, cost, and social trust of urban infrastructures. Author: Roy, S.; Singha, S. K.; Bera, D.
Title: X-BDFL: Explainable Blockchain-Enabled Distributed Federated Learning Against Poisoning Attack in Healthcare
Publication Title: IEEE Access
Abstract Note: Recent advances in 5G have empowered edge devices to generate high-quality data, driving the need for Federated Learning (FL), which enables privacy-preserving model training at the edge (e.g., hospitals) without sharing raw data. However, traditional FL remains vulnerable to poisoning attacks and relies on an overburdened central server. Moreover, the lack of transparent explanations for poisoner elimination raises concerns about model reliability, especially in sensitive domains like healthcare. This article proposes a novel hyperledger-based hierarchical FL scheme called X-BDFL (Explainable blockchain-enabled distributed federated learning) against poisoning attack in healthcare that ensures explainable and verifiable poisoner detection and elimination scheme without exposing sensitive model parameters. The hierarchical FL structure builds trust by filtering unintended anomalies at the edge to protect client reputation and detecting poisoners at the fog for early mitigation and reduced server overhead. The poisoner detection scheme leverages Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP)-based behaviour analysis of client models to justify threat elimination through feature attribution. The novelty of this scheme is its use of JS-Divergence to detect out-of-order malicious clients without assuming any prior data distribution, and maintaining effectiveness even when most participants are compromised. Furthermore, our scheme offers transparent, scalable defence while preserving model integrity without adding overhead to edge medical devices. Experimental results shows that X-BDFL counters label-flipping and backdoor attacks with low success rates of 4% and 9% under 90% poisoning, while preserving task accuracy. It achieves comparable defence accuracy on MINIST dataset and outperforms state-of-the-art method (MOAT) by 28% on complex dataset like COVID-QU-Ex.

Author: Vummaneni, N. S.; Bobba, S.

Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Cognitive Engineering (ICIICE)
Abstract Note: Collaborative threat intelligence holds immense value for cybersecurity, yet its adoption remains limited by a fundamental trust paradox: the security telemetry most useful for detecting emerging threats is precisely the data organisations are least willing to expose. Existing approaches force a choice between cooperation and operational secrecy, relegating threat sharing to the exchange of low-fidelity indicators that omit the rich behavioural patterns needed to detect sophisticated attacks. This paper presents Federated Learning for Threat Signature Exchange (FLTSE), a protocol that enables organisations to collaboratively train threat detection models without revealing proprietary security telemetry. Author: Attaullah, H. M.; Ehsan, M.; Siddiqui, M. S.; Rafi, M.
Title: Trust-Aware Multimodal Multi-Agent Coordination for Secure UAV Swarms in 6G Networks

Abstract Note: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) swarms are expected to play a critical role in future sixth-generation (6G) networks by enabling intelligent sensing, autonomous coordination, and real-time mission execution across smart city, disaster response, industrial Internet-of-Things (IoT), and surveillance applications. The proposed framework integrates multimodal trust fusion using vision-emulated (identity and spatial consistency), radio-frequency (RF), and motion-based observations, cross-modal consistency verification, trust-aware federated learning, semantic communication, and adaptive swarm coordination. A dynamic trust evaluation mechanism is developed to identify trusted, suspicious, and malicious UAVs, while a trust-weighted federated aggregation strategy mitigates the impact of poisoned model updates and compromised agents. Furthermore, semantic communication is employed to reduce communication overhead and improve coordination efficiency. The proposed framework is evaluated using the T-ITS cyber-physical UAV dataset and NS-3-based swarm simulations under various attack scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate that TMMAC achieves a trust classification accuracy of 99.27%, an attack detection rate of 97.82%, a communication latency of 69 ms, a mission success rate of 94.18%, and an energy consumption of 232 Wh, consistently outperforming recently proposed trust management, federated learning, blockchain-assisted, and intrusion detection baselines. The results confirm that the proposed framework significantly enhances security, resilience, communication efficiency, and operational reliability for next-generation 6G-enabled UAV swarm networks.

Author: Gong, X.; Wang, Y.; Li, S.; Sun, M.; Li, S.; Chen, C.; Wang, Q.; Lam, K.-Y.
Title: Sleight: Hidden Data Privacy Breaches in Federated Learning
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing
Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as a paradigm for conducting machine learning across broad and decentralized datasets, promising enhanced privacy by obviating the need for direct data sharing. However, recent studies show that attackers can steal private data through model manipulation or gradient analysis. Existing attacks are constrained by low theft quantity or low-resolution data, and they are often easily detected through anomaly monitoring in gradients or weights. In this paper, we propose Sleight, a novel data-reconstruction attack, supported by two key techniques, i.e., distinctive and sparse encoding design and block partitioning. Unlike conventional methods that require detectable changes to the model, Sleight stealthily embeds a hidden model using parameter sharing to systematically extract sensitive data. The Fibonacci-based index design ensures efficient, structured retrieval of memorized data, while the block partitioning method enhances Sleight’s capability to handle high-resolution images by dividing them into smaller, manageable units. Extensive experiments on 4 datasets confirmed that Sleight is superior to 5 state-of-the-art data-reconstruction attacks under 5 respective detection methods. Sleight can handle large-scale and high-resolution data without being detected or mitigated by state-of-the-art data reconstruction defense methods. In contrast to baselines, Sleight can be directly applied to both FedAvg and FedSGD scenarios, underscoring the need for developers to devise new defenses against such vulnerabilities. We will open-source our code upon acceptance.
Manual Tags: federated learning (FL); and data privacy breaches; Data reconstruction attacks

Author: Dong, S.; Wang, R.; Zhang, J.
Title: RoTEE-Loc: Near-Zero-Trust Location Privacy Protection Scheme for V2X Networks Based on Rotating Roadside TEEs
Publication Title: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
Abstract Note: High-frequency location sharing in vehicle-to-everything (V2X) systems enables the cooperative perception and traffic services, but a compromised roadside unit (RSU) may expose vehicle locations or facilitate long-term trajectory inference. Existing location-privacy methods commonly rely on continuously trustworthy infrastructure or incur substantial computation and communication overhead. This article proposes RoTEE-Loc, a location-privacy scheme that reduces long-term trust in RSUs by combining verifiable-random-function-based Leader rotation, confidential aggregation inside a trusted execution environment (TEE), adaptive differential privacy, and Shamir threshold secret sharing. A Leader RSU is elected for each 5-s slot, while perturbed cluster centers are distributed as shares and reconstructed by vehicles. The term “near-zero trust” is limited to long-term RSU confidentiality: the design still assumes correct TEE isolation and attestation under the stated threat model. Parameterized simulations based on T-Drive trajectories indicate a favorable privacy–utility tradeoff, lower high-density latency and communication overhead than the evaluated baselines, and threshold-based recovery under moderate independent packet loss. At 1,000 vehicles, the modeled end-to-end latency is 125 ms; thus, it exceeds the 100-ms reference target but remains below the compared baselines. These results characterize the evaluated operating range rather than a deployed V2X system.

Author: Ibrahim, H.; Ahakonye, P. N.; Yaddarabullah; Ahakonye, L. A. C.; Lee, J.-M.; Kim, D.-S.
Title: Trustworthy Edge: Active Consensus-Layer Trust Computation for Real-Time Intrusion Detection in Software-Defined Industrial IoT
Publication Title: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
Abstract Note: The Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) faces escalating cybersecurity threats due to its expansive attack surface and the mission-critical nature of industrial operations. Federated learning (FL) enables privacy-preserving collaborative intrusion detection but remains vulnerable to model poisoning and lacks tamper-proof auditability. Blockchain technology provides decentralization and immutability; however, existing blockchain-FL integrations treat the ledger as a passive audit log, creating a fundamental gap: trust scoring remains separate from consensus, allowing malicious nodes to accumulate reputation while poisoning models. This article introduces Trustworthy Edge, a software-defined IIoT (SD-IIoT) architecture featuring active consensus-layer trust computation through PureChain, a lightweight permissioned blockchain employing proof of authority and association (PoA2). Unlike conventional approaches where trust is computed off-chain and merely logged, PoA2 embeds behavioral trust scoring directly into block finalization, requiring both authority validation and association thresholds for consensus. This novel coupling transforms blockchain from passive storage to active security enforcer. PoA2 achieves 125-ms consensus finality while maintaining Byzantine fault tolerance (BFT) through asynchronous architectural separation; detection latency remains sub-2 ms, independent of blockchain operations. The closed-loop architecture dynamically adapts: detected intrusions trigger trust penalties, aggregation reweighting, and automated quarantine. Extensive experiments on four IIoT datasets (IoTForge, ToN-IoT, IoT-CAD, and WUSTL-IIoT-2021) demonstrate that BiLSTM-based detection achieves 97.42% accuracy. Under 20% malicious clients, PoA2 weighted aggregation limits accuracy degradation to 2.4%—a 78% improvement over vanilla FL (11.3% drop). Comprehensive non-IID evaluation across Dirichlet distributions ( \textbackslash{}alpha = 0.1, 0.3, 0.5\ ) and quantity imbalance shows graceful degradation (4%–8% accuracy drop at \textbackslash{}alpha =0.1\ ). Scalability analysis with up to 1000 clients and 25 validators demonstrates linear scaling with consensus latency below 245 ms. Statistical significance testing (paired t-test, p < 0.01) confirms superiority. We further provide formal convergence and stability proofs, real-time deployment guidelines, comprehensive blockchain metrics (storage, energy, and communication), in-depth attack analysis (Sybil, collusion, and smart contract), and cross-dataset generalization across four industrial datasets, confirming the framework’s robustness and practical viability. To our knowledge, this is the first SD-IIoT framework achieving active consensus-layer trust computation for verifiable, real-time intrusion detection in industrial environments.
Manual Tags: blockchain; intrusion detection; trust management; Active trust computation; real-time systems; software-defined networking (SDN)

Author: Qu, X.; Han, S.; Liu, E.; Geng, Y.; Ni, W.; Liu, Y.; Guo, R.; Bi, Y.
Title: Privacy-Preserving Consensus-Oriented Aggregation for Federated Learning With Heterogeneity
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering
Abstract Note: Achieving reliable network-wide consensus formation in distributed learning systems becomes increasingly challenging when edge nodes hold skewed data distributions. Federated learning (FL) enables privacy-preserving collaborative model training without sharing raw data, but statistical heterogeneity across nodes significantly degrades convergence and may expose sensitive label statistics to distribution-inference attacks. To address these limitations, this paper presents a new federated consensus-oriented aggregation (FedCOA) strategy, which improves consensus formation of FL under strong heterogeneity, suppresses skew-induced instability while mitigating distribution-level privacy leakage. FedCOA perturbs local label distributions using differential privacy (DP) and computes a noise-robust Index of Data Heterogeneity (IDH), which guides dynamic aggregation, regulates bias propagation, suppresses the influence of skewed updates, and facilitates consensus formation dynamics. We show theoretically that FedCOA reduces the divergence term in the convergence upper bound. Experiments demonstrate up to 80.3%, 75.1%, and 79.2% reductions in communication rounds on MNIST, FashionMNIST, and CIFAR-10, respectively.
Manual Tags: Federated learning; model aggregation; communication efficiency; data heterogeneity

Author: P, A. M.; Mohan, M.
Title: A Secure Cloud Intrusion Detection Framework Using Deep Learning with Privacy Preservation and Blockchain-Based Data Protection
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Computing Theory and Wireless Communications (ICCTWC)
Abstract Note: Cloud computing environments are increasingly exposed to sophisticated cyber threats due to their distributed and multi-tenant nature, making security and privacy critical concerns. Intrusion detection systems play a vital role in identifying malicious activities; however, existing approaches often suffer from high false alarms, privacy leakage, and limited data protection capabilities. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a privacy-preserving deep learning-based framework for secure intrusion detection and data protection in cloud environments. The proposed methodology integrates data preprocessing, optimized feature extraction, and a deep neural network-based classifier to accurately detect and classify intrusion activities. To protect sensitive information during analysis and storage, a privacy-preserving mechanism and a lightweight data encryption model are incorporated to ensure secure data auditing and controlled retrieval. Furthermore, a blockchain-assisted data mitigation layer is employed to enhance data integrity, transparency, and secure transmission by maintaining immutable audit records. The effectiveness of the proposed framework is evaluated using the CICIoT2023 dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves a detection accuracy of 99%, along with high precision, recall, and F 1 -score, while maintaining low false alarm rates. Comparative analysis confirms that the proposed framework outperforms existing intrusion detection methods, providing a robust, privacy-aware, and trustworthy solution for cloud security.

Author: Agrawal, S.; Ashara, P.; Bhamare, M.; Chaudhari, A.; Patil, S.
Title: Decentralized Healthcare Data Exchange Using Blockchain and Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2026 2nd International Conference on Information, Implementation and Innovation in Technology (I2ITCON)
Abstract Note: Managing health data across institutions remains one of the harder problems in modern healthcare not just technically, but from a trust standpoint. This paper describes a system that combines blockchain-based access governance with federated learning to enable privacy-preserving collaborative training across multiple institutions, without requiring any party to share raw patient data. The intelligence layer consists of two models: a feedforward neural network for five-class disease risk classification and an LSTM autoencoder for real-time anomaly detection, both trained on wearable sensor data (heart rate, SpO2, steps, and calories) and deployed as quantized TFLite models within a Flutter mobile application. Smart contracts on the Ethereum Sepolia testnet handle consent and role-based access control automatically, while patient data is encrypted and stored on IPFS. Differential privacy (ε = 1.0, δ = 10−5) is applied to local gradients before aggregation, and secure multi-party computation protects individual node updates at the coordination step. Across five federated nodes, the global model reached 92.3% classification accuracy compared to 78.6% for a centralized baseline and 73−75% for single-institution models while keeping raw data within institutional boundaries throughout.

Author: Ong, G. A. M.; Tianio, J. S.; Manlapas, O. R.; Cabañeros, J. S.
Title: Evaluating Privacy as a Design Constraint in Cross-Domain Computing Technologies
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Revolutionary Artificial Intelligence and Future Applications (Rev-AI)
Abstract Note: Privacy has emerged as a basic design requirement in contemporary computational systems, and has impacted architectural decisions, data-processing processes, and model-level implementations in a wide variety of fields. In this work, a cross-domain comparative analysis of the operationalization of privacy requirements in real systems is performed, considering 25 representative works in the IT infrastructure, education, healthcare, fitness technologies, and the public-sector systems. Some of the persistent mechanisms identified in the analysis include differential privacy, federated learning, cryptographic protocols, blockchain-based governance, and privacy-aware sensing and how they can be integrated at the data, model, and system layers. The results indicate that privacy-sensitive protocols enhance confidentiality, accountability, and locality of data at the cost of performance, computation, and evaluation causing trade-offs. There is significant benchmarking variability due to heterogeneous datasets, threat models, evaluation metrics, and system assumptions, which limit comparability across studies. To aid in more reliable comparison, and to develop privacy-by-design implementations at more domains of computation, the paper identifies the necessity of unified evaluation standards and quantifiable privacy measures.

Author: Ramachandran, T. P.; Khatib, A.; Syambabu, V.; S, Y.; Padole, G.; M, R.

Author: Goli, P.; Kanan, M.; Anurada, T.; Karunanidhi, P. C.; Panduri, B.; Kumar, M.
Title: Advances in Blockchain and Machine Learning for Privacy-Preserving Healthcare Data Processing: A New Secure Analytics Framework
Publication Title: 2026 9th International Conference on Circuit, Power & Computing Technologies (ICCPCT)
Abstract Note: Hospitals, researchers, and providers are increasingly creating and exchanging sensitive medical data due to the rapid digitization of the healthcare system. While healthcare data processing and storage jeopardize privacy, security, and integrity, advanced data analytics enhance clinical decision-making and patient care. The security and trustworthiness of a centralized healthcare data management system’s patients are vulnerable to cyberattacks, illegal access, and data breaches. For the purpose of protecting patients’ personal health information, this study presents a blockchain-machine learning analytics architecture. Blockchain technology ensures the security, transparency, and tracking of medical records through its distributed, immutable ledger. But machine learning helps with clinical decision support, predictive modeling, and enhanced data analysis from huge healthcare datasets. Without disclosing patient information, the proposed technology enables machine learning models to extract useful insights from encrypted healthcare data. In order to store and analyze patient data, the framework employs distributed authentication, secure smart contracts, and encrypted data access protocols. Data security, transparency of healthcare data transactions, and scalable medical research and diagnostic analytics are all improved by the suggested solution, according to performance evaluation. Integrating blockchain technology with machine learning has the potential to make digital healthcare infrastructures safer, more reliable, and more adept at handling patient data.

Author: AbdelRaouf, H.; Eltoukhy, A. T.; Fouda, M.; Fadlullah, Z. M.; Ibrahem, M. I.
Title: Secure and Privacy-Preserving Frameworks for IoMT: A Survey of Cryptographic and Blockchain-Enabled Approaches
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Secure IoT, Assured and Trusted Computing (SATC)
Abstract Note: The Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) is changing how care is delivered through continuous sensing and analytics. However, it also increases the risk of attacks across devices, edge, and cloud. This survey summarizes the current state of end-to-end privacy and security for IoMT, organized by the data lifecycle: capture, storage and sharing, query and analytics, and learning. We examine lightweight device-side encryption, such as chaos-driven keystreams, that provides real-time protection for constrained wearables. We also examine edge architectures that combine cryptographic techniques with decentralized off-chain storage and blockchain smart contracts to ensure integrity, access control, and auditability. Additionally, we explore ciphertext-friendly analytics that leverage additive homomorphic computation, symmetric searchable encryption, and Bloom-filter indexing. Finally, we discuss privacy-preserving intelligence through federated learning (FL) with semantically secure update sharing. In each area, we evaluate performance trade-offs in computation, latency, scalability, and trust distribution. The survey offers a classification of mechanisms, a comparison matrix of guarantees and costs, and a reference architecture that combines these techniques into a clear, regulation-compliant stack.

Author: Suriya, P.; Balamurugan, G.
Title: A Comparative Analysis of Secure Federated Learning Architectures for Collaborative Training on Distributed Financial Data
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
Abstract Note: Financial institutions deal with huge volumes of sensitive customer data that includes transaction records, account activity, credit histories, and customer-related information. Meanwhile, collaborative learning over distributed financial data might prone to tasks such as fraud detection, credit risk evaluation, and anti-money laundering. Federated learning (FL) deliberates a real-time solution by allowing institutions to train models cooperatively without sharing their local information. However, the FL in financial settings introduces numerous challenges that include gradient leakage, adversarial model updates, free-riding behavior, and data heterogeneity across institutions. In this work, we surveyed recent research work on secure federated learning and clustered the approaches into six key categories: cryptographic techniques, differential privacy, robust aggregation, trusted execution environments, incentivebased mechanisms, and data heterogeneity methods. For each approach, major information such as system design, threat model, and evaluation strategy is discussed. In addition, a comparative summary is also discussed to highlight how various methods handle security and practical constraints. From our analysis, we noticed that most existing approaches tackle only one challenge at a time, and we identified several open pathways that researchers focusing on secure federated learning over distributed financial data should prioritize.

Author: Ethakota, V. V. S. S.; Deepthi, K. K. C.
Title: BeDaSH+: A Comprehensive Framework for Blockchain-Enabled Data-Driven Telehealth Security With Federated Learning, TinyML, and GDPR Compliance
Publication Title: IEEE Access
Abstract Note: Blockchain-enabled telehealth systems with cryptographic protection for physiological sensor data, energy constraints of implant-class wearables, and GDPR compliance have revolutionized patient monitoring and data management. However, AES encryption through Ethereum’s LSTM-based ECG prediction exhibits critical problems, such as prohibitive blockchain costs, single-patient generalization failure, invalidated wearable energy, absence of key recovery, lack of EHR interoperability, unmeasured end-to-end latency, no collusion resistance, and the conflict of the GDPR Article 17. This paper proposes a new Hyperledger Fabric RAFT consortium blockchain, FedAvg of federated learning, quantized TCN INT8 key generation, 3-of-5 Shamir Secret Sharing to protect sensitive data, HL7 FHIR R4 gateway, hash-based ZK commitment for authentication, six-stage pipeline benchmarking for throughput, and chameleon hash to erasure GDPR. Hyperledger Fabric RAFT achieves \63.3{\textbackslash{}pm }4.1\ ms block commit latency at {\textbackslash{}\}0.00\ per-transaction fee (98.4% improvement). FedAvg federated learning on the MIT-BIH ECG yields 71.8% reduction in MAE on three nodes without raw data transmission. A quantized TCN INT8 model reduces the scaled ARM Cortex-M4 inference energy from \22.50 \textbackslash{}mu \ J (BeDaSH estimate) to \0.06 \textbackslash{}mu \ J (MLPerf Tiny scaled estimate), a 99.7% reduction, with all 1000 generated keys confirmed unique on the measurement platform. A 3-of-5 Shamir scheme over \textbackslash{}mathbb {F}(2^{127}{-}1)\ enables key recovery in \37.7 \textbackslash{}mu $ s. HL7 FHIR R4 validation yields 10/10 HTTP 201 responses. Cryptographic pipeline benchmarking shows a P50 latency of 2.7 ms and 317.5 TPS at ten concurrent sessions; including the Fabric commit, full-path P50 is 66.0 ms. ZK-proof authentication blocks 100/100 collusion attacks. Chameleon hash erasure implements the recommended architectural pattern of EDPB Guidelines 02/2025 for GDPR Article 17 compliance in 100 patient records.

Author: Raza, S.; Babar, M.; Naeem, T.; Abbasi, A.; Khan, S.; Din, A.
Title: Secure and Trust-Aware Federated Digital Twin Framework for Next-Generation Healthcare Systems
Publication Title: 2026 5th MEC International Conference on Advanced Data Analytics and Artificial Intelligence for Sustainable Smart Cities (ICADAAI)
Abstract Note: The conventional healthcare systems are transforming into intelligent healthcare at a monumental pace. The introduction of artificial intelligence improves patientcentric treatment, disease diagnosis, and real-time patient monitoring. However, intelligent healthcare faces low-latency analytics, patient privacy, and regulatory challenges. Digital twins in conjunction with federated learning (FL) and edge intelligence (EI) address these challenges. FL advances training predictive models while keeping patient privacy intact, and the EI facilitates low latency, swift decision-making, and crisp responses in emergency situations. This study proposed a standards-compliant Federated Digital Twins Healthcare Framework (FDTHF). It comprises an over-edge-cloud architecture that supports digital twin modelling, edge intelligence, and federated learning for real-time deployment of healthcare systems. FDTHF architecture assures secure federated analytics, patient information privacy, and lowlatency patient examination. In addition, the framework provides a scalable and trustworthy foundation for designing standards-aware digital twin-based healthcare systems.

Author: Sankaran, S.
Title: From Fragmentation to Trust: Standardizing Communication in Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Computer, Data Sciences and Applications (ACDSA)
Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative training of machine learning models without sharing raw data, offering a pathway to privacy-preserving innovation in sensitive domains such as healthcare, finance, and telecommunications. Despite its promise, the FL ecosystem remains fragmented: frameworks like TensorFlow Federated, Flower, and PySyft each define proprietary communication protocols, creating “walled gardens” that hinder interoperability, inflate engineering costs, and restrict participation across heterogeneous infrastructures. This paper argues that standardization of FL communication is essential not only for technical efficiency but also for fostering systemic trust. We propose a Federated Learning Communication and Interoperability Protocol (FL-CIP) as a unifying layer that defines baseline communication primitives for client–server federations—such as handshake, task messaging, model serialization, update reporting, and error codes—while extending to peer-to-peer scenarios with neighbor discovery, model update exchange, and topology synchronization. Through this lens, interoperability becomes the foundation of trust, transparency and auditability strengthen accountability, and open standards prevent vendor lock-in, enabling fair participation. Challenges remain in embedding security, designing governance models, and balancing extensibility with stability, but lessons from past standardization domains underscore the feasibility of this effort. FL-CIP thus provides a blueprint for transforming fragmented frameworks into a trustworthy, inclusive, and scalable federated learning ecosystem.

Author: Hussein, O. A.; Ahmed, R. B.
Title: Blockchain-Based Digital Content Integrity Systems: A Comprehensive Review of Multi-Layered Security Approaches and Tamper Detection Mechanisms
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE 16th Symposium on Computer Applications & Industrial Electronics (ISCAIE)
Abstract Note: We provide a comprehensive review of blockchain technology applications, challenges, and trends facing the field of digital security and data integrity verification. We perform a systematic review of over 60 peer-reviewed papers written between 2008 and 2024 and classify blockchain applications in the following four key domains: Digital Content Integrity, Identity Management & Authentication, Secure Data Storage & Sharing, and Network Security & Intrusion Detection. Following our analysis conclusions, we reasoned that under controlled conditions, blockchain-based systems perform approximately 89%-100% accuracy in applications with multiple security objectives, but these systems had difficulties in scaling, processing overhead \(\textbackslash{}text{5 0 m s}-\textbackslash{}text{2 5 0 0 m s})\, energy consumption, and interoperability across platforms. We emphasize the significant gaps in our research, including quantum-resistant cryptography, real-time processing capabilities, privacy-preserving mechanisms, and universal format-agnostic solutions. We also provide a multi-level reference framework, which we propose to guide and inform system design in the future versus assuming readiness for deployment. This framework is used as a conceptual example for this architecture; the experimental demonstration is provided in the appendix. The experimental results are not intended to provide a benchmark comparison or an in-depth analysis of the current state quo but as a demonstration of the framework's promise in context. We provide future research directions for the incorporation of post-quantum cryptography, federated learning, optimization of edge computing, and standardized cross-chain protocols. This review serves as a foundational source for academics, practitioners, and policymakers in blockchain security, digital forensics, cybersecurity, and integrity verification.

Author: Samuel, J. J. Godson; Balasubramaniya, V.; Kumar, G. G.; Geetha, R.; Shobana, R.
Title: Insider Threat Detection System with Federated Learning and Differential Privacy
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Intelligent Computing, Networks, and Security (IC-ICNS)
Abstract Note: In today’s growing cybersecurity domain, the respresents Insider Threats as a challenge through subtle behavior anomalies which is often failed to be detected by traditional rule-based and statistical methods across all heterogenous enterprise data sources which also include user authentication logs, device telemetry and also file access transactions. These methods always struggle with temporal dependencies, relational context, and also privacy-preserving requirements for enabling multi-organization collaboration. The following paper presents a comprehensive framework for privacy-preserving Insider Threat Detection which is also integrating Graph Network Networks (GTN), Neural Temporal Point Processing (N-TPP), SimCLR, Federated Learning, and Differential Privacy. GTN technique captures all the dynamic user-device-file relationship patterns, N-TPP model capture the bursty sequences and SimCLR generates the robust self-supervised representations even from unlabeled logs. FL along with DP provides secure distributed training across all boundaries without raw sharing of data. EDL provides the undertainity-aware fusion which is calibrated with confidence scores, while SHAP and GNNExplainers offer the granular interpretability. On extensive evaluation on the CERT r4.2 and TWOS datasets which demonstrates almost 15.3% F1-score improvement, 42% false positives reduction and a superior cross-dataset with generalization compared to the 12 state-of-the-art baseline models.

Author: Hu, Y.; Wang, Z.; Xia, Y.; Xiong, H.; Fang, L.; Peng, C.; Wahaballa, A.; Qin, Z.; Qin, Z.
Title: Blockchain-Oriented Certificateless Threshold Signature With Identifiable Abort for Federated Learning in Digital Twin-Assisted IoV
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
Abstract Note: As a promising subdomain of intelligent transportation systems (ITS), Internet of Vehicles (IoV) can be empowered by digital twin (DT) technology for real-time traffic simulation and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven predictive analytics in evolutionary trend projection, demonstrating significant potential in dynamic transportation optimization. Among various machine learning paradigms, federated learning (FL) not only aligns well with IoV, but also provides it with privacy protection. Traditional FL faces single point of failure due to the existence of an aggregation center, so blockchain-based FL with multiple aggregators is utilized to mitigate this issue. Nevertheless, in such distributed environments, both aggregators and model parameters exposed to network are vulnerable to attacks, impeding the normal operation of FL. In this paper, for blockchain-enabled FL with multiple aggregators in IoV, we propose CLTSwNI&IA, the first non-interactive certificateless threshold signature with identifiable abort. This scheme eliminates certificate management and key escrow, adopts a blockchain-oriented approach by utilizing a fully distributed signing paradigm. Additionally, the proposed signing scheme is capable of identifying malicious FL aggregators during the entire process through distributed fine-grained verification and ensuring the integrity of aggregation results. Finally, theoretical and experimental comparisons with related literature demonstrate the advanced functionality and the acceptable efficiency of our approach.

Author: Nagaraju, G.; Kumar, A.
Title: Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning Techniques for Electronic Health Records: A Comprehensive Review
Publication Title: 2026 Contemporary Computing Innovations Conference (CCIC)
Abstract Note: The digitization of the healthcare system has been high and has, in turn, led to the extensive use of Electronic Health Records (EHRs), which have provided better clinical decisions, patient care, and medical research. However, privacy and security of EHR data are quite delicate, in particular, when using machine learning (ML) models, which require access to huge amounts of data. Privacy-preserving machine learning (PPML) is a new paradigm that can assist in addressing these problems, in which sensitive patient information is secure and valuable insights can be derived. This review consists of the description of the existing technologies in PPML of EHRs, including federated learning, differential privacy, homomorphic encryption, and secure multiparty computation. We look at their merits, weaknesses and the ways to incorporate them in real situations of health care. Besides, we highlight the following prominent points: scalability, computational overhead, trade-offs in the model accuracy and compliance with regulatory standards such as HIPAA and GDPR. Emerged trends, including blockchain-based privacy technologies and hybrid solutions, are also stated. By summarizing the existing trends, this paper will guide researchers and health care practitioners to adopt effective PPML practices that would guarantee a reasonable use of data and patient confidentiality, which in the long run will guarantee the establishment of safe and trustful AI-based healthcare models.

Author: Wang, Z.; Noor, R. Md; Sadakane, K.; Kiah, M. L. Mat
Title: Blockchain Intelligence-Based Trust Management System for Internet of Vehicles
Publication Title: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
Abstract Note: The Internet of Vehicles (IoV) extends automotive systems through vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication, creating a collaborative ecosystem to enhance transportation efficiency and road safety. However, the decentralized and open vehicular network is vulnerable to internal malicious participants that disseminate falsified messages or refuse to contribute local resources. While blockchain (BC) and artificial intelligence (AI) have been extensively employed in trust management systems (TMSs), existing solutions lack cross-feature correlation analysis, continuous learning capabilities for emerging threats, and efficient BC consensus mechanisms. This article proposes a novel BC intelligence (BI)-based TMS (BIT) to address these critical challenges. Specifically, BIT establishes a multidimensional feature set based on interfeature physical consistency to empower a deep learning (DL)-based trust evaluation (TE) model, enhancing detection robustness in high-adversary contexts. Furthermore, a trust-driven BC-based federated learning (BFL) framework is designed to facilitate the continuous learning of the TE model using newly collected vehicular data. Local model contributions are subsequently quantified to determine node rewards or penalties by evaluating model quality, training efficiency, and historical reliability. Finally, trust scores and model weights are secured on a consortium BC via an efficient proof-of-model-contribution (PoMC) consensus, which repurposes local training efforts to improve throughput and reduce latency. Simulation results demonstrate that BIT sustainably learns from emerging attack patterns, achieves superior detection accuracy in high-density adversarial scenarios, and maintains secure and efficient storage, outperforming state-of-the-art TMSs.
