Author: Ma, J.; Liu, X.; Li, C.; Xu, H.; Li, K.
Title: FedShard: A Sharding-Based Federated Learning Framework With Layered Incentivization for IoT
Publication Title: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
Abstract Note: The blockchain-based federated learning framework has garnered widespread attention to ensure data privacy and trustworthy computing in IoT devices. Improving the accuracy and scalability are paramount for the increasing demands of IoT tasks. However, existing solutions, such as SIFL and ChainFL, utilize traditional single-chain architecture and fixed models, which exhibit limitations in terms of model generalizability and scalability. To overcome the above problems, this article proposes FedShard, an FL framework that integrates a layered dual-track incentive mechanism and a privacy knowledge distillation module. When implementing FedShard, we address two technical challenges: 1) to ensure efficient training among the numerous clients in the sharding architecture, we propose a layered dual-track incentive mechanism that provides both long- and short-term rewards; and 2) to enhance the framework’s convergence and privacy in sharding-based FL, we design a knowledge distillation module that incorporates local differential privacy (LDP). Furthermore, we propose a bucket-based hash ring to manage clients, enabling the framework to adapt to dynamic network environments. To validate the framework’s generalizability and scalability, we implement FedShard on a 48-core high-performance server using Fabric to conduct both on-chain and off-chain experiments. Our comprehensive experiments, comparing FedShard with SIFL, PEFL, and ChainFL, reveal that our solution outperforms the state-of-the-art methods by achieving a notable 29% increase in accuracy and a 22% improvement in throughput.
Manual Tags: Federated learning; privacy protection; sharding blockchain; incentive mechanism

Author: Dong, S.; Hou, R.
Title: Privacy-Preserving Task Offloading Scheme Based on Blockchain Federated Learning in End-Edge-Cloud Computing Environments
Publication Title: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
Abstract Note: With the continuous advancement of Internet of Things (IoT) and mobile terminal technologies, the massive data generated by end devices poses new challenges for real-time processing in cloud computing. As a beneficial complement to cloud computing, edge computing has garnered significant attention due to its ability to provide low-latency services near the data source. However, user privacy data involved in the task offloading process faces leakage risks in open edge architectures, and existing solutions still lack synergy between privacy protection and computational efficiency. To address this, this article proposes a privacy-preserving task offloading scheme for end-edge-cloud architectures based on blockchain federated learning (FL). The main contributions are as follows: 1) constructing a collaborative computing architecture that integrates end devices, edge servers, and cloud centers; 2) proposing a privacy-preserving task offloading mechanism that integrates FL and blockchain technology, enabling distributed model training and secure auditing without sharing raw data; and 3) validating the superiority of the proposed scheme in terms of energy consumption, latency, and privacy protection level through simulation experiments. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed scheme significantly enhances user privacy protection while maintaining efficient task processing, providing a reliable technical approach for privacy-sensitive applications in edge computing environments.
Manual Tags: privacy protection; federated learning (FL); Edge computing; task offloading; end-edge-cloud architecture

Author: Cristiano, G. M.; D'Antonio, S.; Mazzeo, G.
Title: EigenFL: An EigenLayer-Restaked Blockchain Solution for Secure Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE 50th Annual Computers, Software, and Applications Conference (COMPSAC)
Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative model training while preserving data privacy by keeping data decentralized. However, traditional FL architectures suffer from critical trust issues, including vulnerability to model poisoning attacks, a lack of incentives for honest participation, and the inability to verify the quality of submitted model updates. Blockchain-based solutions have been proposed to address these challenges, but they often require participants to bootstrap independent validator networks and lock additional capital, limiting scalability and practical adoption. This paper proposes EigenFL, a novel FL framework secured through blockchain restaking, leveraging EigenLayer to provide cryptoeconomic security and decentralized validation by reusing Ethereum's existing validator infrastructure. Participants are economically incentivized to submit honest updates, while malicious behavior is discouraged through slashing mechanisms. Model updates are validated off-chain by independent operators, and their outcomes are immutably recorded on-chain, ensuring accountability and robustness. EigenFL demonstrates how blockchain restaking can transform FL from a trust-based paradigm into a cryptoeconomically secured framework, enabling verifiable and decentralized training.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; Federated Learning; Model Poisoning; EigenLayer

Author: G, K.; A, N. M.
Title: TransLLM-H: A Hybrid Federated–Decentralized Post-Quantum Framework for Semantic Trust in 6G Vehicular Networks
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Recent Advances in Electrical, Electronics, Ubiquitous Communication, and Computational Intelligence (RAEEUCCI)
Abstract Note: Future 6G vehicular networks require scalable and trustworthy distributed intelligence under adversarial environments. Existing federated learning and blockchain-based approaches remain vulnerable to Byzantine manipulation and lack quantum-resilient trust mechanisms. This paper proposes TransLLM-H, a hybrid federated–decentralized framework integrating trust-weighted aggregation, post-quantum blockchain authentication, and large language model (LLM)-driven semantic validation. A formal adversarial model satisfying the robustness constraint \f<\textbackslash{}frac{N}{2}\ ensures consistency between theoretical guarantees and practical deployment. Experimental evaluation across 30 independent simulation runs demonstrates statistically significant improvements \p<0.05\, achieving 52% reduction in aggregation latency and 31% improvement in semantic trust accuracy compared with representative baselines. Results further show stable performance under adversarial participation up to 50% malicious nodes, indicating the effectiveness of TransLLM-H for secure and scalable trust-aware learning in 6G vehicular systems.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; Federated Learning; Post-Quantum Cryptography; Large Language Models; 6G Vehicular Networks; Semantic Trust

Author: Murugadoss, R.; Z, A. W.; S, A.; R, A. B.
Title: Securing the Internet of Things: A Byzantine-Resilient Approach to Mitigating Real-Time Cyber Attacks
Publication Title: 2026 2nd International Conference on Intelligent Systems and Computational Networks (ICISCN)
Abstract Note: The rapid expansion of Internet of Things (IoT) networks has significantly increased the vulnerability of distributed systems to cyber attacks. Traditional centralized intrusion detection systems suffer from scalability limitations, privacy risks, and single points of failure when processing large volumes of network data. Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as a promising approach for distributed model training without sharing raw data, thereby preserving data privacy. However, FL systems remain vulnerable to Byzantine attacks in which malicious clients send poisoned model updates that degrade the global model. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a Zero-Trust Agentic Federated Learning (ZTA-FL) framework that integrates trust-score validation, curriculum-based feature blending, and Trusted Platform Module (TPM) attestation to detect malicious updates during the aggregation process. Experiments conducted using the NSL-KDD intrusion detection dataset under a simulated federated environment with 30% malicious clients demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves 97.8 % global accuracy and 98.4 % detection rate, outperforming baseline methods such as FedAvg and median filtering.
Manual Tags: federated learning; intrusion detection; internet of things; byzantine resilience; zero-trust security; curriculum learning

Author: Mallampati, S. B.; Kumar, M. Satish; Medishetti, S. K.; Reddy, T. Krishna; Veerababu, Y.; Kumar, S. A.
Title: Enhancing IoT Security through Blockchain-Assisted Federated Learning and Adam-based Metaheuristic Optimization
Publication Title: 2026 4th International Conference on Inventive Computing and Informatics (ICICI)
Abstract Note: The large-scale adoption of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has made security a challenge more so because centralized systems of intrusion detection are prone to privacy leaks, have high latency, and cannot be scaled. In order to overcome these challenges, this paper will present a scalable and secure federated learning model of intrusion detection using Blockchain-Assisted Federated Learning (BAFL) with a new metaheuristic optimization strategy, Adam Gradient Descent Optimizer (AGDO). The proposed model works based on federated learning to facilitate the distributed training of the IoT nodes and maintain data privacy and blockchain technology can provide a secure, tamper-free update to the model. AGDO increases the convergence speed and efficiency of models optimization. The NSL-KDD dataset is used to evaluate the model and is implemented in the NS-3 simulator, and its performance is compared with that of Random Forest (RF), Honey Badger Algorithm (HBA) and Attention-based BiLSTM (Att-BiLSTM) models. The experimental findings indicate that the proposed BAFL-AGDO model has large gains, namely, a 28.6% decrease in response time, 24.3% reduction in memory overhead, 31.8% higher scalability, and 29.5% higher throughput than typical methods. It has been improved through efficient decentralized learning, parameter tuning through AGDO and secure coordination through blockchain. The results validate that the proposed solution not only enhances intrusion detection precision and system obtainability but also offers a strong, expandable, and privacy-capable construction to subsequent generation IoT conditions.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; Internet of Things (IoT); Federated Learning; Intrusion Detection; Adam Gradient Descent; Network Security Laboratory(NSL)-Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining (KDD)

Author: Kayikci, S.; Khoshgoftaar, T. M.
Title: PoS-FedFraud: A Robust Proof-of-Stake Framework for Decentralized Financial Fraud Detection in Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2026 8th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative model training across decentralized data silos without raw data exchange, making it particularly attractive for privacy-sensitive domains like financial fraud detection. However, FL introduces critical vulnerabilities, notably the poisoning of global models through malicious client updates. Traditional defense mechanisms often rely on computationally expensive aggregation rules or complex anomaly detection. This paper introduces PoSFedFraud, a robust framework that integrates a Proof-of-Stake (PoS) economic layer directly into the federated aggregation process for financial fraud detection. By combining staking mechanisms with a dynamic reputation system, PoS-FedFraud economically disincentivizes adversarial behavior through automatic slashing and trust decay. We simulate a toy fraud detection scenario using a 29-dimensional feature space, demonstrating how the framework defends against norm-based gradient poisoning attacks. Our experimental results show that PoS-FedFraud successfully identifies and penalizes malicious actors—reducing their stake and trust upon detection—while maintaining global model convergence. The proposed method offers an incentive-compatible punitive layer that complements existing robust aggregation and anomaly-detection techniques for decentralized financial applications.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; Federated Learning; Proof-of-Stake

Author: Mughal, M. I. Younas; Sodhro, A. Hassan; Djebbar, F.; Pirbhulal, S.
Title: Blockchain-Assisted Decentralized Federated Learning for Trustworthy Edge-IoT Systems
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE 103rd Vehicular Technology Conference (VTC2026-Spring)
Abstract Note: Federated learning enables collaborative model training across distributed edge-IoT devices without sharing raw data, but most practical deployments still rely on centralized coordination, which introduces strong trust assumptions, limited auditability, and single points of failure. This paper investigates whether blockchain-based decentralized coordination can support federated learning in edge-IoT systems with acceptable learning performance and coordination overhead. We propose a lightweight coordination framework in which a permissioned blockchain and smart contracts are used to manage client registration, round coordination, and auditable participation, while model aggregation is performed off-chain. An experimental evaluation is conducted using an edge-IoT time-series workload under both normal and unauthorized participation scenarios. The results show that blockchain-assisted coordination preserves stable learning convergence and introduces only a modest increase in coordination latency and communication overhead, while enabling verifiable participation and transparent training records. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of employing blockchain as a practical coordination and trust layer for federated learning in edge-IoT environments.
Manual Tags: Federated learning; blockchain; Internet of Things; smart contracts; edge computing; auditability; decentralized coordination; trustworthy learning

Author: Alvarenga, L. F.; Ferreira, N. F.; Peres, A. S. C.; Moioli, R. C.; Rennó-Costa, C.
Title: Legal and Ethical Considerations for Translating Federated Learning Into Cross-Border Healthcare Innovation
Publication Title: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) offers a privacy-enhancing architecture for training artificial intelligence on decentralized healthcare data, yet the prevailing mantra to “move the model, not the data” obscures significant privacy risks, ethical dilemmas, and regulatory conflicts. This article challenges the assumption that FL inherently solves cross-border compliance by analyzing a hypothetical consortium involving the United States, the U.K., EU, China, and Brazil. We identify a specific compliance deadlock arising from the friction between Western rights-based frameworks (HIPAA, GDPR, LGPD) and state-centric security models (China's PIPL/DSL), particularly regarding model inversion attacks and data localization. Moving beyond validatory analysis, we propose a multi-layered Federated Governance Framework to operationalize data diplomacy. This contribution introduces novel legal and structural mechanisms: the Federated Data Sharing & Use Agreement (F-DSA) to codify binding mandates like privacy-enhancing technologies and isolated training; Governance as a Service (GaaS) to neutralize conflicts of interest through third-party administration; and relational mechanisms, including blockchain-based dynamic consent to solve the cascade of consent problem. This framework provides a blueprint for converting theoretical FL potential into a legally compliant, ethically sound, and functioning international Learning Health System (LHS).
Manual Tags: data governance; trustworthy AI; Algorithmic accountability; cross-border data transfer; privacy-enhancing technologies (PETs)

Author: Li, Z.; Chen, X.; Sun, Q.; Lu, Y.; Li, D.; Zhang, J.; Ai, B.
Title: Trustworthy Federated Learning With Authenticated ZKPs in Mobile Edge Intelligence
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing
Abstract Note: Privacy disclosure from model parameters and malicious attacks are critical issues in federated learning (FL). Existing research has yet to effectively address the simultaneous need for efficient communication design, privacy protection, and attack detection, which impedes the widespread adoption of FL in mobile edge networks over 6G wireless communication. In this paper, we propose a trustworthy FL framework that can ensure privacy, robustness, accountability, fairness, and explainability in mobile edge networks. Specifically, we integrate authenticated zero-knowledge proofs (ZKPs) and Pedersen commitments into the FL process. Despite the lack of direct access between servers and mobile devices, the servers can still identify trustworthy clients for specific tasks. Clients can verify the authenticity of the received global model based on the provided proofs and commitments. Furthermore, we leverage Ethereum to act as the verifier and authenticator of models. This verification and authentication process enables the servers to detect abnormal local models and perform trust-based aggregations. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed trustworthy FL framework significantly improves the global model's in terms of accuracy, convergence rate, and security.
Manual Tags: trustworthy federated learning; authenticated zero knowledge proofs; Mobile edge networks; Pedersen commitments

Author: Abdelhady, G.; Ghandoura, A.; Motwakel, A.; Alajmi, A.
Title: Hybrid Machine Learning Anomaly Detection and Lightweight Zero Trust Authentication for LoRaWAN Networks
Publication Title: IEEE Access
Abstract Note: LoRaWAN has become one of the most widely adopted LPWAN technologies, but its large-scale use has also exposed several persistent security weaknesses. Recent studies show that unprotected LoRaWAN links are still vulnerable to basic attacks such as eavesdropping (67% success rate) and replay attempts (about 43%), which highlights the need for more practical and adaptive security solutions suitable for low-power devices. In this work, we develop a security framework that combines a hybrid machine-learning model for anomaly detection with a lightweight Zero Trust authentication mechanism. The anomaly detection module merges a tuned LightGBM classifier with an autoencoder-based unsupervised detector. Across multiple attack categories, the combined model achieved an average detection accuracy of 95% and an AUC-ROC of 0.973 while keeping the memory footprint small enough for LoRa-class devices. We also design a Zero Trust authentication scheme based on an optimized Proof-of-Authority blockchain model and a low-cost mutual authentication protocol. The evaluation shows an average authentication delay of about 187 ms and system availability above 99.9%. Although the full framework introduces an energy overhead of approximately 18%, the projected device lifetime remains more than seven years, which is significantly longer than what existing blockchain-based IoT authentication systems provide.
Manual Tags: IoT security; zero trust architecture; blockchain authentication; LoRaWAN security; LPWAN networks; machine learning anomaly detection

Author: K, S. S.; Butola, S. S.; B, S.; T, N. S.; Nixon, J. S.; Salotagi, S.
Title: A Decentralized Blockchain-Anchored Federated Learning Framework for Real-Time Verification of Crisis-Related Social Media Content
Publication Title: 2026 7th International Conference on Smart Systems and Inventive Technology (ICSSIT)
Abstract Note: During humanitarian crises, natural disasters, and public emergencies, social media platforms serve as vital real-time information sources. However, they are also prone to the rapid propagation of misinformation, rumors, and malicious content. Traditional centralized verification systems present severe limitations, including single points of failure, algorithmic bias, censorship concerns, and data privacy issues. To address these vulnerabilities, this paper proposes DeFL-Crisis, a decentralized, blockchain-anchored federated learning framework designed for real-time verification of crisis-related social media content. DeFL-Crisis utilizes federated learning to allow edge client nodes (e.g., local emergency management centers, news agencies, and academic scrapers) to collaboratively train robust misinformation detection models on local data without sharing raw text, thus preserving user privacy. To secure the federated learning process against Byzantine model-poisoning and data-poisoning attacks, we anchor the model aggregation within a consortium blockchain ledger governed by a consensus-driven verification protocol. We implement a Proof-of-Accuracy (PoAC) consensus mechanism and smart-contract-based validation that evaluates client model updates against isolated, validated local validation sets, dynamically computing client reputation scores. Experimental evaluations using simulated benchmarks modeled after CrisisLexT26 and PHEME datasets show that DeFL-Crisis achieves a global verification accuracy of 94.2%, which is within 1.3% of the centralized training upper bound. Under hostile scenarios where 40% of clients perform aggressive model-poisoning attacks, DeFL-Crisis preserves high classification performance (F1-score of 0.88), whereas standard federated learning collapses to an F1-score of 0.45. Furthermore, we demonstrate that blockchain transaction latency is scalable (under 50 seconds for up to 50 active scaling nodes) and smart contract gas costs are highly optimized, indicating the realworld viability of our framework.
Manual Tags: Federated learning; blockchain; Privacy; Byzantine robustness; crisis informatics; misinformation verification; Proof-of-Accuracy; Reputation Score Update process

Author: Qiqieh, I.; Alzubi, J. A.; Alzubi, O. A.; Khawaja, Y.; Singh, A.
Title: Securing Next-Generation Connected Healthcare: A Privacy-Preserving Explainable AI Framework for Consumer Electronics
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Consumer Electronics
Abstract Note: Connected healthcare systems increasingly rely on consumer electronics, raising critical challenges related to data privacy, trust, and explainability. Existing solutions typically address privacy, decentralization, or explainability in isolation, limiting their suitability for resource-constrained, real-world deployments. This paper proposes SHIELD-XCE (Secure, HIghly Explainable, Lightweight & Decentralized AI for Consumer Electronics), a unified security and explainable AI framework for next-generation connected healthcare. SHIELD-XCE integrates Federated Learning (FL) with differential privacy, blockchain-based auditability, and C-TRACE (Causal, TRAnsportable, Certified Explanations), a causal explainability mechanism providing counterfactual, stable, and privacy-compliant explanations. Experimental results demonstrate a strong privacy–utility balance, achieving up to 93.8% accuracy, AUROC of 0.970, low per-round latency ( \textbackslash{}approx 350\ ms), and energy consumption below 1 J per round on consumer devices. These results confirm that secure, explainable, and efficient AI can be practically deployed in consumer electronics–driven healthcare environments.
Manual Tags: blockchain; federated learning; differential privacy; consumer electronics; Connected Secure healthcare; explainable artificial intelligence (XAI); resource-constrained devices

Author: Chennupati, N. N.; Koneti, L.
Title: An Integrated AI and Blockchain-based Cybersecurity Framework for Smart Cities IoT Infrastructure
Publication Title: 2026 6th International Conference on Inventive Computation and Information Technologies (ICICIT)
Abstract Note: The integration of IoT into smart cities exposes serious cyber security risks, which old centralized designs would fail to combat. In this paper, the model suggests a unified system that would use AI and block chain technology to protect smart city IoT systems. A lightweight hybrid CNN-LSTM model is used to detect anomalies in real-time at the edge nodes and federated learning with differential privacy can be used to train collaboratively without exposing raw data. Permissioned block chain layer provides tamper-proof records and decentralized management of trust. A query fragment caching algorithm is a resource-optimal query strategy to block chain queries. CIC-IDS2017 and BoT-IoT datasets analysis show 98.6% detection, 97.5% F1-score, 134.6 ms latency, and 2,615 transactions-per-second, and 41% less energy usage than un cached block chain access. The framework is more effective than the current methods in all measures.

Author: Wang, G.; Nixon, M.
Title: DI3: Decentralized Intelligent Internet Infrastructure Integrating AI and Blockchain Technologies
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Computing, Networking and Communications (ICNC)
Abstract Note: Current distributed systems face fundamental limitations preventing effective integration of artificial intelligence with blockchain technologies. Existing architectures cannot simultaneously provide decentralized consensus, privacy-preserving collaborative intelligence, and trustless cross-chain coordination-properties essential for decentralized intelligent applications. This paper presents the Decentralized Intelligent Internet Infrastructure (DI), an architectural framework systematically integrating distributed intelligence with blockchain. The DI { }^{\textbackslash{}mathbf{3}}\ architecture introduces four core innovations: adaptive Byzantine fault-tolerant consensus incorporating reinforcement learning for dynamic parameter optimization while maintaining formal safety and liveness guarantees, hierarchical federated learning with zero-knowledge proofs enabling privacypreserving collaborative intelligence through cryptographic verification of gradient computation, trust-minimized cross-chain protocols eliminating centralized validators through recursive zero-knowledge proofs and economic security mechanisms, and intelligent resource orchestration leveraging predictive models for autonomous optimization. We provide formal specifications for each component and establish security properties under well-defined threat models. The framework demonstrates how artificial intelligence and blockchain can be synergistically integrated rather than merely coexisting, establishing theoretical foundations for decentralized infrastructure supporting applications requiring simultaneous guarantees of privacy, fault-tolerant consensus, and cross-chain atomicity-properties unattainable in current systems.
Manual Tags: AI; Decentralized Internet; Decentralized Network; Future Blockchain Architecture; Infrastructure

Author: C, S.; R, G.; N, M. I.; T, G.; Tamilamuthan, R.; Lakshmanan, M.
Title: Fed Block Charge: Secure Federated Learning for Solar EV Charging Optimization
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Secure IoT and Cybersecurity (ICOSICS)
Abstract Note: The boom in electric vehicles (EVs) and smart transport systems has resulted in a bigger desire for harmonious, smart, and sustainable charging infrastructures. The traditional centralized EV charging models have been found to cause communication overhead, result in violation of privacy, increase dependence on the grid, and cause an inefficient management of renewable energy. In fact, previous models have provided only little or no support in their entirety to distributed learning, secure communication or adaptive charging optimization in a broad smart transport environment. This article put forward a federated learning-based Solar EV Charging Optimization Framework for security through a robust blockchain-enabled smart energy management developed using MATLAB/Simulink. This proposed framework consists of an integration of solar photovoltaic (PV) systems, battery energy storage units, federated learning-based distributed optimization, adaptive control of charging, and secure communication through blockchains, which forms a one-charging entity. By using federated learning, multiple charging stations may collectively train smart-charge models without necessarily sharing raw user data, thus preserving privacy and achieving higher communication efficiency. Simulation results reveal that the proposed framework had made the utilization of renewable energy go close to 94%, had prediction accuracy of 97% for federated learning, and was dependent on grid power reduced by about 41% compared to conventional charging systems. Furthermore, a safer form of communication efficiency has been introduced by almost 95% in sharp reduction of charging delay by up to 35%, thus preparing it for future application in intelligent and sustainable smart transportation infrastructure.
Manual Tags: Federated Learning; Blockchain Security; Intelligent Transportation System; Battery Energy Storage System; Electric Vehicle (EV); Renewable Energy Management; Smart Charging Infrastructure; Solar Photovoltaic System

Author: Prasad, G. B.; Rao, M. V.
Title: PABFL: Secure and Privacy-Aware Framework for Electronic Health Record Sharing in IoMT
Publication Title: 2026 9th International Conference on Computing Methodologies and Communication (ICCMC)
Abstract Note: The fast development of Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) devices has also compounded the necessity to have secure, privacy-sensitive, and efficient Electronic Health Record (EHR) sharing mechanisms. To overcome the fundamental issues associated with the IoMT ecosystems of data privacy leakage, excessive communication overhead, and inefficient decentralized learning, this paper suggests a Privacy-Aware Blockchain and Federated Learning (PABFL) system. The suggested framework combines a blockchain-based secure data sharing with federated learning-based distributed model training, which guarantees data confidentiality and integrity without the centralized storage. It is tested with NVIDIA Jetson AGX Xavier nodes, which have CUDA 11.4 acceleration and is tested on both CardioFit and GlucoWatch datasets. Through experiments, it is shown that PABFL greatly outperforms more traditional methods like Federated Averaging (FedAvg), Federated Proximal (FedProx), and Asynchronous Advantage Actor-Critic (A3C) with an accuracy difference of 6.8%-9.5%, energy consumption of 18.2%-24.7%, training time of 21.4%-29.3% These improvements are explained by optimized model aggregation, safe lightweight blockchain operations, and resource-efficient edge device utilization. The suggested framework provides high-quality, scalable, and privacy-friendly EHR sharing that is very appropriate in real-time healthcare applications in IoMT settings and helps to develop safe and smart digital healthcare systems.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; Federated Learning; IoMT; Electronic Health Record; NVIDIA; Privacy-Aware

Author: Khan, S. A.; Khan, F. A.; Ravichandran, R.
Title: Protecting Healthcare Networks from Cyber Threats: How to Use AI and Blockchain to Enable Safe Patient Data Exchange
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Data Science, Agents and Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
Abstract Note: Healthcare digitisation has accelerated in response to rising cybersecurity threats, large-scale data breaches, and heightened privacy concerns during and after the COVID-19 era. Despite the adoption of centralised authentication, encryption, and other conventional safeguards, healthcare systems continue to face persistent risks, including ransomware, insider threats, and phishing attacks. This has motivated the shift toward decentralised, intelligent security architectures built on artificial intelligence and blockchain technologies. AI-enabled threat-detection systems use machine-learning algorithms to identify and mitigate cyber risks in real time. Comparative evaluations of Support Vector Machines (SVM), Random Forest, XGBoost, and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks show that deep-learning approaches-particularly LSTM-significantly outperform traditional methods in detecting complex malware patterns. Blockchain-based security architectures further enhance protection by ensuring data integrity, enabling secure access control, and establishing decentralised trust across private, public, and hybrid blockchain environments. Federated learning adds another layer of privacy preservation by allowing AI models to be trained on distributed healthcare datasets without requiring direct access to sensitive patient information. Experimental results demonstrate that hybrid AI-blockchain frameworks achieve over \98 \textbackslash{}%\ accuracy in identifying cyber threats while substantially reducing attack vectors and unauthorised-access incidents. Several challenges remain before widespread adoption is feasible. Blockchain scalability, AI computation overhead, and regulatory compliance issues must be addressed-particularly in sectors such as the healthcare supply chain, where operational constraints are strict. Future work may focus on optimising AI algorithms for real-time monitoring, integrating quantum-resistant cryptography to prepare for emerging threats, and improving interoperability across heterogeneous blockchain platforms.
Manual Tags: Federated Learning; Intrusion Detection; Smart Healthcare; Privacy-Preserving AI; Secure Data Exchange; Decentralised Security; Healthcare Networks; Patient Data Privacy; Ransomware Mitigation

Author: Kumar, V. N.; Tiwari, R.; Jyothi, E.; Parimala, S.; Poojitha, S. A.
Title: Federated Learning Protocol for Collaborative Model Training in Distributed Industrial Networks
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICACT)
Abstract Note: Contemporary industrial systems operate as interconnected networks of machines, sensors, and control systems to produce large volumes of real-time data, which are essential for proactive maintenance, fault detection, and optimisation of their processes. Nevertheless, the vast majority of industries continue to be based on centralised models of AI training that may presuppose the consolidation of such sensitive data at one point, making it highly challenging in terms of data privacy, cybersecurity, requirements, and timeliness of communication. The inefficiency of exchanging industrial information between different locations is a common cause that creates fragmented intelligence, decreased model updating speed, and reduced overall effectiveness. To address such restrictions, this paper proposes the FLIND Federated Learning Integrated Network for Distributed Industries. This new protocol enables multiple industrial units to jointly train a standard AI model without sharing raw data. FLIND proposes a Reputation-Aware Gradient Consensus Mechanism (RAGCM) that provides a dynamic assessment of the trustworthiness of each node’s individual contribution, ensuring model aggregation is trusted and resistant to malicious updates and data leaks. It also incorporates blockchain validation to enhance transparency and flexibility in communication scheduling, helping to de-jitter the network during model synchronisation. The FLIND collaborative model training enables safe, effective, and private learning across diverse settings and industries by integrating federated learning, blockchain security, and efficient control of intelligent communication. Simulation findings indicate that FLIND increases model accuracy, precision, and recall by a margin of almost 10 per cent over conventional federated learning algorithms, with reduced latency and overall data confidentiality. The new framework is highly effective in remodelling AI partnerships in industrial contexts by making knowledge sharing between factories trustworthy, scalable, and in real-time, which is discussed as a platform of secure and innovative Industry 4.0 environments of the next generation.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; Federated Learning; Industry 4.0; Secure Model Aggregation; Industrial IoT; Data Privacy; Distributed Intelligence; Decentralised AI; FLIND; Reputation-Aware Gradient Consensus Mechanism (RAGCM)

Author: Narkedimilli, S.; Makam, S.; Dewangan, N. K.; Kulkarni, S.; Munjandira, C.
Title: FAPL-DM-BC: Adaptive Privacy-Aware, Blockchain-Backed FL Framework with Dual-Model XAI for the IoVs
Publication Title: 2026 18th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
Abstract Note: The rapid growth of the Internet of Vehicles (IoV) raises critical privacy, security, and scalability challenges that existing centralized and federated learning solutions fail to address fully. To overcome these issues, we propose FAPL-DM-BC. This blockchain-backed federated framework integrates Federated Adaptive Privacy-Aware Learning (FAPL), Dynamic Masking (DM), secure aggregation with FedAvg and SMPC, and a dualmodel explainable AI (XAI) feedback loop. Experiments on the CIC-IoV-2024 dataset show that FAPL-DM-BC achieves strong detection performance (precision 0.92, recall 0.94, F1-score 0.93, accuracy 93.1%) with low latency (42 ms), efficient throughput (208 samples/s), and lightweight resource consumption while resisting a broad range of IoV attacks. This demonstrates that FAPL-DM-BC delivers a scalable, interpretable, and privacy-preserving solution for real-time vehicular networks, enabling safer autonomous driving, resilient traffic management, and secure smart-city integration.

Author: Masendu, H. S.; Pandey, J.; Chiwariro, R.; Simango, D.
Title: A Hybrid Machine Learning Platform for Securing Edge Computing Environments: A Review
Publication Title: 2026 5th MEC International Conference on Advanced Data Analytics and Artificial Intelligence for Sustainable Smart Cities (ICADAAI)
Abstract Note: In distributed environments, edge computing has become essential for processing time-sensitive data, especially for fifth-generation cellular networks, the Internet of Things, and industrial applications. Data privacy violations, sophisticated cyberattacks, and compromised detection systems are among the serious security issues that distributed resource-constrained edge computing must address. This review looks at hybrid learning techniques that combine cryptography methods, detection paradigms, and confidence mechanisms reported in 28 prior research studies. It focuses on dual-discriminator frameworks based on generative adversarial networks and meta-learning systems that are integrated with blockchain. The findings demonstrate that hybrid machine learning reduces false positive rates from approximately 5.2 percent to 1.3 percent (approximately 75 percent reduction) using game-theoretic trust evaluation, achieves 96 to 97.77 percent accuracy in anomaly detection, and reduces communication overhead by 42 to 53 percent. The authors pinpoint eight crucial gaps, such as blockchain scalability, adversarial robustness flaws, and energy limitations. The review proposes a Unified Trusted Hybrid Learning (UTHL) framework integrating GAN-based detection, Meta AdaBoost ensemble, Stackelberg trust games, blockchain verification, federated learning, and explainable artificial intelligence. It also offers a deployment roadmap for production edge environments in the telecommunications sector, smart cities, industrial manufacturing, healthcare, and blockchain applications.

Author: Wang, B.; Xu, X.
Title: DVFL-CPN: A Decentralized and Verifiable Federated Learning Approach for Computing Power Network
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Networking
Abstract Note: The computing power network (CPN) interconnects dispersed heterogeneous computing nodes through a network and achieve rational allocation and efficient utilization of computing power through unified algorithms. Meanwhile, with its decentralized nature, it serves as an ideal platform for decentralized federated learning. However, the mutual distrust among computing providers, computing users, and between computing providers and computing users leads to untrustworthy models in federated learning, and decentralized federated learning also suffers from privacy issues such as data leakage, hindering its application in CPN. Therefore, to address the aforementioned problems, we propose a decentralized and verifiable federated learning approach for computing power network, termed DVFL-CPN. Specifically, we first propose a single-masking encryption algorithm based on pseudorandom numbers, primarily to protect the local models trained by each computing node. Then, we pro- pose a verification algorithm based on homomorphic hashing to verify the aggregated results of computing nodes. Subsequently, we propose a robust aggregation algorithm, enabling online nodes to complete model aggregation and decryption even when some computing nodes go offline. We also deploy a blockchain to record the operation results of each node. Finally, we conduct experiments on real-world datasets. Compared to state-of-the-art decentralized and verifiable federated learning methods, our method achieves a 13.5% improvement in accuracy and demonstrates robustness against offline nodes. Additionally, our method outperforms existing methods in terms of computational efficiency and communication efficiency by approximately {3\textbackslash{}times 1}{0}^{4}\ and {1.6\textbackslash{}times 1}{0}^{5}\ times, respectively.
Manual Tags: decentralized federated learning; verifiable federated learning; privacy preserving; Computing power network

Author: Li, C.; Shen, Y.; Xie, M.; Su, Z.; Wang, Y.; Zhang, C.; Zhu, L.
Title: Fed-CBE: Client-Side Backdoor Elimination in Federated Learning via Persistent Parameter Disruption
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security
Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) inherently preserves privacy but remains highly vulnerable to backdoor attacks due to its open participation architecture. Existing defenses face two fundamental limitations: first, screening-based aggregation strategies prove ineffective against advanced cross-round attacks where adversaries progressively poison model parameters through multi-round collaboration; second, mitigation techniques often cause significant accuracy degradation due to the deep entanglement between backdoor and primary task parameters. To address these challenges, we propose Fed-CBE, a novel client-side defense algorithm that eliminates backdoors through three synergistic mechanisms: 1) periodic alternating layer resetting disrupts deep parameters to dismantle cross-round backdoor accumulation; 2) indiscriminate forgetting employs entropy maximization on non-ground-truth classes to decouple backdoor associations without prior trigger knowledge; and 3) knowledge distillation with historical local models restores primary task performance. Extensive evaluations on three benchmark datasets and model architectures demonstrate that Fed-CBE achieves highly competitive robustness, limiting attack success rates to near-zero levels in most settings and keeping them exceptionally low even under high malicious-client ratios without compromising primary task performance, significantly outperforming existing defenses.
Manual Tags: Federated learning; knowledge distillation; robustness; backdoor defense; client-side defense

Author: Bandrevu, M. S.; Patkar, P.; Kola, J. N.
Title: Trustworthy AI Models for Secure Data Processing Environments
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Natural Language Processing and Computer Vision (ICNPCV)
Abstract Note: As AI becomes a sophisticated power tool in the data-driven world, it has enhanced the efficiency of automated decision-making in Healthcare, Finance, Cybersecurity, Cloud Computing, and Smart Manufacturing. As the complexity of AI models grows, however, issues of trustworthiness have become paramount, such as vulnerabilities, lack of transparency, fairness, privacy protection, and robustness to adversarial attacks. These constraints hinder the application of AI in secure data management scenarios where data integrity, confidentiality, and accountability are crucial. This paper introduces a Trustworthy AI Framework for Secure Data Processing Environments (TAF-SDPE) that is designed to be integrated with a seamless architecture in the context of secure data preprocessing, privacy-preserving feature engineering, explainable learning mechanisms, adversarial robustness, fairness-aware optimization, and continuous trust evaluation. It ensures reliable and transparent AI-driven decision-making through encryption-assisted data protection, anomaly detection, interpretable deep learning, confidence-based prediction validation, and blockchain-enabled audit logging. A large number of experiments are conducted on benchmark cybersecurity and structured data repositories under different attack and operational scenarios. Three criteria are used - namely accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, robustness index, explainability score, fairness index, privacy preservation rate, and computational overhead - to evaluate the proposed model. The results of the experiments confirm that the proposed framework has an accuracy of 98.3%, F1 score of 97.9%, robustness score of 96.8%, explainability score of 95.6%, and preserves the privacy of the data while keeping the processing latency low, outperforming the conventional machine learning and deep learning methods. The results prove that the proposed system, comprising AI principles with trustworthy and secure data processing mechanisms, significantly improves the reliability, resilience, transparency and compliance of data processing models, which allows it to be used for the next generation of intelligent and security-critical data processing applications.

Author: Potluri, S.; Panigrahi, B. S.; Mohanty, S. N.; Albalawi, A.
Title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence With Cloud and Blockchain-as-a-Service Model for Consumer Electronics in Connected Healthcare
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Consumer Electronics
Abstract Note: Smart and connected wearables, Internet of Things-enabled devices, intelligent health equipment, and mobile applications are significant in connected healthcare by empowering smart and real-time patient monitoring, predictive and forecasting analytics, tailored and customized treatments. While these practices deliver valuable and substantial insights, constraints associated with security, privacy, scalability, availability, and transparency in artificial intelligence-based decision-making persist as considerable barriers to adoption in healthcare provision. To deal with these limitations, this research presents an explainable federated learning model combined with Cloud, Blockchain, explainable artificial intelligence, and optimization techniques to design secure, transparent, decentralized, and resilient-enabled healthcare. The cloud platform offers scalable and available data storage with low-latency real-time analytics. Blockchain guarantees decentralized, secured, tamper-proof block management and privacy-preserving access management. The proposed framework is a robust healthcare ecosystem and is a trio of cloud, blockchain, and explainable artificial intelligence with interpretable deep learning, a parallelized inference pipeline, data integrity, and compliance. The proposed system validates measurable enhancements, achieving 93% prediction accuracy, 30% enhanced interpretability, 25% lowered latency, and 40% higher data integrity, assessed relative to the existing intelligent healthcare systems. By integrating availability, explainability, privacy, security, latency, and scalability, this system provided a functional path for implementing transparent, secure, and connected healthcare ecosystems driven by consumer electronics.

Author: Satyanarayana, P.; Mohan, D.; Matta, P. R.; M, A.; Rao, G. V. S. P.; Krishnan, V. G.
Title: Secure Artificial Intelligence Systems for Edge-IoT Environments Using Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2026 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Engineering and Medical Sciences (ICETEMS)
Abstract Note: The fast pace of the Internet of Things (IoT) equipments and edge computing technologies has hastened the realization of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in decentralized settings. Nevertheless, edge integration poses a considerable threat to security, privacy, and data integrity, as a result of distributed sources of data, constrained execution capabilities, and possible adversarial risks. To overcome these challenges, this paper suggests a Secure Federated Learning (SFL) architecture to Edge-IoT environments, which will allow training AI models without exchanging raw data across devices. The designed framework contains a multi-layer encryption algorithm, differential privacy, and trust validation based on blockchain to have a secure model aggregation and communication between central servers and the edge nodes. Furthermore, an adaptive anomaly detection module is also incorporated in order to detect and counter attempts of poisoning and inference attack in the training process. Through experimental analysis, it is proven that the proposed SFL framework is better than the current algorithms like FedAvg and FLTrust in accuracy of the model used, attack detection rate, and its communication efficiency. In particular, the SFL model attains a 12-18 percent accuracy and 12-18 percent security robustness improvement on non-IID data conditions, and also, the communication cost is lower among distributed edge nodes. The findings prove that the suggested framework can increase data privacy, computational resilience, and trust in federated AI systems of large-scale Edge-IoT networks.

Author: Yoon, J.; Heo, G.; Doh, I.
Title: Scalable and Secure Framework for Federated Learning in IoV Applying Committee-based Chained Hotstuff
Publication Title: 2026 28th International Conference on Advanced Communications Technology (ICACT)
Abstract Note: Applying Federated Learning (FL) in the Internet of Vehicles (IoV) presents a critical trade-off between privacy, security, and performance, which conventional blockchains fail to address due to prohibitive latency and overhead. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel framework featuring a stack-based verification engine for deterministic validation, an on-chain management system for conditional privacy, and a Committee-based Chained HotStuff (C-CHS) consensus algorithm. The C-CHS protocol fundamentally resolves the leader bottleneck by enabling parallel block preparation. Our evaluation demonstrates substantial performance gains: C-CHS increases throughput by up to \textbackslash{}mathbf{9 2 \textbackslash{}%}\ (vs. CHS) and \textbackslash{}mathbf{8 7 3 \textbackslash{}%}\ (vs. PBFT), while reducing latency by up to 52 % and 90 %, respectively. These results validate our framework as a secure, scalable, and practical solution for deploying FL in large-scale IoV environments.

Author: Sahu, S.; Mallick, N.; Pattnayak, P.; Sethi, R. C.; Panda, P.; Mohanty, A.

This architecture, in a private first ecosystem, is a great way to create more value by deploying it in a scalable and cost-effective manner. Author: V, V.; D, S.; Alkabbji, R.; Kumar, S.; Samiappan, D.; Karthikeyan, G.
Title: Evaluation of 5G IoT Networks: Modernized Blockchain-Based Validation and Secure Framework
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Connected Intelligence for Industrial Applications (CI2A)
Abstract Note: With the billions of devices that are connected in 5G-enabled Internet of Things (IoT) networks, industries have been revolutionized, due to high-speed data transmission, ultra-low latency as well as large scale connectivity that 5 g offers. Yet, the growing number of IoT devices also creates serious security and privacy issues like unauthorized access, data breaches, and cyber-attacks. Security frameworks are dependent, centralized, and they cannot establish trust, scalability, and resilience against attack. With its potential to offer decentralized validation, secure authentication, and tamper-proof data storage, blockchain technology has therefore emerged as a promising solution to these concerns. Through this work, we investigate the combination of blockchain-based validation mechanisms with 5G Internet of Things networks to allow more secure, private, and integrity-preserving networks. This usually involves lightweight consensus mechanisms like Proof-of-Stake (PoS) and Byzantine Fault Tolerance (BFT) to enhance transaction efficiency while lowering energy consumption. Edge computing along with blockchain also helps in processing of data at the spot while waiting to be encoded which saves time and decrease latency of IoT applications. Beyond that, AI-driven security models provide higher accuracy in threat detection and anomaly identification in 5G IoT networks available in blockchain. However, notwithstanding the benefits, issues such as privacy, scalability, regulatory compliance, and computational overhead are still emergent areas of research. In contrast, on the other hand, enhancing the security frameworks of 5 G IoT ecosystems built on blockchain through post-quantum cryptography, federated learning, and self-sovereign identity management will lay a crucial role in the developments of computer-based solutions coming in the future. Upon learning the state-of-the-art blockchain validation methods and their contributions to the Internet of Things security, we analyze and evaluate the future works and threats on the secure 5G Internet of Things in this study.

Author: Othman, S. Ben
Title: A Quantum-Proof Lattice-Blockchain Federated Learning Framework for Secure Medical IoT Sensing
Publication Title: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
Abstract Note: The rapid proliferation of Medical Internet of Things (MIoT) networks faces two critical security challenges: centralized machine learning paradigms expose sensitive clinical data to privacy breaches, while advancing quantum computing threatens classical cryptographic safeguards. To address these vulnerabilities, we propose BioBlock-Q, a quantum-resilient, blockchain-orchestrated federated learning (FL) framework engineered for decentralized medical sensing. The framework integrates module learning with errors (M-LWEs) encryption and CRYSTALS-Dilithium-3 signatures to enforce end-to-end postquantum security with minimal computational overhead. In addition, a novel Proof-of-Accuracy (PoA) consensus mechanism mitigates Byzantine gradient poisoning through functional validation. Formal security reductions establish IND-CPA confidentiality and strong existential unforgeability under standard lattice hardness assumptions. Extensive evaluations across three benchmark clinical datasets demonstrate that BioBlock-Q maintains a Byzantine resilience score {\textbackslash{}mathcal {B}}_{\textbackslash{}mathrm {res}} {\textbackslash{},}\textbackslash{}geq {\textbackslash{},}0.95\ under 30% adversarial presence, achieves a compute-to-communication ratio (CCR) of \textbackslash{}approx 0.12\ , and reduces cryptographic latency by three orders of magnitude relative to RSA-2048. These results validate BioBlock-Q as a scalable, quantum-hardened architecture for secure Medical IoT Sensing.

Author: J, J. A.; V, G.; P, J.
Title: Canister-Based Blockchain Architecture for Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning in Smart Supply Chains
Publication Title: 2026 7th International Conference on Smart Electronics and Communication (ICOSEC)
Abstract Note: Internet of Things (IoT)-enabled supply chains generate large volumes of distributed operational data that can significantly improve demand forecasting. However, conventional machine learning approaches require centralized data aggregation, raising concerns regarding data privacy, trust, and single points of failure. Although Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative model training without sharing raw data, traditional FL frameworks still depend on a centralized aggregation server. This paper proposes an Internet Computer Protocol (ICP) canister-based federated learning framework for privacy-preserving demand forecasting in smart supply chains. In the proposed architecture, participating organizations perform local model training using their private IoT data, while the ICP canister authenticates participants, verifies Ed25519 digital signatures and SHA-256 model hashes, coordinates the aggregation workflow, manages global model versions, and stores only lightweight verification metadata on the blockchain. Computationally intensive tasks, including local training, model aggregation, and dataset storage, remain off-chain to reduce communication and storage overhead. The framework is implemented using the Flower Federated Learning framework integrated with the ICP local replica. Experimental results demonstrate a prediction accuracy of 95.8%, an RMSE of 0.048, an aggregation latency of 1.9 s, and an on-chain storage requirement of only 2.1 KB, outperforming conventional blockchain-assisted federated learning approaches in communication efficiency and blockchain storage overhead. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides a privacy-preserving and auditable solution for decentralized supply chain demand forecasting, with potential for scalable deployment.

Author: J, U. F.; Daniel, E.; Salaja, S.; Seetha, S.
Title: FOOD-GUARD: A Blockchain-Enabled Multi-Layer Detection Framework for Hybrid Attacks in Food Supply Chain Security
Publication Title: 2026 4th International Conference on Sustainable Computing and Smart Systems (ICSCSS)
Abstract Note: Food supply chain security systems have become increasingly vulnerable to hybrid attacks where insider attackers manipulate sensitive information and use these manipulations for their advantage in order to circumvent existing regulations, thereby posing a significant threat to public health and the liability of the systems. Existing approaches based on blockchain provide data integrity but lack preventive mechanisms against potential threats before any contaminated foods enter the food chain system. This paper introduces FOOD-GUARD, a combined threat detection system intended to detect and manage hybrid insider–outsider attacks in food supply chain networks. The goal is to facilitate the identification of harmful data alterations and guarantee the automatic implementation of corrective measures before regulatory approval. The proposed system combines cryptographic pre-validation with a multi-layered analytical detection framework that assesses behavioral, temporal, and structural anomalies in transaction data. Insider and outsider attack scenarios are represented using a hybrid dataset that has 23,921 records and 39 features, allowing the system to detect coordinated threat patterns. A composite scoring system is used to evaluate threat intensity, and automated response measures are activated upon detection. The experimental findings have shown that the accuracy rate for detection is 94.6%, proving that the model can effectively identify hybrid threats by detecting threats before they arise and automating response processes.

Author: Li, S.; Hu, Q.; Wang, Z.; Xu, M.; Cai, Z.
Title: PoFEL: Energy-Efficient Consensus for Blockchain-Based Hierarchical Federated Learning
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Services Computing
Abstract Note: Facilitated by mobile edge computing, client-edge- cloud hierarchical federated learning (HFL) enables communication-efficient model training in a widespread area but also incurs additional security and privacy challenges from intermediate model aggregations and remains vulnerable to the single point of failure issue. To tackle these challenges, we propose a blockchain-based HFL (BHFL) system that operates a permissioned blockchain among edge servers for model aggregation without the need for a centralized cloud server. The employment of blockchain, however, introduces additional overhead. To enable a compact and efficient workflow, we design a novel lightweight consensus algorithm, named Proof of Federated Edge Learning (PoFEL), to reuse computational work performed for local model training. Specifically, the leader node is selected by evaluating the intermediate FEL models from all edge servers instead of other additional mechanisms used solely for leader elections. This design thus improves the system efficiency compared with traditional BHFL frameworks. To prevent model plagiarism and bribery voting during the consensus process, we propose Hash-based Commitment and Digital Signature (HCDS) and Bayesian Truth Serum-based Voting (BTSV) schemes. Finally, we devise an incentive mechanism to motivate continuous contributions from clients to the learning task. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed BHFL system with the corresponding consensus protocol and incentive mechanism achieves effectiveness, low computational cost, and fairness.
Manual Tags: blockchain; consensus; incentive mechanism; Hierarchical federated learning (HFL)

Author: Gantla, H. R.; Mallavarapu, T.; B, H.; Korukonda, V.; K, R. S.; Nagamalla, V.
Title: Federated Edge Artificial Intelligence Framework for Privacy-Preserving Internet of Medical Things
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Secure Information Systems and Technologies (ICSIST)
Abstract Note: The Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) has been quickly adopted in the intelligent healthcare industry, introducing more and more medical data to be analysed at the network edge, which requires medical information analytics to be secure, privacy-preserving, and low-latency. When deployed in the heterogeneous edge environment, conventional federated learning approaches, however, tend to have high communication overhead, long inference time, long training time and insufficient privacy protection. To solve these problems, this paper presents the Federated Edge Artificial Intelligence (FedEdgeMed-AI) framework for Privacy-Preserving Internet of Medical Things, which incorporates edge intelligence, Federated Model Aggregation, Adaptive Privacy-Preserving Optimization, and Resource Management for distributed healthcare applications. The proposed framework is tested against the MIMIC-IV dataset in EdgeCloudSim environment and compared to FedAvg, FedProx and Blockchain-Assisted Federated Learning (BAFL). Experimental results show that FedEdgeMed-AI can reach an accuracy of 98.94%, a privacy preservation rate of 99.12%, and reduce training time to 31.48 min, response time to 84.67 ms, inference latency to 18.93 ms, and communication cost to 42.15 MB. Compared to the currently best model, the FedEdgeMed-AI model not only achieves a higher privacy preservation rate of 4.2%, but also boosts accuracy by 3.6%, shortens training time by 28.4%, response time by 32.7%, inference latency by 35.1%, and communication cost by 38.9%. These results show that the proposed framework is an effective and scalable solution for secure, privacy-preserving and real-time IoMT-enabled intelligent healthcare applications, which is suitable for next-generation applications in the medical field at the edge.

Author: Kumar, A.; Chatterjee, K.; Singh, A.; Kumar, A.; Aldawsari, H.
Title: Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning With Blockchain Auditing for Consumer Electronics Applications
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Consumer Electronics
Abstract Note: Consumer Electronics (CE) systems increasingly use Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), and Federated Learning (FL) for data-driven intelligence. This integration introduces risks such as privacy leakage during aggregation, poisoning of model updates, and integrity threats from unverified participants. Differentially private FL reduces leakage but often degrades accuracy by more than 10%, while Blockchain (BC)-based FL improves integrity at the cost of up to 12.9% overhead. To address these issues, a hybrid FL framework with BC auditing (BA) is proposed. The design combines Secure Aggregation (SA), Robust Global Update (RGU) rules, and lightweight BC consensus to defend against adaptive adversaries. Experimental results show an 8.3% accuracy gain under non-IID data, a 30.9% reduction in privacy leakage, and a poisoning-induced accuracy drop limited to 6.1% compared to 23.9% in standard FL. The framework maintains 97.8% BC integrity with only 3.2% overhead, demonstrating a balanced trade-off between accuracy, privacy, robustness, and integrity for real-world CE deployments.

Author: N, K.; E, S.; Agoramoorthy, M.; Kanimozhi, K. V.; A, L.; Bhaskar, K. V.
Title: Securing IoT Devices Using Federated Learning and Anomaly Detection for Cyber Threat Prevention
Publication Title: 2026 8th International Conference on Intelligent Sustainable Systems (ICISS)
Abstract Note: The growing adoption of Internet of Things (IoT) devices across industrial facilities, medical institutions, intelligent homes, and urban systems has proportionally increased the risk of cyberattacks and unauthorized access. Traditional, centrally controlled security systems often struggle to manage the substantial quantity, variable types, and sensitive nature of information produced by IoT networks, especially while striving to protect user privacy and maintain operational efficiency. This research presents an IoT security model based on federated learning. This model utilizes distributed machine learning, combined with real-time anomaly detection, to strengthen protection against digital threats. Individual IoT devices autonomously refine anomaly detection models utilizing data generated locally. Importantly, only model updates, rather than the original data, are transmitted to a central server. This enables the creation of a comprehensive threat detection model while preserving data confidentiality. The proposed system promotes data protection, swift threat detection, and adaptable learning within distributed IoT networks. Experimental simulations have confirmed the model's efficacy, demonstrating its ability to accurately identify atypical device behavior, reduce false positives, and significantly decrease communication demands compared to conventional, centralized learning methods. The suggested strategy offers a robust, privacy-centric, and adaptable solution for securing IoT environments. It facilitates proactive responses to evolving digital threats and enhances trust in critical IoT applications across medical, industrial, and smart city environments.

Author: Ramya, R.; Nathiya, R.; Moratanch, N.; Kannan, S.
Title: Efficient Data Management for Secure Healthcare Using Lightweight Blockchain and Enhancement of Internet of Things: A Review and Analysis

Abstract Note: The swift increase in progress of wearable technologies improvement and Internet of Things (IoT) systems both have led to the intermediate steady accumulation of large volumes of highly sensitive healthcare information. The information is crucial to making good clinical decisions and proactive medical diagnoses. Nevertheless, the conventional centralized data storage platforms are severely restricted, such as exposure to privacy, security threats, lack of scalability, and enhanced susceptibility to cyberattacks. In order to deal with these issues, decentralized health care systems using lightweight blockchain systems have come up as an attractive option of secure data management.This paper will carefully review and critique blockchain-based IoT systems that have been built to be used in healthcare. Author: Zhang, H.; Wang, Y.; Sun, R.; Liu, J.; Du, X.; Aitsaadi, N.
Title: TPFed: A Threshold-Free and Privacy-Preserving Defense for Federated Learning
Publication Title: ICC 2026 - IEEE International Conference on Communications
Abstract Note: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training while preserving data privacy, but it remains vulnerable to poisoning attacks. Existing clustering-based defenses under non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) settings often rely on assumptions about malicious client ratios, while their scoring mechanisms inadequately capture gradient characteristics and auxiliary datasets raise privacy concerns. To address these challenges, we propose TPFed, a defense framework that introduces a new client scoring mechanism and leverages clustering to transform the non-IID scenario into an approximately IID setting, thereby enhancing the separability between benign and malicious clients. In addition, we integrate secure multi-party computation (SMC) to preserve privacy and design a dynamic reference update mechanism to enhance adaptability to client distribution shifts while mitigating overfitting. Experimental results demonstrate that TPFed achieves strong robustness against representative poisoning attacks in complex FL scenarios.

Author: Prity, J. A.; Mahdi, A.
Title: BlockFlow: A Scalable Blockchain Integrated Federated Learning Framework for Decentralized Aggregation and Incentive Driven Collaboration

Author: Basheer, F.; Pathak, H. G.; Malik, M.; Gupta, R.
Title: Blockchain-Enabled Cybersecurity Techniques, Challenges, and Future Directions for Secure Smart Grids
Publication Title: 2026 9th International Conference on Circuit, Power & Computing Technologies (ICCPCT)
Abstract Note: The smart grid systems are increasingly becoming digital where the system is taking a new direction into greater operational efficiency and real time energy management. The traditional centralized security controls are not sufficient because of the limitation of single point failure, scalability limitations, and demand decentralized and resilient security controls. The use of blockchain technology in this regard has become a potential solution in order to improve the level of security by utilizing the transparent, decentralized, and immutable features of the technology. To provide cybersecurity approaches of smart grid systems, a taxonomical structure of blockchain technology is proposed in this paper. Besides that it shows the categorization of the various techniques into secure data management, secure energy trading, device authentication, data integrity assurance and communication protection. A detailed analysis of existing works was undertaken to determine their efficiency based on the security, scale and complexity of implementation. The results of the review describe some of the major challenges, such as latency and energy overhead and provide future research opportunities on effective smart grid security frameworks.

Author: Sharma, V.; Singh, A. K.; Raj, M.
Title: Reputation-Aware Federated Learning for Secure Cooperative Spectrum Sensing in Blockchain-Enabled B5G Networks
Publication Title: 2026 2nd International Conference on Sustainable Computing and Integrated Communication in Changing Landscape of AI (ICSCAI)
Abstract Note: Future beyond-5G (B5G) wireless communication systems are projected to face a dramatic increase in data traffic, making efficient spectrum use a key requirement. Cooperative Spectrum Sensing (CSS) has been recognized as a promising technique; nevertheless, its performance can be hampered by the malicious behavior of Secondary Users (SUs), energy limitations, privacy issues, and unreliable sensing reports. To overcome these issues, this paper presents a novel decentralized CSS framework that combines Federated Learning (FL) and Blockchain technology. In the proposed system, SUs work together to train a global sensing model by exchanging model updates instead of raw sensing data, thus ensuring data privacy and minimizing communication overhead. A blockchain-based incentive layer is also introduced to store contribution metadata and automate reward distribution using smart contracts. Moreover, an adaptive reputation system is proposed to assess the trustworthiness of SUs according to the perceived quality of their learning contributions, allowing the system to filter out malicious or lowquality updates and encourage consistent contributions. Simulation experiments show that the proposed system enhances sensing reliability in the presence of malicious SUs and maintains higher SU engagement compared to non-incentivized and reputation-agnostic schemes.

Author: Mahmootha, A. A.; Fathima, S. M. H. S. S.
Title: Adaptive Federated Intelligence Framework for Explainable and Quantum-Resistant Healthcare Systems Using Blockchain Technology
Publication Title: 2026 6th International Conference on Soft Computing for Security Applications (ICSCSA)
Abstract Note: The rapid advancements made in the field of Information and Communication Technology have led to changes in modern healthcare through intelligent decision making, security of the data and improvement of accessibility in healthcare. However, the usage of digital healthcare systems has led to some issues in terms of privacy, security, interoperability and resiliency against the quantum computing attacks. In this context, this paper suggests an Adaptive Hybrid Intelligence Framework for Quantum Resistant Blockchain Enabled Healthcare System by using XGBoost, Federated Learning (FedAvg), SHAP based Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI), Hyperledger Fabric, CRYSTALS-Kyber, CRYSTALS-Dilithium and HL7 FHIR to create a secure, privacy preserving and interoperable healthcare system. Author: Feng, L.; Xie, J.; Liu, X.; He, Z.; Zhang, J.; Yu, Y.; Li, K.
Title: BFLS-APIA: A Blockchain-Based Federated Learning Scheme Against Poisoning and Inference Attacks for Resource-Limited Consumer Electronics
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Consumer Electronics
Abstract Note: Consumer electronics (CE) devices generate privacy-sensitive data while operating under limited computation, memory, and energy budgets. Federated learning (FL) reduces raw-data transmission, but CE-oriented FL must address poisoned updates, update exposure, and cross-organization accountability without placing heavy security functions on terminals. We propose BFLS-APIA, a blockchain-assisted FL scheme based on a cost- and trust-aware placement of security functions. At the intra-organization edge level, an edge gateway performs lightweight Euclidean distance-based screening to reduce the propagation of suspicious updates. During inter-organization collaboration, Shamir secret sharing, encoded homomorphic aggregation, and round-level key management are combined to protect update confidentiality under the stated threat model. At the cross-organization level, a permissioned blockchain records training metadata and encrypted model records as provenance evidence, while computation-intensive operations remain off-chain. Experiments on CIFAR-10 and Fashion-MNIST under label-flipping poisoning attacks and non-IID data partitions show that BFLS-APIA maintains model utility. Author: Yune, E.; Balan, M.
Title: FLAI Protocol: Decentralized Federated Learning with On-Chain Rewards and sPEG-Based Contribution Scoring
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
Abstract Note: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training without data centralization but struggles with incentive alignment, accountability, and robustness under heterogeneous non-IID data. Existing decentralized FL (DeFL) systems leverage blockchains for coordination yet face high on-chain overhead, unverifiable self-reports, and weak fairness guarantees. We present the FLAI Protocol, a trusted execution environment (TEE)-backed DeFL framework that integrates enclave-validated aggregation, sparse Peer Evaluation Graph (sPEG) scoring, and on-chain settlement. sPEG incorporates peer-based quality, class coverage, promptness, effort, and reputation into composite contribution scores. The protocol formalizes contribution evaluation and tokenized incentive distribution, ensuring verifiable fairness and resilience against free-riding and collusion. We evaluate FLAI on image, text, and healthcare datasets and demonstrate parity with FedAvg in utility while improving fairness and accountability. A case study in consumer eHealth—aggregating wearable and electronic health record data for real-world evidence generation—illustrates the protocol’s applicability to privacy-critical domains where equitable rewards, auditability, and data sovereignty are essential.

Author: G, V. G.; A, R.

Author: Santhiya, S.; MadhanKumar, S.; Poongodi, K.
Title: An Integrated Adaptive Security Framework for Data Security Posture Management with AI-Driven Orchestration and Quantum-Resistant Capabilities
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Visual Analytics and Data Visualization (ICVADV)
Abstract Note: Although cloud storage offers the much-needed scalability, flexibility, and economic efficacy, it also presents significant security and privacy issues, which are mostly caused by the fact that, since data are encrypted, the traditional plaintext search approaches are compromised. To overcome this shortcoming, we introduce the Enhanced Aware Record Maintenance (EARM) architecture, a compound, privacy-aware architecture that supports ranked, multi-keyword encrypted data retrieval in the cloud. The fundamental retrieval process of EARM is novel, incorporating ontology-based keyword mapping, enhanced association rule mining, and inner-product similarities to produce highly accurate and relevant search results. The framework deploys a strong multi-layer defense model, which integrates quantum-resistant cryptography (Zero-Knowledge Proofs/Homomorphic Encryption), high-grade cipher suites (AES/RSA), and granular Attribute-Based Encryption (ABE) access controls (such as geofencing and decentralized identity management). Moreover, EARM also brings intelligent defensive layers of AI-based orchestration, which include ransomware, intrusion, and anomaly detection, behavioral biometrics, and a tamper-proof blockchain audit trail. Secure file versioning, rollback, and an encrypted trash bin are other ancillary features that improve the system's resilience. Empirical analyses performed on actual data sets indicate that EARM maintains high privacy and high retrieval rates and suffers only a few system overheads, hence making it an effective and highly secure encrypted cloud storage solution for modern challenges.

Author: Zhu, Y.; Lin, L.; Xiong, J.; Wang, X.; Jin, B.; Huang, R.; Lin, L.
Title: Trust-Adaptive Byzantine Consensus in Dynamic Vehicular Networks
Publication Title: 2026 4th International Conference on Big Data and Privacy Computing (BDPC)
Abstract Note: Dynamic vehicular networks present significant challenges for Byzantine consensus because node reliability, network connectivity, and attack intensity can vary significantly over time. Consequently, conventional Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance (PBFT)-style protocols are difficult to apply directly in such settings because they rely on equal-weight voting, static fault thresholds, and limited responsiveness to intermittent adversarial behaviors such as On-Off attacks. To address these limitations, this paper presents a trust-adaptive consensus framework tailored for dynamic vehicular networks, in which continuous trust assessment guides consensus influence, leader selection, and feedback-based correction within a closed-loop design. By translating trust assessment into a control signal within the consensus process, the framework dynamically adjusts voting weights and effectively mitigates the disruptive impact of unreliable nodes. Author: Zhao, Y.; Ullah, F.; Mohammad, N.; Raza, U.; Ahmad, J.

Abstract Note: The fast development of Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) and the Internet of Vehicles (IoV) has shifted the consumer mobility experience.
