Author: Cai, J.; Shen, W.; Hu, J.; Yang, H.
Title: PFLVA: Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning With Collusion-Resistant Verification and Fair Arbitration
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing
Abstract Note: Federated learning, as a distributed machine learning framework, enables participants to collaboratively train models by uploading only local gradients instead of exchanging local data. However, the malicious server might infer the participants’ private data from the uploaded gradients or return incorrect aggregated results to participants. To tackle the above issues, numerous privacy-preserving and verifiable federated learning schemes have been developed. However, only a few of these schemes address collusion-resistant verification, and none considers the potential disputes between participants and server. In this paper, we put forward a privacy-preserving federated learning scheme with collusion-resistant verification and fair arbitration (PFLVA). In PFLVA, a novel verification method is designed, in which non-colluding participants can verify the correctness of aggregated gradient, even if up to \N-1\N-1 participants collude with the server, where \N\N denotes the total number of online participants. We propose an efficient gradient encryption method to ensure participants’ privacy while substantially reducing the computational overhead. We introduce a smart contract to locate the compromised entity when disputes arise and to achieve fair arbitration. Additionally, PFLVA allows participants to go offline without incurring additional computational or communication overheads for the online participants. We provide a comprehensive security analysis to demonstrate the correctness, verifiability, privacy protection, and collusion resistance of PFLVA. Experimental results demonstrate that PFLVA maintains high model accuracy while significantly reducing the computational and communication overhead for participants compared to related schemes.
Manual Tags: Federated learning; privacy-preserving; verifiability; collusion-resistant

Author: Amasha, N. E.; Nasr, A. A.; Takieldeen, A. E.; Awad, W. A.
Title: A Survey of Blockchain Consensus Manipulation Attacks Based on Machine Learning Detection
Publication Title: 2026 1st International Conference on Innovations and Applications of Artificial Intelligence (ICIAAI)
Abstract Note: The popularity of blockchain technology has been on the increase. Blockchain operates by changing the interaction pattern of businesses, in that it eliminates the use of trusted intermediaries. Being a distributed registry working over decentralized networks, blockchain technology enables the storage of information in an immutable manner across thousands of computers across the world, and also enables the execution of non-executable code segments, called smart contracts. Although the concept of blockchain technology has been recently popularized as a safe way of information exchange in cyber grids, it has been susceptible to attacks that may manipulate the consensus mechanism. These mechanisms remain vulnerable to various threats. The existing security measures tend to be ineffective in dealing with such advanced manipulations as validator collusion or MEV exploitation in Ethereum-based smart contracts. According to this survey, there is an essential gap in the literature on real-time ML identification in resource-constrained settings. Therefore, we suggest a multi-layer attack taxonomy, mapping the canonical six-layer smart contract architecture (infrastructure, blockchain, data, contract, computation, application) onto a seventh, governance layer that captures validator collusion and DAO voting manipulation, and assess the effectiveness of ML methods, including the Random Forest and Federated Learning, in improving intrusion detection. Given that performance metrics and hybrid defenses are analyzed, this work provides protocol designers with a universal guide to constructing flexible blockchain architectures.

Author: R, H. S.; S, Y.; S, V. V.; S, M.
Title: Federated Learning Based Heart Disease Prediction Using a Secure Hierarchical Blockchain Aggregation
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Secure IoT and Cybersecurity (ICOSICS)
Abstract Note: Predicting heart disease accurately while protecting patient privacy is one of the biggest challenges in modern healthcare. However, FL can still face problems when some participants provide poor-quality updates, act maliciously, or try to benefit without contributing. To overcome these challenges, we propose a Hierarchical Blockchain-Enabled Secure Aggregation framework for federated heart disease prediction. Our system uses a layered blockchain to ensure training activity is transparent and tamper-proof, while a Proof-of-Quality (PoQ) mechanism evaluates the reliability of each update. A Bayesian reputation algorithm with time-based decay continuously tracks client trustworthiness, and smart-contract-like routines automate tasks such as registration, reputation posting, and participant selection. Finally, a Federated Random Forest ensemble combines models by weighting them according to reputation and finetunes thresholds for accuracy. Tests on heart-disease datasets show improved security, reliability, and privacy-critical for trustworthy healthcare AI.

Author: Chen, B.; Wang, Y.; Santos, L.; Yang, X.; Liu, C.; Im, S.-K.
Title: A Four-Paradigm Taxonomy and Systematic Survey of Blockchain-Enabled Intrusion Detection Systems for IoT and IIoT
Publication Title: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
Abstract Note: Traditional intrusion detection systems (IDSs) are increasingly challenged by the distributed, heterogeneous, and rapidly evolving threat landscape in Internet of Things (IoT) and Industrial IoT (IIoT) environments. Blockchain has been explored as a promising foundation for decentralized and trustworthy security mechanisms; however, the existing literature remains fragmented and lacks a clear organizing lens for comparing design choices and evaluation practices. To address this, this article presents a problem-driven survey of blockchain-enabled IDS for IoT and IIoT. We organize prior work into four integration paradigms: trusted rule, machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and federated learning (FL)—and relate each paradigm to the recurring design tensions it primarily targets. We further distill three fundamental tensions that frequently shape system design, including distributed architectures versus centralized security management, collaborative information sharing versus privacy preservation, and real-time detection requirements versus resource-constrained devices. In addition, we summarize representative frameworks by consolidating datasets, threat models, and reported performance-related metrics, and discuss common limitations that hinder cross-paper comparability. Finally, we outline a roadmap toward more standardized benchmarking, suggesting candidate evaluation criteria and blockchain-specific KPIs to encourage more transparent and comparable reporting. Overall, this survey aims to provide a structured lens for navigating the design space of blockchain-enabled IDS and to highlight open challenges for future research.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; Internet of Things (IoT); security; intrusion detection systems (IDSs)

Author: Liu, X.; Li, C.; Shi, Y.; Hu, D.; Xu, H.; Wang, J.; Li, K.
Title: CoCFL: A Lightweight Blockchain-Based Federated Learning Framework for Large-Scale IoT Cluster
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Networking
Abstract Note: Blockchain-based Federated Learning (BCFL) has attracted considerable attention in the intelligent IoT domain for its privacy-preserving and decentralized characteristics. Depending on their applicable scenarios, BCFL frameworks are categorized into two types: synchronous and asynchronous. However, synchronous BCFL struggles with low efficiency in heterogeneous IoT environments, while asynchronous BCFL suffers from slow convergence speed. In additional, Both BCFL incur significant resource consumption from blockchain consensus mechanisms which is unrelated to federated learning tasks, leading to resource wastage and poor scalability, making them unsuitable for large-scale IoT networks. To address these challenges, we propose CoCFL, a novel BCFL framework utilizing multi-chain collaboration. CoCFL introduces two lightweight sub-chains: PoCFL-CChain and PC-CChain, based on different FL strategy. PoCFL-CChain uses a synchronous FL strategy for learning devices with similar performance to generate high-accuracy models, while PC-CChain adopts an asynchronous strategy for heterogeneous devices, which can improving training efficiency. CoCFL assigns devices to suitable sub-chains based on their performance to carry out FL tasks and aggregates the sub-chain models into a global model. This multi-chain collaboration strategy enhances model accuracy and convergence speed and significantly improves the scalability of BCFL. In additional, the consensus mechanisms in CoCFL sub-chains not only maintain the blockchain ledger but also handle FL-related tasks such as detecting poisoning attacks, assigning roles, and distributing incentives. This design not only improving the efficiency of BCFL, but also enhances learning security and ensuring fair incentives. Experiments show that CoCFL improves learning accuracy by 6% and efficiency by 18% over existing BCFL frameworks. It also demonstrates excellent scalability, with time consumption liner decreasing as sub-chains increase, and can withstand up to 40% of poisoning attacks while ensuring fair incentives.

Author: Main, H.; Velhal, D.; Nair, A.; Hule, A.; Dalvi, H.

Author: Maheswari, N. U.; Chinnaraju, K.; Swathiga, U. U. A. S.; Ramamurthy, V.; Santhi, K.; Sangeetha, A.
Title: An Energy-Efficient Federated Learning Framework for Privacy-Preserving Intrusion Detection in IOT Networks
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Networks Computers and Communications (ICNCCom)
Abstract Note: Thousands of Internet of Things (IoT) devices are being deployed in various smart home, healthcare, industrial automation and smart city applications, creating a massive attack surface for cyber threats and the need for effective intrusion detection is greater than ever before. However, traditional centralized Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) have a number of drawbacks when implemented in a heterogeneous IoT environment, such as privacy concerns, communication overhead, energy consumption, and scalability. While Federated Learning (FL) has become a very promising method for privacy-preserving model training, current FL-based IDS approaches typically ignore the limited resources of IoT devices and do not consider energy efficiency and communication optimization aspects. Pursuing a robust cybersecurity infrastructure for IoT networks that is scalable, privacy-preserving and resource-efficient, the present research introduces an Energy-efficient federated learning-based intrusion detection system (EEFL-IDS) for privacy preserving IoT networks. The ultimate goal of this research is to design an intrusion detection framework to improve detection accuracy, decrease energy usage, reduce communication overheads and maintain data privacy in distributed IoT environment. The proposed EEFL-IDS introduces Federated Learning, Lightweight Deep Neural Networks (LDNN), Energy-Aware Client Selection (EACS), model pruning, Knowledge Distillation, Top-K sparse parameter transmission and secure federated aggregation into a single framework, to achieve these goals. The framework allows for the formation of a global model for intrusion detection by collaborating a number of distributed IoT devices without losing raw network traffic data to the cloud. Moreover, an energy-based client participation mechanism is dynamically designed to select suitable devices for federated training, which helps to alleviate the computational load and prolong the operational lifetime of the devices. To assess the performance of the proposed framework, the following benchmark IoT intrusion detection datasets were used: CICIoT2023, IoT-23, TON_IoT, and N-BaIoT. The experimental results reveal that the detection accuracy of EEFL-IDS is 98.31%, with a precision of 97.94%, recall of 97.68%, and an F1-score of 97.81%, which greatly surpass the conventional FedAvg IDS and other state-of-the-art federated intrusion detection systems. Moreover, the proposed model can decrease the energy consumption by 33.42%, the communication cost by 46.29%, the number of convergence rounds by 38.33% and the number of false alarms by 53.03% when compared with conventional federated learningbased IDS models. The improvements demonstrate the successful integration of energy-saving optimization with communication-efficient learning strategies within federated IDS. The findings confirm the proposed EEFL-IDS's effectiveness in addressing the primary limitations of existing IDS frameworks, specifically in balancing intrusion detection accuracy, privacy protection, communication efficiency, and energy sustainability. This framework provides a scalable and practical cybersecurity solution for future IoT ecosystems. Upcoming research will focus on incorporating blockchain-based trust management, XAI, adaptive client clustering, and validation through real-world deployment to enhance the robustness and applicability of the proposed method.

Author: Zeng, J.; Lai, J.; Xu, S.; Zhang, Z.; Sun, C.
Title: Efficient and Secure Model Initialization Scheme in Federated Learning
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Cloud Computing
Abstract Note: In Federated Learning (FL), a shared initial global model is distributed by an aggregator through a cloud server to all participating clients for the purpose of local training. To mitigate the threat of a potentially malicious cloud server, consistency verification of the client-received initial model is essential. Public key encryption with equality test (PKEET) enables authorized entities to determine whether two ciphertexts contain an identical message or not without decryption. This property supports consistency verification of the initial global model in FL settings. Identity-based encryption with equality test (IBEET) eliminates the certificate, resolving certificate management issues in PKEET. SM9, as a Chinese identity-based cryptographic standard, has been applied in many fields. However, existing equality test schemes based on SM9 only support equality tests on two ciphertexts, resulting in linear executions of the test algorithm when performing tests on multiple ciphertexts. To enhance efficiency and functionality, we propose an efficient multi-ciphertext equality test scheme based on SM9 (SM9-MET), which is well-suited for verifying the initial model in FL. The proposed SM9-MET scheme supports simultaneous equality testing on multiple ciphertexts while maintaining constant-size ciphertexts. Our method requires only one single execution of the test algorithm. Under the \q\q-BDHI assumption in the random oracle model, we prove that the SM9-MET scheme achieves one-way security and indistinguishability against chosen-plaintext attacks. Author: Vishalakshi, R.; Almatarneh, S.; G, N.; Merline, A.; Y, R. V. S. S. N.; Kumar, S. H.
Title: Predictive Secure Energy Trading Communication Framework for Vehicle-to-Grid Systems Using Blockchain Technology

Author: Kumbhare, R.; Dehalwar, V.; Pateriya, R. K.
Title: A Comprehensive Review of Attacks and Defense Mechanisms in Federated Learning for Autonomous Driving and VANETs
Publication Title: 2026 Fourth International Conference on Secure Cyber Computing and Communications (ICSCCC)
Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) enables privacy preserving collaborative model training for autonomous driving and Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (VANETs); however, its decentralized nature introduces significant security vulnerabilities. This paper presents a comprehensive review of attacks and defense mechanisms in FL-based vehicular systems. Common FL architectures and adversarial threat models are analyzed, and a structured taxonomy is proposed that encompasses data and model poisoning attacks, stealthy and persistent backdoor attacks, Sybil and jamming attacks, as well as poisoning attacks targeting collaborative intrusion detection systems.The effects of these attacks on safety critical applications, including traffic sign recognition, lane detection, steering control, and network security, are examined. Furthermore, state-of-the-art defense strategies such as robust aggregation, trust-based and blockchain assisted mechanisms, backdoor detection techniques, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI)-based intrusion detection frameworks are reviewed, followed by a comparative analysis that highlights their effectiveness and limitations. Author: Kumar, V.; Niazi, M. A.; Sajid, Q.; Koondhar, M. A.; Kim, Y.-S.; Zainuri, M. Ammirrul Atiqi Mohd; Alkoradees, A. F.
Title: A Federated Learning Framework for Proactive Congestion Management in Blockchain-Based P2P Energy Markets
Publication Title: IEEE Access
Abstract Note: The rapid penetration of distributed energy resources (DERs) is transforming consumers into prosumers, enabling decentralized peer-to-peer (P2P) energy markets. However, a major obstacle to their practical use is making sure that trades based on economics don’t break the physical limits of the distribution grid. This paper presents an innovative, entirely decentralized, and contextually aware Federated P2P (FP2P) market framework to tackle this issue. The framework co-optimizes the well-being of all prosumers with the safety of the grid by putting a linearized ac power flow model directly into a blockchain-based market clearing system. The main new thing about it is a proactive congestion management system that uses a Federated Learning (FL) architecture that protects privacy. It uses a Graph Neural Network (GNN) to predict the likelihood of line congestion. This predicted risk is turned into a dynamic grid fee, which keeps the market from going to unsafe operating points. The proposed FP2P framework was rigorously validated through a high-fidelity co-simulation on a modified IEEE 37-bus test feeder using real-world prosumer, weather, and market data. Results demonstrate that our approach successfully eliminates grid congestion events, significantly increases total prosumer profit, and reduces peak substation load compared to centralized, unmanaged P2P, and rule-based control baselines. Author: Pang, X.; Zhou, Y.; Wang, Z.; Hao, X.; Han, T.; Guo, S.
Title: Unlocking the Potential of Asynchronous Federated Learning in Non-IID Edge Environments
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing
Abstract Note: Asynchronous Federated Learning (AFL) enhances the efficiency of edge collaborative learning systems by asynchronously aggregating client updates to prevent slowdowns from slow clients. However, in non-IID scenarios, such operations magnify uneven learning among various local data, degrading global model generalization performance on various local data. Prior solutions work by increasing the contribution of certain slow clients in global aggregation but fail to balance efficiency and generalization performance. In this paper, to deal with such a contradiction, we propose an adaptive fine-tuning-based efficient AFL framework, called AFLTuning, which enables certain clients to contribute high-quality local updates more frequently, thereby facilitating rapid and balanced global learning without introducing additional delay. Specifically, we first propose a data distribution-driven underrepresented client identification mechanism to recognize clients that may have highly skewed data distributions or infrequent participation in global aggregation due to long local processing times, causing the global model to poorly learn their local data. Then, we develop a prediction calibration-based adaptive fine-tuning mechanism to improve these clients’ training efficiency and quality, and a frequency-aware weighted aggregation mechanism to strategically increase their weights during global aggregation. These designs allow underrepresented clients to participate more frequently and contribute more to the global model learning without introducing additional delay, thus mitigating the uneven learning and improving the generalization of AFL while maintaining system efficiency. Extensive experiments demonstrate AFLTuning’s superiority to state-of-the-art methods in both performance and efficiency.

Author: Sezer, B. B.

Module-Lattice-Based Key Encapsulation Mechanism (ML-KEM)-based hybrid encryption protects client models against quantum attacks, while data is securely stored in IPFS. In this study, the accuracy, privacy, and efficiency of the approach are evaluated by simulating the processes of different actors in the supply chain on a scenario-byscenario basis. The experimental results demonstrate the security and feasibility of the system by combining secure data sharing with high model performance of the proposed architecture.

Author: Elezebeth, B.; Ali, S. M.; Ahmad, Y.; Abbas, Y. H. O.; Hari, V.; yousuf, M. k

Author: Ravi, P. K.; Walia, R.
Title: Review and Analyze Federated Learning Frameworks for Social Media Platforms

Abstract Note: The high rate of social media platforms development has caused the mass creation of sensitive user data, which has posed serious privacy and security issues in the traditional centralized machine learning systems. Author: Srivastava, T.; Surabhi, R.; Garlapati, S. P.; Pulipati, N.; Varghese, A.; Kumar, S. A.
Title: FLChain: Federated Learning and Blockchain for CNC Machine Health
Publication Title: IEEE Access
Abstract Note: Modern manufacturing use-cases demand intelligent and secure monitoring systems. The ever increasing complexity of Computer Numerical Control (CNC) machines aid factories in minimizing downtime and maintenance costs. With aggressive production schedules and highly scaled industrial operations, proactive fault detection and predictive maintenance (PdM) has become the need of the hour. Unexpected machine failures can result in significant financial losses and unprecedented down-time. The utilization of intelligent monitoring systems, however, is often hindered by the sensitive and proprietary nature of industrial telemetry, which is brought on by the restriction of data sharing across corporate and organizational boundaries. This research proposes a conceptual prototype that explores the integration of Federated Learning (FL) and Blockchain technology to support data-local CNC tool wear prediction and machine maintenance logging. The proposed prototype demonstrates the feasibility of enabling collaborative model training directly on local edge devices, thereby avoiding the transfer or centralization of raw proprietary data. Because full differential privacy is not implemented, the architecture should be interpreted as a data-locality and confidentiality-oriented proof of concept rather than a system that provides formal privacy guarantees against gradient-level inference or reconstruction attacks. To ensure operational transparency, an immutable Solana-based ledger is integrated to automate maintenance verification through a mandatory 100-cycle attestation protocol. The blockchain layer stores the complete maintenance record for each logged event, not raw machine sensor logs, federated model weights, or only hashes of maintenance records. This ensures the integrity of digital logbooks. Small-scale experimental evaluation demonstrates that the framework achieves a global model accuracy of about 93% along with a standardized Machine Learning Operations (MLOps) orchestration to remove model drift. These findings highlight the feasibility and potential of the proposed architecture to bridge the gap between industrial data confidentiality and diagnostic performance.

Author: J, K. K.; D, N.; S, S. H.
Title: FedChain: AI-Driven Blockchain Security with Quantum-Inspired Encryption for Federated IoT Networks
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
Abstract Note: The rapid growth of Internet-of-Things devices raises significant security and data integrity challenges, particularly in federated networks with autonomous device interactions. This work proposes FedChain, a novel framework integrating blockchain-inspired transaction validation, AI driven device reputation, and quantum-like encryption for secure IoT communication. FedChain features HMAC-backed device registration with deterministic token rotation and phase encoded neuro-fingerprints, providing unique, reproducible device identities. Message security is ensured via entropy-aware quantum-like encryption, combining chaos-key derivation, Merkle-root watermarking, and HMAC checksums. A lightweight transaction ledger with Merkle-like root verification supports integrity audits and AI-based self-healing for compromised devices. The framework is evaluated with 100 simulated devices, including 50 attack devices and 50 benign devices. Results demonstrate effective detection and blocking of malicious devices, secure message transfer among benign devices, dynamic reputation updates, and clear visualization of device distributions. FedChain achieves robust, adaptive security and deterministic device verification, offering a practical solution for secure federated IoT environments.

Author: Gentyala, S.; Sanjeevaiah, K.; Darisi, S. K.
Title: SybilShield-Core: A Composite Trust Scoring Framework for Sybil Attack Mitigation in Permissionless Blockchain Networks
Publication Title: 2026 Third International Conference on Innovations in Cybersecurity and Data Science (ICICDS)
Abstract Note: Sybil attacks represent a persistent structural vulnerability in permissionless peer-to-peer blockchain networks. An adversary who can manufacture pseudonymous identities at sub-linear cost gains the ability to distort consensus outcomes, partition the network, and corrupt decentralized data aggregation pipelines. Established countermeasures either impose computationally expensive Proof-of-Work friction or rely on centralized identity certification, both of which introduce tradeoffs incompatible with trust-minimized operation. This paper proposes SybilShield-Core, a modular mitigation framework that fuses three complementary detection signals (behavioral telemetry, peer-graph topology analysis, and cryptographic economic commitment) into a Composite Trust Score (CTS) assigned continuously to each network participant. The CTS governs quorum voting weight, connection acceptance, and escalating mitigation responses without requiring computational waste or third-party identity validation. Simulation across four attack scenarios (consensus masking, Eclipse partitioning, decentralized federated learning gradient poisoning, and mempool exhaustion) indicates detection rates above 94% with false-positive rates below 2.1% and a consensus latency overhead not exceeding 4.1%. The results demonstrate that multi-signal behavioral scoring, when properly calibrated, provides a scalable and decentralization-preserving alternative to existing identityfriction approaches.

Author: Dinh, T. T. T.; Ho, M. C.; Wondmagegn, A. B.; Kim, J.; Cho, S.
Title: Federated Learning: State-of-the-art, Challenges and Research Opportunities
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Information and Communication (ICAIIC)
Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) is an emerging paradigm in machine learning that enables collaborative model training without centralizing data, thereby addressing privacy and security concerns. Unlike traditional centralized approaches, FL keeps data on local devices and only exchanges model updates, making it highly relevant in the era of strict data governance regulations. This survey provides a comprehensive overview of FL, covering its foundational concepts, related works, and major categories including horizontal, vertical, and transfer learning. We highlight practical applications across healthcare, finance, mobile devices, IoT, autonomous systems, and wireless communications. Furthermore, we examine the challenges faced by FL, such as data heterogeneity, system scalability, communication efficiency, and security vulnerabilities. We also explore solutions proposed in recent literature, ranging from differential privacy and secure aggregation to personalization and hierarchical architectures. Author: Cui, K.; Feng, X.; Wang, L.; Liu, Z.
Title: Dual-Verifiable Federated Learning With Vector Commitments Against Collusion Attacks
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing
Abstract Note: Collusion attacks, where the server and malicious clients collaborate to bypass gradient source confirmation or tamper with aggregation results, cause a fundamental damage to the training process in federated learning (FL). However, existing verifiable FL frameworks typically adopt a split-verification model—clients can independently validate the correctness of aggregation results, while the server is responsible for confirming the legitimacy of gradient sources. Thus, the collusion attack has emerged as a critical and intractable vulnerability, as it completely collapses this split-verification model, thereby invalidating such verification mechanisms. To tackle this fundamental issue, we propose an innovative dual-verifiable FL framework. Specifically, by leveraging vector commitments, our scheme first integrates both gradient source confirmation and aggregation result verification into a unified framework. Based on this unified design, our scheme implements two targeted strategies to defend against collusion attacks. To prevent collusion-enabled gradient source spoofing, our scheme introduces a semi-trusted verification cluster in place of unreliable server-side validation and embeds an anonymized identity-check strategy to collaboratively confirm gradient source legitimacy. To counter collusion-driven manipulation of gradient aggregation results, our scheme customizes auxiliary verification proofs with a computational one-wayness for client-uploaded gradients. This renders it infeasible for adversaries to tamper with the aggregation result through reverse engineering. Under experiments and security analyses, our scheme achieves reliable dual-verification and robust resistance to collusion attacks. Moreover, it reduces computation and communication overhead by at least 40.83\textbackslash{}%\% and 50.47\textbackslash{}%\%, respectively, compared to state-of-the-art verifiable FL schemes.

Author: Duan, L.; Li, Z.; Yuan, X.; Wang, W.; Liu, J.; Ni, W.
Title: FedHydra: Toward Parameter-Efficient and Backdoor-Resistant Federated Unlearning in Human-Centric Metaverse Service
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Services Computing
Abstract Note: Federated learning significantly enhances immersive user experiences in the human-centric metaverse by training machine learning models while keeping distributed data localized. As the right to be forgotten is legislated globally, users in the human-centric metaverse should have the option to have their data forgotten. Federated Unlearning (FU) is an emerging solution that enables the server to remove client contributions from trained global models by calibrating the historical model parameters of participating clients. However, retaining the entire model parameters incurs significant storage overhead, and the involvement of the remaining clients exposes the global model to the risk of backdoor attacks. This paper presents a new parameter-efficient and backdoor-resistant FU framework, called FedHydra. FedHydra segments the model into a base and a classifier layer. By storing the classifier parameters critical to predicting output, FedHydra reduces the storage overhead of the server. FedHydra also calibrates the classifier parameters and compares cosine similarity between the old and new classifier parameters of the remaining clients, reducing the computational overhead of unlearning while effectively preventing the abnormal clients from participating in the calibration. Experiments show that, compared with the full parameter-based storage calibration method, FedHydra achieves comparable unlearning effects, reduces storage overhead on the server, and improves unlearning efficiency. In addition, FedHydra reduces the attack success rates in different backdoor attack settings while maintaining the predictive performance of the global model.

Author: Lakshmi, M. S.; Basavaraju, N.; Basha, S. K.; Johitesh, T.; Sumanth, Y. S.; JayaSunitha, M.
Title: Federated Reinforcement Learning with Blockchain-Integrated Trust for Secure Routing in 5G-Enabled Vehicular Networks
Publication Title: 2026 9th International Conference on Trends in Electronics and Informatics (ICOEI)
Abstract Note: Secure and low-latency routing in 5G-enabled Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (VANETs) is fundamentally challenged by high node mobility, dynamic topology changes, and the threat of malicious routing behaviour. Existing protocols including AODV and standalone reinforcement learning (RL) approaches fail to jointly address privacy-preserving distributed learning, trust-based route verification, and real-time adaptability. This paper proposes the Federated Reinforcement Learning-based Secure Routing (FRL-SR) framework, which integrates decentralized Q-learning at vehicular agents, weighted federated aggregation at roadside unit (RSU) edge servers, and a blockchain-based trust verification layer operating on PBFT consensus. Vehicles learn local routing policies from neighborhood observations without sharing raw data; RSUs periodically aggregate global models via data-weighted FedAvg; and every routing update is validated through blockchain transactions recording node ID, model hash, trust score, and digital signature. Extensive simulations on NS-3.39 with SUMO mobility and 5G NR-V2X communication demonstrate that FRL-SR achieves a mean Packet Delivery Ratio (PDR) of 94.0%, an average End-to-End Delay (E2E) of 42 ms, a Trust Violation Rate (TVR) below 1.5%, and model convergence in 14 federated rounds outperforming AODV, RL-Only, and FedRL baselines by 18–22%, 28–35%, and 23%, respectively. Author: Guo, S.; Zhou, Y.
Title: Big Data Intelligent Analysis Model Based on Trusted Privacy Computing

Abstract Note: Against the background of rapid development of big data and digital economy, traditional centralized big data analysis methods face prominent problems such as frequent privacy leakage, poor heterogeneous data adaptability and rigid access control, which restrict safe data sharing and intelligent application. This paper constructs a four-layer big data intelligent analysis model based on trusted privacy computing, which integrates homomorphic encryption, federated learning and blockchain technology. The model retains original sensitive data locally, only transmits encrypted model parameters, and realizes whole-process trusted protection of data from collection, transmission to analysis. Combined with weighted principal component analysis, it completes efficient data feature mining, and designs fuzzy dynamic access control and intelligent resource scheduling strategies to optimize model operation efficiency and security management. Simulation experiments show that compared with mainstream traditional models, the proposed model achieves an analysis accuracy of 96.20%, reduces the data leakage rate to 0.12%, and has excellent encryption efficiency and low computing delay. It also possesses strong anti-interference and multi-scenario adaptability. The research results can effectively solve the privacy security risks in untrusted computing environments, and provide reliable technical support for intelligent data analysis and secure data circulation in power monitoring, intelligent transportation and industrial manufacturing fields.

Author: Hallaji, E.; Razavi-Far, R.; Saif, M.
Title: TrustChain: A Blockchain Framework for Auditing and Verifying Aggregators in Decentralized Federated Learning
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Big Data
Abstract Note: The serverless nature of Decentralized Federated Learning (DFL) requires allocating the aggregation role to specific participants in each federated round. Current DFL architectures ensure the trustworthiness of the aggregator node upon selection. However, most of these studies overlook the possibility that the aggregating node may turn rogue and act maliciously after being nominated. To address this problem, this paper proposes a DFL structure, called TrustChain, that scores the aggregators before selection based on their past behavior and additionally audits them after the aggregation. To do this, the statistical independence between the client updates and the aggregated model is continuously monitored using the Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion (HSIC). The proposed method relies on several principles, including blockchain, anomaly detection, and concept drift analysis. The designed structure is evaluated on several federated datasets and attack scenarios with different numbers of Byzantine nodes.

Author: He, B.; Feng, T.; Liao, X.; Wu, Z.; Su, C.
Title: BFL-DIAS: A Blockchain and Federated Learning-Based Dynamic Identity Authentication Scheme for Industrial Internet of Things
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics
Abstract Note: The Industrial Internet of Things requires authentication mechanisms that can adapt to dynamic contexts, preserve identity privacy, and support interoperable collaboration across security domains. BFL-DIAS integrates a permissioned consortium ledger, pseudonymous identity management, dynamic key and attribute-state updates, and off-path federated risk scoring into a unified workflow for registration, intradomain authentication, cross-domain authentication, and state maintenance. A prototype implementation on edge, mobile, and virtualized server platforms demonstrates low authentication latency, manageable ledger overhead, and stable off-path risk assessment. These results indicate that BFL-DIAS provides a secure, auditable, and deployable foundation for dynamic cross-domain authentication in industrial environments.

Author: Jiang, L.; Rong, D.; Yu, G.; Chen, J.; He, Q.; Liu, Z.
Title: Reconstruct Private Embeddings: An Interaction-Level Membership Inference Attack Against Federated Social Matching
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing
Abstract Note: Social matching is a task that recommends potential friends to users based on their existing friendships. This user-to-user recommendation setting extends general recommender systems by shifting the focus from user-item interactions to interactions among users themselves, and general recommendation methods are often directly applied to this setting. However, we argue that in federated learning, directly applying existing federated recommendation methods to social matching can result in privacy leakage, due to the specificity of social matching: the mutual nature of friendships. We theoretically and quantitatively reveal these security vulnerabilities and propose a novel interaction-level membership inference attack targeting federated social matching. Our attack employs a reconstruction model combining affine transformations with an MLP to capture both linear and non-linear mappings between users’ public and private embeddings. Trained on a portion of leaking user data, it can reconstruct benign users’ private embeddings and infer their true friends. We conduct numerous experiments on multiple datasets under various experimental settings to verify the effectiveness and robustness of our attack method. Experimental results show that: (i) Our attack approach exhibits strong robustness and effectiveness across diverse experimental setups; (ii) Existing defense methods fail to effectively resist our attack while maintaining satisfactory recommendation performance. Our findings highlight the need for new privacy-preserving techniques specifically designed for federated social matching.
Manual Tags: federated social matching; Interaction-level membership inference attack

Author: R, P.; R, H.

Abstract Note: The high rate of development of generative artificial intelligence, the spread of deepfake content has become a dangerous threat to the digital trust, cybersecurity, and integrity of society. To deal with those issues, this paper will present a new framework of deepfake detection powered by Federated Learning (FL), with the idea that the model can be trained in collaboration among decentralized data sources without exchanging the sensitive information. The proposed method uses a combination of CNN-BiLSTM-Multi-Head Self-Attention model in a Federated Learning setting in order to solve the issues arising due to inconsistency in spatial and temporal data within the manipulated videos. By employing CNNs, the discriminative features of the facial regions from each frame of the video are captured and the temporal correlation of the successive frames is captured by the BiLSTM network. In addition, the Multi-Head Self-Attention model helps to concentrate on the informative spatial-temporal features prior to classification. The proposed CNN-Attention model is trained one by one by the clients without sharing the real data. The gradients of the model are clipped and noise added to them with an appropriate level before they are used to implement DP. Then, prior to applying the FedAvg algorithm, Secure Aggregation is used on the encrypted model updates. This solution not only decreases the number of successful model inversions and membership inference attacks, but also maintains the detection accuracy. The strategy guarantees privacy of data and a high degree of detection. The benchmark datasets used to evaluate the proposed FL-based model include FaceForensics and DeepFake Detection Challenge (DFDC) and show that the proposed method performs similarly to the centralized models in terms of accuracy and provides better generalization to new data distribution variations.

Author: Yao, A.; Shao, D.; Su, W.; Tu, M.; Zhang, W.; Dong, C.; Pal, S.; Gu, Z.

Abstract Note: As facial recognition becomes increasingly integrated into consumer Internet of Things (CIoT) ecosystems such as smart cameras, mobile devices, and home surveillance protecting multimedia identity data while retaining utility and ensuring security has become a pressing challenge. Author: Loussaief, I.; Jaidi, F.; Channoufi, A.; Nouri, K.
Title: Cross-Layer Security Framework for the Internet of Vehicles: Fuzzy Gateway Selection, Hierarchical Blockchain Authentication, and Mobile Edge Computing-Enhanced Public Key Infrastructure
Publication Title: 2026 International Wireless Communications and Mobile Computing (IWCMC)
Abstract Note: The Internet of Vehicles (IoV) paradigm imposes authentication requirements at the intersection of three tensions: cryptographic correctness, rapid response windows for safety-critical decisions, and trust management across networks that can number millions of nodes. Existing public key infrastructure (PKI) schemes, built around centralized validation, remain vulnerable to single points of failure and cannot simultaneously satisfy all three requirements. This paper proposes a cross-layer security framework that treats gateway trustworthiness not as a binary pass/fail condition but as a continuous, multidimensional score. Three tightly integrated components make this possible: a Mamdani fuzzy inference system that scores candidate gateways across six dimensions (PKI capability, certificate health, routing protocol for low-power and lossy networks (RPL) routing security, machine learning (ML)-based threat score, network quality, and node reliability); a hierarchical three-level Merkle tree blockchain with geographic partitioning that achieves O(1) authentication complexity under bounded region sizes; and a mobile edge computing (MEC)-enhanced PKI pipeline that runs distributed certificate revocation list (CRL) caching, batch elliptic curve digital signature algorithm (ECDSA) signature verification, and real-time ensemble threat detection in parallel. Cross-layer correlation of PKI certificate events and RPL routing anomalies enables detection of coordinated multi-vector attacks that escape single-layer observation. The framework’s alignment with European Telecommunications Standards Institute (ETSI) intelligent transport systems (ITS) standards (TS 102 940, TS 102 941, TS 103 097) is maintained throughout the design. It is validated through a coordinated Sybil-sinkhole attack scenario that illustrates how these components work together under adversarial conditions.

Author: Zhilin, Y.
Title: Design of a Multi-Layered Secure Storage Architecture for Distance Learning Based on Federated and Encrypted Data Algorithms
Publication Title: 2026 3rd International Conference on Electronic Circuits and Signaling Technologies (ICECST)
Abstract Note: With the expansion of heterogeneous data scale in remote education platforms, dynamic changes in user permissions, and increased risks of network attacks, in practical terms, traditional single-layer data protection mechanisms are unable to simultaneously meet the requirements of privacy protection, access control, communication security, and robustness of federated learning. Therefore, this paper proposes a multi-layer security storage architecture based on federated learning and hybrid encryption algorithms. This architecture consists of a federated data generation layer, a data storage encryption layer, and a data transmission negotiation layer. At the same time, this research combines differential privacy, multi-party shared key negotiation based on NTRU lattice, multi-layer semantic attribute encryption, and adaptive gradient credibility aggregation mechanism. Such theoretical innovation fully realizes collaborative security protection from the client side, edge servers to the cloud and alliance blockchain. In the method design, first, adaptive Gaussian perturbation is used to protect local gradient privacy. Finally, the federated aggregation weights are dynamically adjusted according to gradient credibility and local data scale. Experiments are conducted in the CIFAR-100 subset, synthetic student behavior logs, and malicious client simulation environments. The results show that in a scenario with 100 participants, the average delay of the proposed key negotiation protocol is 318.1 ms. Meanwhile, the key update costs for dynamic member joining and leaving are 2.8 ms and 1.9 ms respectively. The access success rate of the complete semantic attribute encryption scheme reaches 93.2%, the false matching rate is 0.4%, and the average matching time is 4.8 ms. After 200 rounds of federated training, the final accuracy of the adaptive aggregation mechanism reaches 71.8%. This favorable result is higher than 65.2% of FedAvg, 62.5% of DP-FedAvg, and 68.1% of Krum. Author: Shen, M.; Meng, J.; Peng, B.; Tang, X.; Wang, W.; Niyato, D.; Zhu, L.
Title: Casper: A Causality-Inspired Defense With Confounder Against Label Inference Attacks in Vertical Split Federated Learning
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security
Abstract Note: Vertical Split Federated Learning (VSFL) allows participants to collaboratively train a better model with different features vertically partitioned in the same sample space, where the model is divided into bottom model and top model by the cut layer, trained by passive and active participants respectively. However, in the process, the labels owned by the active participant will still be inferred or stolen by curious or malicious passive participants. In this paper, we propose Casper, a causality-inspired defense mechanism with a confounder against label inference attacks in VSFL. Casper first analyzes the feasibility of optimizing the training process in VSFL at the intervention level from a causal perspective. It then introduces a confounder consisting of cut layer output reconstruction and label obfuscation to disrupt the direct causality between cut layer outputs and labels. Additionally, we integrate selective discrepancy training to further ensure model utility by strategically balancing training between active and passive participants. Extensive experiments conducted on four datasets across different tasks demonstrate that Casper effectively preserves label privacy while maintaining model performance, significantly outperforming current advanced defending methods in VSFL.

Author: Kamepalli, M.; Mehmood, A.
Title: A Multi-Indicator Trust Framework for Detecting Byzantine Clients in Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Blockchain, and Internet of Things (AIBThings)
Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative model training across distributed clients while preserving data privacy, but its decentralized structure makes it vulnerable to Byzantine attacks in which malicious clients submit manipulated updates to degrade the global model. This paper presents a multi-indicator defense framework that assumes a benign, trusted head client holding local validation data to evaluate client updates using HDBSCAN-based clustering, direction analysis, magnitude analysis, and validation-based performance. The four indicators are combined into a unified trust score that is used to filter suspicious client updates prior to global aggregation.The framework is implemented using TensorFlow Federated and evaluated on a healthcare imaging dataset under combined label-flipping and backdoor attacks with malicious-client ratios ranging from 0 to 60%. In the experiment with nine malicious clients out of fifteen participants, the combined trust score achieved a precision of 0.9962, recall of 0.9815, false-positive rate of 0.0056, and F1-score of 0.9888. End-to-end evaluation further shows that trust-based filtering maintains stable global-model convergence across the evaluated attack ratios. The results demonstrate that combining multiple complementary indicators provides stronger and more balanced malicious-client detection than relying on any individual defense mechanism alone. Future work will extend the evaluation to controlled Non-IID data distributions, larger client populations, additional attack strategies, and comparisons with established Byzantine-robust aggregation methods.

Author: Lu, H.; Fan, K.; Guo, Z.; Zhang, K.; Li, H.
Title: When Blockchain and Federated Learning Hit it Off: Forging a Novel Proof of Useful Work
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing
Abstract Note: Traditional Proof-of-Work (PoW) consensus secures blockchains by incurring significant energy and resource wastage on solving valueless puzzles. The Proof-of-Useful-Work (PoUW) paradigm emerges to repurpose this effort for tasks of societal or scientific value. However, existing PoUW approaches face a critical trade-off between the work’s practical utility and its verifiability, as efficiently validating complex computations without full re-execution remains a major open problem. This paper proposes Proof-of-Useful-Federated-Work (PoUFW), a novel consensus protocol that resolves this dilemma by recasting the “work” as Federated Learning (FL) model aggregation. Specifically, PoUFW mandates that miners not only perform the aggregation, but also generate a cryptographic proof of its correctness. To achieve this, we propose a novel proof mechanism that builds upon the Kate-Zaverucha-Goldberg (KZG) polynomial commitment scheme to generate a concise, non-interactive proof. This mechanism enables validators to rapidly verify the aggregation’s integrity without re-executing the computation or accessing the underlying model. Consequently, PoUFW transforms the computational overhead of consensus into valuable, verifiable machine learning outcomes, while simultaneously establishing a decentralized, incentivized framework for FL. Rigorous theoretical analysis substantiates the protocol’s security and correctness. Extensive simulations further demonstrate that PoUFW achieves high verification efficiency alongside robust security, confirming its practical feasibility and scalability. This work provides a robust theoretical and empirical foundation for building blockchain systems with improved resource efficiency and societal value.

Author: Tang, Y.; Wang, K.; Niyato, D.; Chen, W.; Karagiannidis, G. K.
Title: Digital Twin-Assisted Federated Learning With Blockchain in Multi-Tier Computing Systems

Abstract Note: In Industry 4.0 systems, numerous resource-constrained Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) devices frequently exchange data for model training, raising serious security and privacy concerns. To address these issues, this paper proposes a digital twin (DT) and blockchain-assisted federated learning (FL) framework. In the proposed scheme, fog devices with sufficient computational resources generate DTs for edge devices to support local model training. We formulate an FL delay minimization problem that considers both model transmission and synchronization delays while introducing cooperative jamming to secure DT synchronization. To solve this non-convex problem, a decomposition-based optimization algorithm is developed. By introducing upper bounds on local training delay and jamming effects as auxiliary variables, the problem is transformed into a convex form that can be efficiently decomposed and solved. Furthermore, a blockchain-based verification mechanism and a validator selection algorithm are designed to ensure model integrity and participant authentication during the FL process, thereby enhancing blockchain scalability. The final global model is obtained by aggregating verified local updates through deep learning techniques. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed cooperative interference-based DT–blockchain-assisted FL framework outperforms benchmark schemes in execution time, block efficiency, and model accuracy.

Author: Xie, Z.; Lin, Y.; Gao, Z.; Fan, J.
Title: A Dual-Level Selective Unlearning Framework for Multi-Agent Decentralized Federated Learning
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking
Abstract Note: In agentic AI-enabled edge computing, decentralized federated learning (DFL) leverages peer-to-peer model aggregation to improve the performance of on-device large language models (LLMs) without introducing a single point of failure, thereby enhancing local agents’ capabilities for decision-making. To protect the right to be forgotten for each agent, as required by data regulations such as the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), federated unlearning aims to remove the influence of a target agent’s data from the trained LLM while preserving model utility. However, existing federated unlearning methods predominantly assume centralized architectures and face two critical challenges when extended to decentralized federated learning systems: 1) requiring all remaining agents to participate in the unlearning process incurs prohibitive overhead; and 2) updating all Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) modules indiscriminately leads to excessive resource consumption while potentially degrading model performance. To tackle these challenges, we propose a dual-level selective unlearning framework (DSU) for decentralized federated learning. At the agent level, DSU selects retained agents by matching historical LoRA update sketches, label sketches, and exposure to the withdrawn agent. Meanwhile, we derive a sensitivity score from the DFL training trajectory that measures each LoRA module’s accumulated influence from the target agent via the energy of its effective weight changes, and then update only the most sensitive modules while freezing the rest. Theoretical analysis relates selective unlearning to full-participation unlearning, and experiments show that DSU reduces the audited target-agent influence while preserving retained utility and reducing both participating agents and updated LoRA modules in the evaluated settings. The public reproducibility package is available at https://github.com/DGL-codes/LLM-DFL

Title: Latency-Sensitive Covert Federated Learning via UAV

Abstract Note: Federated learning (FL) can preserve data privacy; however, it is limited by the coverage of static edge servers deployed at wireless base stations. To minimize the FL latency while satisfying the covertness constraint, the trajectory of UAV can be dynamically adjusted along with the jamming power and the local accuracy, addressing the demands of latency-sensitive applications. Specifically, we propose an iterative algorithm to divide the original problem into two subproblems, which are alternately optimized via successive convex approximation until convergence. Numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed UAV-assisted covert FL scheme in minimizing the latency while guaranteeing the covertness.

Author: Gao, Y.; Chen, X.; Deng, H.; Xie, Y.; Chen, J.
Title: CVFL-Pro: A Collusion-Resistant Verification Federated Learning Framework With Adaptive Communication Optimization
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security
Abstract Note: Federated learning has gained significant attention for its ability to train models without directly accessing raw data. However, the malicious server may falsify the aggregation results to save computational resources. While existing verifiable federated learning methods can validate the results, they exacerbate communication bottlenecks and fail to achieve collusion-resistant verification in the absence of a trusted authority. In this paper, we propose CVFL-Pro, a collusion-resistant verification federated learning framework with adaptive communication optimization. Specifically, we utilize a mask and Shamir’s secret sharing for privacy protection, and it is robust against client dropout. We combine a lightweight MAC scheme and auxiliary nodes to achieve efficient verifiability. Furthermore, we design an adaptive communication optimization algorithm (AOTop- \k\ ), which dynamically adjusts the compression rate \p\ based on the gradient magnitude and the gradient variation between rounds, ensuring optimal performance with minimal cost. Finally, we instantiate CVFL-Pro and prove its correctness and security against collusion by up to \|N|-2\ clients (where \|N|\ is the total number of clients) and the server. Extensive evaluations on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100 datasets demonstrate that CVFL-Pro reduces communication overhead by 58.07% compared to the optimal Top- \k\ and 95.81% compared to SecAgg. Author: Linda, C. H.; Iram, F.; R, V.; Madugula, S. C.; P.Brinda; B.Jegajothi
Title: Retracted: Optimized Blockchain-Enabled Federated Hybrid Deep Learning Framework for Real-Time Intrusion Detection and Privacy-Preserving Data Governance

Abstract Note: With the rapid proliferation of Internet-of-Things (IoT) and smart cyber-–physical systems, the privacy preserving, trusted, and real time intrusion detection has experienced an extreme surge of demand. Traditional centralized deep learning methods have severe imperfections on data privacy, regulation, and communication overheads; and lightweight baselines such as CNNibased and LSTMbased are prone to overfit in heterogenous IoT environment. Inspired by the aforementioned issues, this paper proposes BC-FedHVAE-GAT – a high-performance Blockchain-Enhanced FedHVGA-GAT-GRU model with Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM) for learning stability. The model integrates hierarchical VAE-based latent encoding, attention mechanism guided graph learning and GRU module for temporal modeling that enables joint representation learning over heterogeneous network flows while also preserving device-level privacy via federated training. In our experiments, we compare the Inner Hybrid model with state-of-the-art baselines on all the models which in boldface are comparisons under their own training strategy, the accuracy of Inner Hybrid model is 88.1 %, compared to 87.1% and 86.7% of CNN and LSTM (best viewed in color). Author: Zhang, X.; Tang, Y.; Zhao, X.; Liu, X.; Liu, K.
Title: Research on a Decentralized Federated Learning Framework Based on Multi-Population Genetic Algorithm for Low-Voltage Distributed Photovoltaic Systems
Publication Title: 2026 7th International Conference on Energy Power and Automation Engineering (ICEPAE)
Abstract Note: To address the challenges of data privacy preservation, collaborative scheduling, and non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data in low-voltage distributed photovoltaic systems, this paper proposes a Multi-Population Decentralized Photovoltaic Federated Learning (MPDFL) framework, which integrates genetic algorithms with blockchain technology to enhance the robustness and security of distributed photovoltaic power forecasting models. First, decentralization is achieved by storing the global model on the blockchain. Second, population partitioning is introduced to enable parallel training, where nodes with similar data distributions are clustered together to mitigate the impact of non-IID data, with a genetic committee performing intra-population selection and aggregation to maintain diversity. Third, Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance consensus is combined to accomplish inter-population crossover and model uploading onto the blockchain, while a migration pool and a reputation-based incentive mechanism are constructed to reinforce attack resistance. Finally, experiments simulate scaling and same-value attacks targeting photovoltaic measurement data under various proportions of malicious clients, comparing MPDFL with Krum and BFL. Results show that MPDFL consistently achieves the optimal and most stable accuracy across all attack scenarios, with the smallest performance degradation, confirming its robustness and efficiency in decentralized low-voltage photovoltaic environments.

Author: Tourky, D.; Eletriby, S.; Keshk, A.; Enany, M. O. A.
Title: Beyond the Hype: Mapping Machine Learning Readiness Across Blockchain Attack Layers, Gaps, Trends, and a Roadmap

Abstract Note: For a decade, blockchain has been the leader in the technology revolution by providing decentralized concepts and an immutable ledger architecture for large-scale applications in different sectors such as finance, supply chain, and healthcare. This paper provides a comprehensive mapping of ML readiness across the multi-layered attack surface of blockchain technology. By analyzing the integration of ML techniques such as deep reinforcement learning, federated learning, and explainable AI (XAI). Author: Rahman, M. M.; Raza, S. Muhammad; Dey, S.; Islam, M. A.; Chatha, H.; Sulane, A.
Title: Federated Learning for Cross-Border FinTech Compliance: A TRACER-Based Framework for Auditable AML/KYC

Abstract Note: FinTech’s global expansion has outpaced harmonised cross-border regulation, resulting in fragmented oversight, jurisdictional conflicts, and rising challenges in AML/KYC, privacy, provenance, and auditability. Federated Learning (FL) and blockchain can support privacy-preserving collaboration, but typical deployments under-specify jurisdiction-aware controls and regulator-grade accountability. This paper introduces C-3F (Compliance-First Federated Framework), a conceptual federated AI architecture that embeds TRACER accountability (Trust, Reliability, Authenticity, Compliance, Enforceable Regulatory oversight) into cross-border FinTech platforms. C-3F integrates jurisdiction-aware policy enforcement, trust-anchored digital identity, authenticated data provenance, privacy-preserving auditability, and adaptive orchestration. A trust-weighted aggregation scheme adjusts client influence using compliance and data-quality signals. We illustrate the design through a cross-border AML/KYC scenario, demonstrating how privacy-preserving collaboration can be structured to remain traceable and legally interoperable. C-3F adopts a compliance-first philosophy that prioritises legal interoperability and enforceable accountability in federated FinTech systems.

Author: Kyriakoulis, N.; Varvarigou, D.; Dimopoulos, C.; Daniil, G.; Filippatos, N.; Tsiamoulis, G.; Kolliopoulos, A.; Denazis, S.; Lampropoulos, K.; Chatzopoulou, A.; Al-Naday, M.; Oprişa, C.
Title: SKYNET - Secure and Resilient Intelligent System for 6G Networked Services and Technologies
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Cyber Security and Resilience (CSR)
Abstract Note: Modern 6G service ecosystems operate across heterogeneous, multi-provider cloud-edge infrastructures where orchestration platforms dynamically compose distributed resources. However, security mechanisms remain largely decoupled from orchestration logic, typically enforced as static add-ons or reactive controls after service deployment. This separation limits the ability of networked systems to adapt to evolving attack surfaces and cross-domain dependencies. This paper presents SKYNET, an AI-assisted security framework designed to embed security directly into a dynamic service design and deployment. SKYNET analyzes the service specification and proposes a new “security-enhanced” specification that can be autonomously deployed across multiple contexts and domains. Then the service is continuously monitored throughout its life cycle and dynamic reconfigurations are automatically triggered by incidents or requirement changes.

Author: Zhao, Y.; Wan, Z.; Guan, Z.; Li, G.; Guo, M.
Title: ClusterGuard: Secure Clustered Aggregation for Federated Learning With Robustness
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing
Abstract Note: Federated Learning, as a multi-party machine learning paradigm, has garnered significant attention, but model updates may still leak sensitive information. Secure aggregation protocols are considered an effective solution for privacy protection in Federated Learning. However, in large-scale federated learning systems, designing efficient and practical secure aggregation remains a critical challenge. Moreover, while secure aggregation effectively conceals model updates, it unintentionally complicates the detection and mitigation of poisoning attacks, thereby exposing the system to vulnerabilities from both data and model poisoning. To address these challenges, we propose ClusterGuard, a secure clustered aggregation scheme. ClusterGuard leverages Verifiable Random Function (VRF) to ensure fair and transparent client clustering. Within each cluster, it employs a lightweight key-homomorphic masking mechanism combined with verifiable secret sharing to enable secure and efficient aggregation. Furthermore, we design a dual filtering mechanism based on cosine similarity and norm to effectively detect and resist poisoning attacks. We provide two variants of ClusterGuard for both client-server and decentralized environments with blockchains, respectively. Extensive experiments on standard datasets demonstrate that ClusterGuard achieves over \2\textbackslash{}times\2× efficiency improvement compared to advanced secure aggregation methods. Even with 20% of clients being malicious, the trained model maintains accuracy comparable to the original model, outperforming state-of-the-art robustness solutions. ClusterGuard provides a more efficient, secure, and robust solution for practical federated learning.
Manual Tags: Federated learning; secure aggregation; Byzantine robustness

Author: Wang, L.; Zhu, F.; Xu, F.; Bao, L.; Hussain, A.; Aurangzeb, K.; Zhong, Y.
Title: AI-Resistant Data Theft Prevention for Consumer Electronics via Context Aware Obfuscation and Post-Quantum Blind Signature
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Consumer Electronics
Abstract Note: The deep integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into Consumer Electronic (CE) systems has greatly enhanced service intelligence, yet poses substantial risks of AI-driven data theft. Existing privacy-preserving approaches often face the dilemma of balancing security, computational efficiency, and compatibility with resource constrained CE devices, failing to effectively combat adaptive AI-driven data theft attacks. To tackle this critical challenge, we propose an AI-resistant data theft prevention scheme for CE systems, which innovatively integrates context aware code obfuscation (CACO) and revised lattice-based post-quantum blind signature to construct a synergistic defense mechanism. Specifically, we design a tailored obfuscation mechanism for AI modules in CE devices by fusing dynamic opaque predicates, context aware control flow flattening, and semantic encryption. This mechanism undermines AI-powered reverse engineering and adversarial sample generation, thereby blocking core attack paths of AI-driven data theft. We also incorporate a lattice-based blind signature scheme to leverage the post-quantum security of lattice cryptography, which safeguards data privacy during transmission authentication and robustly defends against AI-driven interception and correlation attacks. Extensive comparative experiments on benchmark CE platforms demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves the highest resistance rate against state-of-the-art AI-driven data theft attacks, with its computational cost and communication delay reduced by more than 20% compared with existing hybrid solutions. This work establishes a unified end-to-end AI-resistant privacy protection framework and offers a new benchmark for balancing security, efficiency, and compatibility in CE systems.

Author: Arab, A.; Jaber, G.; Mouhoub, N.; Bouabdallah, A.
Title: MLTF-IoT: A Machine Learning-based Trust Framework for IoT
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Smart Sustainable Systems for Computer and Engineering Applications (3SCEA)
Abstract Note: The proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices in critical infrastructures introduces significant security challenges, particularly in establishing and maintaining trust relationships in dynamic network environments. Traditional trust management approaches rely on rule-based systems or simple threshold mechanisms that fail to capture the complex behavioral patterns indicative of malicious activities. To address this issue, we propose MLTF-IoT, a novel Machine Learning-based Trust Framework for IoT that leverages stacking ensemble learning for direct trust prediction with explainable behavioral analysis. Our framework integrates a 20-feature behavioral model organized into three groups: network traffic features, derived behavioral features, and contextual features. The trust prediction is performed by a stacking ensemble combining XGBoost and Random Forest as base learners with Logistic Regression as meta-learner, enhanced with SHAP-based explainability for transparent decision-making. Extensive experiments on the CICIoT2023 dataset demonstrate that MLTF-IoT achieves 98.59% accuracy, 99.49% AUC-ROC, and 99.93% detection rate with zero false alarm rate, outperforming traditional machine learning baselines. The ablation study reveals that derived behavioral features contribute 75.6% to prediction performance, validating our behavioral modeling approach. MLTF-IoT provides a robust, interpretable, and efficient solution for trust management in IoT environments.
Manual Tags: IoT; Machine Learning; Explainable AI; Trust Management; Stacking Ensemble

Author: P, J.; K, H.; K, M. R.; S, S.
Title: Privacy-Preserving Healthcare Imaging using Color Secret Sharing with AI-Driven Hybrid Image Reconstruction Algorithm
Publication Title: 2026 7th International Conference on Inventive Research in Computing Applications (ICIRCA)
Abstract Note: The swift expansion of digital healthcare systems and AI-powered medical imaging has established an immediate demand both in secure and privacy-conscious and smart image processing architectures. Medical records and images of patients are highly sensitive and should not be exposed to any unauthorized view and manipulation. In order to overcome these issues, this paper suggests a multi-layered secure healthcare imaging system that includes 3 joint procedures: Adaptive Hybrid Image Preprocessing Engine (AHIPE) to improve the quality of images and minimize noise; Secure Cryptographic Hybrid Color Secret Sharing (SCHSS) to encrypt and share the image data with high-entropy secret sharing; and AI-Driven Hybrid Image Reconstruction Algorithm (AIHIRA) to reconstruct images, extract features, and make them true to diagnosis. The hybrid framework guarantees the security of encoding, high-level encryption, AI-powered reconstruction, and effective processing. Author: Tauseef, M.; Malini, A. S.; R, U. A.; B, H. J. R.; Santhoshkumar, S. P.; Arora, P.
Title: Blockchain-Assisted Federated Deep Reinforcement Learning (B-FDRL) for Trustworthy Spectrum Allocation in 5G Cognitive Radio Networks
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE 5th World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
Abstract Note: The issue of effective and secure spectrum allocation is a substantial challenge in 5G cognitive radio networks. Author: Huang, Y.; Tiwari, A.; Yen, I.-L.; Bastani, F.
Title: A Blockchain Aided Resource/Role Hierarchy Based Access Control Framework for Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Advances in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (AAIML)
Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative model training while preserving data privacy by keeping raw data decentralized. However, FL privacy requires careful management. ACRRH jointly leverages role hierarchies and resource hierarchies (RRH) to enable group-level permission assignment and hierarchical propagation, significantly reducing security administration overhead in large-scale FL deployments. With the blockchain aided access validation and logging, we define the Blockchain-Aided ACRRH (BARRH) protocol. Author: Zhu, S.; Sun, C.; Zhang, H.; Wang, L.
Title: IIN-Health: A Dual-Chain Federated Learning Framework with Adaptive BFT Consensus for Auditable Medical Data Sharing
Publication Title: Intelligent and Converged Networks
Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) is increasingly deployed in healthcare to enable collaborative intelligence while keeping sensitive data privately at local institutions. However, existing healthcare-oriented FL frameworks still suffer from several limitations: they are vulnerable to adversarial model updates, provide limited transparency and verifiable auditability, and often lack predictable performance under constrained resources. We present IIN-Health, a blockchain-enhanced intelligent fusion network tailored for dependable healthcare FL. IIN-Health adopts a dual-chain architecture with policy-aware access control and auditable provenance tracking to integrate learning, security, and governance in a unified framework. Evidence-Carrying Access Tokens (ECATs), combined with zero-knowledge proofs, are introduced to enforce patient-defined policies and validate access decisions without disclosing sensitive information. In addition, we design MedBFT-Δt a domain-specific Byzantine fault-tolerant protocol that ensures reliable system behavior in the presence of faulty or malicious participants. We conduct several experiments to validate its feasibility and accuracy on the MNIST dataset. The results demonstrate that IIN-Health achieves smooth and stable convergence, exhibits strong resilience against poisoning attacks, and maintains graceful performance degradation under resource constraints, while preserving verifiable auditability of model updates and data flows. These observations indicate that IIN-Health can provide a practical balance among performance, security, and regulatory compliance, and thus offers a promising foundation for trustworthy and scalable FL deployments in healthcare.

Author: Durgaprasad, S.; Abdul, A. M.

Abstract Note: Static rule-based systems are examples of traditional security measures that frequently fail to detect sophisticated assaults like privilege escalation, insider threats, and data breaches. Author: Zhao, B.; Guo, W.; Chen, J.; Xiao, Y.; Zhai, L.; Pei, Q.
Title: FedInf: An Efficient and Secure Inference With Federated Participants
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Computers
Abstract Note: Federated learning is a machine learning paradigm through training on locally private data and aggregating local models to generate a federated model. However, due to the heterogeneity problems (data heterogeneity and model heterogeneity), federated learning suffers from convergence difficulties and excessive aggregation overhead on decentralized participants. Additionally, federated learning faces privacy concerns during the aggregation of local models. To this end, in this work, we propose FedInf, an efficient and secure inference with federated participants. Specifically, FedInf features the following characteristics. FedInf overcomes convergence challenges through federated inference instead of federated training, which reduces computation and communication overhead. Moreover, we design secure computation protocols and aggregation mechanisms to measure contributions, and handle both data and model heterogeneity without sacrificing privacy. Results of experimental evaluations on common datasets demonstrate that the proposed FedInf outperforms the existing federated learning approaches in terms of efficiency and heterogeneity.

Author: Wang, Z.
Title: A Verifiable Accountable Anonymous Authentication Interface for Cross-Silo Federated Learning
Publication Title: IEEE Access
Abstract Note: Cross-silo federated learning must reconcile update authentication, routine identity privacy, and auditable accountability across independently operated institutions. Ordinary digital signatures provide direct attribution but expose the signer of every benign update. Secure aggregation and robust learning address complementary confidentiality and robustness goals, yet they typically do not provide a publicly verifiable interface for post-incident attribution and revocation. We present A3FL, a verifiable accountable anonymous authentication interface for cross-silo federated learning, motivated by regulated institutional collaboration. The interface defines canonical transcripts that bind the payload hash, the complete round context (including the transparency-log digest), registry state, nullifier, auditor-committee key, opening policy, trace ciphertext, and opening evidence. A client proves that an update comes from an authorized, active member without disclosing its identity. An atomic per-round registry-version pin, combined with a round-local nullifier, detects duplicate submissions. A policy-valid incident request and verifiable shares from a threshold quorum of auditors enable publicly verifiable opening and registry-based revocation with respect to the historical state. We instantiate the interface with a Groth16/Edwards backend and implement a prototype that covers registry freshness, duplicate filtering, authorized public opening, revocation, and adversarial transcript validation. Experiments across institutional-scale registry sizes quantify the control-plane costs of anonymous admission, authorized opening, revocation, and the proof backend. A multi-scenario poisoning case study demonstrates how the policy-gated accountability path responds to different incident-evidence conditions.

Author: Paripally, K.; Hossain, G.
