Author: Kumar, S. S.; R, R. K.; K, A. S.; K, E. S.; A, A. N.; P.R, A.

Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Multidisciplinary Innovations For Smart & Sustainable Future (MISSF)
Abstract Note: The rapid urbanisation of Thrissur has increased traffic congestion, air pollution, unpredictable vehicle movements, and inefficiency of older fixed-time signal systems. The system tracks the density of traffic, number of vehicles, length of queues, speed, road occupancy, congestion indices, CO2 emissions, and fuel consumption with low power consumption due to distributed sensing. Edge gateways are used to process data in order to reduce latency, blockchain is used to maintain immutable and tamperproof sensor logs, events, and control commands to enhance trust and security, and Federated Learning is used to train model parameters privately through sharing only parameter updates with prediction accuracies over 93%. Author: Lakshmanan, M.; Ashtankar, N.; Dhanraj, J. A.; R, S.; Tamilamuthan, R.; Hole, S. R.
Title: Privacy-Preserving Federated Blockchain with Adaptive Merkle Compression for Cross-Hospital EHR and AI Model Exchange
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Communication, Computing and Emerging Technologies (IC3ET)
Abstract Note: Cross-hospital EHRs and AI models exchange within secure federated blockchain settings, although obstructed by privacy intricacies and large overheads owing to stoarge requirements as well as absence of model provenance verifiability, remain a prominent challenge. This work proposes a privacypreserving federation blockchain architecture that achieves interoperability by sharing EHR and AI models across hospitals through Advance Merkle Compression (AMC) and homomorphic gradient authentication. AMC has therefore been suggested for dynamically condensing low-entropy Merkle sub-trees, changing hashes for scalability improvement reducing blockchain network overload; on the other hand, homomorphic proof of models encourages verifiability in relation to model update so long the sensitive input remains unknown. The research implementation has been shown by using Hyperledger Fabric and PySyft federated learning on the MIMIC-III dataset across four hospital nodes. Complimentarily, the system has removed 42 % of the information transmission overhead, reducing model-goodness satisfaction margin to 97.5% in regular training with regard to a 15% reduction in latency. Upon data privacy weighting, the failure of preservation was included; 100% of the parameters will be retained within the most severely constrained differential privacy level checked at \textbackslash{}varepsilon<1.0\. By implementing this new approach, investigators have created an enormous potential for any future scalability concern and the ability to handle DP-empowered federated intelligence within a multitude of hospital settings.

Author: Dabhade, D. S.; Thorat, N. N.
Title: Data-Driven Quantum-Inspired Deep Learning Model for Cyber Threat Identification in Imbalanced Security Datasets
Publication Title: 2026 1st International Conference on Computer, Mechatronics, Robotics & Artificial Intelligence (ICCMRAI)
Abstract Note: The expanding digital ecosystem has created increasingly sophisticated cyberattack surfaces, exposing critical infrastructures such as cloud platforms, Internet of Things (IoT) networks, healthcare systems, smart grids, block chain environments, and cyber-physical systems to advanced security threats. Existing rule-driven security mechanisms and conventional artificial intelligence models often encounter limitations when processing large-scale heterogeneous data, identifying emerging attack patterns, and maintaining real-time detection efficiency. This survey explores the role of scalable Quantum Neural Network (QNN) paradigms in strengthening cyber threat identification by synthesizing findings exclusively from the selected reference studies. The review encompasses a broad spectrum of cybersecurity intelligence techniques, including traditional intrusion detection approaches, machine learning and deep learning frameworks, quantum-enhanced learning models, hybrid quantum-classical architectures, quantum reinforcement learning strategies, federated intelligence mechanisms, and post-quantum security solutions. Analysis of the surveyed literature reveals that quantum-inspired approaches can improve the detection and mitigation of diverse cyber threats, including DDoS attacks, ransomware campaigns, malicious web activities, IoT-based intrusions, block chain vulnerabilities, and healthcare data breaches. Nevertheless, widespread implementation remains challenging due to hardware noise in current quantum devices, restricted availability of quantum-ready datasets, scalability concerns, and the lack of universally accepted benchmarking protocols. Motivated by these observations, the paper outlines a future-oriented scalable QNN-based cyber threat identification framework that integrates quantum state encoding, vibrational learning circuits, federated collaboration, intelligent response optimization through reinforcement learning, and post-quantum cryptographic protection to support resilient next-generation cybersecurity systems.

Author: Szabó, M.; Toka, L.
Title: Blockchain-Assisted Reliable Federated Learning in 5G-Powered Vehicular Systems
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
Abstract Note: The transformation of transport systems increasingly relies on connecting vehicles into cooperative networks, promising to reduce traffic congestion, lower emissions, and enhance road safety. Achieving these benefits requires efficient sharing of high definition (HD) map information across vehicles. Federated learning (FL) enables vehicles to collaboratively train shared models for HD maps, supporting accurate localization and dynamic environment understanding, without transferring raw data, thus preserving privacy. However, implementing FL in this context faces significant challenges: malicious participants can disrupt learning, and honest participants may disengage without sufficient incentives. To address these issues, we propose integrating a dual blockchain framework with FL, which evaluates participant reliability, weights contributions accordingly, and provides financial incentives to maintain engagement. This coordinated approach ensures that only trustworthy information contributes to HD map updates, preserving both data privacy and system integrity. By modeling and optimizing the system’s economic utility, and validating through simulations, we demonstrate that the framework is feasible under realistic settings when reward and subscription fees are appropriately calibrated, providing a robust foundation for secure, incentivized, and privacy preserving vehicular networks.

Author: Hao, P.; Liu, Z.; Liu, J.; Sun, G.
Title: Sustainable Incentive for Model Trading in Decentralized and Personalized Federated Learning via DAG-Blockchain Consensus
Publication Title: ICASSP 2026 - 2026 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP)
Abstract Note: Decentralized and personalized federated learning (DPFL) enables collaborative model training across data silos but faces challenges in establishing a sustainable incentive and model trading framework. We propose a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG)-blockchain-based trading framework with sustainable incentives. The framework introduces the Cumulative Reward (CR) model to ensure royalties for model usage and coupling incentives with consensus. Author: Sankar, V.; Murugesan, R.; Gopalan, A.
Title: Blockchain based Secure Data Sharing for Glucose Prediction in IoMT Scenario using Deep Learning
Publication Title: 2026 5th International Conference on Innovative Mechanisms for Industry Applications (ICIMIA)
Abstract Note: The growth of Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) systems makes the continuous health monitoring as the feasible task. Still, the challenges related to data security, privacy and requirement of efficient predictive outcome degrades the performance. To address the challenges, this research proposed the glucose prediction with blockchain technology based on cryptographic hashing and optimization-based key generation along with federated learning-based prediction. Author: Kamble, S.; Bansod, S.
Title: Smart Contract-Driven Detection of Data Poisoning Attacks in Federated Learning for IoT Security
Publication Title: 2026 11th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) enables distributed model training across IoT devices without exposing raw data, yet remains critically vulnerable to data poisoning attacks in which malicious participants corrupt the global model by manipulating local training labels. A two-layer defense framework is proposed for detecting and mitigating label-flipping attacks in FL-based IoT environments. The first layer employs gradient-delta cosine similarity analysis to identify anomalous client updates by comparing each client's gradient update direction against a coordinate-wise median reference computed across all participating clients. The second layer enforces immutable verification decisions through a simulated Ethereum smart contract, which computes SHA-256 hashes of gradient updates, logs all verification events on-chain, and maintains client reputation scores across communication rounds. The framework is evaluated on a synthetic N-BaIoT network traffic dataset distributed across 10 federated clients, of which 50% are designated as malicious label-flipping adversaries. Experimental results demonstrate that standard FedAvg aggregation under label-flipping attack degrades global model accuracy from 99.30% to 54.40%, a drop of 44.90 percentage points. The proposed defense recovers accuracy to 98.85%, representing a gain of 44.45 percentage points over the undefended scenario and within 0.45 percentage points of the clean baseline. The smart contract layer introduces an average overhead of 360,000 gas units per round at a latency of 0.080 ms, confirming feasibility for resource-constrained IoT deployments. Results demonstrate that blockchain-enforced gradient verification provides a robust, auditable, and lightweight defense against data poisoning in federated IoT networks.

Author: Zhang, M.; Zhao, M.; Wang, W.; Zheng, T.; Wang, B.
Title: BadPromptFL: Parameters-Free Backdoor Attack on Vision-Language Federated Learning
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology
Abstract Note: Prompt-based tuning has emerged as a lightweight alternative to full fine-tuning in large vision-language models, enabling efficient adaptation via learned contextual prompts. This paradigm has recently been extended to federated learning settings, where clients collaboratively train prompts under data privacy constraints. However, the security implications of prompt-based aggregation in federated multimodal learning remain largely underexplored, leaving this paradigm vulnerable to prompt-space attacks. In this paper, we introduce BadPromptFL, the first model-parameter-free backdoor attack specifically targeting prompt-based federated learning in vision-language models. Instead of manipulating model weights, BadPromptFL introduces a parameter-free alternating optimization mechanism where malicious clients jointly update stealthy visual triggers and local prompt embeddings to force malicious alignment in the contrastive latent space. Through private collusion, these clients construct a coherent global trigger, crafting poisoned prompts that remain statistically similar to benign ones to covertly hijack the global prompt aggregation process. By jointly optimizing image perturbations with prompts, BadPromptFL activates the backdoor in a manner that is highly effective and difficult to detect. Additionally, we demonstrate that the injected backdoor achieves reliable convergence within the federated learning framework, explaining why malicious prompt updates can be incorporated into the global prompt without causing divergent training behavior. By leveraging the contextual learning behavior of CLIP-style architectures, BadPromptFL delivers high attack success rates (e.g., > 90%) with minimal visibility and limited client participation. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks and aggregation settings further validate the effectiveness, stealth, and adaptability of our method, revealing important security risks in prompt-based federated learning systems. Author: Bouchiha, M. A.; Rabah, M.; Champagnat, R.; Korba, A. A.; Ghamri-Doudane, Y.
Title: \textbackslash{}mathsf {DARTIC}\: Decentralized Anonymous Reputation at Scale for Trustworthy Crowdsourcing
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Services Computing
Abstract Note: On-chain crowdsourcing leverages blockchain’s decentralization, transparency, and tamper-resistance to build trustworthy and verifiable Web3 crowdsourced services. However, existing decentralized reputation frameworks do not reconcile anonymity, reputation binding, and scalability. This paper demonstrates how on-chain crowdsourcing can simultaneously achieve these requirements under a trust-minimized model. We introduce \textbackslash{}mathsf {DARTIC}\DARTIC, a decentralized, anonymous, and scalable reputation-driven framework for crowdsourcing. \textbackslash{}mathsf {DARTIC}\DARTIC presents a dual-ledger system that enables requesters and workers to use distinct pseudonyms across interactions, ensuring unlinkability while maintaining accountability. To mitigate Sybil and reputation-reset attacks, we employ zkSNARK-based set membership proofs, cryptographically binding all user pseudonyms to a single access token without revealing the linkage. For scalability, we investigate two aggregation techniques that compress multiple proofs into a single succinct proof to minimize verification overhead. In addition, we design an automated, privacy-preserving reputation model that dynamically evaluates contributions across diverse crowdsourcing contexts. To demonstrate practicality, we instantiate and assess \textbackslash{}mathsf {DARTIC}\DARTIC in both crowdsensing and federated learning scenarios. Experimental results show that (i) individual proof generation for token spending completes in less than 3 s, (ii) aggregation reduces the verification time of 1024 proofs from 8.7 s to 0.96 s, and (iii) zk-batching lowers gas costs by more than 100× compared to a pure Layer-1 deployment. Author: Lan, H.; Sun, Y.; Huang, T.; Lei, H.
Title: AdaComm: Adaptive Committee Sizing for Resilient and Efficient Decentralized Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2026 6th International Symposium on Computer Technology and Information Science (ISCTIS)
Abstract Note: Federated learning allows multiple clients to train a shared model without transferring their raw data to a central server, but this privacy advantage does not prevent malicious participants from submitting harmful updates. In committee-based decentralized federated learning, one practical difficulty is that the committee size is usually fixed in advance. A large committee improves screening, but it also adds persistent validation cost. A small committee is cheaper to run, yet it can be unreliable when attacks become concentrated. We address this problem with AdaComm, a committee mechanism that changes its size during training instead of keeping it constant. The adjustment is driven by a consensus divergence signal derived from the disagreement among committee members when they score submitted gradients. When that disagreement rises, AdaComm expands the committee for stronger validation; when it stays low, the committee is reduced to save resources. In our experiments on MNIST and CIFAR-10 under label-flipping and back-gradient attacks, AdaComm achieved the best final accuracy among the compared methods, including 98.28% on MNIST and 68.30% on CIFAR-10 in the label-flipping setting. Title: TrustHFL: An Efficient Aggregation Method for Trustworthy Hierarchical Federated Learning

Author: Thiyagarajan, C.; Ganaselvi, J. A.; Venkatraman, K.
Title: AIDefender: An AI-Powered Proactive Auditing and Threat Mitigation Framework for Decentralized Storage Networks

Abstract Note: Decentralized Storage Networks (DSNs) face a critical security limitation: their reliance on periodic cryptographic proofs (PoRep/PoSt) creates a reactive model with inherent “detection lag,” leaving them vulnerable to sophisticated, slow-burn attacks, such as targeted data withholding and gradual corruption. Author: Shen, S.; Li, M.; Shen, Y.; Dong, J.; Ke, W.; Deng, R.; Wang, T.
Title: DeSPU: Privacy-Compliant Decentralized Sparse Personalized Federated Unlearning for Edge Intelligence-Enabled IoT Networks
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
Abstract Note: Edge intelligence-enabled Internet of Things (Edge-IoT) increasingly relies on decentralized on-device learning to reduce cloud dependence and keep locally collected IoT data on terminal devices. However, deployed models may still memorize privacy-sensitive class-level knowledge and must support deletion requests after training. This paper studies class-level federated unlearning in a serverless Edge-IoT workflow where each IoT client maintains a sparse personalized IoT-local model and exchanges model information only with neighbors. We propose DeSPU, a decentralized sparse personalized federated unlearning framework under a practical deletion-window protocol. DeSPU estimates a target-class direction with a lightweight dual-model mechanism, applies semantic-layer adaptive linear unlearning to suppress target knowledge, and performs topology-aware local repair regularized by cached neighbor snapshots collected during routine peer-to-peer training. The online unlearning path does not store historical gradients and does not introduce additional post-request model communication beyond routine decentralized exchanges; the one-time \textbackslash{}beta \ calibration scan is reported separately, and the calibrated \textbackslash{}beta \ can be reused under the same configuration. To propagate deletion status beyond the requester, DeSPU also attaches a metadata-only forgetting flag to those routine exchanges and invalidates affected cached neighbor References at receiving clients. Experiments on CIFAR-10, MNIST, CIFAR-100, and CINIC-10 show near-zero target-class accuracy with high retained accuracy, up to \textbackslash{}sim 4.7\textbackslash{}times 10^{3}\ speedup over full retraining on CIFAR-10, and membership-inference ROC-AUC close to random guessing. Additional analyses over seeds, requester clients, target classes, cache staleness, sparsity, communication, and hardware cost further demonstrate the practicality and limitations of DeSPU for privacy-compliant Edge-IoT deployments. Abstract Note: In the rapidly evolving landscape of Internet of Things (IoT), ensuring secure and privacy-preserving biometric authentication for wearable devices is a critical challenge. The research paper introduces a new paradigm, which combines multi-modal biometric acquisition (ECG, PPG, gait) with a Sparse Phase Encoded representation and Ternary Chaos Map-based cancelable transformation. Homomorphic Encryption is used to achieve secure matching and a Federated Siamese Network with Gradient Obfuscation is used to train models to protect biometric model updates. Lightweight blockchain provides a traceability of authentication logs that do not leak data. Experimental performance on benchmark datasets has shown higher level of performance, whereby the proposed system recorded an authentication accuracy of 98.4% and Equal error rate of 1.4% and a cancelability of 9.6/10. The framework has better security, which does not have a high resource load as compared to current CNN, Transformer, and standard Federated models and is therefore suitable in real-time deployment across the Internet of things. Such a combined solution proves that privacy-first biometric authentication is possible in a decentralized setting. The solution is compliant with international standards of privacy and provides a platform on which similar deployments of the future in the healthcare, defense, and consumer wearable sectors can be based.

Author: Yang, Y.; Zhu, D.; Ning, J.; Feng, Q.; Li, X.; Cheng, Y.; Yang, G.; Ren, K.
Title: Private Set Intersection: A Systematic Review
Publication Title: Chinese Journal of Electronics
Abstract Note: Various services, such as search engines, are increasingly deployed in cloud-based and distributed systems. However, data are typically managed by trusted servers, making user privacy and data security critical concerns. Private set intersection (PSI) is a powerful cryptographic primitive that enables multiple parties to compute the intersection of their datasets without revealing private inputs. It has been extensively studied over the past two decades, leading to significant gains in computational and communication efficiency. Yet, in many real-world scenarios, revealing the raw intersection may still leak sensitive information. To address this, numerous PSI variants have been developed to meet different application needs. In this paper, we present a comprehensive survey of PSI and its variants. We categorize existing protocols by functionality and underlying cryptographic techniques and analyze their theoretical properties. We focus on recent developments from the last five years, including emerging directions such as fuzzy PSI and updatable PSI. We also explore applications of these protocols across various domains. Finally, we identify key research challenges, including improving privacy guarantees, enhancing computational efficiency, and ensuring scalability for large-scale datasets. These findings aim to guide future research, as PSI and its variants play a central role in advancing privacy-preserving applications.
Manual Tags: Private set intersection; Multiparty computation

Author: Ndebele, P.; Akoamah, A. K. A.; Kumar, P.
Title: Integrating AI and IoT in Smart Healthcare Monitoring: Improving Data Privacy and Security During Medical Emergencies in Real-Time
Publication Title: 2026 Eight International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Communication Technologies (CCICT)
Abstract Note: IoT-based healthcare systems have critical security issues, especially during emergency situations where data access is critical and network activity is high, providing attackers with possible cyber threats. The purpose of this paper is to offer a review of blockchain and AI-based methods for privacy and securing IoT-based healthcare systems during emergency scenarios. The paper evaluates different blockchain architectures, smart contracts, machine learning based intrusion detection, federated learning, and explainable AI. A robust security framework is offered, which is a combination of the two techniques that can be employed to offer improved IoT-based healthcare security. An experiment was conducted using simulated data in which the framework demonstrated 96.8% Accuracy with the UNSW-NB15 dataset and an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.98, which demonstrated that the framework is better than applying these techniques individually. Other challenges like computational complexity, interoperability and legal issues have also been brought up. Author: Wu, C.-W.; Hsu, W.-C.; Lien, Y.-A.; Huang, S.-H.; Chou, L.-D.
Title: Conformal Label-Transition Auditing Against Label-Flipping Attacks in Trust-Aware Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2026 8th International Conference on Computer Communication and the Internet (ICCCI)
Abstract Note: Federated learning enables collaborative model training across distributed clients without sharing raw data, but its decentralized nature makes it vulnerable to poisoning attacks from untrusted participants. In tabular-data scenarios, label-flipping attacks are particularly challenging because poisoned samples may preserve normal feature distributions while corrupting the relationship between features and labels. This paper proposes Conformal Label-Transition Auditing (CLTA), a data-side auditing method for trust-aware federated learning. CLTA constructs class-wise nonconformity distributions and label-transition references from clean calibration data using an Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) teacher model. During client auditing, it computes conformal p-values, suspicious transition pairs, and data quality scores to identify abnormal labeltransition behavior before model aggregation. Under poisoned federated learning with two malicious clients, CLTA improves accuracy from 49.38% to 77.93% and restores AUC from 0.9035 to 0.9687. These results demonstrate that CLTA provides a statistically calibrated and traceable defense mechanism for robust federated learning on tabular data.

Author: Calo, J.; Lo, B.
Title: Proof of Reasoning for Privacy-Enhanced Federated Blockchain Learning at the Edge
Publication Title: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
Abstract Note: Consensus mechanisms are the core of any blockchain system. However, the majority of these mechanisms do not target federated learning (FL) directly, nor do they aid in the aggregation step. This article introduces proof of reasoning (PoR), a novel consensus mechanism specifically designed for FL using blockchain, aimed at preserving data privacy, defending against malicious attacks, and enhancing the validation of participating networks. Unlike generic blockchain consensus mechanisms commonly found in the literature, PoR integrates three distinct processes tailored for FL. First, a masked autoencoder (MAE) is trained to generate an encoder that functions as a feature map and obfuscates input data, rendering it resistant to human reconstruction and model inversion attacks. Second, a downstream classifier is trained at the edge, receiving input from the trained encoder. The downstream network’s weights, a single encoded datapoint, the network’s output, and the ground truth are then added to a block for federated aggregation. Lastly, this data facilitates the aggregation of all participating networks, enabling more complex and verifiable aggregation methods than previously possible. This three-stage process results in more robust networks with significantly reduced computational complexity, maintaining high accuracy by training only the downstream classifier at the edge. PoR scales to large Internet of Things (IoT) networks with low latency and storage growth, and adapts to evolving data, regulations, and network conditions.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; Internet of Things (IoT); privacy; machine learning; edge computing; healthcare; distributed computing; federated

Author: Prasad, G. B.; Rao, M. V.
Title: A Scalable Blockchain-IPFS Architecture for Encrypted Electronic Medical Records with Rolebased Smart Contract

Abstract Note: EMRs play a significant role in healthcare delivery and present a significant threat as far as privacy and security is concerned. Conventional central storage is likely to be hacked and accessed non-accessibly, and manipulated too. This paper presents a blockchain system (a smart contract) to have secure, privacy-preserving and decentralized EMR management. The model is integrated with Ethereum smart contracts to apply role-based access control, off-chain storage with IPFS which can be expanded to support large files and cryptography tools (AES-256 encryption and SHA-256 hashing) to provide confidentiality and integrity of data. The analysis experimentally demonstrates that the encryption time of files (\textbackslash{}mathbf{5 M B}\) to \textbackslash{}mathbf{6, 0 0 0 m s} (120 \textbackslash{}text{MB})\ is directly proportional to 250 ms and retrieval time of files using IPFS is minimal \(150 \textbackslash{}text{ms}\ to \3,000 \textbackslash{}text{ms})\. Metadata storage and verification of access to metadata remain effective in gas consumption and roll-based access control is powerful at auditability. It is very resistant to replay, collusion and intrusion attempts and this offers more security, transparency and efficiency in operation compared to the traditional system of operation. It is an option, which can be scaled and is able to meet the future work being undertaken to improve federated learning in order to increase privacy-preserving healthcare analytics.

Author: Runwal, T.; Moger, T.; Saini, D. K. J. B.; Kumar, H.
Title: Securing the Smart Grid: A Comprehensive Survey of AI-Driven Anomaly Detection for Cyber-Physical System Protection
Publication Title: 2026 Smart Technologies for Energy, Sustainability & Industry (STESI)
Abstract Note: The transformation of traditional power systems into Smart Grids through digitalization has created essential security weaknesses. Security systems struggle to protect against advanced threats which include False Data Injection Attacks and Denial-of-Service attacks. The survey delivers complete Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning techniques assessment which researchers use for detecting anomalous behavior. Our research studies methods which include physics-aware modeling and decentralized systems that use Federated Learning and Blockchain technology. The evaluation assesses self-healing infrastructure development through our study of Digital Twins and 6G security systems and secure data aggregation. Our study uses real-time SCADA testbeds to assess how cyber-attacks disrupt system controllability. The synthesis presents current research deficiencies which include adversarial robustness and explainable AI to create a research base that helps researchers improve security and reliability of upcoming cyber-physical energy systems against international security threats. The survey emphasizes the necessity of cross-layer resilience to protect the backbone of modern energy infrastructures from sophisticated multi-vector adversarial campaigns.

Author: Yang, J.; Govindarajan, V.; Khan, M. Attique; Shaikh, Z. Ahmed; Alsenan, S.; Li, Y.; Por, L. Yee; Zhang, Z.; Guo, Q.
Title: CardioTwin-XAI: A Consumer-Centric Digital Twin Framework for Predictive Risk Stratification and Personalized Management of Coronary Artery Disease in Healthcare 5.0
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Consumer Electronics
Abstract Note: Consumer-Centric Digital Twins (CCDT) are emerging as transformative enablers in Healthcare 5.0, offering real-time monitoring, predictive analytics, and patient-specific treatment optimization. This paper introduces CardioTwin-XAI, a novel AI-driven CCDT framework designed for early detection, risk prediction, and personalized management of Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) and related conditions such as atherosclerosis, myocardial infarction (MI), and heart failure (HF). The proposed system integrates IoT-enabled wearable sensors, continuous hemodynamic profiling, and federated multimodal learning to build a dynamic, patient-specific digital replica. The key innovation of CardioTwin-XAI is its unified integration of explainable AI (XAI) with privacy-preserving federated learning, wherein interpretable attribution mechanisms are embedded within distributed model updates, enabling transparent predictions without compromising data confidentiality across healthcare institutions. A hybrid transformer-GNN architecture captures complex spatiotemporal cardiovascular dynamics, while differential privacy and blockchain-based data sharing ensure regulatory compliance. Evaluation on multi-institutional datasets demonstrates 92.6% accuracy in CAD prediction, 31% improvement in treatment planning efficiency, and 40% reduction in unnecessary interventions. Author: Pietri, M.; Martinelli, M.; Turazza, F.; Bertacchini, G.; Picone, M.; Mamei, M.
Title: Digital Twins and Federated Learning in Industrial IoT: Worker-Centric Safety Perspectives
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE 23rd Consumer Communications & Networking Conference (CCNC)
Abstract Note: This paper surveys the integration of Digital Twins (DT) and Federated Learning (FL) in Industrial IoT (IIoT), highlighting opportunities for real-time monitoring, predictive analytics and distributed intelligence. Author: Raj, Y.; Manikandan
Title: Hybrid LSTM-GNN-Driven Blockchain Framework for Secure IoT Device Authentication and Predictive Data Intelligence
Publication Title: 2026 7th International Conference On Computational Vision and Bio Inspired Computing (ICCVBIC)
Abstract Note: This study proposes a hybrid LSTM-GNN-driven blockchain framework for secure IoT device authentication and predictive data intelligence. The framework integrates a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network for temporal anomaly detection, a Graph Neural Network (GNN) for structural anomaly detection, and a blockchain-based trust-management layer that records device identity and communication activity through smart contracts. As the primary contribution of this work, the proposed framework is evaluated independently on a simulated IoT testbed of 500 heterogeneous devices: the LSTM branch achieves 97.0% temporal anomaly detection accuracy (MAE 0.147, RMSE 0.212), the GNN branch achieves a structural anomaly F1-score of 88.9%, and the blockchain trust-management layer sustains a mean latency of 49.9 ms across all 500 simulated devices. To validate the discriminative strength of the underlying feature-engineering pipeline, five classical machine-learning classifiers K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Decision Tree (DT), Gradient Boosting (GB), Extra Trees (ET), and Random Forest (RF) are additionally benchmarked on the NSL-KDD dataset using ExtraTreesClassifier-based feature selection, SMOTE oversampling, and 5-fold cross-validation, with Random Forest attaining the highest binary classification accuracy of 99.92% (F1 = 99.92%) and multi-class accuracy of 99.93%. These NSL-KDD results serve solely as supporting evidence for the engineered feature-preprocessing pipeline and do not, by themselves, validate the proposed hybrid architecture; the framework-level LSTM, GNN, and blockchain metrics remain the central evidence for the paper's claimed contribution. The findings demonstrate that combining deep learning-based behavioral analysis with blockchain-based decentralized trust management provides a scalable and trustworthy foundation for future IoT security systems.

Author: Zha, J.; Zhang, G.; Jin, L.; Dang, S.; Duan, W.
Title: Lightweight Privacy-Preserving IDS for ITS: Integrated Federated Learning and Blockchain
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
Abstract Note: As intelligent transportation systems (ITS) become more integrated into modern infrastructure, vehicular communication systems face increasing cybersecurity threats. Traditional centralized intrusion detection system (IDS) has significant limitations in terms of the scalability, privacy preservation, and trust establishment, which are critical challenges in ITS environments. To address these issues, this paper proposes an intrusion detection method tailored specifically for ITS, integrating federated learning (FL) and blockchain technology to create a secure, scalable, and privacy-preserving threat detection system for the Internet of Vehicle (IoV). The proposed method utilizes FL for distributed model training, avoiding the sharing of raw data and employing encryption techniques to protect user privacy at the edge devices. Blockchain technology ensures the integrity and tamper-proof nature of model updates and fosters trust between entities. Moreover, to accommodate the heterogeneous and dynamic data environment in IoV, the method supports both independent and identically distributed (IID) and non-IID data scenarios, enhancing the system’s adaptability and robustness. Given the computational limitations of vehicular devices, this work incorporates knowledge distillation and lightweight model designs, effectively reducing the local computational burden. Experimental results demonstrate the significant effectiveness of the proposed approach: on the CICIDS2017 dataset, the model achieves an accuracy of 97.10% with 11,904 parameters and a memory consumption of 0.045MB; on the Car-Hacking dataset, it achieves an accuracy of 99.10% with 9,989 parameters and a memory consumption of 0.038MB; on the CICIoV2024 dataset, it achieves an accuracy of 99.65% with 9,861 parameters and a memory consumption of 0.038MB. Compared to traditional baseline models, the proposed approach significantly reduces both the number of training parameters and memory consumption, while maintaining high accuracy, making it highly suitable for deployment in resource-constrained vehicular environments within ITS.

Author: Chai, T.; Han, K.; Shin, S.
Title: Blockchain-Based Decentralized Edge Intelligence Collaboration and Adaptive Incentive Mechanism Research
Publication Title: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
Abstract Note: Edge Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) learning suffers from non-IID data, stragglers, and untrusted coordination that raise latency, energy, and variance. Our objective is to enable reliable, privacy-preserving, and low-latency collaborative learning for edge IIoT under these conditions. We present BEACON, which couples federated learning (FL) with a CTDE-MADDPG adaptive incentive on a permissioned blockchain, uses lightweight robust aggregation (FedProx/Krum/Trimmed-Mean), and anchors only hashes on-chain for audit while keeping model payloads off-chain. The system runs over heterogeneous LoRa/Wi-Fi links and supports optional differential-privacy noise and Byzantine-tolerant modes. On a Raspberry Pi testbed and 10–100-node simulations, BEACON improves task completion and accuracy while lowering latency and CPU/energy relative to a static-incentive approach; the blockchain overhead remains modest at a 1-s block time. We also report sensitivity to reward weights and non-IID levels and outline deployment limits with practical mitigations. Compared with a static-incentive baseline, BEACON increases task completion by 19.7% and throughput by 15.4% while reducing latency by 24.8% and CPU usage by 22.6% under identical budgets; improvements are statistically significant.

Author: Ramal, P. J.; Anbalagan, E.
Title: Blockchain-Enabled Secure and Interoperable Digital Twin Framework for Sustainable Industry 5.0 Smart Cities

Abstract Note: Industry 5.0 also focuses on the human-machine collaboration, sustainability, and resilience in urban ecosystems, in which Digital Twin (DT) technology is crucial to ensure real-time monitoring, forecasting, and optimization. Interoperability, scalability, and data security are problematic to large-scale installations of smart cities. To implement smart cities based on Industry 5.0, this paper proposes a Blockchain-Enabled Secure and Interoperable Digital Twin Framework to ensure trusted, efficient, and sustainability in its operations. The framework involves the use of blockchain technology to provide interoperability between different urban subsystems in terms of cross-domain data sharing, tamper-proofed data sharing, and decentralized trust management. The system applies hybrid deep learning to help make advanced decisions: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) in relational dependency optimization in energy and transportation grids, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models in sequential traffic and energy demand prediction, and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) in spatiotemporal feature extraction. An edge-cloud collaborative architecture ensures the scalable and low-latency provision of DTs in different smart city domains. The proposed framework, compared to traditional cloud-only DT systems, predicts traffic flows with 96.4% accuracy, energy demand with 93.7% and can reduce latency by 37 % based on experimental results, using simulated data of a smart city. Blockchain integration boosts data integrity by 99.2, reduces cybersecurity issues by 42 and speeds up cross-platform interoperability 28 times. Also, it enables the city-scale management cost reduction by 25 percent, operational energy consumption reduction by 21 percent, and carbon emission reduction by 18 percent, which is the purpose of safe, intelligent, and sustainable smart cities. The framework will form the foundation of the Industry 5.0 by addressing critical concerns in dependable data exchange, real-time predictive intelligence, and resource optimization that will be sustainable.

Author: Safa, H.; Vanshika; Saud, T.; Kirmani, S. N. J.; Ronihal, S. S.
Title: A Secure Model for Detecting Credit Card Fraud Using Machine Learning and Blockchain
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE Global Symposium on Emerging and Communication Technologies (GSEACT)
Abstract Note: Credit card scams continue to pose a major problem in today's digital payment systems. This leads to serious financial losses and raises security concerns. While machine learning (ML) techniques have proven effective in detecting fraudulent transactions, many current methods rely on centralised data storage. This kind of storage is vulnerable to tampering and lacks long-term auditability. To overcome these obstacles, this paper presents a secure hybrid structure that blends machine learning-based fraud detection with cryptographic hashing and blockchain for permanent storage. In this system, transaction data gets analysed using supervised ML models to classify transactions as fraudulent or legitimate. The classification result, along with key transaction details, is protected using the SHA-512 cryptographic hash function, ensuring data integrity. The generated hash is then permanently saved on an Ethereum-based blockchain created using Ganache and smart contracts. It provides a permanent, verifiable history that anyone can audit. Instead of just getting a “yes” or “no” from an algorithm, we get a clear look at the “why”- both for individual transactions and across the entire system. When we tested this on real-world European credit card data, the results were clear: it doesn't just catch fraud reliably; it builds trust. By layering machine learning with blockchain and cryptography.

Author: Xu, X.; Yin, S.
Title: FedADP: A Private Quantile-Adaptive Clipping Mechanism for Imbalanced Federated Intrusion Detection
Publication Title: 2026 6th International Conference on Computer Science and Blockchain (CCSB)
Abstract Note: Federated learning enables collaborative intrusion detection without centralizing raw network traffic, but strict differential privacy may further amplify minority-class degradation under imbalanced and non-IID traffic distributions. This paper presents FedADP, an adaptive differential privacy framework for federated intrusion detection, with FedADP-PQ as its core private quantile-adaptive clipping mechanism. Instead of using a fixed clipping threshold, FedADP-PQ privately estimates a local gradient-norm quantile from noisy histogram statistics and constrains the threshold within public clipping bounds for conservative privacy accounting. Experiments on CIC-IDS2017 under strict per-sample DP-SGD and Rényi DP accounting show that FedADP-PQ improves the stability of minority attack detection under a comparable privacy budget. Compared with fixed DP clipping, FedADP-PQ improves attack recall from 74.87% ± 11.80% to 78.03% ± 2.13% and attack F1-score from 82.10% ± 5.83% to 83.93% ± 1.23%, with ϵ ≈ 9.14 at δ = 10–6. These results suggest that private adaptive clipping helps stabilize attack-class detection when DP noise and traffic imbalance are jointly present.

Author: Anitha, A.; Nikita; Kiran, U.
Title: A Comprehensive Review of Blockchain-Based Access Control and Authentication Mechanisms in IoT-Assisted Smart Healthcare Systems
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Secure IoT and Cybersecurity (ICOSICS)
Abstract Note: Blockchain is a distributed system that helps to secure data transactions. It is a decentralized design that makes it useful for ensuring safe and scalable communication between the Internet of Things (IoT) devices. Since IoT often depends on remote sharing and data protection, access control becomes a major security concern. Traditional access control methods often difficult to apply in IoT environments because many devices have limited computing power. Researchers have explored how blockchain can strengthen IoT security ever since the technology emerged. In healthcare, for example, conventional e-health systems allow Electronic Health Records (EHRs) to be shared among the providers, but they also create risks such as unauthorized access and data leaks. With IoT, the challenges grow even bigger, managing privacy and concurrency across a large number of lightweight, distributed devices is more complex. Centralized access control system cannot always be trusted to guarantee security in each setting. A systematic survey is presented in this work to review existing approaches used for access control and authentication in IoT-based healthcare environments. Various models, including role-based, attribute-based, and blockchain-based access control models, are analyzed to ensure their effectiveness and scalability. Moreover, cryptographic methods used for authentication purposes in the existing works are explored. Key limitations like high computational overhead, vulnerability to attacks, and lack of standardization in the conventional access control and authentication methods are reviewed. At last, the growing demands and future ideas for implementing secure and highly efficient models for smart healthcare IoT networks are listed.

Author: Shen, M.; Peng, B.; Zhao, Y.; Qin, Y.; Li, M.; Li, Q.; Zhu, L.
Title: Byzantine-Robust Asynchronous Federated Learning via Feature Fingerprinting
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security
Abstract Note: Asynchronous federated learning (AFL) accelerates collaborative training across heterogeneous devices compared to synchronous federated learning, but increases vulnerability to Byzantine attacks due to its asynchronous aggregation. Existing defenses rely on parametric similarity between models and temporal consistency of updates, which are compromised by data and device heterogeneity, leading to ineffective robustness. To address this limitation, we propose Belisa, a Byzantine-robust AFL framework that enhances fidelity, robustness, and efficiency under heterogeneous scenarios. Belisa introduces novel discrepancies between feature representations of local models to distinguish malicious models from benign ones. By leveraging a reference model trained on publicly available data, Belisa quantifies these discrepancies, referred to as feature fingerprints, and filters out malicious models through clustering. Extensive experiments on six datasets from three types of tasks under five advanced Byzantine attacks demonstrate Belisa’s superiority. Notably, Belisa consistently outperforms existing approaches across both attack and non-attack settings. Under attack scenarios, it lowers the average test error rate to \0.42\textbackslash{}times \ that of baseline methods. Furthermore, Belisa accelerates the aggregation process by an average of \12.3\textbackslash{}times \ compared to other methods. To the best of our knowledge, Belisa is the first Byzantine-robust AFL framework, which provides a broadly applicable countermeasure in heterogeneous scenarios which are more prevalent in real-world settings.

Author: Chouhan, B.; Sharma, A.; Pathak, H.; Raj, R.; Gopi, A.; Joshi, A. P.
Title: A Comprehensive Review of Cybersecurity in 5G and 6G Networks: SDN, NFV, Slicing, and Massive IoT Security
Publication Title: 2026 13th International Conference on Computing for Sustainable Global Development (INDIACom)
Abstract Note: The advancement from 5G through 6G networks has brought sophisticated new features like network softwarization, virtualization and intelligent automation, while at the same time increasing the surface area of cybersecurity dangers. This paper provides a high-level insight in clearly presenting a thorough review of all security challenges in Software-Defined Networking (SDN), Network Function Virtualization (NFV) and network slicing and massive Internet of Things (IoT) deployments in next generation networks. The vulnerability assessment systematically examines architectural vulnerabilities, new attack vectors, and the limited ability of today's use of protective mechanisms in three segments of the settlement control as well as in the data and management plane. Based on a comprehensive study of the latest literature, the latter highlights important security issues, such as controller compromise, poorly executed slice isolation, virtual attacks, and AI attacks. Furthermore, it discusses of the existing measures to mitigate these vulnerabilities, such as blockchain-based trust management, federated learning, secure orchestration, and post-quantum cryptography. The findings underscore the need for integrated, adaptive and intelligence-driven security frameworks for resilience in the future 6G ecosystems. This work is a consolidating information for researchers and practitioners that wish to design secure, scalable and trustworthy next generation networks.

Author: Pathan, Z.; Obaidat, M. S.; Patel, T.; Chavda, S.; Hathaliya, J.; Nair, A.; Gupta, R.; Tanwar, S.
Title: FedChain: Blockchain-assisted Federated Learning Framework for Secure Resource Allocation in Device-to-Device Communication
Publication Title: ICC 2026 - IEEE International Conference on Communications
Abstract Note: In this paper, we propose FedChain, a secure and decentralized blockchain-enabled federated learning (FL) framework for resource allocation (RA) in device-to-device (D2D) communication networks. Traditional D2D RA methods are based on centralized processing, which introduces privacy risks, single-point failures, and limited scalability. FL decentralizes model training, but remains vulnerable to model tampering and insecure parameter exchange between clients and the server. To overcome these challenges, FedChain integrates a permissioned Hyperledger Fabric (HF) blockchain to provide traceable, auditable, and tamper-proof model update transactions. Additionally, the interplanetary file system (IPFS) is employed to store model parameters off-chain, while only their cryptographic content identifiers (CIDs) are recorded on-chain to minimize blockchain storage overhead. The framework applies federated averaging (FedAvg) for collaborative model aggregation without exposing raw data. An experimental evaluation compared the results of 5 models, where Fedchain achieves >95% global accuracy using Random Forest (RF) and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) algorithms. It helps improve security, tamper-resistance, model consistency, and communication efficiency. These results indicate that FedChain offers a scalable and secure foundation for decentralized RA in future 6G-enabled D2D networks.
Manual Tags: federated learning; Hyperledger Fabric; IPFS; model aggregation; Resource allocation; D2D communication

Author: Tang, J.; Dai, Z.; Wu, L.; Sun, P.; Chen, H.
Title: Robust Client–Server Watermarking for Split Federated Learning
Publication Title: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
Abstract Note: Split federated learning (SFL) is renowned for its low computational overhead, extremely suitable for resource-constrained edge computing scenarios while inheriting privacy-preserving characteristics from federated learning (FL). In this framework, clients employ lightweight models to process private data locally and transmit intermediate outputs to a powerful server for further computation. However, SFL is a double-edged sword: while it enables edge computing and enhances privacy, it also introduces intellectual property ambiguity as both clients and the server jointly contribute to training. Existing watermarking techniques fail to protect both sides since no single participant possesses the complete model. To address this, we propose a robust model intellectual property protection scheme using client–server watermark embedding (RISE) for SFL. Specifically, RISE adopts an asymmetric client–server watermarking design: the server embeds feature-based watermarks through a loss regularization term, while clients embed backdoor-based watermarks by injecting predefined trigger samples into private datasets. This co-embedding strategy enables both clients and the server to verify model ownership. Experimental results on standard datasets and multiple network architectures show that RISE achieves over 95% watermark detection rate ( \p\ -value \textbackslash{}lt {\textbackslash{},}0.03\ ) across most settings. It exhibits no mutual interference between client- and server-side watermarks and remains robust against common removal attacks. Our source code is available at GitHub

Author: Li, Z.; Tong, Y.; Wang, Y.; Chang, Y.
Title: Blockchain quantitative credit rating method integrating knowledge graphs and federated learning: privacy-preserving risk assessment for supply chain finance

Abstract Note: With the exponential growth of cross-institutional data in Supply Chain Finance (SCF), traditional centralized credit assessment models struggle to achieve high-precision default risk prediction while maintaining strict accounting data privacy. Author: Yin, Z.; Wang, H.; Liu, C.; Ding, Y.; Li, K.; Li, K.
Title: EBFL: An Efficient Blockchain Framework for Federated Learning Services

Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as a key framework to deliver AI services, recognized for its capability to construct global models while ensuring individual data. Nevertheless, FL heavily relies on a central server, which introduces significant challenges for participants to collaborate effectively and substantially limits the scalability of FL. Blockchain-based FL (BFL) offers a promising solution by replacing the central server with a decentralized blockchain system, thereby establishing a secure and trustworthy environment for FL. However, current BFL approaches face challenges in balancing high computational overhead, consistency, and security. In view of this, this paper introduces EBFL, an efficient blockchain framework for FL services. EBFL incorporates both asynchronous and synchronous advantages. A DAG-based (Directed Acyclic Graph) asynchronous computation enhances computational efficiency by mitigating delays caused by slow devices and reducing unnecessary waiting due to frequent synchronized consensus. Simultaneously, a periodic synchronized consensus mechanism is introduced during asynchronous training to ensure consistency, thereby improving security and model accuracy. Additionally, taking into account the unique characteristics of FL, we have designed a series of operations tailored for EBFL to further enhance the performance. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared to traditional synchronous BFL (TBFL) approaches, EBFL achieved a maximum speedup of up to \2.38\textbackslash{}times\2.38× while retaining 92% of their accuracy. Subsequently, in-depth analytical experiments show that EBFL excels in both convergence speed and security, thereby confirming its potential to balance computational efficiency, consistency, and security.

Author: Shan, X.; Yu, H.; Wang, G.; Chen, Y.; Yang, Z.
Title: AMBER: Robust Federated Learning Based on Client Verification
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security
Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) preserves data privacy by avoiding direct access to local data, but this limits server verification of client model updates. Unreliable participants can inject malformed updates to poison the global model without detection. In this paper, we analyze client-side vulnerabilities in three chained stages of local training: local dataset pollution, model selective inputs, and training process tampering. We refer to this class of threats as Local Chained Attacks (LCAs), which severely degrade global model robustness. To address these challenges, we propose AMBER, a robust FL framework with a novel three-layer verification mechanism for client trust assessment. The first layer ensures dataset integrity via vector commitments for content and distribution of client-held data. The second layer detects selective input attacks through a local consistency-based verification mechanism. The third layer enforces computational integrity by verifying the correlation between model inputs and outputs using secure primitives in a Trusted Execution Environment (TEE). AMBER establishes verifiable integrity links across data, input, and computation stages under an explicit trust boundary. Experimental evaluations covering multiple datasets, models, and attack scenarios show AMBER outperforms existing approaches in defense effectiveness with low overhead, adapting well to Non-IID environments.

Author: Qi, Q.; Lei, Y.; Li, Y.; Li, H.; Zhou, Q.
Title: CPFL: A Cluster-Based Parallel Blockchain Scheme for Secure and Efficient Federated Learning in Intelligent Connected Vehicles

Abstract Note: The rapid evolution of Intelligent Connected Vehicles (ICVs) has transformed automobiles into data-rich edge nodes, enabled by progress in artificial intelligence (AI), federated learning (FL), and 5G-enabled communication. While FL facilitates privacy-preserving model training by retaining data locally, its practical deployment in ICVs faces two key challenges: vulnerability to malicious parameter updates and degraded convergence under non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data. To address these issues, this paper proposes a secure and efficient cluster-based blockchain scheme for Byzantine resilience and model synchronization of FL. The scheme introduces a mainchain for periodic global model aggregation and multiple subchains that coordinate localized training. These subchains dynamically group vehicles into clusters based on the similarity of their model parameters, which is quantified using the Wasserstein distance. This clustering approach effectively handles non-IID data by ensuring that similar nodes train together. Each subchain employs a hybrid consensus protocol, combining stake-weighted validator election with the Byzantine fault-tolerant HotStuff BFT consensus, to robustly validate local models. Malicious updates are filtered using a combination of distance-based aggregation and gradient thresholding. Furthermore, a dynamic reputation mechanism incentivizes reliable participation through token staking and behavior-based rewards. Extensive experiments on MNIST and CIFAR-10 datasets demonstrate our scheme’s superiority over traditional FL methods, particularly in mitigating the impacts of non-IID data and Byzantine attacks.

This approach fundamentally rebalances the energy–accuracy trade space through layerwise quantization sensitivity analysis and radiation-hardened field programmable gate array (FPGA) acceleration. Third, the framework pioneers task-parallel federated updates through decomposed aggregation primitives, enabling simultaneous intraplane model merging and cross-plane gradient validation. Experimental validation across orbital hardware testbeds demonstrates how these architectural innovations collectively resolve the decentralization–security–efficiency trilemma: maintaining 98.7% model fidelity with 3.5× energy reduction versus FP32 baselines while achieving Byzantine fault tolerance through our stochastic proof-of-stake protocol. By redefining the coordination mechanisms and numerical foundations of spaceborne AI, AstraFL establishes an improved paradigm for autonomous learning in next-generation satellite constellations.

Title: Advances and Open Challenges in Federated Foundation Models

Abstract Note: The integration of Foundation Models (FMs) with Federated Learning (FL) presents a transformative paradigm in Artificial Intelligence (AI). Author: Kang, H.; Zhang, C.
Title: KI-SL: An Efficient and Secure Knowledge Index-Based Swarm Learning Method of Data Collaboration
Publication Title: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
Abstract Note: The rapid development of the Internet of Vehicles (IoV) plays a pivotal role in the construction of efficient intelligent transportation systems (ITSs). However, its heterogeneous data collaboration process faces multiple challenges, such as insufficient collaboration efficiency, low communication efficiency, and difficulties in data privacy protection. To address these issues, this study proposes an efficient and secure knowledge index-based swarm learning (KI-SL) method of data collaboration. First, we construct an SL framework based on blockchain identity authentication. Second, a knowledge distillation based on knowledge index (KDKI) algorithm is proposed, constructing the knowledge index via hash encoding to enable cross-node knowledge sharing, establishing association relationships by combining local adjacency lists with nearest neighbor search, and designing an asynchronous distillation mechanism to realize dynamic knowledge updates. In addition, an adaptive sample selection and prototype optimization strategy is introduced, and secure broadcast of the knowledge index is realized through blockchain, thereby improving model performance and reducing communication overhead. Furthermore, a quantization differential privacy algorithm is presented, which applies stochastic quantization to the refined gradients and superimposes Laplacian noise to strengthen data privacy protection. Finally, experimental validation was conducted on real public datasets. The results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves maximum model accuracies of 89.21% and 92.78%. Author: Li, J.; Chen, Y.; Zhao, Q.; Cai, J.; Teng, S.; Wu, N.
Title: EdgeBatch: Efficient Decentralized Batch Verification for Edge Data Integrity via Reputation-Aware Combination Selection
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing
Abstract Note: Data integrity verification in geographically distributed edge systems remains a critical unsolved challenge. While centralized verification introduces bottlenecks and single points of failure, existing decentralized alternatives suffer from inefficiency due to their lack of batch verification capabilities. This limitation leads to prohibitive communication and computational overheads that scale poorly as data volume grows. This paper introduces EdgeBatch, the first decentralized protocol designed for efficient batch integrity verification, reducing communication rounds from \textbackslash{}mathcal {O}(n)\O(n) to \textbackslash{}mathcal {O}(1)\O(1) a small, constant number. At its core is a reputation-aware Combination Selection Algorithm (CSA), a polynomial-time heuristic that identifies near-optimal peer server combinations, balancing verifier group size against servers’ historical trustworthiness through intelligent pruning strategies. This process is orchestrated through distributed ledger technology and smart contracts, ensuring a secure, transparent, and trustless verification environment. The protocol’s design is underpinned by rigorous theoretical analysis, including formal proofs of security and correctness, and a probabilistic model for optimizing key system parameters. Extensive simulations show that EdgeBatch drastically outperforms state-of-the-art methods; it improves computational efficiency by an average of 518.60× over EdgeWatch and 1030.93× over CooperEDI, while also reducing communication overhead by 296.68× and 62.66×, respectively. A concluding ablation study confirms the vital role of our reputation mechanism, demonstrating it reduces the required verification rounds by 73% and is the key to the protocol’s efficiency.

Author: Sharma, A.; Jangwal, T.

Abstract Note: Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) is a quickly developing kind of modern healthcare, allowing to monitor patients remotely and analyze the data in real-time. Exponential growth of inter-connected medical devices, however, has created a paradox of critical security: although strong security is needed to guarantee protection of sensitive physiological data, standard security protocols including traditional Zero Trust frameworks and heavy cryptography requirements, are frequently computationally infeasible on resource-constrained hardware. Implantable sensors and wearables, often with small battery capacities (\<500 \textbackslash{}text{mAh}\) and cheap microcontrollers, have a high potential of uncontrollable failure when subjected to constant authentication. This paper gives an in-depth overview of lightweight Zero Trust architectures and energy-efficient protocols that were published between 2024 and 2025 with the sole purpose of alleviating this bottleneck. We take a look at the recent developments in lightweight cryptography (such as SPECK and Montgomery Ladder-optimized ECC), security that uses hardware assistance (Physical Unclonable Functions) and adaptable system architecture. We find that our comparative study shows that with the transition to optimized algorithms like SPECK the energy consumption can be as low as 1.68 mWh per session and novel system-level structures like SEES-IoMT show a 29% lowering of the total network energy consumption than state of the art approaches. We conclude that the future of secure IoMT is hybrid solutions that unite lightweight algorithms with edge intelligence so that the integrity of data can be ensured without having adverse effects on the performance of the devices.

Author: Xing, Z.; Zhang, Z.; Zhang, Z.; Li, Z.; Li, M.; Liu, J.; Zhang, Z.; Zhao, Y.; Sun, Q.; Zhu, L.; Russello, G.
Title: Zero-Knowledge Proof-Based Verifiable Decentralized Machine Learning in Communication Network: A Comprehensive Survey
Publication Title: IEEE Communications Surveys & Tutorials
Abstract Note: Over recent decades, machine learning has significantly advanced network communication, enabling improved decision-making, user behavior analysis, and fault detection. Simultaneously, the growth of communication networks has facilitated the efficient collection of large-scale training data. Traditional centralized machine learning, however, requires collecting data from users, raising significant concerns about privacy and security. Decentralized approaches, where participants exchange computation results instead of raw private data, mitigate these risks but introduce challenges related to trust and verifiability. A critical issue arises: How can one ensure the integrity and validity of computation results shared by other participants? Existing survey articles predominantly address security and privacy concerns in decentralized machine learning, whereas this survey uniquely highlights the emerging issue of verifiability. Recognizing the critical role of zero-knowledge proofs in ensuring verifiability, we present a comprehensive review of Zero-Knowledge Proof-based Verifiable Machine Learning (ZKP-VML). To clarify the research problem, we present a definition of ZKP-VML consisting of four algorithms and several key security properties. In addition, we provide an overview of the current research landscape by systematically organizing the research timeline and categorizing existing schemes based on their security properties. Furthermore, through an in-depth analysis of each existing scheme, we summarize their technical contributions and optimization strategies, aiming to uncover common design principles underlying ZKP-VML schemes. Building on the reviews and analysis presented, we identify current research challenges and suggest future research directions. To the best of our knowledge, this is the most comprehensive survey to date on verifiable decentralized machine learning and ZKP-VML.

Author: Kanchana, D.; Agoramoorthy, M.
Title: Transparent and Responsible Blockchain Framework for Secure Financial Fraud Detection

Abstract Note: The high rate of digitization of financial services has both increased the possibilities of honest business and created highly efficient means of unlawful actions, such as identity theft, payment fraud, transaction laundering, and synthetic identity fraud. This research offers a Transparent and Responsible Blockchain Framework to a Unified Fraud Detection Architecture to address these challenges. The framework guarantees the end-to-end transaction traceability, decentralization of the fraud alert validation, automated smart contract-based intervention, and auditable decision trails which meet regulatory requirements on transparency and accountability. The proposed model has the potential to convert the fragmented, opaque fraud detection infrastructures to trustworthy, verifiable and ethically optimized systems. It is experimentally proven to show significant increases in fraud detection precision, false positive minimization, traceability of a trace and readiness to comply with regulations when compared to the conventional centralized and rule based methods. The framework is conducive of multi-sector applicability in the banking sector, the insurance sector, the payment processing sector, the cryptocurrency exchanges sector, and the antimoney laundering (AML) compliance. Author: Mahmud, M. I.; Bieniek, J.; Rahouti, M.; Chehri, A.; Jeon, G.
Title: Toward Trustworthy Consumer-Centric IoMT: Reputation-Driven Federated Learning for Secure Medical Data Sharing
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Consumer Electronics
Abstract Note: Consumer Electronics (CE) devices (e.g., wearables and in-home monitors) generate sensitive health/activity data, but centralization in consumer-centric Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) is impractical due to privacy, communication, energy, and regulatory constraints. Federated learning (FL) enables cross-device training on CE/gateways yet remains vulnerable to poisoning, Sybil attacks, inference risks, and unreliable clients. We propose a blockchain-enabled FL architecture that uses a permissioned blockchain for identity, access control, auditability, and incentives, while keeping compute-intensive model updates off-chain for scalability. A novel reputation-based mechanism scores client updates via validation improvement, cross-round consistency, and plausibility checks, updates reputations, and enforces access, incentives, and slashing; robust aggregation, differential privacy, secure aggregation, and communication compression further mitigate adversaries and bandwidth limits. We compare seven reputation scoring methods, Weighted Average, Beta Reputation, Fuzzy Trust, Tanh Utility, Exponential Decay, Entropy-based, and Cosine Similarity, and evaluate on representative IoMT tasks/datasets, demonstrating feasible, secure, privacy-preserving, and auditable learning for next-generation consumer healthcare CE ecosystems.

Author: Rapaka, U.; Vandana, K.; P, R.; Jayanthi, L.; Lakshmi, C. S.; Sravanthi, D.
Title: A Decentralized and Secure Financial Intelligence Framework using Blockchain-Enabled Federated AI
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE World Skills Conference on Universal Data Analytics and Sciences (WorldSUAS)
Abstract Note: Banking, financial services and insurance (BFSI) is a dynamic industry which is on a high speed of adopting innovations of advanced digital technologies to enhance fraud detection, risk management as well as regulatory compliance. However, the traditional centralized AI systems have severe limitations, including the inability to provide privacy of the information and vulnerability to manipulations and inability to control the audit. To address these issues, the paper will propose a Federated AI Framework which already has inbuilt blockchain technology and which will integrate predictive power of Artificial Intelligence with security and transparency of blockchain technology. The model is designed into five main layers: (1) Data Acquisition, (2) Federated AI Training, (3) Blockchain Ledger, (4) Consensus and Incentive, and (5) Security and Compliance. Federated learning is a technology that enables various financial institutions to cooperate, train shared AI models, without exposing sensitive information, and with blockchain ensuring tamper-proof recording, contributions verifiable, and decentralized trust. Author: Jiang, X.; Cheng, Y.; Yang, J.; Song, Z.; Yang, Z.; Yao, L.
Title: Empowering Industrial Federated Learning: Blockchain-Based Model Validation and Incentive Mechanism
Publication Title: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
Abstract Note: In modern industry, industrial federated learning (IFL) has emerged as a promising framework for enabling privacy-preserving machine learning collaboration among factories to eliminate data silos. However, in the IFL setting, the central server may maliciously manipulate the global model by favoring specific clients or launching poisoning attacks. Similarly, malicious clients may degrade the model performance or exploit the system through free-riding, undermining fairness and stability. This article, for the first time, proposes a Blockchain-based Validation and Incentive Mechanism (BVIM) to address these critical challenges. BVIM innovatively integrates blockchain technology with the IFL framework: on the one hand, it removes the dependence on a central server through decentralization, ensuring transparency and traceability in the collaboration process; on the other hand, it incorporates a model validation strategy into the IFL workflow, enabling robustness even when up to half of the participating clients are malicious. Moreover, BVIM penalizes clients engaged in poisoning or free-riding behaviors while rewarding honest participants who contribute valuable local data and computational resources, thus establishing a fair and efficient incentive mechanism. Extensive experiments on the Tennessee–Eastman process (TEP) dataset, non-independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) TEP partitions, and Fashion-MNIST show that BVIM achieves robust model validation, stable global convergence, and contribution-aware incentives under different attack settings. We further compare BVIM with representative defense baselines and analyze the communication overhead introduced by blockchain operations. The results validate the design goals of BVIM and pave the way for the broader adoption of IFL in interfactory data sharing and collaborative machine learning, fostering a more secure, trustworthy, and cooperative industrial ecosystem.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; federated learning; model validation; incentive mechanism

Author: Luo, F.; Wu, J.; Wang, H.; Yan, X.
Title: FreeFL: Privacy-Preserving Cross-Silo Federated Learning Without Third Party
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing
Abstract Note: Cross-silo federated learning (FL) allows organizations to collaboratively train machine learning (ML) models by aggregating local gradients from clients without sharing their training data. Despite its merits, it suffers from privacy concerns due to the leakage of local gradients. A popular approach is to have clients mask their local gradients using homomorphic encryption (HE). However, this not only results in a reliance on a trusted third party (TTP), but also leads to significant computational and communication overhead. In addition, in existing cross-silo FL protocols, the aggregation operation is performed by a centralized aggregator, raising new security issues. One of these issues involves verifying the correctness of the aggregated results returned by the aggregator. The aggregator has been removed in the cross-device setting by leveraging blockchain technology, but not in the cross-silo setting. In this paper, we propose FreeFL, an efficient privacy-preserving cross-silo FL that eliminates the need for the TTP and aggregator, as well as achieves the optimal communication rounds. The high-level idea behind FreeFL is to customize a lightweight decentralized symmetric encryption with additive homomorphism for cross-silo FL. To this end, we design an efficient decentralized multiparty symmetric encryption (DMSE) scheme and two lightweight multiparty computation protocols. We evaluate the performance of FreeFL, and the experimental results indicate that FreeFL exhibits high efficiency in both computation and communication. Additionally, we conduct experimental comparisons between FreeFL and other existing HE-based cross-silo FL protocols to show that FreeFL achieves significant computational efficiency improvements.
Manual Tags: homomorphic encryption; privacy-preserving; Machine learning; cross-silo federated learning

Author: Gao, X.; Liu, Y.; Yuan, S.; Yuwen, X.
Title: Research on Distributed Task Offloading for UAV-Assisted Vehicular Edge Computing Based on Federated Reinforcement Learning and Blockchain
Publication Title: 2026 7th International Conference on Internet of Things, Artificial Intelligence and Electronical Energy (IoTAIEE)
Abstract Note: Aiming at the problems of large volume of raw data transmission, privacy leakage, high communication overhead and vulnerable model parameters in centralized offloading of vehicular edge computing, this paper proposes a distributed task offloading scheme integrating blockchain evidence storage and federated dueling double deep Q network (Fed-DDQN). A multi-layer collaborative architecture consisting of base stations, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and vehicles is constructed to support three types of task offloading modes. Each node only uploads model parameters for federated aggregation after local model training, which avoids raw data exchange to protect privacy. The blockchain is adopted to record the whole interaction process of models, realizing traceability and anti-tampering of parameters. Simulation results demonstrate that on the premise of blockchain-based trusted protection and privacy preservation, the proposed scheme achieves comparable system utility and convergence performance to the centralized dueling DQN algorithm, and can adapt to dynamic vehicular edge scenarios.

Author: Mukiri, R. R.; Satyanarayana, G. S.; Babu, S. A.
Title: Privacy-Aware Hybrid Federated–Homomorphic Learning Framework for Secure Medical Healthcare Diagnostics

Abstract Note: The government and business have been closely watching healthcare industry improvements related to the IoT because of the potential they hold to improve patient diagnosis and research. A privacy-aware healthcare architecture based on federated learning is proposed in this paper to address these difficulties. It allows various entities to work together to train a global Privacy Aware Healthcare model without disclosing personal information. An innovative deep learning architecture called Enhanced Ghost BiNet, which combines GhostNet with the BiGRU is used by the framework to safely train local models. The model is fine-tuned using the CAh algorithm after data is cleaned and features are extracted using cuckoos. The suggested FL-CAh-HE technique is highly effective, as shown experimentally by its 99.05% detection precision. In essence, our research shows that in privacy-aware healthcare settings, federated learning, deep learning, and advanced optimisation methods may work together to improve detection accuracy, safeguard patient privacy, and guarantee secure information exchange.
