Author: Kavitha, A.; Karthika, S.
Title: Adaptive Graph-Based Blockchain Cloud Threat Mitigation Network for Intelligent and Secure Cloud Computing
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Next-Gen Intelligent Computing and Applications (ICONICA)
Abstract Note: Cloud computing environments generate highly interconnected security events involving users, Virtual Machines (VMs), servers, services, and network transactions, requiring intelligent and secure threat detection and mitigation. The dynamic and complex relationships among cloud entities make conventional security approaches less effective for accurate, scalable, and adaptive threat management. Existing methods are further limited by graph-processing complexity, computational overhead, isolated threat detection, and insufficient adaptive mitigation mechanisms. To solve these limitations, this research proposed an Adaptive Graph-Based Blockchain Cloud Threat Mitigation Network (AGBCTM-Net) for intelligent and secure cloud threat detection and mitigation. The proposed framework aims to identify relevant security patterns, model dynamic cloud relationships, assess threat risk, securely validate security events, and select suitable mitigation actions. It integrates XGBoost-based feature selection for extracting important security features and risk prediction for estimating threat levels, dynamic graph construction for representing relationships among cloud entities, Graph Attention Network (GAT) for learning complex attack relationships, blockchain hashing and smart contracts for secure event verification, and adaptive optimization for selecting risk-based mitigation actions. The experimental evaluation demonstrates that AGBCTM-Net achieves 96.72% accuracy in threat classification. Overall, the proposed framework provides accurate, secure, scalable, and adaptive cloud threat detection and mitigation.

Author: Moodu, R.; Singh, M.; Patrot, A.; Amardeep, R.; L, N.; Kaur, A.
Title: Secure Network Slicing in High-Speed 5G and Beyond Networks
Publication Title: 2026 13th International Conference on Computing for Sustainable Global Development (INDIACom)
Abstract Note: Network slicing is essential to support diverse service differents by 5G and the next generation of networks (i.e., 6G); such categories include but are not limited to ultra-reliable low-latency communications (URLLC), enhanced mobile broadband (eMBB) and massive machine-type communications (mMTC). Yet, the virtualization and softwarization of network resources make slices highly vulnerable to serious security attacks such as cross-slice attacks, data leakage, slice hijacking and unauthorized access to resources. This paper addresses the aforementioned challenges of 5G and beyond networks by proposing a network slicing framework secured by AI-based intrusion detection, blockchain-backed authentication, and zero-trust access control mechanisms. Aiming at this problem they proposed a framework isolate slice through dynamic security policy and adaptive threat mitigation strategies. We validate our proposals resulting in a 43% attack propagation rate reduction, through experimental results with an accuracy of slice isolation equal to99.2%, with improvement in terms of latency up to 37% in regards conventional security models. This solution adopts a high-throughput and low-latency communication approach, addressing the confidentiality, integrity, and availability requirements of next-generation mission-critical applications.

Author: Saranya, M.; Velayutham, R.; Gopal, S. V.; Sujatha, S.; Anthony, A.; D, G.
Title: Federated Learning-Based Framework for Secure Healthcare Data Management and Disease Prediction
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Sustainability, Innovation & Technology (ICSIT)

Author: Rawindaran, N.; Wylde, V.; Patel, P.
Title: Ubiquitous,Transparent,Security and Privacy: Challenges and Applications

Abstract Note: As society advances toward Society 5.0, ubiquitous computing, IoT, and cloud-based analytics amplify the need for transparent, privacy-preserving cybersecurity governance particularly for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) that lack the resources and maturity of larger organisations. This study proposes a federated governance architecture that enables secure cross-organisational AI collaboration without centralising sensitive data. The model combines federated learning with blockchain-backed auditability to support data sovereignty, consent-aware participation, and tamper-evident accountability. A feedback-driven governance loop provides continuous monitoring and policy refinement to mitigate governance drift, while secure aggregation and proxy mediation reduce attack surfaces and regulatory exposure for SMEs. The proposed approach operationalises “compliance by design” through policy-driven enforcement, enabling SMEs to contribute to shared intelligence while retaining local control of high-risk datasets. Author: Pahuja, N.; Agarwal, P.; Arya, P. K.
Title: Lightweight ECC-ElGamal Hybrid Encryption for Securing Cloud Data Using Blockchain
Publication Title: 2026 5th International Conference on Innovative Sustainable Computational Technologies (CISCT)
Abstract Note: Data stored in a cloud environments are inherently vulnerable to unauthorized access and modification. Existing hybrid encryption schemes typically trade-off between probabilistic security and third-party verification mechanisms. This paper proposes a lightweight ECC-ElGamal hybrid encryption scheme instantiated over the NIST P-256 curve, combined with a permissioned blockchain to provide decentralized, third-party-free integrity assurance. The proposed algorithm generates distinct ciphertext blocks, ensuring probabilistic non-determinism and mitigating statistical inference attacks on structured data. The blockchain maintains SHA-256 hashes of ciphertext blocks at the time of upload, enabling tamper detection prior to decryption. Security analysis demonstrates IND-CPA confidentiality under the Decisional Diffie-Hellman assumption, tamper detection with probability \1-2^{-256}\, and key recovery resistance on the order of \O\textbackslash{}left(2^{128}\textbackslash{}right)\. Comparative evaluation indicates that the proposed scheme is the first to combine probabilistic encryption with blockchain-based integrity verification and third-party-auditor-free operation within a compact 256-bit key framework.

Author: Jangra, R.; Sharma, A.; Gopi, A.; Bisht, A.; Singh, M.; Pandey, P.
Title: A Study on Research Trends in Machine Learning based WSN Security Monitoring
Publication Title: 2026 13th International Conference on Computing for Sustainable Global Development (INDIACom)
Abstract Note: This paper reviews the intellectual framework, research patterns, and upcoming directions of machine-learningbased security surveillance within Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs). The articles were screened in a structured way, and a total of 776 journal articles indexed in Scopus were selected and subjected to a thorough bibliometric analysis. The analysis of quantitative growth in publications, the leading contributors, influential countries, and sources, and the discovery of the prevailing and emerging themes in the research in the field were conducted through the use of the science-mapping techniques and the quantitative performance analysis. The findings show that the level of scientific output has increased significantly since 2019, which demonstrates the interest of researchers in intelligent and automated security in the context of the IoT-based WSN environment. The most common research topics include the focus on intrusion detection, anomaly detection, machine learning, deep learning, WSN security architectures, and their fundamental implications in the field. The thematic analysis shows that current streams of research on ML-based cybersecurity are rather welldrilled, and the basic research investigating intrusion detection systems and feature selection methods can be found. Further focused research interests cover clustering, routing, and optimization-oriented security measures, whereas the new tendencies focus on deep learning techniques, integration of IoT security, and more sophisticated methods of anomaly detection. On the whole, the results indicate a preference for adaptive, dataintensive, and computationally efficient security models to address the limitations of WSNs. Simultaneously, the analysis reveals serious gaps in research in such areas as federated learning, explainable artificial intelligence, TinyML, and privacypreserving analytics. This research is presented in a wellorganized and current overview that can inform future studies on how to come up with secure, scalable, and intelligent WSN ecosystems.

Author: Liang, Y.; Yan, Y.; Zhu, T.
Title: AI-Based Trusted Governance and Value Allocation Mechanism for Data Elements under the Data Trust Model
Publication Title: 2026 7th International Conference on Big Data & Artificial Intelligence & Software Engineering (ICBASE)
Abstract Note: This study aims to address core challenges in the circulation of data elements under the data trust model, including difficulties in quantifying trustworthiness, executing collaborative governance, and ensuring fair value distribution, with the goal of establishing a trustworthy, efficient, and sustainable data collaboration ecosystem. To this end, an integrated technical framework is proposed. A dynamic trustworthiness evaluation model based on an improved Transformer encoder is designed, integrating static quality, temporal behaviors, and environmental evidence. A collaborative governance architecture combining FATE federated learning with the FISCO BCOS consortium blockchain is constructed, enabling anomaly detection and on-chain automated adjudication while preserving privacy. Finally, a two-stage Shapley value allocation mechanism embedded with trustworthiness weights is introduced, linking quality, behavior, and contribution. Experimental results show that the proposed governance architecture achieves an anomaly detection rate of 97.1%, close to centralized AI (98.2%), while reducing communication overhead by approximately 85% and introducing only about 210 ms of on-chain latency. In 20 rounds of long-term collaboration, the two-stage allocation mechanism drives sustained growth in total collaborative gains and maintains a low Gini coefficient ( 0.20), effectively incentivizing improvements in data quality and compliance behavior. The findings indicate that this framework provides a verifiable and automated solution for trusted circulation and fair value allocation of data elements.

Author: Sultana, N.; Miah, M. K.; Ahmed, K. R.; Goyal, S. K.; Ali, A. H. M. M.; Karim, M. R.
Title: Zero-Trust Access Control Via Blockchain-Backed Identity and AI-Based Anomaly Detection
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Signal Analysis for Smart Systems (SIGNASS)
Abstract Note: Security models need to expand beyond conventional perimeter-based defenses to protect modern organizational networks from progressively sophisticated insider threats. However, current systems are unable to address the crucial gaps in Zero-Trust implementation because they are either unable to confirm identity integrity or identify behavioral abnormalities in real time. We propose BlockZTA-AI, a blockchain-backed, AI-driven Zero-Trust access control framework designed to enforce adaptive anomaly detection and continuous, tamper-proof authentication, as a solution to this problem. The model combines an LSTM-Autoencoder anomaly engine, federated threatintelligence learning, contextual risk scoring, and a cryptographic identity ledger. BlockZTA-AI outperforms baselines like Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, LSTM, and GRU by achieving 98.97% accuracy, 98% precision, 99% recall, and 98% F1-score using the CERT Insider Threat dataset, which contains 2.63 million emails and comprehensive psychometric features. Our main contributions are threefold: a completely decentralized identity validation mechanism, a privacy-preserving federated learning protocol enhanced with blockchain trust scores, and a real-time adaptive anomaly detection pipeline that strengthens Zero-Trust enforcement in dynamic organizational settings.

Author: Chaturbhuj, S.; Meshram, V. S.; Mankar, J. B.; Yadav, S.; Modani, D. G.; Panadiwal, H.
Title: Hybrid Ai and Cryptographic Approaches for Secure and Explainable IoT-Based Cyber-Physical Systems
Publication Title: 2026 6th International Conference on Recent Trends in Computer Science and Technology (ICRTCST)
Abstract Note: Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) integrated with Internet of Things (IoT) devices are subject to growing threats of security issues such as threats of intrusion, malware, data tampering and privacy breaches. While the traditional cryptographic methods successfully guarantee the confidentiality and integrity, they do not possess adaptive threat detection capabilities. Conversely, intrusion detection systems based on AI offer good detection of anomalies, but tend to be black boxes and lack trust and interpretation. This paper proposes a novel hybrid framework which synergies between deep learning based intrusion detection approaches with the blockchain enabled cryptographic security and explainable AI (XAI) techniques. Our architecture integrates a hierarchical edge-fog-cloud computing model with federated learning for privacy-preserving distributed intelligence. We implement a CNN-BiLSTM hybrid neural network for multiclass intrusion detection, coupled with Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC) for lightweight encryption and blockchain for immutable audit trails. SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) and LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations) provide model interpretability. Experimental evaluation on CICIDS2017, BoT-IoT, and Edge-IIoTset datasets demonstrates 99.47% detection accuracy, 98.3% precision, 99.1% recall, and F1-score of 98.7%. The cryptographic overhead remains minimal at 6.2 % with encryption latency of 78 μs. Our framework achieves 99.2% packet delivery ratio while maintaining energy efficiency of 0.089 mJ per transaction. The proposed system provides a comprehensive solution for secure, explainable, and efficient IoTCPS deployments in critical infrastructure.

Author: Nwankwo, O. U.; Ajakwe, S. O.; Kim, D.-S.; Lee, J. M.
Title: Hybrid Blockchain-Assisted Federated Learning Intrusion Detection System for DoS Attacks in UAV Sensor Network
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Information and Communication (ICAIIC)
Abstract Note: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly deployed in mission-critical domains, raising significant security concerns. This paper presents a Federated Learning-based Intrusion Detection System (PureChain-FL) for UAV clients, focusing on Denial-of-Service (DoS) attack detection. The system features client-based localized model training using the WSN-DS dataset and a global FL server for model aggregation. A smart contract governs audit logging, enabling verifiable and tamper-resistant record-keeping. Evaluation of multilayer perceptron (MLP), one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D CNN), and CNN combined with long-short-term memory (CNN-LSTM) models over 20 FL rounds with five clients using the Flower framework and TensorFlow in a Google collaborative environment revealed CNN-LSTM as the best-performing model with 99.3 % accuracy. Figures and diagrams illustrating system architecture, communication flow, and model training are integrated into the discussion for clarity. The results show promise in the system's effectiveness in privacypreserving and trustworthy intrusion detection for unmanned aerial wireless sensor networks.

Author: Singh, P.; Baviskar, L. S.; Kacheru, G.; Mohammad, A.; S, P.; Ramachandran, R.

Author: Sadiqi, M. A. M.; Al-Madi, D. A. A.; Mahmood, S. A.; Saeed, H. E.; Mahmood, I. A.-S.; Hameed, D. W.; Al-Majidi, J. J. A.; Jasim, Q. N.

The framework introduces a practical risk scoring system that translates predictions into early warning alerts for agricultural stakeholders. Author: R, R.; K, H.; M, S. M.; Kartheek, G.; Manimaran, S.
Title: Quantum-Resistant Blockchain: Evaluating Falcon, Dilithium & SPHINCS+
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Interdisciplinary Approaches in Technology and Management for Social Innovation (IATMSI)
Abstract Note: For transactions, up to date blockchain protocols primarily depend on digital signature schemes like RSA and ECC, that are built on traditional cryptography. These cryptography algorithms are at risk by quantum algorithms such as Shor's and Grover's, that form part of the latest advances in quantum computing. To mitigate this risk of vulnerability, post-quantum cryptography (PQC) techniques that are safe from both classical and quantum attacks must be used. As a means to protect and verify transactions in the future, we show and evaluate post-quantum digital signature schemes in blockchain protocols. We outline the cryptographic base of post-quantum digital signatures, consider their suitability for blockchain networks, and present practical deployment implications according to recent National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) standardizations. Our methodology shows that using PQC not only reduces the threat of quantum adversaries but also enables the development of secure, decentralized financial and information exchange systems for the future quantum era.

Author: Fan, K.; Chen, W.; Li, J.; Wu, Q.; Ding, M.; Han, X.; Wei, K.; Deng, X.
Title: Mobility in Hierarchical Federated Learning: Resource Allocation and Convergence Analysis
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking
Abstract Note: The proliferation of fifth-generation (5G) communication technologies and the Internet of Things (IoT) has led to massive distributed datasets across numerous user devices. Traditional centralized machine learning methods suffer from large communication overhead and damage of data privacy. Federated Learning (FL) offers a decentralized approach, allowing collaborative local model training and global aggregation, thus preserving data privacy and reducing communication costs. However, implementing FL in wireless networks is complicated due to limited wireless resources, increasing model complexity, and user mobility. In this paper, we address the impact of user mobility in hierarchical federated learning (HFL) systems and propose a resource allocation and user scheduling strategy to minimize energy consumption while maintaining learning performance. We design a comprehensive model that considers user mobility, wireless communication, and computing resources. Using the Lyapunov optimization method, we transform the long-term optimization problem into manageable subproblems, enabling efficient resource allocation and user selection. Our proposed Low Cost Scheduling Algorithm (LCSA) achieves an \textbackslash{}boldsymbol {O}\textbackslash{}left ({{{}\textbackslash{}frac {1}{N}}}\textbackslash{}right)\ convergence rate, balancing local-edge divergence and improving overall convergence. Experimental results testify that our algorithm significantly reduces energy consumption while achieving high test accuracy compared to baseline methods, highlighting the positive effects of mobility on system performance.

Author: Cheikh, I.; Roy, S.; Sabir, E.; Aouami, R.
Title: Energy, Scalability, Data, and Security in Massive IoT: Current Landscape and Future Directions
Publication Title: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
Abstract Note: The Massive Internet of Things (MIoT) envisions an interconnected ecosystem of billions of devices, fundamentally transforming diverse sectors such as healthcare, smart cities, transportation, agriculture, and energy management. However, the vast scale of MIoT introduces significant challenges, including network scalability, efficient data management, energy conservation, and robust security mechanisms. This article presents a thorough review of existing and emerging MIoT technologies designed to address these challenges, including low-power wide-area networks (LPWANs), 5G/6G capabilities, edge and fog computing architectures, and hybrid access methodologies. We further investigate advanced strategies such as artificial intelligence (AI)-driven resource allocation, federated learning (FL) for privacy-preserving analytics, and decentralized security frameworks using blockchain. Additionally, we analyze sustainable practices, emphasizing energy-harvesting and integrating green technologies to reduce environmental impact. Through extensive comparative analysis, this study identifies critical innovations and architectural adaptations required to support efficient, resilient, and scalable MIoT deployments. Key insights include the role of network slicing and intelligent resource management for scalability, adaptive protocols for real-time data handling, and lightweight AI models suited to the constraints of MIoT devices. This research ultimately contributes to a deeper understanding of how MIoT systems can evolve to meet the growing demand for seamless, reliable connectivity while prioritizing sustainability, security, and performance across diverse applications. Our findings serve as a roadmap for future advancements, underscoring the potential of MIoT to support a globally interconnected, intelligent infrastructure.

Author: Yang, J.; Wang, H.; Chen, Y.; Aldhyani, T. H. H.; Yan, X.; Por, L. Y.; Lin, J.; Wang, J.
Title: KArAt-KidneyNet: Proactive Threat Hunting and Anomaly Detection Framework for Consumer Wearable Healthcare Electronics in Kidney Disease Diagnosis
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Consumer Electronics
Abstract Note: Consumer wearable healthcare electronics, including kidney-monitoring wearables and point-of-care diagnostic devices, generate continuous multimodal physiological and imaging data. Their increasing integration within connected health systems also expands the attack surface, creating vulnerabilities that may affect diagnostic integrity, model reliability, and patient safety. This paper presents KArAt-KidneyNet, a unified framework for kidney disease diagnosis and system-state monitoring that combines Kolmogorov–Arnold Transformer (KArAt) attention, Soft Actor–Critic (SAC)–based adaptive defense, and privacy-preserving federated learning. The proposed KArAt attention module replaces softmax attention with a set of learnable basis functions inspired by the Kolmogorov–Arnold representation concept, enabling structured feature decomposition and interpretable attention maps for ultrasound imaging. The SAC component provides adaptive parameter adjustment for anomaly-aware defensive actions based on system state indicators derived from detection modules. Federated learning with differential privacy is used to train the diagnostic model over decentralized healthcare datasets without sharing raw patient data. Additional protective layers include post-quantum cryptographic signatures resistant to emerging quantum computing threats and blockchain-based logging to ensure authenticity and traceability of diagnostic outputs. Evaluation across multi-center kidney ultrasound datasets and simulated adversarial/anomalous operating conditions shows that the framework achieves 96.8% diagnostic accuracy, 94.0% robustness under attack, and 94.2% anomaly detection rate, with inference latency of 412.3 ms on edge-class hardware (Jetson Xavier), meeting real-time clinical screening requirements. These results indicate that KArAt-KidneyNet can support secure and interpretable kidney disease classification in distributed consumer healthcare environments.

Author: Lu, X.; Xu, D.; Xiong, X.; Guo, Y.
Title: E-TeeDag: A Secure and Efficient Distributed Consensus Protocol for DAG Blockchain
Publication Title: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
Abstract Note: This article proposes a new distributed consensus protocol E-TeeDag, which combines the trusted execution environment (TEE) and the directed acyclic graph (DAG) structure to balance high concurrence and strong security. The core contributions of the protocol include: 1) this article proposes a parallel fault-tolerant mechanism based on TEE and DAG structure, design a dual-key block structure and a parent hash single reference rule, force nodes to only generate unique legal blocks, and reduce the network communication complexity by more than 50% compared with the traditional Byzantine fault-tolerant algorithm, and support multinode parallel block release; and 2) it proposes a causal sorting algorithm driven by dynamic network delay, combined with hash queues and real-time timeout mechanisms, to simultaneously filter out conflicting blocks with the same sequence number during the consensus phase, ensuring that the block order strictly follows the event causal relationship. Experiments show that E-TeeDag has a throughput (BPS) of more than 100% higher than that of TEEDAG, and the block generation time is shortened by more than 50%. It can also maintain stable operation when 49% of Byzantine nodes exist. This protocol provides an efficient and secure solution for high-concurrence low-latency transactions and smart contract deployment in Internet of Things (IoT) consortium chain scenarios.

Author: Zhang, L.; Wang, Z.; Yang, F.; Kan, H.; Zhang, J.
Title: MASH: Mask Shuffling-Based Federated Learning for Both Cross-Silo and Cross-Device Environments
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing
Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) has been extensively studied over the past few years. Cross-silo FL typically involves tens of reliable organizations with larger-scale, high-quality data sources, while cross-device FL may include thousands of devices, each with limited computation and communication capabilities. However, existing research has yet to simultaneously address cross-silo and cross-device scenarios. We propose a novel mask-shuffling scheme that protects clients’ gradient privacy and ensures all masks added to gradients are ultimately canceled out. While gradients are treated as exponentiation values, we eliminate the need to solve the discrete logarithm problem by leveraging a precomputed lookup table. Additionally, we partition all clients into small groups, each performing the mask-shuffling scheme to accelerate mask generation. This partitioning strategy enhances the framework’s resilience to client dropouts. To resist forgery attacks on aggregated gradients, each client publishes a commitment to enable verification of its contribution’s correctness. We further propose a batch verification method for \d\d-dimensional gradients, reducing the complexity from \O(d)\O(d) to \O(1)\O(1). Besides, the blockchain smart contract serves as a verifier, ensuring public trustworthiness. We formally analyze all the required security properties and conduct a comprehensive comparison with related works. Furthermore, we perform systematic experiments to evaluate overall performance, considering both cross-silo and cross-device environments. The results demonstrate reasonable efficiency, even for models with \10^{5}\105-dimensional gradients across \10^{4}\104 devices and \10^{10}\1010-dimensional gradients across 10 organizations.
Manual Tags: Federated learning; blockchain; cross-silo; cross-device; mask shuffling

Author: Khute, T.; Doriya, R.
Title: A Comprehensive Study on Secured Swarm Drone Communication and Coordination in Defence
Publication Title: 2026 Fifth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
Abstract Note: The use of drone swarms in operations is a paradigm change in contemporary warfare, providing unprecedented levels of surveillance, reconnaissance, and synchronized attacks. With the use of wireless communication and distributed coordination, these swarms are, however, extremely susceptible to cyber and electronic warfare attacks such as jamming, spoofing, and data interception. This paper introduces an extensive review of secured communication and coordination methods for military swarms of drones, covering literature between 2015 to 2025. We start with the establishment of the core concepts of swarm coordination and communication, then systematically classify and review algorithms according to key defence requirements: security, robustness, fault-tolerance, real-time avoidance of obstacles, and power limitations. The research critically assesses current methods and recommends three viable approaches for in-depth analysis: Blockchain-Enabled Decentralized Trust Management for the building of tamper-proof trust, Bio-Inspired AI for Adaptive Coordination to provide robust navigation in hostile environments, and Federated Learning for Collaborative Intrusion Detection as a privacy-enhancing framework for shared threat intelligence. In a thorough comparative analysis, we evaluate the unique strengths and compromises of each solution, presenting a basis for choosing and combining these technologies to obtain resilient, secure, and intelligent swarm operations in contested environments. The paper ends with some discussion on implementation issues and avenues for future research.

Author: Kumar, S. S.; Gadi, A. L.; Sheelam, G. K.; Kummari, D. N.; Koppolu, H. K. Reddy; Pamisetty, A.
Title: AI-Driven Compliance and Audit Framework for Manufacturing Infrastructure in Automotive Connected Services and Financial Ecosystems

Author: Prabakar, D.; Puttaswamy, S.; Gowthami, N.; Kumar, S. P.; Pandian, R.; Dhanraj, J. A.
Title: Federated Learning for Distributed Wireless Sensor Networks in IoT
Publication Title: 2026 2nd International Conference on Sustainable Computing and Integrated Communication in Changing Landscape of AI (ICSCAI)
Abstract Note: Federated learning is an innovative methodology used for distributed learning with regards to IoT devices, including wireless sensor networks (WSNs) without data exchange. However, there is a number of issues faced in current methodologies, including the lack of sufficient computational capabilities and communication bottleneck. In order to address these challenges, a novel methodology is introduced with the use of energy-efficient approaches in federated learning of WSNs. Such a methodology ensures maximum communication throughput and minimum energy consumption because it introduces a local update approach allowing training models locally over extended periods of time prior to sending updates. Additionally, the use of a hierarchical aggregation approach is proposed, according to which sensor nodes will perform partial updates’ aggregation and send them to cluster heads, which will perform global model aggregation. Thus, communication overhead is reduced and convergence is accelerated. The proposed methodology has great potential in enhancing scalability, energy efficiency and robustness of federated learning in large-scale IoT systems. Therefore, it can be a viable approach for WSNs.

Author: Jain, Y. K.; Chugh, S.; Mannepalli, P. K.; Modi, R.; Kumar, S.; Beriwala, P.

Author: Qayyum, T.; Trabelsi, Z.; Tariq, A.; Serhani, M. Adel; Din, I.; Ahmad, S.
Title: A Quantum-Resilient Sharded Blockchain Framework for Secure V2X and Federated Learning in Intelligent Transportation Systems
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
Abstract Note: The emergence of large-scale quantum computers threatens the security of classical public-key cryptosystems, making it essential to adopt post-quantum (PQ) security in Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS). We introduce a framework that blends quantum-resilient cryptographic primitives with a sharded blockchain architecture. Each shard maintains a local ledger for its vehicle group, enabling real-time transactions and efficient certificate management without overloading any single chain. A lightweight global chain periodically anchors all shards, preserving system-wide consistency and blocking malicious revocations. Vehicles register or revoke PQ credentials via a lightweight Proof-of-Stake consensus, while roadside units (RSUs) handle signature verification to offload on-board computation. We further demonstrate practicality through a federated-learning case study in which vehicles exchange signed model updates over the same secure channel. SUMO/TraCI simulations with 2 000 vehicles and 10 shards show that despite PQ overhead the system sustains near real-time delays and high throughput. The framework thus offers a decentralized, quantum-resilient solution for secure Vehicle-to-Everything communications in next-generation ITS.

Title: A Post-Quantum Cryptography Framework for Secure IoT-Based E-Healthcare Systems

Author: Li, H.; Yao, K.; Zhou, Y.
Title: Reputation-Aware Behavior Auditing and Closed-Loop Revocation Scheme for Federated Learning in Internet of Vehicles
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE 8th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Computer Science, and Information Processing (AICSIP)
Abstract Note: In federated learning (FL) for the Internet of Vehicles (IoV), identity-legal vehicles may still perform malicious behaviors such as gradient poisoning attacks, severely degrading the robustness of the global model. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a reputation-aware behavior auditing and closed-loop revocation scheme. Specifically, a multi-dimensional gradient auditing mechanism based on cosine similarity and Euclidean distance is designed at the roadside unit (RSU) to evaluate the quality of local model updates in real time. A sliding average model is adopted to dynamically update vehicle reputation scores, which are further stored on the blockchain to ensure transparency and tamper-resistance. When a vehicle's reputation falls below a preset threshold, a smart contract is automatically triggered to update the incremental certificate revocation list (I-CRL), achieving instantaneous isolation of malicious nodes. Extensive simulations under non-independent and identically distributed (Non-IID) data settings demonstrate that the proposed scheme maintains high classification accuracy even when malicious nodes account for up to 40% of participants, outperforming traditional FL aggregation methods.

Author: Bieniek, J.; Mahmud, M. I.; Rahouti, M.; Chehri, A.; Jeon, G.; Ansari, G. A.
Title: ReMerkle: Proof-of-Reputation-Driven Federated Learning With Compact Merkle Verification for Consumer-Centric IoMT
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Consumer Electronics
Abstract Note: Consumer-centric Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) devices, including wearables and in-home health monitors, generate sensitive physiological and activity data for personalized health monitoring. Federated Learning (FL) helps preserve privacy by keeping raw data on local devices, but integrating blockchain-based accountability into FL can introduce prohibitive storage, latency, and gas overhead when model updates are recorded on-chain. This paper introduces ReMerkle, a lightweight blockchain-enabled FL framework for consumer IoMT. ReMerkle combines a three-tier reputation mechanism based on cosine similarity, Beta-history reputation, and entropy-based quality assessment to filter unreliable or low-quality updates before aggregation. To reduce blockchain overhead, ReMerkle stores only a 32-byte Merkle root on-chain through Compact Merkle Tree Verification rather than storing full model updates. Experiments on a WBAN human activity recognition dataset show that ReMerkle achieves 90.2% accuracy after 10 FL rounds, increases honest-node reputation scores from 0.5 to 0.85, and requires \20{,}180\ gas per five-client round, reducing both gas consumption and on-chain storage by 99.96% relative to full-update storage. These results demonstrate a cost-efficient and auditable FL architecture for secure consumer health monitoring.

Author: Prasad, G. B.; Rao, M. V.
Title: Blockchain Enabled Secure Data Sharing for Distributed Healthcare Systems
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Interdisciplinary Approaches in Technology and Management for Social Innovation (IATMSI)
Abstract Note: The increasing adoption of data-driven healthcare analytics is hindered by strict privacy regulations, data heterogeneity and the inability of institutions to centrally share sensitive multimodal patient data. Current methods of distributed learning cannot adequately support a high degree of privacy and auditability and high predictive accuracy at the same time, which restricts their application in a real healthcare environment. This study was to develop and test a blockchain-based, privacy-aware multimodal learning infrastructure that allows sharing data safety and jointly training models in distributed health care organizations. The experiments were carried out on multimodal healthcare datasets of publicly available healthcare information, among which are structured electronic health records, medical imaging, and physiological time-series data, and are simulated across healthcare nodes. The proposed framework integrates federated learning with permissioned blockchain governance, differential privacy, trusted execution environments, zero-knowledge consent verification, and a multimodal Perceiver-based architecture. The performance, privacy and system-level metrics were measured and compared to the centralized and hybrid federated baselines. The most predictive performance (AUROC \=0.925)\ was centralized baseline, but with high privacy leakage with the accuracy of membership inference equal to 0.78. The suggested framework had performed nearly centrally (AUROC \=0.913\, \textbackslash{}text{PR}-\textbackslash{}text{AUC}=0.76\) but the accuracy of membership inferences had dropped to 0.19. This was accomplished at a moderate system overhead and took 1450 GPU-hours, and a mean round latency of 12s. The results demonstrate that secure, auditable, and privacy-preserving multimodal learning in distributed healthcare environments is feasible without substantial loss of clinical utility. The proposed structure offers a feasible basis of reliable cross-institutional medical analytics in an actual administrative setting.

Author: Thandra, P. K.

Abstract Note: The cyber threats affecting cloud computing environments are becoming ever more advanced, such as zero-day attacks, insider attacks and exploits that can target critical infrastructure. The article introduces a new AI-powered secure cloud architecture that uses Large Language Models (LLMs) to track anomalies in real-time and perform automatic mitigation of risks in distributed cloud systems. Author: Rajab, R. M.; Ward, R. P.; Abuhmida, M.
Title: A Standards-Aligned IoMT Federated Learning and Blockchain Framework for MITM Mitigation and Risk Quantification Using NS-3*
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Cybersecurity and AI-Based Systems (Cyber-AI)
Abstract Note: The increasing reliance on Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) systems introduces critical vulnerabilities to advanced cyber threats such as Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attacks, which simultaneously compromise data integrity, availability, and clinical safety. This paper presents a security framework integrating a Federated Learning-based Intrusion Detection System (FL-IDS) with blockchain to enable real-time detection, mitigation, and risk quantification of MITM attacks in IoMT networks. The framework is implemented within an NS-3 simulation environment, where MITM attacks are injected and mitigated using distributed, privacy-preserving anomaly detection across heterogeneous devices. Experimental results reveal that MITM attacks produce selective, high-severity disruptions rather than uniform degradation, with critical flow collapse and hybrid anomaly patterns that evade traditional intrusion detection approaches. To quantify attack impact, derived performance metrics-Throughput Reduction Ratio (TRR), Packet Loss Ratio (PLR), Network Delay Increase (NDI), and Jitter Variation Increase (JVI)-are aggregated into a device-weighted Attack Severity Index (wASI). This enables fine-grained, flow-level assessment of clinically relevant degradation. The framework aligns with ISO/IEEE 11073, ISO 14971, ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 27005, and IEC 80001-1 standards, achieving 94% concordance across clinical, cybersecurity, and governance risk classifications. The proposed approach bridges the gap between fragmented compliance standards by providing a unified, actionable framework for AI-driven intrusion detection, mitigation, and clinically actionable risk assessment in IoMT environments.

Title: Distributed Edge Intelligence Framework for Secure and Efficient Data Sharing in 6G-IoV
Publication Title: IEEE Internet of Things Journal

Author: Evelyn, R. R.; Deepa, N.; T, D.
Title: A Reinforcement Learning with Key Management for Secure Cloud Systems Using Cryptographic Framework and Intelligent Federated Blockchain

Author: Jaszcz, A.; Połap, D.; Srivastava, G.
Title: MultiMOORA-Guided Federated Learning With KD Stabilization for Health Monitoring Devices as Protection Against Poisoning Attacks
Publication Title: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
Abstract Note: Federated learning (FL) has emerged as a practical solution for training deep neural networks while preserving data privacy, particularly in scenarios like the Internet of Things (IoT), where user devices generate sensitive private data. While FL addresses privacy concerns, the existing aggregation methods remain vulnerable to malicious poisoning attacks. Therefore, developing new approaches to optimize client selection as a preventive mechanism is crucial to FL’s strategy. This article introduces a novel enhancement to FL by integrating the MultiMOORA technique into a robust aggregation mechanism with knowledge distillation (KD). During FL rounds, local models are evaluated using classification metrics (loss, accuracy, precision, recall, and \F1\ -score) and ranked using the multicriteria decision maker (MCDM). The resulting ranking is used to select the best-performing models for aggregation and to detect possible infected clients. Furthermore, the top client is chosen as an aggregator. During aggregation, the chosen best models are weight-averaged and form a teacher ensemble, used for stabilizing the newly formed global model via KD. The proposed FL strategy reduces the risk of adversarial poisoning attacks on FL systems and stabilizes the FL training process. The experimental results indicate the system’s resilience and ability to perform reliably in hostile environments, as the proposed FL system achieved 89.50% \F1\ -score under a label-poisoning scenario. Based on further analysis, the proposed methods could be integrated into a digital-twin-based modern healthcare system.
Manual Tags: federated learning (FL); machine learning; Consensus; multiMOORA

Author: Leonhardt, T.; Pruitt, J.; Law, G.; Sherif, A.; Elsersy, M.; Lee, S.; Bayoumi, M.; Khalil, K.
Title: Safeguarding Federated Learning Model in Internet of Vehicles (IoV) Through Utilization of Fake Neurons
Publication Title: SoutheastCon 2026
Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) has revolutionized privacy-preserving Machine Learning (ML) by enabling decentralized data training while maintaining data confidentiality. Author: Syed, K. H.; Poghosyan, R.; Shi, H.; Ma, R.; Luo, Y.; Bassam, E.; Zhou, Z.; Qu, Z.; Guan, H.

Author: Hou, S.; Cao, R.
Title: CARA-FL: Permissioned Blockchain Governance for Authorization-Bound Federated Learning and Auditable Withdrawal Remediation
Publication Title: IEEE Access
Abstract Note: Motivated by sensitive cross-organizational settings such as school mental health, CARA-FL implements authorization and withdrawal governance for federated learning (FL) on a permissioned blockchain. Each signed update is bound to a dynamically revalidated, single-use authorization. A controlled withdrawal identified 15 affected models in total, comprising one directly affected model and 14 descendants, while preserving three sibling models. In the tested implementation, replay and full exclusion retraining produced identical parameter commitments, with \textbackslash{}lVert \textbackslash{}boldsymbol {\textbackslash{}theta }_{\textbackslash{}mathrm {replay}}-\textbackslash{}boldsymbol {\textbackslash{}theta }_{\textbackslash{}mathrm {retrain}}\textbackslash{}rVert _{2}=0\ . Across 1,000 generated one-parent lineage scenarios, the complete protocol recovered every generated impact set; structural ablations produced missed dependencies or unnecessary quarantine. At 32 clients, the single-account serial Link stage limited the strict governance pipeline to 0.963 effective updates/s. The mean within-run 95th-percentile (P95) receipt latency was 18.91 s. Title: Federated Retrieval Over Embedding-Heterogeneous Vector Databases

Abstract Note: Vector databases are increasingly used to manage unstructured data by mapping them into high-dimensional embeddings and enabling efficient similarity retrieval. We formulate this setting as Federated Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search (FANNS), where a server issues a query along with a query embedding model, aiming to retrieve the top- \k\ nearest objects from datasets across all silos. A key challenge in FANNS is embedding heterogeneity, where silos and the server employ different embedding models, a problem overlooked in prior research. To address this challenge, we exploit the nonIID nature of federated data and propose two novel adaptive algorithms for FANNS queries. Title: ByFeDis: Toward Byzantine-Robust Heterogeneous Federated Learning via Knowledge Distillation in Railway Intelligent Control Systems

Abstract Note: Railway intelligent train control system must accommodate a wide range of scenarios due to the extensive variation in its operational environment. However, conventional federated knowledge distillation approaches often exhibit limited robustness against untrusted clients and do not facilitate continuous learning. In this paper, we design a Byzantine-robust federated knowledge distillation scheme, named ByFeDis, which mitigates the impact of malicious clients by removing outliers and low-value learning data, thereby improving learning efficiency. Additionally, we enhance the scalability of federated knowledge distillation in an improved scheme ByFeDis*, which is built on ByFeDis and enables continuous training for newly joined clients. Specifically, ByFeDis measures the soft labels uploaded by clients using Euclidean distance to identify poisoned soft labels that disrupt the training process. These abnormal soft labels include not only malicious perturbed samples that significantly deviate from the distribution of the true labels, but also speculative soft labels that are overly close to the true labels. To further enhance privacy protection, we employ fully homomorphic encryption to enable secure aggregation, thereby safeguarding sensitive client information. Theoretical analysis confirms that our scheme effectively preserves privacy while reducing communication complexity compared with existing approaches. Extensive experiments across multiple datasets demonstrate that ByFeDis achieves, on average, a 2% improvement in accuracy over other Byzantine-robust schemes, while ByFeDis* further enhances model accuracy by 3% and reduces premature convergence by up to 10 training rounds in subsequent learning.

Author: Kale, M.; Elinjulliparambil, S.; Song, H. H.; Faheem, Z. B.; Alghamdi, N. S.; Kim, S. M.; Ali, J.

Author: Koona, A. K.; Babu, V. S.; Battula, A.; Jayaprakash, C.; Rao, D. S.
Title: PrivFaceNet: Federated Deep Learning for Privacy Preserving Face Recognition

Abstract Note: Face recognition is increasingly deployed on distributed edge devices, where centralizing biometric data conflicts with emerging privacy regulations and user expectations. Author: Nguyen, T. L.; Hoang, D. T.; Nguyen, D. N.; Pham, Q.-V.
Title: Carpe Diem: Critical Learning Period-Aware Contract-Based Incentives for Federated Learning
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering
Abstract Note: Critical learning periods (CLPs) in federated learning (FL) refer to early stages during which low-quality contributions (e.g., sparse training data availability, strategic non-participation) can permanently impair the performance of the global model owned by the model owner (i.e., a cloud server). However, existing incentive mechanisms typically assume temporal homogeneity, treating all training rounds as equally important, thereby failing to prioritize and attract high-quality contributions during CLPs. This inefficiency is compounded by information asymmetry due to privacy regulations, where the cloud lacks knowledge of client training capabilities, leading to adverse selection and moral hazard. Thus, in this article, we propose a time-aware contract-theoretic incentive framework, named Right Reward Right Time (R3T), to encourage client involvement, especially during CLPs, to maximize the utility of the cloud server in FL. We formulate a cloud utility function that captures the trade-off between the achieved model performance and rewards allocated for clients’ contributions, explicitly accounting for client heterogeneity in time and system capabilities, effort, and joining time. Then, we devise a CLP-aware incentive mechanism deriving an optimal contract design that satisfies individual rationality, incentive compatibility, and budget feasibility constraints, motivating rational clients to participate early and contribute efforts. By providing the right reward at the right time, our approach can attract the highest-quality contributions during CLPs. Simulation and proof-of-concept studies show that R3T mitigates information asymmetry, increases cloud utility, and yields superior economic efficiency compared to conventional incentive mechanisms. Our proof-of-concept results demonstrate up to a 47.6% reduction in the total number of clients and up to a 300% improvement in convergence speed while achieving competitive test accuracy.
Manual Tags: blockchain; federated learning; incentive mechanism; contract theory; Critical learning periods

Title: FRIL: Blockchain-Powered Heterogeneous Model Fusion for Robust Food Recognition
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Multimedia
Abstract Note: The vast amount of multimedia food data on social platforms remains largely inaccessible for centralized model training due to stringent privacy regulations, leading to fragmented data and model silos. Unlike conventional federated learning that suffers from central server vulnerabilities and homogeneous model constraints, FRIL proposes a serverless “Isomerism Learning” paradigm. This framework facilitates collaborative judgment among heterogeneous models by leveraging a decentralized blockchain backbone, which eliminates single points of failure while ensuring the integrity and traceability of each verdict through an immutable ledger. The core technical contribution is the Quantized Mode Consensus (QMC) mechanism, which enables nodes with diverse architectures to reach a high-fidelity decision without high-dimensional parameter synchronization. Extensive experiments demonstrate that FRIL achieves state-of-the-art performance in food recognition, reducing communication overhead while maintaining high accuracy, thereby offering a viable solution for building trustworthy, cross-platform food monitoring or dietary analysis systems where data privacy and model heterogeneity are paramount.

Author: Bhat, S. M.; Katti, S.
Title: Blockchain in Footwear Supply Chains using POA and XAI
Publication Title: 2026 4th International Conference on Sustainable Computing and Smart Systems (ICSCSS)
Abstract Note: In footwear industry Counterfeit of footwear continues to be one of the major challenges faced by global brands not only because it exposes consumers to low-quality products but also due to substantial monetary and reputational loss of the companies by lack of customer's trust for the brand. Current solutions provide inadequate transparency and lack any cryptographic association between a physical asset and the digital data related to footwear product. A customized blockchain supply chain management system tailored for the footwear industry, FootChain uses the Proof of Authority (PoA) approach with three trusted validatory nodes where the authority of each validator is based on listing their public keys (via ECDSA algorithm). All events occurring along the supply chain such as submission by authorized parties including manufacturer, warehouse manager, logistics provider, and seller are stored in the form of transactions forming blocks linked with each other via SHA-256 hash cryptographic function creating an immutable chain. MongoDB is used as the operational database for instant data retrieval, complex queries, and storing of binary QR codes. Every individual has its physical product cryptographically tied to its unique ECDSA signature during manufacturing and receives two QR codes: the private QR code, which is AES-128 encrypted and available exclusively to the authorized supply chain roles to submit events updating simultaneously and the public QR code, printed in the packaging of the products for end consumers to verify their product's journey. QR code creation is entirely automated with structured information provided by the manufacturer manifest during batch QR generation by creating and signing large numbers of unit records automatically generating QR codes using qrcode from python library. The anomaly detection model utilizes an Entropy Deep Belief Network tuned via Lévy-flight Grasshopper Optimization Algorithm (EDBN-LGOA) to detect anomalies in ten different supply chain behavior attributes that include QR code cloning, theft of transaction hash-codes and complete fraud entry with a detection rate of 96.4%, compared to 88.7% achieved by the SVM baseline method. To facilitate informed decisions for manufacturers, an Explainable AI (XAI) component employs the use of SHAP values to provide the reasoning for each anomaly score in the end.

Author: Kishore, N.; Amaraa, M.; S, H.; Jayagowry, G.
Title: Federated Deep Learning Framework for Ethical Art Attribution and Copyright Protection Across Distributed Creative Platforms
Publication Title: 2026 13th International Conference on Computing for Sustainable Global Development (INDIACom)
Abstract Note: In an increasingly decentralized digital art landscape, the proliferation of creative content across blockchain-based platforms and NFT marketplaces has raised critical concerns about ethical attribution and copyright infringement. Traditional centralized deep learning architectures are not able to scale to a wide variety of art forms, do not provide privacy, and provide little to no transparency in ownership checks. This paper suggests a new Federated Deep Learning Architecture (FDLA) with differential privacy, Grad-CAM-based explainability and blockchain-based traceability, which will allow ethical, secure and transparent art attribution in distributed creative ecosystems. The architecture models federated nodes that model actual art platforms in the real world where local models are used to extract stylistic and semantic features on image metadata pairs without access to raw data. The feature backbone is made of CNN-Transformer hybrid, whereas federated averaging (FedAvg) aggregates encrypted updates. Attribution votes are proven by a consensus-weighted voting system and the result is permanently recorded with a personal blockchain. Experimental findings in ten simulated art platforms showed that global accuracy in attributing was 92.14, and performance of each node was at 87.62 and 94.05. The proposed architecture was also very explainable (Grad-CAM attention overlap \>85 \textbackslash{}%\), and consensus agreement (\>93 \textbackslash{}%\) in the case of rigid privacy noise (distortion \=1.5\). These results show that FDLA does not only provide privacy-preserving attribution but also imposes fairness and auditing on the digital platform. A future ethical infrastructure that could increase with the rising digital art economy is made possible by the study, ensuring the protection of creator rights and allowing transparent cross-platform ownership verification.

Author: Gode, S.; Dhote, A.; Giri, A.; Patel, M.; Reddy, P.; Thamke, N.
Title: Federated Graph Neural Networks with Explainable AI for Privacy-Preserving Credit Scoring and Loan Risk Assessment
Publication Title: 2026 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Engineering and Medical Sciences (ICETEMS)
Abstract Note: We introduce a new federated learning system that combines graph neural networks (GNNs) and explainable AI (XAI) to facilitate privacy-preserving, understandable credit scoring among financial institutions. In our system, every bank learns a local GNN on each of its customers' transaction graphs (accounts, loans, guarantors, etc. as nodes) and sends encrypted model updates only. A global server collects these updates (e.g. through FedAvg) to construct a global Fed-GNN model, preserving intricate relational structures that are lost in conventional models. We finally use explainability techniques (SHAP values, attention viz, counterfactual reasoning) to highlight which features and relations contributed most to every choice. A prototype pipeline is established, encompassing data preprocessing, federated model training, and an interactive explanation portal. Major contributions of this research are: (i) an end-to-end Fed-GNN-XAI system for private and explainable credit risk evaluation, (ii) a comprehensive approach for model architecture and hyperparameter adjustment within this context, and (iii) formal comparisons to state-of-the-art credit scoring techniques. Empirical assessment (on synthetic or available datasets) shows the suggested system has better prediction accuracy compared to traditional models and supports privacy-preserving learning and enables fairness and regulatory analysis, accountability, and trustworthiness in automatic financial decision-making.

Author: Pandey, P.; Sharma, B. K.; Kumar, S.

Abstract Note: The reason digital forensics is important to cybercrime investigation is that it ensures the validity and dependability of digital evidence. Traditional forensic systems, by contrast, fail at handling massive-scale distributed and heterogeneous data that are being generated by IoT, cloud, and mobile contexts. The recent forensics system enabling blockchain technology gives significance to the repository of evidences securely, instead of clever examination, flexibility and data collaboration analysis. In order to manage these limitations, in this paper, a forensics framework is designed in which AI is integrated with blockchain technology for multidomain areas. The ecosystem incorporates blockchain, which provides tamper-resistant evidence logs and chain-of-evidence tracking, with collaborative learning that allows outlier detection in a distributed and privacy-preserving way. The metadata of the collected evidence are stored safely on the blockchain whereas in the forensic analysis, different groups work together without giving the actual original data to each other. It has been proven by experiments that the system keeps our evidence safe, prevents others from changing the data, and helps in finding suspicious and unusual activities more precisely, even when data is from different sources. The proposed architecture aims to make the investigation process evident and easy and also helps prepare reports that can be validated. Having these advantages, still some challenges continue such as adaptability and legal implementation. The proposed work aims to build a federated platform in a more efficient way and provide expansion to smart cities in the future. This will lead to enable a secure online ecosystem.

Author: Gong, Y.; Wang, J.; Zhang, R.; Cheng, X.; Karagiannidis, G. K.; Debbah, M.; Nallanathan, A.
Title: Multi-Modal Enabled Computation Offloading and Secure Communication for Space Satellite Networks
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing
Abstract Note: Satellite-Ground Integrated Networks (SGINs) have become novel network architecture to provide mega-access services for terrestrial users to release network resources, reduce loading pressure and obtain seamless communication functionalities. Nevertheless, due to limited loading capacities and complex constellation configuration of low earth orbit (LEO) satellites, this makes it hard to directly apply conventional resource scheduling policies in the dynamic SGINs environment. Moreover, substantial multi-modal information in the SGINs environment hinders superior service performance. Thus, we establish a multi-modal enabled task scheduling model to minimize network latency and privacy authentication overhead for processing stochastic task types, time-varying channel gains and dynamic LEO locations. Next, we design a transformer based group relative policy optimization (GRPO) algorithm to further optimize the CPU cycle frequency, the number of quantization bits and block size. Meanwhile, we present a blockchain based privacy authentication protocol to guarantee secure task transactions and demonstrate the quantization error bound via extensive mathematical analytical derivations. Finally, massive simulation results show that the proposed Transformer-GRPO algorithm has superior performance gains in term of network latency and privacy overhead compared with some state-of-the-art benchmarks.

Author: Arisdakessian, S.; Wehbi, O.; Wahab, O. Abdel; Mourad, A.; Otrok, H.
Title: Towards Vox Populi in Federated Learning: A Fair and Inclusive Client Selection Framework
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Artificial Intelligence
Abstract Note: Federated learning (FL) enables distributed model training without centralizing raw data, but existing client selection methods frequently marginalize resource-limited devices. To address this imbalance, we propose a novel Stackelberg-game-based framework that shifts decision-making from a server-centric model to a client-to-client paradigm. Resource-rich leaders form coalitions with resource-limited followers, allowing every client, regardless of capacity, to contribute to and benefit from the global model. We further introduce a comprehensive data scoring mechanism that evaluates the quality and diversity of each client’s dataset, ensuring that coalition formation is both fair and inclusive. Experiments on diverse benchmarks demonstrate that our approach outperforms the state-of-the-art, as well as different baselines on multiple metrics while promoting fairness. Our proposed strategy effectively tackles heterogeneous data distributions and uneven resource availability, offering a scalable, equitable solution for real-world FL scenarios.

Author: Zhao, P.; Su, N.; Wang, Y.; Sun, S.; Li, X.
Title: A Survey on Collaboration Computing for Industrial Internet of Things: Digital Twin, Federated Learning, and Swarm Learning
Publication Title: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
Abstract Note: The Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) deepens the collaborative computing between different devices and control layers. In an IIoT, as a dynamic, time-varying, and complex environment, the digital twin (DT) drives the real-time dynamic mapping between physical devices and twins to achieve global control of industrial production lines. This article reviews the relevant research on the application and deployment of DT in the IIoT, which provides technical support for cross-production line data sharing and accurate decision-making. In particular, the related work of the multilayer collaborative computing architecture built by federated learning (FL) in DT-IIoT is reviewed. We systematically explore the key technical breakthroughs of DT and FL in the IIoT, such as data security collaboration, dynamic resource scheduling, computing efficiency improvement, and cross-domain collaborative computing, from four technologies: edge computing, blockchain, deep reinforcement learning (DRL), and personalized learning (PL). On this basis, we have explored and experimented in detail with fully decentralized SL in IIoT. SL-knowledge distillation (KD) can solve the challenge of reducing the reliability of global model decisions in SL due to multisource heterogeneous data in complex industrial scenarios. Experimental results show that swarm learning-based knowledge distillation (SrwamKD) outperforms other baselines by an average of 0.024 and 0.060 in recall and accuracy, respectively. Author: Bai, Q.; Zuo, Q.; Zhang, J.; Xu, L.

Author: R, V. B.; D, V.; S, S. A.; Ramkumar, M. P.; Selvan, G. S. R. Emil

Author: Anirudh, B. S.; Ramarao, N. T.

Abstract Note: Ciphertext-Policy Attribute Based Framework(CP-ABE) is one-to-many detailed secure data sharing but its bothered by delayed attribute revocation, insecure identity tracing and access policy exposure. Our proposal hides the policy information behind an access tree with the hidden leaf nodes, while our blockchain and InterPlanetary File System(IPFS) offer Tamper-proof storage and auditable traces. In addition to existing protocols, our solution adds machine learning-based behavioral analysis learning from past access logs to identify anomalous usage patterns, allowing preventive defense against insider threats and credential abuse. Moreover we develop CP-ABE to Zero-Trust model by adding contextual variables like device trustwothiness, geoloaction and dynamic risk score to access decisions. This allows access control to adapt to evolving environments while preserving auditablity and privacy.

Author: Nikose, B. V.; Borkar, G. M.

Author: Nandhini, D.; Prashanth, K. V.; Sugunavathy, S.; Vinoth, T.; Saravanan, K. Aanandha; Sati, A.
Title: Advancing Pervasive Wearable Communication Models for Seamless and Secure Ubiquitous Connectivity in IoT-Enabled Environments

Abstract Note: In recent years, the rapid development of wearable Internet of Things (IoT) devices has reshaped the field of healthcare monitoring, smart home environments, fitness tracking, and real-time communication systems. But these current mobile communications structures have significant issues like latency, energy consumption, lack of scalability, compromised security, and inadequate real-time data processing. This paper tackles these challenges by proposing an intelligent pervasive wearable communication framework that combines the mechanisms of edge computing, adaptive communication based on artificial intelligence capabilities, blockchain-based security, federated learning, and energy-efficient transmission mechanisms for the next-generation IoT environments. The proposed architecture is a combination of wearable sensing device, edge processing with nodes, and cloud-blockchain infrastructure for enabling secure and scalable communication. To maximize the allocation of bandwidth, transmission reliability, and reduce latency within the hyperloop system, an adaptive communication strategy is used based on the Deep Q-Network (DQN). The data privacy and secure sharing among wearable devices are additionally supported by blockchain based on smart contracts and federated learning mechanisms, which also support the decentralized authentication process. Author: Chen, C.-M.; Chai, K.; Akhtar, Z.; Agrawal, S.; Kumar, R.; Li, Y.
Title: Proactive Federated Anomaly Detection in Consumer Electronic Ecosystems via Adaptive Learning and Lightweight Auditability

Abstract Note: Consumer electronic ecosystems, such as smart vehicles, wearable devices, connected homes, and Internet of Things (IoT)-enabled transportation systems, face increasing cyber threats, privacy risks, and reliability challenges. Experimental results on the CICIDS2017 dataset show that SABFL achieves performance comparable to existing methods under IID conditions, while yielding significantly stronger robustness under non-IID scenarios. In highly heterogeneous settings, SABFL improves the Macro-F1 score by up to 20.58% compared with standard federated baselines, and outperforms the advanced FedNova approach by 16.43%. Author: K, K. S.; K, L.

Author: Isong, J. A.; Ajakwe, S. O.; Kim, D.-S.
Title: XS-FedPRS: Explainable and Secure Federated Learning for Privacy-Preserving Genomic Analytics in Federated Healthcare Networks
Publication Title: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
Abstract Note: In federated healthcare networks (FHNs), collaborative learning enables distributed genomic intelligence across hospital sites and clinical institutions without centralizing sensitive patient data. However, federated polygenic risk prediction (PRS) across heterogeneous healthcare networks faces three critical challenges: population-stratified rare-variant distributions that diverge across clinical sites, Byzantine attacks mimicking rare-variant signals, and lack of interpretability for clinical decision support. We present Explainable and Secure Federated Polygenic Risk Score (XS-FedPRS), a framework that decouples common variants (global aggregation) from rare variants (population-specific clustering), defends against Byzantine attacks through Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium (HWE) testing and gradient plausibility analysis, and provides multilevel explainability for clinical decision support. Proof-of-Authority-and-Association (PoA2) ensures auditable governance across participating sites. Evaluation across three genomic cohorts of increasing scale and realism—CINECA synthetic (483 samples), 1000 Genomes Phase 3 (2504 samples and five continental populations), and msprime-simulated (50 000 samples and Out-of-Africa demography)—demonstrates that XS-FedPRS achieves 84.4% area under the (ROC) curve (AUC) on the largest cohort under population-stratified non-independent and identically distributed (IID) partitioning, detects gradient poisoning, model poisoning, sybil, and combined Byzantine attacks with perfect precision and recall ( \F 1=1.0\ ), maintains privacy (0.026 membership inference attack (MIA) advantage), and incurs only 3.3% communication overhead versus FedAvg. XS-FedPRS enables trustworthy, interpretable federated genomic analytics across heterogeneous healthcare networks devices for precision medicine.

Author: Mishra, N.; Reddy, B. V. Sreedhar; Jaswanth, B.; Gayathri, M.; Kumar, B. S.
Title: AI-Enhanced Blockchain-Based Certificate Verification using Hybrid Deep Learning Models
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Electronics and Renewable Systems (ICEARS)
Abstract Note: In Advancement of digital world, the increase in the pace of issuing the digital certificates has also escalated the threat of fake educational qualifications, including in blockchain-based systems of verification, where the immutability cannot be enough to eliminate the registration of forged documents. In order to overcome this drawback, this research suggests an AI-enhanced blockchain-based certificate verification architecture that combines a hybrid deep learning model and the ElimuChain architecture. The proposed structure uses CNN-BiLSTM model that is able to identify visual and semantic inconsistencies in the certificates before anchoring them to the blockchain thus avoiding the possibility of forged certificates being stored permanently. The checked certificates are then hashed, hosted on the IPFS and permanently recorded on the blockchain through the smart contracts. Experimental assessment on a combined dataset of true and fake certificates proves that the proposed model has an accuracy of 98.3, precision of 97.9, recall of 98.6 and an F1-score of 98.2, which is better than standalone CNN and Transformer-based baselines. Trust, security, and reliability of nationwide systems of certificate verification are greatly increased based on the integration of AI-driven pre-validation.
