Author: Yang, X.; Feng, J.; Ma, L.; Liu, L.; Pei, Q.; Wu, C.
Title: Federated Spatiotemporal Policy Learning for Efficient Resource Management in UAV-Assisted IoT Edge Networks
Publication Title: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
Abstract Note: Federated learning (FL) enables privacy-preserving distributed intelligence in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-assisted Internet of Things (IoT) edge networks. However, the efficient policy design remains challenging due to the hybrid decision space, which couples combinatorial device scheduling with continuous resource allocation, as well as the long-term impact of nonindependent and identically distributed (Non-IID) data on model convergence. In this article, we propose a spatiotemporal resource optimization framework for UAV-assisted edge computing services. We formulate a long-term utility maximization problem that jointly considers learning performance, energy consumption, and latency. To solve this mixed-integer nonlinear problem, a federated spatiotemporal policy optimization (FSTPO) approach is developed based on a constrained Markov game. The proposed method incorporates a dual-channel spatiotemporal representation to capture wireless dynamics and data distribution characteristics. In addition, a hybrid action learning mechanism is introduced to efficiently handle the coupling between discrete scheduling and continuous resource allocation. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms benchmark schemes in terms of system utility, learning accuracy, and resource efficiency, while achieving stable convergence under Non-IID environments.
Manual Tags: federated learning (FL); Edge computing; resource management; spatiotemporal policy learning; unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-assisted Internet of Things (IoT) networks

Author: Nagamani, K.; Lingala, P.; Tejaswi, B.; Divya, E.; Deepa, Y. G.
Title: Adaptive Federated Stream Processing Model for Real-Time Distributed Intelligence
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICACT)
Abstract Note: The blistering pace of mushrooming, high-velocity data sets—including those from IoT ecosystems, cyber-physical systems, social platforms, and autonomous networks —has increased the need for real-time analytics of an intelligent, decentralised, and privacy-maintaining nature. Traditional big data services, such as Apache Spark streaming on Apache Flink or Kafka Streams, provide scalable stream analytics solutions. Still, they are centralised, suffer from high latency, experience communication bottlenecks, and introduce vulnerabilities. New paradigms like Federated Learning (FL), Edge Computing, TensorFlow Federated (TFF), and Blockchain-based Federated Systems have sought to address these problems by performing local computations and enabling distributed cooperation. Nevertheless, these systems continue to face severe challenges in synchronising asynchronous updates, handling non-stationary data streams, accommodating node heterogeneity, and ensuring adaptive model reliability in the face of real-world dynamic events. This paper will overcome these shortcomings by proposing a new Federated Stream Intelligence (FSI) architecture, an enhanced federated stream processing paradigm, and a synthesis of the Dynamic Stream Sharing (DSS), Collaborative Edge-Oriented Aggregation (CEOA), and Adaptive Trust Reinforcement (ATR) paradigms. The proposed FSI offers the benefit of decentralising the computation of streams within the network, splitting continuous data streams smartly among edge participants, performing local micro-stream analytics using lightweight temporal models compatible with Edge TPU devices, and coordinating intelligence on a global scale via a weighted, asynchronous consensus protocol. The trust scoring is implemented using reinforcement and Partial Gradient Masking (PGM) to provide robustness against malicious nodes and privacy leakage. As experimentally shown, FSI is vastly superior to the latest frameworks such as FedAvg, HFL, and blockchain-FL hybrids, achieving 47 per cent lower global synchronisation latency, 22 per cent more accurate event detection, and reducing communication overhead by more than 40 per cent. The FSI model is a robust framework for real-time noncentric big data intelligence, based on adaptive privacy ensured by its synergy, intelligent stream partitioning, and self-organising aggregation, and can be applied to smart city infrastructure, financial surveillance, and self-governing industry structures.
Manual Tags: Federated Learning; Privacy Preservation; Edge Computing; Real-Time Analytics; Adaptive Aggregation; Decentralised Intelligence; Stream Processing

Author: Rathee, D.; Dauterman, E.; Li, A.; Popa, R. A.
Title: CHORUS: Secret Recovery with Ephemeral Client Committees
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (SP)
Abstract Note: End-to-end encrypted applications protect user data by ensuring that user secrets are only available on client devices. However, if a user loses all of their devices, they need a way to recover their data using only a short password. To realize a password-based secret recovery system resilient to brute-force attacks, prior works relied on secure hardware or a few non-colluding servers. In this work, we take a conceptually different approach that distributes trust across the many clients already in the system, while using the server only as an orchestrator without relying on it for privacy. To achieve this, we design and implement Chorus, a secret recovery system that employs ephemeral committees, each consisting of approximately a thousand clients, to provide strong privacy with high scalability. Committees change frequently in Chorus, typically on the order of a few minutes, to severely limit an attacker's ability to compromise clients on a committee. We design Chorus for unreliable, resource-constrained clients and show that the perclient overhead decreases as more clients join the system. Assuming each user performs recovery once a year, the expected per-client overhead in Chorus is under 30 s of computation on a mobile device and 13.2 MB of communication, both incurred only once every four months in a configuration with 100 M clients, up to 50 M of which may be offline and at most 10 M may be compromised. To achieve this performance, we contribute two key techniques: (i) a password-based secret recovery scheme that confines expensive committee interactions to infrequent, latency-tolerant operations, and (ii) a non-interactive verifiable secret-sharing scheme that reduces client overhead by two orders of magnitude by delegating computation to the server.
Manual Tags: identity-based encryption; client committees; non-interactive vss; password-based secret recovery

Author: Wang, P.; Liu, J.; Xian, Y.; Peng, K.; Liu, P.; Li, X.
Title: HFed-CMS: Cluster-Based Hierarchical Federated Multitask Learning With Fair Edge Node Selection
Publication Title: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
Abstract Note: Hierarchical federated learning (HFL) has emerged as a promising paradigm for distributed machine learning in edge computing environments. By introducing intermediate edge servers (ESs) between clients and the central server, HFL enhances system scalability and reduces communication latency. However, the heterogeneity of Internet of Things (IoT) devices—encompassing computational resources, data distributions, and network conditions—poses significant challenges for effective model training. Resource-constrained devices may fail to complete training tasks within designated time windows, resulting in wasted computational efforts, discarded learning rounds, and degraded model performance. To address these challenges, this article proposes HFed-CMS, a novel HFL framework that integrates intelligent client clustering, predictive selection, and fairness mechanisms. Our approach first performs hierarchical clustering (HC) based on the similarity of clients’ local model weights, which implicitly captures underlying data distribution patterns and reduces intracluster heterogeneity. Subsequently, we introduce a predictive client selection strategy that evaluates multidimensional device capabilities—including central processing unit (CPU), memory, energy, and network bandwidth—to ensure that selected clients can successfully complete their assigned training tasks. Furthermore, we incorporate a fairness mechanism through bandwidth reutilization to guarantee equitable participation opportunities for all clients in long-term training scenarios. Through comprehensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets under various heterogeneous settings (both system and statistical heterogeneity), we demonstrate that HFed-CMS significantly outperforms existing approaches.
Manual Tags: federated learning (FL); edge computing; Client selection; hierarchical architecture; nonindependent and identically distributed (Non-IID) data

Author: Zhang, Y.; Jiao, L.; Zhu, K.; Feng, Y.; Zhang, L.; Xu, J.
Title: Budget-Aware Cost-Efficient Edge AI Inference for Data Streams via Blockchain-Empowered Auctions
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Services Computing
Abstract Note: To achieve efficient edge AI inference, edge AI service providers often acquire pre-trained models from the model market. However, this process becomes complex due to unknown bid and inference quality distributions, the strategic behavior of self-interested providers, strict budgetary constraints, and the single-point-of-failure risks inherent in centralized platforms. To address all these challenges, we propose a blockchain-empowered model auction mechanism that facilitates secure and cost-efficient model procurement. Specifically, we design a novel budget-aware auction-assisted dual-learning algorithm framework, named AucLearn, which jointly optimizes model auction and blockchain control decisions. AucLearn leverages real-time performance feedback to minimize long-term total cost while strictly adhering to both financial and computational resource budgets. We further provide rigorous proofs of multiple performance guarantees for AucLearn, including sub-linear regret for both subproblems and the overall problem, sub-linear fit for long-term capacity constraints, as well as truthfulness and individual rationality in each auction. Extensive evaluations driven by real-world traces demonstrate that AucLearn exhibits significant advantages over multiple state-of-the-art solutions.
Manual Tags: blockchain; Edge AI; auction; data stream; online optimization

Author: Telrandhe, A. V.; Puri, C.; Nishane, D.; Katade, R.
Title: Explainable AI Models for Insider Threat Detection in Smart Healthcare Systems
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on AI-Driven Smart Systems and Ubiquitous Computing (ICAUC)
Abstract Note: The Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) and Intelligent Healthcare Systems provide real-time monitoring, anticipatory care, and tailored healthcare services, but the unchecked expansion of these networks brings profound security concerns such as spoofing attack security threats, insider threats, and unprotected break-ins to sensitive data. Conventional security systems are inefficient for the complexities of IoMT networks, system imbalance, and the black-box nature of the majority of Artificial Intelligence models. As such, in this paper, the author introduces the application of the novel Explainable AI (XAI) secure approach for the IoMT network, comprising a designed spoofing attack detection model using a transformer neural network, a designed privacy-preserving intrusion detection model using federated learning, and the HMM-based proactive insider threat controls. The developed model is applied to the CIC-IoMT2024 dataset, employing the sophisticated preprocessing approach including SMOTE-Tomek links and attention-aggregated LSTM models, and various Explainable AI approaches including SHAP, LIME, to assess the results. The results obtained in the current research explicitly evidence immense accuracy with overall spoofing attack precision of 99.71% and maximum inside threat accuracy of 91.7% with overall HMM Confidence of 97-98%.

Author: Li, Y.; Li, Y.; Du, J.; Shao, Y.; Liang, M.; Ye, G.
Title: Trust-free Personalized Decentralized Learning
Abstract Note: Personalized collaborative learning in federated settings faces a critical trade-off between customization and participant trust. Existing approaches typically rely on centralized coordinators or trusted peer groups, limiting their applicability in open, trust-averse environments. While recent decentralized methods explore anonymous knowledge sharing, they often lack global scalability and robust mechanisms against malicious peers. To bridge this gap, we propose TPFed, a Trust-free Personalized Decentralized Federated Learning framework. TPFed replaces central aggregators with a blockchain-based bulletin board, enabling participants to dynamically select global communication partners based on Locality-Sensitive Hashing (LSH) and peer ranking. Crucially, we introduce an "all-in-one"" knowledge distillation protocol that simultaneously handles knowledge transfer

Author: Kundu, A.
Title: Tamper-Resistant Medical Diagnosis via Quantum-Initialised AI and Blockchain-Based Verification
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Trends in Quantum Computing and Emerging Business Technologies (TQCEBT)
Abstract Note: The increasing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in medical diagnosis has raised several questions about trust, integrity, and medico-legal accountability. Although AI models can achieve high diagnostic accuracy, current models are vulnerable to post-hoc attacks and lack transparent audit trails. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a blockchainbased quantum-AI solution for secure and tamper-proof medical diagnosis. In the proposed solution, an AI-powered diagnostic model predicts heart disease based on clinical inputs. A quantum random number generator is used during model initialisation to make the training process unbiased and non-deterministic, thus improving trust in the AI model. To maintain the integrity of the diagnosis, the cryptographic hash values of the input data, AI parameters, and diagnosis results are calculated and stored to simulate the immutability of blockchain technology. Any unauthorised modification to the diagnosis result will immediately cause a mismatch in the hash values, thereby enabling effective tampering detection. The proposed system is validated using the Heart Disease Cleveland dataset. The proposed system achieves a test accuracy of 85.25% and can accurately detect all simulated post-diagnosis attacks. The experimental results clearly demonstrate that the proposed system is capable not only of providing accurate medical diagnoses but also of maintaining transparency, integrity, and auditability of AI-based medical diagnoses.

Author: S, G.; T, D.; Deepa, N.
Title: Federated Edge-Cloud Hybrid Deep Learning Architecture for Privacy-Preserving Fault Prediction in Industrial IoT Systems
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
Abstract Note: Recent developments of the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) systems have transformed the concept of predictive maintenance, allowing fault detection in complex machinery in real-time. Nonetheless, the centralization of sensitive operation data to train the model is highly problematic related to the data privacy, data latency, and the scale issue. To overcome these weaknesses, this paper presents Federated Edge Computing-Cloud Hybrid Deep Learning Architecture, which is privacy-sensitive collaborative learning among distributed HoT nodes. Local sensor data are trained on different edge node lightweight CNN-LSTM fault predictors and global model updates are synchronized by adaptive federated optimization (FedProx, FedOpt) on the cloud. In order to maintain confidentiality further, we add the privacy of differentiation and safe aggregation protocol. The experimental performance of the proposed model on benchmarked HoT datasets shows that the proposed model has a maximum accuracy of 94.65, compared to the conventional edge-only (89.55) and non-private federated baselines \(91.77 \textbackslash{}%)\. Besides this, inference latency is less than 25 milliseconds, therefore can be used in real-time industrial applications. The model is tested with heterogeneous data distributions, bandwidth constraints, and privacy budgets with strong convergence and resistance to client drift. Transformerlite classifiers with the help of LIME which ensure explainability, provide interpretable fault insights. The architecture is data protection, predictive performance, and operational efficiency balancing, which is suitable in smart factories. The future efforts are the blockchain-enabled auditability, federated transfer learning of unknown faults, and the energy-conscious training of ultra-low-power HoT nodes. The outcomes support the practicability of implementing federated AI in delicate industrial settings without any reduction to the level of security and precision.

Author: Al-Abri, A. J. S.; R, W. B. N.; Al-Nasseri, S. H. A.; G, S. S.; C, S. C.; A, C.
Title: AI–based Detection of Credit Card Fraud: Protecting Citizens and Financial Institutions
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on AI-Driven Smart Systems and Ubiquitous Computing (ICAUC)
Abstract Note: In recent years, digital financial transactions have grown rapidly worldwide, especially via bank ATM cards, credit or debit cards, digital wallets, and payment gateways. This growth increases the risk of financial fraud, as traditional rule-based detection systems are limited and public awareness of protecting sensitive banking information is low. This study explores AI-driven solutions for fraud detection. A survey-based analysis was conducted among banking customers in Oman’s Al Dhahirah Region to examine perceptions of trust, accuracy, privacy, and transparency in AI-based systems. Based on the analysis, a novel framework combining federated learning and explainable AI is proposed to enhance fraud detection accuracy while preserving customer data privacy and improving model interpretability. Author: Kumar, M. S.; Jayaraj, V.; Prabhu, R.; R.Senthilkumar; Nayaka, R. J.; Parveen, S. N.
Title: Adaptive Game-Theoretic Cybersecurity Evaluation for Smart City IoT Networks
Publication Title: 2026 9th International Conference on Computing Methodologies and Communication (ICCMC)
Abstract Note: Smart city networks combine large-scale IoT, cloud, and edge systems to provide the necessary urban service, but its excessive complexity and openness greatly increase the area of cyber-attack and risk of operation. Current methods of security assessment are more or less categorized as a static system that does not reflect the dynamic interplay of the attackers and countermeasures in dynamism cities, which drives the perspective towards a more responsive evaluation system. In this paper, a model of dynamic competition is presented, which develops cybersecurity evaluation based on the payoff optimization and resource constraints as the models and approaches of attacker and defender which adapt with the transition of the network state. This model is integrated in a security assessment system to measure the likelihood of the attack, adequacy of defense, and cost of operations and tested it via simulation in a model smart city network. Experimental findings prove that experimental threat containment and lower cost of security are better than static risk assessment and traditional intrusion response, and offer greater resilience to network against coordinated and persistent attacks. The solution is a viable and scalable system to conduct constant appraisal of cybersecurity and make informed and reactive defense readiness towards vital smart city frameworks.

Author: Chu, S.; Li, J.; Wang, J.; Ni, Y.; Wei, K.; Chen, W.; Jin, S.
Title: Resource Efficient Asynchronous Federated Learning for Digital Twin Empowered IoT Network
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Green Communications and Networking
Abstract Note: As an emerging technology, digital twin (DT) can provide real-time status and dynamic topology mapping for Internet of Things (IoT) devices. However, the implementation of DT within IoT networks necessitates substantial, distributed data support, which raises privacy concerns. To address these issues, we develop a dynamic resource scheduling algorithm tailored for the asynchronous federated learning (FL)-based lightweight DT empowered IoT network. Specifically, our approach aims to minimize a multi-objective function that considers both energy consumption and latency by optimizing IoT device selection and transmit power control, while adhering to long-term performance constraints derived from the convergence upper bound for asynchronous FL. We utilize the Lyapunov method to decompose the formulated problem into a series of one-slot optimization problems and design a two-stage optimization algorithm to achieve optimal transmit power control and efficient IoT device scheduling. In the first stage, we derive closed-form solutions for optimal transmit power on the IoT device side. In the second stage, to address the uncertainty in partial state information, the edge server leverages a multi-armed bandit (MAB) framework to model the IoT device selection problem and employs an efficient online algorithm, the client utility-based upper confidence bound (CU-UCB), to solve it. Moreover, we analyze the algorithm’s optimality gap and time-averaged regret, further demonstrating its effectiveness in resource allocation. Numerical results confirm the superior performance of our algorithm compared to benchmark methods, with the CU-UCB algorithm achieving an 18.9% reduction in average cost and a 6% improvement in accuracy on real-world datasets.

Author: Gowthami, S.; Devi, T. K.; Sakthivel, P.; Raj, V. P.
Title: SARRA: A Secure Adaptive and Resilient Routing Framework of FANETs with Hybrid Blockchain and Deep Q-Network Intelligence
Publication Title: 2026 7th International Conference on Mobile Computing and Sustainable Informatics (ICMCSI)
Abstract Note: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), referred to as Flying Ad Hoc Networks (FANETs), play a crucial role in disaster response due to their ability to enable rapid communication without the need for existing infrastructure. However, their high mobility, frequent link disruptions, energy problems, and security risks all have a detrimental effect on the networks' performance and stability. To address these challenges, this paper introduces SARRA (Secure Adaptive Resilient Routing and Authentication), a hybrid intelligent model. SARRA integrates Deep Q-Network-based routing, lightweight blockchain authentication, Particle Swarm Optimization for efficient cluster head selection, Ant Colony Optimization for robust path recovery, and a Federated Learning-based Intrusion Detection System to detect threats while preserving privacy. The DQN agent provides active choices of the best paths to forward by considering multidimensional state variables such as residual energy, the quality of links, hop distance, degree of congestion, and the trust score, and blockchain provides decentralized and tamper-proof node authentication. Decades of simulations on the NS-3 environment demonstrate that the SARRA is superior to standard AODV, LEACH, and base DQN protocols in terms of Packet Delivery Ratio improvement of 19.6 percent, end-to-end delay reduction by 17.3 percent, average energy consumption decrease by 22.8 percent, and throughput increase by 25.1 percent. In addition, In addition, 18.4 more routing overhead is minimized, the network lifetime is prolonged by 21.7 and the FL-IDS detects intrusions with an accuracy of 94.6 with a false positive probability of 3.2. The experiment outcome validates that SARRA is an effective solution to provide highly resilient and fault-tolerant disasterresponse networking by virtue of the fact that it greatly increases the security, adaptability, and fault tolerance of FANET communication systems.

Author: Thiruppathi, K.; P, G. S.; Arivukarasi, M.; Kalaivani, P.; Vennila, G.

Author: Li, M.; Chen, J.; Guo, S.; Qiu, X.; Qi, F.
Title: DDoS Attack Detection in Business Blockchain Networks: A Review, Framework, and Challenges
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering
Abstract Note: With the rapid growth of the Internet of Things and the increasing deployment of blockchain technology in critical applications, distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks pose a significant threat to the security and availability of blockchain networks. However, due to the lack of data sharing among different business chains, existing attack detection systems fail to identify global DDoS attack patterns. This leads to reduced detection accuracy and timeliness, as well as increased risks of false positives and false negatives. Moreover, it prevents the implementation of distributed collaborative defense mechanisms, allowing attackers to bypass local defenses through cross-chain attacks.This paper reviews the current state of DDoS attack detection in blockchain networks and provides a preliminary look at the challenges facing the field.To address these challenges, this paper proposes a new intrusion detection system, BAFL, which utilizes supervision chain and federated learning to detect DDoS attacks in blockchain network layer. We design a distributed DDoS architecture that utilizes a supervised chain of directed acyclic graph (DAG) structures to achieve trusted sharing of model parameters among client nodes and record detected DDoS attacks. The system uses asynchronous federated learning algorithm, weights the client model based on its DDoS attack detection accuracy, and introduces a time attenuation factor to reduce the influence of old model parameters on aggregation and accelerate model convergence. Through comprehensive experiments on data sets such as CIC-DDoS2019, we demonstrated that the accuracy of BAFL in detecting DDoS attacks is more than 99%, which is better than traditional methods, the accuracy is increased by 2%, and the real-time detection delay is reduced by half. The results highlight the robustness and scalability of BAFL, making it a promising solution for protecting blockchain networks from DDoS threats.

Author: Ghadekar, P.; Mane, R.; Mane, M.; Joy, J.; Kharate, P.; Kudale, S.

The digital twin is constantly updated with real-time patient and inventory data, blockchain provides a secure, immutable and auditable transaction. The experimental findings show greater accuracy in the diagnosis, lesser error in prediction and consistent demand forecasting, which can be used by clinicians and supply-chain stakeholders to make appropriate decisions. Author: Sultana, I.; Maheen, S. M.; Kshetri, N.; Pandian, S. K.; Syed, M. M.; Ahmed, M. R.
Title: safeMEDInet: Fed AI Systems for Privacy-Preserving Threat Detection in Healthcare
Publication Title: 2026 14th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
Abstract Note: The explosive growth of digital healthcare data and networked Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) devices has heightened vulnerabilities inside healthcare networks, hence exposing sensitive medical systems to sophisticated cyber assaults. The safeMEDInet framework offers a secure, federated artificial intelligence (AI) architecture that allows decentralized healthcare institutions to cooperatively identify and address problems without disclosing raw patient data. safeMEDInet utilizes federated learning along with privacy-preserving techniques, such as differential privacy, homomorphic encryption, and Byzantine-resilient aggregation, to guarantee confidentiality, integrity, and adherence to regulations in remote settings. The proposed framework integrates a hybrid CNN-LSTM model for spatiotemporal intrusion detection with secure model synchronization and encrypted parameter sharing to ensure robust accuracy against various cyber-attacks, including ransomware, unauthorized access, and distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) intrusions. Empirical assessments utilizing MIMIC-IV, HealthData.gov, and WHO datasets reveal that safeMEDInet achieves a detection accuracy of 96.8% with robust privacy assurances \(\textbackslash{}varepsilon=1.9)\ and sustains an accuracy of 88.4 % despite 30% Byzantine interference, surpassing traditional federated and centralized systems. The findings confirm safeMEDInet's capacity to guarantee high detection reliability, low processing cost, and mathematical assurance of privacy resilience. This research positions safeMEDInet as a pivotal advancement towards safe, scalable, and ethically governed Healthcare 5.0 ecosystems, incorporating AI-driven privacy, federated cooperation, and blockchain-supported data integrity for next-generation medical cybersecurity.

Author: Nurdin; Lawi, A.; Toaha, S.
Title: From Biometric Surfaces to Contextual Intelligence: A Comprehensive Survey of Multimodal Authentication and the Trimodal Fusion Paradigm
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Current Research in Artificial Intelligence and Data Science (ICCRAIDS)
Abstract Note: The rapid advancement of Generative AI-based cyberattacks and deepfakes has exposed the inherent vulnerabilities of unimodal biometric systems. This article presents a systematic and comprehensive survey of multimodal authentication, evolving from traditional physical biometrics to a “Trimodal Fusion” paradigm that integrates physiological (face), behavioral (voice), and contextual intelligence (location). Through a rigorous review of literature from 2008 to 2025, we map the technological transition from classical statistical methods, such as Gaussian Mixture Models (GMM), to adaptive Deep Learning (DL) architectures utilizing attention mechanisms. Our analysis identifies a critical security paradigm shift toward a Zero Trust model. We propose a novel HybridSequential Architecture that prioritizes a Pre-Fusion Validation Layer incorporating liveness detection via internal modalities (e.g., ECG) and data integrity checks before feature-level integration. A unique contribution of this survey is the conceptualization of the “Location Trust Anchor,” which utilizes spatial context to dynamically adjust security thresholds while mitigating privacy risks through Deep Hashing and Blockchain integration. Furthermore, we explore the dual role of Generative AI, identifying it not only as a sophisticated threat vector but also as a defensive mechanism for missing modality recovery. This study concludes by addressing the implementation feasibility of edge devices and providing a roadmap for future research in privacy-preserving, resilient multimodal authentication ecosystems.

Author: Yu, B.; Zhong, Z.; Liu, Y.; Zhao, Y.
Title: Federated Transfer Learning for Personalized Household Financial Services
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Foundation Models (BTFM)
Abstract Note: Household financial services face the dual challenges of data privacy protection and personalized recommendation. Federated learning protects user privacy through distributed training, but heterogeneous data distribution leads to degraded model performance. Transfer learning can leverage source domain knowledge to improve target domain model effectiveness. This study constructs a household financial service framework based on federated transfer learning, designing cross-institutional knowledge transfer mechanisms and personalized adaptive aggregation strategies. Author: Borhan, U. M.; Raza, A.; Uddin, T.; Islam, M.; Islam, A. K. M. M.; Chen, J.
Title: Performance, Adaptability, and Security in AI-Driven IIoT: A Survey
Publication Title: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
Abstract Note: The Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) integrates cyber–physical systems (CPSs), edge–cloud computing, artificial intelligence (AI), and advanced connectivity to enable intelligent, data-driven operations across manufacturing, energy, transportation, and healthcare. The convergence of operational technology (OT) and information technology (IT), together with pervasive AI-driven automation, complicates meeting the joint requirements of performance, adaptability, and security (PAS). This survey adopts an explicitly AI-centric view of PAS and reviews IIoT research spanning deep reinforcement learning (DRL), multiagent reinforcement learning (MARL), digital twins (DTs), federated learning (FL) and collaborative learning, graph neural networks (GNNs), blockchain-assisted analytics, and lightweight and post-quantum cryptography (PQC). The reviewed approaches are analyzed across device, edge, fog, cloud, and application layers under industrial constraints, such as latency, reliability, resource limits, safety requirements, and regulatory compliance. A PAS-centric taxonomy is introduced that links technique families to deployment layers and application domains, and recurring tradeoffs among PAS dimensions are summarized. Open challenges are identified in multiobjective optimization, semantic interoperability, lifecycle validation, and governance, with directions outlined toward secure and sustainable Industry 5.0 IIoT ecosystems.

Author: Shati, I. A. K.; Gernaz, M. F. S.; Jernz, R. S. S.; Arfa, A. S. A.
Title: Green AI Integration for Secure and Sustainable IoT Communications in Wi-Fi 7 Networks: A Comparative Review
Publication Title: 2026 7th International Conference on Computing, Networks and Internet of Things (CNIOT)
Abstract Note: The rapid proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices demands secure and sustainable communication paradigms, particularly with the advent of Wi-Fi 7 (IEEE 802.11be), which offers enhanced throughput, low latency, and multi-link operations for dense deployments. However, integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) for cybersecurity in these networks often incurs high energy costs, conflicting with sustainability goals. This paper addresses this challenge through a comprehensive comparative study on Green AI energy-efficient AI techniques and their integration to advance secure and sustainable IoT communications in Wi-Fi 7 environments. Following an introduction to the problem and key motivations, we review recent literature (\2023-2025\) on Green AI models for threat detection, energy harvesting in IoT, and Wi-Fi 7's role in low-power networking. A novel taxonomy classifies approaches by AI type and application domain, enabling a systematic comparative analysis of energy efficiency, security efficacy, latency, and scalability across 20 representative studies. Key findings reveal significant synergies, such as federated learning and renewable-aware edge inference for substantial carbon reduction, alongside persistent challenges like resource heterogeneity and privacy-efficiency trade-offs. The analysis concludes with targeted future directions toward integrated 6G-convergent frameworks, providing a roadmap for eco-friendly, resilient IoT ecosystems.

Author: Wang, B.; Yan, Y.; Zhang, M.; Wang, W.; Yao, H.
Title: Model Backdoor Attack on Federated Learning Based on Parameter Analysis
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing
Abstract Note: With the increasingly widespread application of federated learning (FL) in various fields, the issue of backdoor attacks against FL has garnered significant attention from both academia and industry. While there has been some progress in researching backdoor attacks against FL, data backdoor attacks are easily mitigated in federated environments, and model backdoor attacks are susceptible to detection by defense mechanisms. Therefore, we propose a refined backdoor attack method tailored for FL under the image classification task. Our method involves the collaborative operation of three key modules. Firstly, the parameter importance analysis module identifies parameters with minimal impact on model performance, and creates parameter importance masks to provide precise targets for subsequent operations. Subsequently, the activation difference computation module calculates the activation differences between backdoor samples and benign samples to locate trigger-sensitive parameters. Our method implants the backdoor by flipping and zeroing the precisely located layer parameters, while maintaining the model’s classification performance on benign samples. Experimental results show that our method is feasible to achieve an average attack success rate more than 99% across the three victim models. This demonstrates the effectiveness of our method in FL environments and its robustness against various FL defense mechanisms.

Author: Liang, Y.; Qiu, Y.
Title: A multimodal data privacy protection framework based on federated learning and blockchain
Publication Title: 7th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Manufacturing (AIAM 2025)
Abstract Note: With the rapid advancement of smart healthcare, financial technology, and the Internet of Things (IoT), multimodal data integration and analysis have emerged as a key driver for breakthroughs in artificial intelligence (AI) model performance. Ensuring collaborative modeling while preserving data privacy across organizations has thus become a critical challenge. This paper proposes an innovative privacy-preserving multimodal data framework that integrates federated learning with blockchain technology. The framework establishes a decentralized, verifiable, and incentive-compatible collaborative learning ecosystem. Specifically, this paper designs a modality-aware differential privacy mechanism that introduces gradient perturbation and lightweight encryption during local training, thereby defending against membership inference and model inversion attacks. Moreover, a token-based economic model is incorporated to incentivize high-quality data contributions while enabling complete traceability of collaborative processes. Extensive experiments results show that the proposed approach achieves an F1-score of 92.7% with less than 2% performance degradation under differential privacy constraints, system robustness against adversarial participants improves significantly from 72% to 89%. These findings highlight that the proposed framework not only ensures strong privacy guarantees but also enhances robustness and trustworthiness, laying a solid theoretical and technological foundation for building next-generation decentralized and sustainable AI infrastructures.

Author: Cheng, Z.; Wang, B.; Chen, Y.; Wu, C.; Deng, X.; Liu, Y.; Zhu, C.
Title: Value-Compensated Decentralized Data Sharing: Can a Dual-Blockchain Framework With a Proof-of-Lightweight-Shapley Algorithm Make It Possible?
Publication Title: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
Abstract Note: The recent convergence of blockchain-based federated learning (BCFL) offers enhanced data privacy, traceability, and ownership protection for decentralized data sharing. However, current research lacks consensus on accurate and fair data valuation methods for decentralized environments—a critical yet unresolved challenge. Existing Shapley value (SV)-based data valuation methods, while promising, rely on centralized frameworks ill-suited for decentralized environments and incur high computational costs. To address this, we propose a scalable dual-chain architecture: the main chain handles primary BCFL data-sharing operations, while a dedicated side-chain offloads data valuation tasks. For the side chain, we introduce the proof-of-lightweight-Shapley (PoLS) protocol, enabling decentralized SV computation with theoretical convergence guarantees. PoLS leverages a proof-of-work (PoW)-inspired mechanism to facilitate parallel and lightweight computation of SVs using Monte Carlo sampling. Furthermore, we develop an SV-based data aggregation protocol to validate PoLS effectiveness and enhance resilience against low-quality data attacks. Extensive experiments confirm that PoLS significantly reduces computational overhead while maintaining an average deviation as low as 2.3% from the true SV. Moreover, in adversarial scenarios, the PoLS-driven aggregation strategy improves model accuracy by 25.7% over baselines, thereby strengthening the robustness and fairness of the decentralized valuable data sharing.

Author: Zekiye, A.; Özkasap, Ö; Bouachir, O.; Aloqaily, M.

Author: Singh, S. K.; Gohel, B.; Kumar, M.; Saxena, S. N.; Restas, A.
Title: Blockchain-Enabled Federated GRU-Based Secure Digital Twin Architecture for Smart Agriculture Recommendation Systems
Publication Title: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
Abstract Note: The continuous digitization of the modern farming sector demands secure, intelligent, privacy-preserving, and scalable infrastructures for real-time data analysis. However, existing smart farming systems face significant challenges, including cyberthreats, data authenticity issues, and the need for reliable decision support. This article proposes a secure digital twin (DT) architecture for smart agriculture recommendation systems, integrated with blockchain and federated gated recurrent units (FGRUs). At the perception layer, Internet of Things (IoT) sensors monitor soil, crop, and environmental data, which are gathered by a request control authority (RCA) and transmitted to local models. To ensure privacy, a GRU-based federated learning (FL) approach is employed to detect cyberattacks—such as Sybil, man-in-the-middle (MITM), DDoS, and Replay attacks—without exposing raw decentralized data. Furthermore, a blockchain-assisted zero-knowledge proof-based authority (ZKPA) mechanism is integrated to ensure data authenticity. The validated farming data are stored at the architecture’s final layer, enabling a physical twin to monitor real-time processes and generate precise recommendations. The architecture was evaluated using a paddy field dataset (26 features, 10 081 samples). Experimental results show that the proposed federated GRU model achieves perfect detection performance for all considered attacks, while the ZKPA-based authentication mechanism achieves a 98%–99% authentication success rate with sub-10 ms verification time and only 15%–25% additional computational overhead, which is better than existing works.

Author: Gurung, D.; Pokhrel, S. R.; Li, G.
Title: Quantum Federated Learning: A Comprehensive Review and Analysis
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Artificial Intelligence
Abstract Note: This article presents a comprehensive review and empirical analysis of quantum federated learning (QFL), an emerging interdisciplinary field integrating quantum machine learning (QML) with federated learning. Driven by the growing capabilities of quantum computing (QC) and the various challenges in classical federated learning (CFL) such as computational capacity, handling large-scale distributed data, etc., we examine the theoretical foundations, methodological developments, and practical challenges of QFL. Our work systematically examines the existing literature, categorizes existing QFL approaches, and assesses their applicability across diverse domains. Leveraging major quantum platforms including Qiskit, PennyLane, and TensorCircuit, we conduct extensive experiments on both simulators and real IBM quantum hardware. We provide comprehensive literature review, extensive experimental analysis showcasing significant discrepancies such as between simulated and real-hardware results, impact of heterogeneity, platform specific limitations with multiple ablation studies examining impact of noise, quantum classifier, simulators, etc. We conclude with discussions on various insights that identify open research challenges and outline future directions for scalable and reliable QFL integration with next-generation technologies.

Author: Gao, S.; Huang, C.; Zhu, J.; Ma, X.; Dong, J.
Title: Density-Aware Adaptive Weight Optimization Against Data Heterogeneity in Federated Learning
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Artificial Intelligence
Abstract Note: Federated learning (FL) provides a privacy-preserving framework for distributed model training across decentralized participating clients (PCs). However, its performance is significantly hindered by data heterogeneity, where non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data across PCs induce client drift, compromise model generalization, and may even impede convergence. Although various optimization schemes have been proposed to alleviate these issues, they still suffer from slow convergence and insufficient generalization. In this article, we propose FedWeight, a novel density-aware adaptive weight optimization in FL that effectively mitigates data heterogeneity without relying on auxiliary data or historical parameters. Specifically, FedWeight allows each client to dynamically and adaptively adjust the loss function weights based on class-wise density derived from kernel density estimation. By assigning larger weights to sparse classes, FedWeight balances learning across sparse and dense classes, thereby accelerating convergence and improving generalization under non-IID settings. Finally, theoretical analysis and extensive experimental results demonstrate that FedWeight achieves more accurate models and significantly faster convergence, improving the performance of integrated baseline approaches.

Author: Swapna, A.; Deepa, K.
Title: Federated AI Framework for Distributed Smart Healthcare at the Edge

The proposed system effectively trains models on each data at the edge nodes, where patient data stays local to meet the most important privacy requirements and comply with HIPAA and GDPR regulations. Author: Swain, S. R.; Parashar, A.; Saxena, D.; Singh, A. Kumar; Lee, C.-N.
Title: A Global Cyber Threat Resilient Cloud Collaboration Framework for Geographically Distributed Data Centers
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Services Computing
Abstract Note: The rapid growth of geographically distributed cloud data centers has intensified the demand for secure, privacy-preserving, and resource-efficient collaboration among mutually untrusted cloud environments. This paper presents BlockFed, a blockchain-empowered federated learning framework designed to enable cyber-threat-resilient collaboration across geographically distributed data centers. In BlockFed, each data center independently trains local models using private workload data and shares only the computed gradients rather than raw data, with a centralized aggregation server through a secure blockchain layer. A Proof-of-Work consensus mechanism is employed to validate gradient transactions and maintain an immutable, tamper-resistant ledger, ensuring trust and integrity among participating entities. The centralized server aggregates blockchain-verified updates to construct a global model, which is iteratively redistributed to support collaborative learning. This integrated learning process enhances task-level resource demand prediction while simultaneously improving system security and operational efficiency across all participating data centers. Extensive simulations on the Google Cluster Dataset show that BlockFed outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, including ISTM, ETP-WE, First-Fit, Best-Fit, and Random-Fit, in resource utilization, power consumption, and active server reduction. BlockFed achieves up to 7-81% higher resource utilization, 41-58% lower power consumption, and 31-65% fewer active servers, while attaining a cyber-threat estimation accuracy of 93.19%.

Author: Khan, A.; Junaid, A.; Iqbal, A.; Husnain, G.
Title: Federated Cloud Intelligence: A Privacy-Preserving, Trustworthy and Sustainable Framework for Multi-Cloud AI
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE 5th International Conference on Computing and Machine Intelligence (ICMI)
Abstract Note: This study proposes a Federated Cloud Intelligence for Privacy-Preserving AI, with new layered framework that can support secure and eco friendly learning across different cloud providers. Instead of centralizing data, our method trains models locally on varied client datasets and combines their updates using federated learning (FL) to stay compliant with data protection rules. The experiment have shown that the federated setup reached an average accuracy of 0.844 over five communication rounds, just slightly lower than the centralized baseline of 0.850. Meanwhile, the loss decreased from 0.367 to 0.285, coming close to the centralized value of 0.318. To build trust, a blockchain-based layer that permanently stored updates with little extra cost, adding blocks each round with an average consensus delay of 0.189 seconds. Tests showed that this consensus process reduced the impact of malicious client attacks, keeping accuracy stable around 0.827. Further it is then incorporated with zero-knowledge proofs (ZKM), where adds only 0.196 seconds of latency and 260–360 MB GPU memory overhead and showcases an accuracy up to 0.844. A reinforcement learning agent optimized workload scheduling by shifting the computation from AWS to GCP, reducing carbon scores by 20% with minimal accuracy trade-off. Finally, explainability analysis revealed balanced provider contributions from 0.021 to 0.023 and highlighted key features such as logPurchases and storePurchases.

Author: Kappannavar, G.; G, N. D.; Kachavimath, A.; Shettar, P.; Hiremath, P. S.
Title: Game-Theoretic Proof of Useful Work for Fair Miner Selection and Reputation Management in Federated Blockchains
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Intelligent and Sustainable Electronics & Computing Technologies (INSECT)
Abstract Note: Traditional Proof of Work (PoW) consensus protocols in blockchain networks have been criticized for being highly energy-intensive, less scalable, and prone to fairness issues that favor the computations of more powerful miners. To address the aforementioned challenges, we have proposed the development of the Game-Theoretic Proof of Useful Work (GT-PoUW) consensus protocol, which combines the concepts of Federated Learning (FL) with dynamic incentive-revision systems. In this proposed system, every node maintains the capability to train an individual machine learning model, while the selection process for the miners would be based on the accuracy across different models, rather than hash power. This would enable the utilization of the computational power for productive work. To this end, a gametheoretical approach is used for controlling miner classification, update performance, and the dynamic downgrade process in order to effectively prevent malicious miners and encourage honest ones. Experiments reveal that GT-PoUW effectively promotes fairness, which improves Jain's Fairness Index values from 0.7196 in the case of PoW to 0.9537 in the case of PoUW, besides eliminating miner centralization by making the block delivery irrelevant to hashing power. Additionally, an energy-effective and honest plus federated learning approach for GT-PoUW helps boost the current state of blockchain security and fairness.

Author: Saeed, H.; Duchesne, M.; Zhang, K.
Title: DP-Shapley: Deterministic, Gas-Bounded Shapley Settlement for on-Chain Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Decentralized Applications and Infrastructures (DAPPS)
Abstract Note: Federated learning enables collaborative model training without centralizing raw data, but fair reward settlement becomes difficult when incentives are enforced on a public blockchain. In this setting, contribution accounting must be auditable, deterministic across validators, and efficient enough to operate within smart-contract gas limits. Exact Shapley value computation is intractable, stochastic approximations are poorly suited to consensus-safe settlement, and off-chain evaluation can introduce attribution bias and confidentiality risks. We present DP-Shapley (Deterministic-Practical Shapley), a decentralized framework for blockchain-assisted federated learning that combines Trusted Execution Environment (TEE)-backed confidential aggregation, a commit-test-reveal protocol for controlled disclosure, and a deterministic fixed-budget weighted Shapley settlement rule that employs a sampling mechanism to bypass exhaustive evaluation, all derived from public round state. We implemented and compared five consensus-safe estimation strategies under deployment-oriented smart-contract budgets. Our results show that once full coalition traversal is no longer feasible, stratified sampling without replacement is the most reliable approximation strategy, achieving the highest overall approximation quality and ranking preservation. These findings demonstrate that practical on-chain contribution accounting depends less on maximizing coalition coverage than on placing a deterministic budget on informative coalition sizes while avoiding redundant evaluations.

Author: G, P.; Srikanth, G. U.; S, P.; M, S.; Valarmathi, K.
Title: A Comprehensive Python-Based Framework for Secure Monitoring and Detection of Fraudulent Bitcoin Transactions Across Blockchain-Driven Cryptocurrency Ecosystems

Detecting fraudulent Bitcoin transactions is therefore vital to maintaining the integrity and trust of digital financial systems. Each algorithm's performance is measured using metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and the confusion matrix. Comparative evaluation reveals that the Random Forest model delivers the highest accuracy and reliability. Additionally, the system supports real-time transaction input and visual analytics, providing instant fraud detection results. This approach strengthens Bitcoin transaction security and demonstrates the potential of machine learning in mitigating fraud within decentralized cryptocurrency ecosystems.

Author: Ghazi, S. S.
Title: Fed-TTC: A Pareto-Efficient Hierarchical Federated Learning Framework
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Data Engineering Workshops (ICDEW)
Abstract Note: Federated learning (FL) has emerged as a transformative paradigm for privacy-preserving collaborative machine learning, yet scaling to millions of clients reveals critical bottlenecks in single-server architectures. Multi-server FL addresses these scalability challenges through distributed aggregation, but existing hierarchical FL (HFL) frameworks suffer from inefficient client-server assignment mechanisms that prioritize stability while neglecting Pareto-efficiency (PE) and strategy-proofness (SP). This work fundamentally reformulates the client-server assignment problem through the lens of market design, drawing an analogy to the school choice problem where clients and servers are agents with preferences and priorities. We introduce a novel framework that applies the Top Trading Cycle (TTC) algorithm to HFL, guaranteeing both PE and SP while achieving minimal instability. Our approach integrates a heuristic-based Shapley value method using the One-Round (OR) approximation to fairly quantify client contributions, enabling servers to form priority rankings that reflect actual utility. To eliminate centralization concerns inherent in traditional HFL architectures, we implement the first blockchain-based deployment of key matching mechanisms, such as TTC, Deferred Acceptance (DA), and Immediate Acceptance with Skip (IAS) as the smart contracts, demonstrating the feasibility of trustless client selection. Preliminary results on CIFAR-10 show that TTC combined with OR-based contribution assessment outperforms baseline assignment strategies including DA, IAS, and the MAAIM frameworks in final model accuracy. This doctoral research further proposes investigations into dynamic TTC mechanisms and their integration with Fed-Prox aggregation in flat multi-server architectures, addressing the statistical heterogeneity challenges of decentralized, non-IID environments while maintaining the theoretical guarantees of SP matching.

Author: Qwayede, O.; Kabaso, B.; Hendricks, W.
Title: Cybersecurity Vulnerabilities and Security Approaches in Weather Station Networks: A Systematic Literature Review
Publication Title: 2026 6th International Conference on Smart Sensors and Applications (ICSSA)
Abstract Note: Weather station networks are widely used in disaster management, climate monitoring, agriculture, public health, and smart cities. These systems remain vulnerable because many rely on insecure communication channels, unattended remote devices, and resource-constrained IoT hardware. Unlike prior reviews that address IoT or wireless sensor network (WSN) security broadly, this review is the first to systematically map vulnerabilities, mitigations, and evidence maturity specifically for weather station and environmental monitoring networks. It synthesizes 28 peer-reviewed studies (2021-2026) from Google Scholar, IEEE Xplore, SpringerLink, and Scopus. For Google Scholar, only the top 450 relevance-ranked results were screened, using the same structured search string as the retrieval query. Key vulnerabilities found include insecure wireless communication (71%), weak authentication (64%), and inadequate encryption (57%). Proposed mitigations cover lightweight cryptography, intrusion detection, machine learning anomaly detection, and blockchain validation. Evidence maturity was classified as strong in 39% of studies, moderate in 50%, and weak in 11%. Major gaps are clear: 68% of studies had no dedicated security framework and 54% lacked real-world attack testing. The review critically compares the reviewed security approaches, maps dominant vulnerabilities, and derives priority research areas, ranked by practical significance, for future weather-station cybersecurity frameworks.

Author: Kaur, R.; Vashisth, A.; Kaur, G.
Title: Securing the Skies: A Systematic Review of Authentication, Access Control, and Threat Detection in UAV Networks
Publication Title: 2026 7th International Conference on Electronics and Sustainable Communication Systems (ICESC)
Abstract Note: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) have become essential infrastructures in the fields of surveillance, disaster management, precision farming, and military services. Nevertheless, their mass implementation has disclosed notable cybersecurity dangers because of unguarded wireless communication pathways, evolving network architecture, and resource-limited operation settings. This review article determines the existing security frameworks on UAV networks in three basic fields of security protocols: authentication procedures, accessibility models, and intrusion detection systems. We study types of lightweight cryptography systems that utilize elliptic curve cryptography and physical unclonable functions, compare access control systems within role-based and attribute-based models, and show machine-learning-based intrusion detection methods. We have found out that cyber-physical fusion techniques have a 96 percent success rate at detection, over 65 percent on conventional signature-based methods, and blockchain-based authentication has 60 percent fewer computing costs than conventional PKI systems. The main research gaps that need filling are associated with the lack of real-time validation of suggested solutions, inadequate implementation of post-quantum cryptographic solutions, and the lack of experimental frameworks. The discussion highlights the importance of lightweight, dynamic security protocols that balance compute-intensiveness and strong security measures against advanced attack vectors. Furthermore, this review points out that urgently needed measures are standardized benchmarking environments that will enable comparisons of UAV security solutions offered in different studies on a level playing field. The wide range of uses of UAVs, such as single operator systems by hobbyists and swarms of large-capacity autonomous computers, demands tiered security systems capable of adapting to varying conditions of operation. There are new threat environments, including adversarial machine learning vulnerabilities, and the insecurity of supply-chain embedded software, which are not well represented in the current frameworks. Future research efforts should then be directed towards cross-layer security integration between crypto, network and application-level security that interacts with each other in a manner of a resource constrained UAV environment, which is energy efficient and optimized.

Author: Zhou, Y.; Pang, X.; Wang, Z.; Hu, J.; Jin, S.; Ren, K.
Title: AFLoRA: Adaptive LoRA for Resource-Efficient Federated Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing
Abstract Note: LoRA-based federated fine-tuning allows clients to fine-tune LoRA adapters locally and aggregates updates on the server, thereby enabling the efficient adaptation of global foundation models to distributed, domain-specific data. However, existing methods assume identical and static LoRA adapters across clients, which not only limits the utilization of heterogeneous resources and adaptation to diverse data distributions, but also prevents dynamic adjustment to clients’ evolving local fine-tuning state. They also struggle to achieve precise and lightweight aggregation of LoRA matrices, hindering learning performance in resource-constrained environments. To address these issues, we propose AFLoRA, an adaptive LoRA-based resource-efficient federated fine-tuning framework. For effectively adapting to Non-IID local data while minimizing resource consumption, AFLoRA introduces diagonal-based dynamic rank assignment, which dynamically adjusts local LoRA ranks based on client resources and local adaptation state guided by a learnable diagonal matrix. It further decouples LoRA matrices updates between clients and the server to reduce overhead, and develops a zero-padding-based rank-aware aggregation mechanism to accurately integrate heterogeneous updates through lossless matrix expansion and rank-aware weighting. These mechanisms enable AFLoRA to balance resource efficiency and fine-tuning performance effectively. Extensive experiments demonstrate that AFLoRA outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both LLM adaptation performance and fine-tuning efficiency in heterogeneous environments.
Manual Tags: Collaborative learning; heterogeneity

The term Chain reflects the consortium blockchain backbone that guarantees immutable provenance, decentralized ownership management, and copyright revocation, while Visage symbolizes the unique visual identity of multimedia content achieved through dual-stage visual hash embedding. The proposed framework integrates Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs) for privacy-preserving ownership verification and employs optimized smart contracts to manage visual rights, provenance records, and ownership transfers efficiently. Evaluations on a large-scale dataset of over 10,000 real-world images and 3,850 video clips from diverse CIoT devices demonstrate Chain-Visage’s superior performance, achieving 97.5% traceability accuracy, 93% tamper detection sensitivity, and low verification latency even under resource-constrained environments. Author: Huang, X.; He, J.; Liang, C.; Zhou, M.; Chen, Q.
Title: Dual-Layer Blockchain-Enabled Federated Reinforcement Learning for Personalized Autonomous Driving
Publication Title: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
Abstract Note: Deep reinforcement learning (RL) has demonstrated outstanding performance in autonomous driving (AD). However, independent single-vehicle training struggles to cope with complex traffic environments, while collaborative training across multiple vehicles causes a security risk in data sharing. The proposed DBFRL algorithm constructs a federated RL (FRL) architecture based on a dual-layer blockchain to ensure data security during training. Author: Soni, J. A.; Anand, A.; Pandey, R. K.
Title: Explainable AI for Expert Knowledge Transfer Systems in Big Data Environments

Abstract Note: Transferring expert knowledge from models operating on big data requires explanations that survive scale. This is usually treated as three separate problems: distributing attribution over large batch datasets, producing it fast enough for streaming inference, and producing it without centralizing data across organizations. This paper presents a unified framework addressing all three under one architecture, in which explanation fidelity is measured against a common centralized reference rather than assumed. Evaluation is two-pronged: large-scale simulation for scalability, and validation on three public benchmarks—MIMIC-III, IEEE-CIS Fraud Detection, and NASA CMAPSS—for explanation quality on public real-world datasets. In simulation, the architecture sustains an explanation fidelity score of 0.78 at 10TB scale with sub-second streaming response times; on the public benchmarks it achieves 0.84–0.88. Author: Sarwar, A.; Zhai, Y.; Shen, J.; Manjang, O.; Yanglin, L.; Zhu, L.
Title: Decoupled Edge Data Integrity Verification via Federated Adaptation and Cryptographic Validation
Publication Title: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
Abstract Note: Mobile edge computing (MEC) accelerates Internet of Things (IoT) applications by caching content near end users. However, cached data remains vulnerable to corruption, misleading applications, and eroding user trust. Traditional centralized edge data integrity verification (EDIV) methods adopt challenge-response protocols involving third-party auditors (TPAs), incurring nontrivial computation and communication costs along with privacy concerns. Recent decentralized frameworks leverage federated learning (FL) to train models for initial screening, eliminating TPAs. However, their performance is impeded by computational and data heterogeneity across edge nodes and the substantial overhead of blockchain-based validation. Furthermore, such frameworks exhibit limited precision in localizing corrupted data. To address these challenges, this article introduces the decoupled EDIV (D-EDIV) framework, which explicitly decouples integrity verification into a two-stage mechanism of corruption detection and corruption localization. During Stage 1, D-EDIV executes corruption detection models at edge nodes. A federated adaptation scheme tailors these models to each node’s computational resources and local data distribution. Upon detecting anomalous instances, a fusion strategy correlates network-layer alerts with cached data modification events to generate perblock suspicion scores, prompting the application vendor (AV) to trigger Stage 2. In this stage, the AV conducts targeted localization on potentially corrupted data. In particular, after authenticating data commitments via a digital signature, the AV utilizes suspicion scores to calculate dynamic decision thresholds, guiding Merkle tree traversal and restricting cryptographic validation to high-risk data blocks. Experimental results demonstrate that D-EDIV improves detection accuracy by 3%–12% and reduces computational overhead by \3\textbackslash{}times \ – \8\textbackslash{}times \ , efficiently achieving fine-grained integrity verification in heterogeneous MEC environments.

Author: Ijaz, A.; Khan, M. A.; Ali, H.; Ullah, F.
Title: Q-Learning-Enhanced GANs for Secure 5G Access Control: Integrating Adaptive Policy Enforcement and Cryptographic Authorization
Publication Title: 2026 3rd International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Information Systems (EEISS)
Abstract Note: The fifth-generation (5 G) mobile network has been introduced on an international scale and has transformed the concept of wireless communication by providing ultra-high data rates, close to zero latency, and seamless connectivity. Nevertheless, its distributed architecture, network slicing, and software-defined settings present new levels of security vulnerability. The current paper suggests a new framework that combines both artificial intelligence (AI) and advanced cryptography schemes to enhance the security of 5 G networks. The core of this strategy is the combination of Q-Learning and Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), as Q-Learning is used to dynamically optimize the resource distribution and reduce computational and energy consumption constraints on GANs and other deep neural networks, including autoencoders. This integration improves the ability to respond to emerging attack patterns and detect threats in real time. We also compare the most popular cryptographic methods, post-quantum cryptography, homomorphic encryption, and blockchain-based authentication, with their effectiveness in preventing unauthorized access and data breaches while maintaining 5 G operational performance. These approaches have serious limitations, despite their promise, such as adversarial attack threats, which undermine AI processing of large-scale blockchain data, and the massive computational cost of quantumresistant algorithms. Our results indicate the importance of further improvement of hybrid AI models, such as the QLearning GAN. Smart AI algorithms combined with strong cryptographic techniques will enable 5 G networks in the future to be resilient, scalable, secure, and reliable global communication.

Author: Zadeh, F. A.; Zeydan, E.; Wang, S.; Liyanage, M.
Title: An Integrated Trustworthiness Framework for Generative AI in 6G Edge Networks
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Future and Intelligent Networking (FINE)
Abstract Note: The integration of Generative AI (GenAI) and Large Foundation Models (LFMs) into 6G networks promises a paradigm shift from data transmission to semantic communication. However, deploying these stochastic models in missioncritical network slices is hindered by their inherent “fragility”, particularly the risks of hallucinations, lack of operational awareness, and opacity in decision-making. In this paper, we analyze key methodological limitations in existing approaches and identify gaps related to lifecycle trust, decentralized learning, and regulatory compliance. Building on this analysis, we propose a five-layer Integrated Trustworthiness Framework for the 6G edge that combines provenance-aware data management, adaptive and hybrid learning, continuous robustness monitoring, explainability for both humans and machines, and embedded governance with human-in-the-loop oversight. Unlike traditional approaches that address robustness and explainability separately, our architecture unifies them to optimize network performance. The novelty of this work is threefold: (i) the formalization of M2M Explainability as a quantifiable network engineering primitive, with a derived Explanation Compression Ratio (ECR) that translates transparency into measurable bandwidth savings; (ii) a provenance-aware federated learning architecture in which blockchain audit trails are structurally coupled to OOD detection, enabling cryptographically traceable fallback decisions; and (iii) a unified five-layer architecture where robustness, explainability, and governance are co-designed interdependencies rather than post-hoc additions, validated through a multidimensional KPI suite purpose-built for 6G trust evaluation.

Author: Navya, N.; Doddi, N.; Borra, T.; Yalla, C.; Chindada, J.; Rajesh, J. T.
Title: An Enhanced Choke Algorithm Framework for Intelligent and Secure Peer-to-Peer Resource Optimization
Publication Title: 2026 6th International Conference on Ubiquitous Computing and Intelligent Information Systems (ICUIS)
Abstract Note: Peer-to-peer (P2P) networks are used for decentralized resource sharing and distributed communication, they have always been plagued with problems with adaptive peer selection, heterogeneous network conditions, communication overhead and unreliable peer behaviour. Conventional choke-unchoke mechanisms are based on peer contribution and availability of bandwidth, and are not effective in securing, fairly allocating and allocating resources effectively in dynamic environments. This paper suggests an Enhanced Choke Algorithm (ECA) framework that combines adaptive peer prioritization, peer evaluation based on trust information, dynamic choke-unchoke decision making and multi-objective resource optimization. The bandwidth availability, communication latency, historical peer contribution, trust level, and resource demand are taken into account as a joint factor in the framework to dynamically rank peers, and allocate network resources. Experimental Evaluation involves a comparison of the proposed ECA with Conventional Choke Algorithm, Greedy Peering and Random Peer Selection with respect to various parameters such as throughput, latency, Packet delivery ratio, resource utilization, communication overhead, and fairness index. Throughput of the ECA is 89.7 Mbps, the latency is 31.6ms, the packet delivery ratio is 99.2%, the resource utilization is 95.8%, the communication overhead is 8.6% and the fairness index is 0.98. It also guarantees throughput of more than 85 Mbps and latency of less than 35 ms in the network scales between 100 peers and 1000 peers. The results show that the proposed framework has a better resource efficiency, reliable communication, fair and scalable, which can be used as a robust framework for intelligent and secure resource optimization in the future decentralized P2P systems.

Author: Ullah, F.; Asmat, H.; Khan, A. A.; Mohmand, M. I.; Ali, F.; Alsisi, R. H.; Aldhyani, T. H. H.; Kwak, D.

Author: Li, J.; Yang, Y.; Yang, J.; Chen, Z.
Title: SEVER: Secure and Efficient Verifiable Credential Expiration and Revocation for Decentralized Crowdsourcing Identity

Abstract Note: Decentralized crowdsourcing mitigates risks inherent in centralized platforms, but managing user identity, particularly the revocation of Verifiable Credentials (VCs), remains a significant challenge. SEVER utilizes Incremental Multiset Hashing (IMH) to aggregate all user VCs into a single, compact on-chain hash. This construction enables efficient generation of non-revocation proofs for individual VCs, ensuring that the revocation of one credential does not affect others associated with the same DID. Title: FedShard-DES: Federated Multi-Objective Sharded Blockchain for Real-Time Secure Smart Home Consumer Electronics

Abstract Note: Smart-home consumer electronics (CE) sharded blockchains face a configuration dilemma: node-resource information is scattered across home gateways, while shard configuration requires global coordination. Centralized optimization exposes local resource states, making it difficult to balance real-time performance and security-related risk exposure. To address this problem, this paper proposes FedShard-DES, a FedPareto-driven double-elite-selection framework for federated multi-objective optimization of sharded blockchain configuration. The proposed model jointly optimizes shard failure probability, transaction throughput, decentralization entropy, and consensus latency. In FedShard-DES, each CE client locally performs double-elite-selection evolutionary search and uploads only its Pareto archive instead of raw node-resource data. The coordinator aggregates local archives through non-dominated sorting, Minkowski-distance-based truncation, and feedback of representative Pareto solutions to support distributed Pareto optimization. Experiments on the smart-home sharded blockchain model and WFG benchmark suites show that FedShard-DES obtains a favorable security-oriented trade-off compared with centralized and federated baselines. This survey breaks down the most significant papers in the field by sorting them into nine distinct tactical baskets: old-school deep learning hybrids, macro-scale multi-crop frameworks, spatial graph networks, vision transformers, remote-sensing models mixed with plant physics, drone-scale imaging, breeding models that look at genetics, federated learning setups, and explainable AI (XAI). Title: A Multi-Point Collaborative Defense Method Against Unknown Attacks for Industrial Cyber-Physical Systems

Abstract Note: As industrial cyber-physical systems (CPS) become increasingly interconnected and attack methods diversify, industrial equipment remains vulnerable to unknown attacks, potentially causing severe consequences. Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) naturally fits intelligent consumer electronics through its privacy-preserving distributed training. Author: Behra, N.; Jumah, K.; Gopinath, V.; Nijhawan, G.; Padole, G.; B, S. P.
Title: Hybrid ML Ensemble for E-Commerce Fraud Governance, Trust Scoring, and Transaction Reliability Management

Abstract Note: E-commerce platforms have also grown, which results in increased advanced online fraud, and therefore, effective and real-time fraud detection is crucial. Author: Tian, L.; Lin, F.; Qin, Z.; Qi, J.; Li, M.; Ren, K.
Title: Practical Federated Unlearning: A Target Client-Driven Approach to Model Forgetting
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security
Abstract Note: To remove the contribution of specific data from the global model in federated learning, federated unlearning has recently emerged. Existing approaches face challenges such as reliance on full client participation, the need to store historical model updates, and high communication costs. To overcome these limitations, we propose Practical Federated Unlearning (PFU), a target client-driven approach to model forgetting with only a single round of interaction between the target client and the aggregation server during the unlearning stage. To fulfill PFU, the aggregation server utilizes the Fisher Information Matrix to identify the most sensitive parameters with respect to the target client’s data and sends their indices to the target client. Then, the target client estimates its contribution to the sensitive parameters using a Bayesian inference-based method, thus avoiding the requirement for data or historical model updates from all other clients. Finally, it prunes the sensitive parameters with a tailored mechanism, which achieves effective unlearning of the data knowledge while preventing catastrophic forgetting. Theoretical analysis under explicit regularity assumptions and experimental results confirm the effectiveness and practical advantages of PFU.
