Author: Zeng, W.; Xu, X.; Zhang, Q.; Shi, J.; Guan, Z.; Li, S.; Qin, Z.
Title: A Secure and Efficient Distributed Semantic Communication System for Heterogeneous Internet of Things
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing
Abstract Note: Semantic communications are expected to improve the transmission efficiency in Internet of Things (IoT) networks. However, the distributed nature of networks and heterogeneity of devices challenge the secure utilization of semantic communication systems. In this paper, we develop a distributed semantic communication system that achieves the security and efficiency during update and usage phases. A blockchain-based trust scheme for update is designed to continuously train and synchronize the system in dynamic IoT environments. To improve the updating efficiency, we propose a flexible semantic coding method base on compressive semantic knowledge bases. It greatly reduces the amount of data shared among devices for system update, and realizes the flexible adjustment of the size of knowledge bases and the number of transmitted signal symbols in model training and inference stages. In the usage phase, a signature mechanism for lossy semantics is introduced to guarantee the integrity and authenticity of the transmitted semantics in lossy semantic communications. We further design a noise-aware differential privacy mechanism, which introduces optimized noise based on the different channel information available to heterogeneous devices. Experiments on transmission tasks show that the proposed system defends against cross-phase attacks of compromising semantics integrity and reduces the data to be shared in the update phase by about 36% to 90%, and in the usage phase by 60% compared with related works.

Author: Zhang, H.; Xu, F.; Yu, Z.; Pang, S.; Hu, C.; Yu, J.
Title: DFPL: Decentralized Federated Prototype Learning Across Heterogeneous Data Distributions
Publication Title: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
Abstract Note: Federated learning (FL) is a distributed machine learning paradigm through centralized model aggregation. However, standard FL relies on a centralized server, making it vulnerable to server failures. While existing solutions utilize blockchain technology to implement decentralized FL (DFL), the statistical heterogeneity of data distributions among clients severely degrades the performance of DFL. Driven by this issue, this article proposes a decentralized federated prototype learning framework (DFPL), which significantly improves the performance of DFL under heterogeneous data distributions. Specifically, DFPL introduces prototype learning into DFL to mitigate the impact of statistical heterogeneity and reduces the number of parameters exchanged between clients. In addition, blockchain is embedded into our framework, enabling the training and mining processes to be executed locally on each client. From a theoretical perspective, we analyze the convergence of DFPL by modeling the required computational resources during both training and mining. The experiment results highlight the superiority of DFPL in both model performance and communication efficiency across four benchmark datasets with heterogeneous data distributions.

Author: Chen, J.; Li, D.; Wang, P.; Liu, P.; Zhang, M.; Xian, Y.
Title: A Game Theory Dynamic Incentive Optimization Model for Decentralized Federated Learning
Publication Title: 2026 29th International Conference on Computer Supported Cooperative Work in Design (CSCWD)
Abstract Note: Federated Learning (FL) faces critical adoption barriers due to inherent centralized trust dependency and the lack of effective participant incentives. To resolve this dual challenge, we propose an innovative framework that integrates Blockchain technology with Game Theory. Blockchain establishes a decentralized and transparent infrastructure. Built upon this foundation, we utilize a Stackelberg Game model to create a dynamic incentive mechanism. The model’s utility function evaluates user contribution based on data quality and a comprehensive computation cost, including model training and Blockchain consensus overhead. This strategic interaction is formulated as a two-stage optimization problem, efficiently solved via Convex Optimization and Backward Induction. Simulation results confirm that our integrated scheme significantly enhances participant utility and resource allocation efficiency, providing a robust foundation for economically viable FL ecosystems.

Author: Xu, D.; Lu, C.; Li, C.; Zhang, C.; Tang, Y.; Zhu, L.
Title: Communication-Efficient Federated Swarm Learning for SAG-CM on Heterogeneous Data
Publication Title: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing
Abstract Note: Federated learning (FL) enables multiple clients to collaboratively train models without sharing private data, but it often struggles under non-IID distributions and tight edge budgets—particularly in systems, such as space–air–ground collaborative monitoring (SAG-CM), where satellite, aerial, and ground sensors generate heterogeneous, large-scale data across constrained networks. Inspired by the biological intelligence of gregarious organisms, we propose multistrategy grey wolf optimization—federated swarm learning (MSGWO-FSL), a novel edge-learning framework for SAG-CM/federated systems. Our design integrates artificial intelligence-enabled stochastic gradient descent with bioinspired multistrategy grey wolf optimization: each client maintains a local (\textbackslash{}alpha,\textbackslash{}beta,\textbackslash{}delta\) leader-set to explore both weights and sparsity, and uploads only the binary mask of the \textbackslash{}alpha\ model. The server aggregates the masks to preserve personalization by consolidating common structure while retaining client-specific sparsity, yielding sparse, faster on-device models with reduced communication overhead. Our convergence analysis theoretically demonstrates that MSGWO-FSL outperforms standard FL under mild conditions, and we derive a model-divergence upper bound that guides stable step-size choices under non-IID data. Extensive experiments on five public benchmarks and two public remote-sensing benchmarks demonstrate MSGWO-FSL surpasses nine state-of-the-art baselines in average accuracy while maintaining communication and computation efficiency.

Author: Ibrahim, H.; Ahakonye, L. A. C.; Lee, J. M.; Kim, D.-S.

Author: Abdalla, A.; Harrye, Y.; Ali, H.; Lari, A.

Abstract Note: Integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into critical infrastructures introduces unique vulnerabilities exploitable through sophisticated attacks. Infrastructure weaknesses in complex deployments are also assessed. The paper explores defensive strategies such as advanced encryption, adaptive self-learning systems, and robust authentication. Sector-specific applications in energy and finance illustrate practical considerations. Ethical and legal dimensions, including privacy regulations, are discussed to ensure compliance and trust. Finally, emerging research directions like AIblockchain integration and generative AI for initiative-taking defense are proposed. This synthesis aims to inform efforts to secure AI-enabled systems against evolving threats while balancing operational effectiveness with ethical obligations.

Author: Kishore, K. V.; Gorintla, S.; Davuluri, S.
Title: Federated Graph Neural Network Framework with Blockchain-Enabled Smart Contracts and Adaptive Energy Demand Forecasting in Electric Vehicle Smart Grids

Abstract Note: The fast-growing electric-vehicle (EV) charging loads require smart and privacy-preserving prediction mechanisms to support efficient grid management. Author: Fan, W.; Deng, X.; Chen, Z.; Zhao, M.; Wu, G.; Qiu, K.; Hu, Y.
Title: DIM-NEG: Dynamic Incentive Model for Federated Learning Based on Smart Contracts and Nested Evolutionary Games
Publication Title: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
Abstract Note: The effectiveness of federated learning (FL) systems relies on extensive client participation. However, the existing incentive mechanisms often overlook the intrinsic coupling between participation and privacy strategies. This oversight leads to mismatches between incentive distributions and clients’ privacy costs and contribution quality, limiting the effectiveness of incentives for enhancing contribution quality and participation scale. To address this, DIM-NEG, a dynamic incentive model based on smart contracts and nested evolutionary games, is proposed. First, we construct a nested evolutionary game framework linking external participation with internal privacy strategies. By utilizing the internal equilibrium payoff as a feedback parameter for the external game, we achieve unified modeling of these coupled decision processes. Second, on the basis of this structure, a functionally decoupled dual-incentive lever mechanism is proposed. The server employs the strategy incentive to guide the internal strategy portfolio and the participation incentive to regulate the participation scale, enabling separate optimization of the strategy composition and overall participation level of the system via hierarchical control. Finally, utilizing blockchain-based smart contracts, we design an automated mechanism that encodes rules on-chain to resolve trust issues associated with centralized servers. A theoretical analysis and simulation results demonstrate that the DIM-NEG model achieves superior global accuracy, training efficiency, and communication cost-effectiveness while exhibiting strong robustness in non-IID environments. The model adequately motivates users to participate in high-quality data sharing tasks and maintains system stability, thereby maximizing the overall effectiveness of the FL system.
Manual Tags: federated learning (FL); smart contracts; Differential privacy (DP); dynamic incentive; evolutionary game theory (EGT)

Author: Feng, H.; Gadekallu, T. R.; Xia, Y.; Zhao, Y.; Wen, Z.; Cai, J.; Bhattacharya, P.; Fang, K.; Liyanage, M.
Title: Agentic AI Security in 6G Networks: A Survey of Emerging Attack Vectors, Vulnerabilities, and Defenses
Publication Title: IEEE Open Journal of the Communications Society
Abstract Note: The emergence of autonomous, goal-driven artificial intelligence (AI) agents as core components of future sixth-generation (6G) networks fundamentally reshapes the network security landscape. Unlike earlier AI-assisted systems, these agents operate with a high degree of autonomy, enabling adaptive decision-making that current security models are not designed to handle. In this survey, we examine how agentic AI in 6G can be exploited by attackers and, conversely, how these AI systems themselves become vulnerable. We discuss how malicious actors can leverage autonomous agents to conduct intelligent, evolving attacks across the radio access network, network control functions, and digital twin environments, while also showing how the agents’ own capabilities for reasoning, memory, and tool use introduce new vulnerabilities to poisoning, hijacking, and manipulation. By integrating these two perspectives, we assess emerging defense strategies, identify gaps in existing standards and governance, and outline key research directions toward building trustworthy, AI-native 6G networks. Our goal is to lay a practical groundwork for securing future intelligent networks.

Author: Jain, V.; Verma, P.; Kumar, M.; Kaushik, A.
Title: Blockchain-Enabled Incentive Mechanism for Federated Learning: A Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient Approach
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
Abstract Note: The expeditious growth of the Internet of Things (IoT) generates massive data, which allows advanced machine learning. However, the traditional approach of centralized model training raises the issue of high bandwidth consumption and privacy. Federated learning (FL) mitigates this by enabling local training on raw data with centralized aggregation to generate the global model. The effectiveness of FL depends upon the active participation of resource-constrained local devices. This article presents a blockchain-enabled incentive mechanism for FL leveraging the Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MA-DDPG) algorithm. Specifically, an incentive scheme is formulated with the MEC (Mobile Edge Computing) server as the leader agent and local devices as learning agents in a cooperative environment. We formalize a two-stage Stackelberg game to establish a Nash equilibrium, which ensures fair and utility-optimized reward distribution for MEC and devices. A Markov Decision Process (MDP) is utilized to solve the equilibrium with incomplete knowledge, and utilities are optimized using the MA-DDPG algorithm. The proposed model considers data quality and device contribution to obtain optimal reward distribution and participation strategies dynamically. The experimental results show an approximate 38% improvement in MEC utility and approx 17% in device utility, with rapid convergence (approximately 300-500 episodes) at a learning rate of 0.0001.

Author: Zhu, K.; Wei, S.; Wu, X.; Jiao, L.; Dong, J.; Zhang, L.
Title: Scheduling Training-Inference Co-Location in Demand Response for Sustainable Edge AI
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Services Computing
Abstract Note: In the pursuit of data privacy and reduced latency, the adoption of edge intelligence has surged. Meanwhile, the enormous increase in AI has resulted in significant energy consumption. Edge intelligence plays a crucial role in Energy Demand Response (EDR). However, existing edge intelligence falls short of meeting the demands of co-locating training and inference tasks while satisfying EDR. Author: Louati, M. A.; Mansour, S.
Title: Wake-on-Anomaly: A Privacy-Preserving Federated Two-Tier Architecture for Early Poultry Health Warning

Abstract Note: Poultry health problems, from highly pathogenic avian influenza to heat stress and silent equipment faults, are often detected late because current monitoring is reactive, manual, and dependent on producers sharing commercially sensitive data. Farms train a shared model by federated learning using an exact federated normalizer that exchanges only per-feature summary statistics, so no raw telemetry, audio, or video ever leaves a farm. On a literature-calibrated testbed of five heterogeneous farms and a 346-recording real audio dataset, the architecture behaves as designed: the audio stage reaches 0.94 macro-F1, and Tier 2 confirmation keeps the end-to-end false-alarm rate low while retaining most true events. Author: Atmoko, R. A.; Pramono, S. H.; Purnomo, M. F. E.; Mudjirahardjo, P.; Rohmatillah, M.; Avian, C.
Title: FedXChain: Blockchain-Inspired Audit Logging and SHAP-Based Heterogeneity Monitoring for Federated Multi-Task Diabetes Prediction

Abstract Note: Federated learning (FL) can support collaborative modeling without pooling patient records, but statistical heterogeneity, limited auditability, and overstated empirical claims impede clinical translation. Author: Lu, Y.; Fang, Z.; Qiao, P.; Lin, Z.; Yang, J.; Zhang, Y.; Yee, P. L.; Chen, Z.; Luo, J.
Title: Conflict-Aware Federated Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models with Mixture-of-Experts

Abstract Note: The continuous scaling of large language models (LLMs) incurs prohibitive computational costs, making Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) a scalable alternative for efficient fine-tuning via sparse activation. While federated learning (FL) emerges as the paradigm for privacy-preserving collaborative optimization, integrating MoE into FL under data heterogeneity may trigger conflicting expert optimizations. Client-specific data distributions force same-indexed experts to optimize under inconsistent or even conflicting feature-label correlations. This mismatch induces destructive interference during aggregation, thus destabilizing the optimization trajectory and degrading model performance. To address this issue, we propose FC-MoE, a federated conflict-aware framework for MoE fine-tuning. Author: Tahera, M. A.; Rahman, S.; Dass, S.; Ullah, S.; Abouyoussef, M.

In this framework, challenges (1) and (2) are jointly addressed through a unified client-side design that integrates RT-DETR training with a Token Engineering Module (TEM). TEM prunes low-utility tokens, reducing encoder complexity and latency on edge hardware, while aggregated updates mitigate non-IID data heterogeneity across clients. To address challenge (3), BlockSecRT-DETR incorporates a decentralized blockchain-secured update validation mechanism that enables tamper-proof and verifiable authenticated model aggregation without relying on a central server. We evaluated the proposed framework under a missing-class Non-IID partition of the KITTI dataset and conducted a blockchain case study to quantify security overhead. Abstract Note: The Internet of Vehicles (IoV) is rapidly evolving, but it also faces significant security threats, including Denial of Service (DoS) attacks and deceptive behaviors. To address these challenges, we propose a novel scheme that integrates Federated Distillation (FD) with blockchain technology to safeguard the IoV from network attacks. First, the scheme combines Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and FD for intrusion detection, which both preserves the privacy of vehicle users’ data and effectively shares knowledge. Subsequently, a mixed optimization algorithm is designed to address the overall problem comprehensively. Numerical results demonstrate the rapid convergence of the proposed mixed optimization algorithm and its effectiveness in minimizing system latency. Author: Wang, Z.; Hu, B.; López-Benítez, M.; Du, J.; Chu, X.; Yu, F. R.
Title: Energy-Efficient Offloading, Caching, and Resource Allocation for Blockchain-Assisted Low-Altitude Flying Networks: An Integrated Federated Learning and MAPPO Approach

Abstract Note: In 6G low-altitude edge intelligent networks, the proliferation of delay-sensitive Internet of Things (IoT) services exacerbates mutual interference among IoT devices, thereby reducing the efficiency of resource allocation. Based on this framework, we define a system utility cost that incorporates the total service delay (including the transmission, computation, queueing, and fetching delays) and the total energy consumption, and formulate an optimisation problem to minimise the long-term system utility cost. To solve the formulated problem, we propose an FL and multi-agent proximal policy optimisation (MAPPO) integrated offloading decisions, caching strategy, and resource allocation. Simulation results show that our proposed algorithm converges faster and achieves a lower system utility cost than the benchmarks.

Author: Tao, Y.; Yin, W.; Xie, H.; Yao, Y.; Yu, D.; Cheng, X.; Wang, D.; Dressler, F.
Title: One-Shot Federated Model Editing for Device Dynamics at the Edge
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Networking
Abstract Note: Standard federated learning (FL) requires persistent device connectivity across multiple communication rounds, making it unsuitable for dynamic environments such as vehicular networks, where devices frequently join and leave. One-shot FL offers a promising alternative by completing training in a single communication round. However, one-shot FL suffers from model solidification and cannot readily adapt to subsequent client dynamics, including new client contributions and the withdrawal of previous contributions. We therefore consider exact model editing, which removes withdrawn contributions through unlearning or incorporates newly contributed ones through incremental learning without retraining from scratch. We identify that efficient editing fundamentally hinges on learning stability. To this end, we propose F-SOSA, the first stable one-shot FL algorithm that enables rapid and exact model editing. F-SOSA leverages sub-sampling of local models with carefully tuned rate for stable aggregation and performs curvature-aware model fusion to preserve utility. We prove that F-SOSA achieves vanishing training error and reasonably small generalization error bounds. Building on this stability, we further develop two single-round editing algorithms: F-SOSA-U for unlearning and F-SOSA-I for incremental learning. They ensure that the edited model, along with all intermediate algorithmic states, is statistically indistinguishable from retraining while incurring only an expected \O(\textbackslash{}rho)\ fraction of its cost, where \textbackslash{}rho \ quantifies stability. Experiments demonstrate that our approach matches retraining performance while reducing cumulative time and communication overhead by at least 36% and 22%, respectively, under realistic urban mobility simulations.

Author: Shi, Y.; Li, Y.; Li, D.; Wu, M.; Hu, J.; Wang, Z.
Title: Edge-Cloud Collaborative Cache Pollution Detection in Vehicular NDN
Publication Title: 2026 6th International Conference on Computer Science and Blockchain (CCSB)
Abstract Note: Vehicular Named Data Networking is highly vulnerable to Cache Pollution Attacks that induce locality disruption and false-locality, causing severe degradation in cache hit ratios and abrupt increases in end-to-end latency. To overcome the drawbacks of conventional detection schemes, such as detection lag, high false positive rates, and poor resource adaptability, this paper proposes an Edge-Cloud Collaborative adaptive detection framework. At the edge layer, a lightweight Actor-Critic model equipped with a shared encoder combining a 1D Convolutional Neural Network and a Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit is deployed on Roadside Units to achieve real-time attack discrimination and multi-grade decision outputs. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed EC-A2C scheme achieves an AUC of 0.96, a detection accuracy of 92%, and a false positive rate of only 6%. Under attack conditions, the cache hit ratio increases from 36% to 76%, and the proportion of malicious requests drops from 48% to 6%, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art baselines and providing a real-time, highly accurate security solution for in-network caching in vehicular networks.

Author: Zhou, S.; Chen, Y.; Liang, W.; Li, K.; Zomaya, A. Y.
Title: MultiSecDFL: Multi-Metric Filtering-Based Secure Aggregation Method for Decentralized Federated Learning
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Consumer Electronics
Abstract Note: As smart devices become more prevalent, consumer electronics have become mainstream, leading to widespread concerns about data privacy and security. In response to these challenges, decentralized federated learning (DFL) has emerged, allowing work nodes to collaboratively train models in a serverless, peer-to-peer manner, thereby eliminating single points of failure and enhancing the privacy protection of private data. However, the decentralized nature of DFL makes it vulnerable to poisoning attacks, where malicious work nodes can manipulate the system by launching attacks on any arbitrary work node. This security challenge is particularly pronounced in resource-constrained environments of consumer electronics, necessitating innovative security measures to ensure both efficiency and safety. To address this issue, we propose MultiSecDFL, a multi-metric filtering method for secure aggregation aimed at enhancing security within distributed and collaborative learning frameworks. In MultiSecDFL, each work node utilizes its local model as a benchmark to evaluate the models exchanged with neighboring nodes based on three dimensions: the distance, statistical characteristics, and directional sensitivity. This approach effectively excludes Byzantine work nodes from local model aggregation, ensuring both the security and efficiency of the learning process. The experimental results indicate that MultiSecDFL effectively defends against poisoning attacks across various interaction topologies, outperforming baseline methods. Overall, compared to the baselines, our method achieves an average improvement of 7.27% in model accuracy and reduces training time by an average of 24.09%. Notably, the performance is even more significant in scenarios with attacks, demonstrating a solid balance between security and efficiency in our approach.

Author: Mohaidat, T.; Khalil, K.

The surveyed studies are further analyzed in terms of their design patterns, performance benefits, and limitations under heterogeneity, mobility, missing data, and resource constraints. IoT botnets use device diversity and poor authentication systems, outdated software, restricted processing power as well as exposed communication channels to take control of devices which then execute malicious operations including DDoS attacks, data theft, unauthorized system access and malware distribution. Botnet activities have become more complex which makes signature-based intrusion detection systems from traditional security systems unable to detect these threats. Author: Tapwal, R.
Title: Stragglers Reimagined: Explainability-Driven Adaptive Federated Learning for Resource Constrained IoMT System

Abstract Note: In this article, we present FlexiFed, a framework designed to enhance federated learning (FL) by addressing the challenges of device inclusivity and data prioritization. FlexiFed overcomes these issues by enabling stragglers to share simplified outputs, such as predictions and key feature importance scores, instead of full model updates. This reduces their computational and communication burden. The framework integrates explainability techniques to identify and emphasize critical data, ensuring rare and significant contributions are prioritized during training. FlexiFed distinguishes itself from similar frameworks by combining hierarchical aggregation with explainability-driven prioritization, directly addressing the need for fairness and transparency in diverse and resource-constrained environments.

Author: Sathish, C.; Khan, A.; Haldankar, D.; G, N.; L, S.
Title: Threat-Adaptive Post-Quantum Authentication Pipeline for Telemedicine
Publication Title: 2026 13th International Conference on Computing for Sustainable Global Development (INDIACom)
Abstract Note: The increasing adoption of telemedicine has amplified concerns regarding the security of patient data, particularly in the context of remote authentication and the growing threat of advanced cyber and quantum-enabled attacks. This paper proposes TAPQ-Health, a Threat-Adaptive Post-Quantum Authentication Pipeline that dynamically adjusts the strength of authentication and cryptographic hardness in real time based on contextual and behavioral risk. The proposed framework integrates four components a lightweight context-bound zero-knowledge proof authentication mechanism, a federated machine learning-based risk assessment model, threat-triggered escalation to lattice-based post-quantum cryptography with adaptive re-encryption, and decentralized, tamper-evident storage using IPFS. Author: Rajpal, T. S.; Naithani, A.
Title: NeuroCrypt: A Neuro Symbolic AI Ecosystem for Advanced Cryptographic Data Security and Transmission
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Artificial Intelligence
Abstract Note: In response to the critical vulnerabilities exposed by quantum computing and AI-driven cryptanalysis in traditional encryption systems, this article introduces NeuroCrypt—a neuro-symbolic AI framework that synergizes adaptive cryptography, decentralized governance, and postquantum security. NeuroCrypt employs three AI groups: CryptAI (multialgorithm encryption), GenAI (neuro-symbolic algorithm synthesis), and TestAI (adversarial validation), to dynamically generate and deploy quantum-resistant cryptographic techniques. The framework uniquely combines five-layer encryption (randomly ordered classical and AI-generated algorithms, e.g., lattice–chaotic hybrids) with metadata-driven security, where encrypted logic is distributed via Shamir’s secret sharing (SSS) over VPNs, eliminating key-exchange dependencies. The system’s lattice-based encryption (1024-dimensional) and frequent AI-driven updates resist Shor/Grover attacks, validated through simulated quantum oracles achieving \textbackslash{}mathcal{O}(10^{38})\ operations for 256-bit keys. Compliance with GDPR, NIST PQC, and FIPS 140-2 ensures readiness for healthcare, fintech, and government applications. NeuroCrypt’s architecture—backward-compatible with legacy systems and optimized for IoT/cloud ecosystems—sets a precedent for self-evolving security, offering a 15% storage overhead trade-off for metadata-driven keyless decryption. Author: Xu, Z.
Title: A Security-Centric Multi-Objective Modeling Approach for Predicting Vulnerabilities in Decentralized Smart Contracts
Publication Title: 2026 9th International Conference on Inventive Computation Technologies (ICICT)
Abstract Note: Decentralized smart contracts are widely deployed in financial infrastructure and cross-chain systems. However, in real-world scenarios, their high complexity and strong coupling make it difficult for traditional single-objective vulnerability detection methods to comprehensively characterize the real attack surface. Therefore, this paper proposes a Security-Centric Multi-Objective Modeling (SCOM) method, which formalizes vulnerability prediction as a multi-dimensional risk regression and joint optimization problem. The algorithm constructs a unified multi-view representation of abstract syntax trees, control flow graphs, data flow graphs, and program dependency graphs. Simultaneously, it introduces security role embedding and a structure-aware Transformer. This operation enables the collaborative modeling of risks at three layers: semantic implementation, interaction flow, and system architecture. Based on this, a similarity measurement mechanism based on the Siamese structure is designed. This mechanism is used to identify vulnerability pattern migrations across versions, platforms, and languages. Finally, economic behavior embedding and risk propagation constraints are introduced to enhance risk differentiation capabilities in high-value contract scenarios. Experiments were conducted on a complex database, comparing the proposed algorithm with several representative methods, including Slither, Mythril, GPTScan, and COBRA. Results show that SCMOM improves the F1-score by approximately 6.0% and the ROC-AUC by approximately 5.7% compared to the best-performing comparison model in the vulnerability classification task. In the 3D risk regression task, it exhibits lower MAE and RMSE and a higher R2 value. In vulnerability pattern migration detection, both the Top-K hit rate and structural similarity index significantly outperform the baseline model. After introducing economic risk propagation constraints, the misclassification rate of high-fund-dependent path contract pairs decreased from 14.3% to 8.1%, and the migration recall rate increased from 63.5% to 71.2%. Robustness evaluation results on 2,500 semantically preserved perturbation samples show that the proposed algorithm exhibits the lowest performance degradation under semantic perturbation.

Author: Chen, H.; Deng, J.; Wu, X.; Jiang, Z.; Zhang, X.; Chen, X.; Ngai, E. C. H.; Liu, J.
Title: LiFeChain: Lightweight Blockchain for Secure and Efficient Federated Lifelong Learning in IoT
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Networking
Abstract Note: Internet of Things (IoT) devices constantly generate heterogeneous data streams, driving demand for continuous, decentralized intelligence. Federated Lifelong Learning (FLL) provides an ideal solution by incorporating federated learning and lifelong learning. However, the extended lifecycle of FLL in IoT systems increases their vulnerability to persistent attacks. This problem is exacerbated by the single point of failure. Furthermore, the single point of trust created by the central server hinders reliable auditing for long-term threats. Blockchain technology provides a tamper-proof foundation for trustworthy FLL. Nevertheless, directly applying blockchain to FLL significantly increases computational and retrieval costs with the expansion of the knowledge base, slowing down the training on resource-constrained IoT devices. To address these challenges, we propose LiFeChain, a lightweight blockchain for secure and efficient federated lifelong learning with minimal on-chain disclosure and bidirectional verification. LiFeChain is the first blockchain tailored for FLL. It incorporates two complementary mechanisms: the Proof-of-Model-Correlation (PoMC) consensus on the server, which couples learning and unlearning mechanisms to mitigate negative transfer; and Segmented Zero-knowledge Arbitration (Seg-ZA) at the client, which detects and arbitrates abnormal committee behavior without compromising privacy. LiFeChain is a plug-and-play component that can be seamlessly integrated into existing FLL algorithms for IoT applications. To demonstrate its practicality and performance, we implement LiFeChain in representative FLL algorithms with Hyperledger Fabric under 6 representative attacks. Rigorous theoretical analysis and extensive evaluations demonstrate that LiFeChain effectively mitigates long-term attacks, maintains high scalability, and significantly reduces latency and storage overhead compared to state-of-the-art blockchain solutions.

Author: Bakshi, A. R.; Rajalakshmi, A.; Kumar, S. G.; J.Umamaheswari
Title: AI-Driven Intrusion Detection and Automated Response for Encrypted Network Traffic
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Data Science and Business Systems (ICDSBS)
Abstract Note: In the last few years, encrypted communication has become more common in almost all kinds of digital networks. Modern protocols like TLS, HTTPS, QUIC, and VPNs are widely used to protect sensitive data from unauthorized access. While they improve security and privacy, they also create challenges for network monitoring systems. Encryption limits traditional intrusion detection methods, as these rely on inspecting packet contents, which are now hidden. Attackers have also started to use this flaw to their advantage. Many modern threats, like DDoS attacks, command-and-control communication, lateral movement, and data exfiltration, now use encrypted channels. Finding them with old methods is harder now.This paper talks about how to make a system that can find and respond to intrusions in encrypted networks. The system doesn't look at the payload; it looks at things like the size of the packets, how they change over time, and the traffic patterns. Author: Wang, X.; Cheng, J.; Wang, L.; Tu, W.; Xiong, N. N.
Title: A Distributed Difference-Aware Alignment Framework for Robust Federated Graph Learning
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering
Abstract Note: Federated Graph Learning (FGL) has emerged as a crucial paradigm for collaborative training across distributed graph data. However, in Non-Independent and Identically Distributed (non-IID) scenarios, heterogeneous data partitions and representational distortion introduced by graph augmentations lead to node-level semantic drift, which restricts the generalization of the global model. Existing approaches mainly rely on graph augmentation or aggregation strategies, but often assume that augmentations preserve semantics, overlooking the drift between original and augmented graphs and leading to local model instability. To address this, we propose Federated Difference-aware Semantic-alignment Learning (FedDSL), a framework that jointly tackles augmentation-induced and distribution-induced drift. Specifically, we design a difference-aware regularization module that quantifies attribute and structural differences between original and augmented graphs to stabilize local embeddings with modest additional computation. Furthermore, a node-level semantic alignment module is proposed to align local embeddings with global representations, improving cross-client consistency without introducing extra communication rounds. Extensive experiments on six benchmark datasets, covering both homophilic and heterophilic graphs, demonstrate that FedDSL consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines under non-IID conditions.
Manual Tags: non-IID data; Federated graph learning; cross-client consistency; distributed representation alignment; robust distributed training; semantic drift mitigation

Author: Paulino, D.; Ferreira, A.; Maldonado, J.; Duarte, C.; Oliveira, M.; Aguiar, A.; Correia, F.; Gajetti, M.; Perboli, G.; Mamei, M.; Paredes, H.

Author: Kishore, A.; Bose, R.; Sutradhar, S.; Roy, S.; Sarkar, I.
Title: FedQuantChain: Privacy-Preserving Federated Intelligence for Agriculture 7.0 Supply Networks
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Sustainability, Innovation & Technology (ICSIT)
Abstract Note: Despite hopes of quantum-blockchain approaches for precision agriculture, three key deficiencies remain: (i) inter-node privacy in federated farm networks, (ii) consensus-energy efficiency under IoT resource limitations, and (iii) lack of verifiable claims of supply chain quality without compromising confidentiality of farm commercial data. Author: AbdelRaouf, H.; Hasnaine, Q. R.; Fouda, M. M.; Fadlullah, Z. M.; Ibrahem, M. I.

Abstract Note: The rapid evolution of beyond fifth-generation (B5G) and sixth-generation (6G) networks is reshaping mobile edge computing (MEC) to support large-scale, heterogeneous Internet of Things (IoT) deployments and complex cyber-physical systems (CPSs). Conventional data-driven intelligence in MEC traditionally relies on centralized learning paradigms that often fail to meet the privacy, latency, scalability, and adaptability requirements in distributed and resource-constrained environments. To address these shortcomings, the objective of our work in this article is to investigate the paradigm shift toward distributed learning and demonstrate how its co-design with emerging communication and system-level technologies can enable scalable and trustworthy intelligence for next-generation IoT and CPS. Building on this objective, we conduct a systematic survey of recent studies and analyze 12 key enabling technologies, including concept drift adaptation, transformers, TinyML, blockchain, integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), digital twins, explainable AI (XAI), federated learning (FL) and unlearning, adversarial ML (AdvML), meta-learning, and multiarmed bandits (MABs). The surveyed literature is organized using a unified taxonomy and an integrated conceptual pipeline, which clarifies how these enablers interact across sensing, communication, computation, trust, and adaptation layers of IoT and CPSs. The main outcomes of this study include: 1) a comprehensive taxonomy characterizing enabling technologies for distributed edge intelligence; 2) a comparative synthesis of representative works highlighting common architectural patterns and evaluation practices; and 3) the identification of research gaps, critical tradeoffs, and open challenges, particularly related to model robustness, energy efficiency, data heterogeneity, and secure real-time inference. Author: Ibrahim, H.; Ahakonye, L. A. C.; Lee, J.-M.; Kim, D.-S.
Title: PureChain Closed-Loop Intrusion Detection and Real-Time Recovery for Industrial IoT
Publication Title: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
Abstract Note: The Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) has transformed critical infrastructure but has also introduced severe security vulnerabilities, with breaches capable of causing catastrophic physical and operational damage. While blockchain technology offers a promising foundation for tamper-proof logging, existing platforms are often ill-suited for IIoT due to high latency, low throughput, and excessive energy consumption. Furthermore, most current research treats intrusion detection, secure logging, and system recovery as isolated components, lacking a unified framework for autonomous, verifiable resilience. To bridge this critical gap, this article introduces PureChain, a holistic, secure, and resilient ecosystem. PureChain integrates a custom lightweight blockchain with a deep learning-based intrusion detection system (IDS) and a novel verifiable recovery protocol, creating a closed-loop security model. The framework leverages a novel proof-of-authority and association (PoA2) consensus mechanism, achieving high throughput (16.82 TPS), low latency (0.0594 s), and minimal energy consumption (12.43 W), demonstrating suitability for resource-constrained IIoT environments compared to general-purpose platforms like Ethereum and Hyperledger, which are optimized for different use cases. Upon intrusion detection by optimized models like XGBoost (99.87% accuracy), immutable blockchain logs actively trigger and cryptographically attest to infrastructure-enforced recovery actions such as device isolation via software-defined network (SDN) switches or state rollback through hardware management controllers. Extensive evaluation on benchmark IIoT datasets (IoT-CAD and IoTForge) demonstrates a detection-to-recovery success rate of up to 98.59% while maintaining 100% data integrity. PureChain establishes a new paradigm that unifies real-time threat intelligence, blockchain-based trust, and provable autonomous recovery for next-generation IIoT security.

Author: Kalaichelvi, N.; B, K.; Arivazhagan, P.; Rajangam, S.; Punitha, V.; Geethamani, G. S.

Author: Kasthuri, J.; P, G. S.; A, J. S.; Gnanavel, V. K.; Agoramoorthy, M.
Title: Proof-of-Training Consensus: Integrating RNN Sequence Modeling with Blockchain for Verifiable On-Chain Learning
Publication Title: 2026 6th International Conference on Inventive Computation and Information Technologies (ICICIT)
Abstract Note: Machine learning and blockchain technology have long been limited by the inherent incompatibility between the resource requirements of on-chain neural network training and the resource constraints of on-chain training. Current consensus algorithms like Proof-of-Work (PoW) use vast amounts of energy to perform cryptographically useless computations, and Proof-of-Stake (PoS) does not provide any direct benefit to society or science other than ledger security. In this paper, a new type of consensus mechanism, which is called Proof-of-Training (PoT) is presented, which replaces the wasteful hash operations with some verifiable Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) training as the mining operation. PoT has miners trying to achieve the biggest decrease in validation loss on a publicly declared sequence modeling task, where block rewards are proportional to shown learning development. The suggested framework combines a simple Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) architecture with a new Gradient Commitment Protocol that allows to verify training claims efficiently without re-running the entire backpropagation. Time-series forecasting and character-level language modeling experiments have shown that PoT can achieve consensus throughput of 125 blocks per hour and verification overhead of just 3.2% of training cost. The framework also creates an ever more precise RNN model as a consensus byproduct, without the energy waste of PoW and with the same security guarantees. Complete blockchain with peer-to-peer networking, UTXO transaction model, and GPU-accelerated mining is proven to be practically viable to decentralized sequence learning applications.
Manual Tags: consensus mechanism; recurrent neural networks; verifiable computation; Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU); blockchain mining; energy-efficient consensus; on-chain learning; Proof-of-Training; sequence modeling

Author: Jain, V.; Mittal, H.; Budhiraja, K.; Bhardwaj, I.; Kumar, P.

Author: Kanji, R. K.; Rellu, N. S. H.; Surasani, V. R.; Mekala, V. R.
Title: Evaluating the Impact of AI on Data Quality and Governance in Cloud - based Systems
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Electronics and Renewable Systems (ICEARS)
Abstract Note: The speedy implementation of cloud based systems has brought about with it most critical issues in guaranteeing quality and effective governance of data, especially as organisations become more dependent on the aid of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to deliver the automation of data management functions. This is because inaccurate or incomplete and inconsistent data can destabilize decision-making and regulatory compliance, and it is thus important to have AI-driven solutions that are robust. This study explores how AI can affect data quality and data governance in the cloud, looking into accuracy, completeness, timeliness, consistency, validity, policy compliance, and auditability, and improving all of these aspects. Qualitative evaluations of data governance stakeholders were in addition to a mixed-methods approach where the AI-enabled, hybrid, and baseline data pipelines were tested quasi-experimentally. AIs such as anomaly detection, AutoML-based data imputation, NLP-driven metadata management and privacy compliance modules were implemented. Quantitative outcomes also show that fully automated AI pipelines were able to provide accuracy and completeness of more than 95 percent, significantly decreasing manual correction and enhancing auditability with hybrid strategies offering a compromise between process automation and auditor oversight. In conclusion, AI has shown a lot of promise in improving the quality and governance of data with hybrid and emerging strategies offering scalable, trustworthy and compliant tools to manage cloud-based data reporting.

Author: Jayageetha, P.; Pandian, R.
Title: A Secure IoMT Framework for Histopathological Breast Cancer Detection Using Transfer Learning
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Recent Innovation in Science, Engineering and Technology (ICRISET)
Abstract Note: Breast cancer is a major cause of death amongst women in the world, and this has necessitated the need to have precise and automated diagnostic models to detect the histopathological disease in its early stages. Current deep learning systems do not have the ability to combine explainability, security, and lightweight deployability in Internet of Medical Things devices, which is a limitation to their practical use in clinical settings. In this work, a secure framework called SecureXAI-IoMT is proposed, which is a lightweight, automated breast cancer histopathological detection system based on optimized explainable transfer learning. The framework proposed will combine Macenko stain normalization, depthwise separable MobileNetV3 backbone with Squeeze-and-Excision channel attention, blockchain-based data integrity verification with SHA-256, Grad-CAM++ lesion localization, and federated differential privacy aggregation to deploy to multiple hospitals. Experiments on the BreakHis dataset of 9,109 histopathological biopsy images show that the proposed framework from 400× magnification gets a 99.34% classification accuracy, 99.21% precision, 99.41% recall, and 99.31% F1-score, which is better than all the compared state-of-the-art methods. The proposed framework is the first framework to integrate diagnostic accuracy, clinical explainability, and IoMT security into a single unified framework that can be deployed on resource-constrained edges.

Author: Zanatta, R.; Vanzin, V.; Matos, S.; Garcia, R.; Moreira, D.; Ueyama, J.
Title: A Decentralized Learning Architecture for Medical Prescription Anomaly Detection via Hybrid Federated-Swarm Learning
Publication Title: IEEE Latin America Transactions
Abstract Note: The increasing use of electronic medical records (EMRs) has improved efficiency, accuracy, and accessibility of patient data. However, conventional centralized architectures suffer from single points of failure and data privacy issues. To address these challenges, this study proposes a decentralized machine learning architecture that combines concepts from Federated Learning (FL) and Swarm Learning (SL) for anomaly detection in medical prescriptions. The proposed architecture leverages blockchain and the InterPlanetary File System (IPFS) to enable secure model sharing and decentralized storage, thereby reducing communication complexity and establishing a transparent, decentralized parameter repository. Experimental evaluations were conducted using logistic regression (LR), a multi-layer perceptron (MLP), and a decision tree (DT) model. Compared with the FL baseline, the proposed system achieved superior efficiency, lower resource consumption, and improved latency, along with smaller block sizes. It, however, exhibited slightly lower transaction throughput and longer training rounds, reflecting the added complexity of decentralization. In predictive performance on the anomaly classification task, DT achieved the highest precision and recall under the evaluated dataset (F1-score=0.9912), followed by MLP (0.5504) and LR (0.2442). The decentralized training approach led to negligible performance loss relative to centralized models, less than 4% for LR and below 1% for both MLP and DT. Overall, the proposed system demonstrates a robust and efficient alternative for decentralized learning in healthcare applications, maintaining strong predictive performance while enhancing architectural transparency.

Author: Zeydan, E.; Mangues-Bafalluy, J.; Turk, Y.; Liyanage, M.

Abstract Note: Images have become a strategic digital asset that powers creative industries, e–commerce, and data–driven services. Author: Vanitha, R.; M.Thenmozhi
Title: A Survey on Hybrid Deep Learning Models for Secure Healthcare Monitoring Using Edge Computing

Abstract Note: The growing adoption of hybrid deep learning models combined with Improved Artificial Rabbit Optimization (IARO) have shown strong potential to support secure and reliable healthcare monitoring in edge computing environments. Author: Khaliq, M. S.; Ahakonye, L. A. C.; Lee, J.-M.; Kim, D.-S.
Title: PureChain-Enabled Framework for Trustworthy and Incentivized Smart Contract Vulnerability Detection
Publication Title: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
Abstract Note: Smart contract vulnerabilities pose a critical threat to blockchain-enabled Internet of Things (IoT) systems, as they can lead to substantial financial losses and undermine trust in decentralized services. While existing studies demonstrate strong vulnerability detection performance, they often overlook trust alignment, incentive compatibility, and verifiable validation under adversarial conditions. This study presents a trustworthy and incentivized framework for smart contract vulnerability governance that integrates decentralized reporting, a proof of authority and association (PoA2) reputation mechanism, proof-of-concept (PoC)-assisted validation, and hybrid on-chain/off-chain orchestration. The main contribution of this study lies in the PoA2-based trust and incentive model, which quantifies the reliability of the participants through the authority, association, and behavioral trust scores. This mechanism effectively discourages Sybil attacks, collusion, and reward manipulation. Within the framework, vulnerability detection is carried out by an optimized DeepFusion model augmented with expert-rule integration, designed as a modular detection engine rather than the primary contribution. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate strong performance, achieving \F1\ -scores of up to 97.14% across multiple vulnerability categories, with inference latency ranging from 0.0011 to 0.0116 s. By offloading computation-intensive tasks while preserving on-chain auditability, PureChain reduces on-chain overhead and improves scalability. In general, the results indicate that the proposed study provides a practical and trustworthy foundation for the reporting, validation, and incentive-driven security governance of decentralized vulnerabilities in blockchain-based IoT environments.
Manual Tags: smart contract; PureChain; Deep learning; incentivization; expert rules; proof of authority and association (PoA2); vulnerability detection

Author: Wan, H.; Li, M.; Guo, J.; Tang, S.; Yang, R.; Sun, E.
Title: Resilient Collaborative Learning over Hierarchical Blockchain for Inter-Cell Aerial MEC Networks

Abstract Note: The rapid growth of computation-intensive and latency-sensitive applications has motivated the adoption of aerial base stations (ABSs)-assisted mobile edge computing (MEC) using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and high-altitude platforms (HAPs) to support regions with limited terrestrial infrastructure. In this paper, we investigate a multi-cell aerial MEC architecture composed of multiple UAVs and multiple HAPs, and develop a blockchain-enabled group relative policy optimization (GRPO) framework based on a federated election mechanism. The proposed approach jointly optimizes computation task scheduling and ABSs resource allocation, while enhancing system robustness against both non-Byzantine and Byzantine attacks through secure policy and agent selection. Author: Vij, P.; Nayak, A.

Author: Poorvi, J.; Kalita, A.; Gurusamy, M.
Title: Reliable and Efficient Data Collection in UAV-Based IoT Networks

Abstract Note: IoT involves sensors for monitoring and wireless networks for efficient communication. Nevertheless, effective data collection in UAV-assisted IoT networks is hampered by factors, including dynamic UAV behaviour, environmental variables, connectivity instability, and security considerations. In this survey, we first explore various communication technologies for UAV-IoT networks, performance metrics, and simulation tools, followed by a categorization of the UAV-IoT system based on the service model of UAV, mode of operation of UAV and UE during data collection, and network topology. Additionally, we discuss efficient data collection strategies in UAV-based IoT networks, covering trajectory planning and constraint management, sensor network clustering, data aggregation, and UAV swarm formations. Further, advanced AI techniques are discussed, which enable efficient and reliable data transfer in UAV-IoT systems. Finally, we discuss future challenges and their possible solutions using different approaches such as Decentralized Reinforcement and Federated Learning, Generative AI, and hybrid optical-RF communication links with integration of blockchain for reliable, efficient, and secure data collection in UAV-assisted IoT networks.

Author: Gowri, C. G.; Amanullah, M.; S, S. P.
Title: A Blockchain-Enabled Decentralized Healthcare Monitoring with LSTM-Based EEG Signal Analysis
Publication Title: 2026 7th International Conference on Smart Electronics and Communication (ICOSEC)
Abstract Note: The intelligent healthcare systems and wearable sensors have allowed for continuous monitoring of neurological disorders through the use of electroencephalogram (EEG) signals. That being said, the centralized architecture of these healthcare systems has created major challenges around the security, privacy, and integrity of the data being collected. To counter this issue, we suggest a new approach for decentralized monitoring of healthcare, utilizing a blockchain-based data management system in conjunction with an LSTM-based analysis algorithm, which would create a reliable and secure method for detecting seizures. Initially, we use techniques such as z-score normalization and band-pass filtering to preprocess the raw EEG signal(s), removing noise and improving the overall quality of the signal(s). Next, we apply an autoencoder-based feature extraction method, allowing us to create robust representations of the EEG data, followed by an attention-enhanced Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) network, which will learn the temporal dependencies found in the EEG sequence and emphasize the most significant patterns within the data. Finally, the extracted features will be classified by using a sigmoid activation function, allowing for prediction of seizure occurrence. The integration of the blockchain creates a secure storage system, as well as the ability to share data without the risk of tampering, through decentralized access control between the different stakeholders involved in a patient's healthcare. The results of testing our proposed framework showed that the framework achieved a predictive accuracy of 97.84%, with precision at 97.62%, recall at 98.10%, and an F1-score of 97.86%, outperforming traditional machine-learning and standalone deep-learning models in relation to both prediction accuracy and data security. As well as increasing the diagnostic accuracy of the system, for healthcare monitoring, the combination of blockchain and deep-learning technologies creates a trustworthy and privacy-preserving solution.

Author: Thakur, A.; Chaurasiya, A.; K.Roopatharshini; Sarraf, A.; T.Hemalatha; P, S.
Title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning-based Optimization Framework for Smart Energy and Resource Management in Cyber-Physical Smart Grid Systems

Scalability analysis shows lower communication costs (55-65%), increased cumulative reward (up to 0.91) with improved stability. Author: Zhou, J.; Zhao, Y.; Gong, Y.; Zhang, R.; Wang, J.; Zhang, S.; Peng, M.
Title: Optimized Federated Reinforcement Learning for Latency and Energy Minimization in Dynamic Satellite-Ground Graph Networks

Abstract Note: Satellite–ground integrated networks (SGIN) represent a novel architectural paradigm that enables seamless spatiotemporal coverage, high-throughput data dissemination, and distributed computation offloading. By reducing end-to-end latency and alleviating resource contention, SGIN support efficient and adaptive task scheduling across heterogeneous network entities. However, the dynamic and time-varying topology of SGIN results in complex, multi-modal graph structures, posing significant challenges for unified representation, modeling, and optimization over space and time. To address these issues, we construct a graph-based model of the SGIN to jointly minimize total network latency and improve energy efficiency. A graph neural network (GNN)-based graph learning approach is developed to capture the dynamic features of satellite nodes. We further introduce a federated reinforcement learning framework to jointly optimize CPU cycle frequency, quantization bit allocation, and transmission power. This framework enhances convergence speed while preserving data privacy. Additionally, a transaction verification mechanism is integrated to illustrate the task execution process and demonstrate graph permutation invariance between the generative model and optimization objectives. Title: A Survey on the Application of Artificial Intelligence in Combating Telecom Fraud
Publication Title: IEEE Access
Abstract Note: Telecommunications fraud is a pervasive security threat in the digital era. It causes large financial losses and affects many users. This survey reviews how artificial intelligence (AI) techniques are used to detect, prevent, and respond to telecommunications fraud. We summarize the methodological shift from rule-based and statistical systems to representation learning. We cover pre-trained language models, graph neural networks, and multimodal fusion. We organize the literature by application scenarios, including voice-call and SMS fraud detection, phishing website identification, deepfake and synthetic-media forensics, and risk control for fraud-related financial transactions. We highlight open challenges, including adversarial evasion, privacy-preserving learning, cross-platform data integration, and the need for interpretable and trustworthy AI. We also outline research directions such as privacy-enhanced collaboration, real-time adaptive detection, and unified multimodal reasoning across text, audio, and visual signals. Finally, we discuss complementary security technologies (e.g., post-quantum cryptography and blockchain-based audit trails), socio-economic implications, and the need for standardized benchmarks and ethical governance.
Manual Tags: deep learning; artificial intelligence; large language models; graph neural networks; Telecommunication fraud detection

Author: Ajakwe, S. Okechukwu; Kim, D.-S.
Title: EQAI: Explainable Quantum-Empowered Antispoofing Intelligence for Trustworthy Connected Autonomous Vehicles Communication
Publication Title: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
Abstract Note: The increasing complexity of connected autonomous vehicles (CAVs) introduces new security challenges in the Internet of Vehicles (IoV), where traditional detection models struggle with real-time interpretability, scalability, and robustness against spoofing attacks. This article proposes an explainable quantum-empowered antispoofing intelligence (EQAI) framework that fuses quantum-enhanced learning with interpretable trust inference for securing vehicular communications. The EQAI model employs an eight-qubit variational quantum circuit (VQC) integrated with lightweight classical layers and explainability modules based on Shapley additive explanation (SHAP) and local interpretable model-agnostic explanation (LIME). Using Canadian Institute for Cybersecurity Internet of Vehicles 2024 Dataset (CICIoV2024), the framework achieves a detection accuracy of 92.85%, a Class \3 F1\ -score of 82.1%, and a low false alarm rate (FAR \textbackslash{}le 0.026\ ), outperforming existing machine learning (ML), blockchain (BC)-based, and federated learning (FL) approaches. Its compact design—with only 4900 trainable parameters and 19.5 k floating point operations per second (FLOPs)—demonstrates real-time deployability and energy efficiency at the network edge. Moreover, LIME and SHAP analyses reveal transparent feature-level reasoning, enhancing operator trust and system explainability. The proposed EQAI architecture thus establishes a scalable, interpretable, and quantum-empowered foundation for secure, trustworthy, and intelligent vehicular networks, advancing toward resilient IoV and next-generation cybercognitive mobility ecosystems.
Manual Tags: explainable AI (XAI); Connected autonomous vehicles (CAVs); quantum information theory; spoofing attacks; trustworthy communication; vehicle-to-everything (V2X)

Author: Ibrahim, H.; Ahakonye, L. A. C.; Lee, J.-M.; Kim, D.-S.
Title: A Unified AI-PureChain Framework for Verifiable Intrusion Prevention in Industrial IoT Systems
Publication Title: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
Abstract Note: Securing industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) systems presents critical challenges due to resource constraints, expanding attack surfaces, and the inadequacy of conventional security solutions against sophisticated cyber threats. While AI-driven detection and blockchain technologies offer promise, existing frameworks suffer from computational inefficiency, a lack of real-time prevention, or insufficient auditability. This article introduces a unified AI-PureChain intrusion prevention framework that tightly integrates deep learning-based threat detection with an immutable PureChain ledger using proof of authority and association (PoA2) consensus. The proposed architecture achieves high-fidelity intrusion detection through hybrid CNN-BiLSTM models, attaining 99.76% accuracy on IoTForge Pro, 98.33% on WUSTL-IIoT-2021, and 98.11% on X-IIoTID datasets, while maintaining low inference latency (0.0016 s). The PureChain layer ensures tamper-proof audit trails with 24.56 transactions per second (TPS) throughput and 68-ms commit time, enabling verifiable prevention actions. Experimental results demonstrate complete attack mitigation (0% success rate) under high-traffic conditions while maintaining minimal resource consumption (14.49% CPU, 448-MB memory, 12.95-W power). This work represents a significant advancement in IIoT security by delivering a tightly coupled framework that simultaneously addresses detection accuracy, prevention reliability, and forensic accountability, thereby bridging critical gaps in current industrial security paradigms.
Manual Tags: Blockchain; PureChain; cyber-physical systems; industrial IoT security; intrusion prevention system (IPS)

Author: Shukla, V.; Agarwal, R.; Tyagi, R. K.
Title: SecureEdge-TDM: A Threat-to-Defense Mapping Framework for Secure Edge Computing Using Machine Learning-Based Iot Intrusion Detection
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Networks Computers and Communications (ICNCCom)
Abstract Note: Edge computing enables low-latency IoT services but also increases exposure to threats such as DDoS, DoS, Mirai, spoofing, reconnaissance, brute-force, malware, and web-based attacks. Most existing intrusion detection studies focus mainly on attack classification and do not link detected threats with suitable defense actions. To address this gap, this paper proposes SecureEdge-TDM, a threat-to-defense mapping framework for secure edge computing. The framework evaluates Decision Tree, Random Forest, Extra Trees, XGBoost, and LightGBM on the CICIoT2023 dataset and maps detected threats to countermeasures such as secure offloading, rate limiting, federated threat intelligence, trusted device verification, policy-as-code enforcement, secure aggregation, and blockchain-based audit logging. Experimental results show that Random Forest achieved 99.628% accuracy and 96.098% macro-F1 for binary detection, while XGBoost achieved 99.499% accuracy and 87.819% macro-F1 for multiclass threat detection. The results show that SecureEdge-TDM supports both effective threat detection and actionable defense recommendation.

Author: Alshammeri, M.; Humayun, M.; Haseeb, K.; Alamri, M.; Chehri, A.; Jeon, G.
Title: Intent-Based Secure Fault Tolerance Model With Integrated AI for Edge-IoT Networks
Publication Title: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
Abstract Note: The development of real-time applications integrated with intent-based networking (IBN) integrates an Internet of Things (IoT), providing interconnection between heterogeneous devices and physical objects for the formulation of smart cities. These systems provide seamless communication and maintain the adaptive network policies and infrastructure. Many existing schemes have proposed solutions for efficient routing with support from intelligent architectures; however, although most of them overlook the bounded and limited resources of IoT networks, they impose additional overhead while addressing unpredictable communications in IBN-IoT. Furthermore, security and trustworthiness are significant research challenges that must be addressed to prevent data breaches and allow only the use of authentic devices. This research presents a scalable model for an IBN-IoT environment that utilizes edge computing to enable trustworthy and fault-tolerant communication with energy efficiency. First, software-defined networking (SDN) is explored for load balancing and effective resource allocation in 6G-IoT systems. Second, the proposed model explores artificial intelligence techniques to analyze the network environment and predict anomalies in the fault tolerance approach. Finally, data is kept private and maintained in integrity using a private blockchain, providing a more reliable, distributed, autonomous system with minimal overhead. Using synthetic data, the proposed model is validated against quantum genetic algorithm and ant colony optimization (QGA-ACO) and metaheuristic energy-aware routing with optimal DL-based anomaly detection technique (MER-ODLADT) solutions for energy consumption, anomaly detection, and time-to-failure metrics across dynamic scenarios.

Author: Hamza, M.; Swapna, M.; Singh, N.; Rao, K. B.; Y, K. B.; G, K. P.
Title: AI-Powered Hybrid Management Framework for Autonomous Vendor Evaluation and Procurement Optimization
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Quantum Photonics, Artificial Intelligence & Networking (QPAIN)
Abstract Note: The optimization of procurement is an acute issue that enterprise organizations face working in unstable supply chains and dynamic regulatory environments. The old vendor management systems tend to be based on restrictive and rule-driven appraisals that just cannot evolve to non-linear and complex procurement world. This paper suggests employing AI-based hybrid management and uses rare and advanced algorithms such as a Quantum-Inspired Decision Matrix (QIDM), Swarm-Driven Contractual Risk Assessment (SDCRA), Graph-Based Trust Propagation Network (GTPN) and Evolutionary Procurement Policy Optimizer (EPPO). The model itself analyses vendors, identifies risks, advances procurement policies, and makes transparency available with blockchain-backed audit trails. The comparison of 50 procurement scenarios conducted through experimental analysis demonstrated that QIDM obtained a vendor ranking accuracy of 96, SDCRA had a risk detection precision of 93.3, and EPPO could allow saving up to 13.4 in procurement costs. Moreover, GTPN achieved a mean error of prediction of trust of only 2.65 which is better than conventional evaluation models. Additional support of multimodal sentiment analysis and neuro-fuzzy reinforcement decision layers further enhanced the profile of vendors and minimized conflict in decision by 47%. This model shows a sound, decipherable, and changeable approach to contemporary procurement issues. The next phase of work will involve the adoption of real-time IoT-built supply chains, including moral AI limits, and joint procurement through federated learning architecture.

Author: Yrjölä, S.; Matinmikko-Blue, M.; Ahokangas, P.
Title: Resilience-Oriented Business Model Designs in 6G
Publication Title: 2026 Joint European Conference on Networks and Communications & 6G Summit (EuCNC/6G Summit)
Abstract Note: This paper investigates diverse range of resilienceoriented business model designs in 6G. The anticipated generalpurpose 6 G technology platform holds the potential to innovating new technologies, services, applications, and business models for enhancing network value and benefiting from novel resilience related business opportunities. Through the analysis, 9 distinct resilience-oriented business model pattern groups and 48 patterns were identified and characterized based on their value creation perspectives. Resilience is fostered by these patterns, which operate through the strategic mitigation of critical weaknesses, the comprehensive situational understanding, and the augmentation of adaptive capabilities. The study's findings underscore the contribution of several factors to resilient \textbackslash{}mathbf{6 G}\ system development, specifically: the unified management of physical assets and data, the robust interoperability and high quality of complementor offerings, and the structured governance of business-to-business platforms. Considering that specific resilience implications on demand-side have not been adequately incorporated into existing business models, it is crucial for standardization, policy, and regulatory frameworks to reinforce 6 G resilience advancements.

Author: Vettriselvan, R.; Sugunakar, M.; Al-Qerem, A.; Swathi, A.; Singh, N.; Panduri, B.
Title: AI-Integrated Hybrid Multi-Objective Governance System for Adaptive Enterprise Management Analytics
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Quantum Photonics, Artificial Intelligence & Networking (QPAIN)
Abstract Note: In the modern world of rapid change of the enterprise environment, the system of governance should be dynamic, multi-purpose, and explanatory. To address these requirements, this research paper introduces an AI-Embedded Hybrid Multi-Objective Governance System which allows the adaptive decision-making process within distributed business environment. The framework builds a semantic knowledge graph by combining both structured and unstructured data of ERP, CRM, HRMS, financial, and logistics systems to build an enterprise context. It continuously measures and streamlines five areas of governance compliance, performance, risk, sustainability, and cyber-resilience with a hybrid AI engine consisting of rule-based reasoning, Gradient Boosting models, and Transformer-based deep learning. Reinforcement learning (RL) agents are incorporated to be able to change the policy thresholds in a real-time fashion. Federated Learning also guarantees the privacy-preserving model training units without exchanging raw data. SHAP and causal inference explainability is incorporated to increase trust and auditability. The system was found to have reached up to 92.6 % accuracy in forecasting SLA adherence and 89.5 % in predicting risk index, and increased performance by 15.1 % and reduced risk exposure by 10.1 % on average. Future innovative contributions are to add our unstructured streams of data such as IoT sensors and news feeds, agent-based game theory to negotiate, and blockchain audit trails. The proposed system provides a base towards the real self-governing, intelligent enterprise governance.

Author: Peng, Y.; Tian, G.
Title: Federated XGBoost with differential privacy for SME innovation quality assessment under inclusive finance
Publication Title: 5th International Conference on Big Data Blockchain and Economy Management (ICBBEM 2026)
Abstract Note: The assessment of small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) innovation quality is critical for inclusive finance policy design, yet traditional centralized evaluation models face dual challenges: data fragmentation across regions and privacy concerns regarding sensitive R&D information. This paper proposes a privacy-preserving federated learning framework that enables collaborative innovation quality prediction while maintaining data locality. We develop a heterogeneity-aware federated XGBoost algorithm that aggregates gradient statistics from geographically distributed SMEs through sample-weighted averaging, integrated with ɛ-differential privacy mechanisms via adaptive gradient clipping and calibrated noise injection. To address regional economic disparities, we design a personalized aggregation strategy that blends global and local models using weights informed by entrepreneurial spirit characteristics, achieving adaptive balance between cross-regional knowledge transfer and local specialization. Experiments on 3,200 Chinese SMEs (2018-2022) demonstrate that our method achieves R²=0.873 with privacy budget ɛ=4, approaching centralized XGBoost performance (R²=0.891) with only 2.1% degradation while reducing communication costs by 40% compared to existing federated tree learning methods. SHAP-based interpretability analysis reveals distinct innovation drivers across eastern (digital finance penetration, SHAP=0.31), central (entrepreneurial risk-taking, SHAP=0.29), and western (traditional finance accessibility, SHAP=0.34) regions, validating the necessity of personalized models. The framework provides a practical solution for financial institutions to conduct privacy-compliant collaborative credit evaluation under data localization regulations, while offering policymakers empirical evidence for designing differentiated inclusive finance interventions. This work advances federated learning theory for structured financial data and establishes a generalizable methodology for privacy-preserving multi-regional economic analysis.

Author: Dash, A.; Samantray, B. S.; Reddy, K. H. K.; Amin, F.; Mishra, S. K.
Title: A Secure Framework for Smart Waste Management Using IoT, Machine Learning, and Blockchain
Publication Title: 2026 1st International Conference on Emerging Trends in Advancements and Applications of Computational Intelligence Techniques (ETAACT)
Abstract Note: Urban areas create more solid waste which needs waste management systems that depend on advanced waste management technologies to operate effectively. The Smart Waste Management (SWM) framework integrates IoT and ML and Blockchain technologies to create a secure and scalable urban waste management system which uses data for waste management operations. IoT sensors collect real-time data on bin fill levels, environmental parameters (ammonia, methane, temperature, humidity), and geolocation. The system employs a privacy-preserving anonymization layer which protects confidential information that is stored permanently on the Hyperledger Fabric blockchain. The ML layer includes predictive models and optimization models which use Quantum-inspired Temporal Fusion Network to forecast time periods and Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning to optimize routes and Neural Architecture Search with Graph Neural Networks to adjust models in real time. The proposed framework is depicted through its architectural layers and system operational model. The experimental results show that the system maintains high reliability because it achieves transaction latencies below 100 milliseconds and success rates above 95% while decreasing both operational expenses and unnecessary resource consumption. The research shows how emerging technologies enable smart city governance to achieve sustainable operations which create a foundation for upcoming urban infrastructure development.
