Author: Mobark, M. S.; Alqahtani, A.; Shaik, N.
Title: Resource Allocation of IoT-Based Edge Computing in Smart Cities
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE 5th International Conference on AI in Cybersecurity (ICAIC)
Abstract Note: The rapid proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices is accelerating the development of smart cities, where billions of sensors and actuators collaborate to enhance safety, efficiency, and sustainability. Applications such as intelligent transportation, smart grids, healthcare, and surveillance generate massive, heterogeneous data streams that demand timely processing and reliable decision-making. Traditional cloud computing provides scalable storage and analysis but struggles to meet latency and bandwidth requirements for mission-critical tasks. Edge computing addresses these limitations by bringing computation closer to data sources, enabling low-latency, energy-aware operations. However, resource allocation in smart city systems remains a critical challenge due to limited computing power, memory, spectrum, and energy, constrained by device capabilities and shared infrastructure. This paper proposes a novel multi-stage framework for IoT-based edge computing that integrates predictive workload modeling, proportional fairness distribution, and adaptive Lagrangian optimization. The framework ensures scalable and fair allocation of heterogeneous resources while minimizing energy consumption and latency. Experimental results demonstrate a significant reduction in latency (62 ms vs. 80–95 ms), increased throughput (182 Mbps vs. 130–150 Mbps), improved energy efficiency (39 J vs. 48–55 J), and enhanced system utilization (92% vs. 71–78%). Reliability improves to 96%, while fairness and security ratings reach 9 on a normalized scale, outperforming existing approaches. By incorporating federated learning and blockchain, the framework enhances privacy, accountability, and resilience. Overall, the proposed model establishes a robust, scalable, and sustainable approach for smart city IoT resource allocation, advancing both technological efficiency and social responsibility. It is important to distinguish between improvements over classical baseline methods (80–95 ms latency) and the performance of next-generation 6G/AI-driven techniques. While certain 6G-based solutions achieve lower P50/P99 latencies, our framework provides a competitive balance across latency, fairness, energy efficiency, and security, rather than being the absolute fastest under all conditions. Future work will focus on extending the framework toward 6G-enabled, AI-driven edge intelligence by incorporating real-world large-scale deployments, cross-domain mobility awareness, and self-adaptive learning mechanisms to further optimize performance under highly dynamic smart city environments.
Manual Tags: Edge computing; Scalability; Reliability; Smart cities; Energy efficiency; IoT resource allocation; Latency optimization

Author: El-Hajj, M.
Title: Trustworthy Digital Health Twins Through Explainable AI and Ethical Governance
Publication Title: 2026 22nd International Conference on Wireless and Mobile Computing, Networking and Communications (WiMob)
Abstract Note: Digital Health Twins (DHTs) are data-driven virtual patient replicas that support precision medicine through continuous integration of clinical and wearable data streams. This paper presents an end-to-end DHT framework formalised as \textbackslash{}mathcal{M}!=!\textbackslash{}langle\textbackslash{}mathcal{S}, \textbackslash{}mathcal{D}, \textbackslash{}mathcal{U}, \textbackslash{}mathcal{F}, \textbackslash{}mathcal{G}\textbackslash{}rangle\ and implemented within a novel sixlayer architecture grounded in five open datasets: MIMIC-IV (94,458 ICU stays), ShanghaiT2DM (100 T2DM patients, CGM), UK Biobank (≈500,000), NHANES 2011-14, and AI-READI (1,067 multimodal T2DM patients). Six ML model families, including a MIMIC-IV-pretrained Transformer, are evaluated under federated learning with (ε,δ)-differential privacy (ε! = !0.5). Explainability is assessed through a novel composite DHT Explainability Score (DES) covering SHAP, LIME, Integrated Gradients, Concept Bottleneck Models, and attention rollout. An Ethical Governance Layer (EGL) implements bias auditing, differential privacy, blockchain consent management, and immutable audit logging, aligned with EU AI Act Articles 9-15 and GDPR. In a Type 2 Diabetes case study, the Transformer achieves AUROC,=,0.940 for 90-day HbA1c exceedance, DES,=,0.86, 76% clinician adoption, and an equalised-odds gap of ∆EO!=!0.027 across all AI-READI demographic subgroups. These results demonstrate that explainability, privacy, and governance can be co-designed without sacrificing predictive performance.

Author: Shrivastava, A.; Said, N. A.; Bathla, G.; Kapoor, T.; Nagaraju, G.; Santoshi, R. V.
Title: Face Spoof Detection in Artificial Neural Network Based on IoT
Publication Title: 2026 2nd International Conference on Sustainable Computing and Integrated Communication in Changing Landscape of AI (ICSCAI)
Abstract Note: Internet of Things (IoT) technologies that enable smart devices have propelled the evolution of face recognition systems in smart home, intelligent surveillance, healthcare, banking, access control and smart city infrastructures for authentication purpose. Although these are convenient and widely adopted systems, face recognition systems are still extremely vulnerable to presentation attacks such as printed photos, repeat videos, three dimensional masks, and digitally altered facial images. The face spoofing attacks greatly undermine the trustworthiness and security of biometric authentication systems. Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) are found to be very successful in extracting discriminative facial representation and detecting the spoofing attempts with high accuracy, especially if the ANNs are based on deep learning architectures. The authors examine the different approaches adopted to extract their features, methods used to detect the presentation attacks, lightweight neural network architectures, multimodal biometric fusion, and on-edge intelligent authentication methods that make use of intelligent devices in an IoT setting, and provide a comprehensive analysis of the ANN-based face spoof detection techniques in IoT setting. Moreover, the paper presents the problem of computational complexity, real-time inference, limited resource IoT devices, generalization across datasets, privacy protection, adversarial attacks, and scalability to deploy. Future directions are also considered, such as emerging technologies, including explainable artificial intelligence, federated learning, edge computing, blockchain-assisted authentication, and lightweight deep neural networks. The study concludes that the use of ANN for face spoof detection can significantly boost the biometric security and offer intelligent, scalable and reliable authentication for next-generation IoT-based ecosystems.

Author: Li, Y.; Li, Y.; Nie, J.; Ercisli, S.
Title: Robust AI-Driven Intrusion Detection and Defense for Next-Generation Consumer Services
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Consumer Electronics
Abstract Note: With the deep integration of 6G, the Internet of Things, and artificial intelligence, this paper proposes an intrusion detection and defense framework that combines robust AI kernel reconstruction, a cross-layer collaborative perception architecture, and a dynamic defense closed-loop mechanism to address advanced persistent threats and dynamically evolving attacks targeting next-generation consumer services. First, a lightweight detection model ATF-KDBC is designed based on adversarial training and online knowledge distillation. Gradient masking and noise injection are employed to enhance robustness against adversarial samples, while a drift-aware module enables adaptive optimization under concept drift scenarios. The model achieves accuracies of 99.25% and 99.84% on the NSL-KDD and IoT-23 hybrid datasets, respectively, and compresses the model size to 1.08 MB, representing a 97.6% reduction compared with the BERT teacher model. Second, a multidimensional attack chain analysis model is developed based on a STHGN. By integrating semantic, structural, and temporal features with a multi-head self-attention mechanism, the model enables cross-layer threat tracing and millisecond-level response, achieving an F1-score exceeding 97.0% on the DARPA dataset. Furthermore, this study explores the construction of a distributed CTIS network by integrating federated learning and blockchain technology. Zero-knowledge proofs are employed to ensure privacy preservation, while a Quality of Data and Quality of Model scoring mechanism enables efficient and precise deployment of defense strategies. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly outperforms traditional methods in terms of robustness, environmental adaptability, and computational efficiency, thereby providing both theoretical support and a technical pathway for enhancing the resilience and security of next-generation consumer services.
Manual Tags: Artificial intelligence; knowledge distillation; consumer services; sixth-generation communication networks

Author: Amritha, S.; Swaroopa, C. N.; Devanna, H.; Narang, M.; Ranga, J.; Mishra, R.
Title: Autoscale-AI: Leveraging Intelligent Automation Through RPA–AI Synergy for Operational Agility and Scalable Growth in Tech Startup
Publication Title: 2026 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Applications Theme: Healthcare and Internet of Things (AIMLA)
Abstract Note: Intelligent automation is revolutionizing operational workflows in tech startups by combining Robotic Process Automation (RPA) with Artificial Intelligence (AI) to achieve enhanced agility and scalability. The average task completion time was reduced by 33%, while the error rate decreased by 65%. Cost savings improved by 24.5%, and automation uptime exceeded 99%, reflecting superior reliability. The combined performance index reached above 91%, confirming the framework's robustness and efficiency. The use of graph neural networks (GNNs) to uncover process interdependencies and few-shot learning for bot adaptation proved critical to sustaining performance in dynamic startup environments. Federated learning ensured collaborative model improvements without compromising data privacy, while blockchain integration guaranteed immutable, transparent compliance records. These advancements make the framework particularly suitable for fast-paced tech startups requiring scalable, adaptive, and secure automation solutions. The results validate that synergizing RPA and AI through innovative techniques can substantially elevate operational efficiency and business continuity, paving the way for next-generation automation in emerging enterprises.

Author: Chen, D.; Lu, Z.; Guo, H.; Duan, Q.; Lin, J.; Huang, S.-C.; Hung, P. C. K.; Luo, C.
Title: On-Chain Detection of Token Manipulation in Collaborative Learning for Consumer Electronics
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Consumer Electronics
Abstract Note: Token-based incentive mechanisms are increasingly adopted in collaborative learning (CL) to encourage resource-constrained consumer electronics (CE) devices to contribute local data and computation. However, these mechanisms introduce a critical security vulnerability: centralized token manipulation, where malicious entities distort reward logic, tamper with token supply, or capture governance, thereby undermining participant trust and system sustainability. Existing detection methods, primarily designed for financial “Rug Pull” scams, struggle to address these risks in CL environments due to their inability to handle benign operational complexity and high detection latency. To address this problem, we propose TM-TxD (Token Manipulation Transaction Detection), a novel on-chain detection framework. TM-TxD employs a decoupled offline-online architecture suitable for CE ecosystems. In the offline phase, a multi-agent system powered by Large Language Models (LLMs) extracts semantic intent from smart contracts, recovering logic even from unverified bytecode. In the online phase, a semantically regularized Graph Neural Network (GNN) analyzes on-chain transaction interaction graphs, aligning structural patterns with pre-fetched semantic insights to identify manipulation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that TM-TxD outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving an accuracy of 93.32% and an F1-score of 95.74% while maintaining low detection latency. This work provides a scalable security solution to safeguard fairness in token-incentivized collaborative learning.
Manual Tags: blockchain; Consumer electronics; collaborative learning; on-chain detection; token manipulation

Author: Verma, S.; Fouda, M.; Fadlullah, Z. M.; Fang, S.; Ibrahem, M. I.
Title: Modern Advances in Secure Multi-Party Computation: Protocols, Implementations, and Emerging Applications
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Secure IoT, Assured and Trusted Computing (SATC)
Abstract Note: The rapid increase in data exchange among distributed parties has led to privacy concerns during joint computation tasks. The need to ensure privacy in these processes has led to the development and application of cryptographic techniques, including Secure Multi-Party Computation (MPC), Homomorphic Encryption (HE), and Secret Sharing. This paper provides a survey analysis of current trends and developments in cryptographic MPC techniques, with an emphasis on architectures, models, and practical implementations. The paper examines secret sharing approaches to privacy-preserving analytics tasks, MPC inference approaches to large-scale language models, integrated verifiable MPC architectures with blockchain technology, and collaboration approaches among multiple parties in the cloud and edge computing zones. These works form the current state-of-the-art development trend in MPC applications that include cryptographic principles in artificial intelligence applications and distributed computing principles. The paper concludes with research areas that include hybrid MPC-HE models, verifiable computation, and post-quantum secure MPC.

Author: Ye, J.; Ge, X.; Zhao, Y.; Yu, Y.; Gharavi, H.
Title: A Tutorial on Future Vehicular Communications: From Performance Metrics to Open Research Directions
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
Abstract Note: The study of vehicular networks has evolved into a new era thanks to rapid advances in electric, transportation, communication, and automobile technologies. However, the realization of modern applications like autonomous driving, intelligent transportation systems, and the smart city remain a major challenge due to the high requirements for performance metrics like data rate, latency, reliability, connectivity, coverage, and security. Moreover, in vehicular network, the performance metrics are not independent and may have a complex coupling relationship, i.e., optimizing one may result in degrading others. In this paper, we begin with discussing the coupling effect among the aforementioned performance metrics, aiming to provide a basic concept of the challenges of future vehicular networks. We aim to provide a comprehensive review of recent developments in vehicular communication technologies, such as the fifth-generation new radio (5G NR), dedicated short-range communications (DSRC), millimeter wave/terahertz communications, mobile edge computing (MEC), integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) assisted vehicular networks, and blockchain-assisted security. The paper also covers the role of AI and its impact on the performance of each of the aforementioned applications. We then summarize several promising areas that can influence the future research in vehicular networks. Lastly, the paper concludes by highlighting key research challenges and future directions in the domain of vehicular networks.
Manual Tags: 6G; vehicular network; V2X; performance metrics; Vehicular communications

Author: Dahule, R.; Dagadkar, S.; Kamdi, N.
Title: Digital Twin for Smart Cities: Enabling Technologies, Applications, Challenges, and Future Scope
Publication Title: 2026 6th International Conference on Image Processing and Capsule Networks (ICIPCN)
Abstract Note: Real-time virtual representations of urban systems are made possible by digital twins (DTs), which facilitate modeling, prediction, and optimization in smart cities that are rapidly urbanizing. Based on peer-reviewed research, this overview examines DT technology and applications (2017-2024). It discusses the integration of key enabling technologies for bidirectional synchronization, including blockchain, IoT with edge computing, AI/ML, and cyber-physical systems. Transportation optimization, energy management, waste/water systems, disaster resilience (e.g., Herrenberg DT), and citizen participation through social and metaverse-enhanced twins are important uses. High prices, interoperability, privacy/security concerns, scalability, gaps in standardization, and socio-ethical concerns are the main issues raised. A succinct overview and strategy for promoting inclusive, sustainable urban digital twin development are presented in this paper.

Author: Toe, E.; Jaafar, F.; Ferrier, L. Charles André
Title: Securing LoRaWAN in the AIoT Era: A Systematic Mapping Study and an MITRE-Based Threat Matrix
Publication Title: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
Abstract Note: The rapid expansion of the Internet of Things (IoT) has established long-range wide-area network (LoRaWAN) as a leading low-power, long-range communication protocol across critical domains such as smart cities, agriculture, and healthcare. However, its minimalist design and reliance on unlicensed spectrum expose vulnerabilities across the entire protocol stack from physical-layer jamming to medium access control (MAC)-layer spoofing and application-layer firmware attacks. Concurrently, the rise of the Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) introduces opportunities to reinforce LoRaWAN security via decentralized, intelligent, and adaptive mechanisms. This article presents a systematic mapping study of 81 peer-reviewed publications (2020–2025), conducted using a Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA)-based methodology. Our objectives are to: 1) identify key trends and research directions in LoRaWAN security; 2) propose an MITRE ATT&CK-inspired taxonomy tailored to the LoRaWAN stack; 3) analyze AIoT-based security contributions; and 4) highlight unresolved challenges and future perspectives. Our findings indicate that 62% of documented cyberattacks target the MAC layer, exploiting vulnerabilities such as static keys and weak integrity checks. AI-driven techniques, including radio frequency fingerprinting (RFF) [97% accuracy using convolutional neural networks (CNNs)], federated learning for anomaly detection, and blockchain-based key management—show promise but raise concerns about scalability and deployment on constrained devices. We introduce the first MITRE ATT&CK-LoRaWAN matrix, detailing 18 attack techniques [e.g., energy depletion and rogue gateways (GWs)] and associated countermeasures, including postquantum Kyber-1024 encryption. Finally, we discuss major technical, methodological, and interoperability challenges and suggest actionable research directions toward secure, AI-native, and resilient LoRaWAN infrastructures.

Author: Özbay, R.; Çelebı, M.; Yavanoğlu, U.
Title: The AI-Cybersecurity Nexus: How Large Language Models are Reshaping Threat Intelligence and Digital Defense

Abstract Note: As cybersecurity threats become more sophisticated, the integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into defensive and analytical systems is transforming the field. Notable developments include decentralized trust-enhanced frameworks, context-aware remediation systems, and simulation-based red teaming. Author: Shakya, S.; Varshney, U.; Gupta, P.

Tackling these limitations will involve converging secure data-sharing mechanisms (e.g., blockchain), scalable AI models, and ethical governance frameworks. Author: Jing, Z.; Mu, J.; Zhu, Y.; Xu, L.; Qi, F.
Title: LLM-Driven Multicast Network Slicing for 6G Non-Terrestrial Networks

Author: Siewruk, G.; Berej, M.
Title: Transformation of Vulnerability Management Through Artificial Intelligence: An Overview of Generative and Learning Models
Publication Title: IEEE Access
Abstract Note: Software teams now uncover far more vulnerabilities than they can reasonably triage or fix. At the same time, learning-based analysis and large code models have matured. Finally, we specify the guardrails-tests, static checks, and policy constraints-needed to keep generated changes reliable and traceable. The result is a practical map: where to integrate capabilities in Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD), what evidence to retain for audit, and how to measure success using program metrics such as triage time, developer acceptance, and change-failure rate. Author: Mahmoud, A. M.; Sayed, A. I. E.
Title: SkyShield: A Hierarchical Defense Architecture for UAVs: Integrating Federated Deep Learning Ensembles and Post-Quantum Cryptography

Abstract Note: Intelligent physical systems, such as smart vehicles and robotic arms, are increasingly integrated into both industrial and everyday applications. Digital twin systems offer a solution by creating real-time digital replicas of physical systems that enhance computational efficiency, overcoming physical limitations. Moreover, multiple digital twins that hold complementary knowledge can conveniently collaborate to share information and computational resources, further improving the performance of physical systems by forming an Internet of Digital Twin (IoDT). This paper presents a comprehensive investigation of the digital twin network, tracing the evolution of digital twins and providing a classification of the key technologies, functional frameworks, and application domains of IoDT. This paper delves into the IoDT communication framework by studying the fundamental communication modes of IoDT, exploring its integration with advanced technologies such as edge computing, blockchain, 5G/6G networks, and machine learning to facilitate data transmission, interaction, and omni-directional sensing. By offering a broad perspective, the paper aims to deepen stakeholders’ understanding of current research and potential future developments, encouraging further exploration of IoDT technologies and their evolution.

Drawing on pioneering implementations across pharmaceutical, automotive, retail, and manufacturing sectors with companies like Walmart, Pfizer, and Siemens, we distill critical lessons learned. Our findings indicate that while technical challenges persist, organizational factors-such as cross-functional governance and partner ecosystem management-often emerge as the most critical determinants of implementation success. Author: Indraganti, S. P.; Vappangi, S.; Mishra, A. K.; Mathe, S. E.; Nasir, A. A.; Deepa, T.; Gupta, N.
Title: Survey of Cooperative NOMA for Beyond 5G: State-of-the-Art, Applications and Research Directions
Publication Title: IEEE Open Journal of the Communications Society
Abstract Note: This survey provides a comprehensive overview of Cooperative non orthogonal multiple access (C-NOMA) systems, where cooperative relaying enhances reliability, extends coverage, and strengthens system robustness. The study begins by classifying the fundamental structures of C-NOMA into two key categories: user-assisted relaying, where end-user devices forward information to other users, and dedicated relaying, where separate relay nodes assist transmission. Beyond its basic principles, the survey explores the integration of C-NOMA with advanced technologies such as cognitive radio (CR), full-duplex (FD) transmission, simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT), power line communication (PLC), multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO), heterogeneous networks (HetNets), rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA), visible light communication (VLC), and intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRS). These integrations significantly improve energy efficiency, spectral utilization, and coverage reliability. Moreover, artificial intelligence (AI), including deep reinforcement learning (DRL) and federated learning (FL), is identified as a vital enabler for intelligent power allocation, relay selection, and user clustering, addressing the limitations of traditional optimization approaches. This survey elaborates in detail the integration of C-NOMA with blockchain, edge computing, quantum computing, extended reality (XR), i.e., virtual reality/augmented reality (VR/AR), and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV). Furthermore, this survey identifies quantum-enabled C-NOMA as a transformative paradigm, where quantum key distribution (QKD) ensures physical layer security (PLS), and quantum machine learning (QML) enhances interference mitigation and large-scale optimization. Performance evaluation in terms of spectral efficiency (SE), energy efficiency, and quality-of-service (QoS) requirements is critically analyzed, with special emphasis on challenges such as accurate channel state information (CSI) acquisition, robust successive interference cancellation (SIC), scalable relay selection, and security in heterogeneous environments. In summary, this survey consolidates the state-of-the-art developments in C-NOMA and outlines future research directions, including AI-driven optimization, quantum-assisted communication, UAV and satellite integration, reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-enabled designs, and hybrid OMA-NOMA switching. By addressing these open challenges, C-NOMA is expected to serve as a cornerstone for secure, energy-efficient, and ultra-reliable connectivity in 6G and beyond, enabling massive IoT, autonomous systems, and next-generation smart city infrastructures.

Abstract Note: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) systems significantly rely on efficient data processing. This paper presents a comprehensive review of data-processing architectures and swarm-learning methodologies for UAV swarm systems using a cross-layer analytical framework. The proposed framework supports practical decision-making by jointly evaluating reliability, autonomy, and operational efficiency in response to real-time mission requirements. It identifies the key challenges that hinder real-world deployment and presents a research roadmap for next-generation UAV systems that emphasizes adaptive communication, resource-aware distributed intelligence, and secure collaborative learning. Author: Agarkar, A. A.; Motewar, S.; Khullar, L.; Kalbhairav, C.; Bhalerao, K.
Title: A Hybrid Machine Learning and Heuristic-Based Framework for Real-Time DDoS Detection in IoT and 5G Networks
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Intelligent and Innovative Technologies in Computing, Electrical and Electronics (IITCEE)
Abstract Note: The rapid growth of Internet of Things (IoT) devices and 5G network capabilities results in a broadened threat landscape and increased the potential of Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks. Whereas detectors can be signature-based (traditional Intrusion Detection Systems - IDS), they are ineffective against zero-day and complex multi-vector attacks; furthermore, while entirely machine learning (ML)-based solutions are available with premier accuracy performance, they also require immense latency and do not guarantee operation in resource-constrained networks. In response to this impasse, we propose a novel, lightweight hybrid DDoS discovery framework that combines a machine learning classifier with adaptive threshold heuristics. We will employ a Logistic Regression model, chosen for its fidelity to predictive performance, along with its ability to relate each feature of the model. We trained the Logistic Regression model with traffic features, which, with the help of network tools, computes packet rate, byte rate, distribution of protocols, and the entropy of TCP flags. This ML model is integrated with a dynamic thresholding mechanism that will send alerts as soon as flood traffic is detected, allowing for near real time responses. The system has been developed in a modular software architecture that combines Scapy for packet processing with a Flask based web interface for visualization and monitoring in real time. We showed extensive evaluation with a custom testbed that simulates a baseline traffic load and several various types of DDoS attack vectors (SYN, UDP, ICMP floods), our hybrid approach achieved an detection accuracy of 95.2 %, precision of 94.8%, recall of 95.5%, and a false positive rate of only 3.9%. Importantly, the threshold heuristic effectively provides initial detection latencies of less than 200ms; the ML classification works in periodic batches every 50 ms. This combination of methods produced a better trade-off between speed, and accuracy, than any of the methods deployed separately. The system's low computational footprint makes it especially suitable for use in small-to-medium enterprises, academic testbeds, and as a peripheral monitoring module in Software-Defined Networking (SDN) environments. We conclude by outlining a future roadmap that includes integrating federated learning to ensure privacy, blockchain for immutable audit logs, and lightweight deep learning models (e.g., Quantized CNNs) for edge-leveraging.

Author: Khan, N. M.; Bhattacharya, P.; Mattar, E. A.; Kumar, A.; Roy, S.; Shetty, S.
Title: B-LATF: blockchain assisted federated unlearning framework for trusted forgetting in 6G edge networks
Publication Title: 9th IET Smart Cities Symposium (SCS 2025)
Abstract Note: Recently, in Sixth Generation (6G) edge networks, Federated Learning (FL) driven communication is marked with rising concerns of privacy and adversarial threats. To address this, Federated Unlearning (FU) introduces a forgetting mechanism on user data, which allows specific data removal. As FU methods employ static policies, this introduces challenges of legal data man-dates, adversarial attacks, and the accumulation of stale data collected over time. Thus, a joint optimization on the aforementioned forgetting issues are required, termed as Legal, Adversarial, and Temporal Forgetting (LATF) in 6G edge networks. The proposed framework, B-LATF, introduces a permissioned Blockchain (BC) assisted LATF that leverages a Smart Contract (SC) based policy-driven service network. Firstly, the framework allows authorized users to communicate via logged events in blockchain. Secondly, an adaptive anomaly filter is presented that quarantines malicious updates, while a data-age policy is employed to prune obsolete client contributions. The framework is simulated over a non-Independently and non-Identically Distributed (non-IID) setting on the CIFAR-10 benchmark dataset over state-of-the-art schemes like FedEraser, FedU, and FedMUA for 100 edge clients. In simulation, LATF demonstrates an average of 85.6% unlearning accuracy, with an improvement of three times over FL retraining cost (against all schemes), at a low forgetting latency of 2.18 seconds approximately. The proposed results demonstrate its resilience to build a trusted LATF deployment in 6G edge networks.

Future research should focus on multi-agent federated reinforcement learning [21], transportation-energy cross-domain coordination, trusted privacy protection, and policy-technology-market coupling simulation, so as to promote the evolution of DRL from theoretical verification to engineering application, and provide theoretical support and technical paths for building a safe, efficient and low-carbon smart grid.
